# Internal architecture specific variables that should not be changed by the [L4024-4025]
# user. x86_64 images get an MBR, the most portable form for BIOS and UEFI. [L4025-4061]
# User controllable size of the HDD image, in MiB. [L4061-4064]
# Internal HDD geometry that should not be changed by the user. Older mtools [L4064-4065]
# require one; 64 heads of 32 sectors make a cylinder exactly 1 MiB in size. [L4065-4070]
# Internal HDD partition layout that should not be changed by the user. sgdisk [L4070-4071]
# lays the partition out as GPT, even where it then converts the table to MBR, [L4071-4072]

# Toolchain for building the 'limine' executable for the host. [L4078-4136]
# Date the source by the tarball, not the release inside it, so that what [L4136-4137]
# is made from it is remade whenever it is extracted. Not by the clock, as [L4137-4138]
# some touch use a finer one than file writes, dating it after what follows. [L4138-4144]
# The utility depends on records of the variables it is built with, named [L4144-4145]

    19	     1	# Rustix agent instructions
    20	     2	
    21	     3	These instructions apply to every coding agent working in this repository. Read this file before changing code. For the architecture and detailed subsystem contracts, use the linked documents under `docs/`; this file summarizes the rules agents must preserve.
    22	     4	
    23	     5	## Project mission
    24	     6	
    25	     7	Rustix is an experimental 64-bit, Unix-like operating system with its own Rust kernel. Limine is the external boot protocol/loader only. Do not describe Limine, a host shell, or a userspace project as the Rustix kernel.
    26	     8	
    27	     9	The kernel is `no_std` and targets `x86_64-unknown-none`. Rust is the implementation language for kernel and OS components. The repository currently uses a Python standard-library script only to assemble and smoke-test the boot image; it does not replace kernel or OS functionality.
    28	    10	
    29	    11	Unix-like behavior is a long-term design goal, not a claim of POSIX compatibility. Make unsupported behavior explicit rather than approximating it silently.
    30	    12	
    31	    13	## Current project status — read before planning
    32	    14	
    33	    15	The source contains:
    34	    16	
    35	    17	- A Limine-based x86_64 kernel entry, linker layout, serial diagnostics, and boot-memory reporting.
    36	    18	- A separate allocation-free `no_std` `crabshell` parser crate and a kernel-mode COM1 shell frontend.
    37	    19	- A volatile, fixed-capacity RAM filesystem used by the shell.
    38	    20	- A validated, fixed-capacity boot memory-map snapshot, CPUID/address-width reporting, and gated read-only EFER.NXE/IA32_PAT reporting.
    39	    21	- A fixed-capacity physical frame allocator retained in `BootInfo`; Crabshell's `meminfo` command reports counts. No kernel service currently allocates frames for mappings or other services.
    40	    22	- Pure 4 KiB mapping-range validation, leaf-PTE bit encoding, and PAT layout parsing in `src/paging.rs`; these helpers check alignment, address widths, canonical virtual ranges, W^X, NXE input, and PAT indices. Boot separately captures EFER.NXE and `IA32_PAT` read-only when supported. No code establishes frame ownership, mapping coverage, or effective MTRR cache semantics, or modifies page tables.
    41	    23	- Bootstrap GDT/TSS/IDT setup and fatal exception handlers for vectors 0–31. Double faults use an IST stack and page faults report CR2. Opt-in QEMU tests inject a page fault and invalid opcode and verify diagnostics plus fatal halt; maskable IRQs remain disabled and exceptions are not recoverable.
    42	    24	
    43	    25	Important incomplete work:
    44	    26	
    45	    27	- Milestone 0's local exit criteria were met on 2026-10-16: `just verify` passed from both the working tree and a clean detached worktree in WSL2 Ubuntu 24.04. The detached worktree had an empty `target` directory, so the run exercised fresh Limine download/host-tool compilation, formatting, 19 host tests, target check, optimized build, image creation, and the 20-second QEMU prompt smoke test. Hosted CI has not been observed.
    46	    28	- A separate interactive `just run` session exercised directory navigation and create/write/append/read/copy/move/list/remove operations; `cp` replaced an existing destination, `rmdir` rejected a nonempty directory and succeeded after its child was removed, and unsupported `memtest` was rejected as expected. Boot snapshot tests and QEMU boot-metadata reporting were exercised. Structural checks still cannot prove that a Limine-provided non-null pointer is mapped or readable; that remains a loader trust boundary.
    47	    29	- Milestone 0 is closed for local acceptance; hosted CI remains pending. Milestone 1's validation criteria are met for the current Limine path, subject to the documented pointer-readability trust boundary. Milestone 2 is **in progress**, not complete. The frame allocator specifies token ownership and preserves the token on failed deallocation; unique allocator-instance use is still caller-enforced. CPU address widths, physical map bounds, protocol-scoped HHDM range arithmetic, Limine executable image bases, page-aligned linker-defined kernel segment bounds, and gated read-only EFER.NXE/IA32_PAT reporting are checked; the segment bounds were reported in QEMU but do not prove inherited page-table coverage or permissions. The transition-critical mapping inventory is documented. `just fault-smoke` has validated controlled page-fault/CR2 and invalid-opcode diagnostics plus fatal halting in QEMU. Rustix still inherits Limine's page tables; their root and complete live mapping extents are not inspected, MTRR interactions are not validated, and there is no kernel-owned page-table manager, heap, or live frame-allocation caller.
    48	    30	- There is no scheduler, userspace, syscall ABI, persistent filesystem, user/kernel isolation, or general IRQ subsystem.
    49	    31

    67	    49	
    68	    50	## Repository map
    69	    51	
    70	    52	- `src/main.rs` — freestanding entry, boot snapshot acquisition, panic path, and shell handoff.
    71	    53	- `src/boot.rs` — mutable Limine requests, structural response/range validation, owned `BootInfo`, and boot diagnostics.
    72	    54	- `src/memory.rs` — allocation-free memory-map, address-width, canonical-address, Limine HHDM-range, and linker-defined kernel segment validation.
    73	    55	- `src/frame.rs` — bounded physical-frame allocator core; it only uses validated `Usable` ranges, reserves the first MiB, and has fixed range metadata.
    74	    56	- `src/paging.rs` — pure checked range and 4 KiB leaf-PTE bit construction for future mappings; no table access or physical-memory dereference.
    75	    57	- `src/shell.rs` — serial line editor and kernel-side Crabshell executor.
    76	    58	- `src/vfs.rs` — fixed-capacity volatile RAM filesystem and host-side tests.
    77	    59	- `crates/crabshell/` — separate `no_std` parser crate. It has no terminal, filesystem, or kernel dependencies.
    78	    60	- `src/arch/x86_64/serial.rs` — polling COM1 driver for shell input/output.
    79	    61	- `src/arch/x86_64/interrupts.rs` — bootstrap GDT/TSS/IDT, assembly stubs, and fatal exception diagnostics.
    80	    62	- `src/arch/x86_64/cpu.rs` — CPUID identification and selected feature reporting.
    81	    63	- `src/arch/x86_64/keyboard.rs` — raw, non-blocking PS/2-compatible scancode polling; not an input subsystem.
    82	    64	- `src/arch/x86_64/io.rs` — narrow port-I/O wrappers.
    83	    65	- `linker.ld`, `.cargo/config.toml`, `rust-toolchain.toml` — target, linker, and toolchain configuration.
    84	    66	- `limine.conf`, `scripts/boot.py` — boot configuration and pinned image/emulator workflow.
    85	    67	- `justfile` — supported development commands.
    86	    68	- `.github/workflows/ci.yml` — CI validation workflow.
    87	    69	
    88	    70	## Engineering rules
    89	    71	
    90	    72	### Keep changes incremental and coherent
    91	    73	
    92	    74	1. Inspect the relevant source, tests, docs, and call sites before editing.
    93	    75	2. State assumptions, invariants, and failure behavior for new kernel interfaces.
    94	    76	3. Prefer small vertical slices that compile and can be tested over broad scaffolding or placeholder APIs.
    95	    77	4. Update tests and documentation alongside behavior changes.
    96	    78	5. Do not change unrelated code, rename files gratuitously, add speculative features, or rewrite project history.
    97	    79	6. Do not commit or create branches unless the user explicitly asks.
    98	    80	
    99	    81	### Rust and dependency policy
   100	    82	
   101	    83	- Preserve the kernel's `no_std`/freestanding constraints. Do not introduce `std` into kernel code.
   102	    84	- Prefer `core` and existing in-tree abstractions. Do not add third-party Rust dependencies without a concrete need and compatibility/security review.
   103	    85	- Keep the Crabshell parser independent of kernel I/O and VFS implementation. Kernel execution belongs in `src/shell.rs` or an appropriate kernel service.
   104	    86	- Do not add allocation-dependent APIs before a real heap exists. Fixed-capacity structures must document their limits and exhaustion behavior.
   105	    87	- Respect the workspace structure and the host-testable `rustix-kernel` library versus freestanding `rustix` binary boundary.
   106	    88	
   107	    89	### Unsafe and hardware code
   108	    90	
   109	    91	Unsafe code is expected only at explicit hardware, boot-protocol, assembly, or raw-memory boundaries. Keep each unsafe block narrow and document the invariant that makes it sound. Do not add broad `unsafe impl`, mutable global references, unchecked pointer arithmetic, or unreviewed inline/global assembly.
   110	    92	
   111	    93	Before changing boot or memory code, account for these facts:
   112	    94	
   113	    95	- Limine fills response pointers before `_start`; the request records must remain writable in the ELF image.
   114	    96	- Rustix validates nullness, alignment, counts, arithmetic, and physical ranges, but cannot prove that a non-null bootloader pointer is readable.
   115	    97	- Physical ranges are half-open `[start, end)` and must use checked arithmetic.
   116	    98	- Only regions classified `Usable` may enter the frame allocator. ACPI, bootloader-reclaimable, framebuffer, reserved, unknown, and other types are not free frames.
   117	    99	- A `Frame` is a physical address, not a dereferenceable pointer. Do not access it through the HHDM or change CR3 until an explicit, reviewed mapping policy and ownership proof exist.
   118	   100	- The kernel currently inherits Limine's page tables. Do not casually replace or mutate them: preserve the executing kernel, boot stack, `BootInfo`, request/response data, exception stacks, and mappings needed to continue execution.
   119	   101	- The exception setup is fatal-only. It does not enable maskable interrupts, configure a PIC/APIC, or provide recovery. Do not call `sti` or claim interrupt support without an IRQ design and tests.
   120	   102	- The shell and VFS run in ring 0 and are not isolated or secure.
   121	   103	
   122	   104	For hardware changes, document assumptions about CPU mode, selectors, stacks, page permissions, interrupt state, and failure handling. Avoid new architecture mechanisms that cannot be statically reviewed or validated.
   123	   105	
   124	   106	### Shell and filesystem contract
   125	   107	
   126	   108	- Crabshell is presently a kernel-mode serial shell, not a userspace program or a POSIX shell.
   127	   109	- Its parser is a separate `no_std`, allocation-free crate; retain that boundary.
   128	   110	- The RAM filesystem is volatile and bounded. Preserve explicit errors and test capacity, path, and mutation edge cases.
   129	   111	- Do not imply persistence, permissions, links, process launching, or shell features that do not exist.
   130	   112	- Update the parser tests and `docs/architecture/crabshell.md` when adding or changing commands.
   131	   113	
   132	   114	## Validation workflow
   133	   115	
   134	   116	Run the narrowest relevant checks first, then broaden them. From the repository root, the supported commands are:
   135	   117	
   136	   118	```sh
   137	   119	just fmt
   138	   120	just test
   139	   121	just check
   140	   122	just build
   141	   123	just image
   142	   124	just smoke
   143	   125	just verify
   144	   126	```
   145	   127	
   146	   128	`just test` runs host-side library tests (memory-map validation, frame allocator, VFS, and Crabshell parser). `just check` checks `x86_64-unknown-none`; `just build` links the optimized ELF. `just verify` includes formatting, host tests, target check, pinned Limine image creation, and QEMU prompt smoke test. Image/boot checks need Python, `xorriso`, QEMU, the Rust target, and network access for the first pinned Limine download; Linux/WSL also needs `cc` to build Limine's host utility.
   147	   129	
   148	   130	For changes to `src/main.rs`, `src/boot.rs`, linker/request configuration, `src/arch/x86_64/`, `src/frame.rs`, or paging/heap code, the intended full validation is `just verify`. If the environment does not permit a check, report the exact blocker and leave the corresponding roadmap criterion pending.
   149	   131	
   150	   132	Do not claim a check passed unless it was run and its successful result was observed. Editor diagnostics are useful but are not a substitute for `cargo test`, a target build, or QEMU. A target check is not a final link; a linked ELF is not proof of boot; a prompt smoke test is not proof of interactive shell behavior or physical-hardware correctness.
   151	   133	
   152	   134	## Completion criteria for agent changes
   153	   135	
   154	   136	Before reporting work complete:
   155	   137	
   156	   138	- Ensure source, tests, docs, and call sites agree.
   157	   139	- Review unsafe and hardware assumptions, including error paths and capacity limits.
   158	   140	- Run appropriate formatting/tests/build/boot checks, or clearly state why they could not run.
   159	   141	- Report files changed, behavior delivered, validation actually observed, and remaining risks.
   160	   142	- Keep milestone status accurate. A subsystem is not complete just because it has code.

````rustix/docs/development/building.md
     1	# Building Rustix
     2	
     3	## Prerequisites
     4	
     5	- Rust stable with `rustfmt`; the repository pins these in `rust-toolchain.toml`.
     6	- The `x86_64-unknown-none` target. The toolchain file requests it automatically; if needed, install it with `rustup target add x86_64-unknown-none`.
     7	- [`just`](https://just.systems/) to run the repository's named tasks.
     8	- Python 3.8 or newer (standard library only), with `python` on `PATH`; `xorriso`; and QEMU with `qemu-system-x86_64` for image creation and boot smoke tests.
     9	- A C compiler providing `cc` on Linux/WSL to build Limine's host utility from the pinned archive; Windows uses the bundled `limine.exe`.
    10	
    11	An ELF inspection tool such as `llvm-readelf` or `readelf` is useful when diagnosing linker output. The first image build downloads the pinned Limine v12.9.3 binary archive into `target/tools/` and verifies its published SHA-256 before extraction.
    12	
    13	## Common commands
    14	
    15	Run from the repository root:
    16	
    17	```sh
    18	just help
    19	just fmt       # check Rust formatting
    20	just test      # parser, RAM-filesystem, memory-map, and frame-allocator tests
    21	just check     # type-check the freestanding kernel target
    22	just build       # optimized kernel ELF
    23	just image       # hybrid BIOS/UEFI ISO at target/rustix.iso
    24	just debug-build # optimized kernel ELF with full debug symbols
    25	just debug-image # ISO built from the debug-symbol-enabled ELF
    26	just debug-run   # paused QEMU with a loopback GDB stub for Zed/CodeLLDB
    27	just smoke       # bounded QEMU boot to the Crabshell prompt
    28	just fault-smoke # inject page fault and invalid opcode, then restore the default image
    29	just run         # interactive serial shell in QEMU (Ctrl+C to stop)
    30	just verify      # fmt, workspace tests, target check, image, and QEMU smoke test
    31	```
    32	
    33	Equivalent Rust checks are `cargo fmt --all -- --check`, `cargo test --workspace --lib`, `cargo check --target x86_64-unknown-none`, and `cargo build --release --target x86_64-unknown-none`. Image creation and QEMU validation are provided by `scripts/boot.py` and are intentionally part of `just verify`.
    34	
    35	The optimized ELF is written to `target/x86_64-unknown-none/release/rustix`. `cargo check` checks the target without producing a boot image. The library tests run on the host and exercise code that does not require privileged instructions.
    36	
    37	## Target-specific linker setup
    38	
    39	`.cargo/config.toml` applies the Rustix linker script and x86_64 kernel constraints only to `x86_64-unknown-none`. `linker.ld` emits an ELF64 x86_64 image at the higher-half base, retains Limine request sections in a writable load segment for bootloader response pointers, defines `_start` as an assembly entry shim, and exports the load-image boundary symbols consumed by `BootInfo`. The shim captures the initial stack pointer before entering Rust. The build uses no third-party Rust crates; the boot protocol is represented by small in-tree Rust structures and constants.
    40	
    41	Changing the target, virtual base, relocation model, or request ABI requires updating the linker script, protocol documentation, and validation plan together. Do not use host builds of the kernel binary as evidence that the freestanding target links correctly.
    42	
    43	## Building and smoke-testing a boot image
    44	
    45	`limine.conf` boots the kernel immediately and enables 38,400-baud serial output. `just image` builds the ELF, fetches Limine v12.9.3's binary ZIP from its immutable GitHub release, checks the pinned SHA-256, prepares a BIOS/UEFI hybrid ISO, and installs the BIOS boot code. The Limine archive and extracted tools remain under ignored `target/`; no third-party binaries are checked into the source tree.
    46	
    47	`just smoke` launches `target/rustix.iso` in `qemu-system-x86_64` with a 256 MiB q35 machine, headless display, captured COM1 output, and a 20-second deadline. QEMU is expected to remain running at the interactive shell; the runner terminates it at the deadline and requires the startup banner, Crabshell-ready message, and initial prompt. On a failure it prints the serial log. The log remains at `target/rustix-qemu-serial.log` for inspection.
    48	
    49	`just run` launches the same image with the serial port attached to the host terminal, allowing interactive shell use. Stop the emulator with `Ctrl+C`.
    50	
    51	## Debugging the kernel from Zed
    52	
    53	On the Windows Zed workspace with the repository built through WSL2, run the `Rustix: QEMU Debug Server` task from the task picker. It builds the release ELF with full DWARF debug information, creates the ISO, and starts QEMU paused with its GDB stub bound only to `127.0.0.1:1234`. Then open Zed's debugger (`F4`) and start `Rustix: QEMU (CodeLLDB)`. The configuration loads the ELF from the Windows worktree, maps WSL compiler paths back to the workspace, and sets a breakpoint at `rustix_start`; continue once from the initial reset stop to reach the Rust entry function. Stop QEMU with `Ctrl+C` in its task terminal.
    54	
    55	The debug build uses a per-command Cargo profile override and does not change the normal release profile. It writes to the usual release ELF and ISO paths, so a later `just build`, `just image`, or `just run` rebuilds the normal image. CodeLLDB remote debugging must be available in Zed. The GDB stub listens on loopback only; do not change this to a public interface.
    56	
    57	`just verify` includes the emulator smoke test and therefore needs Python 3, xorriso, QEMU, network access for the first Limine download, and the Rust target. `.github/workflows/ci.yml` installs the system tools on Ubuntu 24.04 and runs the same command. This verifies the boot path in CI; it is still not a substitute for testing physical hardware.
    58	
    59	## Troubleshooting
    60	
    61	- **Target not installed:** install `x86_64-unknown-none` as shown above.
    62	- **`just` not found:** install `just`; Rust-only checks can still be run with the Cargo commands above.
    63	- **`xorriso` or QEMU not found:** install the host image/emulator tools listed in prerequisites, then retry `just image` or `just smoke`.
    64	- **`cc` not found on Linux/WSL:** install a C compiler (for example, `build-essential` on Ubuntu), then retry `just image`.
    65	- **Limine SHA-256 mismatch:** the pinned archive may have changed or been corrupted; the script removes the mismatched download and refuses to use it. Check the official v12.9.3 release digest before changing the pin.
    66	- **Linker-script error:** build only for `x86_64-unknown-none`; confirm the invocation runs from the repository root so `linker.ld` resolves.
    67	- **No serial output:** inspect `target/rustix-qemu-serial.log` and QEMU's stderr. The image config and Rustix COM1 driver both use 38,400 baud.

```rustix/docs/architecture/memory.md
     1	# Memory-management direction
     2	
     3	## What exists now
     4	
     5	`src/memory.rs` contains an allocation-free `MemoryMapBuilder` that copies Limine ranges into validated half-open physical regions. It rejects empty ranges, `base + length` overflow, overlapping ranges, empty maps, and maps exceeding the fixed 256-region capacity. Known Limine types remain distinct, and unknown type values are preserved. Host-side tests cover range validation/classification, canonical-address boundaries, physical-width bounds, and HHDM range arithmetic. `src/boot.rs` stores the resulting map in an owned boot snapshot and reports usable bytes.
     6	
     7	`src/frame.rs` provides a fixed-capacity allocator core with host-side tests. It only manages complete 4 KiB frames inside validated `Usable` regions, reserves the first MiB, and coalesces adjacent free ranges. The ownership contract assumes one allocator instance per physical map: within that instance, each eligible frame is owned either by its free-range table or by a non-copyable `Frame` token while allocated. The public constructor does not enforce unique instances, so callers must not initialize multiple allocators for the same physical map; the current boot path retains one allocator in `BootInfo`. `allocate` returns `None` when no free frame remains. `deallocate` consumes the token only on success; on any error, including free-range-table exhaustion, it returns a `DeallocationError` containing the original token and leaves allocator state unchanged. The range tables each have a fixed `MAX_FRAME_RANGES` capacity, so fragmentation can prevent a frame from being returned until nearby ranges coalesce. No kernel service currently allocates frames for mappings or other work.
     8	
     9	`Frame::address()` is a physical address value, not a dereferenceable pointer and not a proof that the frame is mapped. CPU diagnostics now read `CR4.LA57` to report the active linear-address width (48 or 57 bits) and query `CPUID.80000008H` for physical and maximum linear-address widths when available. Boot-protocol pointers are checked against the active width, with host tests for 48- and 57-bit canonical boundaries. These facts do not prove that any physical address is mapped.
    10	
    11	`src/paging.rs` adds pure, host-tested 4 KiB mapping groundwork and decodes the inherited CR3 root address plus its low-bit interpretation. The CR3 decoder validates the physical-address width and reserved bits and interprets the low 12 bits according to the active `CR4.PCIDE` state; it does not dereference the root. The mapping-range validator requires a known physical-address width, checked aligned bounds, canonical virtual endpoints in one canonical half, and rejects writable-executable permissions. A validated range can encode the raw bits of one 4 KiB leaf PTE, including supervisor/user and write permissions, NX when the caller confirms EFER.NXE, and a bounded three-bit PAT index. `PatLayout` parses a supplied `IA32_PAT` value and selects WB, UC, or WC indices. `MtrrMemoryType`, `VariableMtrr`, `FixedMtrrRanges`, and `MtrrLayout` parse caller-supplied register values and resolve the MTRR type at one physical address, including fixed-range priority and specified variable-overlap rules; undefined overlaps fail closed. This is a pure model only: `src/arch/x86_64/cpu.rs` does not capture MTRR state, and no code combines PAT with MTRR to establish an effective cache type for a mapping. The CPU reads EFER.NXE only when NX is supported and reads `IA32_PAT` only when PAT is supported; these reads are diagnostic and do not modify CPU state. None of these helpers proves frame ownership or HHDM coverage, inspects table entries, or modifies hardware page tables. No page mapping operation or CR3 transition is implemented.
    12	
    13	The requested Limine base revision is 3. Its protocol maps only `Usable`, `BootloaderReclaimable`, `ExecutableAndModules`, and `Framebuffer` memory-map regions into the HHDM; reserved, ACPI, bad, and unknown regions are not in that mapping set. HHDM mappings use at least 4 KiB granularity and may cover page-aligned bytes beyond unaligned region boundaries. On x86_64, inherited HHDM mappings are supervisor RWX, normally write-back cached, with framebuffer mappings write-combining when PAT is available. Therefore an HHDM offset is not a blanket physical-memory access grant, and inherited HHDM permissions are not Rustix's future W^X policy. See the [Limine base revision 3 protocol](https://github.com/limine-bootloader/limine-protocol/blob/trunk/PROTOCOL.md#base-revision-3) and its memory-layout/caching sections.
    14	
    15	The boot snapshot now rejects physical map ranges beyond the reported CPUID physical-address width when that CPUID leaf is available. For base revision 3 HHDM-mapped types, it also validates the page-rounded physical span, checked `offset + address` arithmetic, and canonical endpoints in the active linear-address width. If the CPU does not report a physical width, the physical-bound check is skipped and no mapping caller may treat the bound as known. These checks are derived from metadata and Limine's protocol contract; they do not inspect page tables or prove that a non-null loader pointer is readable. Rustix still does not dereference physical memory through the HHDM. Rustix-owned mappings should be non-executable by default; executable kernel text must be explicit. MMIO requires an explicit device range and cache policy, and guard regions must remain unmapped. A page-table transition must preserve the kernel image, active stacks, boot data, descriptor tables, and any loader mappings still needed. Rustix does not reclaim bootloader memory, own or replace the inherited Limine page tables, or provide a heap. Bootstrap GDT/TSS/IDT setup and fatal exception diagnostics live in `src/arch/x86_64/interrupts.rs`; they do not enable maskable IRQs.
    16	
    17	## Mapping inventory before a CR3 transition
    18	
    19	The current runtime has several mappings that a future page-table transition must preserve. The address sources and remaining gaps are:
    20	
    21	- **Kernel ELF image:** `linker.ld` places `.text`, `.rodata`, `.limine_requests`, `.data`, `.bss`, and `.got` in three `PT_LOAD` segments: RX text, read-only rodata, and RW data/BSS. It exports `__kernel_start` and `__kernel_end` around the complete loadable image, plus page-aligned bounds for each segment. `BootInfo` checks that Limine's reported virtual base matches the linker start, validates ordered contiguous segment bounds covering the rounded image, derives corresponding half-open physical ranges from the executable physical base with checked arithmetic, and validates canonical virtual and reported physical address widths. The release ELF and QEMU runtime report both showed the three aligned ranges on 2026-10-21. The RX, R/NX, and RW/NX labels describe the linker segment intent; these are linker/boot metadata, not proof that the inherited page tables map every page or enforce those permissions, nor proof that loader pointers are readable. The memory-map `ExecutableAndModules` entries remain illustrative, not an authoritative kernel-image extent.
    22	- **Active stack and `BootInfo`:** The assembly `_start` shim captures Limine's entry `RSP` before any Rust prologue. Under the SysV entry convention the synthetic return slot occupies 8 bytes, so `RSP + 8` is the exclusive stack top. Keep them mapped until the copy and validation finish; any later reclaim must be explicit rather than reclaiming the whole bootloader-reclaimable class.

Rustix does not inspect root entries or inventory the live mappings.     28	## Initial kernel-owned mapping policy (design only)
    29	
    30	A first Rustix-owned x86_64 root should use 4 KiB pages only and require NX support; if NX is unavailable, abort before switching. Preserve ELF permissions exactly: text RX, rodata R/NX, and `.limine_requests`/data/BSS/GOT RW/NX. Reject W+X mappings. Exclude the complete physical kernel-image span from the generic HHDM in the first implementation so no writable direct-map alias can undermine text or rodata permissions. Ordinary RAM HHDM mappings should be RW/NX and WB.
    31	
    32	Preserve the inherited PAT/MTRR configuration during the first transition. The current boot report reads the active `IA32_PAT` value when PAT is supported and parses WB/UC/WC entries, but does not yet inspect MTRRs or establish effective cache types for physical ranges. Under Limine base revision 3 on x86_64, use PAT index 0 for WB, index 3 for UC, and index 5 for WC only when the active configuration is verified. Map MMIO only from explicit device ranges and use UC by default; do not infer MMIO from generic reserved memory-map entries. A framebuffer may use WC only after its response and cache policy are explicitly validated. COM1 uses port I/O and requires no MMIO mapping.
    33	
    34	Do not use huge pages in the first root; add them only when physical coverage, permissions, and cache attributes are uniform across the entire huge-page extent. Future Rustix-owned downward-growing stacks should have at least one 4 KiB unmapped guard page below them. The Limine bootstrap stack has no known guard, so none may be assumed there.
    35	
    36	Never modify Limine's active page tables in place. Build a separate candidate root from owned frames, leave the inherited root and its backing memory intact, and do not switch CR3 until every transition-critical mapping has been preserved and checked. Any pre-switch failure must discard the candidate root and return its frames without changing the active root. This policy is not yet implemented; Rustix does not inspect the inherited root or replace CR3.
    37	
    38	## Planned memory layers
    39	
    40	1. **Validated physical regions:** implemented as a fixed-capacity owned snapshot; allocator ownership and reclaim policy remain future work.
    41	2. **Frame allocator integration:** the bounded core is initialized from `BootInfo`; add real allocation callers only after the page-mapping policy and ownership rules are implemented.
    42	3. **Kernel virtual memory:** Rustix still runs on inherited Limine page tables. Before replacing them, preserve the executing kernel, bootstrap/Ring-0 stacks, request/response data, and exception stacks; define the HHDM extent and explicit mapping permissions/cache attributes.     43	4. **Heap:** add a global allocator only after frame allocation and page mapping are initialized. Define allocation failure behavior for kernel and interrupt contexts.
    44	5. **Process address spaces:** isolate userspace; define copy-in/copy-out helpers and never treat user pointers as kernel references.
    45

    47	
    48	- Physical ranges use checked arithmetic and the half-open convention `[start, end)`.
    49	- Only complete frames in validated `Usable` regions enter the allocator; the first MiB remains reserved. Firmware and loader-reclaimable regions are not silently promoted to free memory.
    50	- Under the single-allocator-per-physical-map contract, a frame is represented by one allocator-free range or one caller-owned, non-copyable `Frame` token. Only a successful `deallocate` transfers the token back to the allocator; errors return the token and leave allocator ranges and accounting unchanged. The current public constructor relies on callers to enforce unique allocator instances.
    51	- `allocate` returns `None` on frame exhaustion. Metadata-capacity exhaustion is an explicit error, never silent loss of a frame.
    52	- A `Frame` address is physical, not directly dereferenceable. No HHDM translation, page-table mutation, or CR3 switch is permitted until address widths, mapping coverage, permissions/cache attributes, and transition-preservation requirements are established.
    53	- Mapping changes validate alignment, canonical addresses, ownership, and permissions before touching tables.
    54	- User-controlled addresses are validated on every syscall boundary; prior validation is not a substitute for access checks during later copies.
    55	- Tests cover unaligned edges, exact-boundary allocations, arithmetic overflow, overlaps, exhaustion, and unchanged state/ownership on failure.

```rustix/docs/security.md
     1	# Security and unsafe-code policy
     2	
     3	Rustix is an early kernel prototype, not a security-reviewed operating system. It has no user/kernel separation implementation, process isolation, security boundary, or supported deployment profile today.
     4	
     5	## Current unsafe boundaries
     6	
     7	- `src/arch/x86_64/io.rs` issues privileged x86 port-I/O instructions behind narrow driver wrappers.
     8	- `src/arch/x86_64/serial.rs` configures and writes to the legacy COM1 UART. It is intended for early kernel context only.
     9	- `src/arch/x86_64/keyboard.rs` reads raw bytes from a legacy PS/2-compatible controller; callers must poll without blocking.
    10	- `src/arch/x86_64/cpu.rs` executes CPUID for boot-time feature reporting and performs gated, read-only `RDMSR` reads of EFER.NXE and `IA32_PAT`. The EFER read is skipped unless CPUID reports NX; the PAT read is skipped unless CPUID reports PAT. These paths assume CPL 0 and architectural feature/MSR availability, and they do not write MSRs.
    11	- `src/arch/x86_64/interrupts.rs` loads the GDT/TSS/IDT and exception-entry assembly, reads CR2 on page faults, and halts after printing the saved context. The exception gates are kernel-only and maskable interrupts remain disabled.
    12	- `src/boot.rs` reads Limine response pointers and entries, then validates and copies range metadata into an owned boot snapshot. Nullness, alignment, count bounds, arithmetic, and range overlap are checked; the kernel still trusts Limine to make non-null response objects readable for the handoff lifetime.
    13	- `src/main.rs` uses `cli` and `hlt` to stop the bootstrap CPU after a fatal startup error.
    14	- `src/vfs.rs` and `src/shell.rs` provide a kernel-mode RAM filesystem and shell. They have no user/kernel isolation, permissions, persistence, or protection from kernel bugs; shell commands are trusted kernel code, not sandboxed applications.
    15	
    16	Unsafe blocks should remain as small as practical and state the assumptions that make each operation valid. Avoid widening `unsafe impl` or introducing raw-pointer-based public APIs without a documented safety argument. The PS/2 routine consumes bytes from the controller, including discarding auxiliary/error bytes, so it must only be used by a single owner of that controller until input serialization is designed. External boot inputs, user pointers, MMIO, and DMA must not be treated as trusted merely because current boot data is trusted.
    17	
    18	## Security requirements for future subsystems
    19	
    20	- Validate every physical range and checked address calculation before mapping or allocating it.
    21	- Enforce least privilege in page mappings; avoid writable-executable pages by default.
    22	- Keep user memory untrusted and use explicit copy-in/copy-out routines at syscall boundaries.
    23	- Define ownership and lifetime rules for descriptors, processes, shared memory, and device buffers.
    24	- Test malformed input and error paths as well as successful operation.
    25	- Do not claim isolation or security guarantees until those properties have end-to-end tests and review.

```

### # Boot protocol and kernel entry › ## Current boot contract › L5-6
```
Rustix currently expects a Limine-compatible x86_64 handoff. Limine is an external loader; it does not implement Rustix's kernel services. The kernel requests protocol base revision 3, the higher-half direct-map (HHDM) offset, the executable physical/virtual base addresses, and the memory map.

```

### # Boot protocol and kernel entry › ## Current boot contract › ### Entry sequence › L14-16
```
4. The kernel reads CPU address widths, active `CR4.PCIDE`, and raw CR3. It decodes CR3's physical root address and low-bit meaning against those CPU properties, without dereferencing the root. It reads EFER.NXE only when CPUID reports NX, and reads `IA32_PAT` only when CPUID reports PAT; these MSR reads do not change CPU state. It copies the HHDM, executable-address, and memory-map responses into an owned `BootInfo` snapshot, validates pointers against the active linear width, derives and validates the linker-defined kernel image span and its page-aligned text/rodata/data segment spans from Limine's executable bases, and derives the protocol-guaranteed minimum initial-stack span from the captured entry `RSP`. It validates physical bounds, stack HHDM arithmetic/coverage, and page-rounded HHDM arithmetic for protocol-mapped memory types. It then builds a frame allocator only from validated usable ranges and rejects malformed metadata before starting the shell.
5. The kernel reports raw CR3 and its decoded physical root/low bits when the reported width permits, physical and virtual kernel-image spans, linker-defined text RX, rodata R/NX, and data RW/NX segment spans, minimum protocol-guaranteed stack span, validated memory ranges, frame counts, CPU features/address widths, NXE state, and the active PAT value plus recognized WB/UC/WC indices, then seeds a volatile RAM filesystem and enters Crabshell on the serial console.
6. The shell busy-polls COM1 because no scheduler or UART interrupt handler exists yet. The kernel does not return to the loader.
```

### # Boot protocol and kernel entry › ## Current boot contract › ### Entry sequence › L18-19
```
The linker exports page-aligned virtual bounds for each of the kernel's three load segments. Boot validates their order, contiguity, coverage of the rounded image span, and derived physical ranges, then reports them with the permissions intended by `linker.ld`. Boot also decodes CR3's root physical address and active low-bit interpretation. These are validated linker/boot metadata only: Rustix does not inspect the inherited page tables, so it has not established that the segments are mapped or that their live permissions match the ELF flags.

```

### # Boot protocol and kernel entry › ## Failure behavior and limitations › L36-37

The repository includes a Limine v12.9.3 binary archive pin with SHA-256 verification, a hybrid ISO recipe, and a bounded QEMU serial smoke test that checks Crabshell's prompt. On 2026-10-16, `just verify` passed in WSL2 Ubuntu 24.04 on both the working tree and a clean detached worktree with an empty `target` directory; the clean run fetched and built the pinned Limine host utility, created the image, and QEMU reported boot metadata before reaching the prompt. Milestone 0's local exit criteria are met. Hosted CI has not been observed. There is still no framebuffer console, reboot/shutdown interface, or broader boot-protocol compatibility test. The available serial and keyboard drivers do not imply a general device model.

### # Crabshell and the early RAM filesystem › ## Commands › L57-58
```
The grammar intentionally does not yet support quoted paths, escaped quotes, variables, pipes, redirection, globbing, command substitution, history, or a process launcher. Input is a single ASCII line (up to 256 bytes) from the serial port.

```

### # Crabshell and the early RAM filesystem › ## RAM filesystem contract › L62-64
```
- Path components are limited to 31 UTF-8 bytes; file contents are limited to 1024 bytes each.
- Paths may be absolute or relative and support repeated `/`, `.`, and `..`.
- `write` replaces a file; `append` adds bytes; `touch` never truncates.
```

### # Crabshell and the early RAM filesystem › ## Tests and limitations › L71-72
```
Host-side tests cover path traversal, file create/write/append/copy/move/remove, entry kinds, path rendering, directory emptiness, and the parser's syntax/arity. The automated QEMU smoke test checks that the serial shell reaches its prompt. A separate manual `just run` session exercised `help`, `ls`, `meminfo`, `mkdir`, `cd`, `touch`, `write`, `append`, `cat`, `cp`, `mv`, `rm`, `rmdir`, and `pwd`; `cat` returned the appended text, `cp` replaced an existing destination with source contents, `rmdir` refused a nonempty directory, and `pwd` returned to `/home/rustix` after cleanup. The unsupported `memtest` command produced the expected unknown-command response. These checks do not emulate reboot persistence, exhaustively test shell interactions, or prove isolation. Since the shell runs in ring 0, a parser or filesystem bug can panic the entire kernel. This implementation must not be presented as a secure or POSIX-compliant shell.

```

## Matches in rustix\docs\architecture\memory.md

### # Memory-management direction › ## What exists now › L7-8
```
`src/frame.rs` provides a fixed-capacity allocator core with host-side tests. It only manages complete 4 KiB frames inside validated `Usable` regions, reserves the first MiB, and coalesces adjacent free ranges. The ownership contract assumes one allocator instance per physical map: within that instance, each eligible frame is owned either by its free-range table or by a non-copyable `Frame` token while allocated. The public constructor does not enforce unique instances, so callers must not initialize multiple allocators for the same physical map; the current boot path retains one allocator in `BootInfo`. `allocate` returns `None` when no free frame remains. `deallocate` consumes the token only on success; on any error, including free-range-table exhaustion, it returns a `DeallocationError` containing the original token and leaves allocator state unchanged. The range tables each have a fixed `MAX_FRAME_RANGES` capacity, so fragmentation can prevent a frame from being returned until nearby ranges coalesce. No kernel service currently allocates frames for mappings or other work.

```

### # Memory-management direction › ## What exists now › L11-12
```
`src/paging.rs` adds pure, host-tested 4 KiB mapping groundwork and decodes the inherited CR3 root address plus its low-bit interpretation. The CR3 decoder validates the physical-address width and reserved bits and interprets the low 12 bits according to the active `CR4.PCIDE` state; it does not dereference the root. The mapping-range validator requires a known physical-address width, checked aligned bounds, canonical virtual endpoints in one canonical half, and rejects writable-executable permissions. A validated range can encode the raw bits of one 4 KiB leaf PTE, including supervisor/user and write permissions, NX when the caller confirms EFER.NXE, and a bounded three-bit PAT index. `PatLayout` parses a supplied `IA32_PAT` value and selects WB, UC, or WC indices. `MtrrMemoryType`, `VariableMtrr`, `FixedMtrrRanges`, and `MtrrLayout` parse caller-supplied register values and resolve the MTRR type at one physical address, including fixed-range priority and specified variable-overlap rules; undefined overlaps fail closed. This is a pure model only: `src/arch/x86_64/cpu.rs` does not capture MTRR state, and no code combines PAT with MTRR to establish an effective cache type for a mapping. The CPU reads EFER.NXE only when NX is supported and reads `IA32_PAT` only when PAT is supported; these reads are diagnostic and do not modify CPU state. None of these helpers proves frame ownership or HHDM coverage, inspects table entries, or modifies hardware page tables. No page mapping operation or CR3 transition is implemented.

```

### # Memory-management direction › ## What exists now › L13-14
```
The requested Limine base revision is 3. Its protocol maps only `Usable`, `BootloaderReclaimable`, `ExecutableAndModules`, and `Framebuffer` memory-map regions into the HHDM; reserved, ACPI, bad, and unknown regions are not in that mapping set. HHDM mappings use at least 4 KiB granularity and may cover page-aligned bytes beyond unaligned region boundaries. On x86_64, inherited HHDM mappings are supervisor RWX, normally write-back cached, with framebuffer mappings write-combining when PAT is available. Therefore an HHDM offset is not a blanket physical-memory access grant, and inherited HHDM permissions are not Rustix's future W^X policy. See the [Limine base revision 3 protocol](https://github.com/limine-bootloader/limine-protocol/blob/trunk/PROTOCOL.md#base-revision-3) and its memory-layout/caching sections.

```

### # Memory-management direction › ## What exists now › L15-16
```
The boot snapshot now rejects physical map ranges beyond the reported CPUID physical-address width when that CPUID leaf is available. For base revision 3 HHDM-mapped types, it also validates the page-rounded physical span, checked `offset + address` arithmetic, and canonical endpoints in the active linear-address width. If the CPU does not report a physical width, the physical-bound check is skipped and no mapping caller may treat the bound as known. These checks are derived from metadata and Limine's protocol contract; they do not inspect page tables or prove that a non-null loader pointer is readable. Rustix still does not dereference physical memory through the HHDM. Rustix-owned mappings should be non-executable by default; executable kernel text must be explicit. MMIO requires an explicit device range and cache policy, and guard regions must remain unmapped. A page-table transition must preserve the kernel image, active stacks, boot data, descriptor tables, and any loader mappings still needed. Rustix does not reclaim bootloader memory, own or replace the inherited Limine page tables, or provide a heap. Bootstrap GDT/TSS/IDT setup and fatal exception diagnostics live in `src/arch/x86_64/interrupts.rs`; they do not enable maskable IRQs.

```

    11	pub struct CpuInfo {
    12	    pub vendor: [u8; 12],
    13	    pub max_basic_leaf: u32,
    14	    pub max_extended_leaf: u32,
    15	    pub has_sse2: bool,
    16	    pub has_nx: bool,
    17	    pub nx_enabled: bool,

    20	    pub has_1g_pages: bool,
    21	    pub has_long_mode: bool,
    22	    pub has_la57: bool,

    25	    pub active_linear_address_bits: u8,
    26	    pub pcid_enabled: bool,
    27	}
    28	
    29	/// Read CPUID identity, selected feature bits, and supported read-only MSR state.
    30	pub fn identify() -> CpuInfo {
    31	    // CPUID is part of the x86_64 architectural baseline.
    32	    let basic = __cpuid(0);
    33	    let mut vendor = [0; 12];
    34	    vendor[0..4].copy_from_slice(&basic.ebx.to_le_bytes());
    35	    vendor[4..8].copy_from_slice(&basic.edx.to_le_bytes());
    36	    vendor[8..12].copy_from_slice(&basic.ecx.to_le_bytes());
    37	
    38	    let basic_features = if basic.eax >= 1 {
    39	        Some(__cpuid(1))
    40	    } else {
    41	        None
    42	    };
    43	    let extended = __cpuid(0x8000_0000);
    44	    let extended_features = if extended.eax >= 0x8000_0001 {
    45	        Some(__cpuid(0x8000_0001))
    46	    } else {
    47	        None
    48	    };
    49	    let structured_features = if basic.eax >= 7 {
    50	        Some(__cpuid_count(7, 0))
    51	    } else {
    52	        None
    53	    };
    54	    let address_widths = if extended.eax >= 0x8000_0008 {
    55	        Some(__cpuid(0x8000_0008).eax)
    56	    } else {
    57	        None
    58	    };
    59	    let cr4 = read_cr4_raw();
    60	    let has_nx = extended_features.is_some_and(|features| features.edx & (1 << 20) != 0);
    61	    let nx_enabled = if has_nx {
    62	        // SAFETY: EFER is available in x86_64 long mode; CPUID confirms NX support,
    63	        // and this boot-time code executes at CPL 0. The read does not change state.
    64	        unsafe { read_msr(IA32_EFER) & EFER_NXE != 0 }
    65	    } else {
    66	        false
    67	    };
    68	    let has_pat = basic_features.is_some_and(|features| features.edx & (1 << 16) != 0);
    69	    let pat_msr_value = if has_pat {
    70	        // SAFETY: CPUID reports PAT support and boot-time kernel code runs at CPL 0.
    71	        Some(unsafe { read_msr(IA32_PAT) })
    72	    } else {
    73	        None
    74	    };
    75	
    76	    CpuInfo {
    77	        vendor,
    78	        max_basic_leaf: basic.eax,
    79	        max_extended_leaf: extended.eax,
    80	        has_sse2: basic_features.is_some_and(|features| features.edx & (1 << 26) != 0),
    81	        has_nx,
    82	        nx_enabled,
    83	        has_pat,
    84	        pat_msr_value,
    85	        has_1g_pages: extended_features.is_some_and(|features| features.edx & (1 << 26) != 0),
    86	        has_long_mode: extended_features.is_some_and(|features| features.edx & (1 << 29) != 0),
    87	        has_la57: structured_features.is_some_and(|features| features.ecx & (1 << 16) != 0),
    88	        physical_address_bits: address_widths.map(|eax| (eax & 0xff) as u8),
    89	        max_linear_address_bits: address_widths.map(|eax| ((eax >> 8) & 0xff) as u8),
    90	        active_linear_address_bits: if cr4 & (1 << 12) != 0 { 57 } else { 48 },
    91	        pcid_enabled: cr4 & (1 << 17) != 0,
    92	    }
    93	}
    94	
    95	/// Read the current raw CR3 value without changing page-table state.
    96	pub fn read_cr3_raw() -> u64 {
    97	    let cr3: u64;
    98	    // SAFETY: Rustix runs at CPL 0; reading CR3 is privileged but non-mutating.
    99	    unsafe { asm!("mov {}, cr3", out(reg) cr3, options(nomem, nostack, preserves_flags)) };
   100	    cr3
   101	}
   102	
   103	/// Read a model-specific register at CPL 0.
   104	///
   105	/// # Safety
   106	/// The caller must ensure the MSR exists on this CPU and that the current
   107	/// privilege level permits the read.
   108	unsafe fn read_msr(index: u32) -> u64 {
   109	    let low: u32;
   110	    let high: u32;
   111	    // SAFETY: The caller guarantees that this MSR is supported and accessible.
   112	    unsafe {
   113	        asm!(
   114	            "rdmsr",
   115	            in("ecx") index,
   116	            out("eax") low,
   117	            out("edx") high,
   118	            options(nomem, nostack)
   119	        );
   120	    }
   121	    (u64::from(high) << 32) | u64::from(low)
   122	}
   123	
   124	/// Read CR4 without changing paging state.
   125	fn read_cr4_raw() -> u64 {
   126	    let cr4: u64;
   127	    // SAFETY: Rustix runs at CPL 0; reading CR4 is privileged but non-mutating.
   128	    unsafe { asm!("mov {}, cr4", out(reg) cr4, options(nomem, nostack, preserves_flags)) };
   129	    cr4
   130	}

```rustix/docs/architecture/boot.md
     1	# Boot protocol and kernel entry
     2	
     3	## Current boot contract
     4	
     5	Rustix currently expects a Limine-compatible x86_64 handoff. Limine is an external loader; it does not implement Rustix's kernel services. The kernel requests protocol base revision 3, the higher-half direct-map (HHDM) offset, the executable physical/virtual base addresses, and the memory map.
     6	
     7	Requests are kept in `.limine_requests_start`, `.limine_requests`, and `.limine_requests_end` by `linker.ld`. The response-bearing request records are mutable and the output `.limine_requests` section is placed in a writable load segment because Limine fills their response pointers before entering Rustix. The ELF entry symbol is `_start`.
     8	
     9	### Entry sequence
    10	
    11	1. Limine loads the ELF and transfers control to the assembly `_start` shim under the x86_64 Limine protocol. The shim captures the entry `RSP`, aligns the stack for a SysV call, and invokes `rustix_start`.
    12	2. `rustix_start` configures the legacy COM1 UART for polling output and input.
    13	3. The kernel disables maskable interrupts and installs its bootstrap GDT, TSS, and fatal-exception IDT. This does not initialize IRQ delivery.
    14	4. The kernel reads CPU address widths, active `CR4.PCIDE`, and raw CR3. It decodes CR3's physical root address and low-bit meaning against those CPU properties, without dereferencing the root. It reads EFER.NXE only when CPUID reports NX, and reads `IA32_PAT` only when CPUID reports PAT; these MSR reads do not change CPU state. It copies the HHDM, executable-address, and memory-map responses into an owned `BootInfo` snapshot, validates pointers against the active linear width, derives and validates the linker-defined kernel image span and its page-aligned text/rodata/data segment spans from Limine's executable bases, and derives the protocol-guaranteed minimum initial-stack span from the captured entry `RSP`. It validates physical bounds, stack HHDM arithmetic/coverage, and page-rounded HHDM arithmetic for protocol-mapped memory types. It then builds a frame allocator only from validated usable ranges and rejects malformed metadata before starting the shell.
    15	5. The kernel reports raw CR3 and its decoded physical root/low bits when the reported width permits, physical and virtual kernel-image spans, linker-defined text RX, rodata R/NX, and data RW/NX segment spans, minimum protocol-guaranteed stack span, validated memory ranges, frame counts, CPU features/address widths, NXE state, and the active PAT value plus recognized WB/UC/WC indices, then seeds a volatile RAM filesystem and enters Crabshell on the serial console.
    16	6. The shell busy-polls COM1 because no scheduler or UART interrupt handler exists yet. The kernel does not return to the loader.
    17	
    18	The linker exports page-aligned virtual bounds for each of the kernel's three load segments. Boot validates their order, contiguity, coverage of the rounded image span, and derived physical ranges, then reports them with the permissions intended by `linker.ld`. Boot also decodes CR3's root physical address and active low-bit interpretation. These are validated linker/boot metadata only: Rustix does not inspect the inherited page tables, so it has not established that the segments are mapped or that their live permissions match the ELF flags.
    19	
    20	The memory-map snapshot stores physical regions as checked half-open ranges `[start, end)` and retains Limine's known classifications plus unknown type values. It does not authorize Rustix to access every region, reclaim loader memory, or mutate the current page tables. Rustix checks physical bounds and calculates canonical HHDM ranges for memory types covered by the requested base revision, but does not dereference physical memory through the HHDM or verify the inherited page tables. These metadata checks cannot prove that a Limine-provided non-null pointer is readable; that remains an explicit handoff trust boundary.
    21	
    22	## Link and target configuration
    23	
    24	- Rust target: `x86_64-unknown-none`
    25	- Linker script: `linker.ld`
    26	- Kernel virtual base: `0xffffffff80000000`
    27	- Required code-generation constraints: kernel code model, static relocation, and disabled red zone
    28	- Rust panic strategy: abort; the panic handler logs and halts
    29	
    30	See [`../development/building.md`](../development/building.md) for commands and toolchain setup.
    31	
    32	## Failure behavior and limitations
    33	
    34	Missing responses, bad pointers/alignment, invalid HHDM values, invalid image or segment bounds, invalid initial-stack spans, excessive counts, null entries, address arithmetic overflow, and invalid or overlapping physical ranges reject the complete boot snapshot. `_start` halts before starting Crabshell rather than continuing with partial memory metadata. Structural checks cannot establish that a non-null loader pointer is mapped and readable; that remains an explicit trust assumption of the Limine handoff. The installed exception handlers print fatal context and halt; no fault recovery or maskable IRQ delivery is provided. COM1 writes use a bounded polling loop so a non-responsive UART does not block forever.
    35	
    36	The repository includes a Limine v12.9.3 binary archive pin with SHA-256 verification, a hybrid ISO recipe, and a bounded QEMU serial smoke test that checks Crabshell's prompt. On 2026-10-16, `just verify` passed in WSL2 Ubuntu 24.04 on both the working tree and a clean detached worktree with an empty `target` directory; the clean run fetched and built the pinned Limine host utility, created the image, and QEMU reported boot metadata before reaching the prompt. Milestone 0's local exit criteria are met. Hosted CI has not been observed. There is still no framebuffer console, reboot/shutdown interface, or broader boot-protocol compatibility test. The available serial and keyboard drivers do not imply a general device model.
    37	
    38	## Future boot work
    39	
    40	The kernel now snapshots and validates the Limine map and preserves firmware and loader-reclaimable classifications without reclaiming them. No region is considered Rustix-owned or free for allocation yet. Loader-reclaimable memory must remain unavailable until Rustix has copied any needed boot data and explicitly reaches a documented reclaim point; ACPI reclaimable memory needs the ACPI tables to be copied or parsed first. Frame allocation, page-table replacement, and ownership transfer remain future work.

```

   306	    pub fn from_msr_values(registers: [u64; 11]) -> Result<Self, MtrrError> {
   307	        let mut memory_types = [MtrrMemoryType::Uncacheable; FIXED_MTRR_TYPE_COUNT];
   308	        for (register_index, value) in registers.iter().enumerate() {
   309	            for slot in 0..8 {
   310	                let memory_type = ((value >> (slot * 8)) & 0xff) as u8;
   311	                memory_types[register_index * 8 + slot] = MtrrMemoryType::from_raw(memory_type)?;

   320	        } else if address < 0xa0_000 {

   322	        } else if address < 0xc0_000 {

   358	            return Err(MtrrError::ReservedMaskBits);
   359	        }
   360	        let memory_type = MtrrMemoryType::from_raw((base & 0xff) as u8)?;
   361	        if mask & MTRR_VALID == 0 {
   362	            return Ok(None);
   363	        }
   364	
   365	        let address_mask = mask & physical_mask;
   366	        Ok(Some(Self {
   367	            base_match: base & address_mask,
   368	            address_mask,
   369	            physical_address_bits,
   370	            memory_type,
   371	        }))
   372	    }

   374	    fn matches(self, address: u64) -> bool {
   375	        address & self.address_mask == self.base_match

   377	}

   379	/// MTRR policy decoded from supplied register values; it does not access MSRs.
   380	#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
   381	pub struct MtrrLayout<'a> {
   382	    physical_address_bits: u8,
   383	    enabled: bool,
   384	    fixed_enabled: bool,
   385	    default_type: MtrrMemoryType,
   386	    fixed_ranges: Option<&'a FixedMtrrRanges>,
   387	    variable_ranges: &'a [VariableMtrr],
   388	}
   389	
   390	impl<'a> MtrrLayout<'a> {
   391	    pub fn new(
   392	        physical_address_bits: u8,
   393	        enabled: bool,
   394	        fixed_enabled: bool,
   395	        default_type: MtrrMemoryType,
   396	        fixed_ranges: Option<&'a FixedMtrrRanges>,
   397	        variable_ranges: &'a [VariableMtrr],
   398	    ) -> Result<Self, MtrrError> {
   399	        if !(12..=MAX_MTRR_PHYSICAL_ADDRESS_BITS).contains(&physical_address_bits) {
   400	            return Err(MtrrError::InvalidPhysicalAddressWidth);
   401	        }
   402	        if enabled && fixed_enabled && fixed_ranges.is_none() {
   403	            return Err(MtrrError::FixedRangesUnavailable);
   404	        }
   405	        if variable_ranges
   406	            .iter()
   407	            .any(|range| range.physical_address_bits != physical_address_bits)
   408	        {
   409	            return Err(MtrrError::PhysicalAddressWidthMismatch);
   410	        }
   411	
   412	        Ok(Self {
   413	            physical_address_bits,
   414	            enabled,
   415	            fixed_enabled,
   416	            default_type,
   417	            fixed_ranges,
   418	            variable_ranges,
   419	        })
   420	    }
   421	
   422	    /// Resolve the MTRR type for one physical address, rejecting undefined overlaps.
   423	    pub fn memory_type_for(&self, address: u64) -> Result<MtrrMemoryType, MtrrError> {
   424	        if address >= (1u64 << self.physical_address_bits) {
   425	            return Err(MtrrError::PhysicalAddressOutOfRange);
   426	        }
   427	        if !self.enabled {
   428	            return Ok(MtrrMemoryType::Uncacheable);
   429	        }
   430	        if self.fixed_enabled {
   431	            if let Some(memory_type) = self
   432	                .fixed_ranges
   433	                .and_then(|ranges| ranges.type_for_address(address))
   434	            {
   435	                return Ok(memory_type);
   436	            }
   437	        }
   438	
   439	        let mut matched_types = 0u8;
   440	        for range in self.variable_ranges {
   441	            if range.matches(address) {
   442	                matched_types |= 1 << range.memory_type as u8;
   443	            }
   444	        }
   445	        if matched_types == 0 {
   446	            return Ok(self.default_type);
   447	        }
   448	        if matched_types & (1 << MtrrMemoryType::Uncacheable as u8) != 0 {
   449	            return Ok(MtrrMemoryType::Uncacheable);
   450	        }
   451	        if matched_types.count_ones() == 1 {
   452	            return MtrrMemoryType::from_raw(matched_types.trailing_zeros() as u8);
   453	        }
   454	        let write_back_and_through =
   455	            (1 << MtrrMemoryType::WriteBack as u8) | (1 << MtrrMemoryType::WriteThrough as u8);
   456	        if matched_types == write_back_and_through {
   457	            return Ok(MtrrMemoryType::WriteThrough);
   458	        }
   459	        Err(MtrrError::UndefinedOverlap)
   460	    }
   461	}
   462

## Matches in rustix\docs\architecture\memory.md

### # Memory-management direction › ## What exists now › L11-12
```
`src/paging.rs` adds pure, host-tested 4 KiB mapping groundwork and decodes the inherited CR3 root address plus its low-bit interpretation. The CR3 decoder validates the physical-address width and reserved bits and interprets the low 12 bits according to the active `CR4.PCIDE` state; it does not dereference the root. The mapping-range validator requires a known physical-address width, checked aligned bounds, canonical virtual endpoints in one canonical half, and rejects writable-executable permissions. A validated range can encode the raw bits of one 4 KiB leaf PTE, including supervisor/user and write permissions, NX when the caller confirms EFER.NXE, and a bounded three-bit PAT index. `PatLayout` parses a supplied `IA32_PAT` value and selects WB, UC, or WC indices. `MtrrMemoryType`, `VariableMtrr`, `FixedMtrrRanges`, and `MtrrLayout` parse caller-supplied register values and resolve the MTRR type at one physical address, including fixed-range priority and specified variable-overlap rules; undefined overlaps fail closed. This is a pure model only: `src/arch/x86_64/cpu.rs` does not capture MTRR state, and no code combines PAT with MTRR to establish an effective cache type for a mapping. The CPU reads EFER.NXE only when NX is supported and reads `IA32_PAT` only when PAT is supported; these reads are diagnostic and do not modify CPU state. None of these helpers proves frame ownership or HHDM coverage, inspects table entries, or modifies hardware page tables. No page mapping operation or CR3 transition is implemented.

```

### # Memory-management direction › ## Initial kernel-owned mapping policy (design only) › L32-33
```
Preserve the inherited PAT/MTRR configuration during the first transition. The current boot report reads the active `IA32_PAT` value when PAT is supported and parses WB/UC/WC entries, but does not yet inspect MTRRs or establish effective cache types for physical ranges. Under Limine base revision 3 on x86_64, use PAT index 0 for WB, index 3 for UC, and index 5 for WC only when the active configuration is verified. Map MMIO only from explicit device ranges and use UC by default; do not infer MMIO from generic reserved memory-map entries. A framebuffer may use WC only after its response and cache policy are explicitly validated. COM1 uses port I/O and requires no MMIO mapping.

```

## Matches in rustix\docs\index.md

### # Rustix documentation › ## Current status › L20-21
```
The repository contains a bare-metal `no_std` Rust kernel for `x86_64-unknown-none`. After Limine handoff it validates and copies memory-map metadata into an owned snapshot, captures the executable's physical and virtual bases, complete linker-defined image span, and page-aligned text/rodata/data segment bounds, reports baseline CPUID features, active/maximum address widths, and gated read-only EFER.NXE/IA32_PAT values, seeds a volatile RAM filesystem, and runs Crabshell over the COM1 serial console. Boot-protocol pointers are checked for canonicality using the active 4- or 5-level paging width; physical map bounds and protocol-scoped HHDM range arithmetic are also validated. Crabshell's allocation-free parser is a separate crate; the kernel handles command execution. On 2026-10-16, `just verify` passed in WSL2 Ubuntu 24.04 both in the working tree and from a clean detached worktree with an empty `target` directory; the clean run downloaded and built the pinned Limine host utility, created the image, and passed the bounded QEMU boot to the shell prompt. The serial log showed memory-map and CPU reporting. Hosted CI has not been observed. A separate interactive QEMU session exercised `help`, `ls`, `meminfo`, directory navigation, and file create/write/append/read/copy/move/remove commands. Milestone 0's local exit criteria are met, and Milestone 1's validation criteria are met for the current Limine path. This is a kernel-mode shell, not a user process. A bounded physical-frame allocator core is initialized from the validated map and reported by `meminfo`; its owned frame token and failed-deallocation semantics are documented and host-tested, but no kernel service allocates or maps frames yet. The Limine base-revision 3 HHDM scope and a conservative initial mapping/alias/cache policy are documented. Pure host-tested helpers validate mapping ranges/PTE bits, parse PAT layouts, and resolve MTRR types from supplied register values; live MTRRs are not captured and PAT/MTRR semantics are not combined for mappings. `BootInfo` records raw CR3 and a validated decode of its root physical address and low-bit interpretation, but Rustix does not use the HHDM to access physical memory, inspect page-table contents, or own/replace the inherited tables. The complete linker-defined kernel-image span and the protocol-guaranteed minimum active boot-stack span are captured; Limine does not provide the exact initial stack allocation or guard status, so Rustix preserves only the known minimum span and does not infer a guard page. There is not yet a heap, a general IRQ subsystem, a scheduler, process isolation, a persistent filesystem, or a Unix compatibility layer. Fatal CPU exceptions have basic GDT/TSS/IDT diagnostics but no recovery. `just fault-smoke` validates a controlled page fault (including CR2) and invalid opcode in QEMU; broader exception coverage and physical-hardware validation remain pending. On 2026-10-21, `just verify` passed after adding CR3 decoding and the pure MTRR resolver, including host tests, target check, release build, ISO creation, and QEMU prompt smoke; this does not inspect page-table entries or exercise live MTRR/PAT mapping semantics.

//! CPU feature and gated, read-only MSR reporting for x86_64 boot diagnostics.

use core::arch::asm;
use core::arch::x86_64::{__cpuid, __cpuid_count};

const IA32_EFER: u32 = 0xc000_0080;
const IA32_PAT: u32 = 0x0000_0277;
const IA32_MTRRCAP: u32 = 0x0000_00fe;
const IA32_MTRR_DEF_TYPE: u32 = 0x0000_02ff;
const IA32_MTRR_PHYSBASE0: u32 = 0x0000_0200;
const EFER_NXE: u64 = 1 << 11;
const MTRRCAP_FIXED_SUPPORTED: u64 = 1 << 8;
const MTRR_FIXED_REGISTER_INDICES: [u32; 11] = [
    0x250, 0x258, 0x259, 0x268, 0x269, 0x26a, 0x26b, 0x26c, 0x26d, 0x26e, 0x26f,
];

/// Maximum variable MTRR pairs retained in the fixed-capacity boot snapshot.
pub const MAX_CAPTURED_VARIABLE_MTRRS: usize = 32;

#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct MtrrRegisterPair {
    pub base: u64,
    pub mask: u64,
}

/// Read-only snapshot of the MTRR registers, retained for later policy checks.
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct MtrrRegisters {
    pub capability: u64,
    pub default_type: u64,
    pub fixed_registers: Option<[u64; 11]>,
    pub variable_register_count: u8,
    pub variable_registers: [MtrrRegisterPair; MAX_CAPTURED_VARIABLE_MTRRS],
}

#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum MtrrState {
    Unsupported,
    VariableRangeCapacityExceeded { reported_count: u8 },
    Captured(MtrrRegisters),
}

#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct CpuInfo {
    pub vendor: [u8; 12],
    pub max_basic_leaf: u32,
    pub max_extended_leaf: u32,
    pub has_sse2: bool,
    pub has_nx: bool,
    pub nx_enabled: bool,
    pub has_pat: bool,
    pub pat_msr_value: Option<u64>,
    pub mtrr: MtrrState,
    pub has_1g_pages: bool,
    pub has_long_mode: bool,
    pub has_la57: bool,
    pub physical_address_bits: Option<u8>,
    pub max_linear_address_bits: Option<u8>,
    pub active_linear_address_bits: u8,
    pub pcid_enabled: bool,
}

/// Read CPUID identity, selected feature bits, and supported read-only MSR state.
pub fn identify() -> CpuInfo {
    // CPUID is part of the x86_64 architectural baseline.
    let basic = __cpuid(0);
    let mut vendor = [0; 12];
    vendor[0..4].copy_from_slice(&basic.ebx.to_le_bytes());
    vendor[4..8].copy_from_slice(&basic.edx.to_le_bytes());
    vendor[8..12].copy_from_slice(&basic.ecx.to_le_bytes());

    let basic_features = if basic.eax >= 1 {
        Some(__cpuid(1))
    } else {
        None
    };
    let extended = __cpuid(0x8000_0000);
    let extended_features = if extended.eax >= 0x8000_0001 {
        Some(__cpuid(0x8000_0001))
    } else {
        None
    };
    let structured_features = if basic.eax >= 7 {
        Some(__cpuid_count(7, 0))
    } else {
        None
    };
    let address_widths = if extended.eax >= 0x8000_0008 {
        Some(__cpuid(0x8000_0008).eax)
    } else {
        None
    };
    let cr4 = read_cr4_raw();
    let has_nx = extended_features.is_some_and(|features| features.edx & (1 << 20) != 0);
    let nx_enabled = if has_nx {
        // SAFETY: EFER is available in x86_64 long mode; CPUID confirms NX support,
        // and this boot-time code executes at CPL 0. The read does not change state.
        unsafe { read_msr(IA32_EFER) & EFER_NXE != 0 }
    } else {
        false
    };
    let has_pat = basic_features.is_some_and(|features| features.edx & (1 << 16) != 0);
    let pat_msr_value = if has_pat {
        // SAFETY: CPUID reports PAT support and boot-time kernel code runs at CPL 0.
        Some(unsafe { read_msr(IA32_PAT) })
    } else {
        None
    };
    let has_mtrr = basic_features.is_some_and(|features| features.edx & (1 << 12) != 0);
    let mtrr = capture_mtrr_state(has_mtrr, |index| {
        // SAFETY: CPUID reports MTRR support; the capture helper only requests
        // architectural MTRR MSRs after that feature check.
        unsafe { read_msr(index) }
    });

    CpuInfo {
        vendor,
        max_basic_leaf: basic.eax,
        max_extended_leaf: extended.eax,
        has_sse2: basic_features.is_some_and(|features| features.edx & (1 << 26) != 0),
        has_nx,
        nx_enabled,
        has_pat,
        pat_msr_value,
        mtrr,
        has_1g_pages: extended_features.is_some_and(|features| features.edx & (1 << 26) != 0),
        has_long_mode: extended_features.is_some_and(|features| features.edx & (1 << 29) != 0),
        has_la57: structured_features.is_some_and(|features| features.ecx & (1 << 16) != 0),
        physical_address_bits: address_widths.map(|eax| (eax & 0xff) as u8),
        max_linear_address_bits: address_widths.map(|eax| ((eax >> 8) & 0xff) as u8),
        active_linear_address_bits: if cr4 & (1 << 12) != 0 { 57 } else { 48 },
        pcid_enabled: cr4 & (1 << 17) != 0,
    }
}

fn capture_mtrr_state(
    has_mtrr: bool,
    mut read_msr: impl FnMut(u32) -> u64,
) -> MtrrState {
    if !has_mtrr {
        return MtrrState::Unsupported;
    }

    let capability = read_msr(IA32_MTRRCAP);
    let variable_register_count = (capability & 0xff) as u8;
    if usize::from(variable_register_count) > MAX_CAPTURED_VARIABLE_MTRRS {
        return MtrrState::VariableRangeCapacityExceeded {
            reported_count: variable_register_count,
        };
    }

    let default_type = read_msr(IA32_MTRR_DEF_TYPE);
    let fixed_registers = if capability & MTRRCAP_FIXED_SUPPORTED != 0 {
        let mut registers = [0; MTRR_FIXED_REGISTER_INDICES.len()];
        for (register, index) in registers.iter_mut().zip(MTRR_FIXED_REGISTER_INDICES) {
            *register = read_msr(index);
        }
        Some(registers)
    } else {
        None
    };

    let mut variable_registers = [MtrrRegisterPair { base: 0, mask: 0 };
        MAX_CAPTURED_VARIABLE_MTRRS];
    for (range_index, registers) in variable_registers
        .iter_mut()
        .take(usize::from(variable_register_count))
        .enumerate()
    {
        let base_index = IA32_MTRR_PHYSBASE0 + 2 * range_index as u32;
        registers.base = read_msr(base_index);
        registers.mask = read_msr(base_index + 1);
    }

    MtrrState::Captured(MtrrRegisters {
        capability,
        default_type,
        fixed_registers,
        variable_register_count,
        variable_registers,
    })
}

/// Read the current raw CR3 value without changing page-table state.
pub fn read_cr3_raw() -> u64 {
    let cr3: u64;
    // SAFETY: Rustix runs at CPL 0; reading CR3 is privileged but non-mutating.
    unsafe { asm!("mov {}, cr3", out(reg) cr3, options(nomem, nostack, preserves_flags)) };
    cr3
}

/// Read a model-specific register at CPL 0.
///
/// # Safety
/// The caller must ensure the MSR exists on this CPU and that the current
/// privilege level permits the read.
unsafe fn read_msr(index: u32) -> u64 {
    let low: u32;
    let high: u32;
    // SAFETY: The caller guarantees that this MSR is supported and accessible.
    unsafe {
        asm!(
            "rdmsr",
            in("ecx") index,
            out("eax") low,
            out("edx") high,
            options(nomem, nostack)
        );
    }
    (u64::from(high) << 32) | u64::from(low)
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;
    use core::cell::Cell;

    #[test]
    fn mtrr_capture_is_gated_by_cpuid_support() {
        let state = capture_mtrr_state(false, |_| panic!("read MSR without MTRR support"));
        assert_eq!(state, MtrrState::Unsupported);
    }

    #[test]
    fn captures_supported_fixed_and_variable_mtrr_registers() {
        let reads = Cell::new(0);
        let state = capture_mtrr_state(true, |index| {
            reads.set(reads.get() + 1);
            match index {
                IA32_MTRRCAP => 2 | MTRRCAP_FIXED_SUPPORTED,
                IA32_MTRR_DEF_TYPE => 0xc06,
                _ => u64::from(index),
            }
        });

        let MtrrState::Captured(registers) = state else {
            panic!("expected a complete MTRR snapshot");
        };
        assert_eq!(reads.get(), 2 + MTRR_FIXED_REGISTER_INDICES.len() + 4);
        assert_eq!(registers.capability, 2 | MTRRCAP_FIXED_SUPPORTED);
        assert_eq!(registers.default_type, 0xc06);
        assert_eq!(registers.variable_register_count, 2);
        let fixed = registers.fixed_registers.expect("fixed ranges are supported");
        assert_eq!(fixed[0], 0x250);
        assert_eq!(fixed[10], 0x26f);
        assert_eq!(registers.variable_registers[0].base, 0x200);
        assert_eq!(registers.variable_registers[0].mask, 0x201);
        assert_eq!(registers.variable_registers[1].base, 0x202);
        assert_eq!(registers.variable_registers[1].mask, 0x203);
        assert_eq!(registers.variable_registers[2], MtrrRegisterPair { base: 0, mask: 0 });
    }

    #[test]
    fn mtrr_capture_reports_capacity_excess_without_partial_reads() {
        let reads = Cell::new(0);
        let state = capture_mtrr_state(true, |index| {
            reads.set(reads.get() + 1);
            if index == IA32_MTRRCAP {
                (MAX_CAPTURED_VARIABLE_MTRRS as u64) + 1
            } else {
                0
            }
        });

        assert_eq!(
            state,
            MtrrState::VariableRangeCapacityExceeded {
                reported_count: (MAX_CAPTURED_VARIABLE_MTRRS + 1) as u8,
            }
        );
        assert_eq!(reads.get(), 1);
    }

    #[test]
    fn mtrr_capture_skips_unsupported_fixed_registers() {
        let reads = Cell::new(0);
        let state = capture_mtrr_state(true, |index| {
            reads.set(reads.get() + 1);
            match index {
                IA32_MTRRCAP => 1,
                IA32_MTRR_DEF_TYPE => 0xc06,
                _ => u64::from(index),
            }
        });

        let MtrrState::Captured(registers) = state else {
            panic!("expected a complete MTRR snapshot");
        };
        assert_eq!(reads.get(), 4);
        assert_eq!(registers.fixed_registers, None);
        assert_eq!(registers.variable_register_count, 1);
        assert_eq!(registers.variable_registers[0].base, 0x200);
        assert_eq!(registers.variable_registers[0].mask, 0x201);
    }
}

/// Read CR4 without changing paging state.
fn read_cr4_raw() -> u64 {
    let cr4: u64;
    // SAFETY: Rustix runs at CPL 0; reading CR4 is privileged but non-mutating.
    unsafe { asm!("mov {}, cr4", out(reg) cr4, options(nomem, nostack, preserves_flags)) };
    cr4
}

     1	# Testing and verification

     3	## Current checks
     4	
     5	`just verify` runs the standard development verification sequence:
     6

     8	2. `just test` — run host-side memory-map, mapping-range/PTE-bit policy, frame-allocator, RAM-filesystem, and Crabshell parser tests.
