## Milestone 3 — IRQs, time, and kernel scheduling

Do not enable interrupts as a side effect of installing exception gates. IRQ delivery needs its own controller, acknowledgement, masking, ownership, and synchronization design.

### Planned work

- [ ] Select and document the initial interrupt controller policy for QEMU and target hardware (for example, legacy PIC compatibility versus local I/O APIC; do not enable both accidentally).
- [ ] Add IRQ vector allocation, controller masking/unmasking, end-of-interrupt acknowledgement, spurious-interrupt handling, and a policy for unexpected IRQs.
- [ ] Add a calibrated/verified timer source and monotonic timekeeping; test interval arithmetic and drift assumptions.
- [ ] Establish interrupt-safe lock primitives and rules for code callable from normal, exception, and IRQ contexts. No allocator or blocking console operation may run in an unsafe interrupt context.
- [ ] Add a minimal kernel-thread context and lifecycle model, stack ownership/guard policy, context-switch tests, and emulator scheduling tests.
- [ ] Add preemption only after lock, stack, timer, and interrupt-return invariants have deterministic tests.
- [ ] Keep application-processor startup/SMP as a separate sub-milestone after per-CPU state, TLB invalidation, and lock semantics exist.

**Exit criteria:** tested IRQ acknowledgement and timer behavior, deterministic thread lifecycle/context-switch tests, and bounded QEMU tests under repeated timer interrupts. No `sti` before the design and tests are ready.

---

## Milestone 4 — isolated processes and syscall ABI

Userspace begins only after page tables, exception handling, scheduling, and controlled memory allocation are trustworthy. The syscall ABI is a product interface and must not emerge accidentally from internal functions.

### Planned work

- [ ] Decide and document the x86_64 user-entry/syscall mechanism, register convention, selector/MSR setup, per-CPU state requirements, and safe return path.
- [ ] Add user/kernel page permissions and process-owned address spaces, including teardown and TLB invalidation rules.
- [ ] Implement copy-in/copy-out helpers that validate lengths, arithmetic, canonical ranges, permissions, and faults; never form a kernel reference directly from a user pointer.
- [ ] Specify version discovery, stable syscall numbers, argument layouts, error encoding, partial-I/O behavior, interruption/restart, and compatibility policy before exposing calls.
- [ ] Add initial process lifecycle and descriptor-table semantics: create/load, exit, wait, close, duplication/inheritance, and process cleanup.
- [ ] Load a deliberately small documented executable format with bounds/segment/permission checks; reject malformed binaries safely.
- [ ] Build adversarial tests for bad pointers, overflow, invalid mappings, process teardown, descriptor misuse, and failed exec.

### First user-visible target

A small controlled `init` process should start from a reproducible image, write through a descriptor, exit with a status, and be waited on by a kernel test harness. Do not claim userspace or process isolation from ring-0 tasks that merely use process-shaped structs.

**Exit criteria:** an isolated init process runs in user mode and uses a versioned, documented syscall subset; invalid user pointers and process teardown are tested without corrupting the kernel.

---

## Milestone 5 — VFS, storage, and device ownership

Keep the current RAM filesystem as a bootstrap/test implementation. Persistence and device drivers require explicit block ownership, error handling, and recovery behavior.

### Planned work

- [ ] Define VFS node, mount, path, metadata, and file-descriptor contracts independently of a particular disk format.
- [ ] Preserve volatile RAMFS as a test backend and add tests for mount/path errors, capacity, partial I/O, and object lifetime.
- [ ] Add a narrowly scoped block-device interface with request validation, timeout/error reporting, and a QEMU-supported initial device driver (such as virtio-blk after PCI discovery is ready).
- [ ] Choose and document the first on-disk filesystem format. Specify partition discovery, byte order, block size, metadata limits, corruption handling, and read-only/recovery behavior before writable support.
- [ ] Add persistent write/read/remount/reboot integration tests; never claim persistence from an in-memory cache alone.
- [ ] Add a driver ownership and DMA policy before any device can write into arbitrary kernel memory.
- [ ] Define file descriptors and basic process I/O semantics before exposing them to applications.

**Exit criteria:** a reproducible image mounts a documented on-disk filesystem, user-visible tools can create/read files across reboot, and corruption/I/O errors fail safely.

---

## Milestone 6 — initial userspace and command-line utilities

Crabshell is currently an in-kernel parser/frontend. The long-term terminal application should reuse its parser model without linking kernel internals or bypassing syscalls.

### Planned work

- [ ] Start a user-mode `init` process and establish executable search, environment, current directory, descriptor inheritance, and process startup rules.
- [ ] Port or adapt Crabshell into a userspace terminal application that uses only the documented syscall/VFS interfaces.
- [ ] Add a small utility set with explicit scope: file listing, text output, create/remove/copy/move, and system information.
- [ ] Add command-line quoting, escaping, history, redirection, and pipelines only with parser tests and process/descriptor/pipe semantics to support them.
- [ ] Add integration tests that launch tools from the filesystem image and exercise them through syscalls; keep unsupported features explicit.

**Exit criteria:** shell and basic tools run as isolated user processes from a reproducible image; no shell command directly calls kernel-private VFS internals.

---

## Milestone 7 — graphical console and GUI (long-term)

A GUI is intentionally downstream of stable memory management, interrupts/input, process isolation, drivers, and userspace. Keep Crabshell's parser independent so a graphical terminal frontend can reuse it.

### Planned work

- [ ] Add validated framebuffer discovery and memory ownership; implement a minimal text/graphics console without compromising serial panic diagnostics.
- [ ] Establish an input subsystem that separates raw device events from key mapping and terminal policy. Plan PS/2 and USB HID support separately; do not treat the current raw scancode poller as a keyboard driver stack.
- [ ] Define a graphics buffer ownership/presentation API, clipping rules, pixel format, and bounds/overflow checks.
- [ ] Implement a minimal compositor/windowing policy only after process isolation and input routing are ready.
- [ ] Run Crabshell as a terminal application in a GUI window using the same parser and userspace services as the serial/TTY path.
- [ ] Preserve serial as a headless recovery/debug console and add repeatable QEMU display/input tests.

**Exit criteria:** a documented GUI session starts from userspace, renders a terminal, accepts tested input, and does not require direct kernel-private VFS access.

---

## Milestone 8 — networking (long-term, after drivers and process isolation)

Networking is not implied by the current device drivers. The initial target should be a tightly scoped virtual-device path with clear ownership and bounded buffers.

### Planned work

- [ ] Complete PCI/device discovery and define DMA buffer ownership, address translation, cache synchronization, and reset/error behavior.
- [ ] Implement one virtual NIC driver with bounded queues and timeouts; test against QEMU user networking.
- [ ] Choose and document a minimal link/network protocol scope before implementation. Keep packet parsing length-checked and fuzzable on the host.
- [ ] Add interface configuration, routing, socket/descriptor ownership, and per-process access policy.
- [ ] Add adversarial packet tests and integration tests for link loss, malformed packets, queue exhaustion, and device reset.
- [ ] Add higher-level transports/services only when the required protocol semantics, entropy source, and security model are designed.

**Exit criteria:** documented user processes can communicate through a tested virtual NIC/network stack, with malformed input and resource exhaustion handled safely. Do not claim internet, TLS, or POSIX sockets merely from a packet driver.

---

## Cross-cutting acceptance gates

Every milestone should include the relevant subset of these gates:

1. **Design:** documented ownership, invariants, resource limits, error semantics, and unsupported cases.
2. **Tests:** host tests for pure policy and malformed/boundary input; integration tests for hardware-facing behavior.
3. **Safety:** review unsafe blocks, pointer provenance/access, integer overflow, privilege boundaries, concurrency, and cleanup/rollback paths.
4. **Build:** format, host tests, target check, and final ELF link as appropriate.
5. **Boot/integration:** QEMU tests for changes to boot, paging, descriptors, interrupts, drivers, processes, or persistence.
6. **Documentation/status:** update architecture and roadmap docs; never check off a criterion without evidence.
7. **Compatibility:** claim Unix/POSIX behavior only for the exact documented subset with conformance-style tests.

## Working rule

Prefer a small end-to-end vertical slice over broad, unbootable scaffolding. A source file, interface, or architecture document is not proof that the corresponding subsystem is operational. When a check cannot run, record the exact environment blocker and leave that acceptance gate pending.

//! Pure validation for future x86_64 4 KiB mappings.
//!
//! This module validates address shape and permissions only. It does not prove
//! frame ownership or mapping coverage, access physical memory, or modify tables.

use crate::memory::{is_canonical_virtual_address, physical_range_fits_address_width};

/// Base page size supported by the initial Rustix mapping policy.
pub const PAGE_SIZE: u64 = 4096;

/// The physical root address and interpretation of CR3's low bits.
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct Cr3Root {
    physical_address: u64,
    low_bits: Cr3LowBits,
}

impl Cr3Root {
    pub const fn physical_address(self) -> u64 {
        self.physical_address
    }

    pub const fn low_bits(self) -> Cr3LowBits {
        self.low_bits
    }
}

/// CR3's low bits are either a PCID or the paging-structure cache controls.
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum Cr3LowBits {
    Pcid(u16),
    CacheControls {
        page_level_write_through: bool,
        page_level_cache_disable: bool,
    },
}

#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum Cr3Error {
    UnknownPhysicalAddressWidth,
    InvalidPhysicalAddressWidth,
    ReservedBits,
}

/// Decode the currently active CR3 value without dereferencing its root table.
///
/// The caller supplies the reported physical-address width and whether CR4.PCIDE
/// is active, since those determine the valid address and low-bit encodings.
pub fn parse_cr3_root(
    raw: u64,
    physical_address_bits: Option<u8>,
    pcid_enabled: bool,
) -> Result<Cr3Root, Cr3Error> {
    let physical_address_bits =
        physical_address_bits.ok_or(Cr3Error::UnknownPhysicalAddressWidth)?;
    if !(12..=MAX_PTE_PHYSICAL_ADDRESS_BITS).contains(&physical_address_bits) {
        return Err(Cr3Error::InvalidPhysicalAddressWidth);
    }

    let physical_mask = ((1u64 << physical_address_bits) - 1) & !(PAGE_SIZE - 1);
    let low_mask = if pcid_enabled {
        PAGE_SIZE - 1
    } else {
        (1 << 3) | (1 << 4)
    };
    if raw & !(physical_mask | low_mask) != 0 {
        return Err(Cr3Error::ReservedBits);
    }

    let low_bits = if pcid_enabled {
        Cr3LowBits::Pcid((raw & (PAGE_SIZE - 1)) as u16)
    } else {
        Cr3LowBits::CacheControls {
            page_level_write_through: raw & (1 << 3) != 0,
            page_level_cache_disable: raw & (1 << 4) != 0,
        }
    };

    Ok(Cr3Root {
        physical_address: raw & physical_mask,
        low_bits,
    })
}

#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct PagePermissions {
    pub writable: bool,
    pub executable: bool,
    pub user_accessible: bool,
}

/// A mapping range whose arithmetic, address widths, alignment, and W^X policy passed validation.
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct ValidatedMappingRange {
    virtual_start: u64,
    virtual_end: u64,
    physical_start: u64,
    physical_end: u64,
    physical_address_bits: u8,
    permissions: PagePermissions,
}

impl ValidatedMappingRange {
    pub const fn virtual_start(self) -> u64 {
        self.virtual_start
    }

    pub const fn virtual_end(self) -> u64 {
        self.virtual_end
    }

    pub const fn physical_start(self) -> u64 {
        self.physical_start
    }

    pub const fn physical_end(self) -> u64 {
        self.physical_end
    }

    pub const fn permissions(self) -> PagePermissions {
        self.permissions
    }

    pub const fn length(self) -> u64 {
        self.virtual_end - self.virtual_start
    }

    /// Encode a single 4 KiB leaf PTE within this validated range.
    ///
    /// `pat_index` is the raw three-bit PAT index; the caller must have verified
    /// that the active PAT MSR gives it the intended cache semantics. `nx_enabled`
    /// must reflect EFER.NXE, not merely CPUID support. This only creates entry
    /// bits—it neither owns the frame nor writes a page table.
    pub fn leaf_4k_entry(
        self,
        page_offset: u64,
        pat_index: u8,
        nx_enabled: bool,
    ) -> Result<PageTableEntry, MappingError> {
        if page_offset & (PAGE_SIZE - 1) != 0 {
            return Err(MappingError::UnalignedPageOffset);
        }
        if page_offset >= self.length() {
            return Err(MappingError::PageOffsetOutOfRange);
        }
        if self.physical_address_bits > MAX_PTE_PHYSICAL_ADDRESS_BITS {
            return Err(MappingError::InvalidPhysicalAddressWidth);
        }
        if pat_index > 7 {
            return Err(MappingError::InvalidPatIndex);
        }
        if !self.permissions.executable && !nx_enabled {
            return Err(MappingError::NxNotEnabled);
        }

        let physical_address = self
            .physical_start
            .checked_add(page_offset)
            .ok_or(MappingError::AddressOverflow)?;
        let mut bits = physical_address | PTE_PRESENT;
        if self.permissions.writable {
            bits |= PTE_WRITABLE;
        }
        if self.permissions.user_accessible {
            bits |= PTE_USER;
        }
        if pat_index & 0b001 != 0 {
            bits |= PTE_WRITE_THROUGH;
        }
        if pat_index & 0b010 != 0 {
            bits |= PTE_CACHE_DISABLE;
        }
        if pat_index & 0b100 != 0 {
            bits |= PTE_PAT_4K;
        }
        if !self.permissions.executable {
            bits |= PTE_NO_EXECUTE;
        }

        Ok(PageTableEntry(bits))
    }
}

/// Maximum x86_64 physical-address width representable by a 4 KiB PTE.
pub const MAX_PTE_PHYSICAL_ADDRESS_BITS: u8 = 52;
const PTE_PRESENT: u64 = 1 << 0;
const PTE_WRITABLE: u64 = 1 << 1;
const PTE_USER: u64 = 1 << 2;
const PTE_WRITE_THROUGH: u64 = 1 << 3;
const PTE_CACHE_DISABLE: u64 = 1 << 4;
const PTE_PAT_4K: u64 = 1 << 7;
const PTE_NO_EXECUTE: u64 = 1 << 63;

/// Raw bits for one x86_64 4 KiB leaf page-table entry.
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct PageTableEntry(u64);

impl PageTableEntry {
    pub const fn bits(self) -> u64 {
        self.0
    }
}

#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum CachePolicy {
    WriteBack,
    Uncacheable,
    WriteCombining,
}

#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum PatLayoutError {
    ReservedBits { index: u8 },
    ReservedMemoryType { index: u8, value: u8 },
}

/// Parsed PAT memory types from an `IA32_PAT` MSR value supplied by the caller.
///
/// Parsing does not read the MSR or establish that this is the active value. The
/// MTRR configuration may also affect the effective cache type for an address.
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct PatLayout {
    memory_types: [u8; 8],
}

impl PatLayout {
    pub fn from_msr_value(value: u64) -> Result<Self, PatLayoutError> {
        let mut memory_types = [0; 8];
        for (index, memory_type) in memory_types.iter_mut().enumerate() {
            let entry = ((value >> (index * 8)) & 0xff) as u8;
            if entry & !0x07 != 0 {
                return Err(PatLayoutError::ReservedBits { index: index as u8 });
            }
            if entry == 0b010 || entry == 0b011 {
                return Err(PatLayoutError::ReservedMemoryType {
                    index: index as u8,
                    value: entry,
                });
            }
            *memory_type = entry;
        }
        Ok(Self { memory_types })
    }

    /// Return the first PAT index with the exact requested memory type.
    pub fn index_for(self, policy: CachePolicy) -> Option<u8> {
        let requested_type = match policy {
            CachePolicy::Uncacheable => 0b000,
            CachePolicy::WriteCombining => 0b001,
            CachePolicy::WriteBack => 0b110,
        };
        self.memory_types
            .iter()
            .position(|memory_type| *memory_type == requested_type)
            .map(|index| index as u8)
    }
}

const IA32_MTRRCAP: u32 = 0x0000_00fe;
const IA32_MTRR_DEF_TYPE: u32 = 0x0000_02ff;
const IA32_MTRR_PHYSBASE0: u32 = 0x0000_0200;
const MTRRCAP_FIXED_SUPPORTED: u64 = 1 << 8;
const FIXED_MTRR_REGISTER_INDICES: [u32; 11] = [
    0x250, 0x258, 0x259, 0x268, 0x269, 0x26a, 0x26b, 0x26c, 0x26d, 0x26e, 0x26f,
];

/// Maximum variable MTRR pairs retained in the fixed-capacity boot snapshot.
pub const MAX_CAPTURED_VARIABLE_MTRRS: usize = 32;

#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct MtrrRegisterPair {
    pub base: u64,
    pub mask: u64,
}

/// Raw MTRR state captured for diagnostics; values still require policy validation.
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct MtrrRegisters {
    pub capability: u64,
    pub default_type: u64,
    pub fixed_registers: Option<[u64; 11]>,
    pub variable_register_count: u8,
    pub variable_registers: [MtrrRegisterPair; MAX_CAPTURED_VARIABLE_MTRRS],
}

#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum MtrrState {
    Unsupported,
    VariableRangeCapacityExceeded { reported_count: u8 },
    Captured(MtrrRegisters),
}

/// Capture a bounded register snapshot using a caller-provided MSR reader.
///
/// This helper performs no hardware access itself. A false support flag returns
/// without invoking the reader; an over-capacity count returns no partial data.
pub fn capture_mtrr_registers(
    supported: bool,
    mut read_msr: impl FnMut(u32) -> u64,
) -> MtrrState {
    if !supported {
        return MtrrState::Unsupported;
    }

    let capability = read_msr(IA32_MTRRCAP);
    let variable_register_count = (capability & 0xff) as u8;
    if usize::from(variable_register_count) > MAX_CAPTURED_VARIABLE_MTRRS {
        return MtrrState::VariableRangeCapacityExceeded {
            reported_count: variable_register_count,
        };
    }

    let default_type = read_msr(IA32_MTRR_DEF_TYPE);
    let fixed_registers = if capability & MTRRCAP_FIXED_SUPPORTED != 0 {
        let mut registers = [0; FIXED_MTRR_REGISTER_INDICES.len()];
        for (register, index) in registers.iter_mut().zip(FIXED_MTRR_REGISTER_INDICES) {
            *register = read_msr(index);
        }
        Some(registers)
    } else {
        None
    };

    let mut variable_registers = [MtrrRegisterPair { base: 0, mask: 0 };
        MAX_CAPTURED_VARIABLE_MTRRS];
    for (range_index, registers) in variable_registers
        .iter_mut()
        .take(usize::from(variable_register_count))
        .enumerate()
    {
        let base_index = IA32_MTRR_PHYSBASE0 + 2 * range_index as u32;
        registers.base = read_msr(base_index);
        registers.mask = read_msr(base_index + 1);
    }

    MtrrState::Captured(MtrrRegisters {
        capability,
        default_type,
        fixed_registers,
        variable_register_count,
        variable_registers,
    })
}

pub const FIXED_MTRR_TYPE_COUNT: usize = 88;
const MAX_MTRR_PHYSICAL_ADDRESS_BITS: u8 = 52;
const MTRR_VALID: u64 = 1 << 11;

#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
#[repr(u8)]
pub enum MtrrMemoryType {
    Uncacheable = 0,
    WriteCombining = 1,
    WriteThrough = 4,
    WriteProtected = 5,
    WriteBack = 6,
}

impl MtrrMemoryType {
    pub fn from_raw(value: u8) -> Result<Self, MtrrError> {
        match value {
            0 => Ok(Self::Uncacheable),
            1 => Ok(Self::WriteCombining),
            4 => Ok(Self::WriteThrough),
            5 => Ok(Self::WriteProtected),
            6 => Ok(Self::WriteBack),
            value => Err(MtrrError::ReservedMemoryType { value }),
        }
    }
}

#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum MtrrError {
    InvalidPhysicalAddressWidth,
    ReservedBaseBits,
    ReservedMaskBits,
    ReservedMemoryType { value: u8 },
    FixedRangesUnavailable,
    PhysicalAddressOutOfRange,
    PhysicalAddressWidthMismatch,
    UndefinedOverlap,
}

/// Decoded fixed MTRR memory types in ascending physical-address order.
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct FixedMtrrRanges {
    memory_types: [MtrrMemoryType; FIXED_MTRR_TYPE_COUNT],
}

impl FixedMtrrRanges {
    /// Decode FIX64K_00000, FIX16K_80000/A0000, and FIX4K_C0000..F8000.
    pub fn from_msr_values(registers: [u64; 11]) -> Result<Self, MtrrError> {
        let mut memory_types = [MtrrMemoryType::Uncacheable; FIXED_MTRR_TYPE_COUNT];
        for (register_index, value) in registers.iter().enumerate() {
            for slot in 0..8 {
                let memory_type = ((value >> (slot * 8)) & 0xff) as u8;
                memory_types[register_index * 8 + slot] = MtrrMemoryType::from_raw(memory_type)?;
            }
        }
        Ok(Self { memory_types })
    }

    fn type_for_address(&self, address: u64) -> Option<MtrrMemoryType> {
        let index = if address < 0x80_000 {
            (address / 0x1_0000) as usize
        } else if address < 0xa0_000 {
            8 + ((address - 0x80_000) / 0x4000) as usize
        } else if address < 0xc0_000 {
            16 + ((address - 0xa0_000) / 0x4000) as usize
        } else if address < 0x10_0000 {
            24 + ((address - 0xc0_000) / 0x1000) as usize
        } else {
            return None;
        };
        Some(self.memory_types[index])
    }
}

/// One valid variable-range MTRR. Address masks need not be contiguous; bits
/// omitted by the mask simply do not participate in matching.
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct VariableMtrr {
    base_match: u64,
    address_mask: u64,
    physical_address_bits: u8,
    memory_type: MtrrMemoryType,
}

impl VariableMtrr {
    /// Decode one IA32_MTRR_PHYSBASE/PHYSMASK pair. A clear valid bit returns `Ok(None).`
    pub fn from_msr_values(
        base: u64,
        mask: u64,
        physical_address_bits: u8,
    ) -> Result<Option<Self>, MtrrError> {
        if !(12..=MAX_MTRR_PHYSICAL_ADDRESS_BITS).contains(&physical_address_bits) {
            return Err(MtrrError::InvalidPhysicalAddressWidth);
        }
        let physical_mask = ((1u64 << physical_address_bits) - 1) & !(PAGE_SIZE - 1);
        if base & !(physical_mask | 0xff) != 0 {
            return Err(MtrrError::ReservedBaseBits);
        }
        if mask & !(physical_mask | MTRR_VALID) != 0 {
            return Err(MtrrError::ReservedMaskBits);
        }
        let memory_type = MtrrMemoryType::from_raw((base & 0xff) as u8)?;
        if mask & MTRR_VALID == 0 {
            return Ok(None);
        }

        let address_mask = mask & physical_mask;
        Ok(Some(Self {
            base_match: base & address_mask,
            address_mask,
            physical_address_bits,
            memory_type,
        }))
    }

    fn matches(self, address: u64) -> bool {
        address & self.address_mask == self.base_match
    }
}

/// MTRR policy decoded from supplied register values; it does not access MSRs.
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct MtrrLayout<'a> {
    physical_address_bits: u8,
    enabled: bool,
    fixed_enabled: bool,
    default_type: MtrrMemoryType,
    fixed_ranges: Option<&'a FixedMtrrRanges>,
    variable_ranges: &'a [VariableMtrr],
}

impl<'a> MtrrLayout<'a> {
    pub fn new(
        physical_address_bits: u8,
        enabled: bool,
        fixed_enabled: bool,
        default_type: MtrrMemoryType,
        fixed_ranges: Option<&'a FixedMtrrRanges>,
        variable_ranges: &'a [VariableMtrr],
    ) -> Result<Self, MtrrError> {
        if !(12..=MAX_MTRR_PHYSICAL_ADDRESS_BITS).contains(&physical_address_bits) {
            return Err(MtrrError::InvalidPhysicalAddressWidth);
        }
        if enabled && fixed_enabled && fixed_ranges.is_none() {
            return Err(MtrrError::FixedRangesUnavailable);
        }
        if variable_ranges
            .iter()
            .any(|range| range.physical_address_bits != physical_address_bits)
        {
            return Err(MtrrError::PhysicalAddressWidthMismatch);
        }

        Ok(Self {
            physical_address_bits,
            enabled,
            fixed_enabled,
            default_type,
            fixed_ranges,
            variable_ranges,
        })
    }

    /// Resolve the MTRR type for one physical address, rejecting undefined overlaps.
    pub fn memory_type_for(&self, address: u64) -> Result<MtrrMemoryType, MtrrError> {
        if address >= (1u64 << self.physical_address_bits) {
            return Err(MtrrError::PhysicalAddressOutOfRange);
        }
        if !self.enabled {
            return Ok(MtrrMemoryType::Uncacheable);
        }
        if self.fixed_enabled {
            if let Some(memory_type) = self
                .fixed_ranges
                .and_then(|ranges| ranges.type_for_address(address))
            {
                return Ok(memory_type);
            }
        }

        let mut matched_types = 0u8;
        for range in self.variable_ranges {
            if range.matches(address) {
                matched_types |= 1 << range.memory_type as u8;
            }
        }
        if matched_types == 0 {
            return Ok(self.default_type);
        }
        if matched_types & (1 << MtrrMemoryType::Uncacheable as u8) != 0 {
            return Ok(MtrrMemoryType::Uncacheable);
        }
        if matched_types.count_ones() == 1 {
            return MtrrMemoryType::from_raw(matched_types.trailing_zeros() as u8);
        }
        let write_back_and_through =
            (1 << MtrrMemoryType::WriteBack as u8) | (1 << MtrrMemoryType::WriteThrough as u8);
        if matched_types == write_back_and_through {
            return Ok(MtrrMemoryType::WriteThrough);
        }
        Err(MtrrError::UndefinedOverlap)
    }
}

#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum MappingError {
    EmptyRange,
    UnalignedRange,
    AddressOverflow,
    InvalidPhysicalAddressWidth,
    UnknownPhysicalAddressWidth,
    InvalidVirtualAddressWidth,
    PhysicalRangeOutOfBounds,
    NonCanonicalVirtualRange,
    CrossesCanonicalHole,
    WritableExecutable,
    UnalignedPageOffset,
    PageOffsetOutOfRange,
    InvalidPatIndex,
    NxNotEnabled,
}

/// Validate one contiguous range for a future 4 KiB page-mapping operation.
///
/// The physical-address width must be known; passing `None` is rejected rather
/// than treating an unknown bound as unbounded. Successful validation does not
/// establish that physical frames are owned by a caller or mapped in the HHDM.
pub fn validate_mapping_range(
    virtual_start: u64,
    physical_start: u64,
    length: u64,
    permissions: PagePermissions,
    physical_address_bits: Option<u8>,
    virtual_address_bits: u8,
) -> Result<ValidatedMappingRange, MappingError> {
    if virtual_address_bits == 0 || virtual_address_bits > 64 {
        return Err(MappingError::InvalidVirtualAddressWidth);
    }
    let physical_address_bits =
        physical_address_bits.ok_or(MappingError::UnknownPhysicalAddressWidth)?;
    if physical_address_bits == 0 || physical_address_bits > 64 {
        return Err(MappingError::InvalidPhysicalAddressWidth);
    }
    if length == 0 {
        return Err(MappingError::EmptyRange);
    }
    if (virtual_start | physical_start | length) & (PAGE_SIZE - 1) != 0 {
        return Err(MappingError::UnalignedRange);
    }
    if permissions.writable && permissions.executable {
        return Err(MappingError::WritableExecutable);
    }

    let virtual_end = virtual_start
        .checked_add(length)
        .ok_or(MappingError::AddressOverflow)?;
    let physical_end = physical_start
        .checked_add(length)
        .ok_or(MappingError::AddressOverflow)?;
    if !physical_range_fits_address_width(physical_start, physical_end, physical_address_bits) {
        return Err(MappingError::PhysicalRangeOutOfBounds);
    }

    let last_virtual_address = virtual_end - 1;
    if !is_canonical_virtual_address(virtual_start, virtual_address_bits)
        || !is_canonical_virtual_address(last_virtual_address, virtual_address_bits)
    {
        return Err(MappingError::NonCanonicalVirtualRange);
    }
    if virtual_address_bits < 64
        && ((virtual_start ^ last_virtual_address) & (1u64 << (virtual_address_bits - 1))) != 0
    {
        return Err(MappingError::CrossesCanonicalHole);
    }

    Ok(ValidatedMappingRange {
        virtual_start,
        virtual_end,
        physical_start,
        physical_end,
        physical_address_bits,
        permissions,
    })
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::{
        capture_mtrr_registers, parse_cr3_root, validate_mapping_range, Cr3Error, Cr3LowBits,
        FixedMtrrRanges, MappingError, MtrrError, MtrrLayout, MtrrMemoryType, MtrrRegisterPair,
        MtrrState, PagePermissions, ValidatedMappingRange, VariableMtrr,
        MAX_CAPTURED_VARIABLE_MTRRS, PAGE_SIZE,
    };
    use core::cell::Cell;

    const KERNEL_READ_ONLY: PagePermissions = PagePermissions {
        writable: false,
        executable: false,
        user_accessible: false,
    };

    fn variable_mtrr(base: u64, size: u64, memory_type: MtrrMemoryType) -> VariableMtrr {
        let physical_address_bits = 36;
        let physical_mask = ((1u64 << physical_address_bits) - 1) & !(PAGE_SIZE - 1);
        let mask = physical_mask & !(size - 1) | (1 << 11);
        VariableMtrr::from_msr_values(base | memory_type as u8 as u64, mask, physical_address_bits)
            .unwrap()
            .unwrap()
    }

    #[test]
    fn mtrr_capture_is_gated_by_support() {
        let state = capture_mtrr_registers(false, |_| panic!("read MSR without MTRR support"));
        assert_eq!(state, MtrrState::Unsupported);
    }

    #[test]
    fn captures_supported_fixed_and_variable_mtrr_registers() {
        let reads = Cell::new(0);
        let state = capture_mtrr_registers(true, |index| {
            reads.set(reads.get() + 1);
            match index {
                0xfe => 2 | (1 << 8),
                0x2ff => 0xc06,
                _ => u64::from(index),
            }
        });

        let MtrrState::Captured(registers) = state else {
            panic!("expected a complete MTRR snapshot");
        };
        assert_eq!(reads.get(), 2 + 11 + 4);
        assert_eq!(registers.capability, 2 | (1 << 8));
        assert_eq!(registers.default_type, 0xc06);
        assert_eq!(registers.variable_register_count, 2);
        let fixed = registers.fixed_registers.expect("fixed ranges are supported");
        assert_eq!(fixed[0], 0x250);
        assert_eq!(fixed[10], 0x26f);
        assert_eq!(registers.variable_registers[0].base, 0x200);
        assert_eq!(registers.variable_registers[0].mask, 0x201);
        assert_eq!(registers.variable_registers[1].base, 0x202);
        assert_eq!(registers.variable_registers[1].mask, 0x203);
        assert_eq!(registers.variable_registers[2], MtrrRegisterPair { base: 0, mask: 0 });
    }

    #[test]
    fn mtrr_capture_reports_capacity_excess_without_partial_reads() {
        let reads = Cell::new(0);
        let state = capture_mtrr_registers(true, |index| {
            reads.set(reads.get() + 1);
            if index == 0xfe {
                (MAX_CAPTURED_VARIABLE_MTRRS as u64) + 1
            } else {
                0
            }
        });

        assert_eq!(
            state,
            MtrrState::VariableRangeCapacityExceeded {
                reported_count: (MAX_CAPTURED_VARIABLE_MTRRS + 1) as u8,
            }
        );
        assert_eq!(reads.get(), 1);
    }

    #[test]
    fn mtrr_capture_skips_unsupported_fixed_registers() {
        let reads = Cell::new(0);
        let state = capture_mtrr_registers(true, |index| {
            reads.set(reads.get() + 1);
            match index {
                0xfe => 1,
                0x2ff => 0xc06,
                _ => u64::from(index),
            }
        });

        let MtrrState::Captured(registers) = state else {
            panic!("expected a complete MTRR snapshot");
        };
        assert_eq!(reads.get(), 4);
        assert_eq!(registers.fixed_registers, None);
        assert_eq!(registers.variable_register_count, 1);
        assert_eq!(registers.variable_registers[0].base, 0x200);
        assert_eq!(registers.variable_registers[0].mask, 0x201);
    }

    #[test]
    fn decodes_cr3_root_with_pcid_enabled() {
        let root = parse_cr3_root(0x1234_5000 | 0x0abc, Some(48), true).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(root.physical_address(), 0x1234_5000);
        assert_eq!(root.low_bits(), Cr3LowBits::Pcid(0x0abc));
    }

    #[test]
    fn decodes_cr3_cache_controls_without_pcid() {
        let root = parse_cr3_root(0x1234_5000 | (1 << 3) | (1 << 4), Some(48), false).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(root.physical_address(), 0x1234_5000);
        assert_eq!(
            root.low_bits(),
            Cr3LowBits::CacheControls {
                page_level_write_through: true,
                page_level_cache_disable: true,
            }
        );
    }

    #[test]
    fn rejects_cr3_reserved_bits_and_invalid_address_widths() {
        assert_eq!(
            parse_cr3_root(0x1000 | 1, Some(48), false),
            Err(Cr3Error::ReservedBits)
        );
        assert_eq!(
            parse_cr3_root(1 << 40, Some(40), true),
            Err(Cr3Error::ReservedBits)
        );
        assert_eq!(
            parse_cr3_root(0x1000, None, false),
            Err(Cr3Error::UnknownPhysicalAddressWidth)
        );
        assert_eq!(
            parse_cr3_root(0x1000, Some(53), false),
            Err(Cr3Error::InvalidPhysicalAddressWidth)
        );
    }

    #[test]
    fn resolves_variable_mtrr_ranges_and_default_type() {
        let ranges = [variable_mtrr(
            0x20_0000,
            0x20_0000,
            MtrrMemoryType::WriteBack,
        )];
        let layout =
            MtrrLayout::new(36, true, false, MtrrMemoryType::Uncacheable, None, &ranges).unwrap();

        assert_eq!(
            layout.memory_type_for(0x20_0000),
            Ok(MtrrMemoryType::WriteBack)
        );
        assert_eq!(
            layout.memory_type_for(0x3f_ffff),
            Ok(MtrrMemoryType::WriteBack)
        );
        assert_eq!(
            layout.memory_type_for(0x40_0000),
            Ok(MtrrMemoryType::Uncacheable)
        );
        assert_eq!(
            layout.memory_type_for(1u64 << 36),
            Err(MtrrError::PhysicalAddressOutOfRange)
        );
    }

    #[test]
    fn fixed_mtrrs_override_variable_and_default_ranges_below_one_mib() {
        let mut registers = [0; 11];
        registers[2] = MtrrMemoryType::WriteThrough as u64;
        let fixed = FixedMtrrRanges::from_msr_values(registers).unwrap();
        let variable = [variable_mtrr(0, 0x10_0000, MtrrMemoryType::WriteBack)];
        let layout = MtrrLayout::new(
            36,
            true,
            true,
            MtrrMemoryType::WriteBack,
            Some(&fixed),
            &variable,
        )
        .unwrap();

        assert_eq!(
            layout.memory_type_for(0xa_0000),
            Ok(MtrrMemoryType::WriteThrough)
        );
        assert_eq!(
            layout.memory_type_for(0xa_4000),
            Ok(MtrrMemoryType::Uncacheable)
        );
        assert_eq!(
            layout.memory_type_for(0x10_0000),
            Ok(MtrrMemoryType::WriteBack)
        );
    }

    #[test]
    fn resolves_defined_variable_mtrr_overlaps_and_rejects_undefined_ones() {
        let write_back_through = [
            variable_mtrr(0x20_0000, 0x20_0000, MtrrMemoryType::WriteBack),
            variable_mtrr(0x20_0000, 0x20_0000, MtrrMemoryType::WriteThrough),
        ];
        let layout = MtrrLayout::new(
            36,
            true,
            false,
            MtrrMemoryType::Uncacheable,
            None,
            &write_back_through,
        )
        .unwrap();
        assert_eq!(
            layout.memory_type_for(0x20_0000),
            Ok(MtrrMemoryType::WriteThrough)
        );

        let uncacheable_override = [
            write_back_through[0],
            variable_mtrr(0x20_0000, 0x20_0000, MtrrMemoryType::Uncacheable),
        ];
        let layout = MtrrLayout::new(
            36,
            true,
            false,
            MtrrMemoryType::WriteBack,
            None,
            &uncacheable_override,
        )
        .unwrap();
        assert_eq!(
            layout.memory_type_for(0x20_0000),
            Ok(MtrrMemoryType::Uncacheable)
        );

        let undefined = [
            variable_mtrr(0x20_0000, 0x20_0000, MtrrMemoryType::WriteCombining),
            variable_mtrr(0x20_0000, 0x20_0000, MtrrMemoryType::WriteProtected),
        ];
        let layout =
            MtrrLayout::new(36, true, false, MtrrMemoryType::WriteBack, None, &undefined).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(
            layout.memory_type_for(0x20_0000),
            Err(MtrrError::UndefinedOverlap)
        );
    }

    #[test]
    fn disabled_mtrrs_force_uncacheable_and_bad_registers_are_rejected() {
        let layout =
            MtrrLayout::new(36, false, true, MtrrMemoryType::WriteBack, None, &[]).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(
            layout.memory_type_for(0x20_0000),
            Ok(MtrrMemoryType::Uncacheable)
        );
        assert_eq!(
            MtrrLayout::new(36, true, true, MtrrMemoryType::WriteBack, None, &[]),
            Err(MtrrError::FixedRangesUnavailable)
        );
        assert_eq!(
            VariableMtrr::from_msr_values(0x1000 | 0x200, 0, 36),
            Err(MtrrError::ReservedBaseBits)
        );
        assert_eq!(
            VariableMtrr::from_msr_values(0x1000 | 6, 1 << 10, 36),
            Err(MtrrError::ReservedMaskBits)
        );
        assert_eq!(VariableMtrr::from_msr_values(0x1000 | 6, 0, 36), Ok(None));
        let width_mismatch = [variable_mtrr(
            0x20_0000,
            0x20_0000,
            MtrrMemoryType::WriteBack,
        )];
        assert_eq!(
            MtrrLayout::new(
                35,
                true,
                false,
                MtrrMemoryType::WriteBack,
                None,
                &width_mismatch,
            ),
            Err(MtrrError::PhysicalAddressWidthMismatch)
        );
        assert_eq!(
            VariableMtrr::from_msr_values(0x1000 | 2, 1 << 11, 36),
            Err(MtrrError::ReservedMemoryType { value: 2 })
        );
        let mut invalid_fixed = [0; 11];
        invalid_fixed[0] = 2;
        assert_eq!(
            FixedMtrrRanges::from_msr_values(invalid_fixed),
            Err(MtrrError::ReservedMemoryType { value: 2 })
        );
    }

    #[test]
    fn accepts_aligned_ranges_at_canonical_boundaries() {
        let lower = validate_mapping_range(
            0x0000_7fff_ffff_e000,
            0x1000,
            0x2000,
            KERNEL_READ_ONLY,
            Some(14),
            48,
        )
        .unwrap();
        assert_eq!(
            lower,
            ValidatedMappingRange {
                virtual_start: 0x0000_7fff_ffff_e000,
                virtual_end: 0x0000_8000_0000_0000,
                physical_start: 0x1000,
                physical_end: 0x3000,
                physical_address_bits: 14,
                permissions: KERNEL_READ_ONLY,
            }
        );

        let upper = validate_mapping_range(
            0xffff_8000_0000_0000,
            0,
            PAGE_SIZE,
            KERNEL_READ_ONLY,
            Some(12),
            48,
        )
        .unwrap();
        assert_eq!(upper.virtual_end(), 0xffff_8000_0000_1000);
    }

    #[test]
    fn rejects_empty_and_unaligned_ranges() {
        assert_eq!(
            validate_mapping_range(0x1000, 0x2000, 0, KERNEL_READ_ONLY, Some(32), 48),
            Err(MappingError::EmptyRange)
        );
        assert_eq!(
            validate_mapping_range(0x1001, 0x2000, PAGE_SIZE, KERNEL_READ_ONLY, Some(32), 48),
            Err(MappingError::UnalignedRange)
        );
        assert_eq!(
            validate_mapping_range(
                0x1000,
                0x2000,
                PAGE_SIZE + 1,
                KERNEL_READ_ONLY,
                Some(32),
                48
            ),
            Err(MappingError::UnalignedRange)
        );
    }

    #[test]
    fn requires_known_valid_address_widths_and_bounded_physical_ranges() {
        assert_eq!(
            validate_mapping_range(0x1000, 0x1000, PAGE_SIZE, KERNEL_READ_ONLY, None, 48),
            Err(MappingError::UnknownPhysicalAddressWidth)
        );
        assert_eq!(
            validate_mapping_range(0x1000, 0x1000, PAGE_SIZE, KERNEL_READ_ONLY, Some(0), 48),
            Err(MappingError::InvalidPhysicalAddressWidth)
        );
        assert_eq!(
            validate_mapping_range(0x1000, 0x1000, PAGE_SIZE, KERNEL_READ_ONLY, Some(52), 0),
            Err(MappingError::InvalidVirtualAddressWidth)
        );
        assert_eq!(
            validate_mapping_range(
                0x1000,
                0x1000,
                PAGE_SIZE * 2,
                KERNEL_READ_ONLY,
                Some(13),
                48
            ),
            Err(MappingError::PhysicalRangeOutOfBounds)
        );
    }

    #[test]
    fn rejects_noncanonical_ranges_and_ranges_crossing_the_canonical_hole() {
        assert_eq!(
            validate_mapping_range(
                0x0000_8000_0000_0000,
                0,
                PAGE_SIZE,
                KERNEL_READ_ONLY,
                Some(52),
                48
            ),
            Err(MappingError::NonCanonicalVirtualRange)
        );

        let crosses_hole = (0xffff_8000_0000_1000u64) - 0x0000_7fff_ffff_f000;
        assert_eq!(
            validate_mapping_range(
                0x0000_7fff_ffff_f000,
                0,
                crosses_hole,
                KERNEL_READ_ONLY,
                Some(64),
                48,
            ),
            Err(MappingError::CrossesCanonicalHole)
        );
    }

    fn pat_value(entries: [u8; 8]) -> u64 {
        entries.iter().enumerate().fold(0, |value, (index, entry)| {
            value | ((*entry as u64) << (index * 8))
        })
    }

    #[test]
    fn resolves_cache_policies_from_the_supplied_pat_layout() {
        let pat = pat_value([6, 4, 7, 0, 6, 1, 7, 0]);
        let layout = super::PatLayout::from_msr_value(pat).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(layout.index_for(super::CachePolicy::WriteBack), Some(0));
        assert_eq!(layout.index_for(super::CachePolicy::Uncacheable), Some(3));
        assert_eq!(
            layout.index_for(super::CachePolicy::WriteCombining),
            Some(5)
        );

        let without_write_combining =
            super::PatLayout::from_msr_value(pat_value([6, 4, 7, 0, 6, 4, 7, 0])).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(
            without_write_combining.index_for(super::CachePolicy::WriteCombining),
            None
        );
    }

    #[test]
    fn rejects_reserved_pat_entries() {
        assert_eq!(
            super::PatLayout::from_msr_value(0x08),
            Err(super::PatLayoutError::ReservedBits { index: 0 })
        );
        assert_eq!(
            super::PatLayout::from_msr_value(0b010 << 24),
            Err(super::PatLayoutError::ReservedMemoryType {
                index: 3,
                value: 0b010,
            })
        );
    }

    #[test]
    fn encodes_4k_leaf_permissions_nx_and_pat_index_bits() {
        let writable_user_page = PagePermissions {
            writable: true,
            executable: false,
            user_accessible: true,
        };
        let mapping = validate_mapping_range(
            0x4000,
            0x20_0000,
            PAGE_SIZE * 2,
            writable_user_page,
            Some(52),
            48,
        )
        .unwrap();

        let first = mapping.leaf_4k_entry(0, 0b101, true).unwrap().bits();
        assert_eq!(
            first,
            0x20_0000 | (1 << 0) | (1 << 1) | (1 << 2) | (1 << 3) | (1 << 7) | (1 << 63)
        );
        let second = mapping
            .leaf_4k_entry(PAGE_SIZE, 0b101, true)
            .unwrap()
            .bits();
        assert_eq!(second & 0x000f_ffff_ffff_f000, 0x20_1000);
        assert_eq!(second & (1 << 63), 1 << 63);

        let all_pat_bits = mapping.leaf_4k_entry(0, 0b111, true).unwrap().bits()
            & ((1 << 3) | (1 << 4) | (1 << 7));
        assert_eq!(all_pat_bits, (1 << 3) | (1 << 4) | (1 << 7));
    }

    #[test]
    fn rejects_unencodable_leaf_attributes_and_page_offsets() {
        let mapping =
            validate_mapping_range(0x4000, 0x20_0000, PAGE_SIZE, KERNEL_READ_ONLY, Some(52), 48)
                .unwrap();
        assert_eq!(
            mapping.leaf_4k_entry(0, 8, true),
            Err(MappingError::InvalidPatIndex)
        );
        assert_eq!(
            mapping.leaf_4k_entry(0, 0, false),
            Err(MappingError::NxNotEnabled)
        );
        assert_eq!(
            mapping.leaf_4k_entry(1, 0, true),
            Err(MappingError::UnalignedPageOffset)
        );
        assert_eq!(
            mapping.leaf_4k_entry(PAGE_SIZE, 0, true),
            Err(MappingError::PageOffsetOutOfRange)
        );

        let too_wide =
            validate_mapping_range(0x4000, 0x20_0000, PAGE_SIZE, KERNEL_READ_ONLY, Some(53), 48)
                .unwrap();
        assert_eq!(
            too_wide.leaf_4k_entry(0, 0, true),
            Err(MappingError::InvalidPhysicalAddressWidth)
        );
    }

    #[test]
    fn executable_leaf_does_not_set_nx() {
        let executable = PagePermissions {
            writable: false,
            executable: true,
            user_accessible: false,
        };
        let mapping =
            validate_mapping_range(0x4000, 0x20_0000, PAGE_SIZE, executable, Some(52), 48).unwrap();
        let entry = mapping.leaf_4k_entry(0, 0, false).unwrap().bits();
        assert_eq!(entry, 0x20_0000 | 1);
    }

    #[test]
    fn rejects_arithmetic_overflow_and_writable_executable_ranges() {
        assert_eq!(
            validate_mapping_range(
                u64::MAX - (PAGE_SIZE - 1),
                0,
                PAGE_SIZE,
                KERNEL_READ_ONLY,
                Some(64),
                64
            ),
            Err(MappingError::AddressOverflow)
        );
        assert_eq!(
            validate_mapping_range(
                0x1000,
                u64::MAX - (PAGE_SIZE - 1),
                PAGE_SIZE,
                KERNEL_READ_ONLY,
                Some(64),
                64
            ),
            Err(MappingError::AddressOverflow)
        );

        let writable_executable = PagePermissions {
            writable: true,
            executable: true,
            user_accessible: false,
        };
        assert_eq!(
            validate_mapping_range(0x1000, 0x2000, PAGE_SIZE, writable_executable, Some(52), 48),
            Err(MappingError::WritableExecutable)
        );
    }
}

//! CPU feature and gated, read-only MSR reporting for x86_64 boot diagnostics.

use core::arch::asm;
use core::arch::x86_64::{__cpuid, __cpuid_count};
use rustix_kernel::paging::{capture_mtrr_registers, MtrrState};

const IA32_EFER: u32 = 0xc000_0080;
const IA32_PAT: u32 = 0x0000_0277;
const EFER_NXE: u64 = 1 << 11;

#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct CpuInfo {
    pub vendor: [u8; 12],
    pub max_basic_leaf: u32,
    pub max_extended_leaf: u32,
    pub has_sse2: bool,
    pub has_nx: bool,
    pub nx_enabled: bool,
    pub has_pat: bool,
    pub pat_msr_value: Option<u64>,
    pub mtrr: MtrrState,
    pub has_1g_pages: bool,
    pub has_long_mode: bool,
    pub has_la57: bool,
    pub physical_address_bits: Option<u8>,
    pub max_linear_address_bits: Option<u8>,
    pub active_linear_address_bits: u8,
    pub pcid_enabled: bool,
}

/// Read CPUID identity, selected feature bits, and supported read-only MSR state.
pub fn identify() -> CpuInfo {
    // CPUID is part of the x86_64 architectural baseline.
    let basic = __cpuid(0);
    let mut vendor = [0; 12];
    vendor[0..4].copy_from_slice(&basic.ebx.to_le_bytes());
    vendor[4..8].copy_from_slice(&basic.edx.to_le_bytes());
    vendor[8..12].copy_from_slice(&basic.ecx.to_le_bytes());

    let basic_features = if basic.eax >= 1 {
        Some(__cpuid(1))
    } else {
        None
    };
    let extended = __cpuid(0x8000_0000);
    let extended_features = if extended.eax >= 0x8000_0001 {
        Some(__cpuid(0x8000_0001))
    } else {
        None
    };
    let structured_features = if basic.eax >= 7 {
        Some(__cpuid_count(7, 0))
    } else {
        None
    };
    let address_widths = if extended.eax >= 0x8000_0008 {
        Some(__cpuid(0x8000_0008).eax)
    } else {
        None
    };
    let cr4 = read_cr4_raw();
    let has_nx = extended_features.is_some_and(|features| features.edx & (1 << 20) != 0);
    let nx_enabled = if has_nx {
        // SAFETY: EFER is available in x86_64 long mode; CPUID confirms NX support,
        // and this boot-time code executes at CPL 0. The read does not change state.
        unsafe { read_msr(IA32_EFER) & EFER_NXE != 0 }
    } else {
        false
    };
    let has_pat = basic_features.is_some_and(|features| features.edx & (1 << 16) != 0);
    let pat_msr_value = if has_pat {
        // SAFETY: CPUID reports PAT support and boot-time kernel code runs at CPL 0.
        Some(unsafe { read_msr(IA32_PAT) })
    } else {
        None
    };
    let has_mtrr = basic_features.is_some_and(|features| features.edx & (1 << 12) != 0);
    let mtrr = capture_mtrr_registers(has_mtrr, |index| {
        // SAFETY: CPUID reports MTRR support; the capture helper only requests
        // architectural MTRR MSRs after that feature check.
        unsafe { read_msr(index) }
    });

    CpuInfo {
        vendor,
        max_basic_leaf: basic.eax,
        max_extended_leaf: extended.eax,
        has_sse2: basic_features.is_some_and(|features| features.edx & (1 << 26) != 0),
        has_nx,
        nx_enabled,
        has_pat,
        pat_msr_value,
        mtrr,
        has_1g_pages: extended_features.is_some_and(|features| features.edx & (1 << 26) != 0),
        has_long_mode: extended_features.is_some_and(|features| features.edx & (1 << 29) != 0),
        has_la57: structured_features.is_some_and(|features| features.ecx & (1 << 16) != 0),
        physical_address_bits: address_widths.map(|eax| (eax & 0xff) as u8),
        max_linear_address_bits: address_widths.map(|eax| ((eax >> 8) & 0xff) as u8),
        active_linear_address_bits: if cr4 & (1 << 12) != 0 { 57 } else { 48 },
        pcid_enabled: cr4 & (1 << 17) != 0,
    }
}


/// Read the current raw CR3 value without changing page-table state.
pub fn read_cr3_raw() -> u64 {
    let cr3: u64;
    // SAFETY: Rustix runs at CPL 0; reading CR3 is privileged but non-mutating.
    unsafe { asm!("mov {}, cr3", out(reg) cr3, options(nomem, nostack, preserves_flags)) };
    cr3
}

/// Read a model-specific register at CPL 0.
///
/// # Safety
/// The caller must ensure the MSR exists on this CPU and that the current
/// privilege level permits the read.
unsafe fn read_msr(index: u32) -> u64 {
    let low: u32;
    let high: u32;
    // SAFETY: The caller guarantees that this MSR is supported and accessible.
    unsafe {
        asm!(
            "rdmsr",
            in("ecx") index,
            out("eax") low,
            out("edx") high,
            options(nomem, nostack)
        );
    }
    (u64::from(high) << 32) | u64::from(low)
}


/// Read CR4 without changing paging state.
fn read_cr4_raw() -> u64 {
    let cr4: u64;
    // SAFETY: Rustix runs at CPL 0; reading CR4 is privileged but non-mutating.
    unsafe { asm!("mov {}, cr4", out(reg) cr4, options(nomem, nostack, preserves_flags)) };
    cr4
}

/// Structural checks can reject malformed pointers and ranges, but cannot prove
/// that a loader-provided pointer is mapped and readable. That remains part of
/// the documented Limine handoff trust boundary until the kernel owns its maps.
pub fn capture_boot_information(entry_rsp: u64) -> Result<BootInfo, BootInfoError> {
    let cpu_info = crate::arch::x86_64::cpu::identify();
    let inherited_cr3_raw = crate::arch::x86_64::cpu::read_cr3_raw();
    let inherited_cr3_root = parse_cr3_root(
        inherited_cr3_raw,
        cpu_info.physical_address_bits,
        cpu_info.pcid_enabled,
    );
    let virtual_address_bits = cpu_info.active_linear_address_bits;
    let (boot_stack_virtual_start, boot_stack_virtual_end) =
        limine_x86_64_stack_bounds(entry_rsp, virtual_address_bits)
            .ok_or(BootInfoError::InvalidInitialStackBounds)?;
    let hhdm_request = core::ptr::addr_of_mut!(HHDM_REQUEST);
    // SAFETY: Limine has completed writing the request response before `_start`.
    let hhdm_pointer =
        unsafe { core::ptr::read_volatile(core::ptr::addr_of!((*hhdm_request).response)) };
    if hhdm_pointer.is_null() {
        return Err(BootInfoError::MissingHhdmResponse);
    }
    if !is_valid_pointer(hhdm_pointer, virtual_address_bits) {
        return Err(BootInfoError::InvalidHhdmResponsePointer);
    }
    // SAFETY: The Limine response pointer is trusted to refer to a readable
    // response object; its nullness and alignment are checked above.
    let hhdm = unsafe { hhdm_pointer.read_volatile() };
    if hhdm.offset & 0xfff != 0 || !is_canonical_virtual_address(hhdm.offset, virtual_address_bits)
    {
        return Err(BootInfoError::InvalidHhdmOffset);
    }

    let executable_address_request = core::ptr::addr_of_mut!(EXECUTABLE_ADDRESS_REQUEST);
    // SAFETY: Limine has completed writing the request response before `_start`.
    let executable_address_pointer = unsafe {
        core::ptr::read_volatile(core::ptr::addr_of!((*executable_address_request).response))
    };
    if executable_address_pointer.is_null() {
        return Err(BootInfoError::MissingExecutableAddressResponse);
    }
    if !is_valid_pointer(executable_address_pointer, virtual_address_bits) {
        return Err(BootInfoError::InvalidExecutableAddressResponsePointer);
    }
    // SAFETY: Limine's response pointer is trusted to refer to a readable object;
    // nullness, alignment, and active-width canonicality were checked above.
    let executable_address = unsafe { executable_address_pointer.read_volatile() };
    // `linker.ld` defines these symbols as the boundaries of the loaded image.
    let (linked_virtual_start, linked_virtual_end) = (
        core::ptr::addr_of!(__kernel_start) as u64,
        core::ptr::addr_of!(__kernel_end) as u64,
    );
    let kernel_physical_end = kernel_image_physical_end(
        executable_address.physical_base,
        executable_address.virtual_base,
        linked_virtual_start,
        linked_virtual_end,
        cpu_info.physical_address_bits,
        virtual_address_bits,
    )
    .ok_or(BootInfoError::InvalidKernelImageRange)?;
    let linked_segments = KernelImageVirtualSegments {
        text: (
            core::ptr::addr_of!(__kernel_text_mapping_start) as u64,
            core::ptr::addr_of!(__kernel_text_mapping_end) as u64,
        ),
        rodata: (
            core::ptr::addr_of!(__kernel_rodata_mapping_start) as u64,
            core::ptr::addr_of!(__kernel_rodata_mapping_end) as u64,
        ),
        data: (
            core::ptr::addr_of!(__kernel_data_mapping_start) as u64,
            core::ptr::addr_of!(__kernel_data_mapping_end) as u64,
        ),
    };
    let kernel_image_segments = kernel_image_segments(
        executable_address.physical_base,
        executable_address.virtual_base,
        linked_virtual_start,
        linked_virtual_end,
        linked_segments,
        cpu_info.physical_address_bits,
        virtual_address_bits,
    )
    .ok_or(BootInfoError::InvalidKernelImageSegments)?;

    let memory_map_request = core::ptr::addr_of_mut!(MEMORY_MAP_REQUEST);
    // SAFETY: Limine has completed writing the request response before `_start`.
    let memory_map_pointer =
        unsafe { core::ptr::read_volatile(core::ptr::addr_of!((*memory_map_request).response)) };
    if memory_map_pointer.is_null() {
        return Err(BootInfoError::MissingMemoryMapResponse);
    }
    if !is_valid_pointer(memory_map_pointer, virtual_address_bits) {
        return Err(BootInfoError::InvalidMemoryMapResponsePointer);
    }
    // SAFETY: The Limine response pointer is trusted to refer to a readable
    // response object; its nullness and alignment are checked above.
    let response = unsafe { memory_map_pointer.read_volatile() };
    let entry_count = usize::try_from(response.entry_count)
        .map_err(|_| BootInfoError::MemoryMapCountDoesNotFit)?;
    if entry_count > MAX_MEMORY_REGIONS {
        return Err(BootInfoError::TooManyMemoryRegions);
    }
    if entry_count == 0 {
        return Err(BootInfoError::EmptyMemoryMap);
    }
    if response.entries.is_null() {
        return Err(BootInfoError::InvalidEntriesPointer);
    }
    if !is_valid_pointer(response.entries, virtual_address_bits) {
        return Err(BootInfoError::InvalidEntriesPointer);
    }
    let entry_bytes = entry_count
        .checked_mul(size_of::<*const MemoryMapEntry>())
        .ok_or(BootInfoError::EntriesAddressOverflow)?;
    let entries_start = response.entries as usize;
    let entries_end = entries_start
        .checked_add(entry_bytes)
        .ok_or(BootInfoError::EntriesAddressOverflow)?;
    if !is_canonical_virtual_address(entries_start as u64, virtual_address_bits)
        || !is_canonical_virtual_address((entries_end - 1) as u64, virtual_address_bits)
    {
        return Err(BootInfoError::InvalidEntriesPointer);
    }

    let mut builder = MemoryMapBuilder::new();
    for index in 0..entry_count {
        // SAFETY: Limine promises an array of `entry_count` pointers. The count
        // is capped and pointer alignment/address arithmetic are checked above.
        let entry_pointer = unsafe { response.entries.add(index).read_volatile() };
        if !is_valid_pointer(entry_pointer, virtual_address_bits) {
            return Err(BootInfoError::InvalidEntryPointer { index });
        }
        // SAFETY: Limine promises each non-null entry pointer is readable.
        let entry = unsafe { entry_pointer.read_volatile() };
        builder
            .push(entry.base, entry.length, entry.kind)
            .map_err(BootInfoError::InvalidMemoryMap)?;
    }

    let memory_map = builder.finish().map_err(|error| match error {
        MemoryMapError::EmptyMap => BootInfoError::EmptyMemoryMap,
        other => BootInfoError::InvalidMemoryMap(other),
    })?;
    for (index, region) in memory_map.regions().iter().enumerate() {
        if let Some(physical_bits) = cpu_info.physical_address_bits {
            if !physical_range_fits_address_width(region.start(), region.end(), physical_bits) {
                return Err(BootInfoError::InvalidPhysicalRange { index });
            }
        }
        if region.kind().is_mapped_by_limine_v3_hhdm()
            && !limine_v3_hhdm_range_is_valid(
                hhdm.offset,
                region.start(),
                region.end(),
                cpu_info.physical_address_bits,
                virtual_address_bits,
            )
        {
            return Err(BootInfoError::InvalidHhdmMappingRange { index });
        }
    }
    let boot_stack_physical_start = boot_stack_virtual_start
        .checked_sub(hhdm.offset)
        .ok_or(BootInfoError::InvalidInitialStackHhdmRange)?;
    let boot_stack_physical_end = boot_stack_virtual_end
        .checked_sub(hhdm.offset)
        .ok_or(BootInfoError::InvalidInitialStackHhdmRange)?;
    if !limine_v3_hhdm_range_is_valid(
        hhdm.offset,
        boot_stack_physical_start,
        boot_stack_physical_end,
        cpu_info.physical_address_bits,
        virtual_address_bits,
    ) {
        return Err(BootInfoError::InvalidInitialStackHhdmRange);
    }
    if !memory_map.range_is_within_region_kind(
        boot_stack_physical_start,
        boot_stack_physical_end,
        RegionKind::BootloaderReclaimable,
    ) {
        return Err(BootInfoError::InitialStackNotBootloaderReclaimable);
    }
    let frame_allocator =
        FrameAllocator::from_memory_map(&memory_map).map_err(BootInfoError::FrameAllocator)?;

    Ok(BootInfo {
        hhdm_revision: hhdm.revision,
        hhdm_offset: hhdm.offset,
        inherited_cr3_raw,
        inherited_cr3_root,
        executable_address_revision: executable_address.revision,
        kernel_physical_base: executable_address.physical_base,
        kernel_physical_end,
        kernel_virtual_base: executable_address.virtual_base,
        kernel_virtual_end: linked_virtual_end,
        kernel_image_segments,
        boot_stack_physical_start,
        boot_stack_physical_end,
        boot_stack_virtual_start,
        boot_stack_virtual_end,
        memory_map_revision: response.revision,
        memory_map,
        frame_allocator,
        cpu_info,
    })
}

/// Print a report from the copied snapshot; no loader pointers are used here.
pub fn report_boot_information(boot_info: &BootInfo) {
    crate::kprintln!(
        "HHDM: offset {:#018x}, response revision {}",
        boot_info.hhdm_offset,
        boot_info.hhdm_revision
    );
    crate::kprintln!(
        "inherited CR3: raw {:#018x} (page-table contents not inspected)",
        boot_info.inherited_cr3_raw
    );
    match boot_info.inherited_cr3_root {
        Ok(root) => crate::kprintln!(
            "inherited CR3 root: physical {:#018x}, low bits {:?}",
            root.physical_address(),
            root.low_bits()
        ),
        Err(error) => crate::kprintln!("inherited CR3 root could not be decoded: {:?}", error),
    }
    crate::kprintln!(
        "kernel image: physical [{:#018x}, {:#018x}), virtual [{:#018x}, {:#018x}), response revision {}",
        boot_info.kernel_physical_base,
        boot_info.kernel_physical_end,
        boot_info.kernel_virtual_base,
        boot_info.kernel_virtual_end,
        boot_info.executable_address_revision
    );
    let segments = &boot_info.kernel_image_segments;
    crate::kprintln!(
        "kernel mapping text RX: physical [{:#018x}, {:#018x}), virtual [{:#018x}, {:#018x})",
        segments.text.physical_start,
        segments.text.physical_end,
        segments.text.virtual_start,
        segments.text.virtual_end
    );
    crate::kprintln!(
        "kernel mapping rodata R/NX: physical [{:#018x}, {:#018x}), virtual [{:#018x}, {:#018x})",
        segments.rodata.physical_start,
        segments.rodata.physical_end,
        segments.rodata.virtual_start,
        segments.rodata.virtual_end
    );
    crate::kprintln!(
        "kernel mapping data RW/NX: physical [{:#018x}, {:#018x}), virtual [{:#018x}, {:#018x})",
        segments.data.physical_start,
        segments.data.physical_end,
        segments.data.virtual_start,
        segments.data.virtual_end
    );
    crate::kprintln!(
        "boot stack (minimum protocol span): physical [{:#018x}, {:#018x}), virtual [{:#018x}, {:#018x})",
        boot_info.boot_stack_physical_start,
        boot_info.boot_stack_physical_end,
        boot_info.boot_stack_virtual_start,
        boot_info.boot_stack_virtual_end
    );
    crate::kprintln!(
        "memory map: {} validated regions, {} MiB usable RAM, response revision {}",
        boot_info.memory_map.regions().len(),
        boot_info.memory_map.usable_bytes() / (1024 * 1024),
        boot_info.memory_map_revision
    );
    crate::kprintln!(
        "physical frames: {} managed, {} free (4 KiB each)",
        boot_info.frame_allocator.managed_frames(),
        boot_info.frame_allocator.free_frames()
    );
    for region in boot_info.memory_map.regions() {
        crate::kprintln!(
            "  [{:#018x}, {:#018x}) {:?}",
            region.start(),
            region.end(),
            region.kind()
        );
    }
    crate::kprintln!("console: COM1 serial (polling)");

    let cpu = &boot_info.cpu_info;
    let vendor = core::str::from_utf8(&cpu.vendor).unwrap_or("unknown");
    let mtrr_supported = !matches!(&cpu.mtrr, MtrrState::Unsupported);
    crate::kprintln!(
        "CPU: {} (basic leaf {}, extended leaf {:#x})",
        vendor,
        cpu.max_basic_leaf,
        cpu.max_extended_leaf
    );
    crate::kprintln!(
        "CPU feature support: SSE2={}, NX={}, NXE-enabled={}, PAT={}, MTRR={}, 1GiB-pages={}, long-mode={}, LA57-supported={}, PCID-enabled={}",
        cpu.has_sse2,
        cpu.has_nx,
        cpu.nx_enabled,
        cpu.has_pat,
        mtrr_supported,
        cpu.has_1g_pages,
        cpu.has_long_mode,
        cpu.has_la57,
        cpu.pcid_enabled
    );
    match cpu.pat_msr_value {
        Some(value) => match PatLayout::from_msr_value(value) {
            Ok(layout) => crate::kprintln!(
                "PAT: IA32_PAT={:#018x}, WB index={:?}, UC index={:?}, WC index={:?}",
                value,
                layout.index_for(CachePolicy::WriteBack),
                layout.index_for(CachePolicy::Uncacheable),
                layout.index_for(CachePolicy::WriteCombining)
            ),
            Err(error) => crate::kprintln!(
                "PAT: IA32_PAT={:#018x} has unsupported layout: {:?}",
                value,
                error
            ),
        },
        None => crate::kprintln!("PAT: unsupported"),
    }
    match &cpu.mtrr {
        MtrrState::Unsupported => {
            crate::kprintln!("MTRR: unsupported")
        }
        MtrrState::VariableRangeCapacityExceeded { reported_count } => {
            crate::kprintln!(
                "MTRR: {} variable pairs exceed the snapshot capacity {}; no partial state retained",
                reported_count,
                MAX_CAPTURED_VARIABLE_MTRRS
            )
        }
        MtrrState::Captured(registers) => {
            crate::kprintln!(
                "MTRR snapshot: MTRRCAP={:#018x}, DEF_TYPE={:#018x}, enabled={}, fixed-enabled={}, fixed-supported={}, WC-supported={}, variable-pairs={}",
                registers.capability,
                registers.default_type,
                registers.default_type & (1 << 11) != 0,
                registers.default_type & (1 << 10) != 0,
                registers.capability & (1 << 8) != 0,
                registers.capability & (1 << 10) != 0,
                registers.variable_register_count
            )
        }
    }
    crate::kprintln!(
        "CPU address widths (bits): physical={:?}, max-linear={:?}, active-linear={} (LA57 active={})",
        cpu.physical_address_bits,
        cpu.max_linear_address_bits,
        cpu.active_linear_address_bits,
        cpu.active_linear_address_bits == 57
    );
}

fn is_valid_pointer<T>(pointer: *const T, virtual_address_bits: u8) -> bool {
    let start = pointer as usize;
    let Some(end) = start.checked_add(size_of::<T>()) else {
        return false;
    };
    !pointer.is_null()
        && start & (align_of::<T>() - 1) == 0
        && is_canonical_virtual_address(start as u64, virtual_address_bits)
        && is_canonical_virtual_address((end - 1) as u64, virtual_address_bits)
}

# Rustix roadmap

This roadmap describes an incremental path from the current bare-metal kernel to a useful Unix-like operating system. It is a dependency plan, not a schedule or a claim of compatibility. Features become current only after the implementation, tests, and exit criteria below agree.

## How to read status

- A checked box means the source/design work exists; it does **not** imply the code compiled, linked, booted, or passed an integration test.
- A milestone is not complete until its stated exit criteria are met and the evidence is recorded.
- Hardware work needs target build and emulator evidence. Host tests cannot validate privileged instructions, bootloader pointers, page tables, device I/O, or exception-entry assembly.
- Future work is intentionally not represented by placeholder APIs or dummy implementations.

## Current status

- **Milestone 0: local exit criteria met from a clean detached worktree; hosted CI pending.** On 2026-10-16, `just verify` passed in WSL2 Ubuntu 24.04 from both the working tree and a clean detached worktree with an empty `target` directory. The clean run downloaded and compiled the pinned Limine host utility, formatted and tested the workspace, checked and built the target, created the image, and passed the 20-second QEMU prompt smoke test. Hosted CI has not been observed.
- **Milestone 1: validation criteria met for the current Limine path.** The bounded boot snapshot, memory-range classification, and CPUID reporting were covered by host tests and QEMU reporting; the Limine pointer-readability trust boundary remains explicit.
- **Milestone 2: in progress, not complete.** A bounded frame allocator is retained in `BootInfo`, and bootstrap GDT/TSS/IDT fatal exception handlers exist. Controlled page-fault and invalid-opcode diagnostics plus fatal halting passed QEMU fault-injection tests. The kernel still inherits Limine's page tables; there is no owned page-table manager, global heap, or live frame-allocation caller.
- **Milestones 3 and later: planned.** There is no general IRQ system, scheduler, userspace, syscall ABI, persistent filesystem, GUI, or networking stack.

## Dependency path

```text
Reliable boot
    -> validated boot state
    -> owned mappings + frame allocation + heap + fault diagnostics
    -> timer/IRQ model + scheduler
    -> isolated processes + syscall ABI
    -> VFS/storage + userland utilities
    -> graphical terminal and other optional services
```

Some device-driver work can proceed in parallel after the core ownership, locking, and testing rules exist. It must not bypass them with direct, unreviewed hardware access.

---

## Milestone 0 — repeatable Rust kernel boot (local exit criteria met)

### Implementation present

- [x] `no_std` Rust kernel binary for `x86_64-unknown-none` with its own ELF linker layout and `_start`.
- [x] Limine boot requests and documented external-loader boundary.
- [x] COM1 serial output/input, startup reporting, and panic/fatal halt path.
- [x] Narrow x86 port-I/O helpers and raw non-blocking PS/2-compatible scancode polling.
- [x] `just` tasks for formatting, host tests, target checks, ELF/image builds, and QEMU smoke/run workflows.
- [x] Pinned Limine v12.9.3 binary archive with SHA-256 verification, BIOS/UEFI hybrid image recipe, and CI workflow.
- [x] Separate allocation-free Crabshell parser, kernel serial frontend, and bounded volatile RAM filesystem.

### Validation evidence and remaining proof

- [x] Current source passed formatting, host tests, target check, and optimized build through `just verify`.
- [x] The pinned image built and the bounded QEMU smoke test reached the Crabshell prompt in WSL2 Ubuntu 24.04 on 2026-10-16.
- [x] A separate interactive QEMU session exercised `help`, `ls`, `meminfo`, directory navigation, and file create/write/append/read/copy/move/remove operations; `cp` replaced an existing destination, `rmdir` refused a nonempty directory, and unsupported `memtest` was rejected as expected.
- [x] Repeat verification from a clean detached worktree with an empty `target` directory and uncached build/tool state; fresh Limine download/host-tool compilation, image creation, and QEMU prompt smoke test all passed on 2026-10-16.
- [ ] Observe the hosted CI workflow; it has not yet been run or verified.

The QEMU serial log showed the startup banner, HHDM offset, validated memory-map summary, frame counts, CPUID report, and initial prompt. The interactive command check is a focused manual test, not exhaustive shell coverage or a persistence test. `cat` returned `hello Rustix from QEMU`, `cp` replaced an existing destination with source data, `rmdir` refused a nonempty directory, and `pwd` returned to `/home/rustix` after cleanup. ## Milestone 2 — memory ownership, paging, heap, and exceptions (in progress)

This milestone must establish a safe basis for future allocation and kernel services. Do not allocate a frame for a mapping or dereference it through the HHDM until the mapping/ownership proof is explicit.

### Source work present

- [x] Fixed-capacity frame allocator over validated `Usable` ranges, with page alignment, first-MiB reservation, deallocation, coalescing, bounded metadata, and host tests (`src/frame.rs`).
- [x] Initialize allocator metadata from the boot snapshot and expose counts through Crabshell `meminfo`.
- [x] Specify frame-token ownership and failure semantics: `Frame` is non-copyable, failed deallocation returns the token without changing allocator state, and the current API documents (but does not enforce) one allocator instance per physical map.
- [x] Bootstrap GDT/TSS/IDT and fatal handlers for exception vectors 0–31.
- [x] Give double faults a dedicated IST stack; report saved register/error context and CR2/error bits for page faults.
- [x] Keep maskable IRQ delivery disabled; current exception handling is fatal-only.

### Required memory-management work

- [x] Read `CR4.LA57` and `CPUID.80000008H` when available to report active/max address widths; validate Limine pointers against active canonical width and host-test 48-/57-bit boundaries.
- [x] Document base revision 3 HHDM region coverage, page-boundary behavior, x86 permissions/cache attributes, and the rule that Rustix does not yet use the HHDM for physical access.
- [x] Reject physical map ranges outside the reported CPUID width when available; validate page-rounded HHDM address arithmetic/canonicality for base revision 3 mapped types. This is protocol-derived validation, not a page-table walk or proof of pointer readability.
- [x] Record current transition-critical objects, their mapping sources/permissions, and unresolved bounds in `docs/architecture/memory.md`.
- [x] Capture Limine's executable physical/virtual bases and resolve the complete linker-defined half-open kernel-image span in `BootInfo`; validate the linker/loader base agreement, canonical virtual span, arithmetic, and reported physical width.
- [x] Capture and validate the linker-defined page-aligned text, rodata, and data segment bounds in `BootInfo`; host-test their ordering, contiguity, rounded image coverage, and derived physical ranges. `just verify` reported all three in QEMU on 2026-10-21. This metadata does not prove inherited page-table coverage or live permissions.
- [x] Capture and validate the protocol-guaranteed minimum 64 KiB active boot-stack span from entry `RSP`; validate its HHDM translation and `BootloaderReclaimable` backing. The actual loader allocation may be larger.
- [x] Record the Limine limitation that exact initial-stack allocation bounds and guard status are not provided; preserve only the known minimum span and do not infer a guard page.
- [x] Decode the inherited CR3 root address and interpret its low bits using the reported physical-address width and active `CR4.PCIDE` state; host-test reserved-bit and width rejection. `just verify` passed on 2026-10-21, including target build, ISO creation, and QEMU prompt smoke. This does not inspect page-table entries or prove live mappings.
- [x] Document the initial W^X/alias, cache, MMIO, huge-page, guard-page, and inherited-root preservation policy in `docs/architecture/memory.md`; this is design only, not an implementation.
- [ ] Design a kernel-owned page-table transition that preserves every mapping needed to execute during and after the switch: kernel text/data/BSS, current stack, `BootInfo`, Limine requests/responses still needed, GDT/TSS/IDT, exception stacks, serial state, and any direct-map access used by the transition.
- [x] Add pure host-tested 4 KiB mapping-range validation and leaf-PTE bit encoding. Validation requires alignment, checked bounds, known physical width, canonical virtual ranges, and W^X; encoding bounds the physical width and PAT index and requires NXE for non-executable entries. These helpers do not prove frame ownership, mapping coverage, or PAT cache semantics, and do not touch tables.
- [ ] Implement page-table allocation and mapping operations with verified cache semantics, frame ownership, and supported page-size behavior; preserve explicit writable-executable rejection.
- [ ] Ensure mapping failure (including no free frame or range-table exhaustion) rolls back partial page-table allocations or leaves the old map active.
- [x] Add host tests for raw PTE-bit encoding and parsing a supplied PAT layout to find WB/UC/WC indexes.
- [x] Read EFER.NXE only when NX is supported and read `IA32_PAT` only when PAT is supported; report these read-only values and recognized PAT indexes at boot.
- [x] Host-test that rejected deallocations preserve free-range state and return the frame token for unaligned, unmanaged, already-free, and range-table-full cases.
- [x] Add a pure host-tested MTRR decoder/resolver for supplied fixed and variable register values, including disabled-MTRR behavior and overlap rules. Host tests and `just verify` passed on 2026-10-21.
- [x] Capture supported MTRR capability, default-type, fixed-range, and variable-range registers read-only at boot. Retain at most 32 variable pairs; report capacity overflow explicitly without a partial snapshot.
