    memory_types: [MtrrMemoryType; FIXED_MTRR_TYPE_COUNT],
}

impl FixedMtrrRanges {
    /// Decode FIX64K_00000, FIX16K_80000/A0000, and FIX4K_C0000..F8000.
    pub fn from_msr_values(registers: [u64; 11]) -> Result<Self, MtrrError> {
        let mut memory_types = [MtrrMemoryType::Uncacheable; FIXED_MTRR_TYPE_COUNT];
        for (register_index, value) in registers.iter().enumerate() {
            for slot in 0..8 {
                let memory_type = ((value >> (slot * 8)) & 0xff) as u8;
                memory_types[register_index * 8 + slot] = MtrrMemoryType::from_raw(memory_type)?;
            }
        }
        Ok(Self { memory_types })
    }

    fn type_for_address(&self, address: u64) -> Option<MtrrMemoryType> {
        let index = if address < 0x80_000 {
            (address / 0x1_0000) as usize
        } else if address < 0xa0_000 {
            8 + ((address - 0x80_000) / 0x4000) as usize
        } else if address < 0xc0_000 {
            16 + ((address - 0xa0_000) / 0x4000) as usize
        } else if address < 0x10_0000 {
            24 + ((address - 0xc0_000) / 0x1000) as usize
        } else {
            return None;
        };
        Some(self.memory_types[index])
    }
}

/// One valid variable-range MTRR with a power-of-two range mask and aligned base.
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct VariableMtrr {
    base_match: u64,
    address_mask: u64,
    physical_address_bits: u8,
    memory_type: MtrrMemoryType,
    enabled: bool,
}

impl VariableMtrr {
    /// Decode one IA32_MTRR_PHYSBASE/PHYSMASK pair. A clear valid bit returns `Ok(None).`
    pub fn from_msr_values(
        base: u64,
        mask: u64,
        physical_address_bits: u8,
    ) -> Result<Option<Self>, MtrrError> {
        if !(12..=MAX_MTRR_PHYSICAL_ADDRESS_BITS).contains(&physical_address_bits) {
            return Err(MtrrError::InvalidPhysicalAddressWidth);
        }
        let physical_mask = ((1u64 << physical_address_bits) - 1) & !(PAGE_SIZE - 1);
        if base & !(physical_mask | 0xff) != 0 {
            return Err(MtrrError::ReservedBaseBits);
        }
        if mask & !(physical_mask | MTRR_VALID) != 0 {
            return Err(MtrrError::ReservedMaskBits);
        }
        let memory_type = MtrrMemoryType::from_raw((base & 0xff) as u8)?;
        if mask & MTRR_VALID == 0 {
            return Ok(None);
        }

        let address_mask = mask & physical_mask;
        let ignored_page_bits = (physical_mask ^ address_mask) >> 12;
        if ignored_page_bits & ignored_page_bits.wrapping_add(1) != 0 {
            return Err(MtrrError::InvalidVariableMask);
        }
        let ignored_address_bits = physical_mask ^ address_mask;
        if base & ignored_address_bits != 0 {
            return Err(MtrrError::MisalignedVariableBase);
        }

        Ok(Some(Self {
            base_match: base & address_mask,
            address_mask,
            physical_address_bits,
            memory_type,
            enabled: true,
        }))
    }

    const fn inactive(physical_address_bits: u8) -> Self {
        Self {
            base_match: 0,
            address_mask: 0,
            physical_address_bits,
            memory_type: MtrrMemoryType::Uncacheable,
            enabled: false,
        }
    }

    fn matches(self, address: u64) -> bool {
        self.enabled && address & self.address_mask == self.base_match
    }
}

/// MTRR policy decoded from supplied register values; it does not access MSRs.
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct MtrrLayout<'a> {
    physical_address_bits: u8,
    enabled: bool,
    fixed_enabled: bool,
    default_type: MtrrMemoryType,
    fixed_ranges: Option<&'a FixedMtrrRanges>,
    variable_ranges: &'a [VariableMtrr],
}

impl<'a> MtrrLayout<'a> {
    pub fn new(
        physical_address_bits: u8,
        enabled: bool,
        fixed_enabled: bool,
        default_type: MtrrMemoryType,
        fixed_ranges: Option<&'a FixedMtrrRanges>,
        variable_ranges: &'a [VariableMtrr],
    ) -> Result<Self, MtrrError> {
        if !(12..=MAX_MTRR_PHYSICAL_ADDRESS_BITS).contains(&physical_address_bits) {
            return Err(MtrrError::InvalidPhysicalAddressWidth);
        }
        if enabled && fixed_enabled && fixed_ranges.is_none() {
            return Err(MtrrError::FixedRangesUnavailable);
        }
        if variable_ranges
            .iter()
            .any(|range| range.physical_address_bits != physical_address_bits)
        {
            return Err(MtrrError::PhysicalAddressWidthMismatch);
        }

        Ok(Self {
            physical_address_bits,
            enabled,
            fixed_enabled,
            default_type,
            fixed_ranges,
            variable_ranges,
        })
    }

    /// Resolve the MTRR type for one physical address, rejecting undefined overlaps.
    pub fn memory_type_for(&self, address: u64) -> Result<MtrrMemoryType, MtrrError> {
        if address >= (1u64 << self.physical_address_bits) {
            return Err(MtrrError::PhysicalAddressOutOfRange);
        }
        if !self.enabled {
            return Ok(MtrrMemoryType::Uncacheable);
        }
        if self.fixed_enabled {
            if let Some(memory_type) = self
                .fixed_ranges
                .and_then(|ranges| ranges.type_for_address(address))
            {
                return Ok(memory_type);
            }
        }

        let mut matched_types = 0u8;
        for range in self.variable_ranges {
            if range.matches(address) {
                matched_types |= 1 << range.memory_type as u8;
            }
        }
        if matched_types == 0 {
            return Ok(self.default_type);
        }
        if matched_types & (1 << MtrrMemoryType::Uncacheable as u8) != 0 {
            return Ok(MtrrMemoryType::Uncacheable);
        }
        if matched_types.count_ones() == 1 {
            return MtrrMemoryType::from_raw(matched_types.trailing_zeros() as u8);
        }
        let write_back_and_through =
            (1 << MtrrMemoryType::WriteBack as u8) | (1 << MtrrMemoryType::WriteThrough as u8);
        if matched_types == write_back_and_through {
            return Ok(MtrrMemoryType::WriteThrough);
        }
        Err(MtrrError::UndefinedOverlap)
    }
}

/// Fully decoded MTRR state. Construction rejects malformed or incomplete
/// captured register snapshots before they can influence a mapping policy.
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct ValidatedMtrrLayout {
    physical_address_bits: u8,
    enabled: bool,
    fixed_enabled: bool,
    default_type: MtrrMemoryType,
    fixed_ranges: Option<FixedMtrrRanges>,
    variable_ranges: [VariableMtrr; MAX_CAPTURED_VARIABLE_MTRRS],
}

impl MtrrRegisters {
    pub fn validated_layout(
        &self,
        physical_address_bits: u8,
    ) -> Result<ValidatedMtrrLayout, MtrrError> {
        if !(12..=MAX_MTRR_PHYSICAL_ADDRESS_BITS).contains(&physical_address_bits) {
            return Err(MtrrError::InvalidPhysicalAddressWidth);
        }
        if self.capability & !0x0dff != 0 {
            return Err(MtrrError::ReservedCapabilityBits);
        }
        if self.default_type & !0x0cff != 0 {
            return Err(MtrrError::ReservedDefaultTypeBits);
        }

        let reported_count = (self.capability & 0xff) as usize;
        if reported_count > MAX_CAPTURED_VARIABLE_MTRRS
            || reported_count != usize::from(self.variable_register_count)
        {
            return Err(MtrrError::VariableRegisterCountMismatch);
        }

        let fixed_supported = self.capability & MTRRCAP_FIXED_SUPPORTED != 0;
        if fixed_supported != self.fixed_registers.is_some() {
            return Err(MtrrError::FixedRegisterSupportMismatch);
        }
        let enabled = self.default_type & MTRR_ENABLED != 0;
        let fixed_enabled = self.default_type & MTRR_FIXED_ENABLED != 0;
        if fixed_enabled && !fixed_supported {
            return Err(MtrrError::FixedRangesUnavailable);
        }

        let default_type = MtrrMemoryType::from_raw((self.default_type & 0xff) as u8)?;
        let write_combining_supported = self.capability & MTRRCAP_WRITE_COMBINING_SUPPORTED != 0;
        if default_type == MtrrMemoryType::WriteCombining && !write_combining_supported {
            return Err(MtrrError::WriteCombiningUnsupported);
        }

        let fixed_ranges = self
            .fixed_registers
            .map(FixedMtrrRanges::from_msr_values)
            .transpose()?;
        if fixed_ranges.as_ref().is_some_and(|ranges| {
            ranges
                .memory_types
                .contains(&MtrrMemoryType::WriteCombining)
        }) && !write_combining_supported
        {
            return Err(MtrrError::WriteCombiningUnsupported);
        }

        let mut variable_ranges =
            [VariableMtrr::inactive(physical_address_bits); MAX_CAPTURED_VARIABLE_MTRRS];
        for (index, pair) in self
            .variable_registers
            .iter()
            .take(reported_count)
            .enumerate()
        {
            if let Some(range) =
                VariableMtrr::from_msr_values(pair.base, pair.mask, physical_address_bits)?
            {
                if range.memory_type == MtrrMemoryType::WriteCombining && !write_combining_supported
                {
                    return Err(MtrrError::WriteCombiningUnsupported);
                }
                variable_ranges[index] = range;
            }
        }

        Ok(ValidatedMtrrLayout {
            physical_address_bits,
            enabled,
            fixed_enabled,
            default_type,
            fixed_ranges,
            variable_ranges,
        })
    }
}

impl ValidatedMtrrLayout {
    fn as_layout(&self) -> MtrrLayout<'_> {
        MtrrLayout {
            physical_address_bits: self.physical_address_bits,
            enabled: self.enabled,
            fixed_enabled: self.fixed_enabled,
            default_type: self.default_type,
            fixed_ranges: self.fixed_ranges.as_ref(),
            variable_ranges: &self.variable_ranges,
        }
    }

    pub fn memory_type_for(&self, address: u64) -> Result<MtrrMemoryType, MtrrError> {
        self.as_layout().memory_type_for(address)
    }

    /// Resolve the Intel SDM PAT/MTRR table for one address and PAT index.
    /// `normal_caching` must reflect CR0.CD=0 and CR0.NW=0.
    pub fn effective_memory_type_for(
        &self,
        address: u64,
        pat: PatLayout,
        pat_index: u8,
        normal_caching: bool,
    ) -> Result<EffectiveMemoryType, EffectiveMemoryTypeError> {
        if !normal_caching {
            return Err(EffectiveMemoryTypeError::NonNormalCachingMode);
        }
        let mtrr_type = self
            .memory_type_for(address)
            .map_err(EffectiveMemoryTypeError::Mtrr)?;
        let pat_type = pat.memory_type_at(pat_index)?;
        Ok(combine_mtrr_pat_types(mtrr_type, pat_type))
    }
}

const MTRR_ENABLED: u64 = 1 << 11;
const MTRR_FIXED_ENABLED: u64 = 1 << 10;
const MTRRCAP_WRITE_COMBINING_SUPPORTED: u64 = 1 << 10;

fn combine_mtrr_pat_types(mtrr: MtrrMemoryType, pat: PatMemoryType) -> EffectiveMemoryType {
    use EffectiveMemoryType as E;
    use MtrrMemoryType as M;
    use PatMemoryType as P;

    match (mtrr, pat) {
        (M::Uncacheable, P::WriteCombining)
        | (M::WriteCombining, P::UncacheableMinus | P::WriteCombining | P::WriteBack)
        | (M::WriteThrough | M::WriteBack | M::WriteProtected, P::WriteCombining) => {
            E::WriteCombining
        }
        (M::WriteThrough, P::WriteThrough | P::WriteBack)
        | (M::WriteBack | M::WriteProtected, P::WriteThrough) => E::WriteThrough,
        (M::WriteThrough, P::WriteProtected)
        | (M::WriteBack, P::WriteProtected)
        | (M::WriteProtected, P::WriteBack | P::WriteProtected) => E::WriteProtected,
        (M::WriteBack, P::WriteBack) => E::WriteBack,
        (
            M::Uncacheable,
            P::Uncacheable
            | P::UncacheableMinus
            | P::WriteThrough
            | P::WriteBack
            | P::WriteProtected,
        )
        | (M::WriteCombining, P::Uncacheable | P::WriteThrough | P::WriteProtected)
        | (
            M::WriteThrough | M::WriteBack | M::WriteProtected,
            P::Uncacheable | P::UncacheableMinus,
        ) => E::Uncacheable,
    }
}

#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum MappingError {
    EmptyRange,
    UnalignedRange,
    AddressOverflow,
    InvalidPhysicalAddressWidth,
    UnknownPhysicalAddressWidth,
    InvalidVirtualAddressWidth,
    PhysicalRangeOutOfBounds,
    NonCanonicalVirtualRange,
    CrossesCanonicalHole,
    WritableExecutable,
    UnalignedPageOffset,
    PageOffsetOutOfRange,
    InvalidPatIndex,
    NxNotEnabled,
}

/// Validate one contiguous range for a future 4 KiB page-mapping operation.
///
/// The physical-address width must be known; passing `None` is rejected rather
/// than treating an unknown bound as unbounded. Successful validation does not
/// establish that physical frames are owned by a caller or mapped in the HHDM.
pub fn validate_mapping_range(
    virtual_start: u64,
    physical_start: u64,
    length: u64,
    permissions: PagePermissions,
    physical_address_bits: Option<u8>,
    virtual_address_bits: u8,
) -> Result<ValidatedMappingRange, MappingError> {
    if virtual_address_bits == 0 || virtual_address_bits > 64 {
        return Err(MappingError::InvalidVirtualAddressWidth);
    }
    let physical_address_bits =
        physical_address_bits.ok_or(MappingError::UnknownPhysicalAddressWidth)?;
    if physical_address_bits == 0 || physical_address_bits > 64 {
        return Err(MappingError::InvalidPhysicalAddressWidth);
    }
    if length == 0 {
        return Err(MappingError::EmptyRange);
    }
    if (virtual_start | physical_start | length) & (PAGE_SIZE - 1) != 0 {
        return Err(MappingError::UnalignedRange);
    }
    if permissions.writable && permissions.executable {
        return Err(MappingError::WritableExecutable);
    }

    let virtual_end = virtual_start
        .checked_add(length)
        .ok_or(MappingError::AddressOverflow)?;
    let physical_end = physical_start
        .checked_add(length)
        .ok_or(MappingError::AddressOverflow)?;
    if !physical_range_fits_address_width(physical_start, physical_end, physical_address_bits) {
        return Err(MappingError::PhysicalRangeOutOfBounds);
    }

    let last_virtual_address = virtual_end - 1;
    if !is_canonical_virtual_address(virtual_start, virtual_address_bits)
        || !is_canonical_virtual_address(last_virtual_address, virtual_address_bits)
    {
        return Err(MappingError::NonCanonicalVirtualRange);
    }
    if virtual_address_bits < 64
        && ((virtual_start ^ last_virtual_address) & (1u64 << (virtual_address_bits - 1))) != 0
    {
        return Err(MappingError::CrossesCanonicalHole);
    }

    Ok(ValidatedMappingRange {
        virtual_start,
        virtual_end,
        physical_start,
        physical_end,
        physical_address_bits,
        permissions,
    })
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::{
        capture_mtrr_registers, parse_cr3_root, validate_mapping_range, Cr3Error, Cr3LowBits,
        EffectiveMemoryType, EffectiveMemoryTypeError, FixedMtrrRanges, MappingError, MtrrError,
        MtrrLayout, MtrrMemoryType, MtrrRegisterPair, MtrrRegisters, MtrrState, PagePermissions,
        PatLayout, ValidatedMappingRange, VariableMtrr, MAX_CAPTURED_VARIABLE_MTRRS, PAGE_SIZE,
    };
    use core::cell::Cell;

    const KERNEL_READ_ONLY: PagePermissions = PagePermissions {
        writable: false,
        executable: false,
        user_accessible: false,
    };

    fn variable_mtrr(base: u64, size: u64, memory_type: MtrrMemoryType) -> VariableMtrr {
        let physical_address_bits = 36;
        let physical_mask = ((1u64 << physical_address_bits) - 1) & !(PAGE_SIZE - 1);
        let mask = physical_mask & !(size - 1) | (1 << 11);
        VariableMtrr::from_msr_values(base | memory_type as u8 as u64, mask, physical_address_bits)
            .unwrap()
            .unwrap()
    }

    fn empty_mtrr_registers(capability: u64, default_type: u64) -> MtrrRegisters {
        MtrrRegisters {
            capability,
            default_type,
            fixed_registers: if capability & (1 << 8) != 0 {
                Some([MtrrMemoryType::WriteBack as u64 * 0x0101_0101_0101_0101; 11])
            } else {
                None
            },
            variable_register_count: (capability & 0xff) as u8,
            variable_registers: [MtrrRegisterPair { base: 0, mask: 0 };
                MAX_CAPTURED_VARIABLE_MTRRS],
        }
    }

    #[test]
    fn mtrr_capture_is_gated_by_support() {
        let state = capture_mtrr_registers(false, |_| panic!("read MSR without MTRR support"));
        assert_eq!(state, MtrrState::Unsupported);
    }

    #[test]
    fn captures_supported_fixed_and_variable_mtrr_registers() {
        let reads = Cell::new(0);
        let state = capture_mtrr_registers(true, |index| {
            reads.set(reads.get() + 1);
            match index {
                0xfe => 2 | (1 << 8),
                0x2ff => 0xc06,
                _ => u64::from(index),
            }
        });

        let MtrrState::Captured(registers) = state else {
            panic!("expected a complete MTRR snapshot");
        };
        assert_eq!(reads.get(), 2 + 11 + 4);
        assert_eq!(registers.capability, 2 | (1 << 8));
        assert_eq!(registers.default_type, 0xc06);
        assert_eq!(registers.variable_register_count, 2);
        let fixed = registers
            .fixed_registers
            .expect("fixed ranges are supported");
        assert_eq!(fixed[0], 0x250);
        assert_eq!(fixed[10], 0x26f);
        assert_eq!(registers.variable_registers[0].base, 0x200);
        assert_eq!(registers.variable_registers[0].mask, 0x201);
        assert_eq!(registers.variable_registers[1].base, 0x202);
        assert_eq!(registers.variable_registers[1].mask, 0x203);
        assert_eq!(
            registers.variable_registers[2],
            MtrrRegisterPair { base: 0, mask: 0 }
        );
    }

    #[test]
    fn mtrr_capture_reports_capacity_excess_without_partial_reads() {
        let reads = Cell::new(0);
        let state = capture_mtrr_registers(true, |index| {
            reads.set(reads.get() + 1);
            if index == 0xfe {
                (MAX_CAPTURED_VARIABLE_MTRRS as u64) + 1
            } else {
                0
            }
        });

        assert_eq!(
            state,
            MtrrState::VariableRangeCapacityExceeded {
                reported_count: (MAX_CAPTURED_VARIABLE_MTRRS + 1) as u8,
            }
        );
        assert_eq!(reads.get(), 1);
    }

    #[test]
    fn mtrr_capture_skips_unsupported_fixed_registers() {
        let reads = Cell::new(0);
        let state = capture_mtrr_registers(true, |index| {
            reads.set(reads.get() + 1);
            match index {
                0xfe => 1,
                0x2ff => 0xc06,
                _ => u64::from(index),
            }
        });

        let MtrrState::Captured(registers) = state else {
            panic!("expected a complete MTRR snapshot");
        };
        assert_eq!(reads.get(), 4);
        assert_eq!(registers.fixed_registers, None);
        assert_eq!(registers.variable_register_count, 1);
        assert_eq!(registers.variable_registers[0].base, 0x200);
        assert_eq!(registers.variable_registers[0].mask, 0x201);
    }

    #[test]
    fn decodes_cr3_root_with_pcid_enabled() {
        let root = parse_cr3_root(0x1234_5000 | 0x0abc, Some(48), true).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(root.physical_address(), 0x1234_5000);
        assert_eq!(root.low_bits(), Cr3LowBits::Pcid(0x0abc));
    }

    #[test]
    fn decodes_cr3_cache_controls_without_pcid() {
        let root = parse_cr3_root(0x1234_5000 | (1 << 3) | (1 << 4), Some(48), false).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(root.physical_address(), 0x1234_5000);
        assert_eq!(
            root.low_bits(),
            Cr3LowBits::CacheControls {
                page_level_write_through: true,
                page_level_cache_disable: true,
            }
        );
    }

    #[test]
    fn rejects_cr3_reserved_bits_and_invalid_address_widths() {
        assert_eq!(
            parse_cr3_root(0x1000 | 1, Some(48), false),
            Err(Cr3Error::ReservedBits)
        );
        assert_eq!(
            parse_cr3_root(1 << 40, Some(40), true),
            Err(Cr3Error::ReservedBits)
        );
        assert_eq!(
            parse_cr3_root(0x1000, None, false),
            Err(Cr3Error::UnknownPhysicalAddressWidth)
        );
        assert_eq!(
            parse_cr3_root(0x1000, Some(53), false),
            Err(Cr3Error::InvalidPhysicalAddressWidth)
        );
    }

    #[test]
    fn resolves_variable_mtrr_ranges_and_default_type() {
        let ranges = [variable_mtrr(
            0x20_0000,
            0x20_0000,
            MtrrMemoryType::WriteBack,
        )];
        let layout =
            MtrrLayout::new(36, true, false, MtrrMemoryType::Uncacheable, None, &ranges).unwrap();

        assert_eq!(
            layout.memory_type_for(0x20_0000),
            Ok(MtrrMemoryType::WriteBack)
        );
        assert_eq!(
            layout.memory_type_for(0x3f_ffff),
            Ok(MtrrMemoryType::WriteBack)
        );
        assert_eq!(
            layout.memory_type_for(0x40_0000),
            Ok(MtrrMemoryType::Uncacheable)
        );
        assert_eq!(
            layout.memory_type_for(1u64 << 36),
            Err(MtrrError::PhysicalAddressOutOfRange)
        );
    }

    #[test]
    fn fixed_mtrrs_override_variable_and_default_ranges_below_one_mib() {
        let mut registers = [0; 11];
        registers[2] = MtrrMemoryType::WriteThrough as u64;
        let fixed = FixedMtrrRanges::from_msr_values(registers).unwrap();
        let variable = [variable_mtrr(0, 0x10_0000, MtrrMemoryType::WriteBack)];
        let layout = MtrrLayout::new(
            36,
            true,
            true,
            MtrrMemoryType::WriteBack,
            Some(&fixed),
            &variable,
        )
        .unwrap();

        assert_eq!(
            layout.memory_type_for(0xa_0000),
            Ok(MtrrMemoryType::WriteThrough)
        );
        assert_eq!(
            layout.memory_type_for(0xa_4000),
            Ok(MtrrMemoryType::Uncacheable)
        );
        assert_eq!(
            layout.memory_type_for(0x10_0000),
            Ok(MtrrMemoryType::WriteBack)
        );
    }

    #[test]
    fn resolves_defined_variable_mtrr_overlaps_and_rejects_undefined_ones() {
        let write_back_through = [
            variable_mtrr(0x20_0000, 0x20_0000, MtrrMemoryType::WriteBack),
            variable_mtrr(0x20_0000, 0x20_0000, MtrrMemoryType::WriteThrough),
        ];
        let layout = MtrrLayout::new(
            36,
            true,
            false,
            MtrrMemoryType::Uncacheable,
            None,
            &write_back_through,
        )
        .unwrap();
        assert_eq!(
            layout.memory_type_for(0x20_0000),
            Ok(MtrrMemoryType::WriteThrough)
        );

        let uncacheable_override = [
            write_back_through[0],
            variable_mtrr(0x20_0000, 0x20_0000, MtrrMemoryType::Uncacheable),
        ];
        let layout = MtrrLayout::new(
            36,
            true,
            false,
            MtrrMemoryType::WriteBack,
            None,
            &uncacheable_override,
        )
        .unwrap();
        assert_eq!(
            layout.memory_type_for(0x20_0000),
            Ok(MtrrMemoryType::Uncacheable)
        );

        let undefined = [
            variable_mtrr(0x20_0000, 0x20_0000, MtrrMemoryType::WriteCombining),
            variable_mtrr(0x20_0000, 0x20_0000, MtrrMemoryType::WriteProtected),
        ];
        let layout =
            MtrrLayout::new(36, true, false, MtrrMemoryType::WriteBack, None, &undefined).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(
            layout.memory_type_for(0x20_0000),
            Err(MtrrError::UndefinedOverlap)
        );
    }

    #[test]
    fn disabled_mtrrs_force_uncacheable_and_bad_registers_are_rejected() {
        let layout =
            MtrrLayout::new(36, false, true, MtrrMemoryType::WriteBack, None, &[]).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(
            layout.memory_type_for(0x20_0000),
            Ok(MtrrMemoryType::Uncacheable)
        );
        assert_eq!(
            MtrrLayout::new(36, true, true, MtrrMemoryType::WriteBack, None, &[]),
            Err(MtrrError::FixedRangesUnavailable)
        );
        assert_eq!(
            VariableMtrr::from_msr_values(0x1000 | 0x200, 0, 36),
            Err(MtrrError::ReservedBaseBits)
        );
        assert_eq!(
            VariableMtrr::from_msr_values(0x1000 | 6, 1 << 10, 36),
            Err(MtrrError::ReservedMaskBits)
        );
        assert_eq!(VariableMtrr::from_msr_values(0x1000 | 6, 0, 36), Ok(None));
        let width_mismatch = [variable_mtrr(
            0x20_0000,
            0x20_0000,
            MtrrMemoryType::WriteBack,
        )];
        assert_eq!(
            MtrrLayout::new(
                35,
                true,
                false,
                MtrrMemoryType::WriteBack,
                None,
                &width_mismatch,
            ),
            Err(MtrrError::PhysicalAddressWidthMismatch)
        );
        assert_eq!(
            VariableMtrr::from_msr_values(0x1000 | 2, 1 << 11, 36),
            Err(MtrrError::ReservedMemoryType { value: 2 })
        );
        let mut invalid_fixed = [0; 11];
        invalid_fixed[0] = 2;
        assert_eq!(
            FixedMtrrRanges::from_msr_values(invalid_fixed),
            Err(MtrrError::ReservedMemoryType { value: 2 })
        );
    }

    #[test]
    fn accepts_aligned_ranges_at_canonical_boundaries() {
        let lower = validate_mapping_range(
            0x0000_7fff_ffff_e000,
            0x1000,
            0x2000,
            KERNEL_READ_ONLY,
            Some(14),
            48,
        )
        .unwrap();
        assert_eq!(
            lower,
            ValidatedMappingRange {
                virtual_start: 0x0000_7fff_ffff_e000,
                virtual_end: 0x0000_8000_0000_0000,
                physical_start: 0x1000,
                physical_end: 0x3000,
                physical_address_bits: 14,
                permissions: KERNEL_READ_ONLY,
            }
        );

        let upper = validate_mapping_range(
            0xffff_8000_0000_0000,
            0,
            PAGE_SIZE,
            KERNEL_READ_ONLY,
            Some(12),
            48,
        )
        .unwrap();
        assert_eq!(upper.virtual_end(), 0xffff_8000_0000_1000);
    }

    #[test]
    fn rejects_empty_and_unaligned_ranges() {
        assert_eq!(
            validate_mapping_range(0x1000, 0x2000, 0, KERNEL_READ_ONLY, Some(32), 48),
            Err(MappingError::EmptyRange)
        );
        assert_eq!(
            validate_mapping_range(0x1001, 0x2000, PAGE_SIZE, KERNEL_READ_ONLY, Some(32), 48),
            Err(MappingError::UnalignedRange)
        );
        assert_eq!(
            validate_mapping_range(
                0x1000,
                0x2000,
                PAGE_SIZE + 1,
                KERNEL_READ_ONLY,
                Some(32),
                48
            ),
            Err(MappingError::UnalignedRange)
        );
    }

    #[test]
    fn requires_known_valid_address_widths_and_bounded_physical_ranges() {
        assert_eq!(
            validate_mapping_range(0x1000, 0x1000, PAGE_SIZE, KERNEL_READ_ONLY, None, 48),
            Err(MappingError::UnknownPhysicalAddressWidth)
        );
        assert_eq!(
            validate_mapping_range(0x1000, 0x1000, PAGE_SIZE, KERNEL_READ_ONLY, Some(0), 48),
            Err(MappingError::InvalidPhysicalAddressWidth)
        );
        assert_eq!(
            validate_mapping_range(0x1000, 0x1000, PAGE_SIZE, KERNEL_READ_ONLY, Some(52), 0),
            Err(MappingError::InvalidVirtualAddressWidth)
        );
        assert_eq!(
            validate_mapping_range(
                0x1000,
                0x1000,
                PAGE_SIZE * 2,
                KERNEL_READ_ONLY,
                Some(13),
                48
            ),
            Err(MappingError::PhysicalRangeOutOfBounds)
        );
    }

    #[test]
    fn rejects_noncanonical_ranges_and_ranges_crossing_the_canonical_hole() {
        assert_eq!(
            validate_mapping_range(
                0x0000_8000_0000_0000,
                0,
                PAGE_SIZE,
                KERNEL_READ_ONLY,
                Some(52),
                48
            ),
            Err(MappingError::NonCanonicalVirtualRange)
        );

        let crosses_hole = (0xffff_8000_0000_1000u64) - 0x0000_7fff_ffff_f000;
        assert_eq!(
            validate_mapping_range(
                0x0000_7fff_ffff_f000,
                0,
                crosses_hole,
                KERNEL_READ_ONLY,
                Some(64),
                48,
            ),
            Err(MappingError::CrossesCanonicalHole)
        );
    }

    fn pat_value(entries: [u8; 8]) -> u64 {
        entries.iter().enumerate().fold(0, |value, (index, entry)| {
            value | ((*entry as u64) << (index * 8))
        })
    }

    #[test]
    fn resolves_cache_policies_from_the_supplied_pat_layout() {
        let pat = pat_value([6, 4, 7, 0, 6, 1, 7, 0]);
        let layout = super::PatLayout::from_msr_value(pat).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(layout.index_for(super::CachePolicy::WriteBack), Some(0));
        assert_eq!(layout.index_for(super::CachePolicy::Uncacheable), Some(3));
        assert_eq!(
            layout.index_for(super::CachePolicy::WriteCombining),
            Some(5)
        );

        let without_write_combining =
            super::PatLayout::from_msr_value(pat_value([6, 4, 7, 0, 6, 4, 7, 0])).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(
            without_write_combining.index_for(super::CachePolicy::WriteCombining),
            None
        );
    }

    #[test]
    fn combines_every_documented_pat_and_mtrr_pair() {
        use EffectiveMemoryType as E;
        use MtrrMemoryType as M;

        let pat = PatLayout::from_msr_value(pat_value([0, 7, 1, 4, 6, 5, 0, 0])).unwrap();
        let rows = [
            (
                M::Uncacheable,
                [
                    E::Uncacheable,
                    E::Uncacheable,
                    E::WriteCombining,
                    E::Uncacheable,
                    E::Uncacheable,
                    E::Uncacheable,
                ],
            ),
            (
                M::WriteCombining,
                [
                    E::Uncacheable,
                    E::WriteCombining,
                    E::WriteCombining,
                    E::Uncacheable,
                    E::WriteCombining,
                    E::Uncacheable,
                ],
            ),
            (
                M::WriteThrough,
                [
                    E::Uncacheable,
                    E::Uncacheable,
                    E::WriteCombining,
                    E::WriteThrough,
                    E::WriteThrough,
                    E::WriteProtected,
                ],
            ),
            (
                M::WriteBack,
                [
                    E::Uncacheable,
                    E::Uncacheable,
                    E::WriteCombining,
                    E::WriteThrough,
                    E::WriteBack,
                    E::WriteProtected,
                ],
            ),
            (
                M::WriteProtected,
                [
                    E::Uncacheable,
                    E::Uncacheable,
                    E::WriteCombining,
                    E::WriteThrough,
                    E::WriteProtected,
                    E::WriteProtected,
                ],
            ),
        ];

        for (mtrr_type, expected) in rows {
            let registers = empty_mtrr_registers(1 << 10, (1 << 11) | mtrr_type as u64);
            let layout = registers.validated_layout(36).unwrap();
            for (pat_index, expected_type) in expected.into_iter().enumerate() {
                assert_eq!(
                    layout.effective_memory_type_for(0x20_0000, pat, pat_index as u8, true),
                    Ok(expected_type),
                    "MTRR={mtrr_type:?}, PAT index={pat_index}"
                );
            }
        }
    }

    #[test]
    fn rejects_invalid_effective_cache_type_inputs() {
        let registers = empty_mtrr_registers(0, (1 << 11) | MtrrMemoryType::WriteBack as u64);
        let layout = registers.validated_layout(36).unwrap();
        let pat = PatLayout::from_msr_value(pat_value([6, 4, 7, 0, 6, 1, 7, 0])).unwrap();

        assert_eq!(
            layout.effective_memory_type_for(0, pat, 8, true),
            Err(EffectiveMemoryTypeError::PatIndexOutOfRange { index: 8 })
        );
        assert_eq!(
            layout.effective_memory_type_for(0, pat, 0, false),
            Err(EffectiveMemoryTypeError::NonNormalCachingMode)
        );
        assert_eq!(
            layout.effective_memory_type_for(1u64 << 36, pat, 0, true),
            Err(EffectiveMemoryTypeError::Mtrr(
                MtrrError::PhysicalAddressOutOfRange
            ))
        );
    }

    #[test]
    fn validates_captured_mtrr_snapshot_before_resolution() {
        let registers = empty_mtrr_registers(
            (1 << 8) | (1 << 10) | 1,
            (1 << 11) | (1 << 10) | MtrrMemoryType::WriteBack as u64,
        );
        let layout = registers.validated_layout(36).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(layout.memory_type_for(0), Ok(MtrrMemoryType::WriteBack));
        assert_eq!(
            layout.memory_type_for(0x10_0000),
            Ok(MtrrMemoryType::WriteBack)
        );

        let mut invalid = empty_mtrr_registers(0, 1 << 11);
        invalid.capability |= 1 << 9;
        assert_eq!(
            invalid.validated_layout(36),
            Err(MtrrError::ReservedCapabilityBits)
        );

        let mut invalid = empty_mtrr_registers(0, 1 << 11);
        invalid.default_type |= 1 << 12;
        assert_eq!(
            invalid.validated_layout(36),
            Err(MtrrError::ReservedDefaultTypeBits)
        );

        let mut invalid = empty_mtrr_registers(0, 1 << 11);
        invalid.variable_register_count = 1;
        assert_eq!(
            invalid.validated_layout(36),
            Err(MtrrError::VariableRegisterCountMismatch)
        );

        let mut invalid = empty_mtrr_registers(1 << 8, 1 << 11);
        invalid.fixed_registers = None;
        assert_eq!(
            invalid.validated_layout(36),
            Err(MtrrError::FixedRegisterSupportMismatch)
        );

        let invalid = empty_mtrr_registers(0, (1 << 11) | MtrrMemoryType::WriteCombining as u64);
        assert_eq!(
            invalid.validated_layout(36),
            Err(MtrrError::WriteCombiningUnsupported)
        );

        let mut invalid = empty_mtrr_registers(1, 1 << 11);
        let physical_mask = ((1u64 << 36) - 1) & !(PAGE_SIZE - 1);
        invalid.variable_registers[0] = MtrrRegisterPair {
            base: MtrrMemoryType::WriteBack as u64,
            mask: (physical_mask ^ (1 << 13)) | (1 << 11),
        };
        assert_eq!(
            invalid.validated_layout(36),
            Err(MtrrError::InvalidVariableMask)
        );
    }

    #[test]
    fn rejects_misaligned_variable_mtrr_bases() {
        let physical_address_bits = 36;
        let physical_mask = ((1u64 << physical_address_bits) - 1) & !(PAGE_SIZE - 1);
        let mask = physical_mask & !(0x2000 - 1) | (1 << 11);
        assert_eq!(
            VariableMtrr::from_msr_values(
                0x1000 | MtrrMemoryType::WriteBack as u64,
                mask,
                physical_address_bits,
            ),
            Err(MtrrError::MisalignedVariableBase)
        );
    }

    #[test]
    fn rejects_reserved_pat_entries() {
        assert_eq!(
            super::PatLayout::from_msr_value(0x08),
            Err(super::PatLayoutError::ReservedBits { index: 0 })
        );
        assert_eq!(
            super::PatLayout::from_msr_value(0b010 << 24),
            Err(super::PatLayoutError::ReservedMemoryType {
                index: 3,
                value: 0b010,
            })
        );
    }

    #[test]
    fn encodes_4k_leaf_permissions_nx_and_pat_index_bits() {
        let writable_user_page = PagePermissions {
            writable: true,
            executable: false,
            user_accessible: true,
        };
        let mapping = validate_mapping_range(
            0x4000,
            0x20_0000,
            PAGE_SIZE * 2,
            writable_user_page,
            Some(52),
            48,
        )
        .unwrap();

        let first = mapping.leaf_4k_entry(0, 0b101, true).unwrap().bits();
        assert_eq!(
            first,
            0x20_0000 | (1 << 0) | (1 << 1) | (1 << 2) | (1 << 3) | (1 << 7) | (1 << 63)
        );
        let second = mapping
            .leaf_4k_entry(PAGE_SIZE, 0b101, true)
            .unwrap()
            .bits();
        assert_eq!(second & 0x000f_ffff_ffff_f000, 0x20_1000);
        assert_eq!(second & (1 << 63), 1 << 63);

        let all_pat_bits = mapping.leaf_4k_entry(0, 0b111, true).unwrap().bits()
            & ((1 << 3) | (1 << 4) | (1 << 7));
        assert_eq!(all_pat_bits, (1 << 3) | (1 << 4) | (1 << 7));
    }

    #[test]
    fn rejects_unencodable_leaf_attributes_and_page_offsets() {
        let mapping =
            validate_mapping_range(0x4000, 0x20_0000, PAGE_SIZE, KERNEL_READ_ONLY, Some(52), 48)
                .unwrap();
        assert_eq!(
            mapping.leaf_4k_entry(0, 8, true),
            Err(MappingError::InvalidPatIndex)
        );
        assert_eq!(
            mapping.leaf_4k_entry(0, 0, false),
            Err(MappingError::NxNotEnabled)
        );
        assert_eq!(
            mapping.leaf_4k_entry(1, 0, true),
            Err(MappingError::UnalignedPageOffset)
        );
        assert_eq!(
            mapping.leaf_4k_entry(PAGE_SIZE, 0, true),
            Err(MappingError::PageOffsetOutOfRange)
        );

        let too_wide =
            validate_mapping_range(0x4000, 0x20_0000, PAGE_SIZE, KERNEL_READ_ONLY, Some(53), 48)
                .unwrap();
        assert_eq!(
            too_wide.leaf_4k_entry(0, 0, true),
            Err(MappingError::InvalidPhysicalAddressWidth)
        );
    }

    #[test]
    fn executable_leaf_does_not_set_nx() {
        let executable = PagePermissions {
            writable: false,
            executable: true,
            user_accessible: false,
        };
        let mapping =
            validate_mapping_range(0x4000, 0x20_0000, PAGE_SIZE, executable, Some(52), 48).unwrap();
        let entry = mapping.leaf_4k_entry(0, 0, false).unwrap().bits();
        assert_eq!(entry, 0x20_0000 | 1);
    }

    #[test]
    fn rejects_arithmetic_overflow_and_writable_executable_ranges() {
        assert_eq!(
            validate_mapping_range(
                u64::MAX - (PAGE_SIZE - 1),
                0,
                PAGE_SIZE,
                KERNEL_READ_ONLY,
                Some(64),
                64
            ),
            Err(MappingError::AddressOverflow)
        );
        assert_eq!(
            validate_mapping_range(
                0x1000,
                u64::MAX - (PAGE_SIZE - 1),
                PAGE_SIZE,
                KERNEL_READ_ONLY,
                Some(64),
                64
            ),
            Err(MappingError::AddressOverflow)
        );

        let writable_executable = PagePermissions {
            writable: true,
            executable: true,
            user_accessible: false,
        };
        assert_eq!(
            validate_mapping_range(0x1000, 0x2000, PAGE_SIZE, writable_executable, Some(52), 48),
            Err(MappingError::WritableExecutable)
        );
    }
}

# Rustix roadmap

This roadmap describes an incremental path from the current bare-metal kernel to a useful Unix-like operating system. It is a dependency plan, not a schedule or a claim of compatibility. Features become current only after the implementation, tests, and exit criteria below agree.

## How to read status

- A checked box means the source/design work exists; it does **not** imply the code compiled, linked, booted, or passed an integration test.
- A milestone is not complete until its stated exit criteria are met and the evidence is recorded.
- Hardware work needs target build and emulator evidence. Host tests cannot validate privileged instructions, bootloader pointers, page tables, device I/O, or exception-entry assembly.
- Future work is intentionally not represented by placeholder APIs or dummy implementations.

## Current status

- **Milestone 0: local exit criteria met from a clean detached worktree; hosted CI pending.** On 2026-10-16, `just verify` passed in WSL2 Ubuntu 24.04 from both the working tree and a clean detached worktree with an empty `target` directory. The clean run downloaded and compiled the pinned Limine host utility, formatted and tested the workspace, checked and built the target, created the image, and passed the 20-second QEMU prompt smoke test. Hosted CI has not been observed.
- **Milestone 1: validation criteria met for the current Limine path.** The bounded boot snapshot, memory-range classification, and CPUID reporting were covered by host tests and QEMU reporting; the Limine pointer-readability trust boundary remains explicit.
- **Milestone 2: in progress, not complete.** A bounded frame allocator is retained in `BootInfo`, and bootstrap GDT/TSS/IDT fatal exception handlers exist. Controlled page-fault and invalid-opcode diagnostics plus fatal halting passed QEMU fault-injection tests. The kernel still inherits Limine's page tables; there is no owned page-table manager, global heap, or live frame-allocation caller.
- **Milestones 3 and later: planned.** There is no general IRQ system, scheduler, userspace, syscall ABI, persistent filesystem, GUI, or networking stack.

## Dependency path

```text
Reliable boot
    -> validated boot state
    -> owned mappings + frame allocation + heap + fault diagnostics
    -> timer/IRQ model + scheduler
    -> isolated processes + syscall ABI
    -> VFS/storage + userland utilities
    -> graphical terminal and other optional services
```

Some device-driver work can proceed in parallel after the core ownership, locking, and testing rules exist. It must not bypass them with direct, unreviewed hardware access.

- [x] Read EFER.NXE only when NX is supported and read `IA32_PAT` only when PAT is supported; report these read-only values and recognized PAT indexes at boot.
- [x] Host-test that rejected deallocations preserve free-range state and return the frame token for unaligned, unmanaged, already-free, and range-table-full cases.
- [x] Add a pure host-tested MTRR decoder/resolver for supplied fixed and variable register values, including disabled-MTRR behavior and overlap rules. Host tests and `just verify` passed on 2026-10-21.
- [x] Capture supported MTRR capability, default-type, fixed-range, and variable-range registers read-only at boot. Retain at most 32 variable pairs; report capacity overflow explicitly without a partial snapshot. Host tests cover feature gating, supported fixed/variable register reads, unsupported fixed ranges, and capacity overflow. `just verify` passed on 2026-10-22; the QEMU serial log reported the live MTRR summary.
- [x] Validate captured MTRR capability/default-type bits, register counts and fixed-range availability, WC support, and variable-range mask/alignment; resolve the Intel SDM Table 11-7 PAT/MTRR combinations for one physical address only when `CR0.CD=0` and `CR0.NW=0`. Host tests cover all 30 documented type pairs and malformed inputs. Boot validates the captured PAT/MTRR state and prints a diagnostic resolution at PA 0; `just verify` passed on 2026-10-22. This policy helper does not establish the cache type of an inherited mapping.
- [ ] Use the validated resolver to select and verify cache indexes for complete target mapping ranges, including alias checks. Add reviewable emulator tests for mapping, unmapping, permission behavior, and frame reclamation before replacing the inherited CR3.
- [ ] Only after a mapping policy works, add a kernel heap with documented alignment, allocation/free semantics, deterministic exhaustion behavior, and an explicit rule for interrupt contexts.

### Required exception/descriptor validation

- [x] Source contains GDT/TSS/IDT setup and normalized stubs for architectural exception vectors 0–31; double fault uses IST1.
- [x] Target-assemble/link and inspect the stubs and descriptor setup; ELF disassembly confirms call-stack alignment and the error-code normalization paths, while compile-time size assertions pin the IDT, TSS, and exception-context layouts.
- [x] Add QEMU fault-injection tests for a controlled page fault and invalid opcode. `just fault-smoke` verifies vector diagnostics, the exact CR2 address, no shell prompt or return marker, and that QEMU remains halted until its timeout; it then restores the default release kernel and ISO.
- [x] Boot the descriptor setup and both tested exception paths in QEMU. These checks cover only the injected page fault and invalid opcode, not all vectors or physical hardware.

**Exit criteria:** the kernel owns and validates its page-table state, frame allocation/mapping invariants are tested, OOM/failure leaves memory state consistent, page faults are diagnosable, and the kernel remains bootable under emulator tests. Not met: page-table ownership/transition and heap work remain outstanding.

---

## Milestone 3 — IRQs, time, and kernel scheduling

Do not enable interrupts as a side effect of installing exception gates. IRQ delivery needs its own controller, acknowledgement, masking, ownership, and synchronization design.

### Planned work

- [ ] Select and document the initial interrupt controller policy for QEMU and target hardware (for example, legacy PIC compatibility versus local I/O APIC; do not enable both accidentally).
- [ ] Add IRQ vector allocation, controller masking/unmasking, end-of-interrupt acknowledgement, spurious-interrupt handling, and a policy for unexpected IRQs.
- [ ] Add a calibrated/verified timer source and monotonic timekeeping; test interval arithmetic and drift assumptions.
- [ ] Establish interrupt-safe lock primitives and rules for code callable from normal, exception, and IRQ contexts. No allocator or blocking console operation may run in an unsafe interrupt context.
- [ ] Add a minimal kernel-thread context and lifecycle model, stack ownership/guard policy, context-switch tests, and emulator scheduling tests.
- [ ] Add preemption only after lock, stack, timer, and interrupt-return invariants have deterministic tests.
- [ ] Keep application-processor startup/SMP as a separate sub-milestone after per-CPU state, TLB invalidation, and lock semantics exist.

**Exit criteria:** tested IRQ acknowledgement and timer behavior, deterministic thread lifecycle/context-switch tests, and bounded QEMU tests under repeated timer interrupts. No `sti` before the design and tests are ready.

---

## Milestone 4 — isolated processes and syscall ABI

Userspace begins only after page tables, exception handling, scheduling, and controlled memory allocation are trustworthy. The syscall ABI is a product interface and must not emerge accidentally from internal functions.

### Planned work

- [ ] Decide and document the x86_64 user-entry/syscall mechanism, register convention, selector/MSR setup, per-CPU state requirements, and safe return path.
- [ ] Add user/kernel page permissions and process-owned address spaces, including teardown and TLB invalidation rules.
- [ ] Implement copy-in/copy-out helpers that validate lengths, arithmetic, canonical ranges, permissions, and faults; never form a kernel reference directly from a user pointer.
- [ ] Specify version discovery, stable syscall numbers, argument layouts, error encoding, partial-I/O behavior, interruption/restart, and compatibility policy before exposing calls.
- [ ] Add initial process lifecycle and descriptor-table semantics: create/load, exit, wait, close, duplication/inheritance, and process cleanup.
- [ ] Load a deliberately small documented executable format with bounds/segment/permission checks; reject malformed binaries safely.
- [ ] Build adversarial tests for bad pointers, overflow, invalid mappings, process teardown, descriptor misuse, and failed exec.

### First user-visible target

A small controlled `init` process should start from a reproducible image, write through a descriptor, exit with a status, and be waited on by a kernel test harness. Do not claim userspace or process isolation from ring-0 tasks that merely use process-shaped structs.

**Exit criteria:** an isolated init process runs in user mode and uses a versioned, documented syscall subset; invalid user pointers and process teardown are tested without corrupting the kernel.

---

## Milestone 5 — VFS, storage, and device ownership

Keep the current RAM filesystem as a bootstrap/test implementation. Persistence and device drivers require explicit block ownership, error handling, and recovery behavior.

### Planned work

- [ ] Define VFS node, mount, path, metadata, and file-descriptor contracts independently of a particular disk format.
- [ ] Preserve volatile RAMFS as a test backend and add tests for mount/path errors, capacity, partial I/O, and object lifetime.
- [ ] Add a narrowly scoped block-device interface with request validation, timeout/error reporting, and a QEMU-supported initial device driver (such as virtio-blk after PCI discovery is ready).
- [ ] Choose and document the first on-disk filesystem format. Specify partition discovery, byte order, block size, metadata limits, corruption handling, and read-only/recovery behavior before writable support.
- [ ] Add persistent write/read/remount/reboot integration tests; never claim persistence from an in-memory cache alone.
- [ ] Add a driver ownership and DMA policy before any device can write into arbitrary kernel memory.
- [ ] Define file descriptors and basic process I/O semantics before exposing them to applications.

**Exit criteria:** a reproducible image mounts a documented on-disk filesystem, user-visible tools can create/read files across reboot, and corruption/I/O errors fail safely.

---

## Milestone 6 — initial userspace and command-line utilities

Crabshell is currently an in-kernel parser/frontend. The long-term terminal application should reuse its parser model without linking kernel internals or bypassing syscalls.

### Planned work

- [ ] Start a user-mode `init` process and establish executable search, environment, current directory, descriptor inheritance, and process startup rules.
- [ ] Port or adapt Crabshell into a userspace terminal application that uses only the documented syscall/VFS interfaces.
- [ ] Add a small utility set with explicit scope: file listing, text output, create/remove/copy/move, and system information.
- [ ] Add command-line quoting, escaping, history, redirection, and pipelines only with parser tests and process/descriptor/pipe semantics to support them.
- [ ] Add integration tests that launch tools from the filesystem image and exercise them through syscalls; keep unsupported features explicit.

**Exit criteria:** shell and basic tools run as isolated user processes from a reproducible image; no shell command directly calls kernel-private VFS internals.

---

## Milestone 7 — graphical console and GUI (long-term)

A GUI is intentionally downstream of stable memory management, interrupts/input, process isolation, drivers, and userspace. Keep Crabshell's parser independent so a graphical terminal frontend can reuse it.

### Planned work

- [ ] Add validated framebuffer discovery and memory ownership; implement a minimal text/graphics console without compromising serial panic diagnostics.
- [ ] Establish an input subsystem that separates raw device events from key mapping and terminal policy. Plan PS/2 and USB HID support separately; do not treat the current raw scancode poller as a keyboard driver stack.
- [ ] Define a graphics buffer ownership/presentation API, clipping rules, pixel format, and bounds/overflow checks.
- [ ] Implement a minimal compositor/windowing policy only after process isolation and input routing are ready.
- [ ] Run Crabshell as a terminal application in a GUI window using the same parser and userspace services as the serial/TTY path.
- [ ] Preserve serial as a headless recovery/debug console and add repeatable QEMU display/input tests.

**Exit criteria:** a documented GUI session starts from userspace, renders a terminal, accepts tested input, and does not require direct kernel-private VFS access.

---

## Milestone 8 — networking (long-term, after drivers and process isolation)

Networking is not implied by the current device drivers. The initial target should be a tightly scoped virtual-device path with clear ownership and bounded buffers.

### Planned work

- [ ] Complete PCI/device discovery and define DMA buffer ownership, address translation, cache synchronization, and reset/error behavior.
- [ ] Implement one virtual NIC driver with bounded queues and timeouts; test against QEMU user networking.
- [ ] Choose and document a minimal link/network protocol scope before implementation. Keep packet parsing length-checked and fuzzable on the host.
- [ ] Add interface configuration, routing, socket/descriptor ownership, and per-process access policy.
- [ ] Add adversarial packet tests and integration tests for link loss, malformed packets, queue exhaustion, and device reset.
- [ ] Add higher-level transports/services only when the required protocol semantics, entropy source, and security model are designed.

**Exit criteria:** documented user processes can communicate through a tested virtual NIC/network stack, with malformed input and resource exhaustion handled safely. Do not claim internet, TLS, or POSIX sockets merely from a packet driver.

---

## Cross-cutting acceptance gates

Every milestone should include the relevant subset of these gates:

1. **Design:** documented ownership, invariants, resource limits, error semantics, and unsupported cases.
2. **Tests:** host tests for pure policy and malformed/boundary input; integration tests for hardware-facing behavior.
3. **Safety:** review unsafe blocks, pointer provenance/access, integer overflow, privilege boundaries, concurrency, and cleanup/rollback paths.
4. **Build:** format, host tests, target check, and final ELF link as appropriate.
5. **Boot/integration:** QEMU tests for changes to boot, paging, descriptors, interrupts, drivers, processes, or persistence.
6. **Documentation/status:** update architecture and roadmap docs; never check off a criterion without evidence.
7. **Compatibility:** claim Unix/POSIX behavior only for the exact documented subset with conformance-style tests.

## Working rule

Prefer a small end-to-end vertical slice over broad, unbootable scaffolding. A source file, interface, or architecture document is not proof that the corresponding subsystem is operational. When a check cannot run, record the exact environment blocker and leave that acceptance gate pending.

# Rustix documentation

Rustix is a 64-bit, Rust-first, Unix-like operating-system project. This index separates current implementation facts from planned interfaces: roadmap items are proposals until the corresponding code and tests exist.

## Start here

- [Project and implementation overview](architecture/overview.md)
- [Boot protocol and current entry path](architecture/boot.md)
- [Memory-management direction](architecture/memory.md)
- [x86_64 drivers and hardware boundary](architecture/drivers.md)
- [Crabshell and the volatile RAM filesystem](architecture/crabshell.md)
- [Unix-like process and syscall direction](architecture/syscall-abi.md)
- [Build and toolchain guide](development/building.md)
- [Testing and verification](development/testing.md)
- [Security and unsafe-code policy](security.md)
- [Milestones and acceptance criteria](roadmap/README.md)

## Current status

The repository contains a bare-metal `no_std` Rust kernel for `x86_64-unknown-none`. After Limine handoff it validates and copies memory-map metadata into an owned snapshot, captures the executable's physical and virtual bases, complete linker-defined image span, and page-aligned text/rodata/data segment bounds, reports baseline CPUID features, active/maximum address widths, read-only CR0 caching state, gated EFER.NXE/IA32_PAT values, and a bounded MTRR snapshot, seeds a volatile RAM filesystem, and runs Crabshell over the COM1 serial console. Boot-protocol pointers are checked for canonicality using the active 4- or 5-level paging width; physical map bounds and protocol-scoped HHDM range arithmetic are also validated. Crabshell's allocation-free parser is a separate crate; the kernel handles command execution. On 2026-10-16, `just verify` passed in WSL2 Ubuntu 24.04 both in the working tree and from a clean detached worktree with an empty `target` directory; the clean run downloaded and built the pinned Limine host utility, created the image, and passed the bounded QEMU boot to the shell prompt. The serial log showed memory-map and CPU reporting. Hosted CI has not been observed. A separate interactive QEMU session exercised `help`, `ls`, `meminfo`, directory navigation, and file create/write/append/read/copy/move/remove commands. Milestone 0's local exit criteria are met, and Milestone 1's validation criteria are met for the current Limine path. This is a kernel-mode shell, not a user process. A bounded physical-frame allocator core is initialized from the validated map and reported by `meminfo`; its owned frame token and failed-deallocation semantics are documented and host-tested, but no kernel service allocates or maps frames yet. The Limine base-revision 3 HHDM scope and a conservative initial mapping/alias/cache policy are documented. Pure host-tested helpers validate mapping ranges/PTE bits, parse PAT layouts, validate captured MTRR snapshots, and combine PAT/MTRR types for one physical address under normal caching according to Intel SDM Table 11-7. Boot validates the captured state and prints a diagnostic effective type at PA 0; this does not inspect inherited PTEs, check aliases, or select cache indexes for live mappings. `BootInfo` records raw CR3 and a validated decode of its root physical address and low-bit interpretation, but Rustix does not use the HHDM to access physical memory, inspect page-table contents, or own/replace the inherited tables. The complete linker-defined kernel-image span and the protocol-guaranteed minimum active boot-stack span are captured; Limine does not provide the exact initial stack allocation or guard status, so Rustix preserves only the known minimum span and does not infer a guard page. There is not yet a heap, a general IRQ subsystem, a scheduler, process isolation, a persistent filesystem, or a Unix compatibility layer. Fatal CPU exceptions have basic GDT/TSS/IDT diagnostics but no recovery. `just fault-smoke` validates a controlled page fault (including CR2) and invalid opcode in QEMU; broader exception coverage and physical-hardware validation remain pending. On 2026-10-21, `just verify` passed after adding CR3 decoding and the pure MTRR resolver, including host tests, target check, release build, ISO creation, and QEMU prompt smoke. On 2026-10-22, `just verify` passed after adding bounded read-only MTRR register capture and after adding validated PAT/MTRR policy resolution, including host tests, target check, release build, ISO creation, and QEMU prompt smoke. The QEMU log confirmed normal caching and a validated PA 0 diagnostic (`PAT[0]` resolved to WB). These checks do not inspect page-table entries or validate live mapping attributes/aliases.

## Documentation conventions

- **Implemented** means present in the repository and checked by current code or tests.
- **Planned** means an architectural direction, not a stable ABI or delivered capability.
- Any future ABI proposal must state versioning, error behavior, memory ownership, and compatibility expectations before it is treated as stable.

# Rustix agent instructions

These instructions apply to every coding agent working in this repository. Read this file before changing code. For the architecture and detailed subsystem contracts, use the linked documents under `docs/`; this file summarizes the rules agents must preserve.

## Project mission

Rustix is an experimental 64-bit, Unix-like operating system with its own Rust kernel. Limine is the external boot protocol/loader only. Do not describe Limine, a host shell, or a userspace project as the Rustix kernel.

The kernel is `no_std` and targets `x86_64-unknown-none`. Rust is the implementation language for kernel and OS components. The repository currently uses a Python standard-library script only to assemble and smoke-test the boot image; it does not replace kernel or OS functionality.

Unix-like behavior is a long-term design goal, not a claim of POSIX compatibility. Make unsupported behavior explicit rather than approximating it silently.

## Current project status — read before planning

The source contains:

- A Limine-based x86_64 kernel entry, linker layout, serial diagnostics, and boot-memory reporting.
- A separate allocation-free `no_std` `crabshell` parser crate and a kernel-mode COM1 shell frontend.
- A volatile, fixed-capacity RAM filesystem used by the shell.
- A validated, fixed-capacity boot memory-map snapshot, CPUID/address-width reporting, read-only CR0 caching-mode reporting, and gated read-only EFER.NXE/IA32_PAT/MTRR reporting.
- A fixed-capacity physical frame allocator retained in `BootInfo`; Crabshell's `meminfo` command reports counts. No kernel service currently allocates frames for mappings or other services.
- Pure 4 KiB mapping-range validation, leaf-PTE bit encoding, PAT layout parsing, and host-tested MTRR/PAT policy in `src/paging.rs`; these helpers check alignment, address widths, canonical virtual ranges, W^X, NXE input, PAT indices, captured-register validity, MTRR overlap rules, and Intel SDM Table 11-7 effective types under normal caching. Boot captures CR0 caching mode, EFER.NXE, `IA32_PAT`, and a bounded MTRR snapshot read-only when supported, validates the captured state, and reports a diagnostic PA 0 resolution. It does not verify inherited PTE attributes, cache aliases, or select cache indexes for live mappings. No code establishes frame ownership or mapping coverage, or modifies page tables.
- Bootstrap GDT/TSS/IDT setup and fatal exception handlers for vectors 0–31. Double faults use an IST stack and page faults report CR2. Opt-in QEMU tests inject a page fault and invalid opcode and verify diagnostics plus fatal halt; maskable IRQs remain disabled and exceptions are not recoverable.

Important incomplete work:

- Milestone 0's local exit criteria were met on 2026-10-16: `just verify` passed from both the working tree and a clean detached worktree in WSL2 Ubuntu 24.04. The detached worktree had an empty `target` directory, so the run exercised fresh Limine download/host-tool compilation, formatting, 19 host tests, target check, optimized build, image creation, and the 20-second QEMU prompt smoke test. Hosted CI has not been observed.
- A separate interactive `just run` session exercised directory navigation and create/write/append/read/copy/move/list/remove operations; `cp` replaced an existing destination, `rmdir` rejected a nonempty directory and succeeded after its child was removed, and unsupported `memtest` was rejected as expected. Boot snapshot tests and QEMU boot-metadata reporting were exercised. Structural checks still cannot prove that a Limine-provided non-null pointer is mapped or readable; that remains a loader trust boundary.
- Milestone 0 is closed for local acceptance; hosted CI remains pending. Milestone 1's validation criteria are met for the current Limine path, subject to the documented pointer-readability trust boundary. Milestone 2 is **in progress**, not complete. The frame allocator specifies token ownership and preserves the token on failed deallocation; unique allocator-instance use is still caller-enforced. CPU address widths, physical map bounds, protocol-scoped HHDM range arithmetic, Limine executable image bases, page-aligned linker-defined kernel segment bounds, and gated read-only EFER.NXE/IA32_PAT/MTRR capture are checked; the QEMU serial report showed the MTRR summary on 2026-10-22. On 2026-10-22, validated MTRR/PAT policy resolution also passed host tests and QEMU boot diagnostics, but those checks do not prove inherited page-table coverage, permissions, cache aliases, or effective attributes of live mappings. The transition-critical mapping inventory is documented. `just fault-smoke` has validated controlled page-fault/CR2 and invalid-opcode diagnostics plus fatal halting in QEMU. Rustix still inherits Limine's page tables; CR3's root address is decoded but table entries and complete live mapping extents are not inspected, and there is no kernel-owned page-table manager, heap, or live frame-allocation caller.
- There is no scheduler, userspace, syscall ABI, persistent filesystem, user/kernel isolation, or general IRQ subsystem.

Never advance status or check off a roadmap item merely because source code or an interface exists. Update `docs/roadmap/README.md` only to reflect implementation and validation actually achieved.

## Source-of-truth documents

Consult the relevant documentation before modifying a subsystem:

- [`docs/index.md`](docs/index.md) — documentation entry point and current status.
- [`docs/roadmap/README.md`](docs/roadmap/README.md) — milestone sequencing and exit criteria.
- [`docs/architecture/overview.md`](docs/architecture/overview.md) — current architecture and intended layers.
- [`docs/architecture/boot.md`](docs/architecture/boot.md) — Limine requests, boot snapshot, and trust boundary.
- [`docs/architecture/memory.md`](docs/architecture/memory.md) — memory ownership, frame allocator, and paging direction.
- [`docs/architecture/crabshell.md`](docs/architecture/crabshell.md) — parser/kernel boundary and shell/VFS contract.
- [`docs/architecture/drivers.md`](docs/architecture/drivers.md) — current driver scope and limitations.
- [`docs/security.md`](docs/security.md) — unsafe boundaries and security policy.
- [`docs/development/building.md`](docs/development/building.md) and [`docs/development/testing.md`](docs/development/testing.md) — supported commands and validation expectations.

When code and documentation disagree, inspect the implementation, resolve the discrepancy deliberately, and update the relevant documentation in the same change.

## Repository map

- `src/main.rs` — freestanding entry, boot snapshot acquisition, panic path, and shell handoff.
- `src/boot.rs` — mutable Limine requests, structural response/range validation, owned `BootInfo`, and boot diagnostics.
- `src/memory.rs` — allocation-free memory-map, address-width, canonical-address, Limine HHDM-range, and linker-defined kernel segment validation.
- `src/frame.rs` — bounded physical-frame allocator core; it only uses validated `Usable` ranges, reserves the first MiB, and has fixed range metadata.
- `src/paging.rs` — pure checked range and 4 KiB leaf-PTE bit construction for future mappings; no table access or physical-memory dereference.
- `src/shell.rs` — serial line editor and kernel-side Crabshell executor.
- `src/vfs.rs` — fixed-capacity volatile RAM filesystem and host-side tests.
- `crates/crabshell/` — separate `no_std` parser crate. It has no terminal, filesystem, or kernel dependencies.
- `src/arch/x86_64/serial.rs` — polling COM1 driver for shell input/output.
- `src/arch/x86_64/interrupts.rs` — bootstrap GDT/TSS/IDT, assembly stubs, and fatal exception diagnostics.
- `src/arch/x86_64/cpu.rs` — CPUID identification and selected feature reporting.
- `src/arch/x86_64/keyboard.rs` — raw, non-blocking PS/2-compatible scancode polling; not an input subsystem.
- `src/arch/x86_64/io.rs` — narrow port-I/O wrappers.
- `linker.ld`, `.cargo/config.toml`, `rust-toolchain.toml` — target, linker, and toolchain configuration.
- `limine.conf`, `scripts/boot.py` — boot configuration and pinned image/emulator workflow.
- `justfile` — supported development commands.
- `.github/workflows/ci.yml` — CI validation workflow.

## Engineering rules

### Keep changes incremental and coherent

1. Inspect the relevant source, tests, docs, and call sites before editing.
2. State assumptions, invariants, and failure behavior for new kernel interfaces.
3. Prefer small vertical slices that compile and can be tested over broad scaffolding or placeholder APIs.
4. Update tests and documentation alongside behavior changes.
5. Do not change unrelated code, rename files gratuitously, add speculative features, or rewrite project history.
6. Do not commit or create branches unless the user explicitly asks.

### Rust and dependency policy

- Preserve the kernel's `no_std`/freestanding constraints. Do not introduce `std` into kernel code.
- Prefer `core` and existing in-tree abstractions. Do not add third-party Rust dependencies without a concrete need and compatibility/security review.
- Keep the Crabshell parser independent of kernel I/O and VFS implementation. Kernel execution belongs in `src/shell.rs` or an appropriate kernel service.
- Do not add allocation-dependent APIs before a real heap exists. Fixed-capacity structures must document their limits and exhaustion behavior.
- Respect the workspace structure and the host-testable `rustix-kernel` library versus freestanding `rustix` binary boundary.

### Unsafe and hardware code

Unsafe code is expected only at explicit hardware, boot-protocol, assembly, or raw-memory boundaries. Keep each unsafe block narrow and document the invariant that makes it sound. Do not add broad `unsafe impl`, mutable global references, unchecked pointer arithmetic, or unreviewed inline/global assembly.

Before changing boot or memory code, account for these facts:

- Limine fills response pointers before `_start`; the request records must remain writable in the ELF image.
- Rustix validates nullness, alignment, counts, arithmetic, and physical ranges, but cannot prove that a non-null bootloader pointer is readable.
- Physical ranges are half-open `[start, end)` and must use checked arithmetic.
- Only regions classified `Usable` may enter the frame allocator. ACPI, bootloader-reclaimable, framebuffer, reserved, unknown, and other types are not free frames.
- A `Frame` is a physical address, not a dereferenceable pointer. Do not access it through the HHDM or change CR3 until an explicit, reviewed mapping policy and ownership proof exist.
- The kernel currently inherits Limine's page tables. Do not casually replace or mutate them: preserve the executing kernel, boot stack, `BootInfo`, request/response data, exception stacks, and mappings needed to continue execution.
- The exception setup is fatal-only. It does not enable maskable interrupts, configure a PIC/APIC, or provide recovery. Do not call `sti` or claim interrupt support without an IRQ design and tests.
- The shell and VFS run in ring 0 and are not isolated or secure.

For hardware changes, document assumptions about CPU mode, selectors, stacks, page permissions, interrupt state, and failure handling. Avoid new architecture mechanisms that cannot be statically reviewed or validated.

### Shell and filesystem contract

- Crabshell is presently a kernel-mode serial shell, not a userspace program or a POSIX shell.
- Its parser is a separate `no_std`, allocation-free crate; retain that boundary.
- The RAM filesystem is volatile and bounded. Preserve explicit errors and test capacity, path, and mutation edge cases.
- Do not imply persistence, permissions, links, process launching, or shell features that do not exist.
- Update the parser tests and `docs/architecture/crabshell.md` when adding or changing commands.

## Validation workflow

Run the narrowest relevant checks first, then broaden them. From the repository root, the supported commands are:

```sh
just fmt
just test
just check
just build
just image
just smoke
just verify
```

`just test` runs host-side library tests (memory-map validation, frame allocator, VFS, and Crabshell parser). `just check` checks `x86_64-unknown-none`; `just build` links the optimized ELF. `just verify` includes formatting, host tests, target check, pinned Limine image creation, and QEMU prompt smoke test. Image/boot checks need Python, `xorriso`, QEMU, the Rust target, and network access for the first pinned Limine download; Linux/WSL also needs `cc` to build Limine's host utility.

For changes to `src/main.rs`, `src/boot.rs`, linker/request configuration, `src/arch/x86_64/`, `src/frame.rs`, or paging/heap code, the intended full validation is `just verify`. If the environment does not permit a check, report the exact blocker and leave the corresponding roadmap criterion pending.

Do not claim a check passed unless it was run and its successful result was observed. Editor diagnostics are useful but are not a substitute for `cargo test`, a target build, or QEMU. A target check is not a final link; a linked ELF is not proof of boot; a prompt smoke test is not proof of interactive shell behavior or physical-hardware correctness.

## Completion criteria for agent changes

Before reporting work complete:

- Ensure source, tests, docs, and call sites agree.
- Review unsafe and hardware assumptions, including error paths and capacity limits.
- Run appropriate formatting/tests/build/boot checks, or clearly state why they could not run.
- Report files changed, behavior delivered, validation actually observed, and remaining risks.
- Keep milestone status accurate. A subsystem is not complete just because it has code.

```

## Current status

The repository contains a bare-metal `no_std` Rust kernel for `x86_64-unknown-none`. After Limine handoff it validates and copies memory-map metadata into an owned snapshot, captures the executable's physical and virtual bases, complete linker-defined image span, and page-aligned text/rodata/data segment bounds, reports baseline CPUID features, active/maximum address widths, and gated read-only EFER.NXE/IA32_PAT values, seeds a volatile RAM filesystem, and runs Crabshell over the COM1 serial console. Boot-protocol pointers are checked for canonicality using the active 4- or 5-level paging width; physical map bounds and protocol-scoped HHDM range arithmetic are also validated. Crabshell's allocation-free parser is a separate crate; the kernel handles command execution. On 2026-10-16, `just verify` passed in WSL2 Ubuntu 24.04 both in the working tree and from a clean detached worktree with an empty `target` directory; the clean run downloaded and built the pinned Limine host utility, created the image, and passed the bounded QEMU boot to the shell prompt. The serial log showed memory-map and CPU reporting. Hosted CI has not been observed. A separate interactive QEMU session exercised `help`, `ls`, `meminfo`, directory navigation, and file create/write/append/read/copy/move/remove commands. Milestone 0's local exit criteria are met, and Milestone 1's validation criteria are met for the current Limine path. This is a kernel-mode shell, not a user process. A bounded physical-frame allocator core is initialized from the validated map and reported by `meminfo`; its owned frame token and failed-deallocation semantics are documented and host-tested, but no kernel service allocates or maps frames yet. The Limine base-revision 3 HHDM scope and a conservative initial mapping/alias/cache policy are documented. Pure host-tested helpers validate mapping ranges/PTE bits, parse PAT layouts, and resolve MTRR types from supplied register values; live MTRRs are not captured and PAT/MTRR semantics are not combined for mappings. `BootInfo` records raw CR3 and a validated decode of its root physical address and low-bit interpretation, but Rustix does not use the HHDM to access physical memory, inspect page-table contents, or own/replace the inherited tables. The complete linker-defined kernel-image span and the protocol-guaranteed minimum active boot-stack span are captured; Limine does not provide the exact initial stack allocation or guard status, so Rustix preserves only the known minimum span and does not infer a guard page. There is not yet a heap, a general IRQ subsystem, a scheduler, process isolation, a persistent filesystem, or a Unix compatibility layer. Fatal CPU exceptions have basic GDT/TSS/IDT diagnostics but no recovery. `just fault-smoke` validates a controlled page fault (including CR2) and invalid opcode in QEMU; broader exception coverage and physical-hardware validation remain pending. On 2026-10-21, `just verify` passed after the CR3 decode addition, including host tests, target check, release build, ISO creation, and QEMU prompt smoke; this does not inspect page-table entries.
