# Memory-management direction

## What exists now

`src/memory.rs` contains an allocation-free `MemoryMapBuilder` that copies Limine ranges into validated half-open physical regions. It rejects empty ranges, `base + length` overflow, overlapping ranges, empty maps, and maps exceeding the fixed 256-region capacity. Known Limine types remain distinct, and unknown type values are preserved. Host-side tests cover range validation/classification, canonical-address boundaries, physical-width bounds, and HHDM range arithmetic. `src/boot.rs` stores the resulting map in an owned boot snapshot and reports usable bytes.

`src/frame.rs` provides a fixed-capacity allocator core with host-side tests. It only manages complete 4 KiB frames inside validated `Usable` regions, reserves the first MiB, and coalesces adjacent free ranges. The ownership contract assumes one allocator instance per physical map: within that instance, each eligible frame is owned either by its free-range table or by a non-copyable `Frame` token while allocated. The public constructor does not enforce unique instances, so callers must not initialize multiple allocators for the same physical map; the current boot path retains one allocator in `BootInfo`. `allocate` returns `None` when no free frame remains. `deallocate` consumes the token only on success; on any error, including free-range-table exhaustion, it returns a `DeallocationError` containing the original token and leaves allocator state unchanged. The range tables each have a fixed `MAX_FRAME_RANGES` capacity, so fragmentation can prevent a frame from being returned until nearby ranges coalesce. No kernel service currently allocates frames for mappings or other work.

`Frame::address()` is a physical address value, not a dereferenceable pointer and not a proof that the frame is mapped. CPU diagnostics now read `CR4.LA57` to report the active linear-address width (48 or 57 bits) and query `CPUID.80000008H` for physical and maximum linear-address widths when available. Boot-protocol pointers are checked against the active width, with host tests for 48- and 57-bit canonical boundaries. These facts do not prove that any physical address is mapped.

`src/paging.rs` adds pure, host-tested 4 KiB mapping groundwork and decodes the inherited CR3 root address plus its low-bit interpretation. The CR3 decoder validates the physical-address width and reserved bits and interprets the low 12 bits according to the active `CR4.PCIDE` state; it does not dereference the root. The mapping-range validator requires a known physical-address width, checked aligned bounds, canonical virtual endpoints in one canonical half, and rejects writable-executable permissions. A validated range can encode the raw bits of one 4 KiB leaf PTE, including supervisor/user and write permissions, NX when the caller confirms EFER.NXE, and a bounded three-bit PAT index. `PatLayout` parses a supplied `IA32_PAT` value and selects WB, UC, or WC indices. `MtrrMemoryType`, `VariableMtrr`, `FixedMtrrRanges`, and `MtrrLayout` resolve MTRR types at one physical address, including fixed-range priority and defined variable-overlap rules; undefined overlaps fail closed. `MtrrRegisters::validated_layout` additionally validates captured capability/default-type reserved bits, register counts and fixed-range presence, WC support, and variable-mask shape/alignment before producing an owned `ValidatedMtrrLayout`. It supports contiguous power-of-two variable masks; Intel permits discontinuous masks on some CPUs, but Rustix rejects them explicitly as unsupported rather than approximating their coverage. The layout combines the address-specific MTRR type with a selected PAT entry according to Intel SDM Table 11-7, but only when `CR0.CD` and `CR0.NW` are clear. Host tests cover all 30 documented MTRR/PAT type pairs and reject invalid indexes, malformed snapshots, out-of-range addresses, and non-normal caching mode. A pure range selector now returns the lowest PAT index that produces one requested effective type throughout a nonempty, aligned physical range, checking fixed- and variable-MTRR transition boundaries rather than iterating every page. It rejects the range if no single index works throughout. `ValidatedMappingRange::select_cache_attributes` composes that selector with a validated mapping extent and returns range-bound PAT attributes; those attributes can encode each 4 KiB leaf in that extent without reselecting per page. This is still policy-only: it trusts the supplied PAT/MTRR and normal-caching state, does not inspect existing PTEs or cache aliases, and does not establish frame ownership. Boot reads CR0 without modifying it, validates supported captured MTRR/PAT state, and reports a diagnostic resolution at physical address zero using PAT index 0; this does not inspect the inherited PTE or assert that the live mapping uses that index. The raw MTRR capture remains bounded to 32 variable pairs and reports capacity overflow without partial state. `Frame::hhdm_address` combines a non-copyable allocated-frame token with a known physical width and a full-page `Usable`-region check to calculate a Limine HHDM address; it returns only an integer and relies on the documented Limine mapping guarantee. The opt-in `just frame-smoke` path writes, reads, clears, and reclaims one such frame in QEMU. This validates one loader-backed HHDM access case, not arbitrary physical access or full page-table coverage. The opt-in walker follows only the paths needed for transition-critical ranges; no table is modified, and no mapping operation or CR3 transition is implemented.

The effective-type resolver follows [Intel SDM Vol. 3A §11.5.2.2, Table 11-7](https://cdrdv2-public.intel.com/671447/325384-sdm-vol-3abcd.pdf), which applies when normal caching is enabled (`CR0.CD=0`, `CR0.NW=0`). Its footnotes distinguish UC selected by an MTRR from UC selected by a page-table entry (the latter involves cache snooping and aliasing concerns); they also identify combinations that older manual editions called undefined but current processors supporting both PAT and MTRRs resolve as shown. The resolver does not cover legacy PCD/PWT-only selection or model-specific combinations outside that table.

The requested Limine base revision is 3. Its protocol maps only `Usable`, `BootloaderReclaimable`, `ExecutableAndModules`, and `Framebuffer` memory-map regions into the HHDM; reserved, ACPI, bad, and unknown regions are not in that mapping set. HHDM mappings use at least 4 KiB granularity and may cover page-aligned bytes beyond unaligned region boundaries. On x86_64, inherited HHDM mappings are supervisor RWX, normally write-back cached, with framebuffer mappings write-combining when PAT is available. Therefore an HHDM offset is not a blanket physical-memory access grant, and inherited HHDM permissions are not Rustix's future W^X policy. See the [Limine base revision 3 protocol](https://github.com/limine-bootloader/limine-protocol/blob/trunk/PROTOCOL.md#base-revision-3) and its memory-layout/caching sections.

The boot snapshot now rejects physical map ranges beyond the reported CPUID physical-address width when that CPUID leaf is available. For base revision 3 HHDM-mapped types, it also validates the page-rounded physical span, checked `offset + address` arithmetic, and canonical endpoints in the active linear-address width. If the CPU does not report a physical width, the physical-bound check is skipped and no mapping caller may treat the bound as known. These checks are derived from metadata and Limine's protocol contract; they do not inspect page tables or prove that a non-null loader pointer is readable. The only HHDM dereference is the opt-in QEMU frame probe, which first validates an allocator-issued frame's full-page `Usable` backing and checked HHDM address; this remains a narrow reliance on Limine's handoff guarantee, not a general physical-memory access service. Rustix-owned mappings should be non-executable by default; executable kernel text must be explicit. MMIO requires an explicit device range and cache policy, and guard regions must remain unmapped. A page-table transition must preserve the kernel image, active stacks, boot data, descriptor tables, and any loader mappings still needed. Rustix does not reclaim bootloader memory, own or replace the inherited Limine page tables, or provide a heap. Bootstrap GDT/TSS/IDT setup and fatal exception diagnostics live in `src/arch/x86_64/interrupts.rs`; they do not enable maskable IRQs.

## Mapping inventory before a CR3 transition

The current runtime has several mappings that a future page-table transition must preserve. The address sources and remaining gaps are:

- **Kernel ELF image:** `linker.ld` places `.text`, `.rodata`, `.limine_requests`, `.data`, `.bss`, and `.got` in three `PT_LOAD` segments: RX text, read-only rodata, and RW data/BSS. It exports `__kernel_start` and `__kernel_end` around the complete loadable image, plus page-aligned bounds for each segment. `BootInfo` checks that Limine's reported virtual base matches the linker start, validates ordered contiguous segment bounds covering the rounded image, derives corresponding half-open physical ranges from the executable physical base with checked arithmetic, and validates canonical virtual and reported physical address widths. The release ELF and QEMU runtime report both showed the three aligned ranges on 2026-10-21. The RX, R/NX, and RW/NX labels describe the linker segment intent; these are linker/boot metadata, not proof that the inherited page tables map every page or enforce those permissions, nor proof that loader pointers are readable. The memory-map `ExecutableAndModules` entries remain illustrative, not an authoritative kernel-image extent.
- **Active stack and `BootInfo`:** The assembly `_start` shim captures Limine's entry `RSP` before any Rust prologue. Under the SysV entry convention the synthetic return slot occupies 8 bytes, so `RSP + 8` is the exclusive stack top. The protocol guarantees at least 64 KiB (without a Stack Size request); `BootInfo` records that minimum virtual span, translates it through the HHDM, and requires it to fit within a single `BootloaderReclaimable` physical region. The full loader allocation may be larger, and neither its exact bounds nor a guard page are known. Preserve the inherited mapping; do not infer a guard page.
- **Kernel static data:** `RAM_FILESYSTEM`, GDT, IDT, TSS, the ring-0 stack, and double-fault IST stack are static BSS/data in the kernel image. Exception entry also requires the handler code and the TSS/IDT references to remain mapped. Preserve the complete relevant data/BSS pages and stack pages.
- **Limine request data:** request records are in the kernel's writable `.limine_requests` segment. Response objects and the memory-map pointer array are bootloader-reclaimable; `capture_boot_information` copies the values used later, and the shell does not retain those pointers. Keep them mapped until the copy and validation finish; any later reclaim must be explicit rather than reclaiming the whole bootloader-reclaimable class.
- **Inherited page tables:** Limine places its page tables in bootloader-reclaimable memory, but their layout is unspecified. `BootInfo` captures raw CR3 and validates a decoded physical root address plus the low-bit interpretation selected by active `CR4.PCIDE`. A pure helper requires the root page to fit in one validated `BootloaderReclaimable` range and calculates its HHDM address when the physical width is known. The opt-in QEMU probe reads the root's 512 entries and counts present bits, then follows bounded paths for every page in the kernel text/rodata/data and minimum boot-stack spans, checking physical translations. It does not enumerate unrelated mappings or verify inherited permissions, effective cache attributes, or aliases. Keep the old root and its backing pages intact while inspecting/building a replacement; do not reclaim them until a verified switch no longer depends on them.
- **Devices:** COM1 uses x86 port I/O and needs no MMIO virtual mapping. Rustix does not currently request or use a framebuffer. Any future framebuffer or device-register mapping needs an explicit physical range and cache policy.

## Initial kernel-owned mapping policy (design only)

A first Rustix-owned x86_64 root should use 4 KiB pages only and require NX support; if NX is unavailable, abort before switching. Preserve ELF permissions exactly: text RX, rodata R/NX, and `.limine_requests`/data/BSS/GOT RW/NX. Reject W+X mappings. Exclude the complete physical kernel-image span from the generic HHDM in the first implementation so no writable direct-map alias can undermine text or rodata permissions. Ordinary RAM HHDM mappings should be RW/NX and WB.

Preserve the inherited PAT/MTRR configuration during the first transition. The boot report validates captured registers and computes a diagnostic effective type from the active PAT/MTRR values under normal caching. A separate pure selector can choose an index whose effective type remains uniform across an aligned physical range, but neither checks inherited PTEs nor detects cache-type aliases. The pure combination follows Intel SDM Table 11-7; it is not a generic rule for legacy PCD/PWT-only selection or model-specific combinations. Under Limine base revision 3 on x86_64, use PAT index 0 for WB, index 3 for UC, and index 5 for WC only after the target physical range and active PAT/MTRR interaction are verified. Map MMIO only from explicit device ranges and use UC by default; do not infer MMIO from generic reserved memory-map entries. A framebuffer may use WC only after its response and cache policy are explicitly validated. COM1 uses port I/O and requires no MMIO mapping.

Do not use huge pages in the first root; add them only when physical coverage, permissions, and cache attributes are uniform across the entire huge-page extent. Future Rustix-owned downward-growing stacks should have at least one 4 KiB unmapped guard page below them. The Limine bootstrap stack has no known guard, so none may be assumed there.

Never modify Limine's active page tables in place. Build a separate candidate root from owned frames, leave the inherited root and its backing memory intact, and do not switch CR3 until every transition-critical mapping has been preserved and checked. Any pre-switch failure must discard the candidate root and return its frames without changing the active root. This policy is not yet implemented; Rustix does not inspect the inherited root or replace CR3.

## Planned memory layers

1. **Validated physical regions:** implemented as a fixed-capacity owned snapshot; allocator ownership and reclaim policy remain future work.
2. **Frame allocator integration:** the bounded core is initialized from `BootInfo`; add real allocation callers only after the page-mapping policy and ownership rules are implemented.
3. **Kernel virtual memory:** Rustix still runs on inherited Limine page tables. Before replacing them, preserve the executing kernel, bootstrap/Ring-0 stacks, request/response data, and exception stacks; define the HHDM extent and explicit mapping permissions/cache attributes. Keep writable-executable mappings disallowed by default and reserve MMIO and guard regions.
4. **Heap:** add a global allocator only after frame allocation and page mapping are initialized. Define allocation failure behavior for kernel and interrupt contexts.
5. **Process address spaces:** isolate userspace; define copy-in/copy-out helpers and never treat user pointers as kernel references.

## Invariants to preserve

- Physical ranges use checked arithmetic and the half-open convention `[start, end)`.
- Only complete frames in validated `Usable` regions enter the allocator; the first MiB remains reserved. Firmware and loader-reclaimable regions are not silently promoted to free memory.
- Under the single-allocator-per-physical-map contract, a frame is represented by one allocator-free range or one caller-owned, non-copyable `Frame` token. Only a successful `deallocate` transfers the token back to the allocator; errors return the token and leave allocator ranges and accounting unchanged. The current public constructor relies on callers to enforce unique allocator instances.
- `allocate` returns `None` on frame exhaustion. Metadata-capacity exhaustion is an explicit error, never silent loss of a frame.
- A `Frame` address is physical, not directly dereferenceable. No HHDM translation, page-table mutation, or CR3 switch is permitted until address widths, mapping coverage, permissions/cache attributes, and transition-preservation requirements are established.
- Mapping changes validate alignment, canonical addresses, ownership, and permissions before touching tables.
- User-controlled addresses are validated on every syscall boundary; prior validation is not a substitute for access checks during later copies.
- Tests cover unaligned edges, exact-boundary allocations, arithmetic overflow, overlaps, exhaustion, and unchanged state/ownership on failure.

These are design requirements for future milestones, not functionality delivered by the current boot summary.

unsafe extern "C" {
    static __kernel_start: u8;

    static __kernel_data_mapping_start: u8;
    static __kernel_data_mapping_end: u8;
}

/// Owned snapshot of bootloader data and CPU state consumed by the kernel.
pub struct BootInfo {
    pub hhdm_revision: u64,
    pub hhdm_offset: u64,
    pub inherited_cr3_raw: u64,
    pub inherited_cr3_root: Result<Cr3Root, Cr3Error>,
    pub executable_address_revision: u64,
    pub kernel_physical_base: u64,
    pub kernel_physical_end: u64,
    pub kernel_virtual_base: u64,
    pub kernel_virtual_end: u64,
    pub kernel_image_segments: KernelImageSegments,
    pub boot_stack_physical_start: u64,
    pub boot_stack_physical_end: u64,
    pub boot_stack_virtual_start: u64,
    pub boot_stack_virtual_end: u64,
    pub memory_map_revision: u64,
    pub memory_map: MemoryMap,
    pub frame_allocator: FrameAllocator,
    pub cpu_info: crate::arch::x86_64::cpu::CpuInfo,
}

#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum BootInfoError {
    MissingHhdmResponse,
    InvalidHhdmResponsePointer,
    InvalidHhdmOffset,
    MissingExecutableAddressResponse,
    InvalidExecutableAddressResponsePointer,
    InvalidKernelImageRange,
    InvalidKernelImageSegments,
    InvalidInitialStackBounds,
    InvalidInitialStackHhdmRange,
    InitialStackNotBootloaderReclaimable,
    MissingMemoryMapResponse,
    InvalidMemoryMapResponsePointer,
    MemoryMapCountDoesNotFit,
    TooManyMemoryRegions,
    EmptyMemoryMap,
    InvalidEntriesPointer,
    EntriesAddressOverflow,
    InvalidEntryPointer { index: usize },
    InvalidPhysicalRange { index: usize },
    InvalidHhdmMappingRange { index: usize },
    InvalidMemoryMap(MemoryMapError),
    FrameAllocator(FrameError),
}

/// Copy and validate the boot data needed by the current kernel.
///
/// Structural checks can reject malformed pointers and ranges, but cannot prove
/// that a loader-provided pointer is mapped and readable. That remains part of
/// the documented Limine handoff trust boundary until the kernel owns its maps.
pub fn capture_boot_information(entry_rsp: u64) -> Result<BootInfo, BootInfoError> {
    let cpu_info = crate::arch::x86_64::cpu::identify();
    let inherited_cr3_raw = crate::arch::x86_64::cpu::read_cr3_raw();
    let inherited_cr3_root = parse_cr3_root(
        inherited_cr3_raw,
        cpu_info.physical_address_bits,
        cpu_info.pcid_enabled,
    );
    let virtual_address_bits = cpu_info.active_linear_address_bits;
    let (boot_stack_virtual_start, boot_stack_virtual_end) =
        limine_x86_64_stack_bounds(entry_rsp, virtual_address_bits)
            .ok_or(BootInfoError::InvalidInitialStackBounds)?;
    let hhdm_request = core::ptr::addr_of_mut!(HHDM_REQUEST);
    // SAFETY: Limine has completed writing the request response before `_start`.
    let hhdm_pointer =
        unsafe { core::ptr::read_volatile(core::ptr::addr_of!((*hhdm_request).response)) };
    if hhdm_pointer.is_null() {
        return Err(BootInfoError::MissingHhdmResponse);
    }
    if !is_valid_pointer(hhdm_pointer, virtual_address_bits) {
        return Err(BootInfoError::InvalidHhdmResponsePointer);
    }
    // SAFETY: The Limine response pointer is trusted to refer to a readable
    // response object; its nullness and alignment are checked above.
    let hhdm = unsafe { hhdm_pointer.read_volatile() };
    if hhdm.offset & 0xfff != 0 || !is_canonical_virtual_address(hhdm.offset, virtual_address_bits)
    {
        return Err(BootInfoError::InvalidHhdmOffset);
    }

    let executable_address_request = core::ptr::addr_of_mut!(EXECUTABLE_ADDRESS_REQUEST);
    // SAFETY: Limine has completed writing the request response before `_start`.
    let executable_address_pointer = unsafe {
        core::ptr::read_volatile(core::ptr::addr_of!((*executable_address_request).response))
    };
    if executable_address_pointer.is_null() {
        return Err(BootInfoError::MissingExecutableAddressResponse);
    }
    if !is_valid_pointer(executable_address_pointer, virtual_address_bits) {
        return Err(BootInfoError::InvalidExecutableAddressResponsePointer);
    }
    // SAFETY: Limine's response pointer is trusted to refer to a readable object;
    // nullness, alignment, and active-width canonicality were checked above.
    let executable_address = unsafe { executable_address_pointer.read_volatile() };
    // `linker.ld` defines these symbols as the boundaries of the loaded image.
    let (linked_virtual_start, linked_virtual_end) = (
        core::ptr::addr_of!(__kernel_start) as u64,
        core::ptr::addr_of!(__kernel_end) as u64,
    );
    let kernel_physical_end = kernel_image_physical_end(
        executable_address.physical_base,
        executable_address.virtual_base,
        linked_virtual_start,
        linked_virtual_end,
        cpu_info.physical_address_bits,
        virtual_address_bits,
    )
    .ok_or(BootInfoError::InvalidKernelImageRange)?;
    let linked_segments = KernelImageVirtualSegments {
        text: (
            core::ptr::addr_of!(__kernel_text_mapping_start) as u64,
            core::ptr::addr_of!(__kernel_text_mapping_end) as u64,
        ),
        rodata: (
            core::ptr::addr_of!(__kernel_rodata_mapping_start) as u64,
            core::ptr::addr_of!(__kernel_rodata_mapping_end) as u64,
        ),
        data: (
            core::ptr::addr_of!(__kernel_data_mapping_start) as u64,
            core::ptr::addr_of!(__kernel_data_mapping_end) as u64,
        ),
    };
    let kernel_image_segments = kernel_image_segments(
        executable_address.physical_base,
        executable_address.virtual_base,
        linked_virtual_start,
        linked_virtual_end,
        linked_segments,
        cpu_info.physical_address_bits,
        virtual_address_bits,
    )
    .ok_or(BootInfoError::InvalidKernelImageSegments)?;

    let memory_map_request = core::ptr::addr_of_mut!(MEMORY_MAP_REQUEST);
    // SAFETY: Limine has completed writing the request response before `_start`.
    let memory_map_pointer =
        unsafe { core::ptr::read_volatile(core::ptr::addr_of!((*memory_map_request).response)) };
    if memory_map_pointer.is_null() {
        return Err(BootInfoError::MissingMemoryMapResponse);
    }
    if !is_valid_pointer(memory_map_pointer, virtual_address_bits) {
        return Err(BootInfoError::InvalidMemoryMapResponsePointer);
    }
    // SAFETY: The Limine response pointer is trusted to refer to a readable
    // response object; its nullness and alignment are checked above.
    let response = unsafe { memory_map_pointer.read_volatile() };
    let entry_count = usize::try_from(response.entry_count)
        .map_err(|_| BootInfoError::MemoryMapCountDoesNotFit)?;
    if entry_count > MAX_MEMORY_REGIONS {
        return Err(BootInfoError::TooManyMemoryRegions);
    }
    if entry_count == 0 {
        return Err(BootInfoError::EmptyMemoryMap);
    }
    if response.entries.is_null() {
        return Err(BootInfoError::InvalidEntriesPointer);
    }
    if !is_valid_pointer(response.entries, virtual_address_bits) {
        return Err(BootInfoError::InvalidEntriesPointer);
    }
    let entry_bytes = entry_count
        .checked_mul(size_of::<*const MemoryMapEntry>())
        .ok_or(BootInfoError::EntriesAddressOverflow)?;
    let entries_start = response.entries as usize;
    let entries_end = entries_start
        .checked_add(entry_bytes)
        .ok_or(BootInfoError::EntriesAddressOverflow)?;
    if !is_canonical_virtual_address(entries_start as u64, virtual_address_bits)
        || !is_canonical_virtual_address((entries_end - 1) as u64, virtual_address_bits)
    {
        return Err(BootInfoError::InvalidEntriesPointer);
    }

    let mut builder = MemoryMapBuilder::new();
    for index in 0..entry_count {
        // SAFETY: Limine promises an array of `entry_count` pointers. The count
        // is capped and pointer alignment/address arithmetic are checked above.
        let entry_pointer = unsafe { response.entries.add(index).read_volatile() };
        if !is_valid_pointer(entry_pointer, virtual_address_bits) {
            return Err(BootInfoError::InvalidEntryPointer { index });
        }
        // SAFETY: Limine promises each non-null entry pointer is readable.
        let entry = unsafe { entry_pointer.read_volatile() };
        builder
            .push(entry.base, entry.length, entry.kind)
            .map_err(BootInfoError::InvalidMemoryMap)?;
    }

    let memory_map = builder.finish().map_err(|error| match error {
        MemoryMapError::EmptyMap => BootInfoError::EmptyMemoryMap,
        other => BootInfoError::InvalidMemoryMap(other),
    })?;
    for (index, region) in memory_map.regions().iter().enumerate() {
        if let Some(physical_bits) = cpu_info.physical_address_bits {
            if !physical_range_fits_address_width(region.start(), region.end(), physical_bits) {
                return Err(BootInfoError::InvalidPhysicalRange { index });
            }
        }
        if region.kind().is_mapped_by_limine_v3_hhdm()
            && !limine_v3_hhdm_range_is_valid(
                hhdm.offset,
                region.start(),
                region.end(),
                cpu_info.physical_address_bits,
                virtual_address_bits,
            )
        {
            return Err(BootInfoError::InvalidHhdmMappingRange { index });
        }
    }
    let boot_stack_physical_start = boot_stack_virtual_start
        .checked_sub(hhdm.offset)
        .ok_or(BootInfoError::InvalidInitialStackHhdmRange)?;
    let boot_stack_physical_end = boot_stack_virtual_end
        .checked_sub(hhdm.offset)
        .ok_or(BootInfoError::InvalidInitialStackHhdmRange)?;
    if !limine_v3_hhdm_range_is_valid(
        hhdm.offset,
        boot_stack_physical_start,
        boot_stack_physical_end,
        cpu_info.physical_address_bits,
        virtual_address_bits,
    ) {
        return Err(BootInfoError::InvalidInitialStackHhdmRange);
    }
    if !memory_map.range_is_within_region_kind(
        boot_stack_physical_start,
        boot_stack_physical_end,
        RegionKind::BootloaderReclaimable,
    ) {
        return Err(BootInfoError::InitialStackNotBootloaderReclaimable);
    }
    let frame_allocator =
        FrameAllocator::from_memory_map(&memory_map).map_err(BootInfoError::FrameAllocator)?;

    Ok(BootInfo {
        hhdm_revision: hhdm.revision,
        hhdm_offset: hhdm.offset,
        inherited_cr3_raw,
        inherited_cr3_root,
        executable_address_revision: executable_address.revision,
        kernel_physical_base: executable_address.physical_base,
        kernel_physical_end,
        kernel_virtual_base: executable_address.virtual_base,
        kernel_virtual_end: linked_virtual_end,
        kernel_image_segments,
        boot_stack_physical_start,
        boot_stack_physical_end,
        boot_stack_virtual_start,
        boot_stack_virtual_end,
        memory_map_revision: response.revision,
        memory_map,
        frame_allocator,
        cpu_info,
    })
}

/// Print a report from the copied snapshot; no loader pointers are used here.
pub fn report_boot_information(boot_info: &BootInfo) {
    crate::kprintln!(
        "HHDM: offset {:#018x}, response revision {}",
        boot_info.hhdm_offset,
        boot_info.hhdm_revision
    );
    crate::kprintln!(
        "inherited CR3: raw {:#018x} (not walked during boot snapshot)",
        boot_info.inherited_cr3_raw
    );
    match boot_info.inherited_cr3_root {
        Ok(root) => crate::kprintln!(
            "inherited CR3 root: physical {:#018x}, low bits {:?}",
            root.physical_address(),
            root.low_bits()
        ),
        Err(error) => crate::kprintln!("inherited CR3 root could not be decoded: {:?}", error),
    }
    crate::kprintln!(
        "kernel image: physical [{:#018x}, {:#018x}), virtual [{:#018x}, {:#018x}), response revision {}",
        boot_info.kernel_physical_base,
        boot_info.kernel_physical_end,
        boot_info.kernel_virtual_base,
        boot_info.kernel_virtual_end,
        boot_info.executable_address_revision
    );
    let segments = &boot_info.kernel_image_segments;
    crate::kprintln!(
        "kernel mapping text RX: physical [{:#018x}, {:#018x}), virtual [{:#018x}, {:#018x})",
        segments.text.physical_start,
        segments.text.physical_end,
        segments.text.virtual_start,
        segments.text.virtual_end
    );
    crate::kprintln!(
        "kernel mapping rodata R/NX: physical [{:#018x}, {:#018x}), virtual [{:#018x}, {:#018x})",
        segments.rodata.physical_start,
        segments.rodata.physical_end,
        segments.rodata.virtual_start,
        segments.rodata.virtual_end
    );
    crate::kprintln!(
        "kernel mapping data RW/NX: physical [{:#018x}, {:#018x}), virtual [{:#018x}, {:#018x})",
        segments.data.physical_start,
        segments.data.physical_end,
        segments.data.virtual_start,
        segments.data.virtual_end
    );
    crate::kprintln!(
        "boot stack (minimum protocol span): physical [{:#018x}, {:#018x}), virtual [{:#018x}, {:#018x})",
        boot_info.boot_stack_physical_start,
        boot_info.boot_stack_physical_end,
        boot_info.boot_stack_virtual_start,
        boot_info.boot_stack_virtual_end
    );
    crate::kprintln!(
        "memory map: {} validated regions, {} MiB usable RAM, response revision {}",
        boot_info.memory_map.regions().len(),
        boot_info.memory_map.usable_bytes() / (1024 * 1024),
        boot_info.memory_map_revision
    );
    crate::kprintln!(
        "physical frames: {} managed, {} free (4 KiB each)",
        boot_info.frame_allocator.managed_frames(),
        boot_info.frame_allocator.free_frames()
    );
    for region in boot_info.memory_map.regions() {
        crate::kprintln!(
            "  [{:#018x}, {:#018x}) {:?}",
            region.start(),
            region.end(),
            region.kind()
        );
    }
    crate::kprintln!("console: COM1 serial (polling)");

    let cpu = &boot_info.cpu_info;
    let vendor = core::str::from_utf8(&cpu.vendor).unwrap_or("unknown");
    let mtrr_supported = !matches!(&cpu.mtrr, MtrrState::Unsupported);
    crate::kprintln!(
        "CPU: {} (basic leaf {}, extended leaf {:#x})",
        vendor,
        cpu.max_basic_leaf,
        cpu.max_extended_leaf
    );
    crate::kprintln!(
        "CPU feature support: SSE2={}, NX={}, NXE-enabled={}, normal-caching={}, PAT={}, MTRR={}, 1GiB-pages={}, long-mode={}, LA57-supported={}, PCID-enabled={}",
        cpu.has_sse2,
        cpu.has_nx,
        cpu.nx_enabled,
        cpu.normal_caching,
        cpu.has_pat,
        mtrr_supported,
        cpu.has_1g_pages,
        cpu.has_long_mode,
        cpu.has_la57,
        cpu.pcid_enabled
    );
    match cpu.pat_msr_value {
        Some(value) => match PatLayout::from_msr_value(value) {
            Ok(layout) => crate::kprintln!(
                "PAT: IA32_PAT={:#018x}, WB index={:?}, UC index={:?}, WC index={:?}",
                value,
                layout.index_for(CachePolicy::WriteBack),
                layout.index_for(CachePolicy::Uncacheable),
                layout.index_for(CachePolicy::WriteCombining)
            ),
            Err(error) => crate::kprintln!(
                "PAT: IA32_PAT={:#018x} has unsupported layout: {:?}",
                value,
                error
            ),
        },
        None => crate::kprintln!("PAT: unsupported"),
    }
    match &cpu.mtrr {
        MtrrState::Unsupported => {
            crate::kprintln!("MTRR: unsupported")
        }
        MtrrState::VariableRangeCapacityExceeded { reported_count } => {
            crate::kprintln!(
                "MTRR: {} variable pairs exceed the snapshot capacity {}; no partial state retained",
                reported_count,
                MAX_CAPTURED_VARIABLE_MTRRS
            )
        }
        MtrrState::Captured(registers) => {
            crate::kprintln!(
                "MTRR snapshot: MTRRCAP={:#018x}, DEF_TYPE={:#018x}, enabled={}, fixed-enabled={}, fixed-supported={}, WC-supported={}, variable-pairs={}",
                registers.capability,
                registers.default_type,
                registers.default_type & (1 << 11) != 0,
                registers.default_type & (1 << 10) != 0,
                registers.capability & (1 << 8) != 0,
                registers.capability & (1 << 10) != 0,
                registers.variable_register_count
            )
        }
    }
    match (&cpu.mtrr, cpu.pat_msr_value, cpu.physical_address_bits) {
        (MtrrState::Captured(registers), Some(pat_value), Some(address_bits)) => {
            match (
                registers.validated_layout(address_bits),
                PatLayout::from_msr_value(pat_value),
            ) {
                (Ok(mtrr), Ok(pat)) => crate::kprintln!(
                    "MTRR/PAT: validated; effective type at PA 0x0 using PAT[0]={:?}",
                    mtrr.effective_memory_type_for(0, pat, 0, cpu.normal_caching)
                ),
                (Err(error), _) => {
                    crate::kprintln!("MTRR/PAT: rejected captured MTRR state: {:?}", error)
                }
                (_, Err(error)) => {
                    crate::kprintln!("MTRR/PAT: rejected captured PAT state: {:?}", error)
                }
            }
        }
        _ => crate::kprintln!(
            "MTRR/PAT: effective type unavailable (missing state or address width)"
        ),
    }
    crate::kprintln!(
        "CPU address widths (bits): physical={:?}, max-linear={:?}, active-linear={} (LA57 active={})",
        cpu.physical_address_bits,
        cpu.max_linear_address_bits,
        cpu.active_linear_address_bits,
        cpu.active_linear_address_bits == 57
    );
}

fn is_valid_pointer<T>(pointer: *const T, virtual_address_bits: u8) -> bool {
    let start = pointer as usize;
    let Some(end) = start.checked_add(size_of::<T>()) else {
        return false;
    };
    !pointer.is_null()
        && start & (align_of::<T>() - 1) == 0
        && is_canonical_virtual_address(start as u64, virtual_address_bits)
        && is_canonical_virtual_address((end - 1) as u64, virtual_address_bits)
}

# Boot protocol and kernel entry

## Current boot contract

Rustix currently expects a Limine-compatible x86_64 handoff. Limine is an external loader; it does not implement Rustix's kernel services. The kernel requests protocol base revision 3, the higher-half direct-map (HHDM) offset, the executable physical/virtual base addresses, and the memory map.

Requests are kept in `.limine_requests_start`, `.limine_requests`, and `.limine_requests_end` by `linker.ld`. The response-bearing request records are mutable and the output `.limine_requests` section is placed in a writable load segment because Limine fills their response pointers before entering Rustix. The ELF entry symbol is `_start`.

### Entry sequence

1. Limine loads the ELF and transfers control to the assembly `_start` shim under the x86_64 Limine protocol. The shim captures the entry `RSP`, aligns the stack for a SysV call, and invokes `rustix_start`.
2. `rustix_start` configures the legacy COM1 UART for polling output and input.
3. The kernel disables maskable interrupts and installs its bootstrap GDT, TSS, and fatal-exception IDT. This does not initialize IRQ delivery.
4. The kernel reads CR0 caching-control state, CPU address widths, active `CR4.PCIDE`, and raw CR3. It decodes CR3's physical root address and low-bit meaning against those CPU properties, without dereferencing the root. It reads EFER.NXE only when CPUID reports NX, `IA32_PAT` only when CPUID reports PAT, and MTRR registers only when CPUID reports MTRR support; these reads do not change CPU state. The MTRR snapshot is bounded to 32 variable pairs and reports an explicit capacity-exceeded state without retaining partial registers. It copies the HHDM, executable-address, and memory-map responses into an owned `BootInfo` snapshot, validates pointers against the active linear width, derives and validates the linker-defined kernel image span and its page-aligned text/rodata/data segment spans from Limine's executable bases, and derives the protocol-guaranteed minimum initial-stack span from the captured entry `RSP`. It validates physical bounds, stack HHDM arithmetic/coverage, and page-rounded HHDM arithmetic for protocol-mapped memory types. It then builds a frame allocator only from validated usable ranges and rejects malformed metadata before starting the shell.
5. The kernel reports raw CR3 and its decoded physical root/low bits when the reported width permits, physical and virtual kernel-image spans, linker-defined text RX, rodata R/NX, and data RW/NX segment spans, minimum protocol-guaranteed stack span, validated memory ranges, frame counts, CPU features/address widths, NXE and normal-caching state, the active PAT value plus recognized WB/UC/WC indices, and a summary of captured MTRR state. It also reports whether the captured PAT/MTRR registers validate and a diagnostic effective type at physical address zero for PAT index 0; this is not a page-table inspection or a live mapping claim. It then seeds a volatile RAM filesystem and enters Crabshell on the serial console.
6. The shell busy-polls COM1 because no scheduler or UART interrupt handler exists yet. The kernel does not return to the loader.

The linker exports page-aligned virtual bounds for each of the kernel's three load segments. Boot validates their order, contiguity, coverage of the rounded image span, and derived physical ranges, then reports them with the permissions intended by `linker.ld`. Boot also decodes CR3's root physical address and active low-bit interpretation. A host-tested helper can validate that the root page is in bootloader-reclaimable memory and calculate its HHDM address. The opt-in `just frame-smoke` path reads the 512 root entries and follows bounded page-table paths for every page in the kernel image segments and minimum stack span, checking physical translations. It does not establish inherited permissions/cache correctness or alias safety. These are validated linker/boot metadata only: Rustix has not established that all live mappings match the ELF flags.

The memory-map snapshot stores physical regions as checked half-open ranges `[start, end)` and retains Limine's known classifications plus unknown type values. It does not authorize Rustix to access every region, reclaim loader memory, or mutate the current page tables. Rustix checks physical bounds and calculates canonical HHDM ranges for memory types covered by the requested base revision, but does not generally dereference physical memory through the HHDM or verify the inherited page tables. The opt-in `just frame-smoke` probe writes one allocator-issued frame contained in a validated `Usable` region and reads the inherited root page after checking that it is bootloader-reclaimable; both accesses rely on the Limine mapping contract after checked address arithmetic. It does not prove full live page-table coverage. These metadata checks cannot prove that a Limine-provided non-null pointer is readable; that remains an explicit trust assumption of the Limine handoff.

## Link and target configuration

- Rust target: `x86_64-unknown-none`
- Linker script: `linker.ld`
- Kernel virtual base: `0xffffffff80000000`
- Required code-generation constraints: kernel code model, static relocation, and disabled red zone
- Rust panic strategy: abort; the panic handler logs and halts

See [`../development/building.md`](../development/building.md) for commands and toolchain setup.

## Failure behavior and limitations

Missing responses, bad pointers/alignment, invalid HHDM values, invalid image or segment bounds, invalid initial-stack spans, excessive counts, null entries, address arithmetic overflow, and invalid or overlapping physical ranges reject the complete boot snapshot. `_start` halts before starting Crabshell rather than continuing with partial memory metadata. Structural checks cannot establish that a non-null loader pointer is mapped and readable; that remains an explicit trust assumption of the Limine handoff. The installed exception handlers print fatal context and halt; no fault recovery or maskable IRQ delivery is provided. COM1 writes use a bounded polling loop so a non-responsive UART does not block forever.

The repository includes a Limine v12.9.3 binary archive pin with SHA-256 verification, a hybrid ISO recipe, and a bounded QEMU serial smoke test that checks Crabshell's prompt. On 2026-10-16, `just verify` passed in WSL2 Ubuntu 24.04 on both the working tree and a clean detached worktree with an empty `target` directory; the clean run fetched and built the pinned Limine host utility, created the image, and QEMU reported boot metadata before reaching the prompt. Milestone 0's local exit criteria are met. Hosted CI has not been observed. There is still no framebuffer console, reboot/shutdown interface, or broader boot-protocol compatibility test. The available serial and keyboard drivers do not imply a general device model.

## Future boot work

The kernel now snapshots and validates the Limine map and preserves firmware and loader-reclaimable classifications without reclaiming them. No region is considered Rustix-owned or free for allocation yet. Loader-reclaimable memory must remain unavailable until Rustix has copied any needed boot data and explicitly reaches a documented reclaim point; ACPI reclaimable memory needs the ACPI tables to be copied or parsed first. Frame allocation, page-table replacement, and ownership transfer remain future work.

//! Pure validation for future x86_64 4 KiB mappings.
//!
//! This module validates address shape and permissions only. It does not prove
//! frame ownership or mapping coverage, access physical memory, or modify tables.

use crate::memory::{
    is_canonical_virtual_address, physical_range_fits_address_width, HhdmAddressError, MemoryMap,
    RegionKind,
};

/// Base page size supported by the initial Rustix mapping policy.
pub const PAGE_SIZE: u64 = 4096;

/// The physical root address and interpretation of CR3's low bits.
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct Cr3Root {
    physical_address: u64,
    low_bits: Cr3LowBits,
}

impl Cr3Root {
    pub const fn physical_address(self) -> u64 {
        self.physical_address
    }

    pub const fn low_bits(self) -> Cr3LowBits {
        self.low_bits
    }
}

/// CR3's low bits are either a PCID or the paging-structure cache controls.
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum Cr3LowBits {
    Pcid(u16),
    CacheControls {
        page_level_write_through: bool,
        page_level_cache_disable: bool,
    },
}

#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum Cr3Error {
    UnknownPhysicalAddressWidth,
    InvalidPhysicalAddressWidth,
    ReservedBits,
}

#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum Cr3RootAccessError {
    NotBootloaderReclaimable,
    Hhdm(HhdmAddressError),
}

/// Decode the currently active CR3 value without dereferencing its root table.
///
/// The caller supplies the reported physical-address width and whether CR4.PCIDE
/// is active, since those determine the valid address and low-bit encodings.
pub fn parse_cr3_root(
    raw: u64,
    physical_address_bits: Option<u8>,
    pcid_enabled: bool,
) -> Result<Cr3Root, Cr3Error> {
    let physical_address_bits =
        physical_address_bits.ok_or(Cr3Error::UnknownPhysicalAddressWidth)?;
    if !(12..=MAX_PTE_PHYSICAL_ADDRESS_BITS).contains(&physical_address_bits) {
        return Err(Cr3Error::InvalidPhysicalAddressWidth);
    }

    let physical_mask = ((1u64 << physical_address_bits) - 1) & !(PAGE_SIZE - 1);
    let low_mask = if pcid_enabled {
        PAGE_SIZE - 1
    } else {
        (1 << 3) | (1 << 4)
    };
    if raw & !(physical_mask | low_mask) != 0 {
        return Err(Cr3Error::ReservedBits);
    }

    let low_bits = if pcid_enabled {
        Cr3LowBits::Pcid((raw & (PAGE_SIZE - 1)) as u16)
    } else {
        Cr3LowBits::CacheControls {
            page_level_write_through: raw & (1 << 3) != 0,
            page_level_cache_disable: raw & (1 << 4) != 0,
        }
    };

    Ok(Cr3Root {
        physical_address: raw & physical_mask,
        low_bits,
    })
}

/// Calculate the protocol-backed HHDM address of Limine's inherited root page.
///
/// This requires the root page to be wholly contained in bootloader-reclaimable
/// memory, as specified for Limine page tables. It does not dereference the page
/// or prove that the active hierarchy contains the HHDM mapping.
pub fn inherited_cr3_root_hhdm_address(
    root: Cr3Root,
    memory_map: &MemoryMap,
    hhdm_offset: u64,
    physical_address_bits: Option<u8>,
    virtual_address_bits: u8,
) -> Result<u64, Cr3RootAccessError> {
    let physical_start = root.physical_address();
    let physical_end = physical_start
        .checked_add(PAGE_SIZE)
        .ok_or(Cr3RootAccessError::Hhdm(HhdmAddressError::AddressOverflow))?;
    if !memory_map.range_is_within_region_kind(
        physical_start,
        physical_end,
        RegionKind::BootloaderReclaimable,
    ) {
        return Err(Cr3RootAccessError::NotBootloaderReclaimable);
    }
    memory_map
        .limine_hhdm_address(
            hhdm_offset,
            physical_start,
            PAGE_SIZE,
            physical_address_bits,
            virtual_address_bits,
        )
        .map_err(Cr3RootAccessError::Hhdm)
}

#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum PageLevel {
    Pml5,
    Pml4,
    Pdpt,
    Pd,
    Pt,
}

#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct PageWalkConfig {
    pub levels: u8,
    pub physical_address_bits: u8,
    pub virtual_address_bits: u8,
    pub nx_enabled: bool,
    pub page_2m_supported: bool,
    pub page_1g_supported: bool,
}

#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct PageTranslation {

    pub leaf_physical_base: u64,
