mod arch;
mod boot;
mod shell;

use core::panic::PanicInfo;
use rustix_kernel::vfs::RamFs;

static mut RAM_FILESYSTEM: RamFs = RamFs::new();

macro_rules! kprintln {
    () => {{
        crate::arch::x86_64::serial::print(format_args!("\r\n"));
    }};
    ($($argument:tt)*) => {{
        crate::arch::x86_64::serial::print(format_args!($($argument)*));
        crate::arch::x86_64::serial::print(format_args!("\r\n"));
    }};
}

pub(crate) use kprintln;

#[cfg(feature = "probe-hhdm-frame")]
struct LimineHhdmPageTableReader<'a> {
    memory_map: &'a rustix_kernel::memory::MemoryMap,
    hhdm_offset: u64,
    physical_address_bits: u8,
    virtual_address_bits: u8,
}

#[cfg(feature = "probe-hhdm-frame")]
impl rustix_kernel::paging::PageTableReader for LimineHhdmPageTableReader<'_> {
    type Error = rustix_kernel::memory::HhdmAddressError;

    fn read_entry(&self, table_physical: u64, index: u16) -> Result<u64, Self::Error> {
        if index >= 512 {
            return Err(rustix_kernel::memory::HhdmAddressError::InvalidHhdmRange);
        }
        let table_end = table_physical
            .checked_add(rustix_kernel::paging::PAGE_SIZE)
            .ok_or(rustix_kernel::memory::HhdmAddressError::AddressOverflow)?;
        if !self.memory_map.range_is_within_region_kind(
            table_physical,
            table_end,
            rustix_kernel::memory::RegionKind::BootloaderReclaimable,
        ) {
            return Err(rustix_kernel::memory::HhdmAddressError::NotLimineMapped);
        }
        let table_address = self.memory_map.limine_hhdm_address(
            self.hhdm_offset,
            table_physical,
            rustix_kernel::paging::PAGE_SIZE,
            Some(self.physical_address_bits),
            self.virtual_address_bits,
        )?;
        let entry_address = table_address
            .checked_add(u64::from(index) * core::mem::size_of::<u64>() as u64)
            .ok_or(rustix_kernel::memory::HhdmAddressError::AddressOverflow)?;
        // SAFETY: The complete table page was restricted to bootloader-reclaimable
        // memory and its HHDM address arithmetic was checked. The reader relies
        // on the Limine base-revision-3 mapping contract and never returns a ref.
        Ok(unsafe { (entry_address as *const u64).read_volatile() })
    }
}

// Capture Limine's entry RSP before a Rust prologue changes it. The synthetic
// return slot is part of the SysV entry stack; realign before calling Rust.
core::arch::global_asm!(
    ".section .text",
    ".code64",
    ".global _start",
    ".type _start, @function",
    "_start:",
    "mov rdi, rsp",
    "and rsp, -16",
    "call rustix_start",
    "ud2",
    ".size _start, . - _start",
);

#[no_mangle]
pub extern "C" fn rustix_start(entry_rsp: u64) -> ! {
    arch::x86_64::serial::initialize();
    kprintln!("Rustix kernel: x86_64 Rust bootstrap");
    arch::x86_64::interrupts::initialize();
    kprintln!("x86_64 exception diagnostics: enabled (IRQs remain disabled)");
    #[cfg_attr(not(feature = "probe-hhdm-frame"), allow(unused_mut))]
    let mut boot_info = match boot::capture_boot_information(entry_rsp) {
        Ok(boot_info) => boot_info,
        Err(error) => {
            kprintln!("boot information rejected: {:?}", error);
            halt_forever();
        }
    };
    boot::report_boot_information(&boot_info);

    #[cfg(feature = "probe-hhdm-frame")]
    probe_hhdm_frame(&mut boot_info);

    #[cfg(any(feature = "inject-page-fault", feature = "inject-invalid-opcode"))]
    run_fault_injection();

    // SAFETY: Crabshell is the only owner of this filesystem. The bootstrap is
    // single-core and has no scheduler or filesystem-touching interrupt handlers.
    let filesystem = unsafe { &mut *core::ptr::addr_of_mut!(RAM_FILESYSTEM) };
    match filesystem.seed_defaults() {
        Ok(home) => shell::run(filesystem, home, &boot_info),
        Err(error) => {
            kprintln!("RAM filesystem initialization failed: {:?}", error);
            halt_forever()
        }
    }
}

#[cfg(feature = "probe-hhdm-frame")]
fn probe_hhdm_frame(boot_info: &mut boot::BootInfo) {
    use rustix_kernel::frame::FRAME_SIZE;

    let frame = match boot_info.frame_allocator.allocate() {
        Some(frame) => frame,
        None => {
            kprintln!("HHDM frame probe failed: no free frame");
            halt_forever();
        }
    };
    let hhdm_address = match frame.hhdm_address(
        &boot_info.memory_map,
        boot_info.hhdm_offset,
        boot_info.cpu_info.physical_address_bits,
        boot_info.cpu_info.active_linear_address_bits,
    ) {
        Ok(address) => address,
        Err(error) => {
            kprintln!("HHDM frame probe rejected frame translation: {:?}", error);
            release_probe_frame(&mut boot_info.frame_allocator, frame);
            halt_forever();
        }
    };

    let words = (FRAME_SIZE / core::mem::size_of::<u64>() as u64) as usize;
    let page = hhdm_address as *mut u64;
    let mut verified = true;
    // SAFETY: The non-copyable `Frame` token is held exclusively; its full page
    // is within validated `Usable` memory and its HHDM arithmetic was checked.
    // Limine base revision 3 guarantees usable memory in the HHDM, and no other
    // Rustix mapping aliases this newly allocated frame. This is an opt-in QEMU
    // probe; a broken loader mapping would fault and be caught by the fatal path.
    unsafe {
        for index in 0..words {
            page.add(index)
                .write_volatile(0xa5a5_0000_0000_0000 ^ index as u64);
        }
        for index in 0..words {
            if page.add(index).read_volatile() != (0xa5a5_0000_0000_0000 ^ index as u64) {
                verified = false;
                break;
            }
        }
        for index in 0..words {
            page.add(index).write_volatile(0);
        }
    }

    release_probe_frame(&mut boot_info.frame_allocator, frame);
    if !verified {
        kprintln!("HHDM frame probe failed: readback mismatch");
        halt_forever();
    }
    kprintln!("HHDM frame probe passed: wrote, read, cleared, and reclaimed one frame");
    probe_inherited_root(&boot_info);
}

#[cfg(feature = "probe-hhdm-frame")]
fn probe_inherited_root(boot_info: &boot::BootInfo) {
    use rustix_kernel::paging::inherited_cr3_root_hhdm_address;

    let root = match boot_info.inherited_cr3_root {
        Ok(root) => root,
        Err(error) => {
            kprintln!(
                "inherited root probe failed: CR3 decode rejected: {:?}",
                error
            );
            halt_forever();
        }
    };
    let address = match inherited_cr3_root_hhdm_address(
        root,
        &boot_info.memory_map,
        boot_info.hhdm_offset,
        boot_info.cpu_info.physical_address_bits,
        boot_info.cpu_info.active_linear_address_bits,
    ) {
        Ok(address) => address,
        Err(error) => {
            kprintln!(
                "inherited root probe failed: HHDM validation rejected: {:?}",
                error
            );
            halt_forever();
        }
    };
    let entries = address as *const u64;
    let mut present_entries = 0;
    // SAFETY: The complete root page was validated as bootloader-reclaimable
    // and its HHDM range arithmetic was checked. The Limine base-revision-3
    // contract maps that region; this read-only opt-in probe trusts that handoff.
    unsafe {
        for index in 0..512 {
            if entries.add(index).read_volatile() & 1 != 0 {
                present_entries += 1;
            }
        }
    }
    kprintln!(
        "inherited root HHDM probe passed: read 512 entries, {} present",
        present_entries
    );
    let physical_address_bits = match boot_info.cpu_info.physical_address_bits {
        Some(bits) => bits,
        None => {
            kprintln!("inherited page-table walk failed: physical width unknown");
            halt_forever();
        }
    };
    let reader = LimineHhdmPageTableReader {
        memory_map: &boot_info.memory_map,
        hhdm_offset: boot_info.hhdm_offset,
        physical_address_bits,
        virtual_address_bits: boot_info.cpu_info.active_linear_address_bits,
    };
    let config = rustix_kernel::paging::PageWalkConfig {
        levels: if boot_info.cpu_info.active_linear_address_bits == 57 {
            5
        } else {
            4
        },
        physical_address_bits,
        virtual_address_bits: boot_info.cpu_info.active_linear_address_bits,
        nx_enabled: boot_info.cpu_info.nx_enabled,
        page_2m_supported: true,
        page_1g_supported: boot_info.cpu_info.has_1g_pages,
    };
    let segments = boot_info.kernel_image_segments;
    verify_inherited_mapping(
        &reader,
        root,
        config,
        "kernel text",
        segments.text.virtual_start,
        segments.text.physical_start,
        segments.text.virtual_end - segments.text.virtual_start,
    );
    verify_inherited_mapping(
        &reader,
        root,
        config,
        "kernel rodata",
        segments.rodata.virtual_start,
        segments.rodata.physical_start,
        segments.rodata.virtual_end - segments.rodata.virtual_start,
    );
    verify_inherited_mapping(
        &reader,
        root,
        config,
        "kernel data",
        segments.data.virtual_start,
        segments.data.physical_start,
        segments.data.virtual_end - segments.data.virtual_start,
    );
    verify_inherited_mapping(
        &reader,
        root,
        config,
        "active boot stack",
        boot_info.boot_stack_virtual_start,
        boot_info.boot_stack_physical_start,
        boot_info.boot_stack_virtual_end - boot_info.boot_stack_virtual_start,
    );
}

#[cfg(feature = "probe-hhdm-frame")]
fn verify_inherited_mapping(
    reader: &impl rustix_kernel::paging::PageTableReader<
        Error = rustix_kernel::memory::HhdmAddressError,
    >,
    root: rustix_kernel::paging::Cr3Root,
    config: rustix_kernel::paging::PageWalkConfig,
    label: &str,
    virtual_start: u64,
    physical_start: u64,
    length: u64,
) {
    use rustix_kernel::paging::{walk_virtual_address, PageWalkOutcome};

    let mut offset = 0;
    let mut pages = 0;
    while offset < length {
        let virtual_address = match virtual_start.checked_add(offset) {
            Some(address) => address,
            None => {
                kprintln!("inherited mapping probe failed: {} virtual overflow", label);
                halt_forever();
            }
        };
        let expected_physical = match physical_start.checked_add(offset) {
            Some(address) => address,
            None => {
                kprintln!(
                    "inherited mapping probe failed: {} physical overflow",
                    label
                );
                halt_forever();
            }
        };
        let translation = match walk_virtual_address(reader, root, virtual_address, config) {
            Ok(PageWalkOutcome::Mapped(translation)) => translation,
            Ok(PageWalkOutcome::NotPresent { level }) => {
                kprintln!(
                    "inherited mapping probe failed: {} absent at {:?}",
                    label,
                    level
                );
                halt_forever();
            }
            Err(error) => {
                kprintln!("inherited mapping probe failed: {}: {:?}", label, error);
                halt_forever();
            }
        };
        if translation.physical_address != expected_physical {
            kprintln!(
                "inherited mapping probe failed: {} {:#018x} mapped to {:#018x}, expected {:#018x}",
                label,
                virtual_address,
                translation.physical_address,
                expected_physical
            );
            halt_forever();
        }
        pages += 1;
        offset += rustix_kernel::paging::PAGE_SIZE;
    }
    kprintln!(
        "inherited mapping probe passed: {} ({} pages)",
        label,
        pages
    );
}

#[cfg(feature = "probe-hhdm-frame")]
fn release_probe_frame(
    allocator: &mut rustix_kernel::frame::FrameAllocator,
    frame: rustix_kernel::frame::Frame,
) {
    if let Err(error) = allocator.deallocate(frame) {
        kprintln!(
            "HHDM frame probe failed to return its frame: {:?}",
            error.error
        );
        halt_forever();
    }
}

#[cfg(feature = "inject-page-fault")]
fn run_fault_injection() {
    kprintln!("fault injection: triggering page fault at 0x00000000deadbeef");
    // SAFETY: This is an opt-in QEMU test that deliberately reads an unmapped
    // low virtual address; the installed page-fault handler is expected to halt.
    unsafe {
        core::arch::asm!(
            "mov rax, 0xdeadbeef",
            "mov rax, qword ptr [rax]",
            out("rax") _,
            options(nostack)
        );
    }
    kprintln!("fault injection unexpectedly returned");
    halt_forever();
}

#[cfg(feature = "inject-invalid-opcode")]
fn run_fault_injection() {
    kprintln!("fault injection: triggering invalid opcode with ud2");
    // SAFETY: This is an opt-in QEMU test that deliberately raises #UD; the
    // installed invalid-opcode handler is expected to halt.
    unsafe { core::arch::asm!("ud2", options(nomem, nostack)) };
    kprintln!("fault injection unexpectedly returned");
    halt_forever();
}

#[panic_handler]
fn panic(info: &PanicInfo<'_>) -> ! {
    arch::x86_64::serial::initialize();
    kprintln!("KERNEL PANIC: {}", info);
    halt_forever()
}

fn halt_forever() -> ! {
    loop {
        // SAFETY: The bootstrap has no interrupt handlers or scheduler to resume.
        unsafe { core::arch::asm!("cli; hlt", options(nomem, nostack)) };
    }
}

macro_rules! kprintln {

    }};
    ($($argument:tt)*) => {{

#[cfg(feature = "probe-hhdm-frame")]
struct LimineHhdmPageTableReader<'a> {
    memory_map: &'a rustix_kernel::memory::MemoryMap,
    hhdm_offset: u64,
    physical_address_bits: u8,
    virtual_address_bits: u8,
}

#[cfg(feature = "probe-hhdm-frame")]
impl rustix_kernel::paging::PageTableReader for LimineHhdmPageTableReader<'_> {
    type Error = rustix_kernel::memory::HhdmAddressError;

    fn read_entry(&self, table_physical: u64, index: u16) -> Result<u64, Self::Error> {
        if index >= 512 {
            return Err(rustix_kernel::memory::HhdmAddressError::InvalidHhdmRange);
        }
        let table_end = table_physical
            .checked_add(rustix_kernel::paging::PAGE_SIZE)
            .ok_or(rustix_kernel::memory::HhdmAddressError::AddressOverflow)?;
        if !self.memory_map.range_is_within_region_kind(
            table_physical,
            table_end,
            rustix_kernel::memory::RegionKind::BootloaderReclaimable,
        ) {
            return Err(rustix_kernel::memory::HhdmAddressError::NotLimineMapped);
        }
        let table_address = self.memory_map.limine_hhdm_address(
            self.hhdm_offset,
            table_physical,
            rustix_kernel::paging::PAGE_SIZE,
            Some(self.physical_address_bits),
            self.virtual_address_bits,
        )?;
        let entry_address = table_address
            .checked_add(u64::from(index) * core::mem::size_of::<u64>() as u64)
            .ok_or(rustix_kernel::memory::HhdmAddressError::AddressOverflow)?;
        // SAFETY: The complete table page was restricted to bootloader-reclaimable
        // memory and its HHDM address arithmetic was checked. The reader relies
        // on the Limine base-revision-3 mapping contract and never returns a ref.
        Ok(unsafe { (entry_address as *const u64).read_volatile() })

    "call rustix_start",
    "ud2",
    ".size _start, . - _start",
);

#[no_mangle]
pub extern "C" fn rustix_start(entry_rsp: u64) -> ! {
    arch::x86_64::serial::initialize();
    kprintln!("Rustix kernel: x86_64 Rust bootstrap");
    arch::x86_64::interrupts::initialize();
    kprintln!("x86_64 exception diagnostics: enabled (IRQs remain disabled)");
    #[cfg_attr(not(feature = "probe-hhdm-frame"), allow(unused_mut))]
    let mut boot_info = match boot::capture_boot_information(entry_rsp) {
        Ok(boot_info) => boot_info,
        Err(error) => {
            kprintln!("boot information rejected: {:?}", error);
            halt_forever();
        }
    };
    boot::report_boot_information(&boot_info);

    #[cfg(feature = "probe-hhdm-frame")]
    probe_hhdm_frame(&mut boot_info);

    #[cfg(any(feature = "inject-page-fault", feature = "inject-invalid-opcode"))]
    run_fault_injection();

    // SAFETY: Crabshell is the only owner of this filesystem. The bootstrap is
    // single-core and has no scheduler or filesystem-touching interrupt handlers.
    let filesystem = unsafe { &mut *core::ptr::addr_of_mut!(RAM_FILESYSTEM) };
    match filesystem.seed_defaults() {
        Ok(home) => shell::run(filesystem, home, &boot_info),
        Err(error) => {
            kprintln!("RAM filesystem initialization failed: {:?}", error);
            halt_forever()
        }
    }
}

    let mut first_translation = None;
    let mut permissions_uniform = true;
    let mut pat_index_uniform = true;
    while offset < length {
        let virtual_address = match virtual_start.checked_add(offset) {
            Some(address) => address,
            None => {
                kprintln!("inherited mapping probe failed: {} virtual overflow", label);
                halt_forever();
            }
        };
        let expected_physical = match physical_start.checked_add(offset) {
            Some(address) => address,
            None => {
                kprintln!(
                    "inherited mapping probe failed: {} physical overflow",
                    label
                );
                halt_forever();
            }
        };
        let translation = match walk_virtual_address(reader, root, virtual_address, config) {
            Ok(PageWalkOutcome::Mapped(translation)) => translation,
            Ok(PageWalkOutcome::NotPresent { level }) => {
                kprintln!(
                    "inherited mapping probe failed: {} absent at {:?}",
                    label,
                    level
                );
                halt_forever();
            }
            Err(error) => {
                kprintln!("inherited mapping probe failed: {}: {:?}", label, error);
                halt_forever();
            }
        };
        if translation.physical_address != expected_physical {
            kprintln!(
                "inherited mapping probe failed: {} {:#018x} mapped to {:#018x}, expected {:#018x}",
                label,
                virtual_address,
                translation.physical_address,
                expected_physical
            );
            halt_forever();
        }
        if let Some(first) = first_translation {
            permissions_uniform &= translation.permissions == first.permissions;
            pat_index_uniform &= translation.pat_index == first.pat_index;
        } else {
            first_translation = Some(translation);
        }
        pages += 1;
        offset += rustix_kernel::paging::PAGE_SIZE;
    }
    if let Some(first) = first_translation {
        kprintln!(
            "inherited mapping probe passed: {} ({} pages), first permissions={:?}, PAT index={}, leaf size={}, uniform permissions={}, uniform PAT index={}",
            label,
            pages,
            first.permissions,
            first.pat_index,
            first.page_size,
            permissions_uniform,
            pat_index_uniform
        );
    }
}

#[cfg(feature = "probe-hhdm-frame")]
fn release_probe_frame(
    allocator: &mut rustix_kernel::frame::FrameAllocator,
    frame: rustix_kernel::frame::Frame,
) {
    if let Err(error) = allocator.deallocate(frame) {
        kprintln!(
            "HHDM frame probe failed to return its frame: {:?}",
            error.error
        );
        halt_forever();
    }
}

#[cfg(feature = "inject-page-fault")]
fn run_fault_injection() {
    kprintln!("fault injection: triggering page fault at 0x00000000deadbeef");
    // SAFETY: This is an opt-in QEMU test that deliberately reads an unmapped
    // low virtual address; the installed page-fault handler is expected to halt.
    unsafe {
        core::arch::asm!(
            "mov rax, 0xdeadbeef",
            "mov rax, qword ptr [rax]",
            out("rax") _,
            options(nostack)
        );

    halt_forever();
}

#[cfg(feature = "inject-invalid-opcode")]
fn run_fault_injection() {
    kprintln!("fault injection: triggering invalid opcode with ud2");
    // SAFETY: This is an opt-in QEMU test that deliberately raises #UD; the

    unsafe { core::arch::asm!("ud2", options(nomem, nostack)) };

    halt_forever();
}

#[panic_handler]
fn panic(info: &PanicInfo<'_>) -> ! {
    arch::x86_64::serial::initialize();
    kprintln!("KERNEL PANIC: {}", info);
    halt_forever()
}

fn halt_forever() -> ! {
    loop {
        // SAFETY: The bootstrap has no interrupt handlers or scheduler to resume.
        unsafe { core::arch::asm!("cli; hlt", options(nomem, nostack)) };
    }
}

struct LimineHhdmPageTableReader<'a> {
    memory_map: &'a rustix_kernel::memory::MemoryMap,
    hhdm_offset: u64,
    physical_address_bits: u8,
    virtual_address_bits: u8,
}

#[cfg(feature = "probe-hhdm-frame")]
impl rustix_kernel::paging::PageTableReader for LimineHhdmPageTableReader<'_> {
    type Error = rustix_kernel::memory::HhdmAddressError;

    fn read_entry(&self, table_physical: u64, index: u16) -> Result<u64, Self::Error> {
        if index >= 512 {
            return Err(rustix_kernel::memory::HhdmAddressError::InvalidHhdmRange);
        }
        let table_end = table_physical
            .checked_add(rustix_kernel::paging::PAGE_SIZE)
            .ok_or(rustix_kernel::memory::HhdmAddressError::AddressOverflow)?;
        if !self.memory_map.range_is_within_region_kind(
            table_physical,
            table_end,
            rustix_kernel::memory::RegionKind::BootloaderReclaimable,
        ) {
            return Err(rustix_kernel::memory::HhdmAddressError::NotLimineMapped);
        }
        let table_address = self.memory_map.limine_hhdm_address(
            self.hhdm_offset,
            table_physical,
            rustix_kernel::paging::PAGE_SIZE,
            Some(self.physical_address_bits),
            self.virtual_address_bits,
        )?;
        let entry_address = table_address
            .checked_add(u64::from(index) * core::mem::size_of::<u64>() as u64)
            .ok_or(rustix_kernel::memory::HhdmAddressError::AddressOverflow)?;
        // SAFETY: The complete table page was restricted to bootloader-reclaimable
        // memory and its HHDM address arithmetic was checked. The reader relies
        // on the Limine base-revision-3 mapping contract and never returns a ref.
        Ok(unsafe { (entry_address as *const u64).read_volatile() })
    }
}

    "call rustix_start",
    "ud2",
    ".size _start, . - _start",
);

#[no_mangle]
pub extern "C" fn rustix_start(entry_rsp: u64) -> ! {
    arch::x86_64::serial::initialize();
    kprintln!("Rustix kernel: x86_64 Rust bootstrap");
    arch::x86_64::interrupts::initialize();
    kprintln!("x86_64 exception diagnostics: enabled (IRQs remain disabled)");
    #[cfg_attr(not(feature = "probe-hhdm-frame"), allow(unused_mut))]
    let mut boot_info = match boot::capture_boot_information(entry_rsp) {
        Ok(boot_info) => boot_info,
        Err(error) => {
            kprintln!("boot information rejected: {:?}", error);
            halt_forever();
        }
    };
    boot::report_boot_information(&boot_info);

    #[cfg(feature = "probe-hhdm-frame")]
    probe_hhdm_frame(&mut boot_info);

    #[cfg(any(feature = "inject-page-fault", feature = "inject-invalid-opcode"))]
    run_fault_injection();

    // SAFETY: Crabshell is the only owner of this filesystem. The bootstrap is
    // single-core and has no scheduler or filesystem-touching interrupt handlers.
    let filesystem = unsafe { &mut *core::ptr::addr_of_mut!(RAM_FILESYSTEM) };
    match filesystem.seed_defaults() {
        Ok(home) => shell::run(filesystem, home, &boot_info),
        Err(error) => {
            kprintln!("RAM filesystem initialization failed: {:?}", error);
            halt_forever()
        }
    }
}

#[cfg(feature = "probe-hhdm-frame")]
fn probe_hhdm_frame(boot_info: &mut boot::BootInfo) {
    use rustix_kernel::frame::FRAME_SIZE;

    let frame = match boot_info.frame_allocator.allocate() {
        Some(frame) => frame,
        None => {
            kprintln!("HHDM frame probe failed: no free frame");
            halt_forever();
        }
    };
    let hhdm_address = match frame.hhdm_address(
        &boot_info.memory_map,
        boot_info.hhdm_offset,
        boot_info.cpu_info.physical_address_bits,
        boot_info.cpu_info.active_linear_address_bits,
    ) {
        Ok(address) => address,
        Err(error) => {
            kprintln!("HHDM frame probe rejected frame translation: {:?}", error);
            release_probe_frame(&mut boot_info.frame_allocator, frame);
            halt_forever();
        }
    };

    let words = (FRAME_SIZE / core::mem::size_of::<u64>() as u64) as usize;
    let page = hhdm_address as *mut u64;
    let mut verified = true;
    // SAFETY: The non-copyable `Frame` token is held exclusively; its full page
    // is within validated `Usable` memory and its HHDM arithmetic was checked.
    // Limine base revision 3 guarantees usable memory in the HHDM, and no other
    // Rustix mapping aliases this newly allocated frame. This is an opt-in QEMU
    // probe; a broken loader mapping would fault and be caught by the fatal path.
    unsafe {
        for index in 0..words {
            page.add(index)
                .write_volatile(0xa5a5_0000_0000_0000 ^ index as u64);
        }
        for index in 0..words {
            if page.add(index).read_volatile() != (0xa5a5_0000_0000_0000 ^ index as u64) {
                verified = false;
                break;
            }
        }
        for index in 0..words {
            page.add(index).write_volatile(0);
        }
    }

    release_probe_frame(&mut boot_info.frame_allocator, frame);
    if !verified {
        kprintln!("HHDM frame probe failed: readback mismatch");
        halt_forever();
    }
    kprintln!("HHDM frame probe passed: wrote, read, cleared, and reclaimed one frame");
    probe_inherited_root(&boot_info);
}

#[cfg(feature = "probe-hhdm-frame")]
fn probe_inherited_root(boot_info: &boot::BootInfo) {
    use rustix_kernel::paging::inherited_cr3_root_hhdm_address;

    let root = match boot_info.inherited_cr3_root {
        Ok(root) => root,
        Err(error) => {
            kprintln!(
                "inherited root probe failed: CR3 decode rejected: {:?}",
                error
            );
            halt_forever();
        }
    };
    let address = match inherited_cr3_root_hhdm_address(
        root,
        &boot_info.memory_map,
        boot_info.hhdm_offset,
        boot_info.cpu_info.physical_address_bits,
        boot_info.cpu_info.active_linear_address_bits,
    ) {
        Ok(address) => address,
        Err(error) => {
            kprintln!(
                "inherited root probe failed: HHDM validation rejected: {:?}",
                error
            );
            halt_forever();
        }
    };
    let entries = address as *const u64;
    let mut present_entries = 0;
    // SAFETY: The complete root page was validated as bootloader-reclaimable
    // and its HHDM range arithmetic was checked. The Limine base-revision-3
    // contract maps that region; this read-only opt-in probe trusts that handoff.
    unsafe {
        for index in 0..512 {
            if entries.add(index).read_volatile() & 1 != 0 {
                present_entries += 1;
            }
        }
    }
    kprintln!(
        "inherited root HHDM probe passed: read 512 entries, {} present",
        present_entries
    );
    let physical_address_bits = match boot_info.cpu_info.physical_address_bits {
        Some(bits) => bits,
        None => {
            kprintln!("inherited page-table walk failed: physical width unknown");
            halt_forever();
        }
    };
    let reader = LimineHhdmPageTableReader {
        memory_map: &boot_info.memory_map,
        hhdm_offset: boot_info.hhdm_offset,
        physical_address_bits,
        virtual_address_bits: boot_info.cpu_info.active_linear_address_bits,
    };
    let config = rustix_kernel::paging::PageWalkConfig {
        levels: if boot_info.cpu_info.active_linear_address_bits == 57 {
            5
        } else {
            4
        },
        physical_address_bits,
        virtual_address_bits: boot_info.cpu_info.active_linear_address_bits,
        nx_enabled: boot_info.cpu_info.nx_enabled,
        page_2m_supported: true,
        page_1g_supported: boot_info.cpu_info.has_1g_pages,
    };
    let segments = boot_info.kernel_image_segments;
    verify_inherited_mapping(
        &reader,
        root,
        config,
        "kernel text",
        segments.text.virtual_start,
        segments.text.physical_start,
        segments.text.virtual_end - segments.text.virtual_start,
    );
    verify_inherited_mapping(
        &reader,
        root,
        config,
        "kernel rodata",
        segments.rodata.virtual_start,
        segments.rodata.physical_start,
        segments.rodata.virtual_end - segments.rodata.virtual_start,
    );
    verify_inherited_mapping(
        &reader,
        root,
        config,
        "kernel data",
        segments.data.virtual_start,
        segments.data.physical_start,
        segments.data.virtual_end - segments.data.virtual_start,
    );
    verify_inherited_mapping(
        &reader,
        root,
        config,
        "active boot stack",
        boot_info.boot_stack_virtual_start,
        boot_info.boot_stack_physical_start,
        boot_info.boot_stack_virtual_end - boot_info.boot_stack_virtual_start,
    );
}

    }

macro_rules! kprintln {
    () => {{
        crate::arch::x86_64::serial::print(format_args!("\r\n"));
    }};
    ($($argument:tt)*) => {{
        crate::arch::x86_64::serial::print(format_args!($($argument)*));

#[cfg(feature = "probe-hhdm-frame")]
struct LimineHhdmPageTableReader<'a> {
    memory_map: &'a rustix_kernel::memory::MemoryMap,
    hhdm_offset: u64,
    physical_address_bits: u8,
    virtual_address_bits: u8,
}

#[cfg(feature = "probe-hhdm-frame")]
impl rustix_kernel::paging::PageTableReader for LimineHhdmPageTableReader<'_> {
    type Error = rustix_kernel::memory::HhdmAddressError;

    fn read_entry(&self, table_physical: u64, index: u16) -> Result<u64, Self::Error> {
        if index >= 512 {
            return Err(rustix_kernel::memory::HhdmAddressError::InvalidHhdmRange);
        }
        let table_end = table_physical
            .checked_add(rustix_kernel::paging::PAGE_SIZE)
            .ok_or(rustix_kernel::memory::HhdmAddressError::AddressOverflow)?;
        if !self.memory_map.range_is_within_region_kind(
            table_physical,
            table_end,
            rustix_kernel::memory::RegionKind::BootloaderReclaimable,
        ) {
            return Err(rustix_kernel::memory::HhdmAddressError::NotLimineMapped);
        }
        let table_address = self.memory_map.limine_hhdm_address(
            self.hhdm_offset,
            table_physical,
            rustix_kernel::paging::PAGE_SIZE,
            Some(self.physical_address_bits),
            self.virtual_address_bits,
        )?;
        let entry_address = table_address
            .checked_add(u64::from(index) * core::mem::size_of::<u64>() as u64)
            .ok_or(rustix_kernel::memory::HhdmAddressError::AddressOverflow)?;
        // SAFETY: The complete table page was restricted to bootloader-reclaimable
        // memory and its HHDM address arithmetic was checked. The reader relies
        // on the Limine base-revision-3 mapping contract and never returns a ref.
        Ok(unsafe { (entry_address as *const u64).read_volatile() })
    }
}

// Capture Limine's entry RSP before a Rust prologue changes it. The synthetic
// return slot is part of the SysV entry stack; realign before calling Rust.
core::arch::global_asm!(
    ".section .text",
    ".code64",
    ".global _start",
    ".type _start, @function",
    "_start:",
    "mov rdi, rsp",
    "and rsp, -16",
    "call rustix_start",
    "ud2",
    ".size _start, . - _start",
);

#[no_mangle]
pub extern "C" fn rustix_start(entry_rsp: u64) -> ! {
    arch::x86_64::serial::initialize();
    kprintln!("Rustix kernel: x86_64 Rust bootstrap");
    arch::x86_64::interrupts::initialize();
    kprintln!("x86_64 exception diagnostics: enabled (IRQs remain disabled)");
    #[cfg_attr(not(feature = "probe-hhdm-frame"), allow(unused_mut))]
    let mut boot_info = match boot::capture_boot_information(entry_rsp) {
        Ok(boot_info) => boot_info,
        Err(error) => {
            kprintln!("boot information rejected: {:?}", error);
            halt_forever();
        }
    };
    boot::report_boot_information(&boot_info);

    #[cfg(feature = "probe-hhdm-frame")]
    probe_hhdm_frame(&mut boot_info);

    #[cfg(any(feature = "inject-page-fault", feature = "inject-invalid-opcode"))]
    run_fault_injection();

    // SAFETY: Crabshell is the only owner of this filesystem. The bootstrap is
    // single-core and has no scheduler or filesystem-touching interrupt handlers.
    let filesystem = unsafe { &mut *core::ptr::addr_of_mut!(RAM_FILESYSTEM) };
    match filesystem.seed_defaults() {
        Ok(home) => shell::run(filesystem, home, &boot_info),
        Err(error) => {
            kprintln!("RAM filesystem initialization failed: {:?}", error);
            halt_forever()
        }
    }
}

#[cfg(feature = "probe-hhdm-frame")]
fn probe_hhdm_frame(boot_info: &mut boot::BootInfo) {
    use rustix_kernel::frame::FRAME_SIZE;

    let frame = match boot_info.frame_allocator.allocate() {
        Some(frame) => frame,
        None => {
            kprintln!("HHDM frame probe failed: no free frame");
            halt_forever();
        }
    };
    let hhdm_address = match frame.hhdm_address(
        &boot_info.memory_map,
        boot_info.hhdm_offset,
        boot_info.cpu_info.physical_address_bits,
        boot_info.cpu_info.active_linear_address_bits,
    ) {
        Ok(address) => address,
        Err(error) => {
            kprintln!("HHDM frame probe rejected frame translation: {:?}", error);
            release_probe_frame(&mut boot_info.frame_allocator, frame);
            halt_forever();
        }
    };

    let words = (FRAME_SIZE / core::mem::size_of::<u64>() as u64) as usize;
    let page = hhdm_address as *mut u64;
    let mut verified = true;
    // SAFETY: The non-copyable `Frame` token is held exclusively; its full page
    // is within validated `Usable` memory and its HHDM arithmetic was checked.
    // Limine base revision 3 guarantees usable memory in the HHDM, and no other
    // Rustix mapping aliases this newly allocated frame. This is an opt-in QEMU
    // probe; a broken loader mapping would fault and be caught by the fatal path.
    unsafe {
        for index in 0..words {
            page.add(index)
                .write_volatile(0xa5a5_0000_0000_0000 ^ index as u64);
        }
        for index in 0..words {
            if page.add(index).read_volatile() != (0xa5a5_0000_0000_0000 ^ index as u64) {
                verified = false;
                break;
            }
        }
        for index in 0..words {
            page.add(index).write_volatile(0);
        }
    }

    release_probe_frame(&mut boot_info.frame_allocator, frame);
    if !verified {
        kprintln!("HHDM frame probe failed: readback mismatch");
        halt_forever();
    }
    kprintln!("HHDM frame probe passed: wrote, read, cleared, and reclaimed one frame");
    probe_inherited_root(&boot_info);
}

#[cfg(feature = "probe-hhdm-frame")]
fn probe_inherited_root(boot_info: &boot::BootInfo) {
    use rustix_kernel::paging::inherited_cr3_root_hhdm_address;

    let root = match boot_info.inherited_cr3_root {
        Ok(root) => root,
        Err(error) => {
            kprintln!(
                "inherited root probe failed: CR3 decode rejected: {:?}",
                error
            );
            halt_forever();
        }
    };
    let address = match inherited_cr3_root_hhdm_address(
        root,
        &boot_info.memory_map,
        boot_info.hhdm_offset,
        boot_info.cpu_info.physical_address_bits,
        boot_info.cpu_info.active_linear_address_bits,
    ) {
        Ok(address) => address,
        Err(error) => {
            kprintln!(
                "inherited root probe failed: HHDM validation rejected: {:?}",
                error
            );
            halt_forever();
        }
    };
    let entries = address as *const u64;
    let mut present_entries = 0;
    // SAFETY: The complete root page was validated as bootloader-reclaimable
    // and its HHDM range arithmetic was checked. The Limine base-revision-3
    // contract maps that region; this read-only opt-in probe trusts that handoff.
    unsafe {
        for index in 0..512 {
            if entries.add(index).read_volatile() & 1 != 0 {
                present_entries += 1;
            }
        }
    }
    kprintln!(
        "inherited root HHDM probe passed: read 512 entries, {} present",
        present_entries
    );
    let physical_address_bits = match boot_info.cpu_info.physical_address_bits {
        Some(bits) => bits,
        None => {
            kprintln!("inherited page-table walk failed: physical width unknown");
            halt_forever();
        }
    };
    let reader = LimineHhdmPageTableReader {
        memory_map: &boot_info.memory_map,
        hhdm_offset: boot_info.hhdm_offset,
        physical_address_bits,
        virtual_address_bits: boot_info.cpu_info.active_linear_address_bits,
    };
    let config = rustix_kernel::paging::PageWalkConfig {
        levels: if boot_info.cpu_info.active_linear_address_bits == 57 {
            5
        } else {
            4
        },
        physical_address_bits,
        virtual_address_bits: boot_info.cpu_info.active_linear_address_bits,
        nx_enabled: boot_info.cpu_info.nx_enabled,
        page_2m_supported: true,
        page_1g_supported: boot_info.cpu_info.has_1g_pages,
    };
    let segments = boot_info.kernel_image_segments;
    verify_inherited_mapping(
        &reader,
        root,
        config,
        "kernel text",
        segments.text.virtual_start,
        segments.text.physical_start,
        segments.text.virtual_end - segments.text.virtual_start,
    );
    verify_inherited_mapping(
        &reader,
        root,
        config,
        "kernel rodata",
        segments.rodata.virtual_start,
        segments.rodata.physical_start,
        segments.rodata.virtual_end - segments.rodata.virtual_start,
    );
    verify_inherited_mapping(
        &reader,
        root,
        config,
        "kernel data",
        segments.data.virtual_start,
        segments.data.physical_start,
        segments.data.virtual_end - segments.data.virtual_start,
    );
    verify_inherited_mapping(
        &reader,
        root,
        config,
        "active boot stack",
        boot_info.boot_stack_virtual_start,
        boot_info.boot_stack_physical_start,
        boot_info.boot_stack_virtual_end - boot_info.boot_stack_virtual_start,
    );

    let pat_value = match boot_info.cpu_info.pat_msr_value {
        Some(value) => value,
        None => {
            kprintln!("cache-alias probe failed: active PAT value unavailable");
            halt_forever();
        }
    };
    let pat = match rustix_kernel::paging::PatLayout::from_msr_value(pat_value) {
        Ok(pat) => pat,
        Err(error) => {
            kprintln!("cache-alias probe failed: invalid PAT layout: {:?}", error);
            halt_forever();
        }
    };
    let registers = match &boot_info.cpu_info.mtrr {
        rustix_kernel::paging::MtrrState::Captured(registers) => registers,
        _ => {
            kprintln!("cache-alias probe failed: captured MTRR state unavailable");
            halt_forever();
        }
    };
    let mtrrs = match registers.validated_layout(physical_address_bits) {
        Ok(mtrrs) => mtrrs,
        Err(error) => {
            kprintln!("cache-alias probe failed: invalid MTRR state: {:?}", error);
            halt_forever();
        }
    };
    if !boot_info.cpu_info.normal_caching {
        kprintln!("cache-alias probe failed: non-normal CR0 caching mode");
        halt_forever();
    }
    verify_kernel_cache_aliases(
        boot_info,
        &reader,
        root,
        config,
        pat,
        &mtrrs,
        "kernel text",
        segments.text.virtual_start,
        segments.text.physical_start,
        segments.text.virtual_end - segments.text.virtual_start,
    );
    verify_kernel_cache_aliases(
        boot_info,
        &reader,
        root,
        config,
        pat,
        &mtrrs,
        "kernel rodata",
        segments.rodata.virtual_start,
        segments.rodata.physical_start,
        segments.rodata.virtual_end - segments.rodata.virtual_start,
    );
    verify_kernel_cache_aliases(
        boot_info,
        &reader,
        root,
        config,
        pat,
        &mtrrs,
        "kernel data",
        segments.data.virtual_start,
        segments.data.physical_start,
        segments.data.virtual_end - segments.data.virtual_start,
    );
}

#[cfg(feature = "probe-hhdm-frame")]
fn verify_inherited_mapping(
    reader: &impl rustix_kernel::paging::PageTableReader<
        Error = rustix_kernel::memory::HhdmAddressError,
    >,
    root: rustix_kernel::paging::Cr3Root,
    config: rustix_kernel::paging::PageWalkConfig,
    label: &str,
    virtual_start: u64,
    physical_start: u64,
    length: u64,
) {
    use rustix_kernel::paging::{walk_virtual_address, PageWalkOutcome};

    let mut offset = 0;
    let mut pages = 0;
    let mut first_translation: Option<rustix_kernel::paging::PageTranslation> = None;
    let mut permissions_uniform = true;
    let mut pat_index_uniform = true;
    while offset < length {
        let virtual_address = match virtual_start.checked_add(offset) {
            Some(address) => address,
            None => {
                kprintln!("inherited mapping probe failed: {} virtual overflow", label);
                halt_forever();
            }
        };
        let expected_physical = match physical_start.checked_add(offset) {
            Some(address) => address,
            None => {
                kprintln!(
                    "inherited mapping probe failed: {} physical overflow",
                    label
                );
                halt_forever();
            }
        };
        let translation = match walk_virtual_address(reader, root, virtual_address, config) {
            Ok(PageWalkOutcome::Mapped(translation)) => translation,
            Ok(PageWalkOutcome::NotPresent { level }) => {
                kprintln!(
                    "inherited mapping probe failed: {} absent at {:?}",
                    label,
                    level
                );
                halt_forever();
            }
            Err(error) => {
                kprintln!("inherited mapping probe failed: {}: {:?}", label, error);
                halt_forever();
            }
        };
        if translation.physical_address != expected_physical {
            kprintln!(
                "inherited mapping probe failed: {} {:#018x} mapped to {:#018x}, expected {:#018x}",
                label,
                virtual_address,
                translation.physical_address,
                expected_physical
            );
            halt_forever();
        }
        if let Some(first) = first_translation {
            permissions_uniform &= translation.permissions == first.permissions;
            pat_index_uniform &= translation.pat_index == first.pat_index;
        } else {
            first_translation = Some(translation);
        }
        pages += 1;
        offset += rustix_kernel::paging::PAGE_SIZE;
    }
    if let Some(first) = first_translation {
        kprintln!(
            "inherited mapping probe passed: {} ({} pages), first permissions={:?}, PAT index={}, leaf size={}, uniform permissions={}, uniform PAT index={}",
            label,
            pages,
            first.permissions,
            first.pat_index,
            first.page_size,
            permissions_uniform,
            pat_index_uniform
        );
    }
}

#[cfg(feature = "probe-hhdm-frame")]
fn verify_kernel_cache_aliases(
    boot_info: &boot::BootInfo,
    reader: &impl rustix_kernel::paging::PageTableReader<
        Error = rustix_kernel::memory::HhdmAddressError,
    >,
    root: rustix_kernel::paging::Cr3Root,
    config: rustix_kernel::paging::PageWalkConfig,
    pat: rustix_kernel::paging::PatLayout,
    mtrrs: &rustix_kernel::paging::ValidatedMtrrLayout,
    label: &str,
    kernel_virtual_start: u64,
    physical_start: u64,
    length: u64,
) {
    use rustix_kernel::paging::{walk_virtual_address, PageWalkOutcome};

    let mut offset = 0;
    let mut pages = 0;
    while offset < length {
        let physical = match physical_start.checked_add(offset) {
            Some(address) => address,
            None => {
                kprintln!("cache-alias probe failed: {} physical overflow", label);
                halt_forever();
            }
        };
        let kernel_virtual = match kernel_virtual_start.checked_add(offset) {
            Some(address) => address,
            None => {
                kprintln!("cache-alias probe failed: {} virtual overflow", label);
                halt_forever();
            }
        };
        let hhdm_virtual = match boot_info.memory_map.limine_hhdm_address(
            boot_info.hhdm_offset,
            physical,
            rustix_kernel::paging::PAGE_SIZE,
            boot_info.cpu_info.physical_address_bits,
            boot_info.cpu_info.active_linear_address_bits,
        ) {
            Ok(address) => address,
            Err(error) => {
                kprintln!("cache-alias probe failed: {} HHDM range: {:?}", label, error);
                halt_forever();
            }
        };
        let kernel_translation = match walk_virtual_address(reader, root, kernel_virtual, config) {
            Ok(PageWalkOutcome::Mapped(translation)) => translation,
            result => {
                kprintln!("cache-alias probe failed: {} kernel walk: {:?}", label, result);
                halt_forever();
            }
        };
        let hhdm_translation = match walk_virtual_address(reader, root, hhdm_virtual, config) {
            Ok(PageWalkOutcome::Mapped(translation)) => translation,
            result => {
                kprintln!("cache-alias probe failed: {} HHDM walk: {:?}", label, result);
                halt_forever();
            }
        };
        if kernel_translation.physical_address != physical
            || hhdm_translation.physical_address != physical
        {
            kprintln!(
                "cache-alias probe failed: {} physical {:#018x} has inconsistent translations",
                label,
                physical
            );
            halt_forever();
        }
        let kernel_type = match mtrrs.effective_memory_type_for(
            physical,
            pat,
            kernel_translation.pat_index,
            boot_info.cpu_info.normal_caching,
        ) {
            Ok(memory_type) => memory_type,
            Err(error) => {
                kprintln!("cache-alias probe failed: {} kernel PAT/MTRR: {:?}", label, error);
                halt_forever();
            }
        };
        let hhdm_type = match mtrrs.effective_memory_type_for(
            physical,
            pat,
            hhdm_translation.pat_index,
            boot_info.cpu_info.normal_caching,
        ) {
            Ok(memory_type) => memory_type,
            Err(error) => {
                kprintln!("cache-alias probe failed: {} HHDM PAT/MTRR: {:?}", label, error);
                halt_forever();
            }
        };
        if kernel_type != hhdm_type {
            kprintln!(
                "cache-alias conflict: {} PA {:#018x}, kernel {:?} vs HHDM {:?}",
                label,
                physical,
                kernel_type,
                hhdm_type
            );
            halt_forever();
        }
        pages += 1;
        offset += rustix_kernel::paging::PAGE_SIZE;
    }
    kprintln!("cache-alias probe passed: {} ({} pages; effective types match)", label, pages);
}

#[cfg(feature = "probe-hhdm-frame")]
fn release_probe_frame(
    allocator: &mut rustix_kernel::frame::FrameAllocator,
    frame: rustix_kernel::frame::Frame,
) {
    if let Err(error) = allocator.deallocate(frame) {
        kprintln!(
            "HHDM frame probe failed to return its frame: {:?}",
            error.error
        );
        halt_forever();
    }
}

#[cfg(feature = "inject-page-fault")]
fn run_fault_injection() {
    kprintln!("fault injection: triggering page fault at 0x00000000deadbeef");
    // SAFETY: This is an opt-in QEMU test that deliberately reads an unmapped
    // low virtual address; the installed page-fault handler is expected to halt.
    unsafe {
        core::arch::asm!(
            "mov rax, 0xdeadbeef",
            "mov rax, qword ptr [rax]",
            out("rax") _,
            options(nostack)
        );
    }
    kprintln!("fault injection unexpectedly returned");
    halt_forever();
}

#[cfg(feature = "inject-invalid-opcode")]
fn run_fault_injection() {
    kprintln!("fault injection: triggering invalid opcode with ud2");
    // SAFETY: This is an opt-in QEMU test that deliberately raises #UD; the
    // installed invalid-opcode handler is expected to halt.
    unsafe { core::arch::asm!("ud2", options(nomem, nostack)) };
    kprintln!("fault injection unexpectedly returned");
    halt_forever();
}

#[panic_handler]
fn panic(info: &PanicInfo<'_>) -> ! {
    arch::x86_64::serial::initialize();
    kprintln!("KERNEL PANIC: {}", info);
    halt_forever()
}

fn halt_forever() -> ! {
    loop {
        // SAFETY: The bootstrap has no interrupt handlers or scheduler to resume.
        unsafe { core::arch::asm!("cli; hlt", options(nomem, nostack)) };
    }
}

## Goal
Continue Rustix Milestone 2 until its exit criteria are met: owned and validated page-table state, tested mapping/frame ownership and rollback invariants, a documented heap, diagnosable faults, and emulator validation. Do not switch CR3 until a reviewed preservation, ownership, permission/cache, and TLB proof is in place.

## State
- The user’s working tree had many pre-existing uncommitted changes. Preserve them; do not reset, commit, or create branches.
- Added a checked HHDM-address calculation for allocator-issued frames in validated `Usable` regions, plus validation for the inherited CR3 root’s `BootloaderReclaimable` HHDM location.
- Added opt-in `just frame-smoke` (`probe-hhdm-frame`): QEMU writes, reads, clears, and returns one allocated frame; reads/counts root entries; performs bounded walks for every page of kernel text/rodata/data and the minimum boot-stack span; checks expected physical translations; and compares effective PAT/MTRR types for kernel-image mappings and their HHDM aliases.
- Added a host-testable 4-/5-level single-address page-table walker supporting 4 KiB, 2 MiB, and 1 GiB leaves; it folds RW/US/NX permissions and extracts leaf PAT indices. Synthetic tests cover 4-/5-level paths, absent entries, permissions, PAT, huge pages, and invalid inputs.
- QEMU `just frame-smoke` passed after these changes. Serial output confirmed:
  - Kernel text: read-only/executable, PAT 0.
  - Rodata: read-only/NX, PAT 0.
  - Data: writable/NX, PAT 0.
  - Boot stack: writable/executable, PAT 0.
  - Kernel-image/HHDM effective cache types matched for all tested pages.
- `just test` passed after walker work: 4 parser tests and 59 kernel tests. `cargo check --target x86_64-unknown-none --features probe-hhdm-frame` passed. Earlier `just verify && just fault-smoke` passed before the walker/alias additions; rerun full checks after current edits.
- Docs updated in `AGENTS.md`, `docs/architecture/{memory,boot}.md`, `docs/development/{testing,building}.md`, and `docs/roadmap/README.md`. Milestone remains explicitly in progress.
- Root read/walk is opt-in and relies on Limine base revision 3 HHDM guarantees. The walker checks only paths for inventoried ranges; it does not enumerate all mappings or modify tables.

## Context / constraints
- `rustix/AGENTS.md` and `docs/architecture/memory.md` are authoritative. Kernel is `no_std`, target `x86_64-unknown-none`.
- Do not access arbitrary physical addresses through HHDM. For frame probes, retain an allocator-issued non-copyable token and validate the full page in `Usable` memory. The inherited root and each table page are restricted to `BootloaderReclaimable` memory before HHDM reads.
- No page-table allocation/mapping/unmapping, CR3 switch, or heap exists yet. Keep the Limine root and its backing pages intact.
- Current transition policy is design-only: 4 KiB pages, NXE required, W^X denied, exact kernel ELF permissions, exclude kernel-image physical span from generic HHDM in a new root, ordinary RAM RW/NX/WB. Existing bootstrap stack is RWX; no guard page is known.
- The pure walker returns permission/cache-selector data, but current QEMU path only logs permissions and confirms effective type equality for kernel-image aliases. It does not validate all cache aliases or all live mappings.
- HHDM root helper assumes Limine page tables reside in `BootloaderReclaimable`; this assumption is documented and QEMU-tested, but remains protocol-dependent.

## Next
1. Review the latest edits for correctness, especially page-walker reserved-bit handling and the HHDM reader’s memory-type restrictions.
2. Update docs/roadmap and `AGENTS.md` to record the newly validated critical-range walk and effective-cache alias comparison without overstating coverage.
3. Run `just verify`, `just fault-smoke`, and `just frame-smoke`; report only observed results.
4. Proceed with an ownership-aware candidate page-table builder and transactional allocation/mapping tests. Keep it separate from active CR3; verify candidate mappings and rollback before any switch.
5. Continue with a reviewed CR3 transition only after proving mappings for kernel segments, current stack/`BootInfo`, descriptor/exception state, loader data still needed, and page-table access; include NXE, CR0.WP, PCID/global/TLB policy.
6. Add and test heap behavior only after page mapping is validated. Do not mark Milestone 2 complete until all roadmap exit criteria are actually implemented and tested.

    70	## Engineering rules
    71	
    72	### Keep changes incremental and coherent
    73	
    74	1. Inspect the relevant source, tests, docs, and call sites before editing.
    75	2. State assumptions, invariants, and failure behavior for new kernel interfaces.
    76	3. Prefer small vertical slices that compile and can be tested over broad scaffolding or placeholder APIs.
    77	4. Update tests and documentation alongside behavior changes.
    78	5. Do not change unrelated code, rename files gratuitously, add speculative features, or rewrite project history.
    79	6. Do not commit or create branches unless the user explicitly asks.
    80	
    81	### Rust and dependency policy
    82	
    83	- Preserve the kernel's `no_std`/freestanding constraints. Do not introduce `std` into kernel code.
    84	- Prefer `core` and existing in-tree abstractions. Do not add third-party Rust dependencies without a concrete need and compatibility/security review.
    85	- Keep the Crabshell parser independent of kernel I/O and VFS implementation. Kernel execution belongs in `src/shell.rs` or an appropriate kernel service.
    86	- Do not add allocation-dependent APIs before a real heap exists. Fixed-capacity structures must document their limits and exhaustion behavior.
    87	- Respect the workspace structure and the host-testable `rustix-kernel` library versus freestanding `rustix` binary boundary.
    88	
    89	### Unsafe and hardware code
    90	
    91	Unsafe code is expected only at explicit hardware, boot-protocol, assembly, or raw-memory boundaries. Keep each unsafe block narrow and document the invariant that makes it sound. Do not add broad `unsafe impl`, mutable global references, unchecked pointer arithmetic, or unreviewed inline/global assembly.
    92	
    93	Before changing boot or memory code, account for these facts:
    94	
    95	- Limine fills response pointers before `_start`; the request records must remain writable in the ELF image.
    96	- Rustix validates nullness, alignment, counts, arithmetic, and physical ranges, but cannot prove that a non-null bootloader pointer is readable.
    97	- Physical ranges are half-open `[start, end)` and must use checked arithmetic.
    98	- Only regions classified `Usable` may enter the frame allocator. ACPI, bootloader-reclaimable, framebuffer, reserved, unknown, and other types are not free frames.
    99	- A `Frame` is a physical address, not a dereferenceable pointer. Do not access it through the HHDM or change CR3 until an explicit, reviewed mapping policy and ownership proof exist.
   100	- The kernel currently inherits Limine's page tables. Do not casually replace or mutate them: preserve the executing kernel, boot stack, `BootInfo`, request/response data, exception stacks, and mappings needed to continue execution.
   101	- The exception setup is fatal-only. It does not enable maskable interrupts, configure a PIC/APIC, or provide recovery. Do not call `sti` or claim interrupt support without an IRQ design and tests.
   102	- The shell and VFS run in ring 0 and are not isolated or secure.
   103	
   104	For hardware changes, document assumptions about CPU mode, selectors, stacks, page permissions, interrupt state, and failure handling. Avoid new architecture mechanisms that cannot be statically reviewed or validated.
   105	
   106	### Shell and filesystem contract
   107	
   108	- Crabshell is presently a kernel-mode serial shell, not a userspace program or a POSIX shell.
   109	- Its parser is a separate `no_std`, allocation-free crate; retain that boundary.
   110	- The RAM filesystem is volatile and bounded. Preserve explicit errors and test capacity, path, and mutation edge cases.
   111	- Do not imply persistence, permissions, links, process launching, or shell features that do not exist.
   112	- Update the parser tests and `docs/architecture/crabshell.md` when adding or changing commands.
   113	
   114	## Validation workflow
   115	
   116	Run the narrowest relevant checks first, then broaden them. From the repository root, the supported commands are:
   117	
   118	```sh
   119	just fmt
   120	just test
   121	just check
   122	just build
   123	just image
   124	just smoke
   125	just verify
   126	```
   127	
   128	`just test` runs host-side library tests (memory-map validation, frame allocator, VFS, and Crabshell parser). `just check` checks `x86_64-unknown-none`; `just build` links the optimized ELF. `just verify` includes formatting, host tests, target check, pinned Limine image creation, and QEMU prompt smoke test. Image/boot checks need Python, `xorriso`, QEMU, the Rust target, and network access for the first pinned Limine download; Linux/WSL also needs `cc` to build Limine's host utility.
   129	
   130	For changes to `src/main.rs`, `src/boot.rs`, linker/request configuration, `src/arch/x86_64/`, `src/frame.rs`, or paging/heap code, the intended full validation is `just verify`. If the environment does not permit a check, report the exact blocker and leave the corresponding roadmap criterion pending.
   131	
   132	Do not claim a check passed unless it was run and its successful result was observed. Editor diagnostics are useful but are not a substitute for `cargo test`, a target build, or QEMU. A target check is not a final link; a linked ELF is not proof of boot; a prompt smoke test is not proof of interactive shell behavior or physical-hardware correctness.
   133	
   134	## Completion criteria for agent changes
   135	
   136	Before reporting work complete:
   137	
   138	- Ensure source, tests, docs, and call sites agree.
   139	- Review unsafe and hardware assumptions, including error paths and capacity limits.
   140	- Run appropriate formatting/tests/build/boot checks, or clearly state why they could not run.
   141	- Report files changed, behavior delivered, validation actually observed, and remaining risks.
   142	- Keep milestone status accurate. A subsystem is not complete just because it has code.

    84	## Milestone 2 — memory ownership, paging, heap, and exceptions (in progress)
    85	
    86	This milestone must establish a safe basis for future allocation and kernel services. Do not allocate a frame for a mapping or dereference it through the HHDM until the mapping/ownership proof is explicit.
    87	
    88	### Source work present
    89	
    90	- [x] Fixed-capacity frame allocator over validated `Usable` ranges, with page alignment, first-MiB reservation, deallocation, coalescing, bounded metadata, and host tests (`src/frame.rs`).
    91	- [x] Initialize allocator metadata from the boot snapshot and expose counts through Crabshell `meminfo`.
    92	- [x] Specify frame-token ownership and failure semantics: `Frame` is non-copyable, failed deallocation returns the token without changing allocator state, and the current API documents (but does not enforce) one allocator instance per physical map.
    93	- [x] Bootstrap GDT/TSS/IDT and fatal handlers for exception vectors 0–31.
    94	- [x] Give double faults a dedicated IST stack; report saved register/error context and CR2/error bits for page faults.
    95	- [x] Keep maskable IRQ delivery disabled; current exception handling is fatal-only.
    96	
    97	### Required memory-management work
    98	
    99	- [x] Read `CR4.LA57` and `CPUID.80000008H` when available to report active/max address widths; validate Limine pointers against active canonical width and host-test 48-/57-bit boundaries.
   100	- [x] Document base revision 3 HHDM region coverage, page-boundary behavior, and x86 permissions/cache attributes. HHDM access is limited to opt-in, checked probes relying on the protocol contract; there is no general physical-memory service.
   101	- [x] Reject physical map ranges outside the reported CPUID width when available; validate page-rounded HHDM address arithmetic/canonicality for base revision 3 mapped types. This is protocol-derived validation, not a page-table walk or proof of pointer readability.
   102	- [x] Record current transition-critical objects, their mapping sources/permissions, and unresolved bounds in `docs/architecture/memory.md`.
   103	- [x] Capture Limine's executable physical/virtual bases and resolve the complete linker-defined half-open kernel-image span in `BootInfo`; validate the linker/loader base agreement, canonical virtual span, arithmetic, and reported physical width.
   104	- [x] Capture and validate the linker-defined page-aligned text, rodata, and data segment bounds in `BootInfo`; host-test their ordering, contiguity, rounded image coverage, and derived physical ranges. `just verify` reported all three in QEMU on 2026-10-21. This metadata does not prove inherited page-table coverage or live permissions.
   105	- [x] Capture and validate the protocol-guaranteed minimum 64 KiB active boot-stack span from entry `RSP`; validate its HHDM translation and `BootloaderReclaimable` backing. The actual loader allocation may be larger.
   106	- [x] Record the Limine limitation that exact initial-stack allocation bounds and guard status are not provided; preserve only the known minimum span and do not infer a guard page.
   107	- [x] Decode the inherited CR3 root address and interpret its low bits using the reported physical-address width and active `CR4.PCIDE` state; host-test reserved-bit and width rejection. `just verify` passed on 2026-10-21, including target build, ISO creation, and QEMU prompt smoke. The opt-in QEMU memory probe now reads the root and follows bounded paths for transition-critical ranges, but this is not full table inventory or permission/cache validation.
   108	- [x] Document the initial W^X/alias, cache, MMIO, huge-page, guard-page, and inherited-root preservation policy in `docs/architecture/memory.md`; this is design only, not an implementation.
   109	- [ ] Design a kernel-owned page-table transition that preserves every mapping needed to execute during and after the switch: kernel text/data/BSS, current stack, `BootInfo`, Limine requests/responses still needed, GDT/TSS/IDT, exception stacks, serial state, and any direct-map access used by the transition.
   110	- [x] Add pure host-tested 4 KiB mapping-range validation and leaf-PTE bit encoding. Validation requires alignment, checked bounds, known physical width, canonical virtual ranges, and W^X; encoding bounds the physical width and PAT index and requires NXE for non-executable entries. These helpers do not prove frame ownership, mapping coverage, or PAT cache semantics, and do not touch tables.
   111	- [ ] Implement page-table allocation and mapping operations with verified cache semantics, frame ownership, and supported page-size behavior; preserve explicit writable-executable rejection.
   112	- [ ] Ensure mapping failure (including no free frame or range-table exhaustion) rolls back partial page-table allocations or leaves the old map active.
   113	- [x] Add host tests for raw PTE-bit encoding and parsing a supplied PAT layout to find WB/UC/WC indexes.
   114	- [x] Read EFER.NXE only when NX is supported and read `IA32_PAT` only when PAT is supported; report these read-only values and recognized PAT indexes at boot.
   115	- [x] Host-test that rejected deallocations preserve free-range state and return the frame token for unaligned, unmanaged, already-free, and range-table-full cases.
   116	- [x] Add a pure host-tested MTRR decoder/resolver for supplied fixed and variable register values, including disabled-MTRR behavior and overlap rules. Host tests and `just verify` passed on 2026-10-21.

Retain at most 32 variable pairs; report capacity overflow explicitly without a partial snapshot.    118	- [x] Validate captured MTRR capability/default-type bits, register counts and fixed-range availability, WC support, and variable-range mask/alignment; resolve the Intel SDM Table 11-7 PAT/MTRR combinations for one physical address only when `CR0.CD=0` and `CR0.NW=0`.
