            variable_mtrr(0x20_0000, 0x20_0000, MtrrMemoryType::WriteProtected),
        ];
        let layout =
            MtrrLayout::new(36, true, false, MtrrMemoryType::WriteBack, None, &undefined).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(
            layout.memory_type_for(0x20_0000),
            Err(MtrrError::UndefinedOverlap)
        );
    }

    #[test]
    fn disabled_mtrrs_force_uncacheable_and_bad_registers_are_rejected() {
        let layout =
            MtrrLayout::new(36, false, true, MtrrMemoryType::WriteBack, None, &[]).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(
            layout.memory_type_for(0x20_0000),
            Ok(MtrrMemoryType::Uncacheable)
        );
        assert_eq!(
            MtrrLayout::new(36, true, true, MtrrMemoryType::WriteBack, None, &[]),
            Err(MtrrError::FixedRangesUnavailable)
        );
        assert_eq!(
            VariableMtrr::from_msr_values(0x1000 | 0x200, 0, 36),
            Err(MtrrError::ReservedBaseBits)
        );
        assert_eq!(
            VariableMtrr::from_msr_values(0x1000 | 6, 1 << 10, 36),
            Err(MtrrError::ReservedMaskBits)
        );
        assert_eq!(VariableMtrr::from_msr_values(0x1000 | 6, 0, 36), Ok(None));
        let width_mismatch = [variable_mtrr(
            0x20_0000,
            0x20_0000,
            MtrrMemoryType::WriteBack,
        )];
        assert_eq!(
            MtrrLayout::new(
                35,
                true,
                false,
                MtrrMemoryType::WriteBack,
                None,
                &width_mismatch,
            ),
            Err(MtrrError::PhysicalAddressWidthMismatch)
        );
        assert_eq!(
            VariableMtrr::from_msr_values(0x1000 | 2, 1 << 11, 36),
            Err(MtrrError::ReservedMemoryType { value: 2 })
        );
        let mut invalid_fixed = [0; 11];
        invalid_fixed[0] = 2;
        assert_eq!(
            FixedMtrrRanges::from_msr_values(invalid_fixed),
            Err(MtrrError::ReservedMemoryType { value: 2 })
        );
    }

    #[test]
    fn accepts_aligned_ranges_at_canonical_boundaries() {
        let lower = validate_mapping_range(
            0x0000_7fff_ffff_e000,
            0x1000,
            0x2000,
            KERNEL_READ_ONLY,
            Some(14),
            48,
        )
        .unwrap();
        assert_eq!(
            lower,
            ValidatedMappingRange {
                virtual_start: 0x0000_7fff_ffff_e000,
                virtual_end: 0x0000_8000_0000_0000,
                physical_start: 0x1000,
                physical_end: 0x3000,
                physical_address_bits: 14,
                permissions: KERNEL_READ_ONLY,
            }
        );

        let upper = validate_mapping_range(
            0xffff_8000_0000_0000,
            0,
            PAGE_SIZE,
            KERNEL_READ_ONLY,
            Some(12),
            48,
        )
        .unwrap();
        assert_eq!(upper.virtual_end(), 0xffff_8000_0000_1000);
    }

    #[test]
    fn rejects_empty_and_unaligned_ranges() {
        assert_eq!(
            validate_mapping_range(0x1000, 0x2000, 0, KERNEL_READ_ONLY, Some(32), 48),
            Err(MappingError::EmptyRange)
        );
        assert_eq!(
            validate_mapping_range(0x1001, 0x2000, PAGE_SIZE, KERNEL_READ_ONLY, Some(32), 48),
            Err(MappingError::UnalignedRange)
        );
        assert_eq!(
            validate_mapping_range(
                0x1000,
                0x2000,
                PAGE_SIZE + 1,
                KERNEL_READ_ONLY,
                Some(32),
                48
            ),
            Err(MappingError::UnalignedRange)
        );
    }

    #[test]
    fn requires_known_valid_address_widths_and_bounded_physical_ranges() {
        assert_eq!(
            validate_mapping_range(0x1000, 0x1000, PAGE_SIZE, KERNEL_READ_ONLY, None, 48),
            Err(MappingError::UnknownPhysicalAddressWidth)
        );
        assert_eq!(
            validate_mapping_range(0x1000, 0x1000, PAGE_SIZE, KERNEL_READ_ONLY, Some(0), 48),
            Err(MappingError::InvalidPhysicalAddressWidth)
        );
        assert_eq!(
            validate_mapping_range(0x1000, 0x1000, PAGE_SIZE, KERNEL_READ_ONLY, Some(52), 0),
            Err(MappingError::InvalidVirtualAddressWidth)
        );
        assert_eq!(
            validate_mapping_range(
                0x1000,
                0x1000,
                PAGE_SIZE * 2,
                KERNEL_READ_ONLY,
                Some(13),
                48
            ),
            Err(MappingError::PhysicalRangeOutOfBounds)
        );
    }

    #[test]
    fn rejects_noncanonical_ranges_and_ranges_crossing_the_canonical_hole() {
        assert_eq!(
            validate_mapping_range(
                0x0000_8000_0000_0000,
                0,
                PAGE_SIZE,
                KERNEL_READ_ONLY,
                Some(52),
                48
            ),
            Err(MappingError::NonCanonicalVirtualRange)
        );

        let crosses_hole = (0xffff_8000_0000_1000u64) - 0x0000_7fff_ffff_f000;
        assert_eq!(
            validate_mapping_range(
                0x0000_7fff_ffff_f000,
                0,
                crosses_hole,
                KERNEL_READ_ONLY,
                Some(64),
                48,
            ),
            Err(MappingError::CrossesCanonicalHole)
        );
    }

    fn pat_value(entries: [u8; 8]) -> u64 {
        entries.iter().enumerate().fold(0, |value, (index, entry)| {
            value | ((*entry as u64) << (index * 8))
        })
    }

    #[test]
    fn resolves_cache_policies_from_the_supplied_pat_layout() {
        let pat = pat_value([6, 4, 7, 0, 6, 1, 7, 0]);
        let layout = super::PatLayout::from_msr_value(pat).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(layout.index_for(super::CachePolicy::WriteBack), Some(0));
        assert_eq!(layout.index_for(super::CachePolicy::Uncacheable), Some(3));
        assert_eq!(
            layout.index_for(super::CachePolicy::WriteCombining),
            Some(5)
        );

        let without_write_combining =
            super::PatLayout::from_msr_value(pat_value([6, 4, 7, 0, 6, 4, 7, 0])).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(
            without_write_combining.index_for(super::CachePolicy::WriteCombining),
            None
        );
    }

    #[test]
    fn combines_every_documented_pat_and_mtrr_pair() {
        use EffectiveMemoryType as E;
        use MtrrMemoryType as M;

        let pat = PatLayout::from_msr_value(pat_value([0, 7, 1, 4, 6, 5, 0, 0])).unwrap();
        let rows = [
            (
                M::Uncacheable,
                [
                    E::Uncacheable,
                    E::Uncacheable,
                    E::WriteCombining,
                    E::Uncacheable,
                    E::Uncacheable,
                    E::Uncacheable,
                ],
            ),
            (
                M::WriteCombining,
                [
                    E::Uncacheable,
                    E::WriteCombining,
                    E::WriteCombining,
                    E::Uncacheable,
                    E::WriteCombining,
                    E::Uncacheable,
                ],
            ),
            (
                M::WriteThrough,
                [
                    E::Uncacheable,
                    E::Uncacheable,
                    E::WriteCombining,
                    E::WriteThrough,
                    E::WriteThrough,
                    E::WriteProtected,
                ],
            ),
            (
                M::WriteBack,
                [
                    E::Uncacheable,
                    E::Uncacheable,
                    E::WriteCombining,
                    E::WriteThrough,
                    E::WriteBack,
                    E::WriteProtected,
                ],
            ),
            (
                M::WriteProtected,
                [
                    E::Uncacheable,
                    E::Uncacheable,
                    E::WriteCombining,
                    E::WriteThrough,
                    E::WriteProtected,
                    E::WriteProtected,
                ],
            ),
        ];

        for (mtrr_type, expected) in rows {
            let registers = empty_mtrr_registers(1 << 10, (1 << 11) | mtrr_type as u64);
            let layout = registers.validated_layout(36).unwrap();
            for (pat_index, expected_type) in expected.into_iter().enumerate() {
                assert_eq!(
                    layout.effective_memory_type_for(0x20_0000, pat, pat_index as u8, true),
                    Ok(expected_type),
                    "MTRR={mtrr_type:?}, PAT index={pat_index}"
                );
            }
        }
    }

    #[test]
    fn rejects_invalid_effective_cache_type_inputs() {
        let registers = empty_mtrr_registers(0, (1 << 11) | MtrrMemoryType::WriteBack as u64);
        let layout = registers.validated_layout(36).unwrap();
        let pat = PatLayout::from_msr_value(pat_value([6, 4, 7, 0, 6, 1, 7, 0])).unwrap();

        assert_eq!(
            layout.effective_memory_type_for(0, pat, 8, true),
            Err(EffectiveMemoryTypeError::PatIndexOutOfRange { index: 8 })
        );
        assert_eq!(
            layout.effective_memory_type_for(0, pat, 0, false),
            Err(EffectiveMemoryTypeError::NonNormalCachingMode)
        );
        assert_eq!(
            layout.effective_memory_type_for(1u64 << 36, pat, 0, true),
            Err(EffectiveMemoryTypeError::Mtrr(
                MtrrError::PhysicalAddressOutOfRange
            ))
        );
    }

    #[test]
    fn selects_a_pat_index_that_is_uniform_across_variable_mtrr_segments() {
        let capability = 1 | (1 << 10);
        let mut registers =
            empty_mtrr_registers(capability, (1 << 11) | MtrrMemoryType::WriteBack as u64);
        let physical_mask = ((1u64 << 36) - 1) & !(PAGE_SIZE - 1);
        registers.variable_registers[0] = MtrrRegisterPair {
            base: 0x20_0000 | MtrrMemoryType::WriteThrough as u64,
            mask: (physical_mask & !(0x20_0000 - 1)) | (1 << 11),
        };
        let layout = registers.validated_layout(36).unwrap();
        let pat = PatLayout::from_msr_value(pat_value([6, 0, 1, 4, 6, 1, 7, 0])).unwrap();

        assert_eq!(
            layout.select_pat_index_for_range(
                0x1f_f000,
                PAGE_SIZE * 2,
                pat,
                EffectiveMemoryType::WriteCombining,
                true,
            ),
            Ok(2)
        );
    }

    #[test]
    fn rejects_range_when_fixed_mtrrs_prevent_one_uniform_pat_index() {
        let mut registers = empty_mtrr_registers(
            1 << 8,
            (1 << 11) | (1 << 10) | MtrrMemoryType::WriteBack as u64,
        );
        registers.fixed_registers.as_mut().unwrap()[0] = MtrrMemoryType::WriteBack as u64;
        let layout = registers.validated_layout(36).unwrap();
        let pat = PatLayout::from_msr_value(pat_value([6, 0, 1, 4, 6, 1, 7, 0])).unwrap();

        assert_eq!(
            layout.select_pat_index_for_range(
                0,
                0x20_000,
                pat,
                EffectiveMemoryType::WriteBack,
                true,
            ),
            Err(EffectiveMemoryTypeError::NoUniformPatIndex {
                requested: EffectiveMemoryType::WriteBack,
            })
        );
    }

    #[test]
    fn rejects_invalid_effective_cache_type_ranges() {
        let registers = empty_mtrr_registers(0, (1 << 11) | MtrrMemoryType::WriteBack as u64);
        let layout = registers.validated_layout(36).unwrap();
        let pat = PatLayout::from_msr_value(pat_value([6, 0, 1, 4, 6, 1, 7, 0])).unwrap();
        let requested = EffectiveMemoryType::WriteBack;

        assert_eq!(
            layout.select_pat_index_for_range(0, 0, pat, requested, true),
            Err(EffectiveMemoryTypeError::EmptyRange)
        );
        assert_eq!(
            layout.select_pat_index_for_range(1, PAGE_SIZE, pat, requested, true),
            Err(EffectiveMemoryTypeError::UnalignedRange)
        );
        assert_eq!(
            layout.select_pat_index_for_range(
                u64::MAX & !(PAGE_SIZE - 1),
                PAGE_SIZE,
                pat,
                requested,
                true,
            ),
            Err(EffectiveMemoryTypeError::AddressOverflow)
        );
        assert_eq!(
            layout.select_pat_index_for_range(1 << 36, PAGE_SIZE, pat, requested, true),
            Err(EffectiveMemoryTypeError::Mtrr(
                MtrrError::PhysicalAddressOutOfRange
            ))
        );
        assert_eq!(
            layout.select_pat_index_for_range(0, PAGE_SIZE, pat, requested, false),
            Err(EffectiveMemoryTypeError::NonNormalCachingMode)
        );
    }

    #[test]
    fn validates_captured_mtrr_snapshot_before_resolution() {
        let registers = empty_mtrr_registers(
            (1 << 12) | (1 << 10) | (1 << 8) | 1,
            (1 << 11) | (1 << 10) | MtrrMemoryType::WriteBack as u64,
        );
        let layout = registers.validated_layout(36).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(layout.memory_type_for(0), Ok(MtrrMemoryType::WriteBack));
        assert_eq!(
            layout.memory_type_for(0x10_0000),
            Ok(MtrrMemoryType::WriteBack)
        );

        let mut invalid = empty_mtrr_registers(0, 1 << 11);
        invalid.capability |= 1 << 9;
        assert_eq!(
            invalid.validated_layout(36),
            Err(MtrrError::ReservedCapabilityBits)
        );

        let mut invalid = empty_mtrr_registers(0, 1 << 11);
        invalid.capability |= 1 << 13;
        assert_eq!(
            invalid.validated_layout(36),
            Err(MtrrError::ReservedCapabilityBits)
        );

        let mut invalid = empty_mtrr_registers(0, 1 << 11);
        invalid.default_type |= 1 << 12;
        assert_eq!(
            invalid.validated_layout(36),
            Err(MtrrError::ReservedDefaultTypeBits)
        );

        let mut invalid = empty_mtrr_registers(0, 1 << 11);
        invalid.variable_register_count = 1;
        assert_eq!(
            invalid.validated_layout(36),
            Err(MtrrError::VariableRegisterCountMismatch)
        );

        let mut invalid = empty_mtrr_registers(1 << 8, 1 << 11);
        invalid.fixed_registers = None;
        assert_eq!(
            invalid.validated_layout(36),
            Err(MtrrError::FixedRegisterSupportMismatch)
        );

        let invalid = empty_mtrr_registers(0, (1 << 11) | MtrrMemoryType::WriteCombining as u64);
        assert_eq!(
            invalid.validated_layout(36),
            Err(MtrrError::WriteCombiningUnsupported)
        );

        let mut invalid = empty_mtrr_registers(1 << 8, (1 << 11) | 6);
        invalid.fixed_registers.as_mut().unwrap()[0] =
            MtrrMemoryType::WriteCombining as u64 * 0x0101_0101_0101_0101;
        assert_eq!(
            invalid.validated_layout(36),
            Err(MtrrError::WriteCombiningUnsupported)
        );

        let mut invalid = empty_mtrr_registers(1, (1 << 11) | 6);
        let physical_mask = ((1u64 << 36) - 1) & !(PAGE_SIZE - 1);
        invalid.variable_registers[0] = MtrrRegisterPair {
            base: 0x20_0000 | MtrrMemoryType::WriteCombining as u64,
            mask: (physical_mask & !(0x20_0000 - 1)) | (1 << 11),
        };
        assert_eq!(
            invalid.validated_layout(36),
            Err(MtrrError::WriteCombiningUnsupported)
        );

        let invalid = empty_mtrr_registers(0, (1 << 11) | (1 << 10));
        assert_eq!(
            invalid.validated_layout(36),
            Err(MtrrError::FixedRangesUnavailable)
        );

        let mut invalid = empty_mtrr_registers(1, 1 << 11);
        let physical_mask = ((1u64 << 36) - 1) & !(PAGE_SIZE - 1);
        invalid.variable_registers[0] = MtrrRegisterPair {
            base: MtrrMemoryType::WriteBack as u64,
            mask: (physical_mask ^ (1 << 13)) | (1 << 11),
        };
        assert_eq!(
            invalid.validated_layout(36),
            Err(MtrrError::UnsupportedDiscontinuousVariableMask)
        );
    }

    #[test]
    fn rejects_misaligned_variable_mtrr_bases() {
        let physical_address_bits = 36;
        let physical_mask = ((1u64 << physical_address_bits) - 1) & !(PAGE_SIZE - 1);
        let mask = physical_mask & !(0x2000 - 1) | (1 << 11);
        assert_eq!(
            VariableMtrr::from_msr_values(
                0x1000 | MtrrMemoryType::WriteBack as u64,
                mask,
                physical_address_bits,
            ),
            Err(MtrrError::MisalignedVariableBase)
        );
    }

    fn rejects_reserved_pat_entries() {

            Err(super::PatLayoutError::ReservedBits { index: 0 })
        );
        assert_eq!(
            super::PatLayout::from_msr_value(0b010 << 24),

    #[test]
    fn selects_uniform_cache_attributes_for_a_mapping_range_and_encodes_each_leaf() {
        let capability = 1 | (1 << 10);
        let mut registers =
            empty_mtrr_registers(capability, (1 << 11) | MtrrMemoryType::WriteBack as u64);
        let physical_mask = ((1u64 << 36) - 1) & !(PAGE_SIZE - 1);
        registers.variable_registers[0] = MtrrRegisterPair {
            base: 0x20_0000 | MtrrMemoryType::WriteThrough as u64,
            mask: (physical_mask & !(0x20_0000 - 1)) | (1 << 11),
        };
        let mtrrs = registers.validated_layout(36).unwrap();
        let pat = PatLayout::from_msr_value(pat_value([6, 0, 1, 4, 6, 1, 7, 0])).unwrap();
        let mapping = validate_mapping_range(
            0x4000,
            0x1f_f000,
            PAGE_SIZE * 2,
            KERNEL_READ_ONLY,
            Some(36),
            48,
        )
        .unwrap();
        let attributes = mapping
            .select_cache_attributes(CachePolicy::WriteCombining, pat, &mtrrs, true)
            .unwrap();

        assert_eq!(attributes.physical_start(), 0x1f_f000);
        assert_eq!(attributes.physical_end(), 0x20_1000);
        assert_eq!(attributes.pat_index(), 2);
        assert_eq!(
            attributes.effective_type(),
            EffectiveMemoryType::WriteCombining
        );
        for offset in [0, PAGE_SIZE] {
            assert_eq!(
                mapping
                    .leaf_4k_entry_with_cache_attributes(offset, attributes, true)
                    .unwrap()
                    .bits()
                    & ((1 << 3) | (1 << 4) | (1 << 7)),
                1 << 4
            );
        }

        let other_mapping = validate_mapping_range(
            0x8000,
            0x30_0000,
            PAGE_SIZE * 2,
            KERNEL_READ_ONLY,
            Some(36),
            48,
        )
        .unwrap();
        assert_eq!(
            other_mapping.leaf_4k_entry_with_cache_attributes(0, attributes, true),
            Err(MappingError::CacheAttributesRangeMismatch)
        );
    }

    #[test]
    fn rejects_cache_attribute_selection_when_physical_widths_disagree() {
        let registers = empty_mtrr_registers(0, (1 << 11) | MtrrMemoryType::WriteBack as u64);
        let mtrrs = registers.validated_layout(36).unwrap();
        let pat = PatLayout::from_msr_value(pat_value([6, 0, 1, 4, 6, 1, 7, 0])).unwrap();
        let mapping =
            validate_mapping_range(0x4000, 0x20_0000, PAGE_SIZE, KERNEL_READ_ONLY, Some(37), 48)
                .unwrap();

        assert_eq!(
            mapping.select_cache_attributes(CachePolicy::WriteBack, pat, &mtrrs, true),
            Err(MappingError::MtrrPhysicalAddressWidthMismatch)
        );
    }

    #[test]
    fn encodes_4k_leaf_permissions_nx_and_pat_index_bits() {
        let writable_user_page = PagePermissions {
            writable: true,
            executable: false,
            user_accessible: true,
        };
        let mapping = validate_mapping_range(
            0x4000,
            0x20_0000,
            PAGE_SIZE * 2,
            writable_user_page,
            Some(52),
            48,
        )
        .unwrap();

        let first = mapping.leaf_4k_entry(0, 0b101, true).unwrap().bits();
        assert_eq!(
            first,
            0x20_0000 | (1 << 0) | (1 << 1) | (1 << 2) | (1 << 3) | (1 << 7) | (1 << 63)
        );
        let second = mapping
            .leaf_4k_entry(PAGE_SIZE, 0b101, true)
            .unwrap()
            .bits();
        assert_eq!(second & 0x000f_ffff_ffff_f000, 0x20_1000);
        assert_eq!(second & (1 << 63), 1 << 63);

        let all_pat_bits = mapping.leaf_4k_entry(0, 0b111, true).unwrap().bits()
            & ((1 << 3) | (1 << 4) | (1 << 7));
        assert_eq!(all_pat_bits, (1 << 3) | (1 << 4) | (1 << 7));
    }

    #[test]
    fn rejects_unencodable_leaf_attributes_and_page_offsets() {
        let mapping =
            validate_mapping_range(0x4000, 0x20_0000, PAGE_SIZE, KERNEL_READ_ONLY, Some(52), 48)
                .unwrap();
        assert_eq!(
            mapping.leaf_4k_entry(0, 8, true),
            Err(MappingError::InvalidPatIndex)
        );
        assert_eq!(
            mapping.leaf_4k_entry(0, 0, false),
            Err(MappingError::NxNotEnabled)
        );
        assert_eq!(
            mapping.leaf_4k_entry(1, 0, true),
            Err(MappingError::UnalignedPageOffset)
        );
        assert_eq!(
            mapping.leaf_4k_entry(PAGE_SIZE, 0, true),
            Err(MappingError::PageOffsetOutOfRange)
        );

        let too_wide =
            validate_mapping_range(0x4000, 0x20_0000, PAGE_SIZE, KERNEL_READ_ONLY, Some(53), 48)
                .unwrap();
        assert_eq!(
            too_wide.leaf_4k_entry(0, 0, true),
            Err(MappingError::InvalidPhysicalAddressWidth)
        );
    }

    #[test]
    fn executable_leaf_does_not_set_nx() {
        let executable = PagePermissions {
            writable: false,
            executable: true,
            user_accessible: false,
        };
        let mapping =
            validate_mapping_range(0x4000, 0x20_0000, PAGE_SIZE, executable, Some(52), 48).unwrap();
        let entry = mapping.leaf_4k_entry(0, 0, false).unwrap().bits();
        assert_eq!(entry, 0x20_0000 | 1);
    }

    #[test]
    fn candidate_page_tables_reject_root_frames_outside_the_configured_width() {
        let high_address = 1u64 << 40;
        let map = MemoryMap::from_raw(&[RawMemoryRegion {
            base: high_address,
            length: PAGE_SIZE,
            kind: 0,
        }])
        .unwrap();
        let mut allocator = FrameAllocator::from_memory_map(&map).unwrap();
        let mut memory = CandidateTestMemory::new();
        let failure =
            match CandidatePageTables::new(&mut allocator, &mut memory, four_level_walk_config()) {
                Err(error) => error,
                Ok(_) => panic!("candidate creation accepted an out-of-range root frame"),
            };
        assert_eq!(failure.cause, CandidateCreateErrorKind::RootFrameOutOfRange);
        let frame = failure
            .frame
            .expect("root token is returned on validation failure");
        assert_eq!(frame.address(), high_address);
        allocator.deallocate(frame).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(allocator.free_frames(), 1);
    }

    #[test]
    fn candidate_mapping_rejects_out_of_width_table_frames_transactionally() {
        let high_address = 1u64 << 40;
        let map = MemoryMap::from_raw(&[
            RawMemoryRegion {
                base: 0x10_0000,
                length: PAGE_SIZE,
                kind: 0,
            },
            RawMemoryRegion {
                base: 0x10_1000,
                length: PAGE_SIZE,
                kind: 0,
            },
            RawMemoryRegion {
                base: high_address,
                length: PAGE_SIZE,
                kind: 0,
            },
        ])
        .unwrap();
        let mut allocator = FrameAllocator::from_memory_map(&map).unwrap();
        let mut memory = CandidateTestMemory::new();
        let mut candidate =
            CandidatePageTables::new(&mut allocator, &mut memory, four_level_walk_config())
                .unwrap();
        let frame = allocator.allocate().unwrap();
        assert_eq!(frame.address(), 0x10_1000);
        let (mapping, attributes) = candidate_mapping(
            &frame,
            0xffff_9000_0000_1000,
            PagePermissions {
                writable: false,
                executable: false,
                user_accessible: false,
            },
        );
        let free_before_map = allocator.free_frames();

        let failure = candidate
            .map_owned_page(&mut allocator, &mut memory, frame, mapping, attributes)
            .unwrap_err();
        assert_eq!(failure.cause, CandidateMapErrorKind::TableFrameOutOfRange);
        assert_eq!(failure.rollback_retained_table_frames, 0);
        assert_eq!(candidate.table_count(), 1);
        assert_eq!(candidate.mapping_count(), 0);
        assert_eq!(allocator.free_frames(), free_before_map);
        allocator.deallocate(failure.frame).unwrap();
        candidate.release(&mut allocator).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(allocator.free_frames(), 3);
    }

    #[test]
    fn candidate_walk_rejects_intermediate_tables_without_owned_tokens() {
        let mut allocator = candidate_allocator(2);
        let mut memory = CandidateTestMemory::new();
        let candidate_config = four_level_walk_config();
        let candidate =
            CandidatePageTables::new(&mut allocator, &mut memory, candidate_config).unwrap();
        let root = candidate.root_physical_address().unwrap();
        let foreign_frame = allocator.allocate().unwrap();
        let virtual_address = 0xffff_9000_0000_1000;
        let root_index = super::page_table_indexes(virtual_address, candidate_config.levels)[0];
        memory.write_entry(root, root_index, foreign_frame.address() | 0x3);

        assert_eq!(
            candidate.walk(&memory, virtual_address),
            Err(PageWalkError::Reader(
                CandidatePageTableReadError::UnownedTable
            ))
        );
        candidate.release(&mut allocator).unwrap();
        allocator.deallocate(foreign_frame).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(allocator.free_frames(), 2);
    }

    #[test]
    fn candidate_page_tables_require_nx_and_report_unmapped_pages() {
        let mut allocator = candidate_allocator(2);
        let mut memory = CandidateTestMemory::new();
        let invalid = CandidatePageTables::new(
            &mut allocator,
            &mut memory,
            PageWalkConfig {
                nx_enabled: false,
                ..four_level_walk_config()
            },
        );
        let error = match invalid {
            Err(error) => error,
            Ok(_) => panic!("candidate creation unexpectedly accepted disabled NX"),
        };
        assert_eq!(error.cause, CandidateCreateErrorKind::InvalidConfiguration);
        assert_eq!(error.frame, None);

        let mut candidate =
            CandidatePageTables::new(&mut allocator, &mut memory, four_level_walk_config())
                .unwrap();
        assert_eq!(
            candidate.unmap_owned_page(&mut memory, 0xffff_9000_0000_1000),
            Err(CandidateUnmapError::NotMapped)
        );
        assert!(candidate.release(&mut allocator).is_ok());
    }

    #[test]
    fn candidate_page_tables_map_unmap_and_release_owned_frames() {
        let total_frames = 8;
        let mut allocator = candidate_allocator(total_frames);
        let mut memory = CandidateTestMemory::new();
        let mut candidate =
            CandidatePageTables::new(&mut allocator, &mut memory, four_level_walk_config())
                .unwrap();
        let root = candidate.root_physical_address().unwrap();
        assert_eq!(candidate.root_physical_address(), Some(root));
        let frame = allocator.allocate().unwrap();
        let physical = frame.address();
        let virtual_address = 0xffff_9000_0000_1000;
        let permissions = PagePermissions {
            writable: true,
            executable: false,
            user_accessible: true,
        };
        let (mapping, attributes) = candidate_mapping(&frame, virtual_address, permissions);

        candidate
            .map_owned_page(&mut allocator, &mut memory, frame, mapping, attributes)
            .unwrap();
        assert_eq!(candidate.table_count(), 4);
        assert_eq!(candidate.mapping_count(), 1);

        assert_eq!(
            candidate.walk(&memory, virtual_address).unwrap(),
            PageWalkOutcome::Mapped(PageTranslation {
                physical_address: physical,
                leaf_physical_base: physical,
                page_size: PAGE_SIZE,
                permissions,
                pat_index: 0,
                raw_leaf_entry: physical | 0x3 | (1 << 2) | (1 << 63),
            })
        );

        let duplicate_frame = allocator.allocate().unwrap();
        let (duplicate_mapping, duplicate_attributes) =
            candidate_mapping(&duplicate_frame, virtual_address, permissions);
        let free_before_duplicate = allocator.free_frames();
        let failure = candidate
            .map_owned_page(
                &mut allocator,
                &mut memory,
                duplicate_frame,
                duplicate_mapping,
                duplicate_attributes,
            )
            .unwrap_err();
        assert_eq!(failure.cause, CandidateMapErrorKind::MappingAlreadyPresent);
        assert_eq!(candidate.mapping_count(), 1);
        assert_eq!(allocator.free_frames(), free_before_duplicate);
        allocator.deallocate(failure.frame).unwrap();

        let returned = candidate
            .unmap_owned_page(&mut memory, virtual_address)
            .unwrap();
        assert_eq!(returned.address(), physical);
        assert_eq!(candidate.mapping_count(), 0);
        assert_eq!(
            candidate.walk(&memory, virtual_address).unwrap(),
            PageWalkOutcome::NotPresent {
                level: PageLevel::Pt,
            }
        );
        allocator.deallocate(returned).unwrap();
        candidate.release(&mut allocator).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(allocator.free_frames(), total_frames as u64);
    }

    #[test]
    fn candidate_page_table_mapping_rolls_back_on_frame_exhaustion() {
        let total_frames = 4;
        let mut allocator = candidate_allocator(total_frames);
        let mut memory = CandidateTestMemory::new();
        let mut candidate =
            CandidatePageTables::new(&mut allocator, &mut memory, four_level_walk_config())
                .unwrap();
        let frame = allocator.allocate().unwrap();
        let virtual_address = 0xffff_9000_0000_1000;
        let (mapping, attributes) = candidate_mapping(
            &frame,
            virtual_address,
            PagePermissions {
                writable: false,
                executable: false,
                user_accessible: false,
            },
        );
        let free_before_map = allocator.free_frames();

        let failure = candidate
            .map_owned_page(&mut allocator, &mut memory, frame, mapping, attributes)
            .unwrap_err();
        assert_eq!(failure.cause, CandidateMapErrorKind::OutOfFrames);
        assert_eq!(failure.rollback_retained_table_frames, 0);
        assert_eq!(allocator.free_frames(), free_before_map);
        assert_eq!(candidate.table_count(), 1);
        assert_eq!(candidate.mapping_count(), 0);
        allocator.deallocate(failure.frame).unwrap();
        candidate.release(&mut allocator).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(allocator.free_frames(), total_frames as u64);
    }

    #[test]
    fn candidate_page_table_mapping_rolls_back_after_prepare_failure() {
        let total_frames = 8;
        let mut allocator = candidate_allocator(total_frames);
        let mut memory = CandidateTestMemory::new();
        let mut candidate =
            CandidatePageTables::new(&mut allocator, &mut memory, four_level_walk_config())
                .unwrap();
        memory.fail_prepare_at = Some(3);
        let frame = allocator.allocate().unwrap();
        let virtual_address = 0xffff_9000_0000_1000;
        let (mapping, attributes) = candidate_mapping(
            &frame,
            virtual_address,
            PagePermissions {
                writable: false,
                executable: false,
                user_accessible: false,
            },
        );
        let free_before_map = allocator.free_frames();

        let failure = candidate
            .map_owned_page(&mut allocator, &mut memory, frame, mapping, attributes)
            .unwrap_err();
        assert_eq!(
            failure.cause,
            CandidateMapErrorKind::TableMemory(CandidateTestMemoryError::InjectedPrepareFailure)
        );
        assert_eq!(failure.rollback_retained_table_frames, 0);
        assert_eq!(allocator.free_frames(), free_before_map);
        assert_eq!(candidate.table_count(), 1);
        assert_eq!(candidate.mapping_count(), 0);
        allocator.deallocate(failure.frame).unwrap();
        candidate.release(&mut allocator).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(allocator.free_frames(), total_frames as u64);
    }

    #[test]
    fn candidate_page_tables_support_five_level_virtual_paths() {
        let total_frames = 8;
        let mut allocator = candidate_allocator(total_frames);
        let mut memory = CandidateTestMemory::new();
        let config = PageWalkConfig {
            levels: 5,
            virtual_address_bits: 57,
            ..four_level_walk_config()
        };
        let mut candidate = CandidatePageTables::new(&mut allocator, &mut memory, config).unwrap();
        let root = candidate.root_physical_address().unwrap();
        assert_eq!(candidate.root_physical_address(), Some(root));
        let frame = allocator.allocate().unwrap();
        let physical = frame.address();
        let virtual_address = 0xff00_0000_0020_1000;
        let (mapping, attributes) = candidate_mapping(
            &frame,
            virtual_address,
            PagePermissions {
                writable: false,
                executable: true,
                user_accessible: false,
            },
        );

        candidate
            .map_owned_page(&mut allocator, &mut memory, frame, mapping, attributes)
            .unwrap();
        assert_eq!(candidate.table_count(), 5);
        assert_eq!(
            candidate.walk(&memory, virtual_address).unwrap(),
            PageWalkOutcome::Mapped(PageTranslation {
                physical_address: physical,
                leaf_physical_base: physical,
                page_size: PAGE_SIZE,
                permissions: PagePermissions {
                    writable: false,
                    executable: true,
                    user_accessible: false,
                },
                pat_index: 0,
                raw_leaf_entry: physical | 0x1,
            })
        );
        candidate.release(&mut allocator).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(allocator.free_frames(), total_frames as u64);
    }

    #[test]
    fn rejects_arithmetic_overflow_and_writable_executable_ranges() {
        assert_eq!(
            validate_mapping_range(
                u64::MAX - (PAGE_SIZE - 1),
                0,
                PAGE_SIZE,
                KERNEL_READ_ONLY,
                Some(64),
                64
            ),
            Err(MappingError::AddressOverflow)
        );
        assert_eq!(
            validate_mapping_range(
                0x1000,
                u64::MAX - (PAGE_SIZE - 1),
                PAGE_SIZE,
                KERNEL_READ_ONLY,
                Some(64),
                64
            ),
            Err(MappingError::AddressOverflow)
        );

        let writable_executable = PagePermissions {
            writable: true,
            executable: true,
            user_accessible: false,
        };
        assert_eq!(
            validate_mapping_range(0x1000, 0x2000, PAGE_SIZE, writable_executable, Some(52), 48),
            Err(MappingError::WritableExecutable)
        );
    }
}

    70	## Engineering rules
    71	
    72	### Keep changes incremental and coherent
    73	
    74	1. Inspect the relevant source, tests, docs, and call sites before editing.
    75	2. State assumptions, invariants, and failure behavior for new kernel interfaces.
    76	3. Prefer small vertical slices that compile and can be tested over broad scaffolding or placeholder APIs.
    77	4. Update tests and documentation alongside behavior changes.
    78	5. Do not change unrelated code, rename files gratuitously, add speculative features, or rewrite project history.
    79	6. Do not commit or create branches unless the user explicitly asks.
    80	
    81	### Rust and dependency policy
    82	
    83	- Preserve the kernel's `no_std`/freestanding constraints. Do not introduce `std` into kernel code.
    84	- Prefer `core` and existing in-tree abstractions. Do not add third-party Rust dependencies without a concrete need and compatibility/security review.
    85	- Keep the Crabshell parser independent of kernel I/O and VFS implementation. Kernel execution belongs in `src/shell.rs` or an appropriate kernel service.
    86	- Do not add allocation-dependent APIs before a real heap exists. Fixed-capacity structures must document their limits and exhaustion behavior.
    87	- Respect the workspace structure and the host-testable `rustix-kernel` library versus freestanding `rustix` binary boundary.
    88	
    89	### Unsafe and hardware code
    90	
    91	Unsafe code is expected only at explicit hardware, boot-protocol, assembly, or raw-memory boundaries. Keep each unsafe block narrow and document the invariant that makes it sound. Do not add broad `unsafe impl`, mutable global references, unchecked pointer arithmetic, or unreviewed inline/global assembly.
    92	
    93	Before changing boot or memory code, account for these facts:
    94	
    95	- Limine fills response pointers before `_start`; the request records must remain writable in the ELF image.
    96	- Rustix validates nullness, alignment, counts, arithmetic, and physical ranges, but cannot prove that a non-null bootloader pointer is readable.
    97	- Physical ranges are half-open `[start, end)` and must use checked arithmetic.
    98	- Only regions classified `Usable` may enter the frame allocator. ACPI, bootloader-reclaimable, framebuffer, reserved, unknown, and other types are not free frames.
    99	- A `Frame` is a physical address, not a dereferenceable pointer. Do not access it through the HHDM or change CR3 until an explicit, reviewed mapping policy and ownership proof exist.
   100	- The kernel currently inherits Limine's page tables. Do not casually replace or mutate them: preserve the executing kernel, boot stack, `BootInfo`, request/response data, exception stacks, and mappings needed to continue execution.
   101	- The exception setup is fatal-only. It does not enable maskable interrupts, configure a PIC/APIC, or provide recovery. Do not call `sti` or claim interrupt support without an IRQ design and tests.
   102	- The shell and VFS run in ring 0 and are not isolated or secure.
   103	
   104	For hardware changes, document assumptions about CPU mode, selectors, stacks, page permissions, interrupt state, and failure handling. Avoid new architecture mechanisms that cannot be statically reviewed or validated.
   105	
   106	### Shell and filesystem contract
   107	
   108	- Crabshell is presently a kernel-mode serial shell, not a userspace program or a POSIX shell.
   109	- Its parser is a separate `no_std`, allocation-free crate; retain that boundary.
   110	- The RAM filesystem is volatile and bounded. Preserve explicit errors and test capacity, path, and mutation edge cases.
   111	- Do not imply persistence, permissions, links, process launching, or shell features that do not exist.
   112	- Update the parser tests and `docs/architecture/crabshell.md` when adding or changing commands.
   113	
   114	## Validation workflow
   115	
   116	Run the narrowest relevant checks first, then broaden them. From the repository root, the supported commands are:
   117	
   118	```sh
   119	just fmt
   120	just test
   121	just check
   122	just build
   123	just image
   124	just smoke
   125	just verify
   126	```
   127	
   128	`just test` runs host-side library tests (memory-map validation, frame allocator, VFS, and Crabshell parser). `just check` checks `x86_64-unknown-none`; `just build` links the optimized ELF. `just verify` includes formatting, host tests, target check, pinned Limine image creation, and QEMU prompt smoke test. Image/boot checks need Python, `xorriso`, QEMU, the Rust target, and network access for the first pinned Limine download; Linux/WSL also needs `cc` to build Limine's host utility.
   129	
   130	For changes to `src/main.rs`, `src/boot.rs`, linker/request configuration, `src/arch/x86_64/`, `src/frame.rs`, or paging/heap code, the intended full validation is `just verify`. If the environment does not permit a check, report the exact blocker and leave the corresponding roadmap criterion pending.
   131	
   132	Do not claim a check passed unless it was run and its successful result was observed. Editor diagnostics are useful but are not a substitute for `cargo test`, a target build, or QEMU. A target check is not a final link; a linked ELF is not proof of boot; a prompt smoke test is not proof of interactive shell behavior or physical-hardware correctness.
   133	
   134	## Completion criteria for agent changes
   135	
   136	Before reporting work complete:
   137	
   138	- Ensure source, tests, docs, and call sites agree.
   139	- Review unsafe and hardware assumptions, including error paths and capacity limits.
   140	- Run appropriate formatting/tests/build/boot checks, or clearly state why they could not run.
   141	- Report files changed, behavior delivered, validation actually observed, and remaining risks.
   142	- Keep milestone status accurate. A subsystem is not complete just because it has code.

````

     1	# Memory-management direction
     2	
     3	## What exists now
     4	
     5	`src/memory.rs` contains an allocation-free `MemoryMapBuilder` that copies Limine ranges into validated half-open physical regions. It rejects empty ranges, `base + length` overflow, overlapping ranges, empty maps, and maps exceeding the fixed 256-region capacity. Known Limine types remain distinct, and unknown type values are preserved. Host-side tests cover range validation/classification, canonical-address boundaries, physical-width bounds, and HHDM range arithmetic. `src/boot.rs` stores the resulting map in an owned boot snapshot and reports usable bytes.
     6	
     7	`src/frame.rs` provides a fixed-capacity allocator core with host-side tests. It only manages complete 4 KiB frames inside validated `Usable` regions, reserves the first MiB, and coalesces adjacent free ranges. The ownership contract assumes one allocator instance per physical map: within that instance, each eligible frame is owned either by its free-range table or by a non-copyable `Frame` token while allocated. The public constructor does not enforce unique instances, so callers must not initialize multiple allocators for the same physical map; the current boot path retains one allocator in `BootInfo`. `allocate` returns `None` when no free frame remains. `deallocate` consumes the token only on success; on any error, including free-range-table exhaustion, it returns a `DeallocationError` containing the original token and leaves allocator state unchanged. The range tables each have a fixed `MAX_FRAME_RANGES` capacity, so fragmentation can prevent a frame from being returned until nearby ranges coalesce. No kernel service currently allocates frames for mappings or other work.
     8	
     9	`Frame::address()` is a physical address value, not a dereferenceable pointer and not a proof that the frame is mapped. CPU diagnostics now read `CR4.LA57` to report the active linear-address width (48 or 57 bits) and query `CPUID.80000008H` for physical and maximum linear-address widths when available. Boot-protocol pointers are checked against the active width, with host tests for 48- and 57-bit canonical boundaries. These facts do not prove that any physical address is mapped.
    10	
    11	`src/paging.rs` adds pure, host-tested 4 KiB mapping groundwork and decodes the inherited CR3 root address plus its low-bit interpretation. The CR3 decoder validates the physical-address width and reserved bits and interprets the low 12 bits according to the active `CR4.PCIDE` state; it does not dereference the root. The mapping-range validator requires a known physical-address width, checked aligned bounds, canonical virtual endpoints in one canonical half, and rejects writable-executable permissions. A validated range can encode the raw bits of one 4 KiB leaf PTE, including supervisor/user and write permissions, NX when the caller confirms EFER.NXE, and a bounded three-bit PAT index. `PatLayout` parses a supplied `IA32_PAT` value and selects WB, UC, or WC indices. `MtrrMemoryType`, `VariableMtrr`, `FixedMtrrRanges`, and `MtrrLayout` resolve MTRR types at one physical address, including fixed-range priority and defined variable-overlap rules; undefined overlaps fail closed. `MtrrRegisters::validated_layout` additionally validates captured capability/default-type reserved bits, register counts and fixed-range presence, WC support, and variable-mask shape/alignment before producing an owned `ValidatedMtrrLayout`. It supports contiguous power-of-two variable masks; Intel permits discontinuous masks on some CPUs, but Rustix rejects them explicitly as unsupported rather than approximating their coverage. The layout combines the address-specific MTRR type with a selected PAT entry according to Intel SDM Table 11-7, but only when `CR0.CD` and `CR0.NW` are clear. Host tests cover all 30 documented MTRR/PAT type pairs and reject invalid indexes, malformed snapshots, out-of-range addresses, and non-normal caching mode. A pure range selector now returns the lowest PAT index that produces one requested effective type throughout a nonempty, aligned physical range, checking fixed- and variable-MTRR transition boundaries rather than iterating every page. It rejects the range if no single index works throughout. `ValidatedMappingRange::select_cache_attributes` composes that selector with a validated mapping extent and returns range-bound PAT attributes; those attributes can encode each 4 KiB leaf in that extent without reselecting per page. This is still policy-only: it trusts the supplied PAT/MTRR and normal-caching state, does not inspect existing PTEs or cache aliases, and does not establish frame ownership. Boot reads CR0 without modifying it, validates supported captured MTRR/PAT state, and reports a diagnostic resolution at physical address zero using PAT index 0; this does not inspect the inherited PTE or assert that the live mapping uses that index. The raw MTRR capture remains bounded to 32 variable pairs and reports capacity overflow without partial state. `Frame::hhdm_address` combines a non-copyable allocated-frame token with a known physical width and a full-page `Usable`-region check to calculate a Limine HHDM address; it returns only an integer and relies on the documented Limine mapping guarantee. The opt-in `just frame-smoke` path writes, reads, clears, and reclaims one such frame in QEMU. This validates one loader-backed HHDM access case, not arbitrary physical access or full page-table coverage. The opt-in walker follows only the paths needed for transition-critical ranges; no table is modified, and no mapping operation or CR3 transition is implemented.
    12	
    13	The effective-type resolver follows [Intel SDM Vol. 3A §11.5.2.2, Table 11-7](https://cdrdv2-public.intel.com/671447/325384-sdm-vol-3abcd.pdf), which applies when normal caching is enabled (`CR0.CD=0`, `CR0.NW=0`). Its footnotes distinguish UC selected by an MTRR from UC selected by a page-table entry (the latter involves cache snooping and aliasing concerns); they also identify combinations that older manual editions called undefined but current processors supporting both PAT and MTRRs resolve as shown. The resolver does not cover legacy PCD/PWT-only selection or model-specific combinations outside that table.
    14	
    15	The requested Limine base revision is 3. Its protocol maps only `Usable`, `BootloaderReclaimable`, `ExecutableAndModules`, and `Framebuffer` memory-map regions into the HHDM; reserved, ACPI, bad, and unknown regions are not in that mapping set. HHDM mappings use at least 4 KiB granularity and may cover page-aligned bytes beyond unaligned region boundaries. On x86_64, inherited HHDM mappings are supervisor RWX, normally write-back cached, with framebuffer mappings write-combining when PAT is available. Therefore an HHDM offset is not a blanket physical-memory access grant, and inherited HHDM permissions are not Rustix's future W^X policy. See the [Limine base revision 3 protocol](https://github.com/limine-bootloader/limine-protocol/blob/trunk/PROTOCOL.md#base-revision-3) and its memory-layout/caching sections.
    16	
    17	The boot snapshot now rejects physical map ranges beyond the reported CPUID physical-address width when that CPUID leaf is available. For base revision 3 HHDM-mapped types, it also validates the page-rounded physical span, checked `offset + address` arithmetic, and canonical endpoints in the active linear-address width. If the CPU does not report a physical width, the physical-bound check is skipped and no mapping caller may treat the bound as known. These checks are derived from metadata and Limine's protocol contract; they do not inspect page tables or prove that a non-null loader pointer is readable. The only HHDM dereference is the opt-in QEMU frame probe, which first validates an allocator-issued frame's full-page `Usable` backing and checked HHDM address; this remains a narrow reliance on Limine's handoff guarantee, not a general physical-memory access service. Rustix-owned mappings should be non-executable by default; executable kernel text must be explicit. MMIO requires an explicit device range and cache policy, and guard regions must remain unmapped. A page-table transition must preserve the kernel image, active stacks, boot data, descriptor tables, and any loader mappings still needed. Rustix does not reclaim bootloader memory, own or replace the inherited Limine page tables, or provide a heap. Bootstrap GDT/TSS/IDT setup and fatal exception diagnostics live in `src/arch/x86_64/interrupts.rs`; they do not enable maskable IRQs.
    18	
    19	## Mapping inventory before a CR3 transition
    20	
    21	The current runtime has several mappings that a future page-table transition must preserve. The address sources and remaining gaps are:
    22	
    23	- **Kernel ELF image:** `linker.ld` places `.text`, `.rodata`, `.limine_requests`, `.data`, `.bss`, and `.got` in three `PT_LOAD` segments: RX text, read-only rodata, and RW data/BSS. It exports `__kernel_start` and `__kernel_end` around the complete loadable image, plus page-aligned bounds for each segment. `BootInfo` checks that Limine's reported virtual base matches the linker start, validates ordered contiguous segment bounds covering the rounded image, derives corresponding half-open physical ranges from the executable physical base with checked arithmetic, and validates canonical virtual and reported physical address widths. The release ELF and QEMU runtime report both showed the three aligned ranges on 2026-10-21. The RX, R/NX, and RW/NX labels describe the linker segment intent; these are linker/boot metadata, not proof that the inherited page tables map every page or enforce those permissions, nor proof that loader pointers are readable. The memory-map `ExecutableAndModules` entries remain illustrative, not an authoritative kernel-image extent.
    24	- **Active stack and `BootInfo`:** The assembly `_start` shim captures Limine's entry `RSP` before any Rust prologue. Under the SysV entry convention the synthetic return slot occupies 8 bytes, so `RSP + 8` is the exclusive stack top. The protocol guarantees at least 64 KiB (without a Stack Size request); `BootInfo` records that minimum virtual span, translates it through the HHDM, and requires it to fit within a single `BootloaderReclaimable` physical region. The full loader allocation may be larger, and neither its exact bounds nor a guard page are known. Preserve the inherited mapping; do not infer a guard page.
    25	- **Kernel static data:** `RAM_FILESYSTEM`, GDT, IDT, TSS, the ring-0 stack, and double-fault IST stack are static BSS/data in the kernel image. Exception entry also requires the handler code and the TSS/IDT references to remain mapped. Preserve the complete relevant data/BSS pages and stack pages.
    26	- **Limine request data:** request records are in the kernel's writable `.limine_requests` segment. Response objects and the memory-map pointer array are bootloader-reclaimable; `capture_boot_information` copies the values used later, and the shell does not retain those pointers. Keep them mapped until the copy and validation finish; any later reclaim must be explicit rather than reclaiming the whole bootloader-reclaimable class.
    27	- **Inherited page tables:** Limine places its page tables in bootloader-reclaimable memory, but their layout is unspecified. `BootInfo` captures raw CR3 and validates a decoded physical root address plus the low-bit interpretation selected by active `CR4.PCIDE`. A pure helper requires the root page to fit in one validated `BootloaderReclaimable` range and calculates its HHDM address when the physical width is known. The opt-in QEMU probe reads the root's 512 entries and counts present bits, then follows bounded paths for every page in the kernel text/rodata/data and minimum boot-stack spans, checking physical translations. It does not enumerate unrelated mappings or verify inherited permissions, effective cache attributes, or aliases. Keep the old root and its backing pages intact while inspecting/building a replacement; do not reclaim them until a verified switch no longer depends on them.
    28	- **Devices:** COM1 uses x86 port I/O and needs no MMIO virtual mapping. Rustix does not currently request or use a framebuffer. Any future framebuffer or device-register mapping needs an explicit physical range and cache policy.
    29	
    30	## Initial kernel-owned mapping policy (design only)
    31	
    32	A first Rustix-owned x86_64 root should use 4 KiB pages only and require NX support; if NX is unavailable, abort before switching. Preserve ELF permissions exactly: text RX, rodata R/NX, and `.limine_requests`/data/BSS/GOT RW/NX. Reject W+X mappings. Exclude the complete physical kernel-image span from the generic HHDM in the first implementation so no writable direct-map alias can undermine text or rodata permissions. Ordinary RAM HHDM mappings should be RW/NX and WB.
    33	
    34	Preserve the inherited PAT/MTRR configuration during the first transition. The boot report validates captured registers and computes a diagnostic effective type from the active PAT/MTRR values under normal caching. A separate pure selector can choose an index whose effective type remains uniform across an aligned physical range, but neither checks inherited PTEs nor detects cache-type aliases. The pure combination follows Intel SDM Table 11-7; it is not a generic rule for legacy PCD/PWT-only selection or model-specific combinations. Under Limine base revision 3 on x86_64, use PAT index 0 for WB, index 3 for UC, and index 5 for WC only after the target physical range and active PAT/MTRR interaction are verified. Map MMIO only from explicit device ranges and use UC by default; do not infer MMIO from generic reserved memory-map entries. A framebuffer may use WC only after its response and cache policy are explicitly validated. COM1 uses port I/O and requires no MMIO mapping.
    35	
    36	Do not use huge pages in the first root; add them only when physical coverage, permissions, and cache attributes are uniform across the entire huge-page extent. Future Rustix-owned downward-growing stacks should have at least one 4 KiB unmapped guard page below them. The Limine bootstrap stack has no known guard, so none may be assumed there.
    37	
    38	Never modify Limine's active page tables in place. Build a separate candidate root from owned frames, leave the inherited root and its backing memory intact, and do not switch CR3 until every transition-critical mapping has been preserved and checked. Any pre-switch failure must discard the candidate root and return its frames without changing the active root. This policy is not yet implemented; Rustix does not inspect the inherited root or replace CR3.
    39	
    40	## Planned memory layers
    41	
    42	1. **Validated physical regions:** implemented as a fixed-capacity owned snapshot; allocator ownership and reclaim policy remain future work.
    43	2. **Frame allocator integration:** the bounded core is initialized from `BootInfo`; add real allocation callers only after the page-mapping policy and ownership rules are implemented.
    44	3. **Kernel virtual memory:** Rustix still runs on inherited Limine page tables. Before replacing them, preserve the executing kernel, bootstrap/Ring-0 stacks, request/response data, and exception stacks; define the HHDM extent and explicit mapping permissions/cache attributes. Keep writable-executable mappings disallowed by default and reserve MMIO and guard regions.
    45	4. **Heap:** add a global allocator only after frame allocation and page mapping are initialized. Define allocation failure behavior for kernel and interrupt contexts.
    46	5. **Process address spaces:** isolate userspace; define copy-in/copy-out helpers and never treat user pointers as kernel references.
    47	
    48	## Invariants to preserve
    49	
    50	- Physical ranges use checked arithmetic and the half-open convention `[start, end)`.
    51	- Only complete frames in validated `Usable` regions enter the allocator; the first MiB remains reserved. Firmware and loader-reclaimable regions are not silently promoted to free memory.
    52	- Under the single-allocator-per-physical-map contract, a frame is represented by one allocator-free range or one caller-owned, non-copyable `Frame` token. Only a successful `deallocate` transfers the token back to the allocator; errors return the token and leave allocator ranges and accounting unchanged. The current public constructor relies on callers to enforce unique allocator instances.
    53	- `allocate` returns `None` on frame exhaustion. Metadata-capacity exhaustion is an explicit error, never silent loss of a frame.
    54	- A `Frame` address is physical, not directly dereferenceable. No HHDM translation, page-table mutation, or CR3 switch is permitted until address widths, mapping coverage, permissions/cache attributes, and transition-preservation requirements are established.
    55	- Mapping changes validate alignment, canonical addresses, ownership, and permissions before touching tables.
    56	- User-controlled addresses are validated on every syscall boundary; prior validation is not a substitute for access checks during later copies.
    57	- Tests cover unaligned edges, exact-boundary allocations, arithmetic overflow, overlaps, exhaustion, and unchanged state/ownership on failure.
    58	
    59	These are design requirements for future milestones, not functionality delivered by the current boot summary.

     2	
     3	## Current checks
     4	
     5	`just verify` runs the standard development verification sequence:
     6	
     7	1. `just fmt` — fail on formatting differences across the workspace.
     8	2. `just test` — run host-side memory-map, mapping-range/PTE-bit policy, frame-allocator, RAM-filesystem, and Crabshell parser tests.
     9	3. `just check` — check the `x86_64-unknown-none` kernel target.
    10	4. `just smoke` — build the pinned hybrid ISO, boot it in QEMU, and check that Crabshell reaches its prompt within a deadline.
    11	
    12	`just frame-smoke` builds an opt-in kernel variant that allocates one `Usable` frame, validates its HHDM address, writes and reads the whole page, clears it, returns the frame, and checks the normal prompt in QEMU. It also validates and reads the inherited root page, then follows bounded 4-/5-level page-table paths for every page in the kernel image segments and minimum boot-stack span, checking translations against boot metadata. The workflow restores the default release kernel and ISO. The walk relies on Limine's HHDM contract; it does not change tables or prove full mapping, permission, cache-alias, or physical-hardware correctness. `just fault-smoke` separately builds opt-in kernel variants that deliberately trigger a page fault and an invalid opcode. It requires each QEMU run to report the expected exception (and CR2 for the page fault), avoid the shell prompt, and remain halted until timeout. It then rebuilds and restores the default release kernel and ISO. These are fatal-path diagnostics, not exception recovery tests; diagnostic Cargo features are disabled by default and mutually exclusive.
    13	
    14	Keep the Crabshell parser, VFS, memory-map validator, paging policy helpers, and frame allocator independent of hardware so syntax, path handling, address and leaf-PTE bit policy, PAT/MTRR policy, storage semantics, frame ownership, and HHDM/root-range calculations can be tested without booting. Pure tests validate captured MTRR register snapshots, resolve the Intel SDM Table 11-7 PAT/MTRR combinations for one physical address, select a PAT index that remains uniform across MTRR boundaries in an aligned range, bind that selection to validated mapping metadata before encoding leaves, and walk synthetic four-/five-level page tables including large-page leaves. They reject malformed state, unsupported discontinuous masks, invalid indexes/ranges, out-of-range addresses, mismatched physical widths, and non-normal caching mode. The pure walker does not access hardware tables; the opt-in QEMU reader does so through checked HHDM addresses. Neither path reads the active PAT MSR during a walk, proves frame ownership for inherited mappings, or validates live cache aliases. Boot separately captures the registers and CR0 caching mode read-only and reports a diagnostic resolution; this is not a page-table or mapping test. The GDT/TSS/IDT and CPU-register paths are privileged kernel code; QEMU boot and fault-injection checks complement, but do not replace, static review and target builds. Add tests for boundaries and failure behavior when introducing new pure kernel helpers. The kernel binary is not a host test target.
    15	
    16	## What current checks do not prove
    17	
    18	- `cargo check` does not perform a final target link.
    19	- A successful ELF link does not prove the boot protocol is recognized or `_start` is reached.
    20	- Host unit tests do not validate privileged instructions, UART behavior, memory-map pointer validity, page tables, interrupts, or actual hardware. The QEMU boot path exercises the gated EFER/PAT reads and bounded MTRR capture and prints diagnostic summaries, but the prompt smoke assertion does not make those facts a mapping-safety proof.
    21	- The automated QEMU prompt smoke test checks only that the kernel reaches the shell. `just frame-smoke` exercises one allocator-owned frame and bounded inherited page-table walks through the Limine HHDM contract, but does not modify tables or prove physical-hardware behavior. `just fault-smoke` separately exercises only the controlled page-fault and invalid-opcode fatal paths; it does not test every exception vector or recovery.
    22	- A separate manual QEMU session exercised directory navigation and file create/write/append/read/copy/move/remove operations, including `cp` replacing an existing destination and rejection of `rmdir` on a nonempty directory. This is not exhaustive shell coverage and does not prove persistence across reboot.
    23	- There is no on-disk filesystem integration test, syscall/userspace test, fuzz target, or physical-hardware test.
    24	
    25	## Validation policy
    26	
    27	For changes to the kernel entry, linker script, boot requests, architecture code, shell, or VFS, run `just verify`. For memory-management and ABI code, add negative tests for overflow, malformed ranges, permission failures, and invalid user pointers before exposing those paths to userspace.
    28	
    29	Record commands actually run and any environment limitation in change summaries; never call an unexecuted build “passing.”

//! Pure validation for future x86_64 4 KiB mappings.
//!
//! This module validates address shape and permissions only. It does not prove
//! frame ownership or mapping coverage, access physical memory, or modify tables.

use crate::frame::{Frame, FrameAllocator, FrameError};
use crate::memory::{
    is_canonical_virtual_address, physical_range_fits_address_width, HhdmAddressError, MemoryMap,
    RegionKind,
};

/// Base page size supported by the initial Rustix mapping policy.
pub const PAGE_SIZE: u64 = 4096;

/// The physical root address and interpretation of CR3's low bits.
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct Cr3Root {
    physical_address: u64,
    low_bits: Cr3LowBits,
}

impl Cr3Root {
    pub const fn physical_address(self) -> u64 {
        self.physical_address
    }

    pub const fn low_bits(self) -> Cr3LowBits {
        self.low_bits
    }
}

/// CR3's low bits are either a PCID or the paging-structure cache controls.
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum Cr3LowBits {
    Pcid(u16),
    CacheControls {
        page_level_write_through: bool,
        page_level_cache_disable: bool,
    },
}

#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum Cr3Error {
    UnknownPhysicalAddressWidth,
    InvalidPhysicalAddressWidth,
    ReservedBits,
}

#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum Cr3RootAccessError {
    NotBootloaderReclaimable,
    Hhdm(HhdmAddressError),
}

/// Decode the currently active CR3 value without dereferencing its root table.
///
/// The caller supplies the reported physical-address width and whether CR4.PCIDE
/// is active, since those determine the valid address and low-bit encodings.
pub fn parse_cr3_root(
    raw: u64,
    physical_address_bits: Option<u8>,
    pcid_enabled: bool,
) -> Result<Cr3Root, Cr3Error> {
    let physical_address_bits =
        physical_address_bits.ok_or(Cr3Error::UnknownPhysicalAddressWidth)?;
    if !(12..=MAX_PTE_PHYSICAL_ADDRESS_BITS).contains(&physical_address_bits) {
        return Err(Cr3Error::InvalidPhysicalAddressWidth);
    }

    let physical_mask = ((1u64 << physical_address_bits) - 1) & !(PAGE_SIZE - 1);
    let low_mask = if pcid_enabled {
        PAGE_SIZE - 1
    } else {
        (1 << 3) | (1 << 4)
    };
    if raw & !(physical_mask | low_mask) != 0 {
        return Err(Cr3Error::ReservedBits);
    }

    let low_bits = if pcid_enabled {
        Cr3LowBits::Pcid((raw & (PAGE_SIZE - 1)) as u16)
    } else {
        Cr3LowBits::CacheControls {
            page_level_write_through: raw & (1 << 3) != 0,
            page_level_cache_disable: raw & (1 << 4) != 0,
        }
    };

    Ok(Cr3Root {
        physical_address: raw & physical_mask,
        low_bits,
    })
}

/// Calculate the protocol-backed HHDM address of Limine's inherited root page.
///
/// This requires the root page to be wholly contained in bootloader-reclaimable
/// memory, as specified for Limine page tables. It does not dereference the page
/// or prove that the active hierarchy contains the HHDM mapping.
pub fn inherited_cr3_root_hhdm_address(
    root: Cr3Root,
    memory_map: &MemoryMap,
    hhdm_offset: u64,
    physical_address_bits: Option<u8>,
    virtual_address_bits: u8,
) -> Result<u64, Cr3RootAccessError> {
    let physical_start = root.physical_address();
    let physical_end = physical_start
        .checked_add(PAGE_SIZE)
        .ok_or(Cr3RootAccessError::Hhdm(HhdmAddressError::AddressOverflow))?;
    if !memory_map.range_is_within_region_kind(
        physical_start,
        physical_end,
        RegionKind::BootloaderReclaimable,
    ) {
        return Err(Cr3RootAccessError::NotBootloaderReclaimable);
    }
    memory_map
        .limine_hhdm_address(
            hhdm_offset,
            physical_start,
            PAGE_SIZE,
            physical_address_bits,
            virtual_address_bits,
        )
        .map_err(Cr3RootAccessError::Hhdm)
}

#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum PageLevel {
    Pml5,
    Pml4,
    Pdpt,
    Pd,
    Pt,
}

#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct PageWalkConfig {
    pub levels: u8,
    pub physical_address_bits: u8,
    pub virtual_address_bits: u8,
    pub nx_enabled: bool,
    pub page_2m_supported: bool,
    pub page_1g_supported: bool,
}

#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct PageTranslation {
    pub physical_address: u64,
    pub leaf_physical_base: u64,
    pub page_size: u64,
    pub permissions: PagePermissions,
    pub pat_index: u8,
    pub raw_leaf_entry: u64,
}

#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum PageWalkOutcome {
    NotPresent { level: PageLevel },
    Mapped(PageTranslation),
}

#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum PageTableEntryError {
    PhysicalAddressOutOfRange,
    NxDisabled,
    LargePageUnsupported,
    LargePageAtInvalidLevel,
    LargePageMisaligned,
}

#[derive(Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum PageWalkError<E> {
    InvalidConfiguration,
    NonCanonicalAddress,
    InvalidRoot,
    InvalidEntry {
        level: PageLevel,

    },

/// Read one raw entry from a table at a validated physical page address.
pub trait PageTableReader {
    type Error;

    fn read_entry(&self, table_physical: u64, index: u16) -> Result<u64, Self::Error>;
}

/// Translate one virtual address by following at most five page-table entries.
///
/// The reader owns all physical-memory access policy. This walker does not turn
/// physical addresses into pointers, modify tables, or infer effective cache
/// types from the leaf PAT selector.
pub fn walk_virtual_address<R: PageTableReader>(
    reader: &R,
    root: Cr3Root,
    virtual_address: u64,
    config: PageWalkConfig,
) -> Result<PageWalkOutcome, PageWalkError<R::Error>> {
    if !(12..=MAX_PTE_PHYSICAL_ADDRESS_BITS).contains(&config.physical_address_bits)
        || (config.levels != 4 && config.levels != 5)
        || config.virtual_address_bits != if config.levels == 4 { 48 } else { 57 }
    {
        return Err(PageWalkError::InvalidConfiguration);
    }
    if !is_canonical_virtual_address(virtual_address, config.virtual_address_bits) {
        return Err(PageWalkError::NonCanonicalAddress);
    }
    let root_physical = root.physical_address();
    let root_end = root_physical
        .checked_add(PAGE_SIZE)
        .ok_or(PageWalkError::InvalidRoot)?;
    if root_physical & (PAGE_SIZE - 1) != 0
        || !physical_range_fits_address_width(root_physical, root_end, config.physical_address_bits)
    {
        return Err(PageWalkError::InvalidRoot);
    }

    const PRESENT: u64 = 1;
    const WRITABLE: u64 = 1 << 1;
    const USER: u64 = 1 << 2;
    const WRITE_THROUGH: u64 = 1 << 3;
    const CACHE_DISABLE: u64 = 1 << 4;
    const PAGE_SIZE_OR_PAT: u64 = 1 << 7;
    const LARGE_PAGE_PAT: u64 = 1 << 12;
    const NO_EXECUTE: u64 = 1 << 63;
    const ADDRESS_FIELD_MASK: u64 = 0x000f_ffff_ffff_f000;

    let physical_mask = ((1u64 << config.physical_address_bits) - 1) & !(PAGE_SIZE - 1);
    let mut table_physical = root_physical;
    let mut writable = true;
    let mut user_accessible = true;
    let mut executable = true;
    let mut level_number = config.levels;

    loop {
        let shift = 12 + 9 * (level_number - 1);
        let index = ((virtual_address >> shift) & 0x1ff) as u16;
        let entry = reader
            .read_entry(table_physical, index)
            .map_err(PageWalkError::Reader)?;
        let level = match level_number {
            5 => PageLevel::Pml5,
            4 => PageLevel::Pml4,
            3 => PageLevel::Pdpt,
            2 => PageLevel::Pd,
            1 => PageLevel::Pt,
            _ => return Err(PageWalkError::InvalidConfiguration),
        };
        if entry & PRESENT == 0 {
            return Ok(PageWalkOutcome::NotPresent { level });
        }

        let address_field = entry & ADDRESS_FIELD_MASK;
        if address_field & !physical_mask != 0 {
            return Err(PageWalkError::InvalidEntry {
                level,
                error: PageTableEntryError::PhysicalAddressOutOfRange,
            });
        }
        if !config.nx_enabled && entry & NO_EXECUTE != 0 {
            return Err(PageWalkError::InvalidEntry {
                level,
                error: PageTableEntryError::NxDisabled,
            });
        }

        user_accessible &= entry & USER != 0;
        executable &= entry & NO_EXECUTE == 0;

        let large_page = level_number > 1 && entry & PAGE_SIZE_OR_PAT != 0;
        let leaf_shift = if level_number == 1 {
            12
        } else if large_page && level_number == 2 && config.page_2m_supported {
            21
        } else if large_page && level_number == 3 && config.page_1g_supported {
            30
        } else if large_page && level_number <= 3 {
            return Err(PageWalkError::InvalidEntry {
                level,
                error: PageTableEntryError::LargePageUnsupported,
            });
        } else if large_page {
            return Err(PageWalkError::InvalidEntry {
                level,
                error: PageTableEntryError::LargePageAtInvalidLevel,
            });
        } else {
            table_physical = address_field;
            level_number -= 1;
            continue;
        };

        if large_page {
            let reserved_alignment_bits = ((1u64 << leaf_shift) - 1) & !0x1fff;
            if entry & reserved_alignment_bits != 0 {
                return Err(PageWalkError::InvalidEntry {
                    level,
                    error: PageTableEntryError::LargePageMisaligned,
                });
            }
        }
        let page_size = 1u64 << leaf_shift;
        let leaf_physical_base = address_field & !(page_size - 1);
        let leaf_physical_end =
            leaf_physical_base
                .checked_add(page_size)
                .ok_or(PageWalkError::InvalidEntry {
                    level,
                    error: PageTableEntryError::PhysicalAddressOutOfRange,
                })?;
        if !physical_range_fits_address_width(
            leaf_physical_base,
            leaf_physical_end,
            config.physical_address_bits,
        ) {
            return Err(PageWalkError::InvalidEntry {
                level,
                error: PageTableEntryError::PhysicalAddressOutOfRange,
            });
        }
        let pat_bit = if large_page {
            entry & LARGE_PAGE_PAT != 0
        } else {
            entry & PAGE_SIZE_OR_PAT != 0
        };
        let pat_index = (u8::from(pat_bit) << 2)
            | (u8::from(entry & CACHE_DISABLE != 0) << 1)
            | u8::from(entry & WRITE_THROUGH != 0);
        return Ok(PageWalkOutcome::Mapped(PageTranslation {
            physical_address: leaf_physical_base | (virtual_address & (page_size - 1)),
            leaf_physical_base,
            page_size,
            permissions: PagePermissions {
                writable,
                executable,
                user_accessible,
            },
            pat_index,
            raw_leaf_entry: entry,
        }));
    }
}

#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct PagePermissions {
    pub writable: bool,
    pub executable: bool,
    pub user_accessible: bool,
}

/// A mapping range whose arithmetic, address widths, alignment, and W^X policy passed validation.
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct ValidatedMappingRange {
    virtual_start: u64,
    virtual_end: u64,
    physical_start: u64,
    physical_end: u64,
    physical_address_bits: u8,
    permissions: PagePermissions,
}

/// PAT selection for one physical extent, derived from supplied PAT/MTRR state.
///
/// This records a uniform effective type across the range, but does not inspect
/// existing mappings or prove that aliases use compatible cache attributes.
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct SelectedCacheAttributes {
    physical_start: u64,
    physical_end: u64,
    pat_index: u8,
    effective_type: EffectiveMemoryType,
}

impl SelectedCacheAttributes {
    pub const fn physical_start(self) -> u64 {
        self.physical_start
    }

    pub const fn physical_end(self) -> u64 {
        self.physical_end
    }

    pub const fn pat_index(self) -> u8 {
        self.pat_index
    }

    pub const fn effective_type(self) -> EffectiveMemoryType {
        self.effective_type
    }
}

impl ValidatedMappingRange {
    pub const fn virtual_start(self) -> u64 {
        self.virtual_start
    }

    pub const fn virtual_end(self) -> u64 {
        self.virtual_end
    }

    pub const fn physical_start(self) -> u64 {
        self.physical_start
    }

    pub const fn physical_end(self) -> u64 {
        self.physical_end
    }

    pub const fn permissions(self) -> PagePermissions {
        self.permissions
    }

    pub const fn length(self) -> u64 {
        self.virtual_end - self.virtual_start
    }

    /// Select PAT attributes that yield one effective type across this range.
    ///
    /// The supplied PAT/MTRR snapshot and `normal_caching` flag must reflect the
    /// active hardware state. This is a policy calculation only; it does not
    /// inspect existing mappings or detect cache-type aliases.
    pub fn select_cache_attributes(
        self,
        policy: CachePolicy,
        pat: PatLayout,
        mtrrs: &ValidatedMtrrLayout,
        normal_caching: bool,
    ) -> Result<SelectedCacheAttributes, MappingError> {
        if self.physical_address_bits != mtrrs.physical_address_bits {
            return Err(MappingError::MtrrPhysicalAddressWidthMismatch);
        }

        let effective_type = match policy {
            CachePolicy::WriteBack => EffectiveMemoryType::WriteBack,
            CachePolicy::Uncacheable => EffectiveMemoryType::Uncacheable,
            CachePolicy::WriteCombining => EffectiveMemoryType::WriteCombining,
        };
        let pat_index = mtrrs
            .select_pat_index_for_range(
                self.physical_start,
                self.length(),
                pat,
                effective_type,
                normal_caching,
            )
            .map_err(MappingError::CachePolicy)?;

        Ok(SelectedCacheAttributes {
            physical_start: self.physical_start,
            physical_end: self.physical_end,
            pat_index,
            effective_type,
        })
    }

    /// Encode a 4 KiB leaf PTE using attributes selected for this physical range.
    pub fn leaf_4k_entry_with_cache_attributes(
        self,
        page_offset: u64,
        cache_attributes: SelectedCacheAttributes,
        nx_enabled: bool,
    ) -> Result<PageTableEntry, MappingError> {
        if cache_attributes.physical_start != self.physical_start
            || cache_attributes.physical_end != self.physical_end
        {
            return Err(MappingError::CacheAttributesRangeMismatch);
        }
        self.leaf_4k_entry(page_offset, cache_attributes.pat_index, nx_enabled)
    }

    /// Encode a single 4 KiB leaf PTE within this validated range.
    ///
    /// `pat_index` is the raw three-bit PAT index; the caller must have verified
