```
    if arch::x86_64::cpu::read_cr3_raw() != inherited_cr3 {
        kprintln!("page-table transition aborted: active CR3 changed before switch");
        release_candidate_after_probe_failure(candidate, &mut boot_info.frame_allocator);
    }
    // SAFETY: The candidate is a complete clone of every present inherited
    // hierarchy entry, with all referenced intermediate tables owned and the
    // critical code/data/stack paths compared before this point. The inherited
    // root's paging mode, address widths, PAT/MTRR state, and low CR3 mode are
    // preserved; interrupts are disabled from bootstrap initialization onward.
    unsafe { arch::x86_64::cpu::write_cr3_raw(new_cr3) };
    if arch::x86_64::cpu::read_cr3_raw() != new_cr3
        || !spans
            .iter()
            .all(|(_, virtual_start, physical_start, length)| {
                candidate_span_matches_source(
                    &candidate,
                    &reader,
                    inherited_root,
                    config,
                    *virtual_start,
                    *physical_start,
                    *length,
                )
            })
    {
        // SAFETY: The inherited root and its backing memory remain untouched and
        // mapped by the candidate, so restoring its validated CR3 value is safe.
        unsafe { arch::x86_64::cpu::write_cr3_raw(inherited_cr3) };
        kprintln!("page-table transition failed post-switch verification; restored inherited CR3");
        release_candidate_after_probe_failure(candidate, &mut boot_info.frame_allocator);
    }
    kprintln!(
        "page-table transition passed: active CR3={:#x}, cloned root={:#x}, {} owned tables",
        new_cr3,
        candidate_root,
        candidate.table_count()
    );

    // Keep the candidate and its frame tokens alive for as long as this root is
    // active. The shell runs forever and does not return to this stack frame.
    // SAFETY: The bootstrap is single-core, interrupts remain disabled, and the
    // shell is the only filesystem owner.
    let filesystem = unsafe { &mut *core::ptr::addr_of_mut!(RAM_FILESYSTEM) };
    match filesystem.seed_defaults() {
        Ok(home) => shell::run(filesystem, home, boot_info),
        Err(error) => {
            kprintln!("RAM filesystem initialization failed: {:?}", error);
            halt_forever()
        }
    }
}

#[cfg(feature = "probe-hhdm-frame")]
fn probe_hhdm_frame(boot_info: &mut boot::BootInfo) {
    use rustix_kernel::frame::FRAME_SIZE;

    let frame = match boot_info.frame_allocator.allocate() {
        Some(frame) => frame,
        None => {
            kprintln!("HHDM frame probe failed: no free frame");
            halt_forever();
        }
    };
    let hhdm_address = match frame.hhdm_address(
        &boot_info.memory_map,
        boot_info.hhdm_offset,
        boot_info.cpu_info.physical_address_bits,
        boot_info.cpu_info.active_linear_address_bits,
    ) {
        Ok(address) => address,
        Err(error) => {
            kprintln!("HHDM frame probe rejected frame translation: {:?}", error);
            release_probe_frame(&mut boot_info.frame_allocator, frame);
            halt_forever();
        }
    };

    let words = (FRAME_SIZE / core::mem::size_of::<u64>() as u64) as usize;
    let page = hhdm_address as *mut u64;
    let mut verified = true;
    // SAFETY: The non-copyable `Frame` token is held exclusively; its full page
    // is within validated `Usable` memory and its HHDM arithmetic was checked.
    // Limine base revision 3 guarantees usable memory in the HHDM, and no other
    // Rustix mapping aliases this newly allocated frame. This is an opt-in QEMU
    // probe; a broken loader mapping would fault and be caught by the fatal path.
    unsafe {
        for index in 0..words {
            page.add(index)
                .write_volatile(0xa5a5_0000_0000_0000 ^ index as u64);
        }
        for index in 0..words {
            if page.add(index).read_volatile() != (0xa5a5_0000_0000_0000 ^ index as u64) {
                verified = false;
                break;
            }
        }
        for index in 0..words {
            page.add(index).write_volatile(0);
        }
    }

    release_probe_frame(&mut boot_info.frame_allocator, frame);
    if !verified {
        kprintln!("HHDM frame probe failed: readback mismatch");
        halt_forever();
    }
    kprintln!("HHDM frame probe passed: wrote, read, cleared, and reclaimed one frame");
    probe_inherited_root(boot_info);
}

#[cfg(feature = "probe-hhdm-frame")]
fn probe_inherited_root(boot_info: &mut boot::BootInfo) {
    use rustix_kernel::paging::inherited_cr3_root_hhdm_address;

    let root = match boot_info.inherited_cr3_root {
        Ok(root) => root,
        Err(error) => {
            kprintln!(
                "inherited root probe failed: CR3 decode rejected: {:?}",
                error
            );
            halt_forever();
        }
    };
    let address = match inherited_cr3_root_hhdm_address(
        root,
        &boot_info.memory_map,
        boot_info.hhdm_offset,
        boot_info.cpu_info.physical_address_bits,
        boot_info.cpu_info.active_linear_address_bits,
    ) {
        Ok(address) => address,
        Err(error) => {
            kprintln!(
                "inherited root probe failed: HHDM validation rejected: {:?}",
                error
            );
            halt_forever();
        }
    };
    let entries = address as *const u64;
    let mut present_entries = 0;
    // SAFETY: The complete root page was validated as bootloader-reclaimable
    // and its HHDM range arithmetic was checked. The Limine base-revision-3
    // contract maps that region; this read-only opt-in probe trusts that handoff.
    unsafe {
        for index in 0..512 {
            if entries.add(index).read_volatile() & 1 != 0 {
                present_entries += 1;
            }
        }
    }
    kprintln!(
        "inherited root HHDM probe passed: read 512 entries, {} present",
        present_entries
    );
    let physical_address_bits = match boot_info.cpu_info.physical_address_bits {
        Some(bits) => bits,
        None => {
            kprintln!("inherited page-table walk failed: physical width unknown");
            halt_forever();
        }
    };
    let reader = LimineHhdmPageTableReader {
        memory_map: &boot_info.memory_map,
        hhdm_offset: boot_info.hhdm_offset,
        physical_address_bits,
        virtual_address_bits: boot_info.cpu_info.active_linear_address_bits,
    };
    let config = rustix_kernel::paging::PageWalkConfig {
        levels: if boot_info.cpu_info.active_linear_address_bits == 57 {
            5
        } else {
            4
        },
        physical_address_bits,
        virtual_address_bits: boot_info.cpu_info.active_linear_address_bits,
        nx_enabled: boot_info.cpu_info.nx_enabled,
        page_2m_supported: true,
        page_1g_supported: boot_info.cpu_info.has_1g_pages,
    };
    let segments = boot_info.kernel_image_segments;
    verify_inherited_mapping(
        &reader,
        root,
        config,
        "kernel text",
        segments.text.virtual_start,
        segments.text.physical_start,
        segments.text.virtual_end - segments.text.virtual_start,
    );
    verify_inherited_mapping(
        &reader,
        root,
        config,
        "kernel rodata",
        segments.rodata.virtual_start,
        segments.rodata.physical_start,
        segments.rodata.virtual_end - segments.rodata.virtual_start,
    );
    verify_inherited_mapping(
        &reader,
        root,
        config,
        "kernel data",
        segments.data.virtual_start,
        segments.data.physical_start,
        segments.data.virtual_end - segments.data.virtual_start,
    );
    verify_inherited_mapping(
        &reader,
        root,
        config,
        "active boot stack",
        boot_info.boot_stack_virtual_start,
        boot_info.boot_stack_physical_start,
        boot_info.boot_stack_virtual_end - boot_info.boot_stack_virtual_start,
    );

    let pat_value = match boot_info.cpu_info.pat_msr_value {
        Some(value) => value,
        None => {
            kprintln!("cache-alias probe failed: active PAT value unavailable");
            halt_forever();
        }
    };
    let pat = match rustix_kernel::paging::PatLayout::from_msr_value(pat_value) {
        Ok(pat) => pat,
        Err(error) => {
            kprintln!("cache-alias probe failed: invalid PAT layout: {:?}", error);
            halt_forever();
        }
    };
    let registers = match &boot_info.cpu_info.mtrr {
        rustix_kernel::paging::MtrrState::Captured(registers) => registers,
        _ => {
            kprintln!("cache-alias probe failed: captured MTRR state unavailable");
            halt_forever();
        }
    };
    let mtrrs = match registers.validated_layout(physical_address_bits) {
        Ok(mtrrs) => mtrrs,
        Err(error) => {
            kprintln!("cache-alias probe failed: invalid MTRR state: {:?}", error);
            halt_forever();
        }
    };
    if !boot_info.cpu_info.normal_caching {
        kprintln!("cache-alias probe failed: non-normal CR0 caching mode");
        halt_forever();
    }
    verify_kernel_cache_aliases(
        boot_info,
        &reader,
        root,
        config,
        pat,
        &mtrrs,
        "kernel text",
        segments.text.virtual_start,
        segments.text.physical_start,
        segments.text.virtual_end - segments.text.virtual_start,
    );
    verify_kernel_cache_aliases(
        boot_info,
        &reader,
        root,
        config,
        pat,
        &mtrrs,
        "kernel rodata",
        segments.rodata.virtual_start,
        segments.rodata.physical_start,
        segments.rodata.virtual_end - segments.rodata.virtual_start,
    );
    verify_kernel_cache_aliases(
        boot_info,
        &reader,
        root,
        config,
        pat,
        &mtrrs,
        "kernel data",
        segments.data.virtual_start,
        segments.data.physical_start,
        segments.data.virtual_end - segments.data.virtual_start,
    );
    probe_cloned_page_tables(
        &mut boot_info.frame_allocator,
        &boot_info.memory_map,
        boot_info.hhdm_offset,
        physical_address_bits,
        boot_info.cpu_info.active_linear_address_bits,
        &reader,
        root,
        config,
        [
            (
                "kernel text",
                segments.text.virtual_start,
                segments.text.physical_start,
                segments.text.virtual_end - segments.text.virtual_start,
            ),
            (
                "kernel rodata",
                segments.rodata.virtual_start,
                segments.rodata.physical_start,
                segments.rodata.virtual_end - segments.rodata.virtual_start,
            ),
            (
                "kernel data",
                segments.data.virtual_start,
                segments.data.physical_start,
                segments.data.virtual_end - segments.data.virtual_start,
            ),
            (
                "active boot stack",
                boot_info.boot_stack_virtual_start,
                boot_info.boot_stack_physical_start,
                boot_info.boot_stack_virtual_end - boot_info.boot_stack_virtual_start,
            ),
        ],
    );
    probe_candidate_page_tables(boot_info);
}

#[cfg(feature = "probe-hhdm-frame")]
fn probe_cloned_page_tables(
    allocator: &mut rustix_kernel::frame::FrameAllocator,
    memory_map: &rustix_kernel::memory::MemoryMap,
    hhdm_offset: u64,
    physical_address_bits: u8,
    virtual_address_bits: u8,
    source_reader: &impl rustix_kernel::paging::PageTableReader<
        Error = rustix_kernel::memory::HhdmAddressError,
    >,
    source_root: rustix_kernel::paging::Cr3Root,
    config: rustix_kernel::paging::PageWalkConfig,
    spans: [(&str, u64, u64, u64); 4],
) {
    use rustix_kernel::paging::CandidatePageTables;

    let mut memory = LimineHhdmCandidateMemory {
        memory_map,
        hhdm_offset,
        physical_address_bits,
        virtual_address_bits,
    };
    let mut candidate = match CandidatePageTables::new(allocator, &mut memory, config) {
        Ok(candidate) => candidate,
        Err(error) => {
            kprintln!(
                "candidate clone probe failed to create root: {:?}",
                error.cause
            );
            if let Some(frame) = error.frame {
                release_probe_frame(allocator, frame);
            }
            halt_forever();
        }
    };
    if let Err(error) = candidate.clone_inherited_hierarchy(allocator, source_reader, source_root) {
        kprintln!("candidate clone probe failed: {:?}", error);
        release_candidate_after_probe_failure(candidate, allocator);
    }
    for (label, virtual_start, physical_start, length) in spans {
        if !candidate_span_matches_source(
            &candidate,
            source_reader,
            source_root,
            config,
            virtual_start,
            physical_start,
            length,
        ) {
            kprintln!(
                "candidate clone probe failed: {} translation mismatch",
                label
            );
            release_candidate_after_probe_failure(candidate, allocator);
        }
    }
    let table_count = candidate.table_count();
    if let Err(failure) = candidate.release(allocator) {
        kprintln!(
            "candidate clone probe failed to release frames: {:?}",
            failure
        );
        halt_forever();
    }
    kprintln!(
        "candidate inherited-root clone probe passed: {} owned table pages preserve critical paths; CR3 unchanged",
        table_count
    );
}

fn candidate_span_matches_source(
    candidate: &rustix_kernel::paging::CandidatePageTables<'_, LimineHhdmCandidateMemory<'_>>,
    source_reader: &impl rustix_kernel::paging::PageTableReader<
        Error = rustix_kernel::memory::HhdmAddressError,
    >,
    source_root: rustix_kernel::paging::Cr3Root,
    config: rustix_kernel::paging::PageWalkConfig,
    virtual_start: u64,
    physical_start: u64,
    length: u64,
) -> bool {
    use rustix_kernel::paging::{walk_virtual_address, PageWalkOutcome};

    let mut offset = 0;
    while offset < length {
        let Some(virtual_address) = virtual_start.checked_add(offset) else {
            return false;
        };
        let Some(expected_physical) = physical_start.checked_add(offset) else {
            return false;
        };
        let source_result =
            walk_virtual_address(source_reader, source_root, virtual_address, config);
        let candidate_result = candidate.walk(virtual_address);
        let (source_translation, candidate_translation) = match (source_result, candidate_result) {
            (Ok(PageWalkOutcome::Mapped(source)), Ok(PageWalkOutcome::Mapped(candidate))) => {
                (source, candidate)
            }
            (source, candidate) => {
                kprintln!(
                    "candidate clone walk mismatch at {:#018x}: inherited={:?}, candidate={:?}",
                    virtual_address,
                    source,
                    candidate
                );
                return false;
            }
        };
        // The CPU may update Accessed/Dirty in the active hierarchy after the
        // clone; they are hardware tracking state, not translation policy.
        let hardware_tracking_bits = (1 << 5) | (1 << 6);
        if source_translation.physical_address != candidate_translation.physical_address
            || source_translation.leaf_physical_base != candidate_translation.leaf_physical_base
            || source_translation.page_size != candidate_translation.page_size
            || source_translation.permissions != candidate_translation.permissions
            || source_translation.pat_index != candidate_translation.pat_index
            || source_translation.raw_leaf_entry & !hardware_tracking_bits
                != candidate_translation.raw_leaf_entry & !hardware_tracking_bits
            || candidate_translation.physical_address != expected_physical
        {
            kprintln!(
                "candidate clone translation mismatch at {:#018x}: inherited={:?}, candidate={:?}, expected PA={:#x}",
                virtual_address,
                source_translation,
                candidate_translation,
                expected_physical
            );
            return false;
        }
        let Some(next_offset) = offset.checked_add(rustix_kernel::paging::PAGE_SIZE) else {
            return false;
        };
        offset = next_offset;
    }
    true
}

#[cfg(feature = "probe-hhdm-frame")]
fn probe_candidate_page_tables(boot_info: &mut boot::BootInfo) {
    use rustix_kernel::paging::{
        validate_mapping_range, CachePolicy, CandidatePageTables, PagePermissions, PageWalkOutcome,
    };

    let Some(physical_address_bits) = boot_info.cpu_info.physical_address_bits else {
        kprintln!("candidate page-table probe failed: physical width unknown");
        halt_forever();
    };
    if !boot_info.cpu_info.nx_enabled || !boot_info.cpu_info.normal_caching {
        kprintln!("candidate page-table probe failed: NXE or normal caching unavailable");
        halt_forever();
    }
    let pat_value = boot_info
        .cpu_info
        .pat_msr_value
        .expect("inherited cache-alias probe validated active PAT");
    let pat = rustix_kernel::paging::PatLayout::from_msr_value(pat_value).unwrap_or_else(|error| {
        kprintln!(
            "candidate page-table probe failed: invalid PAT: {:?}",
            error
        );
        halt_forever();
    });
    let registers = match &boot_info.cpu_info.mtrr {
        rustix_kernel::paging::MtrrState::Captured(registers) => registers,
        _ => {
            kprintln!("candidate page-table probe failed: captured MTRR state unavailable");
            halt_forever();
        }
    };
    let mtrrs = match registers.validated_layout(physical_address_bits) {
        Ok(mtrrs) => mtrrs,
        Err(error) => {
            kprintln!(
                "candidate page-table probe failed: invalid MTRR: {:?}",
                error
            );
            halt_forever();
        }
    };
    let config = rustix_kernel::paging::PageWalkConfig {
        levels: if boot_info.cpu_info.active_linear_address_bits == 57 {
            5
        } else {
            4
        },
        physical_address_bits,
        virtual_address_bits: boot_info.cpu_info.active_linear_address_bits,
        nx_enabled: true,
        page_2m_supported: true,
        page_1g_supported: boot_info.cpu_info.has_1g_pages,
    };
    let virtual_address = 0xffff_9000_ffff_f000;
    let permissions = PagePermissions {
        writable: true,
        executable: false,
        user_accessible: false,
    };
    let frame = match boot_info.frame_allocator.allocate() {
        Some(frame) => frame,
        None => {
            kprintln!("candidate page-table probe failed: no leaf frame available");
            halt_forever();
        }
    };
    let mapping = match validate_mapping_range(
        virtual_address,
        frame.address(),
        rustix_kernel::paging::PAGE_SIZE,
        permissions,
        Some(physical_address_bits),
        config.virtual_address_bits,
    ) {
        Ok(mapping) => mapping,
        Err(error) => {
            kprintln!(
                "candidate page-table probe failed: invalid mapping: {:?}",
                error
            );
            release_probe_frame(&mut boot_info.frame_allocator, frame);
            halt_forever();
        }
    };
    let cache_attributes = match mapping.select_cache_attributes(
        CachePolicy::WriteBack,
        pat,
        &mtrrs,
        boot_info.cpu_info.normal_caching,
    ) {
        Ok(attributes) => attributes,
        Err(error) => {
            kprintln!(
                "candidate page-table probe failed: cache policy: {:?}",
                error
            );
            release_probe_frame(&mut boot_info.frame_allocator, frame);
            halt_forever();
        }
    };

    let mut memory = LimineHhdmCandidateMemory {
        memory_map: &boot_info.memory_map,
        hhdm_offset: boot_info.hhdm_offset,
        physical_address_bits,
        virtual_address_bits: boot_info.cpu_info.active_linear_address_bits,
    };
    let mut candidate =
        match CandidatePageTables::new(&mut boot_info.frame_allocator, &mut memory, config) {
            Ok(candidate) => candidate,
            Err(error) => {
                kprintln!(
                    "candidate page-table probe failed to create root: {:?}",
                    error.cause
                );
                release_probe_frame(&mut boot_info.frame_allocator, frame);
                if let Some(root_frame) = error.frame {
                    release_probe_frame(&mut boot_info.frame_allocator, root_frame);
                }
                halt_forever();
            }
        };
    let root = candidate.root_physical_address();
    let frame_address = frame.address();
    if let Err(failure) = candidate.map_owned_page(
        &mut boot_info.frame_allocator,
        frame,
        mapping,
        cache_attributes,
    ) {
        kprintln!(
            "candidate page-table probe failed to map leaf: {:?}",
            failure.cause
        );
        release_probe_frame(&mut boot_info.frame_allocator, failure.frame);
        release_candidate_after_probe_failure(candidate, &mut boot_info.frame_allocator);
    }

    let walk = candidate.walk(virtual_address);
    let returned_frame = match candidate.unmap_owned_page(virtual_address) {
        Ok(frame) => frame,
        Err(error) => {
            kprintln!(
                "candidate page-table probe failed to unmap leaf: {:?}",
                error
            );
            release_candidate_after_probe_failure(candidate, &mut boot_info.frame_allocator);
        }
    };
    let translation_valid = match &walk {
        Ok(PageWalkOutcome::Mapped(translation)) => {
            translation.physical_address == frame_address
                && translation.page_size == rustix_kernel::paging::PAGE_SIZE
                && translation.permissions == permissions
                && translation.pat_index == cache_attributes.pat_index()
        }
        _ => false,
    };
    if returned_frame.address() != frame_address {
        kprintln!("candidate page-table probe failed: unmap returned the wrong frame");
        release_probe_frame(&mut boot_info.frame_allocator, returned_frame);
        release_candidate_after_probe_failure(candidate, &mut boot_info.frame_allocator);
    }
    release_probe_frame(&mut boot_info.frame_allocator, returned_frame);
    if !translation_valid {
        kprintln!(
            "candidate page-table probe failed: candidate walk: {:?}",
            walk
        );
        release_candidate_after_probe_failure(candidate, &mut boot_info.frame_allocator);
    }
    if let Err(failure) = candidate.release(&mut boot_info.frame_allocator) {
        kprintln!(
            "candidate page-table probe failed to release frames: {:?}",
            failure
        );
        halt_forever();
    }
    kprintln!(
        "candidate page-table probe passed: mapped, walked, unmapped, and released root {:#x}; CR3 unchanged",
        root.expect("candidate retains root until release")
    );
}

fn release_candidate_after_probe_failure(
    candidate: rustix_kernel::paging::CandidatePageTables<'_, LimineHhdmCandidateMemory<'_>>,
    allocator: &mut rustix_kernel::frame::FrameAllocator,
) -> ! {
    if let Err(failure) = candidate.release(allocator) {
        kprintln!("candidate page-table cleanup also failed: {:?}", failure);
    }
    halt_forever()
}

#[cfg(feature = "probe-hhdm-frame")]
fn verify_inherited_mapping(
    reader: &impl rustix_kernel::paging::PageTableReader<
        Error = rustix_kernel::memory::HhdmAddressError,
    >,
    root: rustix_kernel::paging::Cr3Root,
    config: rustix_kernel::paging::PageWalkConfig,
    label: &str,
    virtual_start: u64,
    physical_start: u64,
    length: u64,
) {
    use rustix_kernel::paging::{walk_virtual_address, PageWalkOutcome};

    let mut offset = 0;
    let mut pages = 0;
    let mut first_translation: Option<rustix_kernel::paging::PageTranslation> = None;
    let mut permissions_uniform = true;
    let mut pat_index_uniform = true;
    while offset < length {
        let virtual_address = match virtual_start.checked_add(offset) {
            Some(address) => address,
            None => {
                kprintln!("inherited mapping probe failed: {} virtual overflow", label);
                halt_forever();
            }
        };
        let expected_physical = match physical_start.checked_add(offset) {
            Some(address) => address,
            None => {
                kprintln!(
                    "inherited mapping probe failed: {} physical overflow",
                    label
                );
                halt_forever();
            }
        };
        let translation = match walk_virtual_address(reader, root, virtual_address, config) {
            Ok(PageWalkOutcome::Mapped(translation)) => translation,
            Ok(PageWalkOutcome::NotPresent { level }) => {
                kprintln!(
                    "inherited mapping probe failed: {} absent at {:?}",
                    label,
                    level
                );
                halt_forever();
            }
            Err(error) => {
                kprintln!("inherited mapping probe failed: {}: {:?}", label, error);
                halt_forever();
            }
        };
        if translation.physical_address != expected_physical {
            kprintln!(
                "inherited mapping probe failed: {} {:#018x} mapped to {:#018x}, expected {:#018x}",
                label,
                virtual_address,
                translation.physical_address,
                expected_physical
            );
            halt_forever();
        }
        if let Some(first) = first_translation {
            permissions_uniform &= translation.permissions == first.permissions;
            pat_index_uniform &= translation.pat_index == first.pat_index;
        } else {
            first_translation = Some(translation);
        }
        pages += 1;
        offset += rustix_kernel::paging::PAGE_SIZE;
    }
    if let Some(first) = first_translation {
        kprintln!(
            "inherited mapping probe passed: {} ({} pages), first permissions={:?}, PAT index={}, leaf size={}, uniform permissions={}, uniform PAT index={}",
            label,
            pages,
            first.permissions,
            first.pat_index,
            first.page_size,
            permissions_uniform,
            pat_index_uniform
        );
    }
}

#[cfg(feature = "probe-hhdm-frame")]
fn verify_kernel_cache_aliases(
    boot_info: &boot::BootInfo,
    reader: &impl rustix_kernel::paging::PageTableReader<
        Error = rustix_kernel::memory::HhdmAddressError,
    >,
    root: rustix_kernel::paging::Cr3Root,
    config: rustix_kernel::paging::PageWalkConfig,
    pat: rustix_kernel::paging::PatLayout,
    mtrrs: &rustix_kernel::paging::ValidatedMtrrLayout,
    label: &str,
    kernel_virtual_start: u64,
    physical_start: u64,
    length: u64,
) {
    use rustix_kernel::paging::{walk_virtual_address, PageWalkOutcome};

    let mut offset = 0;
    let mut pages = 0;
    while offset < length {
        let physical = match physical_start.checked_add(offset) {
            Some(address) => address,
            None => {
                kprintln!("cache-alias probe failed: {} physical overflow", label);
                halt_forever();
            }
        };
        let kernel_virtual = match kernel_virtual_start.checked_add(offset) {
            Some(address) => address,
            None => {
                kprintln!("cache-alias probe failed: {} virtual overflow", label);
                halt_forever();
            }
        };
        let hhdm_virtual = match boot_info.memory_map.limine_hhdm_address(
            boot_info.hhdm_offset,
            physical,
            rustix_kernel::paging::PAGE_SIZE,
            boot_info.cpu_info.physical_address_bits,
            boot_info.cpu_info.active_linear_address_bits,
        ) {
            Ok(address) => address,
            Err(error) => {
                kprintln!(
                    "cache-alias probe failed: {} HHDM range: {:?}",
                    label,
                    error
                );
                halt_forever();
            }
        };
        let kernel_translation = match walk_virtual_address(reader, root, kernel_virtual, config) {
            Ok(PageWalkOutcome::Mapped(translation)) => translation,
            result => {
                kprintln!(
                    "cache-alias probe failed: {} kernel walk: {:?}",
                    label,
                    result
                );
                halt_forever();
            }
        };
        let hhdm_translation = match walk_virtual_address(reader, root, hhdm_virtual, config) {
            Ok(PageWalkOutcome::Mapped(translation)) => translation,
            result => {
                kprintln!(
                    "cache-alias probe failed: {} HHDM walk: {:?}",
                    label,
                    result
                );
                halt_forever();
            }
        };
        if kernel_translation.physical_address != physical
            || hhdm_translation.physical_address != physical
        {
            kprintln!(
                "cache-alias probe failed: {} physical {:#018x} has inconsistent translations",
                label,
                physical
            );
            halt_forever();
        }
        let kernel_type = match mtrrs.effective_memory_type_for(
            physical,
            pat,
            kernel_translation.pat_index,
            boot_info.cpu_info.normal_caching,
        ) {
            Ok(memory_type) => memory_type,
            Err(error) => {
                kprintln!(
                    "cache-alias probe failed: {} kernel PAT/MTRR: {:?}",
                    label,
                    error
                );
                halt_forever();
            }
        };
        let hhdm_type = match mtrrs.effective_memory_type_for(
            physical,
            pat,
            hhdm_translation.pat_index,
            boot_info.cpu_info.normal_caching,
        ) {
            Ok(memory_type) => memory_type,
            Err(error) => {
                kprintln!(
                    "cache-alias probe failed: {} HHDM PAT/MTRR: {:?}",
                    label,
                    error
                );
                halt_forever();
            }
        };
        if kernel_type != hhdm_type {
            kprintln!(
                "cache-alias conflict: {} PA {:#018x}, kernel {:?} vs HHDM {:?}",
                label,
                physical,
                kernel_type,
                hhdm_type
            );
            halt_forever();
        }
        pages += 1;
        offset += rustix_kernel::paging::PAGE_SIZE;
    }
    kprintln!(
        "cache-alias probe passed: {} ({} pages; effective types match)",
        label,
        pages
    );
}

fn release_probe_frame(
    allocator: &mut rustix_kernel::frame::FrameAllocator,
    frame: rustix_kernel::frame::Frame,
) {
    if let Err(error) = allocator.deallocate(frame) {
        kprintln!(
            "HHDM frame probe failed to return its frame: {:?}",
            error.error
        );
        halt_forever();
    }
}

#[cfg(feature = "inject-page-fault")]
fn run_fault_injection() {
    kprintln!("fault injection: triggering page fault at 0x00000000deadbeef");
    // SAFETY: This is an opt-in QEMU test that deliberately reads an unmapped
    // low virtual address; the installed page-fault handler is expected to halt.
    unsafe {
        core::arch::asm!(
            "mov rax, 0xdeadbeef",
            "mov rax, qword ptr [rax]",
            out("rax") _,
            options(nostack)
        );
    }
    kprintln!("fault injection unexpectedly returned");
    halt_forever();
}

#[cfg(feature = "inject-invalid-opcode")]
fn run_fault_injection() {
    kprintln!("fault injection: triggering invalid opcode with ud2");
    // SAFETY: This is an opt-in QEMU test that deliberately raises #UD; the
    // installed invalid-opcode handler is expected to halt.
    unsafe { core::arch::asm!("ud2", options(nomem, nostack)) };
    kprintln!("fault injection unexpectedly returned");
    halt_forever();
}

#[panic_handler]
fn panic(info: &PanicInfo<'_>) -> ! {
    arch::x86_64::serial::initialize();
    kprintln!("KERNEL PANIC: {}", info);
    halt_forever()
}

fn halt_forever() -> ! {
    loop {
        // SAFETY: The bootstrap has no interrupt handlers or scheduler to resume.
        unsafe { core::arch::asm!("cli; hlt", options(nomem, nostack)) };
    }
}
```

## Context Compaction (Completed)

## Goal
Complete Rustix Milestone 2: safe, owned paging state and CR3 transition, a documented heap, diagnosable exceptions, and emulator validation. Keep the working tree’s existing changes; do not reset, commit, or create branches.

## State
- The project has many pre-existing uncommitted changes. `src/paging.rs` was untracked in the initial status. Preserve all of them.
- The candidate page-table backend refactor is complete so far:
  - `CandidatePageTables<'a, M>` holds a unique mutable borrow of its backend.
  - Backend is an `unsafe trait`; unsafe reads/writes are wrapped in documented narrow blocks.
  - Candidate maps/unmaps allocator-issued frames transactionally; host tests include rollback, owned-table walk restrictions, and retryable release failure.
- Added inherited page-table hierarchy cloning:
  - Copies present entries and non-present entries, rewrites intermediate references to owned cloned tables, preserves shared same-level tables, rejects unsupported cross-level aliases/malformed entries, and clears the candidate root on failure.
  - Host tests cover cloning and malformed large pages.
- Added `encode_cr3_value` and CR3-write wrapper in `src/arch/x86_64/cpu.rs`.
- `src/main.rs` now has an unconditional `activate_cloned_page_tables_and_run` path that clones the inherited root, checks critical spans and candidate-root HHDM translation, writes CR3, verifies the active root and critical spans, then enters the shell while retaining the candidate in scope. Interrupts remain disabled. **This transition has only passed target compilation so far; it has not yet been QEMU-tested.**
- The opt-in `probe-hhdm-frame` path now checks kernel/HHDM cache aliases, clones/compares/releases a separate candidate hierarchy, and exercises map/walk/unmap/release.
- `just frame-smoke` passed before the unconditional CR3 transition was added. Its latest run failed while comparing cloned entries because Accessed/Dirty bits can change asynchronously; the comparison was corrected to ignore bits 5 and 6. The subsequent frame-smoke passed with the cloned-root marker.
- Last observed checks after adding clone and CR3 encoding: `cargo fmt`, 4 Crabshell tests, 75 kernel tests, and target `cargo check` passed. That check showed one unused `label` warning; the warning was just fixed, but no checks have been rerun after the fix or after the CR3 activation code.
- A prior `just verify`, `just fault-smoke`, and `just frame-smoke` passed before the clone/activation additions. WSL works; Windows `xorriso` is unavailable.

## Context / constraints
- Follow `rustix/AGENTS.md`, `docs/roadmap/README.md`, `docs/architecture/memory.md`, and `docs/development/testing.md`.
- Kernel is `no_std`, `x86_64-unknown-none`; no heap exists yet.
- Only `Usable` frames enter the allocator. `Frame` is a non-copyable token, never a direct pointer. HHDM accesses must validate complete allocator-owned frames and rely on Limine base revision 3.
- Do not alter Limine’s active root without preserving the executing kernel, stack, boot data, descriptors, exception stacks, HHDM, cache settings, and error behavior.
- CR3 activation now clones the full inherited table graph rather than constructing a new permissions policy. Cloning is bounded to 32 table pages; it rejects page-table aliases reused at different levels and fails closed. Limine QEMU previously reported only two present root entries, and the clone probe passed.
- `CandidatePageTables` owns table tokens and explicitly mapped leaf tokens; cloned inherited leaf frames remain externally owned. Dropping an active candidate would leak tokens, so retain it for the entire active-root lifetime.
- Interrupts are disabled in `interrupts::initialize`; keep them disabled during transition. Preserve CR3 PCID or PWT/PCD low bits; `encode_cr3_value` clears the PCID no-flush bit.
- Do not mark Milestone 2 complete until transition, heap behavior, and validation are actually observed.
- Run WSL commands from `C:\Users\ethan\Projects\rustix` with:
  `wsl --distribution Ubuntu --exec bash -lc "cd /mnt/c/Users/ethan/Projects/rustix && <command>"`
- Image/QEMU workflows restore the default kernel/ISO; run sequentially, not in parallel.

## Next
1. Review `src/main.rs` transition code closely. Check safety and correctness of CR3 restoration, candidate lifetime, alias permissions, and post-switch checks. Confirm `candidate_span_matches_source` now uses `_` for the unused label.
2. Run `cargo fmt --all`, `cargo test --workspace --lib`, and `cargo check --target x86_64-unknown-none`; resolve any errors/warnings.
3. Run `just verify` in WSL. This now exercises the unconditional CR3 transition through the normal QEMU shell smoke test. If it fails, inspect `target/rustix-qemu-serial.log`; do not continue to heap work until the transition is understood.
4. Run `just fault-smoke` and `just frame-smoke` sequentially in WSL. Update `scripts/boot.py` markers if the transition marker should be asserted.
5. Update documentation accurately for cloned active-root behavior and observed QEMU results. Current docs/AGENTS describe only an inactive candidate and still claim no CR3 transition; they are stale after the latest code edits.
6. Implement a bounded heap with explicit alignment, exhaustion and free semantics, plus a documented interrupt-context rule. Test host-side allocator behavior and boot it under QEMU. Then update roadmap/architecture docs and rerun full validation.
7. Keep Milestone 2 **in progress** until heap and all exit criteria pass.

## Pitfalls
- A `std::vec::Vec` test failed because `src/lib.rs` is `#![no_std]`; the release-failure test now uses a fixed array.
- A clone test initially used incorrect page-table indices and failed its expected table count; it was corrected to model PML4→PDPT→PD→PT.
- A recursive-root synthetic clone test exposed that reusing the same physical table at different levels is ambiguous for exact cloning. The builder now rejects cross-level aliases instead of attempting an unsafe/incorrect clone.
- The first QEMU clone comparison failed because active hardware updates PTE Accessed/Dirty bits after cloning; comparison now ignores bits 5 and 6 while still checking translation, permissions, page size, PAT index, and remaining raw bits.
- Latest unconditional CR3 transition has not been run in QEMU yet. Do not claim it works based on target check alone.

## Assistant

I’ll resume from the CR3-transition work, first checking the current diff and reviewing the transition path against the paging ownership invariants. Then I’ll run the host/target checks and QEMU validation before making any further milestone changes.

```rustix/src/arch/x86_64/cpu.rs
    32	/// Read CPUID identity, selected feature bits, and supported read-only MSR state.
    33	pub fn identify() -> CpuInfo {
    34	    // CPUID is part of the x86_64 architectural baseline.
    35	    let basic = __cpuid(0);
    36	    let mut vendor = [0; 12];
    37	    vendor[0..4].copy_from_slice(&basic.ebx.to_le_bytes());
    38	    vendor[4..8].copy_from_slice(&basic.edx.to_le_bytes());
    39	    vendor[8..12].copy_from_slice(&basic.ecx.to_le_bytes());
    40	
    41	    let basic_features = if basic.eax >= 1 {
    42	        Some(__cpuid(1))
    43	    } else {
    44	        None
    45	    };
    46	    let extended = __cpuid(0x8000_0000);
    47	    let extended_features = if extended.eax >= 0x8000_0001 {
    48	        Some(__cpuid(0x8000_0001))
    49	    } else {
    50	        None
    51	    };
    52	    let structured_features = if basic.eax >= 7 {
    53	        Some(__cpuid_count(7, 0))
    54	    } else {
    55	        None
    56	    };
    57	    let address_widths = if extended.eax >= 0x8000_0008 {
    58	        Some(__cpuid(0x8000_0008).eax)
    59	    } else {
    60	        None
    61	    };
    62	    let cr0 = read_cr0_raw();
    63	    let cr4 = read_cr4_raw();
    64	    let has_nx = extended_features.is_some_and(|features| features.edx & (1 << 20) != 0);
    65	    let nx_enabled = if has_nx {
    66	        // SAFETY: EFER is available in x86_64 long mode; CPUID confirms NX support,
    67	        // and this boot-time code executes at CPL 0. The read does not change state.
    68	        unsafe { read_msr(IA32_EFER) & EFER_NXE != 0 }
    69	    } else {

    71	    };
    72	    let has_pat = basic_features.is_some_and(|features| features.edx & (1 << 16) != 0);

    75	        Some(unsafe { read_msr(IA32_PAT) })

    78	    };

   107	/// Read the current raw CR3 value without changing page-table state.
   108	pub fn read_cr3_raw() -> u64 {
   109	    let cr3: u64;
   110	    // SAFETY: Rustix runs at CPL 0; reading CR3 is privileged but non-mutating.
   111	    unsafe { asm!("mov {}, cr3", out(reg) cr3, options(nomem, nostack, preserves_flags)) };
   112	    cr3
   113	}
   114	
   115	/// Install a pre-validated CR3 value.
   116	///
   117	/// # Safety
   118	/// The root must name a complete, valid page-table hierarchy that preserves the
   119	/// current instruction, stack, data, exception, and HHDM mappings. Paging mode
   120	/// and address-width controls must already match the hierarchy, and interrupts
   121	/// must remain disabled during the transition.
   122	pub unsafe fn write_cr3_raw(value: u64) {
   123	    // SAFETY: The caller establishes the page-table and transition invariants.
   124	    unsafe { asm!("mov cr3, {}", in(reg) value, options(nostack, preserves_flags)) };
   125	}
   126	
   127	/// Read a model-specific register at CPL 0.
   128	///
   129	/// # Safety
   130	/// The caller must ensure the MSR exists on this CPU and that the current
   131	/// privilege level permits the read.
   132	unsafe fn read_msr(index: u32) -> u64 {
   133	    let low: u32;
   134	    let high: u32;
   135	    // SAFETY: The caller guarantees that this MSR is supported and accessible.
   136	    unsafe {
   137	        asm!(
   138	            "rdmsr",
   139	            in("ecx") index,
   140	            out("eax") low,
   141	            out("edx") high,
   142	            options(nomem, nostack)
   143	        );
   144	    }
   145	    (u64::from(high) << 32) | u64::from(low)
   146	}
   147

   150	    let cr0: u64;
   151	    // SAFETY: Rustix runs at CPL 0; reading CR0 is privileged but non-mutating.
   152	    unsafe { asm!("mov {}, cr0", out(reg) cr0, options(nomem, nostack, preserves_flags)) };
   153	    cr0
   154	}
```

```rustix/src/paging.rs
    72	    }

   106	        return Err(Cr3Error::InvalidPhysicalAddressWidth);
   107	    }
   108	
   109	    let physical_mask = ((1u64 << physical_address_bits) - 1) & !(PAGE_SIZE - 1);

   112	    } else {
   113	        (1 << 3) | (1 << 4)

   117	    }

   123	            page_level_write_through: raw & (1 << 3) != 0,
   124	            page_level_cache_disable: raw & (1 << 4) != 0,

   134	/// Calculate the protocol-backed HHDM address of Limine's inherited root page.

   136	/// This requires the root page to be wholly contained in bootloader-reclaimable

   139	pub fn inherited_cr3_root_hhdm_address(
   140	    root: Cr3Root,
   141	    memory_map: &MemoryMap,
   142	    hhdm_offset: u64,
   143	    physical_address_bits: Option<u8>,
   144	    virtual_address_bits: u8,
```

```rustix/docs/architecture/memory.md
     1	# Memory-management direction
     2	
     3	## What exists now
     4	
     5	`src/memory.rs` contains an allocation-free `MemoryMapBuilder` that copies Limine ranges into validated half-open physical regions. It rejects empty ranges, `base + length` overflow, overlapping ranges, empty maps, and maps exceeding the fixed 256-region capacity. Known Limine types remain distinct, and unknown type values are preserved. Host-side tests cover range validation/classification, canonical-address boundaries, physical-width bounds, and HHDM range arithmetic. `src/boot.rs` stores the resulting map in an owned boot snapshot and reports usable bytes.
     6	
     7	`src/frame.rs` provides a fixed-capacity allocator core with host-side tests. It only manages complete 4 KiB frames inside validated `Usable` regions, reserves the first MiB, and coalesces adjacent free ranges. The ownership contract assumes one allocator instance per physical map: within that instance, each eligible frame is owned either by its free-range table or by a non-copyable `Frame` token while allocated. The public constructor does not enforce unique instances, so callers must not initialize multiple allocators for the same physical map; the current boot path retains one allocator in `BootInfo`. `allocate` returns `None` when no free frame remains. `deallocate` consumes the token only on success; on any error, including free-range-table exhaustion, it returns a `DeallocationError` containing the original token and leaves allocator state unchanged. The range tables each have a fixed `MAX_FRAME_RANGES` capacity, so fragmentation can prevent a frame from being returned until nearby ranges coalesce. The inactive candidate-root builder allocates table frames only in the opt-in probe today; there is no active general-purpose mapping service.
     8	
     9	`Frame::address()` is a physical address value, not a dereferenceable pointer and not a proof that the frame is mapped. CPU diagnostics now read `CR4.LA57` to report the active linear-address width (48 or 57 bits) and query `CPUID.80000008H` for physical and maximum linear-address widths when available. Boot-protocol pointers are checked against the active width, with host tests for 48- and 57-bit canonical boundaries. These facts do not prove that any physical address is mapped.
    10	
    11	`src/paging.rs` contains host-tested mapping and cache policy plus an inactive candidate-root builder. The CR3 decoder validates physical-address width and reserved bits and interprets its low 12 bits according to active `CR4.PCIDE`; it does not dereference the root. The mapping-range validator requires known physical width, checked aligned bounds, canonical virtual endpoints in one canonical half, and rejects writable-executable permissions. It can encode one 4 KiB leaf PTE with supervisor/user and write permissions, NX when EFER.NXE is confirmed, and a bounded PAT index. `PatLayout` parses supplied `IA32_PAT` values and selects WB, UC, or WC indexes. `MtrrMemoryType`, `VariableMtrr`, `FixedMtrrRanges`, and `MtrrLayout` resolve address-specific MTRR types, including fixed-range priority and defined variable-overlap rules; undefined overlaps fail closed. `MtrrRegisters::validated_layout` validates captured capability/default-type bits, register counts and fixed-range presence, WC support, and variable-mask shape/alignment before producing an owned layout. Rustix supports contiguous power-of-two variable masks and explicitly rejects unsupported discontinuous masks. The layout combines address-specific MTRR type and PAT selection according to Intel SDM Table 11-7 only when `CR0.CD` and `CR0.NW` are clear. Host tests cover all 30 documented MTRR/PAT pairs and malformed inputs. A pure range selector chooses an index only when its effective type is uniform throughout all fixed/variable MTRR boundaries in an aligned extent; selected attributes remain bound to that physical extent. The selector itself does not inspect PTEs, aliases, or frame ownership. Boot reads CR0 without modifying it, validates captured MTRR/PAT state, and reports a diagnostic PA 0 resolution; this does not assert the live PTE's type. MTRR capture is bounded to 32 variable pairs and rejects excess capacity without partial state.
    12	
    13	`CandidatePageTables` owns a separate root, bounded to 32 table frames and 256 leaf mappings. It accepts only allocator-issued `Frame` tokens, requires NXE, supports four- and five-level 4 KiB paths, and holds one exclusive mutable borrow of its unsafe memory backend so prepared handles cannot be mixed across backends. Mapping validates ownership, permissions, physical width, and range-bound cache attributes, preflights the path, and prepares all missing tables before linking entries. Host tests cover mapping/unmapping, owned-table walks, 4-/5-level paths, frame exhaustion, prepare rollback, and retryable release failure. Dropping a candidate without `release` intentionally leaves its frames allocated; the builder never modifies or installs the active root. The opt-in QEMU adapter derives table pointers only from complete allocator-owned `Usable` frames through checked HHDM arithmetic. `just frame-smoke` verifies one candidate mapping end-to-end without activating its root.
    14	
    15	The inherited-root QEMU probe reads the root's 512 entries and follows bounded paths for every page in kernel text/rodata/data and the minimum boot-stack span, checking physical translations. It compares effective PAT/MTRR types for kernel-image and HHDM aliases. This is a bounded transition-critical check, not a complete mapping or alias inventory, and it does not prove inherited permissions match the linker policy or justify a CR3 transition.
    16	
    17	The effective-type resolver follows [Intel SDM Vol. 3A §11.5.2.2, Table 11-7](https://cdrdv2-public.intel.com/671447/325384-sdm-vol-3abcd.pdf), which applies when normal caching is enabled (`CR0.CD=0`, `CR0.NW=0`). On x86_64, inherited HHDM mappings are supervisor RWX, normally write-back cached, with framebuffer mappings write-combining when PAT is available. Therefore an HHDM offset is not a blanket physical-memory access grant, and inherited HHDM permissions are not Rustix's future W^X policy.     23	## Mapping inventory before a CR3 transition
    24	
    25	The current runtime has several mappings that a future page-table transition must preserve. The address sources and remaining gaps are:
    26	
    27	- **Kernel ELF image:** `linker.ld` places `.text`, `.rodata`, `.limine_requests`, `.data`, `.bss`, and `.got` in three `PT_LOAD` segments: RX text, read-only rodata, and RW data/BSS. It exports `__kernel_start` and `__kernel_end` around the complete loadable image, plus page-aligned bounds for each segment. `BootInfo` checks that Limine's reported virtual base matches the linker start, validates ordered contiguous segment bounds covering the rounded image, derives corresponding half-open physical ranges from the executable physical base with checked arithmetic, and validates canonical virtual and reported physical address widths. The release ELF and QEMU runtime report both showed the three aligned ranges on 2026-10-21. The RX, R/NX, and RW/NX labels describe the linker segment intent; these are linker/boot metadata, not proof that the inherited page tables map every page or enforce those permissions, nor proof that loader pointers are readable. The memory-map `ExecutableAndModules` entries remain illustrative, not an authoritative kernel-image extent.
    28	- **Active stack and `BootInfo`:** The assembly `_start` shim captures Limine's entry `RSP` before any Rust prologue. Under the SysV entry convention the synthetic return slot occupies 8 bytes, so `RSP + 8` is the exclusive stack top. The protocol guarantees at least 64 KiB (without a Stack Size request); `BootInfo` records that minimum virtual span, translates it through the HHDM, and requires it to fit within a single `BootloaderReclaimable` physical region. The full loader allocation may be larger, and neither its exact bounds nor a guard page are known. Preserve the inherited mapping; do not infer a guard page.
    29	- **Kernel static data:** `RAM_FILESYSTEM`, GDT, IDT, TSS, the ring-0 stack, and double-fault IST stack are static BSS/data in the kernel image. Exception entry also requires the handler code and the TSS/IDT references to remain mapped. Preserve the complete relevant data/BSS pages and stack pages.
    30	- **Limine request data:** request records are in the kernel's writable `.limine_requests` segment. Response objects and the memory-map pointer array are bootloader-reclaimable; `capture_boot_information` copies the values used later, and the shell does not retain those pointers. Keep them mapped until the copy and validation finish; any later reclaim must be explicit rather than reclaiming the whole bootloader-reclaimable class.
    31	- **Inherited page tables:** Limine places its page tables in bootloader-reclaimable memory, but their layout is unspecified. `BootInfo` captures raw CR3 and validates a decoded physical root address plus the low-bit interpretation selected by active `CR4.PCIDE`. A pure helper requires the root page to fit in one validated `BootloaderReclaimable` range and calculates its HHDM address when the physical width is known. The opt-in QEMU probe reads the root's 512 entries and counts present bits, then follows bounded paths for every page in the kernel text/rodata/data and minimum boot-stack spans, checking physical translations. It also compares effective PAT/MTRR types for each kernel-image page and its HHDM alias. It does not enumerate unrelated mappings or prove that inherited permissions match the linker policy. Keep the old root and its backing pages intact while inspecting/building a replacement; do not reclaim them until a verified switch no longer depends on them.
    32	- **Devices:** COM1 uses x86 port I/O and needs no MMIO virtual mapping. Rustix does not currently request or use a framebuffer. Any future framebuffer or device-register mapping needs an explicit physical range and cache policy.
    33	
    34	## Initial kernel-owned mapping policy (design only)
    35	
    36	A first Rustix-owned x86_64 root should use 4 KiB pages only and require NX support; if NX is unavailable, abort before switching. Preserve ELF permissions exactly: text RX, rodata R/NX, and `.limine_requests`/data/BSS/GOT RW/NX. Reject W+X mappings. Exclude the complete physical kernel-image span from the generic HHDM in the first implementation so no writable direct-map alias can undermine text or rodata permissions. Ordinary RAM HHDM mappings should be RW/NX and WB.
    37	
    38	Preserve the inherited PAT/MTRR configuration during the first transition. The boot report validates captured registers and computes a diagnostic effective type from the active PAT/MTRR values under normal caching. A separate pure selector can choose an index whose effective type remains uniform across an aligned physical range; the selector itself does not inspect PTEs or aliases. The opt-in `just frame-smoke` probe now compares effective types of the inherited kernel and HHDM aliases for kernel-image pages, but it is not a full alias inventory. The pure combination follows Intel SDM Table 11-7; it is not a generic rule for legacy PCD/PWT-only selection or model-specific combinations. Under Limine base revision 3 on x86_64, use PAT index 0 for WB, index 3 for UC, and index 5 for WC only after the target physical range and active PAT/MTRR interaction are verified. Map MMIO only from explicit device ranges and use UC by default; do not infer MMIO from generic reserved memory-map entries. A framebuffer may use WC only after its response and cache policy are explicitly validated. COM1 uses port I/O and requires no MMIO mapping.
    39	
    40	Do not use huge pages in the first root; add them only when physical coverage, permissions, and cache attributes are uniform across the entire huge-page extent. Future Rustix-owned downward-growing stacks should have at least one 4 KiB unmapped guard page below them. The Limine bootstrap stack has no known guard, so none may be assumed there.
    41	
    42	Never modify Limine's active page tables in place. `src/paging.rs` now builds a bounded, inactive candidate root from allocator-owned frames and supports transactional 4 KiB map/unmap operations. Its checked QEMU backend has built, walked, unmapped, and released one candidate mapping without changing CR3. This is not a transition implementation: the current probe does not preserve every transition-critical mapping, and the active Limine root remains in use. Keep the inherited root and its backing memory intact; do not switch CR3 until every required mapping, permission, cache attribute, ownership relation, and failure path has been reviewed and tested.
    43	
    44	## Planned memory layers
    45	
    46	1. **Validated physical regions:** implemented as a fixed-capacity owned snapshot; allocator ownership and reclaim policy remain future work.
    47	4. **Frame allocator integration:** the bounded core is initialized from `BootInfo`; the inactive candidate builder and diagnostic QEMU probe are its only mapping callers so far. Add active mapping services only after the transition policy and ownership rules are complete.
    48	3. **Kernel virtual memory:** Rustix still runs on inherited Limine page tables. A bounded inactive candidate-root builder now supports allocator-owned 4 KiB mapping and unmapping, but no kernel-owned root is active. Before replacing Limine's tables, preserve the executing kernel, bootstrap/Ring-0 stacks, request/response data, and exception stacks; define the HHDM extent and explicit mapping permissions/cache attributes. Keep writable-executable mappings disallowed by default and reserve MMIO and guard regions.
    49	4. **Heap:** add a global allocator only after frame allocation and page mapping are initialized. Define allocation failure behavior for kernel and interrupt contexts.
    50	5. **Process address spaces:** isolate userspace; define copy-in/copy-out helpers and never treat user pointers as kernel references.
    51	
    52	## Invariants to preserve
    53	
    54	- Physical ranges use checked arithmetic and the half-open convention `[start, end)`.
    55	- Only complete frames in validated `Usable` regions enter the allocator; the first MiB remains reserved. Firmware and loader-reclaimable regions are not silently promoted to free memory.
    56	- Under the single-allocator-per-physical-map contract, a frame is represented by one allocator-free range or one caller-owned, non-copyable `Frame` token. Only a successful `deallocate` transfers the token back to the allocator; errors return the token and leave allocator ranges and accounting unchanged. The current public constructor relies on callers to enforce unique allocator instances.
    57	- `allocate` returns `None` on frame exhaustion. Metadata-capacity exhaustion is an explicit error, never silent loss of a frame.
    58	- A `Frame` address is physical, not directly dereferenceable. HHDM translation and table access are limited to checked full-frame token-based paths that rely on Limine's documented mapping contract. Candidate mutations must remain within allocator-owned inactive tables. No active-root mutation or CR3 switch is permitted until address widths, mapping coverage, permissions/cache attributes, and transition-preservation requirements are established.
    59	- Mapping changes validate alignment, canonical addresses, ownership, and permissions before touching tables.
    60	- User-controlled addresses are validated on every syscall boundary; prior validation is not a substitute for access checks during later copies.
    61	- Tests cover unaligned edges, exact-boundary allocations, arithmetic overflow, overlaps, exhaustion, and unchanged state/ownership on failure.
    62	
    63	The complete transition and heap requirements remain design requirements; the inactive candidate builder and bounded QEMU probes are implemented, but do not deliver a replacement active address space.
```

```rustix/src/main.rs
   738	    candidate: &rustix_kernel::paging::CandidatePageTables<'_, LimineHhdmCandidateMemory<'_>>,
   739	    source_reader: &impl rustix_kernel::paging::PageTableReader<

   750	    let mut offset = 0;
   751	    while offset < length {
   752	        let Some(virtual_address) = virtual_start.checked_add(offset) else {
   753	            return false;
   754	        };

   780	            || source_translation.page_size != candidate_translation.page_size
```

```rustix/docs/development/testing.md
     1	# Testing and verification
     2	
     3	## Current checks
     4	
     5	`just verify` runs the standard development verification sequence:
     6	
     7	1. `just fmt` — fail on formatting differences across the workspace.
     8	2. `just test` — run host-side memory-map, mapping-range/PTE-bit policy, frame-allocator, RAM-filesystem, and Crabshell parser tests.
     9	3. `just check` — check the `x86_64-unknown-none` kernel target.
    10	4. `just smoke` — build the pinned hybrid ISO, boot it in QEMU, and check that Crabshell reaches its prompt within a deadline.
    11	
    12	`just frame-smoke` builds an opt-in kernel variant that allocates one `Usable` frame, validates its HHDM address, writes and reads the whole page, clears it, returns the frame, and checks the normal prompt in QEMU. It also validates and reads the inherited root page, then follows bounded 4-/5-level page-table paths for every page in the kernel image segments and minimum boot-stack span, checking translations against boot metadata. For each kernel-image page, it compares the effective PAT/MTRR type of the kernel and HHDM aliases. Finally, a checked HHDM backend creates an inactive candidate root, maps and walks one allocator-owned 4 KiB leaf, unmaps it, and returns all frames without changing CR3. The workflow restores the default release kernel and ISO. These probes rely on Limine's HHDM contract; they do not inventory every mapping or alias, prove all inherited permissions, activate the candidate, or establish physical-hardware correctness. `just fault-smoke` separately builds opt-in kernel variants that deliberately trigger a page fault and an invalid opcode. It requires each QEMU run to report the expected exception (and CR2 for the page fault), avoid the shell prompt, and remain halted until timeout. It then rebuilds and restores the default release kernel and ISO. These are fatal-path diagnostics, not exception recovery tests; diagnostic Cargo features are disabled by default and mutually exclusive.
    13	
    14	Keep the Crabshell parser, VFS, memory-map validator, paging policy helpers, and frame allocator independent of hardware so syntax, path handling, address and leaf-PTE bit policy, PAT/MTRR policy, storage semantics, frame ownership, and HHDM/root-range calculations can be tested without booting. Pure tests validate captured MTRR register snapshots, resolve the Intel SDM Table 11-7 PAT/MTRR combinations for one physical address, select a PAT index that remains uniform across MTRR boundaries in an aligned range, bind that selection to validated mapping metadata before encoding leaves, and walk synthetic four-/five-level page tables including large-page leaves. Host tests also exercise the inactive candidate builder's owned-table walk, 4-/5-level mapping, unmapping, transactional allocation/prepare rollback, and retryable frame-release failure. They reject malformed state, unsupported discontinuous masks, invalid indexes/ranges, out-of-range addresses, mismatched physical widths, and non-normal caching mode. The pure inherited-table walker does not access hardware tables; the opt-in QEMU reader and candidate backend use checked HHDM addresses. Boot-time QEMU checks a subset of live kernel/HHDM aliases but does not inventory all aliases or prove complete transition safety. Boot separately captures the registers and CR0 caching mode read-only and reports a diagnostic resolution; this is not a page-table or mapping test. The GDT/TSS/IDT and CPU-register paths are privileged kernel code; QEMU boot and fault-injection checks complement, but do not replace, static review and target builds. struct LimineHhdmPageTableReader<'a> {
```
```
    memory_map: &'a rustix_kernel::memory::MemoryMap,
    hhdm_offset: u64,
    physical_address_bits: u8,
    virtual_address_bits: u8,
}

impl rustix_kernel::paging::PageTableReader for LimineHhdmPageTableReader<'_> {
    type Error = rustix_kernel::memory::HhdmAddressError;

    fn read_entry(&self, table_physical: u64, index: u16) -> Result<u64, Self::Error> {
        if index >= 512 {
            return Err(rustix_kernel::memory::HhdmAddressError::InvalidHhdmRange);
        }
        let table_end = table_physical
            .checked_add(rustix_kernel::paging::PAGE_SIZE)
            .ok_or(rustix_kernel::memory::HhdmAddressError::AddressOverflow)?;
        if !self.memory_map.range_is_within_region_kind(
            table_physical,
            table_end,
            rustix_kernel::memory::RegionKind::BootloaderReclaimable,
        ) {
            return Err(rustix_kernel::memory::HhdmAddressError::NotLimineMapped);
        }
        let table_address = self.memory_map.limine_hhdm_address(
            self.hhdm_offset,
            table_physical,
            rustix_kernel::paging::PAGE_SIZE,
            Some(self.physical_address_bits),
            self.virtual_address_bits,
        )?;
        let entry_address = table_address
            .checked_add(u64::from(index) * core::mem::size_of::<u64>() as u64)
            .ok_or(rustix_kernel::memory::HhdmAddressError::AddressOverflow)?;
        // SAFETY: The complete table page was restricted to bootloader-reclaimable
        // memory and its HHDM address arithmetic was checked. The reader relies
        // on the Limine base-revision-3 mapping contract and never returns a ref.
        Ok(unsafe { (entry_address as *const u64).read_volatile() })
    }
}

struct LimineHhdmCandidateMemory<'a> {
    memory_map: &'a rustix_kernel::memory::MemoryMap,
    hhdm_offset: u64,
    physical_address_bits: u8,
    virtual_address_bits: u8,
}

// SAFETY: `prepare_table` accepts only an allocator-issued frame and validates
// its complete usable span and HHDM address. Handles are only used while the
// candidate retains the frame token and this unique backend borrow.
unsafe impl rustix_kernel::paging::CandidatePageTableMemory for LimineHhdmCandidateMemory<'_> {
    type PreparedTable = u64;
    type Error = rustix_kernel::memory::HhdmAddressError;

    fn prepare_table(
        &mut self,
        frame: &rustix_kernel::frame::Frame,
    ) -> Result<Self::PreparedTable, Self::Error> {
        frame.hhdm_address(
            self.memory_map,
            self.hhdm_offset,
            Some(self.physical_address_bits),
            self.virtual_address_bits,
        )
    }

    unsafe fn read_entry(
        &self,
        table: Self::PreparedTable,
        index: u16,
    ) -> Result<u64, Self::Error> {
        if index >= 512 {
            return Err(rustix_kernel::memory::HhdmAddressError::InvalidHhdmRange);
        }
        let entry_address = table
            .checked_add(u64::from(index) * core::mem::size_of::<u64>() as u64)
            .ok_or(rustix_kernel::memory::HhdmAddressError::AddressOverflow)?;
        // SAFETY: The unsafe trait contract requires `table` to be the prepared
        // HHDM address of a complete writable frame; the index is in [0, 512).
        Ok(unsafe { (entry_address as *const u64).read_volatile() })
    }

    unsafe fn clear_table(&mut self, table: Self::PreparedTable) {
        let entries = table as *mut u64;
        // SAFETY: The caller provides a handle prepared by this backend for a
        // complete writable frame retained by its candidate.
        unsafe {
            for index in 0..512 {
                entries.add(index).write_volatile(0);
            }
        }
    }

    unsafe fn write_entry(&mut self, table: Self::PreparedTable, index: u16, value: u64) {
        if index >= 512 {
            return;
        }
        let entry = (table as *mut u64).wrapping_add(usize::from(index));
        // SAFETY: The caller provides a prepared complete frame and an index in
        // range; this writes one entry without creating a Rust reference.
        unsafe { entry.write_volatile(value) };
    }
}

// Capture Limine's entry RSP before a Rust prologue changes it. The synthetic

core::arch::global_asm!(
    ".section .text",
    ".code64",

    "_start:",
    "mov rdi, rsp",
    "and rsp, -16",

    "ud2",
    ".size _start, . - _start",

#[no_mangle]
pub extern "C" fn rustix_start(entry_rsp: u64) -> ! {
    arch::x86_64::serial::initialize();
    kprintln!("Rustix kernel: x86_64 Rust bootstrap");
    arch::x86_64::interrupts::initialize();
    kprintln!("x86_64 exception diagnostics: enabled (IRQs remain disabled)");
    let mut boot_info = match boot::capture_boot_information(entry_rsp) {
        Ok(boot_info) => boot_info,
        Err(error) => {
            kprintln!("boot information rejected: {:?}", error);
            halt_forever();
        }
    };
    boot::report_boot_information(&boot_info);

    #[cfg(feature = "probe-hhdm-frame")]
    probe_hhdm_frame(&mut boot_info);

    #[cfg(any(feature = "inject-page-fault", feature = "inject-invalid-opcode"))]
    run_fault_injection();

    activate_cloned_page_tables_and_run(&mut boot_info)
}

fn activate_cloned_page_tables_and_run(boot_info: &mut boot::BootInfo) -> ! {
    use rustix_kernel::paging::{
        encode_cr3_value, CandidatePageTables, PageWalkConfig, PageWalkOutcome,
    };

    let physical_address_bits = match boot_info.cpu_info.physical_address_bits {
        Some(bits) => bits,
        None => {
            kprintln!("page-table transition rejected: physical width unknown");

    };
    let inherited_root = match boot_info.inherited_cr3_root {
        Ok(root) => root,

        }

        kprintln!("page-table transition rejected: NXE is not enabled");
        halt_forever();
    }

        levels: if boot_info.cpu_info.active_linear_address_bits == 57 {
            5
        } else {
            4
        },
        physical_address_bits,
        virtual_address_bits: boot_info.cpu_info.active_linear_address_bits,
        nx_enabled: boot_info.cpu_info.nx_enabled,
        page_2m_supported: true,
        page_1g_supported: boot_info.cpu_info.has_1g_pages,
    };
    let reader = LimineHhdmPageTableReader {
        memory_map: &boot_info.memory_map,
        hhdm_offset: boot_info.hhdm_offset,
        physical_address_bits,
        virtual_address_bits: boot_info.cpu_info.active_linear_address_bits,
    };
    let mut memory = LimineHhdmCandidateMemory {
        memory_map: &boot_info.memory_map,
        hhdm_offset: boot_info.hhdm_offset,
        physical_address_bits,
        virtual_address_bits: boot_info.cpu_info.active_linear_address_bits,
    };
    let mut candidate =
        match CandidatePageTables::new(&mut boot_info.frame_allocator, &mut memory, config) {
            Ok(candidate) => candidate,
            Err(error) => {
                kprintln!(
                    "page-table transition failed to create root: {:?}",
                    error.cause
                );
                if let Some(frame) = error.frame {
                    release_probe_frame(&mut boot_info.frame_allocator, frame);
                }
                halt_forever();
            }
        };
    if let Err(error) =
        candidate.clone_inherited_hierarchy(&mut boot_info.frame_allocator, &reader, inherited_root)
    {

            "page-table transition failed to clone inherited root: {:?}",
            error
        );
        release_candidate_after_probe_failure(candidate, &mut boot_info.frame_allocator);
    }

    let spans = [
        (
            "kernel text",
            segments.text.virtual_start,
            segments.text.physical_start,
            segments.text.virtual_end - segments.text.virtual_start,

        (
            "kernel rodata",
            segments.rodata.virtual_start,
            segments.rodata.physical_start,
            segments.rodata.virtual_end - segments.rodata.virtual_start,

        (

            segments.data.virtual_start,
            segments.data.physical_start,
            segments.data.virtual_end - segments.data.virtual_start,
        ),
        (
            "active boot stack",
            boot_info.boot_stack_virtual_start,
            boot_info.boot_stack_physical_start,
            boot_info.boot_stack_virtual_end - boot_info.boot_stack_virtual_start,
        ),
    ];
    for (label, virtual_start, physical_start, length) in spans {
        if !candidate_span_matches_source(
            &candidate,
            &reader,
            inherited_root,
            config,
            virtual_start,
            physical_start,
            length,
        ) {
            kprintln!(
                "page-table transition rejected: {} was not preserved",

            );
            release_candidate_after_probe_failure(candidate, &mut boot_info.frame_allocator);
        }

        .root_physical_address()

    let root_hhdm_address = match boot_info.memory_map.limine_hhdm_address(
        boot_info.hhdm_offset,
        candidate_root,
        rustix_kernel::paging::PAGE_SIZE,
        Some(physical_address_bits),
        boot_info.cpu_info.active_linear_address_bits,
    ) {
        Ok(address) => address,
        Err(error) => {
            kprintln!(
                "page-table transition rejected: candidate root HHDM: {:?}",
                error
            );
            release_candidate_after_probe_failure(candidate, &mut boot_info.frame_allocator);
        }
    };

            if translation.physical_address == candidate_root =>
        {
            translation
        }
        result => {
            kprintln!(
                "page-table transition rejected: candidate root HHDM alias: {:?}",

        }

    if !root_alias.permissions.writable || root_alias.permissions.user_accessible {

        release_candidate_after_probe_failure(candidate, &mut boot_info.frame_allocator);

        release_candidate_after_probe_failure(candidate, &mut boot_info.frame_allocator);
    }
    // SAFETY: The candidate is a complete clone of every present inherited

    unsafe { arch::x86_64::cpu::write_cr3_raw(new_cr3) };

        new_cr3,
        candidate_root,

fn probe_hhdm_frame(boot_info: &mut boot::BootInfo) {
    use rustix_kernel::frame::FRAME_SIZE;

    let frame = match boot_info.frame_allocator.allocate() {
        Some(frame) => frame,
        None => {
            kprintln!("HHDM frame probe failed: no free frame");
            halt_forever();
        }
    };
```
