```
/// Copy and validate the boot data needed by the current kernel.
///
/// Structural checks can reject malformed pointers and ranges, but cannot prove
/// that a loader-provided pointer is mapped and readable. That remains part of
/// the documented Limine handoff trust boundary until the kernel owns its maps.
pub fn capture_boot_information(entry_rsp: u64) -> Result<BootInfo, BootInfoError> {
    let cpu_info = crate::arch::x86_64::cpu::identify();
    let inherited_cr3_raw = crate::arch::x86_64::cpu::read_cr3_raw();
    let inherited_cr3_root = parse_cr3_root(
        inherited_cr3_raw,
        cpu_info.physical_address_bits,
        cpu_info.pcid_enabled,
    );
    let virtual_address_bits = cpu_info.active_linear_address_bits;
    let stack_size_request = core::ptr::addr_of_mut!(STACK_SIZE_REQUEST);
    // SAFETY: Limine completes supported request responses before `_start`.
    let stack_size_response_pointer = unsafe {
        core::ptr::read_volatile(core::ptr::addr_of!((*stack_size_request).response))
    };
    if stack_size_response_pointer.is_null() {
        return Err(BootInfoError::MissingStackSizeResponse);
    }
    if !is_valid_pointer(stack_size_response_pointer, virtual_address_bits) {
        return Err(BootInfoError::InvalidStackSizeResponsePointer);
    }
    // SAFETY: The response pointer is non-null, aligned, and canonical. As with
    // the other Limine responses, readability relies on the handoff contract.
    let _stack_size_response = unsafe { stack_size_response_pointer.read_volatile() };
    let (boot_stack_virtual_start, boot_stack_virtual_end) = limine_x86_64_stack_bounds(
        entry_rsp,
        virtual_address_bits,
        REQUESTED_BOOT_STACK_SIZE,
    )
    .ok_or(BootInfoError::InvalidInitialStackBounds)?;
    let hhdm_request = core::ptr::addr_of_mut!(HHDM_REQUEST);
    // SAFETY: Limine has completed writing the request response before `_start`.
    let hhdm_pointer =
        unsafe { core::ptr::read_volatile(core::ptr::addr_of!((*hhdm_request).response)) };
    if hhdm_pointer.is_null() {
        return Err(BootInfoError::MissingHhdmResponse);
    }
    if !is_valid_pointer(hhdm_pointer, virtual_address_bits) {
        return Err(BootInfoError::InvalidHhdmResponsePointer);
    }
    // SAFETY: The Limine response pointer is trusted to refer to a readable
    // response object; its nullness and alignment are checked above.
    let hhdm = unsafe { hhdm_pointer.read_volatile() };
    if hhdm.offset & 0xfff != 0 || !is_canonical_virtual_address(hhdm.offset, virtual_address_bits)
    {
        return Err(BootInfoError::InvalidHhdmOffset);
    }

    let executable_address_request = core::ptr::addr_of_mut!(EXECUTABLE_ADDRESS_REQUEST);
    // SAFETY: Limine has completed writing the request response before `_start`.
    let executable_address_pointer = unsafe {
        core::ptr::read_volatile(core::ptr::addr_of!((*executable_address_request).response))
    };
    if executable_address_pointer.is_null() {
        return Err(BootInfoError::MissingExecutableAddressResponse);
    }
    if !is_valid_pointer(executable_address_pointer, virtual_address_bits) {
        return Err(BootInfoError::InvalidExecutableAddressResponsePointer);
    }
    // SAFETY: Limine's response pointer is trusted to refer to a readable object;
    // nullness, alignment, and active-width canonicality were checked above.
    let executable_address = unsafe { executable_address_pointer.read_volatile() };
    // `linker.ld` defines these symbols as the boundaries of the loaded image.
    let (linked_virtual_start, linked_virtual_end) = (
        core::ptr::addr_of!(__kernel_start) as u64,
        core::ptr::addr_of!(__kernel_end) as u64,
    );
    let kernel_physical_end = kernel_image_physical_end(
        executable_address.physical_base,
        executable_address.virtual_base,
        linked_virtual_start,
        linked_virtual_end,
        cpu_info.physical_address_bits,
        virtual_address_bits,
    )
    .ok_or(BootInfoError::InvalidKernelImageRange)?;
    let linked_segments = KernelImageVirtualSegments {
        text: (
            core::ptr::addr_of!(__kernel_text_mapping_start) as u64,
            core::ptr::addr_of!(__kernel_text_mapping_end) as u64,
        ),
        rodata: (
            core::ptr::addr_of!(__kernel_rodata_mapping_start) as u64,
            core::ptr::addr_of!(__kernel_rodata_mapping_end) as u64,
        ),
        data: (
            core::ptr::addr_of!(__kernel_data_mapping_start) as u64,
            core::ptr::addr_of!(__kernel_data_mapping_end) as u64,
        ),
    };
    let kernel_image_segments = kernel_image_segments(
        executable_address.physical_base,
        executable_address.virtual_base,
        linked_virtual_start,
        linked_virtual_end,
        linked_segments,
        cpu_info.physical_address_bits,
        virtual_address_bits,
    )
    .ok_or(BootInfoError::InvalidKernelImageSegments)?;

    let memory_map_request = core::ptr::addr_of_mut!(MEMORY_MAP_REQUEST);
    // SAFETY: Limine has completed writing the request response before `_start`.
    let memory_map_pointer =
        unsafe { core::ptr::read_volatile(core::ptr::addr_of!((*memory_map_request).response)) };
    if memory_map_pointer.is_null() {
        return Err(BootInfoError::MissingMemoryMapResponse);
    }
    if !is_valid_pointer(memory_map_pointer, virtual_address_bits) {
        return Err(BootInfoError::InvalidMemoryMapResponsePointer);
    }
    // SAFETY: The Limine response pointer is trusted to refer to a readable
    // response object; its nullness and alignment are checked above.
    let response = unsafe { memory_map_pointer.read_volatile() };
    let entry_count = usize::try_from(response.entry_count)
        .map_err(|_| BootInfoError::MemoryMapCountDoesNotFit)?;
    if entry_count > MAX_MEMORY_REGIONS {
        return Err(BootInfoError::TooManyMemoryRegions);
    }
    if entry_count == 0 {
        return Err(BootInfoError::EmptyMemoryMap);
    }
    if response.entries.is_null() {
        return Err(BootInfoError::InvalidEntriesPointer);
    }
    if !is_valid_pointer(response.entries, virtual_address_bits) {
        return Err(BootInfoError::InvalidEntriesPointer);
    }
    let entry_bytes = entry_count
        .checked_mul(size_of::<*const MemoryMapEntry>())
        .ok_or(BootInfoError::EntriesAddressOverflow)?;
    let entries_start = response.entries as usize;
    let entries_end = entries_start
        .checked_add(entry_bytes)
        .ok_or(BootInfoError::EntriesAddressOverflow)?;
    if !is_canonical_virtual_address(entries_start as u64, virtual_address_bits)
        || !is_canonical_virtual_address((entries_end - 1) as u64, virtual_address_bits)
    {
        return Err(BootInfoError::InvalidEntriesPointer);
    }

    let mut builder = MemoryMapBuilder::new();
    for index in 0..entry_count {
        // SAFETY: Limine promises an array of `entry_count` pointers. The count
        // is capped and pointer alignment/address arithmetic are checked above.
        let entry_pointer = unsafe { response.entries.add(index).read_volatile() };
        if !is_valid_pointer(entry_pointer, virtual_address_bits) {
            return Err(BootInfoError::InvalidEntryPointer { index });
        }
        // SAFETY: Limine promises each non-null entry pointer is readable.
        let entry = unsafe { entry_pointer.read_volatile() };
        builder
            .push(entry.base, entry.length, entry.kind)
            .map_err(BootInfoError::InvalidMemoryMap)?;
    }

    let memory_map = builder.finish().map_err(|error| match error {
        MemoryMapError::EmptyMap => BootInfoError::EmptyMemoryMap,
        other => BootInfoError::InvalidMemoryMap(other),
    })?;
    for (index, region) in memory_map.regions().iter().enumerate() {
        if let Some(physical_bits) = cpu_info.physical_address_bits {
            if !physical_range_fits_address_width(region.start(), region.end(), physical_bits) {
                return Err(BootInfoError::InvalidPhysicalRange { index });
            }
        }
        if region.kind().is_mapped_by_limine_v3_hhdm()
            && !limine_v3_hhdm_range_is_valid(
                hhdm.offset,
                region.start(),
                region.end(),
                cpu_info.physical_address_bits,
                virtual_address_bits,
            )
        {
            return Err(BootInfoError::InvalidHhdmMappingRange { index });
        }
    }
    let boot_stack_physical_start = boot_stack_virtual_start
        .checked_sub(hhdm.offset)
        .ok_or(BootInfoError::InvalidInitialStackHhdmRange)?;
    let boot_stack_physical_end = boot_stack_virtual_end
        .checked_sub(hhdm.offset)
        .ok_or(BootInfoError::InvalidInitialStackHhdmRange)?;
    if !limine_v3_hhdm_range_is_valid(
        hhdm.offset,
        boot_stack_physical_start,
        boot_stack_physical_end,
        cpu_info.physical_address_bits,
        virtual_address_bits,
    ) {
        return Err(BootInfoError::InvalidInitialStackHhdmRange);
    }
    if !memory_map.range_is_within_region_kind(
        boot_stack_physical_start,
        boot_stack_physical_end,
        RegionKind::BootloaderReclaimable,
    ) {
        return Err(BootInfoError::InitialStackNotBootloaderReclaimable);
    }
    let frame_allocator =
        FrameAllocator::from_memory_map(&memory_map).map_err(BootInfoError::FrameAllocator)?;

    Ok(BootInfo {
        hhdm_revision: hhdm.revision,
        hhdm_offset: hhdm.offset,
        inherited_cr3_raw,
        inherited_cr3_root,
        executable_address_revision: executable_address.revision,
        kernel_physical_base: executable_address.physical_base,
        kernel_physical_end,
        kernel_virtual_base: executable_address.virtual_base,
        kernel_virtual_end: linked_virtual_end,
        kernel_image_segments,
        boot_stack_physical_start,
        boot_stack_physical_end,
        boot_stack_virtual_start,
        boot_stack_virtual_end,
        memory_map_revision: response.revision,
        memory_map,
        frame_allocator,
        cpu_info,
    })
}

/// Print a report from the copied snapshot; no loader pointers are used here.
pub fn report_boot_information(boot_info: &BootInfo) {
    crate::kprintln!(
        "HHDM: offset {:#018x}, response revision {}",
        boot_info.hhdm_offset,
        boot_info.hhdm_revision
    );
    crate::kprintln!(
        "inherited CR3: raw {:#018x} (not walked during boot snapshot)",
        boot_info.inherited_cr3_raw
    );
    match boot_info.inherited_cr3_root {
        Ok(root) => crate::kprintln!(
            "inherited CR3 root: physical {:#018x}, low bits {:?}",
            root.physical_address(),
            root.low_bits()
        ),
        Err(error) => crate::kprintln!("inherited CR3 root could not be decoded: {:?}", error),
    }
    crate::kprintln!(
        "kernel image: physical [{:#018x}, {:#018x}), virtual [{:#018x}, {:#018x}), response revision {}",
        boot_info.kernel_physical_base,
        boot_info.kernel_physical_end,
        boot_info.kernel_virtual_base,
        boot_info.kernel_virtual_end,
        boot_info.executable_address_revision
    );
    let segments = &boot_info.kernel_image_segments;
    crate::kprintln!(
        "kernel mapping text RX: physical [{:#018x}, {:#018x}), virtual [{:#018x}, {:#018x})",
        segments.text.physical_start,
        segments.text.physical_end,
        segments.text.virtual_start,
        segments.text.virtual_end
    );
    crate::kprintln!(
        "kernel mapping rodata R/NX: physical [{:#018x}, {:#018x}), virtual [{:#018x}, {:#018x})",
        segments.rodata.physical_start,
        segments.rodata.physical_end,
        segments.rodata.virtual_start,
        segments.rodata.virtual_end
    );
    crate::kprintln!(
        "kernel mapping data RW/NX: physical [{:#018x}, {:#018x}), virtual [{:#018x}, {:#018x})",
        segments.data.physical_start,
        segments.data.physical_end,
        segments.data.virtual_start,
        segments.data.virtual_end
    );
    crate::kprintln!(
        "boot stack (requested span: {} KiB): physical [{:#018x}, {:#018x}), virtual [{:#018x}, {:#018x})",
        (boot_info.boot_stack_virtual_end - boot_info.boot_stack_virtual_start) / 1024,
        boot_info.boot_stack_physical_start,
        boot_info.boot_stack_physical_end,
        boot_info.boot_stack_virtual_start,
        boot_info.boot_stack_virtual_end
    );
    crate::kprintln!(
        "memory map: {} validated regions, {} MiB usable RAM, response revision {}",
        boot_info.memory_map.regions().len(),
        boot_info.memory_map.usable_bytes() / (1024 * 1024),
        boot_info.memory_map_revision
    );
    crate::kprintln!(
        "physical frames: {} managed, {} free (4 KiB each)",
        boot_info.frame_allocator.managed_frames(),
        boot_info.frame_allocator.free_frames()
    );
    for region in boot_info.memory_map.regions() {
        crate::kprintln!(
            "  [{:#018x}, {:#018x}) {:?}",
            region.start(),
            region.end(),
            region.kind()
        );
    }
    crate::kprintln!("console: COM1 serial (polling)");

    let cpu = &boot_info.cpu_info;
    let vendor = core::str::from_utf8(&cpu.vendor).unwrap_or("unknown");
    let mtrr_supported = !matches!(&cpu.mtrr, MtrrState::Unsupported);
    crate::kprintln!(
        "CPU: {} (basic leaf {}, extended leaf {:#x})",
        vendor,
        cpu.max_basic_leaf,
        cpu.max_extended_leaf
    );
    crate::kprintln!(
        "CPU feature support: SSE2={}, NX={}, NXE-enabled={}, normal-caching={}, PAT={}, MTRR={}, 1GiB-pages={}, long-mode={}, LA57-supported={}, PCID-enabled={}",
        cpu.has_sse2,
        cpu.has_nx,
        cpu.nx_enabled,
        cpu.normal_caching,
        cpu.has_pat,
        mtrr_supported,
        cpu.has_1g_pages,
        cpu.has_long_mode,
        cpu.has_la57,
        cpu.pcid_enabled
    );
    match cpu.pat_msr_value {
        Some(value) => match PatLayout::from_msr_value(value) {
            Ok(layout) => crate::kprintln!(
                "PAT: IA32_PAT={:#018x}, WB index={:?}, UC index={:?}, WC index={:?}",
                value,
                layout.index_for(CachePolicy::WriteBack),
                layout.index_for(CachePolicy::Uncacheable),
                layout.index_for(CachePolicy::WriteCombining)
            ),
            Err(error) => crate::kprintln!(
                "PAT: IA32_PAT={:#018x} has unsupported layout: {:?}",
                value,
                error
            ),
        },
        None => crate::kprintln!("PAT: unsupported"),
    }
    match &cpu.mtrr {
        MtrrState::Unsupported => {
            crate::kprintln!("MTRR: unsupported")
        }
        MtrrState::VariableRangeCapacityExceeded { reported_count } => {
            crate::kprintln!(
                "MTRR: {} variable pairs exceed the snapshot capacity {}; no partial state retained",
                reported_count,
                MAX_CAPTURED_VARIABLE_MTRRS
            )
        }
        MtrrState::Captured(registers) => {
            crate::kprintln!(
                "MTRR snapshot: MTRRCAP={:#018x}, DEF_TYPE={:#018x}, enabled={}, fixed-enabled={}, fixed-supported={}, WC-supported={}, variable-pairs={}",
                registers.capability,
                registers.default_type,
                registers.default_type & (1 << 11) != 0,
                registers.default_type & (1 << 10) != 0,
                registers.capability & (1 << 8) != 0,
                registers.capability & (1 << 10) != 0,
                registers.variable_register_count
            )
        }
    }
    match (&cpu.mtrr, cpu.pat_msr_value, cpu.physical_address_bits) {
        (MtrrState::Captured(registers), Some(pat_value), Some(address_bits)) => {
            match (
                registers.validated_layout(address_bits),
                PatLayout::from_msr_value(pat_value),
            ) {
                (Ok(mtrr), Ok(pat)) => crate::kprintln!(
                    "MTRR/PAT: validated; effective type at PA 0x0 using PAT[0]={:?}",
                    mtrr.effective_memory_type_for(0, pat, 0, cpu.normal_caching)
                ),
                (Err(error), _) => {
                    crate::kprintln!("MTRR/PAT: rejected captured MTRR state: {:?}", error)
                }
                (_, Err(error)) => {
                    crate::kprintln!("MTRR/PAT: rejected captured PAT state: {:?}", error)
                }
            }
        }
        _ => crate::kprintln!(
            "MTRR/PAT: effective type unavailable (missing state or address width)"
        ),
    }
    crate::kprintln!(
        "CPU address widths (bits): physical={:?}, max-linear={:?}, active-linear={} (LA57 active={})",
        cpu.physical_address_bits,
        cpu.max_linear_address_bits,
        cpu.active_linear_address_bits,
        cpu.active_linear_address_bits == 57
    );
}

fn is_valid_pointer<T>(pointer: *const T, virtual_address_bits: u8) -> bool {
    let start = pointer as usize;
    let Some(end) = start.checked_add(size_of::<T>()) else {
        return false;
    };
    !pointer.is_null()
        && start & (align_of::<T>() - 1) == 0
        && is_canonical_virtual_address(start as u64, virtual_address_bits)
        && is_canonical_virtual_address((end - 1) as u64, virtual_address_bits)
}

```

```
#![no_main]

#[cfg(any(
    all(feature = "inject-page-fault", feature = "inject-invalid-opcode"),
    all(feature = "inject-page-fault", feature = "probe-hhdm-frame"),
    all(feature = "inject-invalid-opcode", feature = "probe-hhdm-frame")
))]
compile_error!("opt-in QEMU diagnostic features are mutually exclusive");

mod arch;
mod boot;
mod shell;

use core::panic::PanicInfo;
use rustix_kernel::vfs::RamFs;

static mut RAM_FILESYSTEM: RamFs = RamFs::new();

macro_rules! kprintln {
    () => {{
        crate::arch::x86_64::serial::print(format_args!("\r\n"));
    }};
    ($($argument:tt)*) => {{
        crate::arch::x86_64::serial::print(format_args!($($argument)*));
        crate::arch::x86_64::serial::print(format_args!("\r\n"));
    }};
}

pub(crate) use kprintln;

struct LimineHhdmPageTableReader<'a> {
    memory_map: &'a rustix_kernel::memory::MemoryMap,
    hhdm_offset: u64,
    physical_address_bits: u8,
    virtual_address_bits: u8,
}

impl rustix_kernel::paging::PageTableReader for LimineHhdmPageTableReader<'_> {
    type Error = rustix_kernel::memory::HhdmAddressError;

    fn read_entry(&self, table_physical: u64, index: u16) -> Result<u64, Self::Error> {
        if index >= 512 {
            return Err(rustix_kernel::memory::HhdmAddressError::InvalidHhdmRange);
        }
        let table_end = table_physical
            .checked_add(rustix_kernel::paging::PAGE_SIZE)
            .ok_or(rustix_kernel::memory::HhdmAddressError::AddressOverflow)?;
        if !self.memory_map.range_is_within_region_kind(
            table_physical,
            table_end,
            rustix_kernel::memory::RegionKind::BootloaderReclaimable,
        ) {
            return Err(rustix_kernel::memory::HhdmAddressError::NotLimineMapped);
        }
        let table_address = self.memory_map.limine_hhdm_address(
            self.hhdm_offset,
            table_physical,
            rustix_kernel::paging::PAGE_SIZE,
            Some(self.physical_address_bits),
            self.virtual_address_bits,
        )?;
        let entry_address = table_address
            .checked_add(u64::from(index) * core::mem::size_of::<u64>() as u64)
            .ok_or(rustix_kernel::memory::HhdmAddressError::AddressOverflow)?;
        // SAFETY: The complete table page was restricted to bootloader-reclaimable
        // memory and its HHDM address arithmetic was checked. The reader relies
        // on the Limine base-revision-3 mapping contract and never returns a ref.
        Ok(unsafe { (entry_address as *const u64).read_volatile() })
    }
}

struct LimineHhdmCandidateMemory<'a> {
    memory_map: &'a rustix_kernel::memory::MemoryMap,
    hhdm_offset: u64,
    physical_address_bits: u8,
    virtual_address_bits: u8,
}

// SAFETY: `prepare_table` accepts only an allocator-issued frame and validates
// its complete usable span and HHDM address. Handles are only used while the
// candidate retains the frame token and this unique backend borrow.
unsafe impl rustix_kernel::paging::CandidatePageTableMemory for LimineHhdmCandidateMemory<'_> {
    type PreparedTable = u64;
    type Error = rustix_kernel::memory::HhdmAddressError;

    fn prepare_table(
        &mut self,
        frame: &rustix_kernel::frame::Frame,
    ) -> Result<Self::PreparedTable, Self::Error> {
        frame.hhdm_address(
            self.memory_map,
            self.hhdm_offset,
            Some(self.physical_address_bits),
            self.virtual_address_bits,
        )
    }

    unsafe fn read_entry(
        &self,
        table: Self::PreparedTable,
        index: u16,
    ) -> Result<u64, Self::Error> {
        if index >= 512 {
            return Err(rustix_kernel::memory::HhdmAddressError::InvalidHhdmRange);
        }
        let entry_address = table
            .checked_add(u64::from(index) * core::mem::size_of::<u64>() as u64)
            .ok_or(rustix_kernel::memory::HhdmAddressError::AddressOverflow)?;
        // SAFETY: The unsafe trait contract requires `table` to be the prepared
        // HHDM address of a complete writable frame; the index is in [0, 512).
        Ok(unsafe { (entry_address as *const u64).read_volatile() })
    }

    unsafe fn clear_table(&mut self, table: Self::PreparedTable) {
        let entries = table as *mut u64;
        // SAFETY: The caller provides a handle prepared by this backend for a
        // complete writable frame retained by its candidate.
        unsafe {
            for index in 0..512 {
                entries.add(index).write_volatile(0);
            }
        }
    }

    unsafe fn write_entry(&mut self, table: Self::PreparedTable, index: u16, value: u64) {
        if index >= 512 {
            return;
        }
        let entry = (table as *mut u64).wrapping_add(usize::from(index));
        // SAFETY: The caller provides a prepared complete frame and an index in
        // range; this writes one entry without creating a Rust reference.
        unsafe { entry.write_volatile(value) };
    }
}

// Capture Limine's entry RSP before a Rust prologue changes it. The synthetic
// return slot is part of the SysV entry stack; realign before calling Rust.
core::arch::global_asm!(
    ".section .text",
    ".code64",
    ".global _start",
    ".type _start, @function",
    "_start:",
    "mov rdi, rsp",
    "and rsp, -16",
    "call rustix_start",
    "ud2",
    ".size _start, . - _start",
);

#[no_mangle]
pub extern "C" fn rustix_start(entry_rsp: u64) -> ! {
    arch::x86_64::serial::initialize();
    kprintln!("Rustix kernel: x86_64 Rust bootstrap");
    arch::x86_64::interrupts::initialize();
    kprintln!("x86_64 exception diagnostics: enabled (IRQs remain disabled)");
    let mut boot_info = match boot::capture_boot_information(entry_rsp) {
        Ok(boot_info) => boot_info,
        Err(error) => {
            kprintln!("boot information rejected: {:?}", error);
            halt_forever();
        }
    };
    boot::report_boot_information(&boot_info);

    #[cfg(feature = "probe-hhdm-frame")]
    probe_hhdm_frame(&mut boot_info);

    #[cfg(any(feature = "inject-page-fault", feature = "inject-invalid-opcode"))]
    run_fault_injection();

    activate_cloned_page_tables_and_run(&mut boot_info)
}

fn activate_cloned_page_tables_and_run(boot_info: &mut boot::BootInfo) -> ! {
    use rustix_kernel::paging::{
        encode_cr3_value, CandidatePageTables, PageWalkConfig, PageWalkOutcome,
    };

    let physical_address_bits = match boot_info.cpu_info.physical_address_bits {
        Some(bits) => bits,
        None => {
            kprintln!("page-table transition rejected: physical width unknown");
            halt_forever();
        }
    };
    let inherited_root = match boot_info.inherited_cr3_root {
        Ok(root) => root,
        Err(error) => {
            kprintln!("page-table transition rejected: inherited CR3: {:?}", error);
            halt_forever();
        }
    };
    if !boot_info.cpu_info.nx_enabled {
        kprintln!("page-table transition rejected: NXE is not enabled");
        halt_forever();
    }
    let config = PageWalkConfig {
        levels: if boot_info.cpu_info.active_linear_address_bits == 57 {
            5
        } else {
            4
        },
        physical_address_bits,
        virtual_address_bits: boot_info.cpu_info.active_linear_address_bits,
        nx_enabled: boot_info.cpu_info.nx_enabled,
        page_2m_supported: true,
        page_1g_supported: boot_info.cpu_info.has_1g_pages,
    };
    let reader = LimineHhdmPageTableReader {
        memory_map: &boot_info.memory_map,
        hhdm_offset: boot_info.hhdm_offset,
        physical_address_bits,
        virtual_address_bits: boot_info.cpu_info.active_linear_address_bits,
    };
    let mut memory = LimineHhdmCandidateMemory {
        memory_map: &boot_info.memory_map,
        hhdm_offset: boot_info.hhdm_offset,
        physical_address_bits,
        virtual_address_bits: boot_info.cpu_info.active_linear_address_bits,
    };
    let mut candidate =
        match CandidatePageTables::new(&mut boot_info.frame_allocator, &mut memory, config) {
            Ok(candidate) => candidate,
            Err(error) => {
                kprintln!(
                    "page-table transition failed to create root: {:?}",
                    error.cause
                );
                if let Some(frame) = error.frame {
                    release_probe_frame(&mut boot_info.frame_allocator, frame);
                }
                halt_forever();
            }
        };
    if let Err(error) =
        candidate.clone_inherited_hierarchy(&mut boot_info.frame_allocator, &reader, inherited_root)
    {
        kprintln!(
            "page-table transition failed to clone inherited root: {:?}",
            error
        );
        release_candidate_after_probe_failure(candidate, &mut boot_info.frame_allocator);
    }

    let segments = boot_info.kernel_image_segments;
    let spans = [
        (
            "kernel text",
            segments.text.virtual_start,
            segments.text.physical_start,
            segments.text.virtual_end - segments.text.virtual_start,
        ),
        (
            "kernel rodata",
            segments.rodata.virtual_start,
            segments.rodata.physical_start,
            segments.rodata.virtual_end - segments.rodata.virtual_start,
        ),
        (
            "kernel data",
            segments.data.virtual_start,
            segments.data.physical_start,
            segments.data.virtual_end - segments.data.virtual_start,
        ),
        (
            "active boot stack",
            boot_info.boot_stack_virtual_start,
            boot_info.boot_stack_physical_start,
            boot_info.boot_stack_virtual_end - boot_info.boot_stack_virtual_start,
        ),
    ];
    for (label, virtual_start, physical_start, length) in spans {
        if !candidate_span_matches_source(
            &candidate,
            &reader,
            inherited_root,
            config,
            virtual_start,
            physical_start,
            length,
        ) {
            kprintln!(
                "page-table transition rejected: {} was not preserved",
                label
            );
            release_candidate_after_probe_failure(candidate, &mut boot_info.frame_allocator);
        }
    }
    let candidate_root = candidate
        .root_physical_address()
        .expect("a live candidate retains its root frame");
    let root_hhdm_address = match boot_info.memory_map.limine_hhdm_address(
        boot_info.hhdm_offset,
        candidate_root,
        rustix_kernel::paging::PAGE_SIZE,
        Some(physical_address_bits),
        boot_info.cpu_info.active_linear_address_bits,
    ) {
        Ok(address) => address,
        Err(error) => {
            kprintln!(
                "page-table transition rejected: candidate root HHDM: {:?}",
                error
            );
            release_candidate_after_probe_failure(candidate, &mut boot_info.frame_allocator);
        }
    };
    let root_alias = match candidate.walk(root_hhdm_address) {
        Ok(PageWalkOutcome::Mapped(translation))
            if translation.physical_address == candidate_root =>
        {
            translation
        }
        result => {
            kprintln!(
                "page-table transition rejected: candidate root HHDM alias: {:?}",
                result
            );
            release_candidate_after_probe_failure(candidate, &mut boot_info.frame_allocator);
        }
    };
    if !root_alias.permissions.writable || root_alias.permissions.user_accessible {
        kprintln!("page-table transition rejected: candidate root alias permissions are unsafe");
        release_candidate_after_probe_failure(candidate, &mut boot_info.frame_allocator);
    }

    let new_cr3 = match encode_cr3_value(
        candidate_root,
        inherited_root.low_bits(),
        physical_address_bits,
    ) {
        Ok(value) => value,
        Err(error) => {
            kprintln!("page-table transition rejected: new CR3: {:?}", error);
            release_candidate_after_probe_failure(candidate, &mut boot_info.frame_allocator);
        }
    };
    let inherited_cr3 = boot_info.inherited_cr3_raw;
    if arch::x86_64::cpu::read_cr3_raw() != inherited_cr3 {
        kprintln!("page-table transition aborted: active CR3 changed before switch");
        release_candidate_after_probe_failure(candidate, &mut boot_info.frame_allocator);
    }
    // SAFETY: The candidate is a complete clone of every present inherited
    // hierarchy entry, with all referenced intermediate tables owned and the
    // critical code/data/stack paths compared before this point. The inherited
    // root's paging mode, address widths, PAT/MTRR state, and low CR3 mode are
    // preserved; interrupts are disabled from bootstrap initialization onward.
    unsafe { arch::x86_64::cpu::write_cr3_raw(new_cr3) };
    if arch::x86_64::cpu::read_cr3_raw() != new_cr3
        || !spans
            .iter()
            .all(|(_, virtual_start, physical_start, length)| {
                candidate_span_matches_source(
                    &candidate,
                    &reader,
                    inherited_root,
                    config,
                    *virtual_start,
                    *physical_start,
                    *length,
                )
            })
    {
        // SAFETY: The inherited root and its backing memory remain untouched and
        // mapped by the candidate, so restoring its validated CR3 value is safe.
        unsafe { arch::x86_64::cpu::write_cr3_raw(inherited_cr3) };
        kprintln!("page-table transition failed post-switch verification; restored inherited CR3");
        release_candidate_after_probe_failure(candidate, &mut boot_info.frame_allocator);
    }
    kprintln!(
        "page-table transition passed: active CR3={:#x}, cloned root={:#x}, {} owned tables",
        new_cr3,
        candidate_root,
        candidate.table_count()
    );

    // Keep the candidate and its frame tokens alive for as long as this root is
    // active. The shell runs forever and does not return to this stack frame.
    // SAFETY: The bootstrap is single-core, interrupts remain disabled, and the
    // shell is the only filesystem owner.
    let filesystem = unsafe { &mut *core::ptr::addr_of_mut!(RAM_FILESYSTEM) };
    match filesystem.seed_defaults() {
        Ok(home) => shell::run(filesystem, home, boot_info),
        Err(error) => {
            kprintln!("RAM filesystem initialization failed: {:?}", error);
            halt_forever()
        }
    }
}

#[cfg(feature = "probe-hhdm-frame")]
fn probe_hhdm_frame(boot_info: &mut boot::BootInfo) {
    use rustix_kernel::frame::FRAME_SIZE;

    let frame = match boot_info.frame_allocator.allocate() {
        Some(frame) => frame,
        None => {
            kprintln!("HHDM frame probe failed: no free frame");
            halt_forever();
        }
    };
    let hhdm_address = match frame.hhdm_address(
        &boot_info.memory_map,
        boot_info.hhdm_offset,
        boot_info.cpu_info.physical_address_bits,
        boot_info.cpu_info.active_linear_address_bits,
    ) {
        Ok(address) => address,
        Err(error) => {
            kprintln!("HHDM frame probe rejected frame translation: {:?}", error);
            release_probe_frame(&mut boot_info.frame_allocator, frame);
            halt_forever();
        }
    };

    let words = (FRAME_SIZE / core::mem::size_of::<u64>() as u64) as usize;
    let page = hhdm_address as *mut u64;
    let mut verified = true;
    // SAFETY: The non-copyable `Frame` token is held exclusively; its full page
    // is within validated `Usable` memory and its HHDM arithmetic was checked.
    // Limine base revision 3 guarantees usable memory in the HHDM, and no other
    // Rustix mapping aliases this newly allocated frame. This is an opt-in QEMU
    // probe; a broken loader mapping would fault and be caught by the fatal path.
    unsafe {
        for index in 0..words {
            page.add(index)
                .write_volatile(0xa5a5_0000_0000_0000 ^ index as u64);
        }
        for index in 0..words {
            if page.add(index).read_volatile() != (0xa5a5_0000_0000_0000 ^ index as u64) {
                verified = false;
                break;
            }
        }
        for index in 0..words {
            page.add(index).write_volatile(0);
        }
    }

    release_probe_frame(&mut boot_info.frame_allocator, frame);
    if !verified {
        kprintln!("HHDM frame probe failed: readback mismatch");
        halt_forever();
    }
    kprintln!("HHDM frame probe passed: wrote, read, cleared, and reclaimed one frame");
    probe_inherited_root(boot_info);
}

#[cfg(feature = "probe-hhdm-frame")]
fn probe_inherited_root(boot_info: &mut boot::BootInfo) {
    use rustix_kernel::paging::inherited_cr3_root_hhdm_address;

    let root = match boot_info.inherited_cr3_root {
        Ok(root) => root,
        Err(error) => {
            kprintln!(
                "inherited root probe failed: CR3 decode rejected: {:?}",
                error
            );
            halt_forever();
        }
    };
    let address = match inherited_cr3_root_hhdm_address(
        root,
        &boot_info.memory_map,
        boot_info.hhdm_offset,
        boot_info.cpu_info.physical_address_bits,
        boot_info.cpu_info.active_linear_address_bits,
    ) {
        Ok(address) => address,
        Err(error) => {
            kprintln!(
                "inherited root probe failed: HHDM validation rejected: {:?}",
                error
            );
            halt_forever();
        }
    };
    let entries = address as *const u64;
    let mut present_entries = 0;
    // SAFETY: The complete root page was validated as bootloader-reclaimable
    // and its HHDM range arithmetic was checked. The Limine base-revision-3
    // contract maps that region; this read-only opt-in probe trusts that handoff.
    unsafe {
        for index in 0..512 {
            if entries.add(index).read_volatile() & 1 != 0 {
                present_entries += 1;
            }
        }
    }
    kprintln!(
        "inherited root HHDM probe passed: read 512 entries, {} present",
        present_entries
    );
    let physical_address_bits = match boot_info.cpu_info.physical_address_bits {
        Some(bits) => bits,
        None => {
            kprintln!("inherited page-table walk failed: physical width unknown");
            halt_forever();
        }
    };
    let reader = LimineHhdmPageTableReader {
        memory_map: &boot_info.memory_map,
        hhdm_offset: boot_info.hhdm_offset,
        physical_address_bits,
        virtual_address_bits: boot_info.cpu_info.active_linear_address_bits,
    };
    let config = rustix_kernel::paging::PageWalkConfig {
        levels: if boot_info.cpu_info.active_linear_address_bits == 57 {
            5
        } else {
            4
        },
        physical_address_bits,
        virtual_address_bits: boot_info.cpu_info.active_linear_address_bits,
        nx_enabled: boot_info.cpu_info.nx_enabled,
        page_2m_supported: true,
        page_1g_supported: boot_info.cpu_info.has_1g_pages,
    };
    let segments = boot_info.kernel_image_segments;
    verify_inherited_mapping(
        &reader,
        root,
        config,
        "kernel text",
        segments.text.virtual_start,
        segments.text.physical_start,
        segments.text.virtual_end - segments.text.virtual_start,
    );
    verify_inherited_mapping(
        &reader,
        root,
        config,
        "kernel rodata",
        segments.rodata.virtual_start,
        segments.rodata.physical_start,
        segments.rodata.virtual_end - segments.rodata.virtual_start,
    );
    verify_inherited_mapping(
        &reader,
        root,
        config,
        "kernel data",
        segments.data.virtual_start,
        segments.data.physical_start,
        segments.data.virtual_end - segments.data.virtual_start,
    );
    verify_inherited_mapping(
        &reader,
        root,
        config,
        "active boot stack",
        boot_info.boot_stack_virtual_start,
        boot_info.boot_stack_physical_start,
        boot_info.boot_stack_virtual_end - boot_info.boot_stack_virtual_start,
    );

    let pat_value = match boot_info.cpu_info.pat_msr_value {
        Some(value) => value,
        None => {
            kprintln!("cache-alias probe failed: active PAT value unavailable");
            halt_forever();
        }
    };
    let pat = match rustix_kernel::paging::PatLayout::from_msr_value(pat_value) {
        Ok(pat) => pat,
        Err(error) => {
            kprintln!("cache-alias probe failed: invalid PAT layout: {:?}", error);
            halt_forever();
        }
    };
    let registers = match &boot_info.cpu_info.mtrr {
        rustix_kernel::paging::MtrrState::Captured(registers) => registers,
        _ => {
            kprintln!("cache-alias probe failed: captured MTRR state unavailable");
            halt_forever();
        }
    };
    let mtrrs = match registers.validated_layout(physical_address_bits) {
        Ok(mtrrs) => mtrrs,
        Err(error) => {
            kprintln!("cache-alias probe failed: invalid MTRR state: {:?}", error);
            halt_forever();
        }
    };
    if !boot_info.cpu_info.normal_caching {
        kprintln!("cache-alias probe failed: non-normal CR0 caching mode");
        halt_forever();
    }
    verify_kernel_cache_aliases(
        boot_info,
        &reader,
        root,
        config,
        pat,
        &mtrrs,
        "kernel text",
        segments.text.virtual_start,
        segments.text.physical_start,
        segments.text.virtual_end - segments.text.virtual_start,
    );
    verify_kernel_cache_aliases(
        boot_info,
        &reader,
        root,
        config,
        pat,
        &mtrrs,
        "kernel rodata",
        segments.rodata.virtual_start,
        segments.rodata.physical_start,
        segments.rodata.virtual_end - segments.rodata.virtual_start,
    );
    verify_kernel_cache_aliases(
        boot_info,
        &reader,
        root,
        config,
        pat,
        &mtrrs,
        "kernel data",
        segments.data.virtual_start,
        segments.data.physical_start,
        segments.data.virtual_end - segments.data.virtual_start,
    );
    probe_cloned_page_tables(
        &mut boot_info.frame_allocator,
        &boot_info.memory_map,
        boot_info.hhdm_offset,
        physical_address_bits,
        boot_info.cpu_info.active_linear_address_bits,
        &reader,
        root,
        config,
        [
            (
                "kernel text",
                segments.text.virtual_start,
                segments.text.physical_start,
                segments.text.virtual_end - segments.text.virtual_start,
            ),
            (
                "kernel rodata",
                segments.rodata.virtual_start,
                segments.rodata.physical_start,
                segments.rodata.virtual_end - segments.rodata.virtual_start,
            ),
            (
                "kernel data",
                segments.data.virtual_start,
                segments.data.physical_start,
                segments.data.virtual_end - segments.data.virtual_start,
            ),
            (
                "active boot stack",
                boot_info.boot_stack_virtual_start,
                boot_info.boot_stack_physical_start,
                boot_info.boot_stack_virtual_end - boot_info.boot_stack_virtual_start,
            ),
        ],
    );
    probe_candidate_page_tables(boot_info);
}

#[cfg(feature = "probe-hhdm-frame")]
fn probe_cloned_page_tables(
    allocator: &mut rustix_kernel::frame::FrameAllocator,
    memory_map: &rustix_kernel::memory::MemoryMap,
    hhdm_offset: u64,
    physical_address_bits: u8,
    virtual_address_bits: u8,
    source_reader: &impl rustix_kernel::paging::PageTableReader<
        Error = rustix_kernel::memory::HhdmAddressError,
    >,
    source_root: rustix_kernel::paging::Cr3Root,
    config: rustix_kernel::paging::PageWalkConfig,
    spans: [(&str, u64, u64, u64); 4],
) {
    use rustix_kernel::paging::CandidatePageTables;

    let mut memory = LimineHhdmCandidateMemory {
        memory_map,
        hhdm_offset,
        physical_address_bits,
        virtual_address_bits,
    };
    let mut candidate = match CandidatePageTables::new(allocator, &mut memory, config) {
        Ok(candidate) => candidate,
        Err(error) => {
            kprintln!(
                "candidate clone probe failed to create root: {:?}",
                error.cause
            );
            if let Some(frame) = error.frame {
                release_probe_frame(allocator, frame);
            }
            halt_forever();
        }
    };
    if let Err(error) = candidate.clone_inherited_hierarchy(allocator, source_reader, source_root) {
        kprintln!("candidate clone probe failed: {:?}", error);
        release_candidate_after_probe_failure(candidate, allocator);
    }
    for (label, virtual_start, physical_start, length) in spans {
        if !candidate_span_matches_source(
            &candidate,
            source_reader,
            source_root,
            config,
            virtual_start,
            physical_start,
            length,
        ) {
            kprintln!(
                "candidate clone probe failed: {} translation mismatch",
                label
            );
            release_candidate_after_probe_failure(candidate, allocator);
        }
    }
    let table_count = candidate.table_count();
    if let Err(failure) = candidate.release(allocator) {
        kprintln!(
            "candidate clone probe failed to release frames: {:?}",
            failure
        );
        halt_forever();
    }
    kprintln!(
        "candidate inherited-root clone probe passed: {} owned table pages preserve critical paths; CR3 unchanged",
        table_count
    );
}

fn candidate_span_matches_source(
    candidate: &rustix_kernel::paging::CandidatePageTables<'_, LimineHhdmCandidateMemory<'_>>,
    source_reader: &impl rustix_kernel::paging::PageTableReader<
        Error = rustix_kernel::memory::HhdmAddressError,
    >,
    source_root: rustix_kernel::paging::Cr3Root,
    config: rustix_kernel::paging::PageWalkConfig,
    virtual_start: u64,
    physical_start: u64,
    length: u64,
) -> bool {
    use rustix_kernel::paging::{walk_virtual_address, PageWalkOutcome};

    let mut offset = 0;
    while offset < length {
        let Some(virtual_address) = virtual_start.checked_add(offset) else {
            return false;
        };
        let Some(expected_physical) = physical_start.checked_add(offset) else {
            return false;
        };
        let source_result =
            walk_virtual_address(source_reader, source_root, virtual_address, config);
        let candidate_result = candidate.walk(virtual_address);
        let (source_translation, candidate_translation) = match (source_result, candidate_result) {
            (Ok(PageWalkOutcome::Mapped(source)), Ok(PageWalkOutcome::Mapped(candidate))) => {
                (source, candidate)
            }
            (source, candidate) => {
                kprintln!(
                    "candidate clone walk mismatch at {:#018x}: inherited={:?}, candidate={:?}",
                    virtual_address,
                    source,
                    candidate
                );
                return false;
            }
        };
        // The CPU may update Accessed/Dirty in the active hierarchy after the
        // clone; they are hardware tracking state, not translation policy.
        let hardware_tracking_bits = (1 << 5) | (1 << 6);
        if source_translation.physical_address != candidate_translation.physical_address
            || source_translation.leaf_physical_base != candidate_translation.leaf_physical_base
            || source_translation.page_size != candidate_translation.page_size
            || source_translation.permissions != candidate_translation.permissions
            || source_translation.pat_index != candidate_translation.pat_index
            || source_translation.raw_leaf_entry & !hardware_tracking_bits
                != candidate_translation.raw_leaf_entry & !hardware_tracking_bits
            || candidate_translation.physical_address != expected_physical
        {
            kprintln!(
                "candidate clone translation mismatch at {:#018x}: inherited={:?}, candidate={:?}, expected PA={:#x}",
                virtual_address,
                source_translation,
                candidate_translation,
                expected_physical
            );
            return false;
        }
        let Some(next_offset) = offset.checked_add(rustix_kernel::paging::PAGE_SIZE) else {
            return false;
        };
        offset = next_offset;
    }
    true
}

#[cfg(feature = "probe-hhdm-frame")]
fn probe_candidate_page_tables(boot_info: &mut boot::BootInfo) {
    use rustix_kernel::paging::{
        validate_mapping_range, CachePolicy, CandidatePageTables, PagePermissions, PageWalkOutcome,
    };

    let Some(physical_address_bits) = boot_info.cpu_info.physical_address_bits else {
        kprintln!("candidate page-table probe failed: physical width unknown");
        halt_forever();
    };
    if !boot_info.cpu_info.nx_enabled || !boot_info.cpu_info.normal_caching {
        kprintln!("candidate page-table probe failed: NXE or normal caching unavailable");
        halt_forever();
    }
    let pat_value = boot_info
        .cpu_info
        .pat_msr_value
        .expect("inherited cache-alias probe validated active PAT");
    let pat = rustix_kernel::paging::PatLayout::from_msr_value(pat_value).unwrap_or_else(|error| {
        kprintln!(
            "candidate page-table probe failed: invalid PAT: {:?}",
            error
        );
        halt_forever();
    });
    let registers = match &boot_info.cpu_info.mtrr {
        rustix_kernel::paging::MtrrState::Captured(registers) => registers,
        _ => {
            kprintln!("candidate page-table probe failed: captured MTRR state unavailable");
            halt_forever();
        }
    };
    let mtrrs = match registers.validated_layout(physical_address_bits) {
        Ok(mtrrs) => mtrrs,
        Err(error) => {
            kprintln!(
                "candidate page-table probe failed: invalid MTRR: {:?}",
                error
            );
            halt_forever();
        }
    };
    let config = rustix_kernel::paging::PageWalkConfig {
        levels: if boot_info.cpu_info.active_linear_address_bits == 57 {
            5
        } else {
            4
        },
        physical_address_bits,
        virtual_address_bits: boot_info.cpu_info.active_linear_address_bits,
        nx_enabled: true,
        page_2m_supported: true,
        page_1g_supported: boot_info.cpu_info.has_1g_pages,
    };
    let virtual_address = 0xffff_9000_ffff_f000;
    let permissions = PagePermissions {
        writable: true,
        executable: false,
        user_accessible: false,
    };
    let frame = match boot_info.frame_allocator.allocate() {
        Some(frame) => frame,
        None => {
            kprintln!("candidate page-table probe failed: no leaf frame available");
            halt_forever();
        }
    };
    let mapping = match validate_mapping_range(
        virtual_address,
        frame.address(),
        rustix_kernel::paging::PAGE_SIZE,
        permissions,
        Some(physical_address_bits),
        config.virtual_address_bits,
    ) {
        Ok(mapping) => mapping,
        Err(error) => {
            kprintln!(
                "candidate page-table probe failed: invalid mapping: {:?}",
                error
            );
            release_probe_frame(&mut boot_info.frame_allocator, frame);
            halt_forever();
        }
    };
    let cache_attributes = match mapping.select_cache_attributes(
        CachePolicy::WriteBack,
        pat,
        &mtrrs,
        boot_info.cpu_info.normal_caching,
    ) {
        Ok(attributes) => attributes,
        Err(error) => {
            kprintln!(
                "candidate page-table probe failed: cache policy: {:?}",
                error
            );
            release_probe_frame(&mut boot_info.frame_allocator, frame);
            halt_forever();
        }
    };

    let mut memory = LimineHhdmCandidateMemory {
        memory_map: &boot_info.memory_map,
        hhdm_offset: boot_info.hhdm_offset,
        physical_address_bits,
        virtual_address_bits: boot_info.cpu_info.active_linear_address_bits,
    };
    let mut candidate =
        match CandidatePageTables::new(&mut boot_info.frame_allocator, &mut memory, config) {
            Ok(candidate) => candidate,
            Err(error) => {
                kprintln!(
                    "candidate page-table probe failed to create root: {:?}",
                    error.cause
                );
                release_probe_frame(&mut boot_info.frame_allocator, frame);
                if let Some(root_frame) = error.frame {
                    release_probe_frame(&mut boot_info.frame_allocator, root_frame);
                }
                halt_forever();
            }
        };
    let root = candidate.root_physical_address();
    let frame_address = frame.address();
    if let Err(failure) = candidate.map_owned_page(
        &mut boot_info.frame_allocator,
        frame,
        mapping,
        cache_attributes,
    ) {
        kprintln!(
            "candidate page-table probe failed to map leaf: {:?}",
            failure.cause
        );
        release_probe_frame(&mut boot_info.frame_allocator, failure.frame);
        release_candidate_after_probe_failure(candidate, &mut boot_info.frame_allocator);
    }

    let walk = candidate.walk(virtual_address);
    let returned_frame = match candidate.unmap_owned_page(virtual_address) {
        Ok(frame) => frame,
        Err(error) => {
            kprintln!(
                "candidate page-table probe failed to unmap leaf: {:?}",
                error
            );
            release_candidate_after_probe_failure(candidate, &mut boot_info.frame_allocator);
        }
    };
    let translation_valid = match &walk {
        Ok(PageWalkOutcome::Mapped(translation)) => {
            translation.physical_address == frame_address
                && translation.page_size == rustix_kernel::paging::PAGE_SIZE
                && translation.permissions == permissions
                && translation.pat_index == cache_attributes.pat_index()
        }
        _ => false,
    };
    if returned_frame.address() != frame_address {
        kprintln!("candidate page-table probe failed: unmap returned the wrong frame");
        release_probe_frame(&mut boot_info.frame_allocator, returned_frame);
        release_candidate_after_probe_failure(candidate, &mut boot_info.frame_allocator);
    }
    release_probe_frame(&mut boot_info.frame_allocator, returned_frame);
    if !translation_valid {
        kprintln!(
            "candidate page-table probe failed: candidate walk: {:?}",
            walk
        );
        release_candidate_after_probe_failure(candidate, &mut boot_info.frame_allocator);
    }
    if let Err(failure) = candidate.release(&mut boot_info.frame_allocator) {
        kprintln!(
            "candidate page-table probe failed to release frames: {:?}",
            failure
        );
        halt_forever();
    }
    kprintln!(
        "candidate page-table probe passed: mapped, walked, unmapped, and released root {:#x}; CR3 unchanged",
        root.expect("candidate retains root until release")
    );
}

fn release_candidate_after_probe_failure(
    candidate: rustix_kernel::paging::CandidatePageTables<'_, LimineHhdmCandidateMemory<'_>>,
    allocator: &mut rustix_kernel::frame::FrameAllocator,
) -> ! {
    if let Err(failure) = candidate.release(allocator) {
        kprintln!("candidate page-table cleanup also failed: {:?}", failure);
    }
    halt_forever()
}

#[cfg(feature = "probe-hhdm-frame")]
fn verify_inherited_mapping(
    reader: &impl rustix_kernel::paging::PageTableReader<
        Error = rustix_kernel::memory::HhdmAddressError,
    >,
    root: rustix_kernel::paging::Cr3Root,
    config: rustix_kernel::paging::PageWalkConfig,
    label: &str,
    virtual_start: u64,
    physical_start: u64,
    length: u64,
) {
    use rustix_kernel::paging::{walk_virtual_address, PageWalkOutcome};

    let mut offset = 0;
    let mut pages = 0;
    let mut first_translation: Option<rustix_kernel::paging::PageTranslation> = None;
    let mut permissions_uniform = true;
    let mut pat_index_uniform = true;
    while offset < length {
        let virtual_address = match virtual_start.checked_add(offset) {
            Some(address) => address,
            None => {
                kprintln!("inherited mapping probe failed: {} virtual overflow", label);
                halt_forever();
            }
        };
        let expected_physical = match physical_start.checked_add(offset) {
            Some(address) => address,
            None => {
                kprintln!(
                    "inherited mapping probe failed: {} physical overflow",
                    label
                );
                halt_forever();
            }
        };
        let translation = match walk_virtual_address(reader, root, virtual_address, config) {
            Ok(PageWalkOutcome::Mapped(translation)) => translation,
            Ok(PageWalkOutcome::NotPresent { level }) => {
                if level == rustix_kernel::paging::PageLevel::Pml4 {
                    let pml4_index = ((virtual_address >> 39) & 0x1ff) as u16;
                    let root_entry = reader.read_entry(root.physical_address(), pml4_index);
                    kprintln!(
                        "inherited mapping PML4 detail: VA={:#018x}, index={}, root={:#x}, entry={:?}",
                        virtual_address,
                        pml4_index,
                        root.physical_address(),
                        root_entry
                    );
                }
                kprintln!(
                    "inherited mapping probe failed: {} absent at {:?}",
                    label,
                    level
                );
                halt_forever();
            }
            Err(error) => {
                kprintln!("inherited mapping probe failed: {}: {:?}", label, error);
                halt_forever();
            }
        };
        if translation.physical_address != expected_physical {
            kprintln!(
                "inherited mapping probe failed: {} {:#018x} mapped to {:#018x}, expected {:#018x}",
                label,
                virtual_address,
                translation.physical_address,
                expected_physical
            );
            halt_forever();
        }
        if let Some(first) = first_translation {
            permissions_uniform &= translation.permissions == first.permissions;
            pat_index_uniform &= translation.pat_index == first.pat_index;
        } else {
            first_translation = Some(translation);
        }
        pages += 1;
        offset += rustix_kernel::paging::PAGE_SIZE;
    }
    if let Some(first) = first_translation {
        kprintln!(
            "inherited mapping probe passed: {} ({} pages), first permissions={:?}, PAT index={}, leaf size={}, uniform permissions={}, uniform PAT index={}",
            label,
            pages,
            first.permissions,
            first.pat_index,
            first.page_size,
            permissions_uniform,
            pat_index_uniform
        );
    }
}

#[cfg(feature = "probe-hhdm-frame")]
fn verify_kernel_cache_aliases(
    boot_info: &boot::BootInfo,
    reader: &impl rustix_kernel::paging::PageTableReader<
        Error = rustix_kernel::memory::HhdmAddressError,
    >,
    root: rustix_kernel::paging::Cr3Root,
    config: rustix_kernel::paging::PageWalkConfig,
    pat: rustix_kernel::paging::PatLayout,
    mtrrs: &rustix_kernel::paging::ValidatedMtrrLayout,
    label: &str,
    kernel_virtual_start: u64,
    physical_start: u64,
    length: u64,
) {
    use rustix_kernel::paging::{walk_virtual_address, PageWalkOutcome};

    let mut offset = 0;
    let mut pages = 0;
    while offset < length {
        let physical = match physical_start.checked_add(offset) {
            Some(address) => address,
            None => {
                kprintln!("cache-alias probe failed: {} physical overflow", label);
                halt_forever();
            }
        };
        let kernel_virtual = match kernel_virtual_start.checked_add(offset) {
            Some(address) => address,
            None => {
                kprintln!("cache-alias probe failed: {} virtual overflow", label);
                halt_forever();
            }
        };
        let hhdm_virtual = match boot_info.memory_map.limine_hhdm_address(
            boot_info.hhdm_offset,
            physical,
            rustix_kernel::paging::PAGE_SIZE,
            boot_info.cpu_info.physical_address_bits,
            boot_info.cpu_info.active_linear_address_bits,
        ) {
            Ok(address) => address,
            Err(error) => {
                kprintln!(
                    "cache-alias probe failed: {} HHDM range: {:?}",
                    label,
                    error
                );
                halt_forever();
            }
        };
        let kernel_translation = match walk_virtual_address(reader, root, kernel_virtual, config) {
            Ok(PageWalkOutcome::Mapped(translation)) => translation,
            result => {
                kprintln!(
                    "cache-alias probe failed: {} kernel walk: {:?}",
                    label,
                    result
                );
                halt_forever();
            }
        };
        let hhdm_translation = match walk_virtual_address(reader, root, hhdm_virtual, config) {
            Ok(PageWalkOutcome::Mapped(translation)) => translation,
            result => {
                kprintln!(
                    "cache-alias probe failed: {} HHDM walk: {:?}",
                    label,
                    result
                );
                halt_forever();
            }
        };
        if kernel_translation.physical_address != physical
            || hhdm_translation.physical_address != physical
        {
            kprintln!(
                "cache-alias probe failed: {} physical {:#018x} has inconsistent translations",
                label,
                physical
            );
            halt_forever();
        }
        let kernel_type = match mtrrs.effective_memory_type_for(
            physical,
            pat,
            kernel_translation.pat_index,
            boot_info.cpu_info.normal_caching,
        ) {
            Ok(memory_type) => memory_type,
            Err(error) => {
                kprintln!(
                    "cache-alias probe failed: {} kernel PAT/MTRR: {:?}",
                    label,
                    error
                );
                halt_forever();
            }
        };
        let hhdm_type = match mtrrs.effective_memory_type_for(
            physical,
            pat,
            hhdm_translation.pat_index,
            boot_info.cpu_info.normal_caching,
        ) {
            Ok(memory_type) => memory_type,
            Err(error) => {
                kprintln!(
                    "cache-alias probe failed: {} HHDM PAT/MTRR: {:?}",
                    label,
                    error
                );
                halt_forever();
            }
        };
        if kernel_type != hhdm_type {
            kprintln!(
                "cache-alias conflict: {} PA {:#018x}, kernel {:?} vs HHDM {:?}",
                label,
                physical,
                kernel_type,
                hhdm_type
            );
            halt_forever();
        }
        pages += 1;
        offset += rustix_kernel::paging::PAGE_SIZE;
    }
    kprintln!(
        "cache-alias probe passed: {} ({} pages; effective types match)",
        label,
        pages
    );
}

fn release_probe_frame(
    allocator: &mut rustix_kernel::frame::FrameAllocator,
    frame: rustix_kernel::frame::Frame,
) {
    if let Err(error) = allocator.deallocate(frame) {
        kprintln!(
            "HHDM frame probe failed to return its frame: {:?}",
            error.error
        );
        halt_forever();
    }
}

#[cfg(feature = "inject-page-fault")]
fn run_fault_injection() {
    kprintln!("fault injection: triggering page fault at 0x00000000deadbeef");
    // SAFETY: This is an opt-in QEMU test that deliberately reads an unmapped
    // low virtual address; the installed page-fault handler is expected to halt.
    unsafe {
        core::arch::asm!(
            "mov rax, 0xdeadbeef",
            "mov rax, qword ptr [rax]",
            out("rax") _,
            options(nostack)
        );
    }
    kprintln!("fault injection unexpectedly returned");
    halt_forever();
}

#[cfg(feature = "inject-invalid-opcode")]
fn run_fault_injection() {
    kprintln!("fault injection: triggering invalid opcode with ud2");
    // SAFETY: This is an opt-in QEMU test that deliberately raises #UD; the
    // installed invalid-opcode handler is expected to halt.
    unsafe { core::arch::asm!("ud2", options(nomem, nostack)) };
    kprintln!("fault injection unexpectedly returned");
    halt_forever();
}

#[panic_handler]
fn panic(info: &PanicInfo<'_>) -> ! {
    arch::x86_64::serial::initialize();
    kprintln!("KERNEL PANIC: {}", info);
    halt_forever()
}

fn halt_forever() -> ! {
    loop {
        // SAFETY: The bootstrap has no interrupt handlers or scheduler to resume.
        unsafe { core::arch::asm!("cli; hlt", options(nomem, nostack)) };
    }
}
```

```
`src/frame.rs` provides a fixed-capacity allocator core with host-side tests. It only manages complete 4 KiB frames inside validated `Usable` regions, reserves the first MiB, and coalesces adjacent free ranges. The ownership contract assumes one allocator instance per physical map: within that instance, each eligible frame is owned either by its free-range table or by a non-copyable `Frame` token while allocated. The public constructor does not enforce unique instances, so callers must not initialize multiple allocators for the same physical map; the current boot path retains one allocator in `BootInfo`. `allocate` returns `None` when no free frame remains. `deallocate` consumes the token only on success; on any error, including free-range-table exhaustion, it returns a `DeallocationError` containing the original token and leaves allocator state unchanged. The range tables each have a fixed `MAX_FRAME_RANGES` capacity, so fragmentation can prevent a frame from being returned until nearby ranges coalesce. The inactive candidate-root builder allocates table frames only in the opt-in probe today; there is no active general-purpose mapping service.
```

```rustix/docs/index.md
     1	# Rustix documentation
     2	
     3	Rustix is a 64-bit, Rust-first, Unix-like operating-system project. This index separates current implementation facts from planned interfaces: roadmap items are proposals until the corresponding code and tests exist.
     4	
     5	## Start here
     6	
     7	- [Project and implementation overview](architecture/overview.md)
     8	- [Boot protocol and current entry path](architecture/boot.md)
     9	- [Memory-management direction](architecture/memory.md)
    10	- [x86_64 drivers and hardware boundary](architecture/drivers.md)
    11	- [Crabshell and the volatile RAM filesystem](architecture/crabshell.md)
    12	- [Unix-like process and syscall direction](architecture/syscall-abi.md)
    13	- [Build and toolchain guide](development/building.md)
    14	- [Testing and verification](development/testing.md)
    15	- [Security and unsafe-code policy](security.md)
    16	- [Milestones and acceptance criteria](roadmap/README.md)
    17	
    18	## Current status
    19	
    20	The repository contains a bare-metal `no_std` Rust kernel for `x86_64-unknown-none`. After Limine handoff it validates and copies memory-map metadata into an owned snapshot, captures the executable's physical and virtual bases, complete linker-defined image span, and page-aligned text/rodata/data segment bounds, reports baseline CPUID features, active/maximum address widths, read-only CR0 caching state, gated EFER.NXE/IA32_PAT values, and a bounded MTRR snapshot, seeds a volatile RAM filesystem, and runs Crabshell over the COM1 serial console. Boot-protocol pointers are checked for canonicality using the active 4- or 5-level paging width; physical map bounds and protocol-scoped HHDM range arithmetic are also validated. Crabshell's allocation-free parser is a separate crate; the kernel handles command execution. On 2026-10-16, `just verify` passed in WSL2 Ubuntu 24.04 both in the working tree and from a clean detached worktree with an empty `target` directory; the clean run downloaded and built the pinned Limine host utility, created the image, and passed the bounded QEMU boot to the shell prompt. The serial log showed memory-map and CPU reporting. Hosted CI has not been observed. A separate interactive QEMU session exercised `help`, `ls`, `meminfo`, directory navigation, and file create/write/append/read/copy/move/remove commands. Milestone 0's local exit criteria are met, and Milestone 1's validation criteria are met for the current Limine path. This is a kernel-mode shell, not a user process. A bounded physical-frame allocator core is initialized from the validated map and reported by `meminfo`; its owned frame token and failed-deallocation semantics are documented and host-tested, but no kernel service allocates or maps frames yet. The Limine base-revision 3 HHDM scope and a conservative initial mapping/alias/cache policy are documented. Pure host-tested helpers validate mapping ranges/PTE bits, parse PAT layouts, validate captured MTRR snapshots, combine PAT/MTRR types under normal caching according to Intel SDM Table 11-7, and select a PAT index only when it yields one effective type across an aligned physical range. Boot validates the captured state and prints a diagnostic effective type at PA 0; neither this report nor the range selector inspects inherited PTEs or cache aliases, and no live mapping consumes a selected index. `BootInfo` records raw CR3 and a validated decode of its root physical address and low-bit interpretation, but Rustix does not use the HHDM to access physical memory, inspect page-table contents, or own/replace the inherited tables. The complete linker-defined kernel-image span and the protocol-guaranteed minimum active boot-stack span are captured; Limine does not provide the exact initial stack allocation or guard status, so Rustix preserves only the known minimum span and does not infer a guard page. There is not yet a heap, a general IRQ subsystem, a scheduler, process isolation, a persistent filesystem, or a Unix compatibility layer. Fatal CPU exceptions have basic GDT/TSS/IDT diagnostics but no recovery. `just fault-smoke` validates a controlled page fault (including CR2) and invalid opcode in QEMU; broader exception coverage and physical-hardware validation remain pending. On 2026-10-21, `just verify` passed after adding CR3 decoding and the pure MTRR resolver, including host tests, target check, release build, ISO creation, and QEMU prompt smoke. On 2026-10-22, `just verify` passed after adding bounded read-only MTRR register capture and after adding validated PAT/MTRR policy resolution, including host tests, target check, release build, ISO creation, and QEMU prompt smoke. The QEMU log confirmed normal caching and a validated PA 0 diagnostic (`PAT[0]` resolved to WB). These checks do not inspect page-table entries or validate live mapping attributes/aliases.
    21	
    22	## Documentation conventions
    23	
    24	- **Implemented** means present in the repository and checked by current code or tests.
    25	- **Planned** means an architectural direction, not a stable ABI or delivered capability.
    26	- Any future ABI proposal must state versioning, error behavior, memory ownership, and compatibility expectations before it is treated as stable.
```

```rustix/docs/architecture/boot.md
     1	# Boot protocol and kernel entry
     2	
     3	## Current boot contract
     4	
     5	Rustix currently expects a Limine-compatible x86_64 handoff. Limine is an external loader; it does not implement Rustix's kernel services. The kernel requests protocol base revision 3, the higher-half direct-map (HHDM) offset, the executable physical/virtual base addresses, and the memory map.
     6	
     7	Requests are kept in `.limine_requests_start`, `.limine_requests`, and `.limine_requests_end` by `linker.ld`. The response-bearing request records are mutable and the output `.limine_requests` section is placed in a writable load segment because Limine fills their response pointers before entering Rustix. The ELF entry symbol is `_start`.
     8	
     9	### Entry sequence
    10	
    11	1. Limine loads the ELF and transfers control to the assembly `_start` shim under the x86_64 Limine protocol. The shim captures the entry `RSP`, aligns the stack for a SysV call, and invokes `rustix_start`.
    12	2. `rustix_start` configures the legacy COM1 UART for polling output and input.
    13	3. The kernel disables maskable interrupts and installs its bootstrap GDT, TSS, and fatal-exception IDT. This does not initialize IRQ delivery.
    14	4. The kernel reads CR0 caching-control state, CPU address widths, active `CR4.PCIDE`, and raw CR3. It decodes CR3's physical root address and low-bit meaning against those CPU properties, without dereferencing the root. It reads EFER.NXE only when CPUID reports NX, `IA32_PAT` only when CPUID reports PAT, and MTRR registers only when CPUID reports MTRR support; these reads do not change CPU state. The MTRR snapshot is bounded to 32 variable pairs and reports an explicit capacity-exceeded state without retaining partial registers. It copies the HHDM, executable-address, and memory-map responses into an owned `BootInfo` snapshot, validates pointers against the active linear width, derives and validates the linker-defined kernel image span and its page-aligned text/rodata/data segment spans from Limine's executable bases, and derives the protocol-guaranteed minimum initial-stack span from the captured entry `RSP`. It validates physical bounds, stack HHDM arithmetic/coverage, and page-rounded HHDM arithmetic for protocol-mapped memory types. It then builds a frame allocator only from validated usable ranges and rejects malformed metadata before starting the shell.
    15	5. The kernel reports raw CR3 and its decoded physical root/low bits when the reported width permits, physical and virtual kernel-image spans, linker-defined text RX, rodata R/NX, and data RW/NX segment spans, minimum protocol-guaranteed stack span, validated memory ranges, frame counts, CPU features/address widths, NXE and normal-caching state, the active PAT value plus recognized WB/UC/WC indices, and a summary of captured MTRR state. It also reports whether the captured PAT/MTRR registers validate and a diagnostic effective type at physical address zero for PAT index 0; this is not a page-table inspection or a live mapping claim. It then seeds a volatile RAM filesystem and enters Crabshell on the serial console.
    16	6. The shell busy-polls COM1 because no scheduler or UART interrupt handler exists yet. The kernel does not return to the loader.
    17	
    18	The linker exports page-aligned virtual bounds for each of the kernel's three load segments. Boot validates their order, contiguity, coverage of the rounded image span, and derived physical ranges, then reports them with the permissions intended by `linker.ld`. Boot also decodes CR3's root physical address and active low-bit interpretation. A host-tested helper can validate that the root page is in bootloader-reclaimable memory and calculate its HHDM address. The opt-in `just frame-smoke` path reads the 512 root entries and follows bounded page-table paths for every page in the kernel image segments and minimum stack span, checking physical translations. It does not establish inherited permissions/cache correctness or alias safety. These are validated linker/boot metadata only: Rustix has not established that all live mappings match the ELF flags.
    19	
    20	The memory-map snapshot stores physical regions as checked half-open ranges `[start, end)` and retains Limine's known classifications plus unknown type values. It does not authorize Rustix to access every region, reclaim loader memory, or mutate the current page tables. Rustix checks physical bounds and calculates canonical HHDM ranges for memory types covered by the requested base revision, but does not generally dereference physical memory through the HHDM or verify the inherited page tables. The opt-in `just frame-smoke` probe writes one allocator-issued frame contained in a validated `Usable` region and reads the inherited root page after checking that it is bootloader-reclaimable; both accesses rely on the Limine mapping contract after checked address arithmetic. It does not prove full live page-table coverage. These metadata checks cannot prove that a Limine-provided non-null pointer is readable; that remains an explicit trust assumption of the Limine handoff.
    21	
    22	## Link and target configuration
    23	
    24	- Rust target: `x86_64-unknown-none`
    25	- Linker script: `linker.ld`
    26	- Kernel virtual base: `0xffffffff80000000`
    27	- Required code-generation constraints: kernel code model, static relocation, and disabled red zone
    28	- Rust panic strategy: abort; the panic handler logs and halts
    29	
    30	See [`../development/building.md`](../development/building.md) for commands and toolchain setup.
    31	
    32	## Failure behavior and limitations
    33	
    34	Missing responses, bad pointers/alignment, invalid HHDM values, invalid image or segment bounds, invalid initial-stack spans, excessive counts, null entries, address arithmetic overflow, and invalid or overlapping physical ranges reject the complete boot snapshot. `_start` halts before starting Crabshell rather than continuing with partial memory metadata. Structural checks cannot establish that a non-null loader pointer is mapped and readable; that remains an explicit trust assumption of the Limine handoff. The installed exception handlers print fatal context and halt; no fault recovery or maskable IRQ delivery is provided. COM1 writes use a bounded polling loop so a non-responsive UART does not block forever.
    35	
    36	The repository includes a Limine v12.9.3 binary archive pin with SHA-256 verification, a hybrid ISO recipe, and a bounded QEMU serial smoke test that checks Crabshell's prompt. On 2026-10-16, `just verify` passed in WSL2 Ubuntu 24.04 on both the working tree and a clean detached worktree with an empty `target` directory; the clean run fetched and built the pinned Limine host utility, created the image, and QEMU reported boot metadata before reaching the prompt. Milestone 0's local exit criteria are met. Hosted CI has not been observed. There is still no framebuffer console, reboot/shutdown interface, or broader boot-protocol compatibility test. The available serial and keyboard drivers do not imply a general device model.
    37	
    38	## Future boot work
    39	
    40	The kernel now snapshots and validates the Limine map and preserves firmware and loader-reclaimable classifications without reclaiming them. No region is considered Rustix-owned or free for allocation yet. Loader-reclaimable memory must remain unavailable until Rustix has copied any needed boot data and explicitly reaches a documented reclaim point; ACPI reclaimable memory needs the ACPI tables to be copied or parsed first. Frame allocation, page-table replacement, and ownership transfer remain future work.

```
