//! A bounded kernel heap backed by a static, page-mapped kernel data arena.
//!
//! The arena is 256 KiB and tracks at most 128 simultaneous allocations. It
//! uses first-fit placement with the requested `Layout` alignment, reclaims
//! exact allocations on free, and returns allocation failure when either the
//! arena or metadata table is exhausted. It never grows or requests frames.
//!
//! The global wrapper serializes access with a spin lock. Allocation is not
//! permitted from interrupt context: an interrupt that preempts a lock holder
//! could otherwise deadlock. The current kernel is single-core and keeps
//! maskable interrupts disabled; future IRQ or scheduling support must provide
//! an IRQ-safe allocation policy before allocating in those contexts.

use core::alloc::{GlobalAlloc, Layout};
use core::cell::UnsafeCell;
use core::hint::spin_loop;
use core::ptr::NonNull;
use core::sync::atomic::{AtomicBool, Ordering};

/// Fixed capacity of the initial BSS-backed kernel heap.
pub const KERNEL_HEAP_CAPACITY: usize = 256 * 1024;
/// Maximum number of live allocations tracked by the initial kernel heap.
pub const KERNEL_HEAP_MAX_ALLOCATIONS: usize = 128;

/// The statically allocated heap type used by the kernel binary.
pub type KernelHeap = LockedHeap<KERNEL_HEAP_CAPACITY, KERNEL_HEAP_MAX_ALLOCATIONS>;

#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
enum HeapError {
    ZeroSizedAllocation,
    AllocationTableFull,
    OutOfMemory,
    AddressOverflow,
    InvalidPointer,
    LayoutMismatch,
}

#[derive(Clone, Copy)]
struct Allocation {
    start: usize,
    size: usize,
    alignment: usize,
}

struct FixedHeap<const HEAP_SIZE: usize, const MAX_ALLOCATIONS: usize> {
    arena: [u8; HEAP_SIZE],
    allocations: [Option<Allocation>; MAX_ALLOCATIONS],
}

impl<const HEAP_SIZE: usize, const MAX_ALLOCATIONS: usize>
    FixedHeap<HEAP_SIZE, MAX_ALLOCATIONS>
{
    const fn new() -> Self {
        Self {
            arena: [0; HEAP_SIZE],
            allocations: [None; MAX_ALLOCATIONS],
        }
    }

    fn allocate(&mut self, layout: Layout) -> Result<NonNull<u8>, HeapError> {
        if layout.size() == 0 {
            return Err(HeapError::ZeroSizedAllocation);
        }
        let slot = self
            .allocations
            .iter()
            .position(Option::is_none)
            .ok_or(HeapError::AllocationTableFull)?;
        let start = self.find_gap(layout)?;
        self.allocations[slot] = Some(Allocation {
            start,
            size: layout.size(),
            alignment: layout.align(),
        });

        let pointer = self.arena.as_mut_ptr().wrapping_add(start);
        NonNull::new(pointer).ok_or(HeapError::AddressOverflow)
    }

    fn deallocate(&mut self, pointer: NonNull<u8>, layout: Layout) -> Result<(), HeapError> {
        if layout.size() == 0 {
            return Err(HeapError::ZeroSizedAllocation);
        }
        let arena_start = self.arena.as_ptr() as usize;
        let allocation_start = (pointer.as_ptr() as usize)
            .checked_sub(arena_start)
            .filter(|offset| *offset < HEAP_SIZE)
            .ok_or(HeapError::InvalidPointer)?;

        for allocation in &mut self.allocations {
            let Some(active) = *allocation else {
                continue;
            };
            if active.start != allocation_start {
                continue;
            }
            if active.size != layout.size() || active.alignment != layout.align() {
                return Err(HeapError::LayoutMismatch);
            }
            *allocation = None;
            return Ok(());
        }
        Err(HeapError::InvalidPointer)
    }

    fn find_gap(&self, layout: Layout) -> Result<usize, HeapError> {
        let arena_start = self.arena.as_ptr() as usize;
        let mut candidate = 0usize;

        loop {
            let candidate_address = arena_start
                .checked_add(candidate)
                .ok_or(HeapError::AddressOverflow)?;
            let aligned_address = candidate_address
                .checked_add(layout.align() - 1)
                .ok_or(HeapError::AddressOverflow)?
                & !(layout.align() - 1);
            let start = aligned_address
                .checked_sub(arena_start)
                .ok_or(HeapError::AddressOverflow)?;
            let end = start
                .checked_add(layout.size())
                .ok_or(HeapError::AddressOverflow)?;
            if end > HEAP_SIZE {
                return Err(HeapError::OutOfMemory);
            }

            let mut conflicting_end = None;
            for allocation in self.allocations.iter().flatten() {
                let allocation_end = allocation
                    .start
                    .checked_add(allocation.size)
                    .ok_or(HeapError::AddressOverflow)?;
                if start < allocation_end && allocation.start < end {
                    conflicting_end = Some(
                        conflicting_end.map_or(allocation_end, |end: usize| end.max(allocation_end)),
                    );
                }
            }

            match conflicting_end {
                Some(end) => candidate = end,
                None => return Ok(start),
            }
        }
    }
}

/// A `GlobalAlloc` wrapper for the fixed kernel arena.
///
/// The lock prevents concurrent mutation of allocation metadata. The arena
/// storage must remain at a stable address while allocations are live; the
/// kernel's `#[global_allocator]` static has that property.
pub struct LockedHeap<const HEAP_SIZE: usize, const MAX_ALLOCATIONS: usize> {
    locked: AtomicBool,
    heap: UnsafeCell<FixedHeap<HEAP_SIZE, MAX_ALLOCATIONS>>,
}

// SAFETY: `heap` is accessed mutably only while the Acquire/Release spin lock
// is held. The allocator is not IRQ-safe; callers must follow the module's
// interrupt-context restriction.
unsafe impl<const HEAP_SIZE: usize, const MAX_ALLOCATIONS: usize> Sync
    for LockedHeap<HEAP_SIZE, MAX_ALLOCATIONS>
{
}

impl<const HEAP_SIZE: usize, const MAX_ALLOCATIONS: usize>
    LockedHeap<HEAP_SIZE, MAX_ALLOCATIONS>
{
    /// Construct an empty allocator. The backing arena is zero-initialized BSS.
    pub const fn new() -> Self {
        Self {
            locked: AtomicBool::new(false),
            heap: UnsafeCell::new(FixedHeap::new()),
        }
    }

    fn acquire(&self) -> HeapLock<'_> {
        while self
            .locked
            .compare_exchange_weak(false, true, Ordering::Acquire, Ordering::Relaxed)
            .is_err()
        {
            spin_loop();
        }
        HeapLock { locked: &self.locked }
    }
}

struct HeapLock<'a> {
    locked: &'a AtomicBool,
}

impl Drop for HeapLock<'_> {
    fn drop(&mut self) {
        self.locked.store(false, Ordering::Release);
    }
}

unsafe impl<const HEAP_SIZE: usize, const MAX_ALLOCATIONS: usize> GlobalAlloc
    for LockedHeap<HEAP_SIZE, MAX_ALLOCATIONS>
{
    unsafe fn alloc(&self, layout: Layout) -> *mut u8 {
        let _lock = self.acquire();
        // SAFETY: The lock grants exclusive access to the heap state.
        let heap = unsafe { &mut *self.heap.get() };
        heap.allocate(layout)
            .map(NonNull::as_ptr)
            .unwrap_or(core::ptr::null_mut())
    }

    unsafe fn dealloc(&self, pointer: *mut u8, layout: Layout) {
        let Some(pointer) = NonNull::new(pointer) else {
            return;
        };
        let _lock = self.acquire();
        // SAFETY: The lock grants exclusive access to the heap state. The
        // GlobalAlloc caller must provide a live allocation and its original layout.
        let heap = unsafe { &mut *self.heap.get() };
        let _ = heap.deallocate(pointer, layout);
    }
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use core::alloc::Layout;
    use core::assert_eq;

    use super::{FixedHeap, HeapError};

    #[test]
    fn honors_layout_alignment_and_reuses_freed_allocations() {
        let mut heap = FixedHeap::<256, 4>::new();
        let layout = Layout::from_size_align(37, 64).unwrap();
        let allocation = heap.allocate(layout).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(allocation.as_ptr() as usize % layout.align(), 0);

        // SAFETY: The pointer names a live allocation of the requested size.
        unsafe { allocation.as_ptr().write_bytes(0xa5, layout.size()) };
        for index in 0..layout.size() {
            // SAFETY: `index` is bounded by the live allocation's size.
            assert_eq!(unsafe { allocation.as_ptr().add(index).read() }, 0xa5);
        }

        heap.deallocate(allocation, layout).unwrap();
        let reused = heap.allocate(layout).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(reused, allocation);
        heap.deallocate(reused, layout).unwrap();
    }

    #[test]
    fn reports_arena_exhaustion_and_reuses_a_coalesced_gap() {
        let mut heap = FixedHeap::<128, 4>::new();
        let full_layout = Layout::from_size_align(64, 1).unwrap();
        let first = heap.allocate(full_layout).unwrap();
        let second = heap.allocate(full_layout).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(heap.allocate(Layout::from_size_align(1, 1).unwrap()), Err(HeapError::OutOfMemory));

        heap.deallocate(first, full_layout).unwrap();
        let smaller_layout = Layout::from_size_align(32, 1).unwrap();
        let reused = heap.allocate(smaller_layout).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(reused, first);
        heap.deallocate(reused, smaller_layout).unwrap();
        heap.deallocate(second, full_layout).unwrap();
    }

    #[test]
    fn reports_allocation_metadata_exhaustion() {
        let mut heap = FixedHeap::<128, 1>::new();
        let layout = Layout::from_size_align(8, 1).unwrap();
        let allocation = heap.allocate(layout).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(heap.allocate(layout), Err(HeapError::AllocationTableFull));
        heap.deallocate(allocation, layout).unwrap();
        assert!(heap.allocate(layout).is_ok());
    }

    #[test]
    fn rejects_invalid_pointer_and_layout_without_releasing_memory() {
        let mut heap = FixedHeap::<128, 4>::new();
        let layout = Layout::from_size_align(16, 8).unwrap();
        let allocation = heap.allocate(layout).unwrap();
        let wrong_layout = Layout::from_size_align(8, 8).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(
            heap.deallocate(allocation, wrong_layout),
            Err(HeapError::LayoutMismatch)
        );
        assert_eq!(
            heap.deallocate(NonNull::dangling(), layout),
            Err(HeapError::InvalidPointer)
        );
        heap.deallocate(allocation, layout).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(
            heap.deallocate(allocation, layout),
            Err(HeapError::InvalidPointer)
        );
    }

    #[test]
    fn rejects_zero_sized_layouts() {
        let mut heap = FixedHeap::<128, 4>::new();
        let layout = Layout::from_size_align(0, 8).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(heap.allocate(layout), Err(HeapError::ZeroSizedAllocation));
    }

    use core::ptr::NonNull;
}

struct LimineHhdmPageTableReader<'a> {
    memory_map: &'a rustix_kernel::memory::MemoryMap,
    hhdm_offset: u64,
    physical_address_bits: u8,
    virtual_address_bits: u8,
}

impl rustix_kernel::paging::PageTableReader for LimineHhdmPageTableReader<'_> {
    type Error = rustix_kernel::memory::HhdmAddressError;

    fn read_entry(&self, table_physical: u64, index: u16) -> Result<u64, Self::Error> {
        if index >= 512 {
            return Err(rustix_kernel::memory::HhdmAddressError::InvalidHhdmRange);
        }
        let table_end = table_physical
            .checked_add(rustix_kernel::paging::PAGE_SIZE)
            .ok_or(rustix_kernel::memory::HhdmAddressError::AddressOverflow)?;
        if !self.memory_map.range_is_within_region_kind(
            table_physical,
            table_end,
            rustix_kernel::memory::RegionKind::BootloaderReclaimable,
        ) {
            return Err(rustix_kernel::memory::HhdmAddressError::NotLimineMapped);
        }
        let table_address = self.memory_map.limine_hhdm_address(
            self.hhdm_offset,
            table_physical,
            rustix_kernel::paging::PAGE_SIZE,
            Some(self.physical_address_bits),
            self.virtual_address_bits,
        )?;
        let entry_address = table_address
            .checked_add(u64::from(index) * core::mem::size_of::<u64>() as u64)
            .ok_or(rustix_kernel::memory::HhdmAddressError::AddressOverflow)?;
        // SAFETY: The complete table page was restricted to bootloader-reclaimable
        // memory and its HHDM address arithmetic was checked. The reader relies
        // on the Limine base-revision-3 mapping contract and never returns a ref.
        Ok(unsafe { (entry_address as *const u64).read_volatile() })
    }
}

struct LimineHhdmCandidateMemory<'a> {
    memory_map: &'a rustix_kernel::memory::MemoryMap,
    hhdm_offset: u64,
    physical_address_bits: u8,
    virtual_address_bits: u8,
}

// SAFETY: `prepare_table` accepts only an allocator-issued frame and validates
// its complete usable span and HHDM address. Handles are only used while the
// candidate retains the frame token and this unique backend borrow.
unsafe impl rustix_kernel::paging::CandidatePageTableMemory for LimineHhdmCandidateMemory<'_> {
    type PreparedTable = u64;
    type Error = rustix_kernel::memory::HhdmAddressError;

    fn prepare_table(
        &mut self,
        frame: &rustix_kernel::frame::Frame,
    ) -> Result<Self::PreparedTable, Self::Error> {
        frame.hhdm_address(
            self.memory_map,
            self.hhdm_offset,
            Some(self.physical_address_bits),
            self.virtual_address_bits,
        )
    }

    unsafe fn read_entry(
        &self,
        table: Self::PreparedTable,
        index: u16,
    ) -> Result<u64, Self::Error> {
        if index >= 512 {
            return Err(rustix_kernel::memory::HhdmAddressError::InvalidHhdmRange);
        }
        let entry_address = table
            .checked_add(u64::from(index) * core::mem::size_of::<u64>() as u64)
            .ok_or(rustix_kernel::memory::HhdmAddressError::AddressOverflow)?;
        // SAFETY: The unsafe trait contract requires `table` to be the prepared
        // HHDM address of a complete writable frame; the index is in [0, 512).
        Ok(unsafe { (entry_address as *const u64).read_volatile() })
    }

    unsafe fn clear_table(&mut self, table: Self::PreparedTable) {
        let entries = table as *mut u64;
        // SAFETY: The caller provides a handle prepared by this backend for a
        // complete writable frame retained by its candidate.
        unsafe {
            for index in 0..512 {
                entries.add(index).write_volatile(0);
            }
        }
    }

    unsafe fn write_entry(&mut self, table: Self::PreparedTable, index: u16, value: u64) {
        if index >= 512 {
            return;
        }
        let entry = (table as *mut u64).wrapping_add(usize::from(index));
        // SAFETY: The caller provides a prepared complete frame and an index in
        // range; this writes one entry without creating a Rust reference.
        unsafe { entry.write_volatile(value) };
    }
}

// Capture Limine's entry RSP before a Rust prologue changes it. The synthetic
// return slot is part of the SysV entry stack; realign before calling Rust.
core::arch::global_asm!(
    ".section .text",
    ".code64",
    ".global _start",
    ".type _start, @function",
    "_start:",
    "mov rdi, rsp",
    "and rsp, -16",
    "call rustix_start",
    "ud2",
    ".size _start, . - _start",

#[no_mangle]
pub extern "C" fn rustix_start(entry_rsp: u64) -> ! {
    arch::x86_64::serial::initialize();
    kprintln!("Rustix kernel: x86_64 Rust bootstrap");
    arch::x86_64::interrupts::initialize();
    kprintln!("x86_64 exception diagnostics: enabled (IRQs remain disabled)");
    let mut boot_info = match boot::capture_boot_information(entry_rsp) {
        Ok(boot_info) => boot_info,
        Err(error) => {
            kprintln!("boot information rejected: {:?}", error);
            halt_forever();
        }
    };
    boot::report_boot_information(&boot_info);

    #[cfg(feature = "probe-hhdm-frame")]
    probe_hhdm_frame(&mut boot_info);

    #[cfg(any(feature = "inject-page-fault", feature = "inject-invalid-opcode"))]
    run_fault_injection();

    activate_cloned_page_tables_and_run(&mut boot_info)
}

fn activate_cloned_page_tables_and_run(boot_info: &mut boot::BootInfo) -> ! {
    use rustix_kernel::paging::{
        encode_cr3_value, CandidatePageTables, PageWalkConfig, PageWalkOutcome,
    };

    let physical_address_bits = match boot_info.cpu_info.physical_address_bits {
        Some(bits) => bits,
        None => {
            kprintln!("page-table transition rejected: physical width unknown");
            halt_forever();
        }
    };
    let inherited_root = match boot_info.inherited_cr3_root {
        Ok(root) => root,
        Err(error) => {
            kprintln!("page-table transition rejected: inherited CR3: {:?}", error);
            halt_forever();
        }
    };
    if !boot_info.cpu_info.nx_enabled {
        kprintln!("page-table transition rejected: NXE is not enabled");
        halt_forever();
    }
    let config = PageWalkConfig {
        levels: if boot_info.cpu_info.active_linear_address_bits == 57 {
            5
        } else {
            4
        },
        physical_address_bits,
        virtual_address_bits: boot_info.cpu_info.active_linear_address_bits,
        nx_enabled: boot_info.cpu_info.nx_enabled,
        page_2m_supported: true,
        page_1g_supported: boot_info.cpu_info.has_1g_pages,
    };
    let reader = LimineHhdmPageTableReader {
        memory_map: &boot_info.memory_map,
        hhdm_offset: boot_info.hhdm_offset,
        physical_address_bits,
        virtual_address_bits: boot_info.cpu_info.active_linear_address_bits,
    };
    let mut memory = LimineHhdmCandidateMemory {
        memory_map: &boot_info.memory_map,
        hhdm_offset: boot_info.hhdm_offset,
        physical_address_bits,
        virtual_address_bits: boot_info.cpu_info.active_linear_address_bits,
    };
    let mut candidate =
        match CandidatePageTables::new(&mut boot_info.frame_allocator, &mut memory, config) {
            Ok(candidate) => candidate,
            Err(error) => {
                kprintln!(
                    "page-table transition failed to create root: {:?}",
                    error.cause
                );
                if let Some(frame) = error.frame {
                    release_probe_frame(&mut boot_info.frame_allocator, frame);
                }
                halt_forever();
            }
        };
    if let Err(error) =
        candidate.clone_inherited_hierarchy(&mut boot_info.frame_allocator, &reader, inherited_root)
    {
        kprintln!(
            "page-table transition failed to clone inherited root: {:?}",
            error
        );
        release_candidate_after_probe_failure(candidate, &mut boot_info.frame_allocator);
    }

    let segments = boot_info.kernel_image_segments;
    let spans = [
        (
            "kernel text",
            segments.text.virtual_start,
            segments.text.physical_start,
            segments.text.virtual_end - segments.text.virtual_start,
        ),
        (
            "kernel rodata",
            segments.rodata.virtual_start,
            segments.rodata.physical_start,
            segments.rodata.virtual_end - segments.rodata.virtual_start,
        ),
        (
            "kernel data",
            segments.data.virtual_start,
            segments.data.physical_start,
            segments.data.virtual_end - segments.data.virtual_start,
        ),
        (
            "active boot stack",
            boot_info.boot_stack_virtual_start,
            boot_info.boot_stack_physical_start,
            boot_info.boot_stack_virtual_end - boot_info.boot_stack_virtual_start,
        ),
    ];
    for (label, virtual_start, physical_start, length) in spans {
        if !candidate_span_matches_source(
            &candidate,
            &reader,
            inherited_root,
            config,
            virtual_start,
            physical_start,
            length,
        ) {
            kprintln!(
                "page-table transition rejected: {} was not preserved",
                label
            );
            release_candidate_after_probe_failure(candidate, &mut boot_info.frame_allocator);
        }
    }
    let candidate_root = candidate
        .root_physical_address()
        .expect("a live candidate retains its root frame");
    let root_hhdm_address = match boot_info.memory_map.limine_hhdm_address(
        boot_info.hhdm_offset,
        candidate_root,
        rustix_kernel::paging::PAGE_SIZE,
        Some(physical_address_bits),
        boot_info.cpu_info.active_linear_address_bits,
    ) {
        Ok(address) => address,
        Err(error) => {
            kprintln!(
                "page-table transition rejected: candidate root HHDM: {:?}",
                error
            );
            release_candidate_after_probe_failure(candidate, &mut boot_info.frame_allocator);
        }
    };
    let root_alias = match candidate.walk(root_hhdm_address) {
        Ok(PageWalkOutcome::Mapped(translation))
            if translation.physical_address == candidate_root =>
        {
            translation
        }
        result => {
            kprintln!(
                "page-table transition rejected: candidate root HHDM alias: {:?}",
                result
            );
            release_candidate_after_probe_failure(candidate, &mut boot_info.frame_allocator);
        }
    };
    if !root_alias.permissions.writable || root_alias.permissions.user_accessible {
        kprintln!("page-table transition rejected: candidate root alias permissions are unsafe");
        release_candidate_after_probe_failure(candidate, &mut boot_info.frame_allocator);
    }

    let new_cr3 = match encode_cr3_value(
        candidate_root,
        inherited_root.low_bits(),
        physical_address_bits,
    ) {
        Ok(value) => value,
        Err(error) => {
            kprintln!("page-table transition rejected: new CR3: {:?}", error);
            release_candidate_after_probe_failure(candidate, &mut boot_info.frame_allocator);
        }
    };
    let inherited_cr3 = boot_info.inherited_cr3_raw;
    if arch::x86_64::cpu::read_cr3_raw() != inherited_cr3 {
        kprintln!("page-table transition aborted: active CR3 changed before switch");
        release_candidate_after_probe_failure(candidate, &mut boot_info.frame_allocator);
    }
    // SAFETY: The candidate is a complete clone of every present inherited
    // hierarchy entry, with all referenced intermediate tables owned and the
    // critical code/data/stack paths compared before this point. The inherited
    // root's paging mode, address widths, PAT/MTRR state, and low CR3 mode are
    // preserved; interrupts are disabled from bootstrap initialization onward.
    unsafe { arch::x86_64::cpu::write_cr3_raw(new_cr3) };
    if arch::x86_64::cpu::read_cr3_raw() != new_cr3
        || !spans
            .iter()
            .all(|(_, virtual_start, physical_start, length)| {
                candidate_span_matches_source(
                    &candidate,
                    &reader,
                    inherited_root,
                    config,
                    *virtual_start,
                    *physical_start,
                    *length,
                )
            })
    {
        // SAFETY: The inherited root and its backing memory remain untouched and
        // mapped by the candidate, so restoring its validated CR3 value is safe.
        unsafe { arch::x86_64::cpu::write_cr3_raw(inherited_cr3) };
        kprintln!("page-table transition failed post-switch verification; restored inherited CR3");
        release_candidate_after_probe_failure(candidate, &mut boot_info.frame_allocator);
    }
    kprintln!(
        "page-table transition passed: active CR3={:#x}, cloned root={:#x}, {} owned tables",
        new_cr3,
        candidate_root,
        candidate.table_count()
    );
    probe_kernel_heap();

    // Keep the candidate and its frame tokens alive for as long as this root is
    // active. The shell runs forever and does not return to this stack frame.
    // SAFETY: The bootstrap is single-core, interrupts remain disabled, and the
    // shell is the only filesystem owner.
    let filesystem = unsafe { &mut *core::ptr::addr_of_mut!(RAM_FILESYSTEM) };
    match filesystem.seed_defaults() {
        Ok(home) => shell::run(filesystem, home, boot_info),
        Err(error) => {
            kprintln!("RAM filesystem initialization failed: {:?}", error);
            halt_forever()
        }
    }
}

fn probe_kernel_heap() {
    use core::alloc::{GlobalAlloc, Layout};

    let full_layout = match Layout::from_size_align(
        rustix_kernel::heap::KERNEL_HEAP_CAPACITY,
        1,
    ) {
        Ok(layout) => layout,
        Err(error) => {
            kprintln!("kernel heap probe failed to construct full-arena layout: {:?}", error);
            halt_forever();
        }
    };
    // SAFETY: The heap static is initialized before use and maskable interrupts
    // remain disabled; this probe requests a valid nonzero layout.
    let full_arena = unsafe { KERNEL_HEAP.alloc(full_layout) };
    if full_arena.is_null() {
        kprintln!("kernel heap probe failed: full-arena allocation was rejected");
        halt_forever();
    }
    let small_layout = Layout::new::<u8>();
    // SAFETY: The heap lock serializes this valid nonzero allocation request.
    let exhausted = unsafe { KERNEL_HEAP.alloc(small_layout) };
    if !exhausted.is_null() {
        // SAFETY: Both pointers are live allocations with their original layouts.
        unsafe {
            KERNEL_HEAP.dealloc(exhausted, small_layout);
            KERNEL_HEAP.dealloc(full_arena, full_layout);
        }
        kprintln!("kernel heap probe failed: exhaustion was not deterministic");
        halt_forever();
    }
    // SAFETY: `full_arena` is the complete live allocation created above.
    unsafe { KERNEL_HEAP.dealloc(full_arena, full_layout) };

    let layout = match Layout::from_size_align(257, 64) {
        Ok(layout) => layout,
        Err(error) => {
            kprintln!("kernel heap probe failed to construct aligned layout: {:?}", error);
            halt_forever();
        }
    };
    // SAFETY: The heap is available after releasing the full-arena allocation.
    let allocation = unsafe { KERNEL_HEAP.alloc(layout) };
    if allocation.is_null() || allocation as usize % layout.align() != 0 {
        if !allocation.is_null() {
            // SAFETY: This is the live allocation returned for `layout`.
            unsafe { KERNEL_HEAP.dealloc(allocation, layout) };
        }
        kprintln!("kernel heap probe failed: aligned allocation was rejected or misaligned");
        halt_forever();
    }
    // SAFETY: The allocator returned `layout.size()` writable bytes.
    unsafe { core::ptr::write_bytes(allocation, 0xa5, layout.size()) };
    for index in 0..layout.size() {
        // SAFETY: `index` remains inside the live allocation.
        if unsafe { allocation.add(index).read_volatile() } != 0xa5 {
            // SAFETY: The allocation is still live with its original layout.
            unsafe { KERNEL_HEAP.dealloc(allocation, layout) };
            kprintln!("kernel heap probe failed: allocation data did not round-trip");
            halt_forever();
        }
    }
    // SAFETY: The allocation is live and the original layout is supplied.
    unsafe { KERNEL_HEAP.dealloc(allocation, layout) };
    // SAFETY: The previous allocation was returned; first-fit should reuse it.
    let reused = unsafe { KERNEL_HEAP.alloc(layout) };
    if reused != allocation {
        if !reused.is_null() {
            // SAFETY: `reused` is a live allocation with `layout`.
            unsafe { KERNEL_HEAP.dealloc(reused, layout) };
        }
        kprintln!("kernel heap probe failed: freed space was not reused");
        halt_forever();
    }
    // SAFETY: The reused allocation is live and has the same layout.
    unsafe { KERNEL_HEAP.dealloc(reused, layout) };
    kprintln!("kernel heap probe passed: alignment, reuse, deterministic exhaustion");
}

#[cfg(feature = "probe-hhdm-frame")]
fn probe_hhdm_frame(boot_info: &mut boot::BootInfo) {
    use rustix_kernel::frame::FRAME_SIZE;

    let frame = match boot_info.frame_allocator.allocate() {
        Some(frame) => frame,
        None => {
            kprintln!("HHDM frame probe failed: no free frame");
            halt_forever();
        }
    };
    let hhdm_address = match frame.hhdm_address(
        &boot_info.memory_map,
        boot_info.hhdm_offset,
        boot_info.cpu_info.physical_address_bits,
        boot_info.cpu_info.active_linear_address_bits,
    ) {
        Ok(address) => address,
        Err(error) => {
            kprintln!("HHDM frame probe rejected frame translation: {:?}", error);
            release_probe_frame(&mut boot_info.frame_allocator, frame);
            halt_forever();
        }
    };

    let words = (FRAME_SIZE / core::mem::size_of::<u64>() as u64) as usize;
    let page = hhdm_address as *mut u64;
    let mut verified = true;
    // SAFETY: The non-copyable `Frame` token is held exclusively; its full page
    // is within validated `Usable` memory and its HHDM arithmetic was checked.
    // Limine base revision 3 guarantees usable memory in the HHDM, and no other
    // Rustix mapping aliases this newly allocated frame. This is an opt-in QEMU
    // probe; a broken loader mapping would fault and be caught by the fatal path.
    unsafe {
        for index in 0..words {
            page.add(index)
                .write_volatile(0xa5a5_0000_0000_0000 ^ index as u64);
        }
        for index in 0..words {
            if page.add(index).read_volatile() != (0xa5a5_0000_0000_0000 ^ index as u64) {
                verified = false;
                break;
            }
        }
        for index in 0..words {
            page.add(index).write_volatile(0);
        }
    }

    release_probe_frame(&mut boot_info.frame_allocator, frame);
    if !verified {
        kprintln!("HHDM frame probe failed: readback mismatch");
        halt_forever();
    }
    kprintln!("HHDM frame probe passed: wrote, read, cleared, and reclaimed one frame");
    probe_inherited_root(boot_info);
}

        }
    };
    let pat = match rustix_kernel::paging::PatLayout::from_msr_value(pat_value) {
        Ok(pat) => pat,
        Err(error) => {
            kprintln!("cache-alias probe failed: invalid PAT layout: {:?}", error);
            halt_forever();
        }
    };
    let registers = match &boot_info.cpu_info.mtrr {
        rustix_kernel::paging::MtrrState::Captured(registers) => registers,
        _ => {
            kprintln!("cache-alias probe failed: captured MTRR state unavailable");
            halt_forever();
        }
    };
    let mtrrs = match registers.validated_layout(physical_address_bits) {
        Ok(mtrrs) => mtrrs,
        Err(error) => {
            kprintln!("cache-alias probe failed: invalid MTRR state: {:?}", error);
            halt_forever();
        }
    };
    if !boot_info.cpu_info.normal_caching {
        kprintln!("cache-alias probe failed: non-normal CR0 caching mode");
        halt_forever();
    }
    verify_kernel_cache_aliases(
        boot_info,
        &reader,
        root,
        config,
        pat,
        &mtrrs,
        "kernel text",
        segments.text.virtual_start,
        segments.text.physical_start,
        segments.text.virtual_end - segments.text.virtual_start,
    );
    verify_kernel_cache_aliases(
        boot_info,
        &reader,
        root,
        config,
        pat,
        &mtrrs,
        "kernel rodata",
        segments.rodata.virtual_start,
        segments.rodata.physical_start,
        segments.rodata.virtual_end - segments.rodata.virtual_start,
    );
    verify_kernel_cache_aliases(
        boot_info,
        &reader,
        root,
        config,
        pat,
        &mtrrs,
        "kernel data",
        segments.data.virtual_start,
        segments.data.physical_start,
        segments.data.virtual_end - segments.data.virtual_start,
    );
    probe_cloned_page_tables(
        &mut boot_info.frame_allocator,
        &boot_info.memory_map,
        boot_info.hhdm_offset,
        physical_address_bits,
        boot_info.cpu_info.active_linear_address_bits,
        &reader,
        root,
        config,
        [
            (
                "kernel text",
                segments.text.virtual_start,
                segments.text.physical_start,
                segments.text.virtual_end - segments.text.virtual_start,
            ),
            (
                "kernel rodata",
                segments.rodata.virtual_start,
                segments.rodata.physical_start,
                segments.rodata.virtual_end - segments.rodata.virtual_start,
            ),
            (
                "kernel data",
                segments.data.virtual_start,
                segments.data.physical_start,
                segments.data.virtual_end - segments.data.virtual_start,
            ),
            (
                "active boot stack",
                boot_info.boot_stack_virtual_start,
                boot_info.boot_stack_physical_start,
                boot_info.boot_stack_virtual_end - boot_info.boot_stack_virtual_start,
            ),
        ],
    );
    probe_candidate_page_tables(boot_info);
}

#[cfg(feature = "probe-hhdm-frame")]
fn probe_cloned_page_tables(
    allocator: &mut rustix_kernel::frame::FrameAllocator,
    memory_map: &rustix_kernel::memory::MemoryMap,
    hhdm_offset: u64,
    physical_address_bits: u8,
    virtual_address_bits: u8,
    source_reader: &impl rustix_kernel::paging::PageTableReader<
        Error = rustix_kernel::memory::HhdmAddressError,
    >,
    source_root: rustix_kernel::paging::Cr3Root,
    config: rustix_kernel::paging::PageWalkConfig,
    spans: [(&str, u64, u64, u64); 4],
) {
    use rustix_kernel::paging::CandidatePageTables;

    let mut memory = LimineHhdmCandidateMemory {
        memory_map,
        hhdm_offset,
        physical_address_bits,
        virtual_address_bits,
    };
    let mut candidate = match CandidatePageTables::new(allocator, &mut memory, config) {
        Ok(candidate) => candidate,
        Err(error) => {
            kprintln!(
                "candidate clone probe failed to create root: {:?}",
                error.cause
            );
            if let Some(frame) = error.frame {
                release_probe_frame(allocator, frame);
            }
            halt_forever();
        }
    };
    if let Err(error) = candidate.clone_inherited_hierarchy(allocator, source_reader, source_root) {
        kprintln!("candidate clone probe failed: {:?}", error);
        release_candidate_after_probe_failure(candidate, allocator);
    }
    for (label, virtual_start, physical_start, length) in spans {
        if !candidate_span_matches_source(
            &candidate,
            source_reader,
            source_root,
            config,
            virtual_start,
            physical_start,
            length,
        ) {
            kprintln!(
                "candidate clone probe failed: {} translation mismatch",
                label
            );
            release_candidate_after_probe_failure(candidate, allocator);
        }
    }
    let table_count = candidate.table_count();
    if let Err(failure) = candidate.release(allocator) {
        kprintln!(
            "candidate clone probe failed to release frames: {:?}",
            failure
        );
        halt_forever();
    }
    kprintln!(
        "candidate inherited-root clone probe passed: {} owned table pages preserve critical paths; CR3 unchanged",
        table_count
    );
}

fn candidate_span_matches_source(
    candidate: &rustix_kernel::paging::CandidatePageTables<'_, LimineHhdmCandidateMemory<'_>>,
    source_reader: &impl rustix_kernel::paging::PageTableReader<
        Error = rustix_kernel::memory::HhdmAddressError,
    >,
    source_root: rustix_kernel::paging::Cr3Root,
    config: rustix_kernel::paging::PageWalkConfig,
    virtual_start: u64,
    physical_start: u64,
    length: u64,
) -> bool {
    use rustix_kernel::paging::{walk_virtual_address, PageWalkOutcome};

    let mut offset = 0;
    while offset < length {
        let Some(virtual_address) = virtual_start.checked_add(offset) else {
            return false;
        };
        let Some(expected_physical) = physical_start.checked_add(offset) else {
            return false;
        };
        let source_result =
            walk_virtual_address(source_reader, source_root, virtual_address, config);
        let candidate_result = candidate.walk(virtual_address);
        let (source_translation, candidate_translation) = match (source_result, candidate_result) {
            (Ok(PageWalkOutcome::Mapped(source)), Ok(PageWalkOutcome::Mapped(candidate))) => {
                (source, candidate)
            }
            (source, candidate) => {
                kprintln!(
                    "candidate clone walk mismatch at {:#018x}: inherited={:?}, candidate={:?}",
                    virtual_address,
                    source,
                    candidate
                );
                return false;
            }
        };
        // The CPU may update Accessed/Dirty in the active hierarchy after the
        // clone; they are hardware tracking state, not translation policy.
        let hardware_tracking_bits = (1 << 5) | (1 << 6);
        if source_translation.physical_address != candidate_translation.physical_address
            || source_translation.leaf_physical_base != candidate_translation.leaf_physical_base
            || source_translation.page_size != candidate_translation.page_size
            || source_translation.permissions != candidate_translation.permissions
            || source_translation.pat_index != candidate_translation.pat_index
            || source_translation.raw_leaf_entry & !hardware_tracking_bits
                != candidate_translation.raw_leaf_entry & !hardware_tracking_bits
            || candidate_translation.physical_address != expected_physical
        {
            kprintln!(
                "candidate clone translation mismatch at {:#018x}: inherited={:?}, candidate={:?}, expected PA={:#x}",
                virtual_address,
                source_translation,
                candidate_translation,
                expected_physical
            );
            return false;
        }
        let Some(next_offset) = offset.checked_add(rustix_kernel::paging::PAGE_SIZE) else {
            return false;
        };
        offset = next_offset;
    }
    true
}

#[cfg(feature = "probe-hhdm-frame")]
fn probe_candidate_page_tables(boot_info: &mut boot::BootInfo) {
    use rustix_kernel::paging::{
        validate_mapping_range, CachePolicy, CandidatePageTables, PagePermissions, PageWalkOutcome,
    };

    let Some(physical_address_bits) = boot_info.cpu_info.physical_address_bits else {
        kprintln!("candidate page-table probe failed: physical width unknown");
        halt_forever();
    };
    if !boot_info.cpu_info.nx_enabled || !boot_info.cpu_info.normal_caching {
        kprintln!("candidate page-table probe failed: NXE or normal caching unavailable");
        halt_forever();
    }
    let pat_value = boot_info
        .cpu_info
        .pat_msr_value
        .expect("inherited cache-alias probe validated active PAT");
    let pat = rustix_kernel::paging::PatLayout::from_msr_value(pat_value).unwrap_or_else(|error| {
        kprintln!(
            "candidate page-table probe failed: invalid PAT: {:?}",
            error
        );
        halt_forever();
    });
    let registers = match &boot_info.cpu_info.mtrr {
        rustix_kernel::paging::MtrrState::Captured(registers) => registers,
        _ => {
            kprintln!("candidate page-table probe failed: captured MTRR state unavailable");
            halt_forever();
        }
    };
    let mtrrs = match registers.validated_layout(physical_address_bits) {
        Ok(mtrrs) => mtrrs,
        Err(error) => {
            kprintln!(
                "candidate page-table probe failed: invalid MTRR: {:?}",
                error
            );
            halt_forever();
        }
    };
    let config = rustix_kernel::paging::PageWalkConfig {
        levels: if boot_info.cpu_info.active_linear_address_bits == 57 {
            5
        } else {
            4
        },
        physical_address_bits,
        virtual_address_bits: boot_info.cpu_info.active_linear_address_bits,
        nx_enabled: true,
        page_2m_supported: true,
        page_1g_supported: boot_info.cpu_info.has_1g_pages,
    };
    let virtual_address = 0xffff_9000_ffff_f000;
    let permissions = PagePermissions {
        writable: true,
        executable: false,
        user_accessible: false,
    };
    let frame = match boot_info.frame_allocator.allocate() {
        Some(frame) => frame,
        None => {
            kprintln!("candidate page-table probe failed: no leaf frame available");
            halt_forever();
        }
    };
    let mapping = match validate_mapping_range(
        virtual_address,
        frame.address(),
        rustix_kernel::paging::PAGE_SIZE,
        permissions,
        Some(physical_address_bits),
        config.virtual_address_bits,
    ) {
        Ok(mapping) => mapping,
        Err(error) => {
            kprintln!(
                "candidate page-table probe failed: invalid mapping: {:?}",
                error
            );
            release_probe_frame(&mut boot_info.frame_allocator, frame);
            halt_forever();
        }
    };
    let cache_attributes = match mapping.select_cache_attributes(
        CachePolicy::WriteBack,
        pat,
        &mtrrs,
        boot_info.cpu_info.normal_caching,
    ) {
        Ok(attributes) => attributes,
        Err(error) => {
            kprintln!(
                "candidate page-table probe failed: cache policy: {:?}",
                error
            );
            release_probe_frame(&mut boot_info.frame_allocator, frame);
            halt_forever();
        }
    };

    let mut memory = LimineHhdmCandidateMemory {
        memory_map: &boot_info.memory_map,
        hhdm_offset: boot_info.hhdm_offset,
        physical_address_bits,
        virtual_address_bits: boot_info.cpu_info.active_linear_address_bits,
    };
    let mut candidate =
        match CandidatePageTables::new(&mut boot_info.frame_allocator, &mut memory, config) {
            Ok(candidate) => candidate,
            Err(error) => {
                kprintln!(
                    "candidate page-table probe failed to create root: {:?}",
                    error.cause
                );
                release_probe_frame(&mut boot_info.frame_allocator, frame);
                if let Some(root_frame) = error.frame {
                    release_probe_frame(&mut boot_info.frame_allocator, root_frame);
                }
                halt_forever();
            }
        };
    let root = candidate.root_physical_address();
    let frame_address = frame.address();
    if let Err(failure) = candidate.map_owned_page(
        &mut boot_info.frame_allocator,
        frame,
        mapping,
        cache_attributes,
    ) {
        kprintln!(
            "candidate page-table probe failed to map leaf: {:?}",
            failure.cause
        );
        release_probe_frame(&mut boot_info.frame_allocator, failure.frame);
        release_candidate_after_probe_failure(candidate, &mut boot_info.frame_allocator);
    }

    let walk = candidate.walk(virtual_address);
    let returned_frame = match candidate.unmap_owned_page(virtual_address) {
        Ok(frame) => frame,
        Err(error) => {
            kprintln!(
                "candidate page-table probe failed to unmap leaf: {:?}",
                error
            );
            release_candidate_after_probe_failure(candidate, &mut boot_info.frame_allocator);
        }
    };
    let translation_valid = match &walk {
        Ok(PageWalkOutcome::Mapped(translation)) => {
            translation.physical_address == frame_address
                && translation.page_size == rustix_kernel::paging::PAGE_SIZE
                && translation.permissions == permissions
                && translation.pat_index == cache_attributes.pat_index()
        }
        _ => false,
    };
    if returned_frame.address() != frame_address {
        kprintln!("candidate page-table probe failed: unmap returned the wrong frame");
        release_probe_frame(&mut boot_info.frame_allocator, returned_frame);
        release_candidate_after_probe_failure(candidate, &mut boot_info.frame_allocator);
    }
    release_probe_frame(&mut boot_info.frame_allocator, returned_frame);
    if !translation_valid {
        kprintln!(
            "candidate page-table probe failed: candidate walk: {:?}",
            walk
        );
        release_candidate_after_probe_failure(candidate, &mut boot_info.frame_allocator);
    }
    if let Err(failure) = candidate.release(&mut boot_info.frame_allocator) {
        kprintln!(
            "candidate page-table probe failed to release frames: {:?}",
            failure
        );
        halt_forever();
    }
    kprintln!(
        "candidate page-table probe passed: mapped, walked, unmapped, and released root {:#x}; CR3 unchanged",
        root.expect("candidate retains root until release")
    );
}

fn release_candidate_after_probe_failure(
    candidate: rustix_kernel::paging::CandidatePageTables<'_, LimineHhdmCandidateMemory<'_>>,
    allocator: &mut rustix_kernel::frame::FrameAllocator,
) -> ! {
    if let Err(failure) = candidate.release(allocator) {
        kprintln!("candidate page-table cleanup also failed: {:?}", failure);
    }
    halt_forever()
}

#[cfg(feature = "probe-hhdm-frame")]
fn verify_inherited_mapping(
    reader: &impl rustix_kernel::paging::PageTableReader<
        Error = rustix_kernel::memory::HhdmAddressError,
    >,
    root: rustix_kernel::paging::Cr3Root,
    config: rustix_kernel::paging::PageWalkConfig,
    label: &str,
    virtual_start: u64,
    physical_start: u64,
    length: u64,
) {
    use rustix_kernel::paging::{walk_virtual_address, PageWalkOutcome};

    let mut offset = 0;
    let mut pages = 0;
    let mut first_translation: Option<rustix_kernel::paging::PageTranslation> = None;
    let mut permissions_uniform = true;
    let mut pat_index_uniform = true;
    while offset < length {
        let virtual_address = match virtual_start.checked_add(offset) {
            Some(address) => address,
            None => {
                kprintln!("inherited mapping probe failed: {} virtual overflow", label);
                halt_forever();
            }
        };
        let expected_physical = match physical_start.checked_add(offset) {
            Some(address) => address,
            None => {
                kprintln!(
                    "inherited mapping probe failed: {} physical overflow",
                    label
                );
                halt_forever();
            }
        };
        let translation = match walk_virtual_address(reader, root, virtual_address, config) {
            Ok(PageWalkOutcome::Mapped(translation)) => translation,
            Ok(PageWalkOutcome::NotPresent { level }) => {
                if level == rustix_kernel::paging::PageLevel::Pml4 {
                    let pml4_index = ((virtual_address >> 39) & 0x1ff) as u16;
                    let root_entry = reader.read_entry(root.physical_address(), pml4_index);
                    kprintln!(
                        "inherited mapping PML4 detail: VA={:#018x}, index={}, root={:#x}, entry={:?}",
                        virtual_address,
                        pml4_index,
                        root.physical_address(),
                        root_entry
                    );
                }
                kprintln!(
                    "inherited mapping probe failed: {} absent at {:?}",
                    label,
                    level
                );
                halt_forever();
            }
            Err(error) => {
                kprintln!("inherited mapping probe failed: {}: {:?}", label, error);
                halt_forever();
            }
        };
        if translation.physical_address != expected_physical {
            kprintln!(
                "inherited mapping probe failed: {} {:#018x} mapped to {:#018x}, expected {:#018x}",
                label,
                virtual_address,
                translation.physical_address,
                expected_physical
            );
            halt_forever();
        }
        if let Some(first) = first_translation {
            permissions_uniform &= translation.permissions == first.permissions;
            pat_index_uniform &= translation.pat_index == first.pat_index;
        } else {
            first_translation = Some(translation);
        }
        pages += 1;
        offset += rustix_kernel::paging::PAGE_SIZE;
    }
    if let Some(first) = first_translation {
        kprintln!(
            "inherited mapping probe passed: {} ({} pages), first permissions={:?}, PAT index={}, leaf size={}, uniform permissions={}, uniform PAT index={}",
            label,
            pages,
            first.permissions,
            first.pat_index,
            first.page_size,
            permissions_uniform,
            pat_index_uniform
        );
    }
}

#[cfg(feature = "probe-hhdm-frame")]
fn verify_kernel_cache_aliases(
    boot_info: &boot::BootInfo,
    reader: &impl rustix_kernel::paging::PageTableReader<
        Error = rustix_kernel::memory::HhdmAddressError,
    >,
    root: rustix_kernel::paging::Cr3Root,
    config: rustix_kernel::paging::PageWalkConfig,
    pat: rustix_kernel::paging::PatLayout,
    mtrrs: &rustix_kernel::paging::ValidatedMtrrLayout,
    label: &str,
    kernel_virtual_start: u64,
    physical_start: u64,
    length: u64,
) {
    use rustix_kernel::paging::{walk_virtual_address, PageWalkOutcome};

    let mut offset = 0;
    let mut pages = 0;
    while offset < length {
        let physical = match physical_start.checked_add(offset) {
            Some(address) => address,
            None => {
                kprintln!("cache-alias probe failed: {} physical overflow", label);
                halt_forever();
            }
        };
        let kernel_virtual = match kernel_virtual_start.checked_add(offset) {
            Some(address) => address,
            None => {
                kprintln!("cache-alias probe failed: {} virtual overflow", label);
                halt_forever();
            }
        };
        let hhdm_virtual = match boot_info.memory_map.limine_hhdm_address(
            boot_info.hhdm_offset,
            physical,
            rustix_kernel::paging::PAGE_SIZE,
            boot_info.cpu_info.physical_address_bits,
            boot_info.cpu_info.active_linear_address_bits,
        ) {
            Ok(address) => address,
            Err(error) => {
                kprintln!(
                    "cache-alias probe failed: {} HHDM range: {:?}",
                    label,
                    error
                );
                halt_forever();
            }
        };
        let kernel_translation = match walk_virtual_address(reader, root, kernel_virtual, config) {
            Ok(PageWalkOutcome::Mapped(translation)) => translation,
            result => {
                kprintln!(
                    "cache-alias probe failed: {} kernel walk: {:?}",
                    label,
                    result
                );
                halt_forever();
            }
        };
        let hhdm_translation = match walk_virtual_address(reader, root, hhdm_virtual, config) {
            Ok(PageWalkOutcome::Mapped(translation)) => translation,
            result => {
                kprintln!(
                    "cache-alias probe failed: {} HHDM walk: {:?}",
                    label,
                    result
                );
                halt_forever();
            }
        };
        if kernel_translation.physical_address != physical
            || hhdm_translation.physical_address != physical
        {
            kprintln!(
                "cache-alias probe failed: {} physical {:#018x} has inconsistent translations",
                label,
                physical
            );
            halt_forever();
        }
        let kernel_type = match mtrrs.effective_memory_type_for(
            physical,
            pat,
            kernel_translation.pat_index,
            boot_info.cpu_info.normal_caching,
        ) {
            Ok(memory_type) => memory_type,
            Err(error) => {
                kprintln!(
                    "cache-alias probe failed: {} kernel PAT/MTRR: {:?}",
                    label,
                    error
                );
                halt_forever();
            }
        };
        let hhdm_type = match mtrrs.effective_memory_type_for(
            physical,
            pat,
            hhdm_translation.pat_index,
            boot_info.cpu_info.normal_caching,
        ) {
            Ok(memory_type) => memory_type,
            Err(error) => {
                kprintln!(
                    "cache-alias probe failed: {} HHDM PAT/MTRR: {:?}",
                    label,
                    error
                );
                halt_forever();
            }
        };
        if kernel_type != hhdm_type {
            kprintln!(
                "cache-alias conflict: {} PA {:#018x}, kernel {:?} vs HHDM {:?}",
                label,
                physical,
                kernel_type,
                hhdm_type
            );
            halt_forever();
        }
        pages += 1;
        offset += rustix_kernel::paging::PAGE_SIZE;
    }
    kprintln!(
        "cache-alias probe passed: {} ({} pages; effective types match)",
        label,
        pages
    );
}

fn release_probe_frame(
    allocator: &mut rustix_kernel::frame::FrameAllocator,
    frame: rustix_kernel::frame::Frame,
) {
    if let Err(error) = allocator.deallocate(frame) {
        kprintln!(
            "HHDM frame probe failed to return its frame: {:?}",
            error.error
        );
        halt_forever();
    }
}

#[cfg(feature = "inject-page-fault")]
fn run_fault_injection() {
    kprintln!("fault injection: triggering page fault at 0x00000000deadbeef");
    // SAFETY: This is an opt-in QEMU test that deliberately reads an unmapped
    // low virtual address; the installed page-fault handler is expected to halt.
    unsafe {
        core::arch::asm!(
            "mov rax, 0xdeadbeef",
            "mov rax, qword ptr [rax]",
            out("rax") _,
            options(nostack)
        );
    }
    kprintln!("fault injection unexpectedly returned");
    halt_forever();
}

#[cfg(feature = "inject-invalid-opcode")]
fn run_fault_injection() {
    kprintln!("fault injection: triggering invalid opcode with ud2");
    // SAFETY: This is an opt-in QEMU test that deliberately raises #UD; the
    // installed invalid-opcode handler is expected to halt.
    unsafe { core::arch::asm!("ud2", options(nomem, nostack)) };
    kprintln!("fault injection unexpectedly returned");
    halt_forever();
}

#[panic_handler]
fn panic(info: &PanicInfo<'_>) -> ! {
    arch::x86_64::serial::initialize();
    kprintln!("KERNEL PANIC: {}", info);
    halt_forever()
}

fn halt_forever() -> ! {
    loop {
        // SAFETY: The bootstrap has no interrupt handlers or scheduler to resume.
        unsafe { core::arch::asm!("cli; hlt", options(nomem, nostack)) };
    }
}

ISO_PATH = TARGET_DIR / "rustix.iso"

REQUIRED_LIMINE_FILES = (
    "limine-bios.sys",
    "limine-bios-cd.bin",
    "limine-uefi-cd.bin",
    "BOOTX64.EFI",
)


class BuildError(RuntimeError):
    """An actionable error while preparing or testing the boot image."""


def require_tool(name: str) -> str:
    path = shutil.which(name)
    if path is None:
        raise BuildError(f"required tool '{name}' was not found on PATH")
    return path


def sha256(path: Path) -> str:
    digest = hashlib.sha256()
    with path.open("rb") as source:
        for block in iter(lambda: source.read(1024 * 1024), b""):
            digest.update(block)
    return digest.hexdigest()


def safe_extract(archive: zipfile.ZipFile, destination: Path) -> None:
    root = destination.resolve()
    for member in archive.infolist():
        name = PurePosixPath(member.filename)
        mode = member.external_attr >> 16
        if not name.parts or name.is_absolute() or ".." in name.parts or ":" in name.parts[0]:
            raise BuildError(f"unsafe path in Limine archive: {member.filename}")
        if stat.S_ISLNK(mode):
            raise BuildError(f"symlink in Limine archive is not allowed: {member.filename}")
        output = (destination / Path(*name.parts)).resolve()
        if output != root and root not in output.parents:
            raise BuildError(f"archive member escapes extraction directory: {member.filename}")
    archive.extractall(destination)


def ensure_limine() -> tuple[Path, Path]:
    cache = TARGET_DIR / "tools" / f"limine-{LIMINE_VERSION}"
    archive_path = TARGET_DIR / "tools" / LIMINE_ARCHIVE_NAME
    extracted = cache / "archive"
    cache.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    extracted.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)

    if not archive_path.exists():
        print(f"Downloading Limine {LIMINE_VERSION} binary release...")
        request = urllib.request.Request(
            LIMINE_ARCHIVE_URL,
            headers={"User-Agent": "Rustix-OS-build/0.1"},
        )
        try:
            with urllib.request.urlopen(request, timeout=60) as response, archive_path.open(
                "wb"
            ) as output:
                shutil.copyfileobj(response, output)
        except Exception as error:
            archive_path.unlink(missing_ok=True)
            raise BuildError(f"could not download pinned Limine release: {error}") from error

    actual_hash = sha256(archive_path)
    if actual_hash != LIMINE_ARCHIVE_SHA256:
        archive_path.unlink(missing_ok=True)
        raise BuildError(
            "Limine archive SHA-256 mismatch: "
            f"expected {LIMINE_ARCHIVE_SHA256}, got {actual_hash}"
        )

    try:
        with zipfile.ZipFile(archive_path) as archive:
            safe_extract(archive, extracted)
    except (OSError, zipfile.BadZipFile) as error:
        raise BuildError(f"could not extract the pinned Limine archive: {error}") from error

    def find_asset(name: str) -> Path:
        matches = sorted(extracted.rglob(name))
        if not matches:
            raise BuildError(f"Limine {LIMINE_VERSION} archive is missing {name}")
        return matches[0]

    if sys.platform == "win32":
        limine_tool = find_asset("limine.exe")
    else:
        limine_source = find_asset("limine.c")
        limine_tool = limine_source.with_name("limine")
        if not limine_tool.is_file():
            compiler = require_tool("cc")
            print("Building Limine host utility from the pinned source...")
            subprocess.run(
                [
                    compiler,
                    "-g",
                    "-O2",
                    "-pipe",
                    "-std=c99",
                    "-D_FILE_OFFSET_BITS=64",
                    limine_source.name,
                    "-o",
                    str(limine_tool),
                ],
                cwd=limine_source.parent,
                check=True,
            )
        limine_tool.chmod(
            limine_tool.stat().st_mode | stat.S_IXUSR | stat.S_IXGRP | stat.S_IXOTH
        )
    return limine_tool, extracted


def build_image() -> None:
    if not KERNEL.is_file():
        raise BuildError("kernel ELF not found; run 'just build' first")
    xorriso = require_tool("xorriso")
    limine_tool, limine_root = ensure_limine()

    shutil.rmtree(ISO_ROOT, ignore_errors=True)
    boot_dir = ISO_ROOT / "boot" / "limine"
    efi_dir = ISO_ROOT / "EFI" / "BOOT"
    boot_dir.mkdir(parents=True)
    efi_dir.mkdir(parents=True)
    shutil.copy2(KERNEL, ISO_ROOT / "boot" / "rustix")
    shutil.copy2(ROOT / "limine.conf", ISO_ROOT / "limine.conf")

    for name in REQUIRED_LIMINE_FILES:
        source = next(iter(sorted(limine_root.rglob(name))), None)
        if source is None:
            raise BuildError(f"Limine archive is missing required file {name}")
        if name == "BOOTX64.EFI":
            shutil.copy2(source, efi_dir / name)
        else:
            shutil.copy2(source, boot_dir / name)

    ISO_PATH.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    xorriso_command = [
        xorriso,
        "-as",
        "mkisofs",
        "-R",
        "-r",
        "-J",
        "-b",
        "boot/limine/limine-bios-cd.bin",
        "-no-emul-boot",
        "-boot-load-size",
        "4",
        "-boot-info-table",
        "-hfsplus",
        "-apm-block-size",
        "2048",
        "--efi-boot",
        "boot/limine/limine-uefi-cd.bin",
        "-efi-boot-part",
        "--efi-boot-image",
        "--protective-msdos-label",
        str(ISO_ROOT),
        "-o",
        str(ISO_PATH),
    ]
    subprocess.run(xorriso_command, cwd=ROOT, check=True)
    subprocess.run([str(limine_tool), "bios-install", str(ISO_PATH)], cwd=ROOT, check=True)
    print(f"Created hybrid BIOS/UEFI image: {ISO_PATH.relative_to(ROOT)}")


def smoke_test(timeout: int) -> None:
    qemu = require_tool("qemu-system-x86_64")
    if not ISO_PATH.is_file():
        raise BuildError("boot image not found; run 'just image' first")

    serial_log = TARGET_DIR / "rustix-qemu-serial.log"
    serial_log.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    serial_log.unlink(missing_ok=True)
    serial_device = "file:" + serial_log.relative_to(ROOT).as_posix()
    command = [
        qemu,
        "-machine",
        "q35",
        "-m",
        "256M",
        "-cdrom",
        str(ISO_PATH),
        "-boot",
        "d",
        "-display",
        "none",
        "-monitor",
        "none",
        "-serial",
        serial_device,
        "-no-reboot",
        "-no-shutdown",
    ]

    timed_out = False
    try:
        result = subprocess.run(command, cwd=ROOT, timeout=timeout, check=False)
    except subprocess.TimeoutExpired:
        timed_out = True
        result = None

    if not timed_out and result is not None and result.returncode != 0:
        details = serial_log.read_text(encoding="latin-1") if serial_log.exists() else ""
        raise BuildError(
            f"QEMU exited with status {result.returncode} before the smoke-test timeout.\n"
            f"Serial output:\n{details}"
        )

    output = serial_log.read_text(encoding="latin-1") if serial_log.exists() else ""
    expected = (
        "Rustix kernel: x86_64 Rust bootstrap",
        "page-table transition passed:",
        "kernel heap probe passed: alignment, reuse, deterministic exhaustion",
        "crabshell: ready (volatile RAM filesystem)",
        "root@rustix:/home/rustix# ",
    )
    missing = [marker for marker in expected if marker not in output]
    if missing:
        raise BuildError(
            "QEMU did not reach the expected kernel state; missing serial markers: "
            + ", ".join(repr(marker) for marker in missing)
            + f"\nSerial output:\n{output or '<empty>'}"
        )

    print(f"QEMU boot smoke test passed (bounded to {timeout}s).")
    print(f"Captured serial log: {serial_log.relative_to(ROOT)}")


def fault_smoke_test(kind: str, timeout: int) -> None:
    qemu = require_tool("qemu-system-x86_64")
    if not ISO_PATH.is_file():
        raise BuildError("boot image not found; build the fault-injection image first")

    serial_log = TARGET_DIR / f"rustix-qemu-fault-{kind}.log"
    serial_log.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    serial_log.unlink(missing_ok=True)
    serial_device = "file:" + serial_log.relative_to(ROOT).as_posix()
    command = [
        qemu,
        "-machine",
        "q35",
        "-m",
        "256M",
        "-cdrom",
        str(ISO_PATH),
        "-boot",
        "d",
        "-display",
        "none",
        "-monitor",
        "none",
        "-serial",
        serial_device,
        "-no-reboot",
        "-no-shutdown",
    ]

    timed_out = False
    try:
        result = subprocess.run(command, cwd=ROOT, timeout=timeout, check=False)
    except subprocess.TimeoutExpired:
        timed_out = True
        result = None

    output = serial_log.read_text(encoding="latin-1") if serial_log.exists() else ""
    if kind == "page-fault":
        expected = (
            "fault injection: triggering page fault at 0x00000000deadbeef",
            "KERNEL EXCEPTION: vector 14 (page fault)",
            "page fault address (CR2): 0x00000000deadbeef",
        )
    elif kind == "invalid-opcode":
        expected = (
            "fault injection: triggering invalid opcode with ud2",
            "KERNEL EXCEPTION: vector 6 (invalid opcode)",
        )
    else:
        raise BuildError(f"unsupported fault-injection test: {kind}")

    missing = [marker for marker in expected if marker not in output]
    if missing:
        raise BuildError(
            f"QEMU did not report the expected {kind} exception; missing serial markers: "
            + ", ".join(repr(marker) for marker in missing)
            + f"\nSerial output:\n{output or '<empty>'}"
        )
    if "root@rustix:/home/rustix# " in output:
        raise BuildError(f"kernel reached the shell after {kind} injection\nSerial output:\n{output}")
    if "fault injection unexpectedly returned" in output:
        raise BuildError(f"{kind} instruction returned instead of faulting\nSerial output:\n{output}")
    if not timed_out:
        status = result.returncode if result is not None else "unknown"
        raise BuildError(
            f"QEMU did not remain halted after {kind} (exit status {status})\n"
            f"Serial output:\n{output}"
        )

    print(f"QEMU {kind} fault-injection test passed (halt observed within {timeout}s).")
    print(f"Captured serial log: {serial_log.relative_to(ROOT)}")


def build_kernel(features: tuple[str, ...] = ()) -> None:
    command = ["cargo", "build", "--release", "--target", "x86_64-unknown-none"]
    if features:
        command.extend(["--features", ",".join(features)])
    subprocess.run(command, cwd=ROOT, check=True)


def frame_smoke_workflow(timeout: int) -> None:
    failure: BaseException | None = None
    try:
        build_kernel(("probe-hhdm-frame",))
        build_image()
        smoke_test(timeout)
        serial_log = TARGET_DIR / "rustix-qemu-serial.log"
        output = serial_log.read_text(encoding="latin-1") if serial_log.exists() else ""
        markers = (
            "HHDM frame probe passed: wrote, read, cleared, and reclaimed one frame",
            "inherited root HHDM probe passed: read 512 entries",
            "candidate inherited-root clone probe passed:",
            "candidate page-table probe passed: mapped, walked, unmapped, and released",
        )
        missing = [marker for marker in markers if marker not in output]
        if missing:
            raise BuildError(
                "QEMU did not report successful HHDM access probes; missing markers: "
                + ", ".join(repr(marker) for marker in missing)
                + f"\nSerial output:\n{output}"
            )
        print("QEMU HHDM, inherited-mapping, cloned-root, and candidate-map probes passed.")
    except BaseException as error:
        failure = error

    try:
        build_kernel()
        build_image()
    except BaseException as restore_error:
        if failure is not None:
            raise BuildError(
                f"HHDM frame workflow failed ({failure}); restoring the default image "
                f"also failed ({restore_error})"
            ) from restore_error
        raise

    if failure is not None:
        raise BuildError(
            f"HHDM frame workflow failed; the default release image was restored: {failure}"
        ) from failure
    print("Restored the default release kernel and ISO after the HHDM frame probe.")


def fault_smoke_workflow(timeout: int) -> None:
    tests = (
        ("page-fault", "inject-page-fault"),
        ("invalid-opcode", "inject-invalid-opcode"),
    )
    failure: BaseException | None = None
    try:
        for kind, feature in tests:
            build_kernel((feature,))
            build_image()
            fault_smoke_test(kind, timeout)
    except BaseException as error:
        failure = error

    try:
        build_kernel()
        build_image()
    except BaseException as restore_error:
        if failure is not None:
            raise BuildError(
                f"fault-injection workflow failed ({failure}); restoring the default image "
                f"also failed ({restore_error})"
            ) from restore_error
        raise

    if failure is not None:
        raise BuildError(
            f"fault-injection workflow failed; the default release image was restored: {failure}"
        ) from failure
    print("Restored the default release kernel and ISO after fault-injection tests.")


def run_interactive() -> None:
    qemu = require_tool("qemu-system-x86_64")
    if not ISO_PATH.is_file():
        raise BuildError("boot image not found; run 'just image' first")
    command = [
        qemu,
        "-machine",
        "q35",
        "-m",
        "256M",
        "-cdrom",
        str(ISO_PATH),
        "-boot",
        "d",
        "-display",
        "none",
        "-monitor",
        "none",
        "-serial",
        "stdio",
        "-no-reboot",
        "-no-shutdown",
    ]
    result = subprocess.run(command, cwd=ROOT, check=False)
    if result.returncode != 0:
        raise BuildError(f"QEMU exited with status {result.returncode}")


def run_debug() -> None:
    qemu = require_tool("qemu-system-x86_64")
    if not ISO_PATH.is_file():
        raise BuildError("boot image not found; run 'just debug-image' first")

    command = [
        qemu,
        "-machine",
        "q35",
        "-m",
        "256M",
        "-cdrom",
        str(ISO_PATH),
        "-boot",
        "d",
        "-display",
        "none",
        "-monitor",
        "none",
        "-serial",
        "stdio",
        "-gdb",
        "tcp:127.0.0.1:1234",
        "-S",
        "-no-reboot",
        "-no-shutdown",
    ]
    print("QEMU is paused; GDB stub listening on 127.0.0.1:1234.", flush=True)
    print("Attach with the Rustix: QEMU (CodeLLDB) debug configuration.", flush=True)
    result = subprocess.run(command, cwd=ROOT, check=False)
    if result.returncode != 0:
        raise BuildError(f"QEMU exited with status {result.returncode}")


def main() -> int:
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__)
    subparsers = parser.add_subparsers(dest="command", required=True)
    subparsers.add_parser("image", help="create a pinned Limine BIOS/UEFI hybrid ISO")
    smoke = subparsers.add_parser("smoke", help="boot the ISO and check its serial output")
    smoke.add_argument("--timeout", type=int, default=20, help="QEMU time limit in seconds")
    frame_smoke = subparsers.add_parser(
        "frame-smoke", help="probe HHDM access and an inactive candidate root in QEMU"
    )
    frame_smoke.add_argument("--timeout", type=int, default=20, help="QEMU time limit in seconds")
    fault_smoke = subparsers.add_parser(
        "fault-smoke", help="test fatal exceptions in QEMU, then restore the default image"
    )
    fault_smoke.add_argument("--timeout", type=int, default=10, help="per-test QEMU time limit")
    subparsers.add_parser("run", help="run the ISO with an interactive serial terminal")
    subparsers.add_parser("debug", help="run the ISO paused with a loopback GDB stub")
    args = parser.parse_args()

    try:
        if args.command == "image":
            build_image()
        elif args.command == "run":
            run_interactive()
        elif args.command == "debug":
            run_debug()
        elif args.command == "frame-smoke":
            if args.timeout <= 0:
                raise BuildError("--timeout must be a positive number of seconds")
            frame_smoke_workflow(args.timeout)
        elif args.command == "fault-smoke":
            if args.timeout <= 0:
                raise BuildError("--timeout must be a positive number of seconds")
            fault_smoke_workflow(args.timeout)
        else:
            if args.timeout <= 0:
                raise BuildError("--timeout must be a positive number of seconds")
            smoke_test(args.timeout)
    except (BuildError, OSError, subprocess.CalledProcessError) as error:
        print(f"Rustix boot workflow failed: {error}", file=sys.stderr)
        return 1
    return 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    raise SystemExit(main())

//! Checked x86_64 mapping policy and an inactive candidate page-table builder.
//!
//! Pure helpers validate addresses, permissions, and cache policy. Candidate
//! table access is delegated to an unsafe backend contract and remains separate
//! from the active root; this module never installs a root in CR3.

use crate::frame::{Frame, FrameAllocator, FrameError};
use crate::memory::{
    is_canonical_virtual_address, physical_range_fits_address_width, HhdmAddressError, MemoryMap,
    RegionKind,
};

/// Base page size supported by the initial Rustix mapping policy.
pub const PAGE_SIZE: u64 = 4096;

/// The physical root address and interpretation of CR3's low bits.
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct Cr3Root {
    physical_address: u64,
    low_bits: Cr3LowBits,
}

impl Cr3Root {
    pub const fn physical_address(self) -> u64 {
        self.physical_address
    }

    pub const fn low_bits(self) -> Cr3LowBits {
        self.low_bits
    }
}

/// CR3's low bits are either a PCID or the paging-structure cache controls.
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum Cr3LowBits {
    Pcid(u16),
    CacheControls {
        page_level_write_through: bool,
        page_level_cache_disable: bool,
    },
}

#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum Cr3Error {
    UnknownPhysicalAddressWidth,
    InvalidPhysicalAddressWidth,
    InvalidRootAddress,
    ReservedBits,
}

#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum Cr3RootAccessError {
    NotBootloaderReclaimable,
    Hhdm(HhdmAddressError),
}

/// Decode the currently active CR3 value without dereferencing its root table.
///
/// The caller supplies the reported physical-address width and whether CR4.PCIDE
/// is active, since those determine the valid address and low-bit encodings.
/// Encode a replacement CR3 value while preserving the active low-bit mode.
///
/// PCID is retained but the no-flush bit is always cleared so the selected PCID
/// is invalidated on load. Legacy PWT/PCD controls are preserved unchanged.
pub fn encode_cr3_value(
    root_physical_address: u64,
    low_bits: Cr3LowBits,
    physical_address_bits: u8,
) -> Result<u64, Cr3Error> {
    if !(12..=MAX_PTE_PHYSICAL_ADDRESS_BITS).contains(&physical_address_bits) {
        return Err(Cr3Error::InvalidPhysicalAddressWidth);
    }
    let root_end = root_physical_address
        .checked_add(PAGE_SIZE)
        .ok_or(Cr3Error::InvalidRootAddress)?;
    if root_physical_address & (PAGE_SIZE - 1) != 0
        || !physical_range_fits_address_width(
            root_physical_address,
            root_end,
            physical_address_bits,
        )
    {
        return Err(Cr3Error::InvalidRootAddress);
    }
    let low = match low_bits {
        Cr3LowBits::Pcid(pcid) if pcid <= 0x0fff => u64::from(pcid),
        Cr3LowBits::Pcid(_) => return Err(Cr3Error::ReservedBits),
        Cr3LowBits::CacheControls {
            page_level_write_through,
            page_level_cache_disable,
        } => {
            (u64::from(page_level_write_through) << 3) | (u64::from(page_level_cache_disable) << 4)
        }
    };
    Ok(root_physical_address | low)
}

pub fn parse_cr3_root(
    raw: u64,
    physical_address_bits: Option<u8>,
    pcid_enabled: bool,
) -> Result<Cr3Root, Cr3Error> {
    let physical_address_bits =
        physical_address_bits.ok_or(Cr3Error::UnknownPhysicalAddressWidth)?;
    if !(12..=MAX_PTE_PHYSICAL_ADDRESS_BITS).contains(&physical_address_bits) {
        return Err(Cr3Error::InvalidPhysicalAddressWidth);
    }

    let physical_mask = ((1u64 << physical_address_bits) - 1) & !(PAGE_SIZE - 1);
    let low_mask = if pcid_enabled {
        PAGE_SIZE - 1
    } else {
        (1 << 3) | (1 << 4)
    };
    if raw & !(physical_mask | low_mask) != 0 {
        return Err(Cr3Error::ReservedBits);
    }

    let low_bits = if pcid_enabled {
        Cr3LowBits::Pcid((raw & (PAGE_SIZE - 1)) as u16)
    } else {
        Cr3LowBits::CacheControls {
            page_level_write_through: raw & (1 << 3) != 0,
            page_level_cache_disable: raw & (1 << 4) != 0,
        }
    };

    Ok(Cr3Root {
        physical_address: raw & physical_mask,
        low_bits,
    })
}

/// Calculate the protocol-backed HHDM address of Limine's inherited root page.
///
/// This requires the root page to be wholly contained in bootloader-reclaimable
/// memory, as specified for Limine page tables. It does not dereference the page
/// or prove that the active hierarchy contains the HHDM mapping.
pub fn inherited_cr3_root_hhdm_address(
    root: Cr3Root,
    memory_map: &MemoryMap,
    hhdm_offset: u64,
    physical_address_bits: Option<u8>,
    virtual_address_bits: u8,
) -> Result<u64, Cr3RootAccessError> {
    let physical_start = root.physical_address();
    let physical_end = physical_start
        .checked_add(PAGE_SIZE)
        .ok_or(Cr3RootAccessError::Hhdm(HhdmAddressError::AddressOverflow))?;
    if !memory_map.range_is_within_region_kind(
        physical_start,
        physical_end,
        RegionKind::BootloaderReclaimable,
    ) {
        return Err(Cr3RootAccessError::NotBootloaderReclaimable);
    }
    memory_map
        .limine_hhdm_address(
            hhdm_offset,
            physical_start,
            PAGE_SIZE,
            physical_address_bits,
            virtual_address_bits,
        )
        .map_err(Cr3RootAccessError::Hhdm)
}

#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum PageLevel {
    Pml5,
    Pml4,
    Pdpt,
    Pd,
    Pt,
}

#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct PageWalkConfig {
    pub levels: u8,
    pub physical_address_bits: u8,
    pub virtual_address_bits: u8,
    pub nx_enabled: bool,
    pub page_2m_supported: bool,
    pub page_1g_supported: bool,
}

#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct PageTranslation {
    pub physical_address: u64,
    pub leaf_physical_base: u64,
    pub page_size: u64,
    pub permissions: PagePermissions,
    pub pat_index: u8,
    pub raw_leaf_entry: u64,
}

#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum PageWalkOutcome {
    NotPresent { level: PageLevel },
    Mapped(PageTranslation),
}

#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum PageTableEntryError {
    PhysicalAddressOutOfRange,
    NxDisabled,
    LargePageUnsupported,
    LargePageAtInvalidLevel,
    LargePageMisaligned,
}

#[derive(Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum PageWalkError<E> {
    InvalidConfiguration,
    NonCanonicalAddress,
    InvalidRoot,
    InvalidEntry {
        level: PageLevel,
        error: PageTableEntryError,
    },
    Reader(E),
}

/// Read one raw entry from a table at a validated physical page address.
pub trait PageTableReader {
    type Error;
