        assert_eq!(registers.default_type, 0xc06);
        assert_eq!(registers.variable_register_count, 2);
        let fixed = registers
            .fixed_registers
            .expect("fixed ranges are supported");
        assert_eq!(fixed[0], 0x250);
        assert_eq!(fixed[10], 0x26f);
        assert_eq!(registers.variable_registers[0].base, 0x200);
        assert_eq!(registers.variable_registers[0].mask, 0x201);
        assert_eq!(registers.variable_registers[1].base, 0x202);
        assert_eq!(registers.variable_registers[1].mask, 0x203);
        assert_eq!(
            registers.variable_registers[2],
            MtrrRegisterPair { base: 0, mask: 0 }
        );
    }

    #[test]
    fn mtrr_capture_reports_capacity_excess_without_partial_reads() {
        let reads = Cell::new(0);
        let state = capture_mtrr_registers(true, |index| {
            reads.set(reads.get() + 1);
            if index == 0xfe {
                (MAX_CAPTURED_VARIABLE_MTRRS as u64) + 1
            } else {
                0
            }
        });

        assert_eq!(
            state,
            MtrrState::VariableRangeCapacityExceeded {
                reported_count: (MAX_CAPTURED_VARIABLE_MTRRS + 1) as u8,
            }
        );
        assert_eq!(reads.get(), 1);
    }

    #[test]
    fn mtrr_capture_skips_unsupported_fixed_registers() {
        let reads = Cell::new(0);
        let state = capture_mtrr_registers(true, |index| {
            reads.set(reads.get() + 1);
            match index {
                0xfe => 1,
                0x2ff => 0xc06,
                _ => u64::from(index),
            }
        });

        let MtrrState::Captured(registers) = state else {
            panic!("expected a complete MTRR snapshot");
        };
        assert_eq!(reads.get(), 4);
        assert_eq!(registers.fixed_registers, None);
        assert_eq!(registers.variable_register_count, 1);
        assert_eq!(registers.variable_registers[0].base, 0x200);
        assert_eq!(registers.variable_registers[0].mask, 0x201);
    }

    #[test]
    fn decodes_cr3_root_with_pcid_enabled() {
        let root = parse_cr3_root(0x1234_5000 | 0x0abc, Some(48), true).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(root.physical_address(), 0x1234_5000);
        assert_eq!(root.low_bits(), Cr3LowBits::Pcid(0x0abc));
    }

    #[test]
    fn walks_four_level_tables_and_folds_permissions_and_pat_bits() {
        let root = parse_cr3_root(0x1000, Some(40), false).unwrap();
        let address = 0xffff_8000_0000_1234;
        let mut reader = SyntheticReader::new();
        reader.set(0x1000, 256, 0x2000 | 0b111);
        reader.set(0x2000, 0, 0x3000 | 0b111);
        reader.set(0x3000, 0, 0x4000 | 0b001);
        reader.set(0x4000, 1, 0x8000 | 0b111 | (1 << 3) | (1 << 7));

        let result =
            super::walk_virtual_address(&reader, root, address, four_level_walk_config()).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(
            result,
            PageWalkOutcome::Mapped(PageTranslation {
                physical_address: 0x8234,
                leaf_physical_base: 0x8000,
                page_size: PAGE_SIZE,
                permissions: PagePermissions {
                    writable: false,
                    executable: true,
                    user_accessible: false,
                },
                pat_index: 5,
                raw_leaf_entry: 0x8000 | 0b111 | (1 << 3) | (1 << 7),
            })
        );
    }

    #[test]
    fn walks_five_levels_and_2mib_leaf_pages() {
        let root = parse_cr3_root(0x1000, Some(40), false).unwrap();
        let address = 0xff00_0000_0020_1234;
        let mut reader = SyntheticReader::new();
        reader.set(0x1000, 256, 0x2000 | 0b11);
        reader.set(0x2000, 0, 0x3000 | 0b11);
        reader.set(0x3000, 0, 0x4000 | 0b11);
        reader.set(0x4000, 1, 0x400000 | 0x83 | (1 << 12));
        let config = PageWalkConfig {
            levels: 5,
            virtual_address_bits: 57,
            ..four_level_walk_config()
        };

        assert_eq!(
            super::walk_virtual_address(&reader, root, address, config).unwrap(),
            PageWalkOutcome::Mapped(PageTranslation {
                physical_address: 0x401234,
                leaf_physical_base: 0x400000,
                page_size: 1 << 21,
                permissions: PagePermissions {
                    writable: true,
                    executable: true,
                    user_accessible: false,
                },
                pat_index: 4,
                raw_leaf_entry: 0x400000 | 0x83 | (1 << 12),
            })
        );
    }

    #[test]
    fn walks_a_one_gibibyte_leaf_and_extracts_large_page_pat() {
        let root = parse_cr3_root(0x1000, Some(40), false).unwrap();
        let address = 0xffff_8000_4000_1234;
        let mut reader = SyntheticReader::new();
        reader.set(0x1000, 256, 0x2000 | 0b11);
        reader.set(0x2000, 1, 0x8000_0000 | 0x83 | (1 << 12));

        assert_eq!(
            super::walk_virtual_address(&reader, root, address, four_level_walk_config()).unwrap(),
            PageWalkOutcome::Mapped(PageTranslation {
                physical_address: 0x8000_1234,
                leaf_physical_base: 0x8000_0000,
                page_size: 1 << 30,
                permissions: PagePermissions {
                    writable: true,
                    executable: true,
                    user_accessible: false,
                },
                pat_index: 4,
                raw_leaf_entry: 0x8000_0000 | 0x83 | (1 << 12),
            })
        );

        assert_eq!(
            super::walk_virtual_address(
                &reader,
                root,
                address,
                PageWalkConfig {
                    page_1g_supported: false,
                    ..four_level_walk_config()
                },
            ),
            Err(PageWalkError::InvalidEntry {
                level: PageLevel::Pdpt,
                error: PageTableEntryError::LargePageUnsupported,
            })
        );
    }

    #[test]
    fn rejects_invalid_page_walk_inputs_and_leaf_encodings() {
        let root = parse_cr3_root(0x1000, Some(40), false).unwrap();
        let mut reader = SyntheticReader::new();
        assert_eq!(
            super::walk_virtual_address(
                &reader,
                root,
                0x0000_8000_0000_0000,
                four_level_walk_config(),
            ),
            Err(PageWalkError::NonCanonicalAddress)
        );
        assert_eq!(
            super::walk_virtual_address(
                &reader,
                root,
                0xffff_8000_0000_0000,
                PageWalkConfig {
                    levels: 4,
                    physical_address_bits: 40,
                    virtual_address_bits: 57,
                    ..four_level_walk_config()
                },
            ),
            Err(PageWalkError::InvalidConfiguration)
        );
        reader.set(0x1000, 256, 0x2000 | 0b11 | (1 << 63));
        assert_eq!(
            super::walk_virtual_address(
                &reader,
                root,
                0xffff_8000_0000_0000,
                PageWalkConfig {
                    nx_enabled: false,
                    ..four_level_walk_config()
                }
            ),
            Err(PageWalkError::InvalidEntry {
                level: PageLevel::Pml4,
                error: PageTableEntryError::NxDisabled,
            })
        );
    }

    #[test]
    fn reports_missing_page_table_entries_without_following_them() {
        let root = parse_cr3_root(0x1000, Some(40), false).unwrap();
        let reader = SyntheticReader::new();
        assert_eq!(
            super::walk_virtual_address(
                &reader,
                root,
                0xffff_8000_0000_0000,
                four_level_walk_config(),
            )
            .unwrap(),
            PageWalkOutcome::NotPresent {
                level: PageLevel::Pml4,
            }
        );
    }

    #[test]
    fn validates_inherited_root_hhdm_location_before_any_dereference() {
        let offset = 0xffff_8000_0000_0000;
        let root = parse_cr3_root(0x20_0000, Some(40), false).unwrap();
        let bootloader_map = MemoryMap::from_raw(&[RawMemoryRegion {
            base: 0x20_0000,
            length: PAGE_SIZE,
            kind: 5,
        }])
        .unwrap();

        assert_eq!(
            inherited_cr3_root_hhdm_address(root, &bootloader_map, offset, Some(40), 48),
            Ok(offset + 0x20_0000)
        );
        assert_eq!(
            inherited_cr3_root_hhdm_address(root, &bootloader_map, offset, None, 48),
            Err(Cr3RootAccessError::Hhdm(
                HhdmAddressError::UnknownPhysicalAddressWidth
            ))
        );

        let usable_map = MemoryMap::from_raw(&[RawMemoryRegion {
            base: 0x20_0000,
            length: PAGE_SIZE,
            kind: 0,
        }])
        .unwrap();
        assert_eq!(
            inherited_cr3_root_hhdm_address(root, &usable_map, offset, Some(40), 48),
            Err(Cr3RootAccessError::NotBootloaderReclaimable)
        );
    }

    #[test]
    fn encodes_cr3_values_preserving_low_bit_mode_and_flushing_pcid() {
        assert_eq!(
            encode_cr3_value(
                0x12_3000,
                super::Cr3LowBits::CacheControls {
                    page_level_write_through: true,
                    page_level_cache_disable: true,
                },
                40,
            ),
            Ok(0x12_3018),
        );
        assert_eq!(
            encode_cr3_value(0x12_3000, super::Cr3LowBits::Pcid(0x123), 40),
            Ok(0x12_3123),
        );
        assert_eq!(
            encode_cr3_value(0x12_3001, super::Cr3LowBits::Pcid(0), 40),
            Err(Cr3Error::InvalidRootAddress),
        );
        assert_eq!(
            encode_cr3_value(1 << 40, super::Cr3LowBits::Pcid(0), 40),
            Err(Cr3Error::InvalidRootAddress),
        );
        assert_eq!(
            encode_cr3_value(0x12_3000, super::Cr3LowBits::Pcid(0x1000), 40),
            Err(Cr3Error::ReservedBits),
        );
    }

    #[test]
    fn decodes_cr3_cache_controls_without_pcid() {
        let root = parse_cr3_root(0x1234_5000 | (1 << 3) | (1 << 4), Some(48), false).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(root.physical_address(), 0x1234_5000);
        assert_eq!(
            root.low_bits(),
            Cr3LowBits::CacheControls {
                page_level_write_through: true,
                page_level_cache_disable: true,
            }
        );
    }

    #[test]
    fn rejects_cr3_reserved_bits_and_invalid_address_widths() {
        assert_eq!(
            parse_cr3_root(0x1000 | 1, Some(48), false),
            Err(Cr3Error::ReservedBits)
        );
        assert_eq!(
            parse_cr3_root(1 << 40, Some(40), true),
            Err(Cr3Error::ReservedBits)
        );
        assert_eq!(
            parse_cr3_root(0x1000, None, false),
            Err(Cr3Error::UnknownPhysicalAddressWidth)
        );
        assert_eq!(
            parse_cr3_root(0x1000, Some(53), false),
            Err(Cr3Error::InvalidPhysicalAddressWidth)
        );
    }

    #[test]
    fn resolves_variable_mtrr_ranges_and_default_type() {
        let ranges = [variable_mtrr(
            0x20_0000,
            0x20_0000,
            MtrrMemoryType::WriteBack,
        )];
        let layout =
            MtrrLayout::new(36, true, false, MtrrMemoryType::Uncacheable, None, &ranges).unwrap();

        assert_eq!(
            layout.memory_type_for(0x20_0000),
            Ok(MtrrMemoryType::WriteBack)
        );
        assert_eq!(
            layout.memory_type_for(0x3f_ffff),
            Ok(MtrrMemoryType::WriteBack)
        );
        assert_eq!(
            layout.memory_type_for(0x40_0000),
            Ok(MtrrMemoryType::Uncacheable)
        );
        assert_eq!(
            layout.memory_type_for(1u64 << 36),
            Err(MtrrError::PhysicalAddressOutOfRange)
        );
    }

    #[test]
    fn fixed_mtrrs_override_variable_and_default_ranges_below_one_mib() {
        let mut registers = [0; 11];
        registers[2] = MtrrMemoryType::WriteThrough as u64;
        let fixed = FixedMtrrRanges::from_msr_values(registers).unwrap();
        let variable = [variable_mtrr(0, 0x10_0000, MtrrMemoryType::WriteBack)];
        let layout = MtrrLayout::new(
            36,
            true,
            true,
            MtrrMemoryType::WriteBack,
            Some(&fixed),
            &variable,
        )
        .unwrap();

        assert_eq!(
            layout.memory_type_for(0xa_0000),
            Ok(MtrrMemoryType::WriteThrough)
        );
        assert_eq!(
            layout.memory_type_for(0xa_4000),
            Ok(MtrrMemoryType::Uncacheable)
        );
        assert_eq!(
            layout.memory_type_for(0x10_0000),
            Ok(MtrrMemoryType::WriteBack)
        );
    }

    #[test]
    fn resolves_defined_variable_mtrr_overlaps_and_rejects_undefined_ones() {
        let write_back_through = [
            variable_mtrr(0x20_0000, 0x20_0000, MtrrMemoryType::WriteBack),
            variable_mtrr(0x20_0000, 0x20_0000, MtrrMemoryType::WriteThrough),
        ];
        let layout = MtrrLayout::new(
            36,
            true,
            false,
            MtrrMemoryType::Uncacheable,
            None,
            &write_back_through,
        )
        .unwrap();
        assert_eq!(
            layout.memory_type_for(0x20_0000),
            Ok(MtrrMemoryType::WriteThrough)
        );

        let uncacheable_override = [
            write_back_through[0],
            variable_mtrr(0x20_0000, 0x20_0000, MtrrMemoryType::Uncacheable),
        ];
        let layout = MtrrLayout::new(
            36,
            true,
            false,
            MtrrMemoryType::WriteBack,
            None,
            &uncacheable_override,
        )
        .unwrap();
        assert_eq!(
            layout.memory_type_for(0x20_0000),
            Ok(MtrrMemoryType::Uncacheable)
        );

        let undefined = [
            variable_mtrr(0x20_0000, 0x20_0000, MtrrMemoryType::WriteCombining),
            variable_mtrr(0x20_0000, 0x20_0000, MtrrMemoryType::WriteProtected),
        ];
        let layout =
            MtrrLayout::new(36, true, false, MtrrMemoryType::WriteBack, None, &undefined).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(
            layout.memory_type_for(0x20_0000),
            Err(MtrrError::UndefinedOverlap)
        );
    }

    #[test]
    fn disabled_mtrrs_force_uncacheable_and_bad_registers_are_rejected() {
        let layout =
            MtrrLayout::new(36, false, true, MtrrMemoryType::WriteBack, None, &[]).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(
            layout.memory_type_for(0x20_0000),
            Ok(MtrrMemoryType::Uncacheable)
        );
        assert_eq!(
            MtrrLayout::new(36, true, true, MtrrMemoryType::WriteBack, None, &[]),
            Err(MtrrError::FixedRangesUnavailable)
        );
        assert_eq!(
            VariableMtrr::from_msr_values(0x1000 | 0x200, 0, 36),
            Err(MtrrError::ReservedBaseBits)
        );
        assert_eq!(
            VariableMtrr::from_msr_values(0x1000 | 6, 1 << 10, 36),
            Err(MtrrError::ReservedMaskBits)
        );
        assert_eq!(VariableMtrr::from_msr_values(0x1000 | 6, 0, 36), Ok(None));
        let width_mismatch = [variable_mtrr(
            0x20_0000,
            0x20_0000,
            MtrrMemoryType::WriteBack,
        )];
        assert_eq!(
            MtrrLayout::new(
                35,
                true,
                false,
                MtrrMemoryType::WriteBack,
                None,
                &width_mismatch,
            ),
            Err(MtrrError::PhysicalAddressWidthMismatch)
        );
        assert_eq!(
            VariableMtrr::from_msr_values(0x1000 | 2, 1 << 11, 36),
            Err(MtrrError::ReservedMemoryType { value: 2 })
        );
        let mut invalid_fixed = [0; 11];
        invalid_fixed[0] = 2;
        assert_eq!(
            FixedMtrrRanges::from_msr_values(invalid_fixed),
            Err(MtrrError::ReservedMemoryType { value: 2 })
        );
    }

    #[test]
    fn accepts_aligned_ranges_at_canonical_boundaries() {
        let lower = validate_mapping_range(
            0x0000_7fff_ffff_e000,
            0x1000,
            0x2000,
            KERNEL_READ_ONLY,
            Some(14),
            48,
        )
        .unwrap();
        assert_eq!(
            lower,
            ValidatedMappingRange {
                virtual_start: 0x0000_7fff_ffff_e000,
                virtual_end: 0x0000_8000_0000_0000,
                physical_start: 0x1000,
                physical_end: 0x3000,
                physical_address_bits: 14,
                permissions: KERNEL_READ_ONLY,
            }
        );

        let upper = validate_mapping_range(
            0xffff_8000_0000_0000,
            0,
            PAGE_SIZE,
            KERNEL_READ_ONLY,
            Some(12),
            48,
        )
        .unwrap();
        assert_eq!(upper.virtual_end(), 0xffff_8000_0000_1000);
    }

    #[test]
    fn rejects_empty_and_unaligned_ranges() {
        assert_eq!(
            validate_mapping_range(0x1000, 0x2000, 0, KERNEL_READ_ONLY, Some(32), 48),
            Err(MappingError::EmptyRange)
        );
        assert_eq!(
            validate_mapping_range(0x1001, 0x2000, PAGE_SIZE, KERNEL_READ_ONLY, Some(32), 48),
            Err(MappingError::UnalignedRange)
        );
        assert_eq!(
            validate_mapping_range(
                0x1000,
                0x2000,
                PAGE_SIZE + 1,
                KERNEL_READ_ONLY,
                Some(32),
                48
            ),
            Err(MappingError::UnalignedRange)
        );
    }

    #[test]
    fn requires_known_valid_address_widths_and_bounded_physical_ranges() {
        assert_eq!(
            validate_mapping_range(0x1000, 0x1000, PAGE_SIZE, KERNEL_READ_ONLY, None, 48),
            Err(MappingError::UnknownPhysicalAddressWidth)
        );
        assert_eq!(
            validate_mapping_range(0x1000, 0x1000, PAGE_SIZE, KERNEL_READ_ONLY, Some(0), 48),
            Err(MappingError::InvalidPhysicalAddressWidth)
        );
        assert_eq!(
            validate_mapping_range(0x1000, 0x1000, PAGE_SIZE, KERNEL_READ_ONLY, Some(52), 0),
            Err(MappingError::InvalidVirtualAddressWidth)
        );
        assert_eq!(
            validate_mapping_range(
                0x1000,
                0x1000,
                PAGE_SIZE * 2,
                KERNEL_READ_ONLY,
                Some(13),
                48
            ),
            Err(MappingError::PhysicalRangeOutOfBounds)
        );
    }

    #[test]
    fn rejects_noncanonical_ranges_and_ranges_crossing_the_canonical_hole() {
        assert_eq!(
            validate_mapping_range(
                0x0000_8000_0000_0000,
                0,
                PAGE_SIZE,
                KERNEL_READ_ONLY,
                Some(52),
                48
            ),
            Err(MappingError::NonCanonicalVirtualRange)
        );

        let crosses_hole = (0xffff_8000_0000_1000u64) - 0x0000_7fff_ffff_f000;
        assert_eq!(
            validate_mapping_range(
                0x0000_7fff_ffff_f000,
                0,
                crosses_hole,
                KERNEL_READ_ONLY,
                Some(64),
                48,
            ),
            Err(MappingError::CrossesCanonicalHole)
        );
    }

    fn pat_value(entries: [u8; 8]) -> u64 {
        entries.iter().enumerate().fold(0, |value, (index, entry)| {
            value | ((*entry as u64) << (index * 8))
        })
    }

    #[test]
    fn resolves_cache_policies_from_the_supplied_pat_layout() {
        let pat = pat_value([6, 4, 7, 0, 6, 1, 7, 0]);
        let layout = super::PatLayout::from_msr_value(pat).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(layout.index_for(super::CachePolicy::WriteBack), Some(0));
        assert_eq!(layout.index_for(super::CachePolicy::Uncacheable), Some(3));
        assert_eq!(
            layout.index_for(super::CachePolicy::WriteCombining),
            Some(5)
        );

        let without_write_combining =
            super::PatLayout::from_msr_value(pat_value([6, 4, 7, 0, 6, 4, 7, 0])).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(
            without_write_combining.index_for(super::CachePolicy::WriteCombining),
            None
        );
    }

    #[test]
    fn combines_every_documented_pat_and_mtrr_pair() {
        use EffectiveMemoryType as E;
        use MtrrMemoryType as M;

        let pat = PatLayout::from_msr_value(pat_value([0, 7, 1, 4, 6, 5, 0, 0])).unwrap();
        let rows = [
            (
                M::Uncacheable,
                [
                    E::Uncacheable,
                    E::Uncacheable,
                    E::WriteCombining,
                    E::Uncacheable,
                    E::Uncacheable,
                    E::Uncacheable,
                ],
            ),
            (
                M::WriteCombining,
                [
                    E::Uncacheable,
                    E::WriteCombining,
                    E::WriteCombining,
                    E::Uncacheable,
                    E::WriteCombining,
                    E::Uncacheable,
                ],
            ),
            (
                M::WriteThrough,
                [
                    E::Uncacheable,
                    E::Uncacheable,
                    E::WriteCombining,
                    E::WriteThrough,
                    E::WriteThrough,
                    E::WriteProtected,
                ],
            ),
            (
                M::WriteBack,
                [
                    E::Uncacheable,
                    E::Uncacheable,
                    E::WriteCombining,
                    E::WriteThrough,
                    E::WriteBack,
                    E::WriteProtected,
                ],
            ),
            (
                M::WriteProtected,
                [
                    E::Uncacheable,
                    E::Uncacheable,
                    E::WriteCombining,
                    E::WriteThrough,
                    E::WriteProtected,
                    E::WriteProtected,
                ],
            ),
        ];

        for (mtrr_type, expected) in rows {
            let registers = empty_mtrr_registers(1 << 10, (1 << 11) | mtrr_type as u64);
            let layout = registers.validated_layout(36).unwrap();
            for (pat_index, expected_type) in expected.into_iter().enumerate() {
                assert_eq!(
                    layout.effective_memory_type_for(0x20_0000, pat, pat_index as u8, true),
                    Ok(expected_type),
                    "MTRR={mtrr_type:?}, PAT index={pat_index}"
                );
            }
        }
    }

    #[test]
    fn rejects_invalid_effective_cache_type_inputs() {
        let registers = empty_mtrr_registers(0, (1 << 11) | MtrrMemoryType::WriteBack as u64);
        let layout = registers.validated_layout(36).unwrap();
        let pat = PatLayout::from_msr_value(pat_value([6, 4, 7, 0, 6, 1, 7, 0])).unwrap();

        assert_eq!(
            layout.effective_memory_type_for(0, pat, 8, true),
            Err(EffectiveMemoryTypeError::PatIndexOutOfRange { index: 8 })
        );
        assert_eq!(
            layout.effective_memory_type_for(0, pat, 0, false),
            Err(EffectiveMemoryTypeError::NonNormalCachingMode)
        );
        assert_eq!(
            layout.effective_memory_type_for(1u64 << 36, pat, 0, true),
            Err(EffectiveMemoryTypeError::Mtrr(
                MtrrError::PhysicalAddressOutOfRange
            ))
        );
    }

    #[test]
    fn selects_a_pat_index_that_is_uniform_across_variable_mtrr_segments() {
        let capability = 1 | (1 << 10);
        let mut registers =
            empty_mtrr_registers(capability, (1 << 11) | MtrrMemoryType::WriteBack as u64);
        let physical_mask = ((1u64 << 36) - 1) & !(PAGE_SIZE - 1);
        registers.variable_registers[0] = MtrrRegisterPair {
            base: 0x20_0000 | MtrrMemoryType::WriteThrough as u64,
            mask: (physical_mask & !(0x20_0000 - 1)) | (1 << 11),
        };
        let layout = registers.validated_layout(36).unwrap();
        let pat = PatLayout::from_msr_value(pat_value([6, 0, 1, 4, 6, 1, 7, 0])).unwrap();

        assert_eq!(
            layout.select_pat_index_for_range(
                0x1f_f000,
                PAGE_SIZE * 2,
                pat,
                EffectiveMemoryType::WriteCombining,
                true,
            ),
            Ok(2)
        );
    }

    #[test]
    fn rejects_range_when_fixed_mtrrs_prevent_one_uniform_pat_index() {
        let mut registers = empty_mtrr_registers(
            1 << 8,
            (1 << 11) | (1 << 10) | MtrrMemoryType::WriteBack as u64,
        );
        registers.fixed_registers.as_mut().unwrap()[0] = MtrrMemoryType::WriteBack as u64;
        let layout = registers.validated_layout(36).unwrap();
        let pat = PatLayout::from_msr_value(pat_value([6, 0, 1, 4, 6, 1, 7, 0])).unwrap();

        assert_eq!(
            layout.select_pat_index_for_range(
                0,
                0x20_000,
                pat,
                EffectiveMemoryType::WriteBack,
                true,
            ),
            Err(EffectiveMemoryTypeError::NoUniformPatIndex {
                requested: EffectiveMemoryType::WriteBack,
            })
        );
    }

    #[test]
    fn rejects_invalid_effective_cache_type_ranges() {
        let registers = empty_mtrr_registers(0, (1 << 11) | MtrrMemoryType::WriteBack as u64);
        let layout = registers.validated_layout(36).unwrap();
        let pat = PatLayout::from_msr_value(pat_value([6, 0, 1, 4, 6, 1, 7, 0])).unwrap();
        let requested = EffectiveMemoryType::WriteBack;

        assert_eq!(
            layout.select_pat_index_for_range(0, 0, pat, requested, true),
            Err(EffectiveMemoryTypeError::EmptyRange)
        );
        assert_eq!(
            layout.select_pat_index_for_range(1, PAGE_SIZE, pat, requested, true),
            Err(EffectiveMemoryTypeError::UnalignedRange)
        );
        assert_eq!(
            layout.select_pat_index_for_range(
                u64::MAX & !(PAGE_SIZE - 1),
                PAGE_SIZE,
                pat,
                requested,
                true,
            ),
            Err(EffectiveMemoryTypeError::AddressOverflow)
        );
        assert_eq!(
            layout.select_pat_index_for_range(1 << 36, PAGE_SIZE, pat, requested, true),
            Err(EffectiveMemoryTypeError::Mtrr(
                MtrrError::PhysicalAddressOutOfRange
            ))
        );
        assert_eq!(
            layout.select_pat_index_for_range(0, PAGE_SIZE, pat, requested, false),
            Err(EffectiveMemoryTypeError::NonNormalCachingMode)
        );
    }

    #[test]
    fn validates_captured_mtrr_snapshot_before_resolution() {
        let registers = empty_mtrr_registers(
            (1 << 12) | (1 << 10) | (1 << 8) | 1,
            (1 << 11) | (1 << 10) | MtrrMemoryType::WriteBack as u64,
        );
        let layout = registers.validated_layout(36).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(layout.memory_type_for(0), Ok(MtrrMemoryType::WriteBack));
        assert_eq!(
            layout.memory_type_for(0x10_0000),
            Ok(MtrrMemoryType::WriteBack)
        );

        let mut invalid = empty_mtrr_registers(0, 1 << 11);
        invalid.capability |= 1 << 9;
        assert_eq!(
            invalid.validated_layout(36),
            Err(MtrrError::ReservedCapabilityBits)
        );

        let mut invalid = empty_mtrr_registers(0, 1 << 11);
        invalid.capability |= 1 << 13;
        assert_eq!(
            invalid.validated_layout(36),
            Err(MtrrError::ReservedCapabilityBits)
        );

        let mut invalid = empty_mtrr_registers(0, 1 << 11);
        invalid.default_type |= 1 << 12;
        assert_eq!(
            invalid.validated_layout(36),
            Err(MtrrError::ReservedDefaultTypeBits)
        );

        let mut invalid = empty_mtrr_registers(0, 1 << 11);
        invalid.variable_register_count = 1;
        assert_eq!(
            invalid.validated_layout(36),
            Err(MtrrError::VariableRegisterCountMismatch)
        );

        let mut invalid = empty_mtrr_registers(1 << 8, 1 << 11);
        invalid.fixed_registers = None;
        assert_eq!(
            invalid.validated_layout(36),
            Err(MtrrError::FixedRegisterSupportMismatch)
        );

        let invalid = empty_mtrr_registers(0, (1 << 11) | MtrrMemoryType::WriteCombining as u64);
        assert_eq!(
            invalid.validated_layout(36),
            Err(MtrrError::WriteCombiningUnsupported)
        );

        let mut invalid = empty_mtrr_registers(1 << 8, (1 << 11) | 6);
        invalid.fixed_registers.as_mut().unwrap()[0] =
            MtrrMemoryType::WriteCombining as u64 * 0x0101_0101_0101_0101;
        assert_eq!(
            invalid.validated_layout(36),
            Err(MtrrError::WriteCombiningUnsupported)
        );

        let mut invalid = empty_mtrr_registers(1, (1 << 11) | 6);
        let physical_mask = ((1u64 << 36) - 1) & !(PAGE_SIZE - 1);
        invalid.variable_registers[0] = MtrrRegisterPair {
            base: 0x20_0000 | MtrrMemoryType::WriteCombining as u64,
            mask: (physical_mask & !(0x20_0000 - 1)) | (1 << 11),
        };
        assert_eq!(
            invalid.validated_layout(36),
            Err(MtrrError::WriteCombiningUnsupported)
        );

        let invalid = empty_mtrr_registers(0, (1 << 11) | (1 << 10));
        assert_eq!(
            invalid.validated_layout(36),
            Err(MtrrError::FixedRangesUnavailable)
        );

        let mut invalid = empty_mtrr_registers(1, 1 << 11);
        let physical_mask = ((1u64 << 36) - 1) & !(PAGE_SIZE - 1);
        invalid.variable_registers[0] = MtrrRegisterPair {
            base: MtrrMemoryType::WriteBack as u64,
            mask: (physical_mask ^ (1 << 13)) | (1 << 11),
        };
        assert_eq!(
            invalid.validated_layout(36),
            Err(MtrrError::UnsupportedDiscontinuousVariableMask)
        );
    }

    #[test]
    fn rejects_misaligned_variable_mtrr_bases() {
        let physical_address_bits = 36;
        let physical_mask = ((1u64 << physical_address_bits) - 1) & !(PAGE_SIZE - 1);
        let mask = physical_mask & !(0x2000 - 1) | (1 << 11);
        assert_eq!(
            VariableMtrr::from_msr_values(
                0x1000 | MtrrMemoryType::WriteBack as u64,
                mask,
                physical_address_bits,
            ),
            Err(MtrrError::MisalignedVariableBase)
        );
    }

    #[test]
    fn rejects_reserved_pat_entries() {
        assert_eq!(
            super::PatLayout::from_msr_value(0x08),
            Err(super::PatLayoutError::ReservedBits { index: 0 })
        );
        assert_eq!(
            super::PatLayout::from_msr_value(0b010 << 24),
            Err(super::PatLayoutError::ReservedMemoryType {
                index: 3,
                value: 0b010,
            })
        );
    }

    #[test]
    fn selects_uniform_cache_attributes_for_a_mapping_range_and_encodes_each_leaf() {
        let capability = 1 | (1 << 10);
        let mut registers =
            empty_mtrr_registers(capability, (1 << 11) | MtrrMemoryType::WriteBack as u64);
        let physical_mask = ((1u64 << 36) - 1) & !(PAGE_SIZE - 1);
        registers.variable_registers[0] = MtrrRegisterPair {
            base: 0x20_0000 | MtrrMemoryType::WriteThrough as u64,
            mask: (physical_mask & !(0x20_0000 - 1)) | (1 << 11),
        };
        let mtrrs = registers.validated_layout(36).unwrap();
        let pat = PatLayout::from_msr_value(pat_value([6, 0, 1, 4, 6, 1, 7, 0])).unwrap();
        let mapping = validate_mapping_range(
            0x4000,
            0x1f_f000,
            PAGE_SIZE * 2,
            KERNEL_READ_ONLY,
            Some(36),
            48,
        )
        .unwrap();
        let attributes = mapping
            .select_cache_attributes(CachePolicy::WriteCombining, pat, &mtrrs, true)
            .unwrap();

        assert_eq!(attributes.physical_start(), 0x1f_f000);
        assert_eq!(attributes.physical_end(), 0x20_1000);
        assert_eq!(attributes.pat_index(), 2);
        assert_eq!(
            attributes.effective_type(),
            EffectiveMemoryType::WriteCombining
        );
        for offset in [0, PAGE_SIZE] {
            assert_eq!(
                mapping
                    .leaf_4k_entry_with_cache_attributes(offset, attributes, true)
                    .unwrap()
                    .bits()
                    & ((1 << 3) | (1 << 4) | (1 << 7)),
                1 << 4
            );
        }

        let other_mapping = validate_mapping_range(
            0x8000,
            0x30_0000,
            PAGE_SIZE * 2,
            KERNEL_READ_ONLY,
            Some(36),
            48,
        )
        .unwrap();
        assert_eq!(
            other_mapping.leaf_4k_entry_with_cache_attributes(0, attributes, true),
            Err(MappingError::CacheAttributesRangeMismatch)
        );
    }

    #[test]
    fn rejects_cache_attribute_selection_when_physical_widths_disagree() {
        let registers = empty_mtrr_registers(0, (1 << 11) | MtrrMemoryType::WriteBack as u64);
        let mtrrs = registers.validated_layout(36).unwrap();
        let pat = PatLayout::from_msr_value(pat_value([6, 0, 1, 4, 6, 1, 7, 0])).unwrap();
        let mapping =
            validate_mapping_range(0x4000, 0x20_0000, PAGE_SIZE, KERNEL_READ_ONLY, Some(37), 48)
                .unwrap();

        assert_eq!(
            mapping.select_cache_attributes(CachePolicy::WriteBack, pat, &mtrrs, true),
            Err(MappingError::MtrrPhysicalAddressWidthMismatch)
        );
    }

    #[test]
    fn encodes_4k_leaf_permissions_nx_and_pat_index_bits() {
        let writable_user_page = PagePermissions {
            writable: true,
            executable: false,
            user_accessible: true,
        };
        let mapping = validate_mapping_range(
            0x4000,
            0x20_0000,
            PAGE_SIZE * 2,
            writable_user_page,
            Some(52),
            48,
        )
        .unwrap();

        let first = mapping.leaf_4k_entry(0, 0b101, true).unwrap().bits();
        assert_eq!(
            first,
            0x20_0000 | (1 << 0) | (1 << 1) | (1 << 2) | (1 << 3) | (1 << 7) | (1 << 63)
        );
        let second = mapping
            .leaf_4k_entry(PAGE_SIZE, 0b101, true)
            .unwrap()
            .bits();
        assert_eq!(second & 0x000f_ffff_ffff_f000, 0x20_1000);
        assert_eq!(second & (1 << 63), 1 << 63);

        let all_pat_bits = mapping.leaf_4k_entry(0, 0b111, true).unwrap().bits()
            & ((1 << 3) | (1 << 4) | (1 << 7));
        assert_eq!(all_pat_bits, (1 << 3) | (1 << 4) | (1 << 7));
    }

    #[test]
    fn rejects_unencodable_leaf_attributes_and_page_offsets() {
        let mapping =
            validate_mapping_range(0x4000, 0x20_0000, PAGE_SIZE, KERNEL_READ_ONLY, Some(52), 48)
                .unwrap();
        assert_eq!(
            mapping.leaf_4k_entry(0, 8, true),
            Err(MappingError::InvalidPatIndex)
        );
        assert_eq!(
            mapping.leaf_4k_entry(0, 0, false),
            Err(MappingError::NxNotEnabled)
        );
        assert_eq!(
            mapping.leaf_4k_entry(1, 0, true),
            Err(MappingError::UnalignedPageOffset)
        );
        assert_eq!(
            mapping.leaf_4k_entry(PAGE_SIZE, 0, true),
            Err(MappingError::PageOffsetOutOfRange)
        );

        let too_wide =
            validate_mapping_range(0x4000, 0x20_0000, PAGE_SIZE, KERNEL_READ_ONLY, Some(53), 48)
                .unwrap();
        assert_eq!(
            too_wide.leaf_4k_entry(0, 0, true),
            Err(MappingError::InvalidPhysicalAddressWidth)
        );
    }

    #[test]

        let entry = mapping.leaf_4k_entry(0, 0, false).unwrap().bits();

    #[test]
    fn candidate_page_tables_reject_root_frames_outside_the_configured_width() {
        let high_address = 1u64 << 40;
        let map = MemoryMap::from_raw(&[RawMemoryRegion {
            base: high_address,
            length: PAGE_SIZE,
            kind: 0,
        }])
        .unwrap();
        let mut allocator = FrameAllocator::from_memory_map(&map).unwrap();
        let mut memory = CandidateTestMemory::new();
        let failure =
            match CandidatePageTables::new(&mut allocator, &mut memory, four_level_walk_config()) {
                Err(error) => error,
                Ok(_) => panic!("candidate creation accepted an out-of-range root frame"),
            };
        assert_eq!(failure.cause, CandidateCreateErrorKind::RootFrameOutOfRange);
        let frame = failure
            .frame
            .expect("root token is returned on validation failure");
        assert_eq!(frame.address(), high_address);
        allocator.deallocate(frame).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(allocator.free_frames(), 1);
    }

    #[test]
    fn candidate_mapping_rejects_out_of_width_table_frames_transactionally() {
        let high_address = 1u64 << 40;
        let map = MemoryMap::from_raw(&[
            RawMemoryRegion {
                base: 0x10_0000,
                length: PAGE_SIZE,
                kind: 0,
            },
            RawMemoryRegion {
                base: 0x10_1000,
                length: PAGE_SIZE,
                kind: 0,
            },
            RawMemoryRegion {
                base: high_address,
                length: PAGE_SIZE,
                kind: 0,
            },
        ])
        .unwrap();
        let mut allocator = FrameAllocator::from_memory_map(&map).unwrap();
        let mut memory = CandidateTestMemory::new();
        let mut candidate =
            CandidatePageTables::new(&mut allocator, &mut memory, four_level_walk_config())
                .unwrap();
        let frame = allocator.allocate().unwrap();
        assert_eq!(frame.address(), 0x10_1000);
        let (mapping, attributes) = candidate_mapping(
            &frame,
            0xffff_9000_0000_1000,
            PagePermissions {
                writable: false,
                executable: false,
                user_accessible: false,
            },
        );
        let free_before_map = allocator.free_frames();

        let failure = candidate
            .map_owned_page(&mut allocator, frame, mapping, attributes)
            .unwrap_err();
        assert_eq!(failure.cause, CandidateMapErrorKind::TableFrameOutOfRange);
        assert_eq!(failure.rollback_retained_table_frames, 0);
        assert_eq!(candidate.table_count(), 1);
        assert_eq!(candidate.mapping_count(), 0);
        assert_eq!(allocator.free_frames(), free_before_map);
        allocator.deallocate(failure.frame).unwrap();
        candidate.release(&mut allocator).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(allocator.free_frames(), 3);
    }

    #[test]
    fn candidate_walk_rejects_intermediate_tables_without_owned_tokens() {
        let mut allocator = candidate_allocator(2);
        let foreign_frame = allocator.allocate().unwrap();
        let virtual_address = 0xffff_9000_0000_1000;
        let root_index = super::page_table_indexes(virtual_address, 4)[0];
        let mut memory = CandidateTestMemory::new();
        memory.foreign_child = Some((root_index, foreign_frame.address()));
        let candidate =
            CandidatePageTables::new(&mut allocator, &mut memory, four_level_walk_config())
                .unwrap();

        assert_eq!(
            candidate.walk(virtual_address),
            Err(PageWalkError::Reader(
                CandidatePageTableReadError::UnownedTable
            ))
        );
        candidate.release(&mut allocator).unwrap();
        allocator.deallocate(foreign_frame).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(allocator.free_frames(), 2);
    }

    #[test]
    fn candidate_release_failure_retains_owned_frames_for_retry() {
        const TOTAL_FRAMES: usize = 513;
        let mut allocator = candidate_allocator(TOTAL_FRAMES);
        let mut memory = CandidateTestMemory::new();
        let candidate =
            CandidatePageTables::new(&mut allocator, &mut memory, four_level_walk_config())
                .unwrap();
        let mut remaining_frames: [Option<Frame>; TOTAL_FRAMES - 1] =
            core::array::from_fn(|_| Some(allocator.allocate().unwrap()));
        for index in (1..remaining_frames.len()).step_by(2) {
            allocator
                .deallocate(remaining_frames[index].take().unwrap())
                .unwrap();
        }

        let failure = match candidate.release(&mut allocator) {
            Err(failure) => failure,
            Ok(()) => panic!("release unexpectedly fit a full range table"),
        };
        assert_eq!(
            failure.error,
            CandidateReleaseError::Frame(FrameError::RangeTableFull)
        );
        assert_eq!(failure.candidate.table_count(), 1);
        assert_eq!(failure.candidate.mapping_count(), 0);

        allocator
            .deallocate(remaining_frames[0].take().unwrap())
            .unwrap();
        failure.candidate.release(&mut allocator).unwrap();
        for frame in remaining_frames.into_iter().flatten() {
            allocator.deallocate(frame).unwrap();
        }
        assert_eq!(allocator.free_frames(), TOTAL_FRAMES as u64);
    }

    #[test]
    fn active_candidate_rejects_mutation_and_release_until_deactivated() {
        let mut allocator = candidate_allocator(4);
        let mut memory = CandidateTestMemory::new();
        let mut candidate =
            CandidatePageTables::new(&mut allocator, &mut memory, four_level_walk_config())
                .unwrap();
        let root = candidate.root_physical_address();
        // SAFETY: This is a synthetic test of the active-state guard; no CPU
        // actually uses the test candidate's root.
        unsafe { candidate.mark_active() };
        assert!(candidate.is_active());
        assert!(matches!(
            candidate.unmap_owned_page(0xffff_9000_0000_1000),
            Err(CandidateUnmapError::Active)
        ));

        let failure = candidate.release(&mut allocator).unwrap_err();
        assert_eq!(failure.error, CandidateReleaseError::ActiveRoot);
        let mut candidate = failure.candidate;
        assert_eq!(candidate.root_physical_address(), root);
        // SAFETY: The synthetic test never installed this root in CR3.
        unsafe { candidate.mark_inactive() };
        candidate.release(&mut allocator).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(allocator.free_frames(), 4);
    }

        reader.set(0x9000, indexes[1], 0xa000 | 0x3);
        reader.set(0xa000, indexes[2], 0xb000 | 0x3);

    #[test]
    fn inherited_large_page_permission_change_splits_and_preserves_cache_type() {
        let total_frames = 16;
        let mut allocator = candidate_allocator(total_frames);
        let mut memory = CandidateTestMemory::new();
        let mut candidate =
            CandidatePageTables::new(&mut allocator, &mut memory, four_level_walk_config())
                .unwrap();
        let virtual_address = 0xffff_9000_0000_1000;
        let indexes = super::page_table_indexes(virtual_address, 4);
        let source_root = 0x8000;
        let mut reader = SyntheticReader::new();
        reader.set(source_root, indexes[0], 0x9000 | 0x3);
        reader.set(0x9000, indexes[1], 0xa000 | 0x3);
        reader.set(0xa000, indexes[2], 0x20_0000 | 0x3 | (1 << 7) | (1 << 12));
        let root = parse_cr3_root(source_root, Some(40), false).unwrap();
        candidate
            .clone_inherited_hierarchy(&mut allocator, &reader, root)
            .unwrap();

        candidate
            .set_inherited_page_permissions(
                &mut allocator,
                virtual_address,
                0x20_1000,
                PagePermissions {
                    writable: false,
                    executable: false,
                    user_accessible: false,
                },
            )
            .unwrap();
        let protected = match candidate.walk(virtual_address).unwrap() {
            PageWalkOutcome::Mapped(translation) => translation,
            PageWalkOutcome::NotPresent { .. } => panic!("split mapping disappeared"),
        };
        assert_eq!(protected.physical_address, 0x20_1000);
        assert_eq!(protected.page_size, PAGE_SIZE);
        assert_eq!(
            protected.permissions,
            PagePermissions {
                writable: false,
                executable: false,
                user_accessible: false,
            }
        );
        assert_eq!(protected.pat_index, 4);

        let neighbor = match candidate.walk(virtual_address + PAGE_SIZE).unwrap() {
            PageWalkOutcome::Mapped(translation) => translation,
            PageWalkOutcome::NotPresent { .. } => panic!("neighbor mapping disappeared"),
        };
        assert_eq!(neighbor.physical_address, 0x20_2000);
        assert_eq!(neighbor.page_size, PAGE_SIZE);
        assert_eq!(neighbor.permissions.writable, true);
        assert_eq!(neighbor.permissions.executable, true);
        assert_eq!(neighbor.pat_index, 4);

        candidate.release(&mut allocator).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(allocator.free_frames(), total_frames as u64);
    }

    #[test]
    fn candidate_page_tables_map_unmap_and_release_owned_frames() {
        let total_frames = 8;
        let mut allocator = candidate_allocator(total_frames);
        let mut memory = CandidateTestMemory::new();
        let mut candidate =
            CandidatePageTables::new(&mut allocator, &mut memory, four_level_walk_config())
                .unwrap();
        let root = candidate.root_physical_address().unwrap();
        assert_eq!(candidate.root_physical_address(), Some(root));
        let frame = allocator.allocate().unwrap();
        let physical = frame.address();
        let virtual_address = 0xffff_9000_0000_1000;
        let permissions = PagePermissions {
            writable: true,
            executable: false,
            user_accessible: true,
        };
        let (mapping, attributes) = candidate_mapping(&frame, virtual_address, permissions);

        candidate
            .map_owned_page(&mut allocator, frame, mapping, attributes)
            .unwrap();
        assert_eq!(candidate.table_count(), 4);
        assert_eq!(candidate.mapping_count(), 1);

        assert_eq!(
            candidate.walk(virtual_address).unwrap(),
            PageWalkOutcome::Mapped(PageTranslation {
                physical_address: physical,
                leaf_physical_base: physical,
                page_size: PAGE_SIZE,
                permissions,
                pat_index: 0,
                raw_leaf_entry: physical | 0x3 | (1 << 2) | (1 << 63),
            })
        );

        let duplicate_frame = allocator.allocate().unwrap();
        let (duplicate_mapping, duplicate_attributes) =
            candidate_mapping(&duplicate_frame, virtual_address, permissions);
        let free_before_duplicate = allocator.free_frames();
        let failure = candidate
            .map_owned_page(
                &mut allocator,
                duplicate_frame,
                duplicate_mapping,
                duplicate_attributes,
            )
            .unwrap_err();
        assert_eq!(failure.cause, CandidateMapErrorKind::MappingAlreadyPresent);
        assert_eq!(candidate.mapping_count(), 1);
        assert_eq!(allocator.free_frames(), free_before_duplicate);
        allocator.deallocate(failure.frame).unwrap();

        let returned = candidate.unmap_owned_page(virtual_address).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(returned.address(), physical);
        assert_eq!(candidate.mapping_count(), 0);
        assert_eq!(
            candidate.walk(virtual_address).unwrap(),
            PageWalkOutcome::NotPresent {
                level: PageLevel::Pt,
            }
        );
        allocator.deallocate(returned).unwrap();
        candidate.release(&mut allocator).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(allocator.free_frames(), total_frames as u64);
    }

    #[test]
    fn rejects_arithmetic_overflow_and_writable_executable_ranges() {
        assert_eq!(
            validate_mapping_range(
                u64::MAX - (PAGE_SIZE - 1),
                0,
                PAGE_SIZE,
                KERNEL_READ_ONLY,
                Some(64),
                64
            ),
            Err(MappingError::AddressOverflow)
        );
        assert_eq!(
            validate_mapping_range(
                0x1000,
                u64::MAX - (PAGE_SIZE - 1),
                PAGE_SIZE,
                KERNEL_READ_ONLY,
                Some(64),
                64
            ),
            Err(MappingError::AddressOverflow)
        );

        let writable_executable = PagePermissions {
            writable: true,
            executable: true,
            user_accessible: false,
        };
        assert_eq!(
            validate_mapping_range(0x1000, 0x2000, PAGE_SIZE, writable_executable, Some(52), 48),
            Err(MappingError::WritableExecutable)
        );
    }
}

# Memory-management direction

## What exists now

`src/memory.rs` contains an allocation-free `MemoryMapBuilder` that copies Limine ranges into validated half-open physical regions. It rejects empty ranges, `base + length` overflow, overlapping ranges, empty maps, and maps exceeding the fixed 256-region capacity. Known Limine types remain distinct, and unknown type values are preserved. Host-side tests cover range validation/classification, canonical-address boundaries, physical-width bounds, and HHDM range arithmetic. `src/boot.rs` stores the resulting map in an owned boot snapshot and reports usable bytes.

`src/frame.rs` provides a fixed-capacity allocator core with host-side tests. It only manages complete 4 KiB frames inside validated `Usable` regions, reserves the first MiB, and coalesces adjacent free ranges. The ownership contract assumes one allocator instance per physical map: within that instance, each eligible frame is owned either by its free-range table or by a non-copyable `Frame` token while allocated. The public constructor does not enforce unique instances, so callers must not initialize multiple allocators for the same physical map; the boot path retains one allocator in `BootInfo`. `allocate` returns `None` when no free frame remains. `deallocate` consumes the token only on success; on any error, including free-range-table exhaustion, it returns a `DeallocationError` containing the original token and leaves allocator state unchanged. The range tables each have a fixed `MAX_FRAME_RANGES` capacity, so fragmentation can prevent a frame from being returned until nearby ranges coalesce. The active cloned page-table hierarchy owns its page-table frames; the frame allocator is otherwise not yet a general-purpose virtual-memory service.

`Frame::address()` is a physical address value, not a dereferenceable pointer and not a proof that the frame is mapped. CPU diagnostics now read `CR4.LA57` to report the active linear-address width (48 or 57 bits) and query `CPUID.80000008H` for physical and maximum linear-address widths when available. Boot-protocol pointers are checked against the active width, with host tests for 48- and 57-bit canonical boundaries. These facts do not prove that any physical address is mapped.

`src/paging.rs` contains host-tested mapping and cache policy plus a bounded candidate-root builder. The CR3 decoder validates physical-address width and reserved bits and interprets its low 12 bits according to active `CR4.PCIDE`; it does not dereference the root. The mapping-range validator requires known physical width, checked aligned bounds, canonical virtual endpoints in one canonical half, and rejects writable-executable permissions. It can encode one 4 KiB leaf PTE with supervisor/user and write permissions, NX when EFER.NXE is confirmed, and a bounded PAT index. `PatLayout` parses supplied `IA32_PAT` values and selects WB, UC, or WC indexes. `MtrrMemoryType`, `VariableMtrr`, `FixedMtrrRanges`, and `MtrrLayout` resolve address-specific MTRR types, including fixed-range priority and defined variable-overlap rules; undefined overlaps fail closed. `MtrrRegisters::validated_layout` validates captured capability/default-type bits, register counts and fixed-range presence, WC support, and variable-mask shape/alignment before producing an owned layout. Rustix supports contiguous power-of-two variable masks and explicitly rejects unsupported discontinuous masks. The layout combines address-specific MTRR type and PAT selection according to Intel SDM Table 11-7 only when `CR0.CD` and `CR0.NW` are clear. Host tests cover all 30 documented MTRR/PAT pairs and malformed inputs. A pure range selector chooses an index only when its effective type is uniform throughout all fixed/variable MTRR boundaries in an aligned extent; selected attributes remain bound to that physical extent. The selector itself does not inspect PTEs, aliases, or frame ownership. Boot reads CR0 without modifying it, validates captured MTRR/PAT state, and reports a diagnostic PA 0 resolution; this does not assert the live PTE's type. MTRR capture is bounded to 32 variable pairs and rejects excess capacity without partial state.

`CandidatePageTables` owns a separate root, bounded to 32 table frames and 256 explicitly mapped leaf frames. It accepts only allocator-issued `Frame` tokens, requires NXE, supports four- and five-level paths, and holds one exclusive mutable borrow of its unsafe memory backend so prepared handles cannot be mixed across backends. The default boot path clones the complete reachable Limine hierarchy, rewrites inherited kernel HHDM aliases to text/rodata R/NX and data RW/NX while preserving PAT bits, verifies critical translations, activates the cloned CR3, and retains the candidate tokens for the active root's lifetime. Active candidates reject mapping, unmapping, and release; the type never writes CR3. Host tests cover clone ownership, huge-page splitting, cache-bit preservation, mutation guards, transactional map rollback, and retryable release failure. The QEMU adapter derives table pointers only from complete allocator-owned `Usable` frames through checked HHDM arithmetic.

The opt-in `just frame-smoke` probe reads the inherited root and follows paths for every page in kernel text/rodata/data and the requested stack span. The transition clones every reachable present table and preserves leaf mappings, then rewrites and validates the kernel-image HHDM aliases. The kernel and HHDM aliases retain the same PAT index; MTRR state is unchanged. This is not a fresh address-space policy or a hardware-level exhaustive inventory, and it does not reclaim the inherited root or bootloader memory.

The effective-type resolver follows [Intel SDM Vol. 3A §11.5.2.2, Table 11-7](https://cdrdv2-public.intel.com/671447/325384-sdm-vol-3abcd.pdf), which applies when normal caching is enabled (`CR0.CD=0`, `CR0.NW=0`). Its footnotes distinguish UC selected by an MTRR from UC selected by a page-table entry (the latter involves cache snooping and aliasing concerns); they also identify combinations that older manual editions called undefined but current processors supporting both PAT and MTRRs resolve as shown. The resolver does not cover legacy PCD/PWT-only selection or model-specific combinations outside that table.

The requested Limine base revision is 3. Its protocol maps only `Usable`, `BootloaderReclaimable`, `ExecutableAndModules`, and `Framebuffer` memory-map regions into the HHDM; reserved, ACPI, bad, and unknown regions are not in that mapping set. HHDM mappings use at least 4 KiB granularity and may cover page-aligned bytes beyond unaligned region boundaries. Limine's inherited HHDM mappings are supervisor RWX, normally write-back cached, with framebuffer mappings write-combining when PAT is available. Before activating the cloned root, Rustix splits inherited huge pages where needed and changes the kernel image HHDM aliases to the matching R/NX or RW/NX policy while retaining PAT bits. The rest of the HHDM remains inherited; an HHDM offset is not a blanket physical-memory access grant. See the [Limine base revision 3 protocol](https://github.com/limine-bootloader/limine-protocol/blob/trunk/PROTOCOL.md#base-revision-3) and its memory-layout/caching sections.

The boot snapshot now rejects physical map ranges beyond the reported CPUID physical-address width when that CPUID leaf is available. For base revision 3 HHDM-mapped types, it also validates the page-rounded physical span, checked `offset + address` arithmetic, and canonical endpoints in the active linear-address width. If the CPU does not report a physical width, the physical-bound check is skipped and no mapping caller may treat the bound as known. These checks are derived from metadata and Limine's protocol contract; they do not inspect page tables or prove that a non-null loader pointer is readable. HHDM dereferences are limited to the opt-in QEMU frame probe and candidate-table backend. Both first validate a complete allocator-owned `Usable` frame and its checked HHDM address, then rely narrowly on Limine's base-revision-3 guarantee; this is not a general physical-memory access service. Rustix-owned mappings should be non-executable by default; executable kernel text must be explicit. MMIO requires an explicit device range and cache policy, and guard regions must remain unmapped. A page-table transition must preserve the kernel image, active stacks, boot data, descriptor tables, and any loader mappings still needed. Rustix does not reclaim bootloader memory or provide a general-purpose physical-memory service. It owns the page-table frames of the active cloned hierarchy but leaves inherited leaf frames and the old root unreclaimed. The initial 256 KiB global heap is a bounded BSS arena and does not grow from physical frames. Bootstrap GDT/TSS/IDT setup and fatal exception diagnostics live in `src/arch/x86_64/interrupts.rs`; they do not enable maskable IRQs.

## Mapping inventory before a CR3 transition

The current runtime has several mappings that a future page-table transition must preserve. The address sources and remaining gaps are:

- **Kernel ELF image:** `linker.ld` places `.text`, `.rodata`, `.limine_requests`, `.data`, `.bss`, and `.got` in three `PT_LOAD` segments: RX text, read-only rodata, and RW data/BSS. It exports `__kernel_start` and `__kernel_end` around the complete loadable image, plus page-aligned bounds for each segment. `BootInfo` checks that Limine's reported virtual base matches the linker start, validates ordered contiguous segment bounds covering the rounded image, derives corresponding half-open physical ranges from the executable physical base with checked arithmetic, and validates canonical virtual and reported physical address widths. The release ELF and QEMU runtime report both showed the three aligned ranges on 2026-10-21. The RX, R/NX, and RW/NX labels describe the linker segment intent; these are linker/boot metadata, not proof that the inherited page tables map every page or enforce those permissions, nor proof that loader pointers are readable. The memory-map `ExecutableAndModules` entries remain illustrative, not an authoritative kernel-image extent.
- **Active stack and `BootInfo`:** The assembly `_start` shim captures Limine's entry `RSP` before any Rust prologue. Under the SysV entry convention the synthetic return slot occupies 8 bytes, so `RSP + 8` is the exclusive stack top. The protocol guarantees at least 64 KiB (without a Stack Size request); `BootInfo` records that minimum virtual span, translates it through the HHDM, and requires it to fit within a single `BootloaderReclaimable` physical region. The full loader allocation may be larger, and neither its exact bounds nor a guard page are known. Preserve the inherited mapping; do not infer a guard page.
- **Kernel static data:** `RAM_FILESYSTEM`, GDT, IDT, TSS, the ring-0 stack, and double-fault IST stack are static BSS/data in the kernel image. Exception entry also requires the handler code and the TSS/IDT references to remain mapped. Preserve the complete relevant data/BSS pages and stack pages.
- **Limine request data:** request records are in the kernel's writable `.limine_requests` segment. Response objects and the memory-map pointer array are bootloader-reclaimable; `capture_boot_information` copies the values used later, and the shell does not retain those pointers. Keep them mapped until the copy and validation finish; any later reclaim must be explicit rather than reclaiming the whole bootloader-reclaimable class.
- **Inherited page tables:** Limine places its page tables in bootloader-reclaimable memory, but their layout is unspecified. `BootInfo` captures raw CR3 and validates a decoded physical root address plus the low-bit interpretation selected by active `CR4.PCIDE`. A pure helper requires the root page to fit in one validated `BootloaderReclaimable` range and calculates its HHDM address when the physical width is known. The opt-in QEMU probe reads the root's 512 entries and counts present bits, then follows bounded paths for every page in the kernel text/rodata/data and minimum boot-stack spans, checking physical translations. It also compares effective PAT/MTRR types for each kernel-image page and its HHDM alias. It does not enumerate unrelated mappings or prove that inherited permissions match the linker policy. Keep the old root and its backing pages intact while inspecting/building a replacement; do not reclaim them until a verified switch no longer depends on them.
- **Devices:** COM1 uses x86 port I/O and needs no MMIO virtual mapping. Rustix does not currently request or use a framebuffer. Any future framebuffer or device-register mapping needs an explicit physical range and cache policy.

## Initial kernel-owned mapping policy (design only)

A first Rustix-owned x86_64 root should use 4 KiB pages only and require NX support; if NX is unavailable, abort before switching. Preserve ELF permissions exactly: text RX, rodata R/NX, and `.limine_requests`/data/BSS/GOT RW/NX. Reject W+X mappings. Exclude the complete physical kernel-image span from the generic HHDM in the first implementation so no writable direct-map alias can undermine text or rodata permissions. Ordinary RAM HHDM mappings should be RW/NX and WB.

Preserve the inherited PAT/MTRR configuration during the first transition. The boot report validates captured registers and computes a diagnostic effective type from the active PAT/MTRR values under normal caching. A separate pure selector can choose an index whose effective type remains uniform across an aligned physical range; the selector itself does not inspect PTEs or aliases. The opt-in `just frame-smoke` probe now compares effective types of the inherited kernel and HHDM aliases for kernel-image pages, but it is not a full alias inventory. The pure combination follows Intel SDM Table 11-7; it is not a generic rule for legacy PCD/PWT-only selection or model-specific combinations. Under Limine base revision 3 on x86_64, use PAT index 0 for WB, index 3 for UC, and index 5 for WC only after the target physical range and active PAT/MTRR interaction are verified. Map MMIO only from explicit device ranges and use UC by default; do not infer MMIO from generic reserved memory-map entries. A framebuffer may use WC only after its response and cache policy are explicitly validated. COM1 uses port I/O and requires no MMIO mapping.

Do not use huge pages in the first root; add them only when physical coverage, permissions, and cache attributes are uniform across the entire huge-page extent. Future Rustix-owned downward-growing stacks should have at least one 4 KiB unmapped guard page below them. The Limine bootstrap stack has no known guard, so none may be assumed there.

Never modify Limine's active page tables in place. `src/paging.rs` now builds a bounded, inactive candidate root from allocator-owned frames and supports transactional 4 KiB map/unmap operations. Its checked QEMU backend has built, walked, unmapped, and released one candidate mapping without changing CR3. This is not a transition implementation: the current probe does not preserve every transition-critical mapping, and the active Limine root remains in use. Keep the inherited root and its backing memory intact; do not switch CR3 until every required mapping, permission, cache attribute, ownership relation, and failure path has been reviewed and tested.

## Planned memory layers

1. **Validated physical regions:** implemented as a fixed-capacity owned snapshot; allocator ownership and reclaim policy remain future work.
4. **Frame allocator integration:** the bounded core is initialized from `BootInfo`; the inactive candidate builder and diagnostic QEMU probe are its only mapping callers so far. Add active mapping services only after the transition policy and ownership rules are complete.
3. **Kernel virtual memory:** Rustix still runs on inherited Limine page tables. A bounded inactive candidate-root builder now supports allocator-owned 4 KiB mapping and unmapping, but no kernel-owned root is active. Before replacing Limine's tables, preserve the executing kernel, bootstrap/Ring-0 stacks, request/response data, and exception stacks; define the HHDM extent and explicit mapping permissions/cache attributes. Keep writable-executable mappings disallowed by default and reserve MMIO and guard regions.
4. **Heap:** add a global allocator only after frame allocation and page mapping are initialized. Define allocation failure behavior for kernel and interrupt contexts.
5. **Process address spaces:** isolate userspace; define copy-in/copy-out helpers and never treat user pointers as kernel references.

## Invariants to preserve

- Physical ranges use checked arithmetic and the half-open convention `[start, end)`.
- Only complete frames in validated `Usable` regions enter the allocator; the first MiB remains reserved. Firmware and loader-reclaimable regions are not silently promoted to free memory.
- Under the single-allocator-per-physical-map contract, a frame is represented by one allocator-free range or one caller-owned, non-copyable `Frame` token. Only a successful `deallocate` transfers the token back to the allocator; errors return the token and leave allocator ranges and accounting unchanged. The current public constructor relies on callers to enforce unique allocator instances.
- `allocate` returns `None` on frame exhaustion. Metadata-capacity exhaustion is an explicit error, never silent loss of a frame.
- A `Frame` address is physical, not directly dereferenceable. HHDM translation and table access are limited to checked full-frame token-based paths that rely on Limine's documented mapping contract. Candidate mutations must remain within allocator-owned inactive tables. No active-root mutation or CR3 switch is permitted until address widths, mapping coverage, permissions/cache attributes, and transition-preservation requirements are established.
- Mapping changes validate alignment, canonical addresses, ownership, and permissions before touching tables.
- User-controlled addresses are validated on every syscall boundary; prior validation is not a substitute for access checks during later copies.
- Tests cover unaligned edges, exact-boundary allocations, arithmetic overflow, overlaps, exhaustion, and unchanged state/ownership on failure.

The complete transition and heap requirements remain design requirements; the inactive candidate builder and bounded QEMU probes are implemented, but do not deliver a replacement active address space.

The active transition retains the inherited PAT and MTRR state and changes no cache-selection bits. The page-table split copies large-page PAT selection to the equivalent 4 KiB/2 MiB entries. Future MMIO mappings must still use explicit device ranges and a verified cache policy; do not infer MMIO from generic reserved memory-map entries. COM1 uses port I/O and requires no MMIO mapping.

Do not use huge pages in the first root; add them only when physical coverage, permissions, and cache attributes are uniform across the entire huge-page extent. Future Rustix-owned downward-growing stacks should have at least one 4 KiB unmapped guard page below them. The Limine bootstrap stack has no known guard, so none may be assumed there.

Never modify Limine's active page tables in place. `src/paging.rs` builds an owned clone in allocator-issued frames, can split inherited large pages to update leaf permissions, and supports transactional 4 KiB map/unmap operations before activation. The default boot path validates critical translations and kernel alias permissions, switches CR3, verifies the active root, and retains its frame tokens for the active lifetime. The inherited root and backing memory remain intact. This preserves inherited mappings rather than constructing a new address space; broader mapping inventory, non-kernel permission policy, reclamation, and a general mapping service remain future work.

## Planned memory layers

1. **Validated physical regions:** implemented as a fixed-capacity owned snapshot; allocator ownership and reclaim policy remain future work.
4. **Frame allocator integration:** the bounded core is initialized from `BootInfo`; the inactive candidate builder and diagnostic QEMU probe are its only mapping callers so far. Add active mapping services only after the transition policy and ownership rules are complete.
3. **Kernel virtual memory:** Rustix runs on an active cloned hierarchy whose page-table frames it owns. The clone preserves Limine's mappings and applies R/NX or RW/NX permissions to kernel-image HHDM aliases. It is not a clean address-space rebuild, and general mapping/unmapping after activation is deliberately rejected without a TLB policy.
4. **Heap:** an initial global allocator uses a fixed 256 KiB BSS arena and at most 128 live allocations. It has deterministic exhaustion and exact-layout free semantics, does not grow from frames, and must not be called in interrupt context.
5. **Process address spaces:** isolate userspace; define copy-in/copy-out helpers and never treat user pointers as kernel references.

## Invariants to preserve

- Physical ranges use checked arithmetic and the half-open convention `[start, end)`.
- Only complete frames in validated `Usable` regions enter the allocator; the first MiB remains reserved. Firmware and loader-reclaimable regions are not silently promoted to free memory.
- Under the single-allocator-per-physical-map contract, a frame is represented by one allocator-free range or one caller-owned, non-copyable `Frame` token. Only a successful `deallocate` transfers the token back to the allocator; errors return the token and leave allocator ranges and accounting unchanged. The current public constructor relies on callers to enforce unique allocator instances.
- `allocate` returns `None` on frame exhaustion. Metadata-capacity exhaustion is an explicit error, never silent loss of a frame.
- A `Frame` address is physical, not directly dereferenceable. HHDM translation and table access are limited to checked full-frame token-based paths that rely on Limine's documented mapping contract. Candidate mutations are allowed only before activation and only in owned tables. The active cloned root retains its ownership tokens and rejects mutation/release until an explicit, reviewed CR3 transition away from it.
- Mapping changes validate alignment, canonical addresses, ownership, and permissions before touching tables.
- User-controlled addresses are validated on every syscall boundary; prior validation is not a substitute for access checks during later copies.
- Tests cover unaligned edges, exact-boundary allocations, arithmetic overflow, overlaps, exhaustion, and unchanged state/ownership on failure.

The active root is a full clone of Limine's reachable hierarchy with kernel HHDM alias W^X hardening, not a clean-room Rustix address space. The fixed BSS heap is bounded and non-growing. General mapping policy, broader alias/MMIO coverage, frame reclamation, and physical-hardware validation remain outstanding.

# Rustix roadmap

This roadmap describes an incremental path from the current bare-metal kernel to a useful Unix-like operating system. It is a dependency plan, not a schedule or a claim of compatibility. Features become current only after the implementation, tests, and exit criteria below agree.

## How to read status

- A checked box means the source/design work exists; it does **not** imply the code compiled, linked, booted, or passed an integration test.
- A milestone is not complete until its stated exit criteria are met and the evidence is recorded.
- Hardware work needs target build and emulator evidence. Host tests cannot validate privileged instructions, bootloader pointers, page tables, device I/O, or exception-entry assembly.
- Future work is intentionally not represented by placeholder APIs or dummy implementations.

## Current status

- **Milestone 0: local exit criteria met from a clean detached worktree; hosted CI pending.** On 2026-10-16, `just verify` passed in WSL2 Ubuntu 24.04 from both the working tree and a clean detached worktree with an empty `target` directory. The clean run downloaded and compiled the pinned Limine host utility, formatted and tested the workspace, checked and built the target, created the image, and passed the 20-second QEMU prompt smoke test. Hosted CI has not been observed.
- **Milestone 1: validation criteria met for the current Limine path.** The bounded boot snapshot, memory-range classification, and CPUID reporting were covered by host tests and QEMU reporting; the Limine pointer-readability trust boundary remains explicit.
- **Milestone 2: in progress, not complete.** The boot path owns and activates a clone of Limine's reachable page-table hierarchy, preserves inherited mappings, hardens kernel HHDM aliases to R/NX or RW/NX while retaining PAT attributes, and retains table-frame tokens. QEMU has exercised the 256 KiB requested stack, active CR3 transition, fixed BSS heap alignment/reuse/exhaustion, frame probes, and fatal exception diagnostics. The bounded heap does not grow from frames; broad mapping policy, reclamation, IRQ-safe allocation, and physical-hardware validation remain outstanding.
- **Milestones 3 and later: planned.** There is no general IRQ system, scheduler, userspace, syscall ABI, persistent filesystem, GUI, or networking stack.

## Dependency path

```text
Reliable boot
    -> validated boot state
    -> owned mappings + frame allocation + heap + fault diagnostics
    -> timer/IRQ model + scheduler
    -> isolated processes + syscall ABI
    -> VFS/storage + userland utilities
    -> graphical terminal and other optional services
```

Some device-driver work can proceed in parallel after the core ownership, locking, and testing rules exist. It must not bypass them with direct, unreviewed hardware access.

- [x] Specify frame-token ownership and failure semantics: `Frame` is non-copyable, failed deallocation returns the token without changing allocator state, and the current API documents (but does not enforce) one allocator instance per physical map.
- [x] Bootstrap GDT/TSS/IDT and fatal handlers for exception vectors 0–31.
- [x] Give double faults a dedicated IST stack; report saved register/error context and CR2/error bits for page faults.
- [x] Keep maskable IRQ delivery disabled; current exception handling is fatal-only.
