struct LimineHhdmPageTableReader<'a> {
    memory_map: &'a rustix_kernel::memory::MemoryMap,
    hhdm_offset: u64,
    physical_address_bits: u8,
    virtual_address_bits: u8,
}

impl rustix_kernel::paging::PageTableReader for LimineHhdmPageTableReader<'_> {
    type Error = rustix_kernel::memory::HhdmAddressError;

    fn read_entry(&self, table_physical: u64, index: u16) -> Result<u64, Self::Error> {
        if index >= 512 {
            return Err(rustix_kernel::memory::HhdmAddressError::InvalidHhdmRange);
        }
        let table_end = table_physical
            .checked_add(rustix_kernel::paging::PAGE_SIZE)
            .ok_or(rustix_kernel::memory::HhdmAddressError::AddressOverflow)?;
        if !self.memory_map.range_is_within_region_kind(
            table_physical,
            table_end,
            rustix_kernel::memory::RegionKind::BootloaderReclaimable,
        ) {
            return Err(rustix_kernel::memory::HhdmAddressError::NotLimineMapped);
        }
        let table_address = self.memory_map.limine_hhdm_address(
            self.hhdm_offset,
            table_physical,
            rustix_kernel::paging::PAGE_SIZE,
            Some(self.physical_address_bits),
            self.virtual_address_bits,
        )?;
        let entry_address = table_address
            .checked_add(u64::from(index) * core::mem::size_of::<u64>() as u64)
            .ok_or(rustix_kernel::memory::HhdmAddressError::AddressOverflow)?;
        // SAFETY: The complete table page was restricted to bootloader-reclaimable
        // memory and its HHDM address arithmetic was checked. The reader relies
        // on the Limine base-revision-3 mapping contract and never returns a ref.
        Ok(unsafe { (entry_address as *const u64).read_volatile() })
    }
}

struct LimineHhdmCandidateMemory<'a> {
    memory_map: &'a rustix_kernel::memory::MemoryMap,
    hhdm_offset: u64,
    physical_address_bits: u8,
    virtual_address_bits: u8,
}

// SAFETY: `prepare_table` accepts only an allocator-issued frame and validates
// its complete usable span and HHDM address. Handles are only used while the
// candidate retains the frame token and this unique backend borrow.
unsafe impl rustix_kernel::paging::CandidatePageTableMemory for LimineHhdmCandidateMemory<'_> {
    type PreparedTable = u64;
    type Error = rustix_kernel::memory::HhdmAddressError;

    fn prepare_table(
        &mut self,
        frame: &rustix_kernel::frame::Frame,
    ) -> Result<Self::PreparedTable, Self::Error> {
        frame.hhdm_address(
            self.memory_map,
            self.hhdm_offset,
            Some(self.physical_address_bits),
            self.virtual_address_bits,
        )
    }

    unsafe fn read_entry(
        &self,
        table: Self::PreparedTable,
        index: u16,
    ) -> Result<u64, Self::Error> {
        if index >= 512 {
            return Err(rustix_kernel::memory::HhdmAddressError::InvalidHhdmRange);
        }
        let entry_address = table
            .checked_add(u64::from(index) * core::mem::size_of::<u64>() as u64)
            .ok_or(rustix_kernel::memory::HhdmAddressError::AddressOverflow)?;
        // SAFETY: The unsafe trait contract requires `table` to be the prepared
        // HHDM address of a complete writable frame; the index is in [0, 512).
        Ok(unsafe { (entry_address as *const u64).read_volatile() })
    }

    unsafe fn clear_table(&mut self, table: Self::PreparedTable) {
        let entries = table as *mut u64;
        // SAFETY: The caller provides a handle prepared by this backend for a
        // complete writable frame retained by its candidate.
        unsafe {
            for index in 0..512 {
                entries.add(index).write_volatile(0);
            }
        }
    }

    unsafe fn write_entry(&mut self, table: Self::PreparedTable, index: u16, value: u64) {
        if index >= 512 {
            return;
        }
        let entry = (table as *mut u64).wrapping_add(usize::from(index));
        // SAFETY: The caller provides a prepared complete frame and an index in
        // range; this writes one entry without creating a Rust reference.
        unsafe { entry.write_volatile(value) };
    }
}

// Capture Limine's entry RSP before a Rust prologue changes it. The synthetic
// return slot is part of the SysV entry stack; realign before calling Rust.
core::arch::global_asm!(
    ".section .text",
    ".code64",
    ".global _start",
    ".type _start, @function",
    "_start:",
    "mov rdi, rsp",
    "and rsp, -16",
    "call rustix_start",
    "ud2",
    ".size _start, . - _start",
);

#[no_mangle]
pub extern "C" fn rustix_start(entry_rsp: u64) -> ! {
    arch::x86_64::serial::initialize();
    kprintln!("Rustix kernel: x86_64 Rust bootstrap");
    arch::x86_64::interrupts::initialize();
    kprintln!("x86_64 exception diagnostics: enabled (IRQs remain disabled)");
    let mut boot_info = match boot::capture_boot_information(entry_rsp) {
        Ok(boot_info) => boot_info,
        Err(error) => {
            kprintln!("boot information rejected: {:?}", error);
            halt_forever();
        }
    };
    boot::report_boot_information(&boot_info);

    #[cfg(feature = "probe-hhdm-frame")]
    probe_hhdm_frame(&mut boot_info);

    #[cfg(any(feature = "inject-page-fault", feature = "inject-invalid-opcode"))]
    run_fault_injection();

    activate_cloned_page_tables_and_run(&mut boot_info)
}

fn activate_cloned_page_tables_and_run(boot_info: &mut boot::BootInfo) -> ! {
    use rustix_kernel::paging::{
        encode_cr3_value, CandidatePageTables, PageWalkConfig, PageWalkOutcome,
    };

    let physical_address_bits = match boot_info.cpu_info.physical_address_bits {
        Some(bits) => bits,
        None => {
            kprintln!("page-table transition rejected: physical width unknown");
            halt_forever();
        }
    };
    let inherited_root = match boot_info.inherited_cr3_root {
        Ok(root) => root,
        Err(error) => {
            kprintln!("page-table transition rejected: inherited CR3: {:?}", error);
            halt_forever();
        }
    };
    if !boot_info.cpu_info.nx_enabled {
        kprintln!("page-table transition rejected: NXE is not enabled");
        halt_forever();
    }
    let config = PageWalkConfig {
        levels: if boot_info.cpu_info.active_linear_address_bits == 57 {
            5
        } else {
            4
        },
        physical_address_bits,
        virtual_address_bits: boot_info.cpu_info.active_linear_address_bits,
        nx_enabled: boot_info.cpu_info.nx_enabled,
        page_2m_supported: true,
        page_1g_supported: boot_info.cpu_info.has_1g_pages,
    };
    let reader = LimineHhdmPageTableReader {
        memory_map: &boot_info.memory_map,
        hhdm_offset: boot_info.hhdm_offset,
        physical_address_bits,
        virtual_address_bits: boot_info.cpu_info.active_linear_address_bits,
    };
    let mut memory = LimineHhdmCandidateMemory {
        memory_map: &boot_info.memory_map,
        hhdm_offset: boot_info.hhdm_offset,
        physical_address_bits,
        virtual_address_bits: boot_info.cpu_info.active_linear_address_bits,
    };
    let mut candidate =
        match CandidatePageTables::new(&mut boot_info.frame_allocator, &mut memory, config) {
            Ok(candidate) => candidate,
            Err(error) => {
                kprintln!(
                    "page-table transition failed to create root: {:?}",
                    error.cause
                );
                if let Some(frame) = error.frame {
                    release_probe_frame(&mut boot_info.frame_allocator, frame);
                }
                halt_forever();
            }
        };
    if let Err(error) =
        candidate.clone_inherited_hierarchy(&mut boot_info.frame_allocator, &reader, inherited_root)
    {
        kprintln!(
            "page-table transition failed to clone inherited root: {:?}",
            error
        );
        release_candidate_after_probe_failure(candidate, &mut boot_info.frame_allocator);
    }

    let segments = boot_info.kernel_image_segments;
    let spans = [
        (
            "kernel text",
            segments.text.virtual_start,
            segments.text.physical_start,
            segments.text.virtual_end - segments.text.virtual_start,
        ),
        (
            "kernel rodata",
            segments.rodata.virtual_start,
            segments.rodata.physical_start,
            segments.rodata.virtual_end - segments.rodata.virtual_start,
        ),
        (
            "kernel data",
            segments.data.virtual_start,
            segments.data.physical_start,
            segments.data.virtual_end - segments.data.virtual_start,
        ),
        (
            "active boot stack",
            boot_info.boot_stack_virtual_start,
            boot_info.boot_stack_physical_start,
            boot_info.boot_stack_virtual_end - boot_info.boot_stack_virtual_start,
        ),
    ];
    for (label, virtual_start, physical_start, length) in spans {
        if !candidate_span_matches_source(
            &candidate,
            &reader,
            inherited_root,
            config,
            virtual_start,
            physical_start,
            length,
        ) {
            kprintln!(
                "page-table transition rejected: {} was not preserved",
                label
            );
            release_candidate_after_probe_failure(candidate, &mut boot_info.frame_allocator);
        }
    }
    if !harden_kernel_hhdm_aliases(
        &mut candidate,
        &mut boot_info.frame_allocator,
        &boot_info.memory_map,
        boot_info.hhdm_offset,
        boot_info.cpu_info.physical_address_bits,
        boot_info.cpu_info.active_linear_address_bits,
        boot_info.kernel_image_segments,
        &reader,
        inherited_root,
        config,
    ) {
        release_candidate_after_probe_failure(candidate, &mut boot_info.frame_allocator);
    }
    kprintln!("kernel HHDM aliases validated: text/rodata R/NX, data RW/NX, PAT preserved");
    let candidate_root = candidate
        .root_physical_address()
        .expect("a live candidate retains its root frame");
    let root_hhdm_address = match boot_info.memory_map.limine_hhdm_address(
        boot_info.hhdm_offset,
        candidate_root,
        rustix_kernel::paging::PAGE_SIZE,
        Some(physical_address_bits),
        boot_info.cpu_info.active_linear_address_bits,
    ) {
        Ok(address) => address,
        Err(error) => {
            kprintln!(
                "page-table transition rejected: candidate root HHDM: {:?}",
                error
            );
            release_candidate_after_probe_failure(candidate, &mut boot_info.frame_allocator);
        }
    };
    let root_alias = match candidate.walk(root_hhdm_address) {
        Ok(PageWalkOutcome::Mapped(translation))
            if translation.physical_address == candidate_root =>
        {
            translation
        }
        result => {
            kprintln!(
                "page-table transition rejected: candidate root HHDM alias: {:?}",
                result
            );
            release_candidate_after_probe_failure(candidate, &mut boot_info.frame_allocator);
        }
    };
    if !root_alias.permissions.writable || root_alias.permissions.user_accessible {
        kprintln!("page-table transition rejected: candidate root alias permissions are unsafe");
        release_candidate_after_probe_failure(candidate, &mut boot_info.frame_allocator);
    }

    let new_cr3 = match encode_cr3_value(
        candidate_root,
        inherited_root.low_bits(),
        physical_address_bits,
    ) {
        Ok(value) => value,
        Err(error) => {
            kprintln!("page-table transition rejected: new CR3: {:?}", error);
            release_candidate_after_probe_failure(candidate, &mut boot_info.frame_allocator);
        }
    };
    let inherited_cr3 = boot_info.inherited_cr3_raw;
    if arch::x86_64::cpu::read_cr3_raw() != inherited_cr3 {
        kprintln!("page-table transition aborted: active CR3 changed before switch");
        release_candidate_after_probe_failure(candidate, &mut boot_info.frame_allocator);
    }
    // SAFETY: The candidate is a complete clone of every present inherited
    // hierarchy entry, with all referenced intermediate tables owned and the
    // critical code/data/stack paths compared before this point. The inherited
    // root's paging mode, address widths, PAT/MTRR state, and low CR3 mode are
    // preserved; interrupts are disabled from bootstrap initialization onward.
    let global_tlb_flushed = unsafe { arch::x86_64::cpu::write_cr3_with_global_flush(new_cr3) };
    if global_tlb_flushed {
        kprintln!("page-table transition: global TLB flushed via CR4.PGE toggle");
    } else {
        kprintln!("page-table transition: CR4.PGE clear; CR3 reload flushed active translations");
    }
    if arch::x86_64::cpu::read_cr3_raw() != new_cr3
        || !spans
            .iter()
            .all(|(_, virtual_start, physical_start, length)| {
                candidate_span_matches_source(
                    &candidate,
                    &reader,
                    inherited_root,
                    config,
                    *virtual_start,
                    *physical_start,
                    *length,
                )
            })
    {
        // SAFETY: The inherited root and its backing memory remain untouched and
        // mapped by the candidate, so restoring its validated CR3 value is safe.
        unsafe { arch::x86_64::cpu::write_cr3_with_global_flush(inherited_cr3) };
        if arch::x86_64::cpu::read_cr3_raw() != inherited_cr3 {
            kprintln!("page-table transition failed to restore inherited CR3; candidate retained");
            halt_forever();
        }
        kprintln!("page-table transition failed post-switch verification; restored inherited CR3");
        release_candidate_after_probe_failure(candidate, &mut boot_info.frame_allocator);
    }
    // SAFETY: CR3 matches `new_cr3` and post-switch translation checks passed;
    // interrupts are disabled and the candidate root must remain allocated.
    unsafe { candidate.mark_active() };
    kprintln!(
        "page-table transition passed: active CR3={:#x}, cloned root={:#x}, {} owned tables",
        new_cr3,
        candidate_root,
        candidate.table_count()
    );
    probe_kernel_heap();

    // Keep the candidate and its frame tokens alive for as long as this root is
    // active. The shell runs forever and does not return to this stack frame.
    // SAFETY: The bootstrap is single-core, interrupts remain disabled, and the
    // shell is the only filesystem owner.
    let filesystem = unsafe { &mut *core::ptr::addr_of_mut!(RAM_FILESYSTEM) };
    match filesystem.seed_defaults() {
        Ok(home) => shell::run(filesystem, home, boot_info),
        Err(error) => {
            kprintln!("RAM filesystem initialization failed: {:?}", error);
            halt_forever()
        }
    }
}

fn harden_kernel_hhdm_aliases(
    candidate: &mut rustix_kernel::paging::CandidatePageTables<'_, LimineHhdmCandidateMemory<'_>>,
    allocator: &mut rustix_kernel::frame::FrameAllocator,
    memory_map: &rustix_kernel::memory::MemoryMap,
    hhdm_offset: u64,
    physical_address_bits: Option<u8>,
    virtual_address_bits: u8,
    segments: rustix_kernel::memory::KernelImageSegments,
    reader: &impl rustix_kernel::paging::PageTableReader<
        Error = rustix_kernel::memory::HhdmAddressError,
    >,
    inherited_root: rustix_kernel::paging::Cr3Root,
    config: rustix_kernel::paging::PageWalkConfig,
) -> bool {
    use rustix_kernel::paging::{
        walk_virtual_address, PagePermissions, PageWalkOutcome, PAGE_SIZE,
    };

    let image_segments = [
        ("kernel text", segments.text, false),
        ("kernel rodata", segments.rodata, false),
        ("kernel data", segments.data, true),
    ];
    for (label, segment, writable) in image_segments {
        let length = segment.physical_end - segment.physical_start;
        let mut offset = 0;
        while offset < length {
            let Some(physical_address) = segment.physical_start.checked_add(offset) else {
                kprintln!(
                    "kernel HHDM alias check failed: {} physical overflow",
                    label
                );
                return false;
            };
            let alias = match memory_map.limine_hhdm_address(
                hhdm_offset,
                physical_address,
                PAGE_SIZE,
                physical_address_bits,
                virtual_address_bits,
            ) {
                Ok(alias) => alias,
                Err(error) => {
                    kprintln!(
                        "kernel HHDM alias check failed: {} address: {:?}",
                        label,
                        error
                    );
                    return false;
                }
            };
            let source = match walk_virtual_address(reader, inherited_root, alias, config) {
                Ok(PageWalkOutcome::Mapped(translation)) => translation,
                result => {
                    kprintln!(
                        "kernel HHDM alias check failed: {} inherited walk: {:?}",
                        label,
                        result
                    );
                    return false;
                }
            };
            let permissions = PagePermissions {
                writable,
                executable: false,
                user_accessible: false,
            };
            if let Err(error) = candidate.set_inherited_page_permissions(
                allocator,
                alias,
                physical_address,
                permissions,
            ) {
                kprintln!(
                    "kernel HHDM alias check failed: {} protection: {:?}",
                    label,
                    error
                );
                return false;
            }
            match candidate.walk(alias) {
                Ok(PageWalkOutcome::Mapped(translation))
                    if translation.physical_address == physical_address
                        && translation.permissions == permissions
                        && translation.pat_index == source.pat_index => {}
                result => {
                    kprintln!(
                        "kernel HHDM alias check failed: {} candidate walk: {:?}",
                        label,
                        result
                    );
                    return false;
                }
            }
            offset += PAGE_SIZE;
        }
    }
    true
}

fn probe_kernel_heap() {
    use core::alloc::{GlobalAlloc, Layout};

    let full_layout = match Layout::from_size_align(rustix_kernel::heap::KERNEL_HEAP_CAPACITY, 1) {
        Ok(layout) => layout,
        Err(error) => {
            kprintln!(
                "kernel heap probe failed to construct full-arena layout: {:?}",
                error
            );
            halt_forever();
        }
    };
    // SAFETY: The heap static is initialized before use and maskable interrupts
    // remain disabled; this probe requests a valid nonzero layout.
    let full_arena = unsafe { KERNEL_HEAP.alloc(full_layout) };
    if full_arena.is_null() {
        kprintln!("kernel heap probe failed: full-arena allocation was rejected");
        halt_forever();
    }
    let small_layout = Layout::new::<u8>();
    // SAFETY: The heap lock serializes this valid nonzero allocation request.
    let exhausted = unsafe { KERNEL_HEAP.alloc(small_layout) };
    if !exhausted.is_null() {
        // SAFETY: Both pointers are live allocations with their original layouts.
        unsafe {
            KERNEL_HEAP.dealloc(exhausted, small_layout);
            KERNEL_HEAP.dealloc(full_arena, full_layout);
        }
        kprintln!("kernel heap probe failed: exhaustion was not deterministic");
        halt_forever();
    }
    // SAFETY: `full_arena` is the complete live allocation created above.
    unsafe { KERNEL_HEAP.dealloc(full_arena, full_layout) };

    let layout = match Layout::from_size_align(257, 64) {
        Ok(layout) => layout,
        Err(error) => {
            kprintln!(
                "kernel heap probe failed to construct aligned layout: {:?}",
                error
            );
            halt_forever();
        }
    };
    // SAFETY: The heap is available after releasing the full-arena allocation.
    let allocation = unsafe { KERNEL_HEAP.alloc(layout) };
    if allocation.is_null() || allocation as usize % layout.align() != 0 {
        if !allocation.is_null() {
            // SAFETY: This is the live allocation returned for `layout`.
            unsafe { KERNEL_HEAP.dealloc(allocation, layout) };
        }
        kprintln!("kernel heap probe failed: aligned allocation was rejected or misaligned");
        halt_forever();
    }
    // SAFETY: The allocator returned `layout.size()` writable bytes.
    unsafe { core::ptr::write_bytes(allocation, 0xa5, layout.size()) };
    for index in 0..layout.size() {
        // SAFETY: `index` remains inside the live allocation.
        if unsafe { allocation.add(index).read_volatile() } != 0xa5 {
            // SAFETY: The allocation is still live with its original layout.
            unsafe { KERNEL_HEAP.dealloc(allocation, layout) };
            kprintln!("kernel heap probe failed: allocation data did not round-trip");
            halt_forever();
        }
    }
    // SAFETY: The allocation is live and the original layout is supplied.
    unsafe { KERNEL_HEAP.dealloc(allocation, layout) };
    // SAFETY: The previous allocation was returned; first-fit should reuse it.
    let reused = unsafe { KERNEL_HEAP.alloc(layout) };
    if reused != allocation {
        if !reused.is_null() {
            // SAFETY: `reused` is a live allocation with `layout`.
            unsafe { KERNEL_HEAP.dealloc(reused, layout) };
        }
        kprintln!("kernel heap probe failed: freed space was not reused");
        halt_forever();
    }
    // SAFETY: The reused allocation is live and has the same layout.
    unsafe { KERNEL_HEAP.dealloc(reused, layout) };
    kprintln!("kernel heap probe passed: alignment, reuse, deterministic exhaustion");
}

#[cfg(feature = "probe-hhdm-frame")]
fn probe_hhdm_frame(boot_info: &mut boot::BootInfo) {
    use rustix_kernel::frame::FRAME_SIZE;

    let frame = match boot_info.frame_allocator.allocate() {
        Some(frame) => frame,
        None => {
            kprintln!("HHDM frame probe failed: no free frame");
            halt_forever();
        }
    };
    let hhdm_address = match frame.hhdm_address(
        &boot_info.memory_map,
        boot_info.hhdm_offset,
        boot_info.cpu_info.physical_address_bits,
        boot_info.cpu_info.active_linear_address_bits,
    ) {
        Ok(address) => address,
        Err(error) => {
            kprintln!("HHDM frame probe rejected frame translation: {:?}", error);
            release_probe_frame(&mut boot_info.frame_allocator, frame);
            halt_forever();
        }
    };

    let words = (FRAME_SIZE / core::mem::size_of::<u64>() as u64) as usize;
    let page = hhdm_address as *mut u64;
    let mut verified = true;
    // SAFETY: The non-copyable `Frame` token is held exclusively; its full page
    // is within validated `Usable` memory and its HHDM arithmetic was checked.
    // Limine base revision 3 guarantees usable memory in the HHDM, and no other
    // Rustix mapping aliases this newly allocated frame. This is an opt-in QEMU
    // probe; a broken loader mapping would fault and be caught by the fatal path.
    unsafe {
        for index in 0..words {
            page.add(index)
                .write_volatile(0xa5a5_0000_0000_0000 ^ index as u64);
        }
        for index in 0..words {
            if page.add(index).read_volatile() != (0xa5a5_0000_0000_0000 ^ index as u64) {
                verified = false;
                break;
            }
        }
        for index in 0..words {
            page.add(index).write_volatile(0);
        }
    }

    release_probe_frame(&mut boot_info.frame_allocator, frame);
    if !verified {
        kprintln!("HHDM frame probe failed: readback mismatch");
        halt_forever();
    }
    kprintln!("HHDM frame probe passed: wrote, read, cleared, and reclaimed one frame");
    probe_inherited_root(boot_info);
}

#[cfg(feature = "probe-hhdm-frame")]
fn probe_inherited_root(boot_info: &mut boot::BootInfo) {
    use rustix_kernel::paging::inherited_cr3_root_hhdm_address;

    let root = match boot_info.inherited_cr3_root {
        Ok(root) => root,
        Err(error) => {
            kprintln!(
                "inherited root probe failed: CR3 decode rejected: {:?}",
                error
            );
            halt_forever();
        }
    };
    let address = match inherited_cr3_root_hhdm_address(
        root,
        &boot_info.memory_map,
        boot_info.hhdm_offset,
        boot_info.cpu_info.physical_address_bits,
        boot_info.cpu_info.active_linear_address_bits,
    ) {
        Ok(address) => address,
        Err(error) => {
            kprintln!(
                "inherited root probe failed: HHDM validation rejected: {:?}",
                error
            );
            halt_forever();
        }
    };
    let entries = address as *const u64;
    let mut present_entries = 0;
    // SAFETY: The complete root page was validated as bootloader-reclaimable
    // and its HHDM range arithmetic was checked. The Limine base-revision-3
    // contract maps that region; this read-only opt-in probe trusts that handoff.
    unsafe {
        for index in 0..512 {
            if entries.add(index).read_volatile() & 1 != 0 {
                present_entries += 1;
            }
        }
    }
    kprintln!(
        "inherited root HHDM probe passed: read 512 entries, {} present",
        present_entries
    );
    let physical_address_bits = match boot_info.cpu_info.physical_address_bits {
        Some(bits) => bits,
        None => {
            kprintln!("inherited page-table walk failed: physical width unknown");
            halt_forever();
        }
    };
    let reader = LimineHhdmPageTableReader {
        memory_map: &boot_info.memory_map,
        hhdm_offset: boot_info.hhdm_offset,
        physical_address_bits,
        virtual_address_bits: boot_info.cpu_info.active_linear_address_bits,
    };
    let config = rustix_kernel::paging::PageWalkConfig {
        levels: if boot_info.cpu_info.active_linear_address_bits == 57 {
            5
        } else {
            4
        },
        physical_address_bits,
        virtual_address_bits: boot_info.cpu_info.active_linear_address_bits,
        nx_enabled: boot_info.cpu_info.nx_enabled,
        page_2m_supported: true,
        page_1g_supported: boot_info.cpu_info.has_1g_pages,
    };
    let segments = boot_info.kernel_image_segments;
    verify_inherited_mapping(
        &reader,
        root,
        config,
        "kernel text",
        segments.text.virtual_start,
        segments.text.physical_start,
        segments.text.virtual_end - segments.text.virtual_start,
    );
    verify_inherited_mapping(
        &reader,
        root,
        config,
        "kernel rodata",
        segments.rodata.virtual_start,
        segments.rodata.physical_start,
        segments.rodata.virtual_end - segments.rodata.virtual_start,
    );
    verify_inherited_mapping(
        &reader,
        root,
        config,
        "kernel data",
        segments.data.virtual_start,
        segments.data.physical_start,
        segments.data.virtual_end - segments.data.virtual_start,
    );
    verify_inherited_mapping(
        &reader,
        root,
        config,
        "active boot stack",
        boot_info.boot_stack_virtual_start,
        boot_info.boot_stack_physical_start,
        boot_info.boot_stack_virtual_end - boot_info.boot_stack_virtual_start,
    );

    let pat_value = match boot_info.cpu_info.pat_msr_value {
        Some(value) => value,
        None => {
            kprintln!("cache-alias probe failed: active PAT value unavailable");
            halt_forever();
        }
    };
    let pat = match rustix_kernel::paging::PatLayout::from_msr_value(pat_value) {
        Ok(pat) => pat,
        Err(error) => {
            kprintln!("cache-alias probe failed: invalid PAT layout: {:?}", error);
            halt_forever();
        }
    };
    let registers = match &boot_info.cpu_info.mtrr {
        rustix_kernel::paging::MtrrState::Captured(registers) => registers,
        _ => {
            kprintln!("cache-alias probe failed: captured MTRR state unavailable");
            halt_forever();
        }
    };
    let mtrrs = match registers.validated_layout(physical_address_bits) {
        Ok(mtrrs) => mtrrs,
        Err(error) => {
            kprintln!("cache-alias probe failed: invalid MTRR state: {:?}", error);
            halt_forever();
        }
    };
    if !boot_info.cpu_info.normal_caching {
        kprintln!("cache-alias probe failed: non-normal CR0 caching mode");
        halt_forever();
    }
    verify_kernel_cache_aliases(
        boot_info,
        &reader,
        root,
        config,
        pat,
        &mtrrs,
        "kernel text",
        segments.text.virtual_start,
        segments.text.physical_start,
        segments.text.virtual_end - segments.text.virtual_start,
    );
    verify_kernel_cache_aliases(
        boot_info,
        &reader,
        root,
        config,
        pat,
        &mtrrs,
        "kernel rodata",
        segments.rodata.virtual_start,
        segments.rodata.physical_start,
        segments.rodata.virtual_end - segments.rodata.virtual_start,
    );
    verify_kernel_cache_aliases(
        boot_info,
        &reader,
        root,
        config,
        pat,
        &mtrrs,
        "kernel data",
        segments.data.virtual_start,
        segments.data.physical_start,
        segments.data.virtual_end - segments.data.virtual_start,
    );
    probe_cloned_page_tables(
        &mut boot_info.frame_allocator,
        &boot_info.memory_map,
        boot_info.hhdm_offset,
        physical_address_bits,
        boot_info.cpu_info.active_linear_address_bits,
        &reader,
        root,
        config,
        [
            (
                "kernel text",
                segments.text.virtual_start,
                segments.text.physical_start,
                segments.text.virtual_end - segments.text.virtual_start,
            ),
            (
                "kernel rodata",
                segments.rodata.virtual_start,
                segments.rodata.physical_start,
                segments.rodata.virtual_end - segments.rodata.virtual_start,
            ),
            (
                "kernel data",
                segments.data.virtual_start,
                segments.data.physical_start,
                segments.data.virtual_end - segments.data.virtual_start,
            ),
            (
                "active boot stack",
                boot_info.boot_stack_virtual_start,
                boot_info.boot_stack_physical_start,
                boot_info.boot_stack_virtual_end - boot_info.boot_stack_virtual_start,
            ),
        ],
    );
    probe_candidate_page_tables(boot_info);
}

#[cfg(feature = "probe-hhdm-frame")]
fn probe_cloned_page_tables(
    allocator: &mut rustix_kernel::frame::FrameAllocator,
    memory_map: &rustix_kernel::memory::MemoryMap,
    hhdm_offset: u64,
    physical_address_bits: u8,
    virtual_address_bits: u8,
    source_reader: &impl rustix_kernel::paging::PageTableReader<
        Error = rustix_kernel::memory::HhdmAddressError,
    >,
    source_root: rustix_kernel::paging::Cr3Root,
    config: rustix_kernel::paging::PageWalkConfig,
    spans: [(&str, u64, u64, u64); 4],
) {
    use rustix_kernel::paging::CandidatePageTables;

    let mut memory = LimineHhdmCandidateMemory {
        memory_map,
        hhdm_offset,
        physical_address_bits,
        virtual_address_bits,
    };
    let mut candidate = match CandidatePageTables::new(allocator, &mut memory, config) {
        Ok(candidate) => candidate,
        Err(error) => {
            kprintln!(
                "candidate clone probe failed to create root: {:?}",
                error.cause
            );
            if let Some(frame) = error.frame {
                release_probe_frame(allocator, frame);
            }
            halt_forever();
        }
    };
    if let Err(error) = candidate.clone_inherited_hierarchy(allocator, source_reader, source_root) {
        kprintln!("candidate clone probe failed: {:?}", error);
        release_candidate_after_probe_failure(candidate, allocator);
    }
    for (label, virtual_start, physical_start, length) in spans {
        if !candidate_span_matches_source(
            &candidate,
            source_reader,
            source_root,
            config,
            virtual_start,
            physical_start,
            length,
        ) {
            kprintln!(
                "candidate clone probe failed: {} translation mismatch",
                label
            );
            release_candidate_after_probe_failure(candidate, allocator);
        }
    }
    let table_count = candidate.table_count();
    if let Err(failure) = candidate.release(allocator) {
        kprintln!(
            "candidate clone probe failed to release frames: {:?}",
            failure
        );
        halt_forever();
    }
    kprintln!(
        "candidate inherited-root clone probe passed: {} owned table pages preserve critical paths; CR3 unchanged",
        table_count
    );
}

fn candidate_span_matches_source(
    candidate: &rustix_kernel::paging::CandidatePageTables<'_, LimineHhdmCandidateMemory<'_>>,
    source_reader: &impl rustix_kernel::paging::PageTableReader<
        Error = rustix_kernel::memory::HhdmAddressError,
    >,
    source_root: rustix_kernel::paging::Cr3Root,
    config: rustix_kernel::paging::PageWalkConfig,
    virtual_start: u64,
    physical_start: u64,
    length: u64,
) -> bool {
    use rustix_kernel::paging::{walk_virtual_address, PageWalkOutcome};

    let mut offset = 0;
    while offset < length {
        let Some(virtual_address) = virtual_start.checked_add(offset) else {
            return false;
        };
        let Some(expected_physical) = physical_start.checked_add(offset) else {
            return false;
        };
        let source_result =
            walk_virtual_address(source_reader, source_root, virtual_address, config);
        let candidate_result = candidate.walk(virtual_address);
        let (source_translation, candidate_translation) = match (source_result, candidate_result) {
            (Ok(PageWalkOutcome::Mapped(source)), Ok(PageWalkOutcome::Mapped(candidate))) => {
                (source, candidate)
            }
            (source, candidate) => {
                kprintln!(
                    "candidate clone walk mismatch at {:#018x}: inherited={:?}, candidate={:?}",
                    virtual_address,
                    source,
                    candidate
                );
                return false;
            }
        };
        // The CPU may update Accessed/Dirty in the active hierarchy after the
        // clone; they are hardware tracking state, not translation policy.
        let hardware_tracking_bits = (1 << 5) | (1 << 6);
        if source_translation.physical_address != candidate_translation.physical_address
            || source_translation.leaf_physical_base != candidate_translation.leaf_physical_base
            || source_translation.page_size != candidate_translation.page_size
            || source_translation.permissions != candidate_translation.permissions
            || source_translation.pat_index != candidate_translation.pat_index
            || source_translation.raw_leaf_entry & !hardware_tracking_bits
                != candidate_translation.raw_leaf_entry & !hardware_tracking_bits
            || candidate_translation.physical_address != expected_physical
        {
            kprintln!(
                "candidate clone translation mismatch at {:#018x}: inherited={:?}, candidate={:?}, expected PA={:#x}",
                virtual_address,
                source_translation,
                candidate_translation,
                expected_physical
            );
            return false;
        }
        let Some(next_offset) = offset.checked_add(rustix_kernel::paging::PAGE_SIZE) else {
            return false;
        };
        offset = next_offset;
    }
    true
}

#[cfg(feature = "probe-hhdm-frame")]
fn probe_candidate_page_tables(boot_info: &mut boot::BootInfo) {
    use rustix_kernel::paging::{
        validate_mapping_range, CachePolicy, CandidatePageTables, PagePermissions, PageWalkOutcome,
    };

    let Some(physical_address_bits) = boot_info.cpu_info.physical_address_bits else {
        kprintln!("candidate page-table probe failed: physical width unknown");
        halt_forever();
    };
    if !boot_info.cpu_info.nx_enabled || !boot_info.cpu_info.normal_caching {
        kprintln!("candidate page-table probe failed: NXE or normal caching unavailable");
        halt_forever();
    }
    let pat_value = boot_info
        .cpu_info
        .pat_msr_value
        .expect("inherited cache-alias probe validated active PAT");
    let pat = rustix_kernel::paging::PatLayout::from_msr_value(pat_value).unwrap_or_else(|error| {
        kprintln!(
            "candidate page-table probe failed: invalid PAT: {:?}",
            error
        );
        halt_forever();
    });
    let registers = match &boot_info.cpu_info.mtrr {
        rustix_kernel::paging::MtrrState::Captured(registers) => registers,
        _ => {
            kprintln!("candidate page-table probe failed: captured MTRR state unavailable");
            halt_forever();
        }
    };
    let mtrrs = match registers.validated_layout(physical_address_bits) {
        Ok(mtrrs) => mtrrs,
        Err(error) => {
            kprintln!(
                "candidate page-table probe failed: invalid MTRR: {:?}",
                error
            );
            halt_forever();
        }
    };
    let config = rustix_kernel::paging::PageWalkConfig {
        levels: if boot_info.cpu_info.active_linear_address_bits == 57 {
            5
        } else {
            4
        },
        physical_address_bits,
        virtual_address_bits: boot_info.cpu_info.active_linear_address_bits,
        nx_enabled: true,
        page_2m_supported: true,
        page_1g_supported: boot_info.cpu_info.has_1g_pages,
    };
    let virtual_address = 0xffff_9000_ffff_f000;
    let permissions = PagePermissions {
        writable: true,
        executable: false,
        user_accessible: false,
    };
    let frame = match boot_info.frame_allocator.allocate() {
        Some(frame) => frame,
        None => {
            kprintln!("candidate page-table probe failed: no leaf frame available");
            halt_forever();
        }
    };
    let mapping = match validate_mapping_range(
        virtual_address,
        frame.address(),
        rustix_kernel::paging::PAGE_SIZE,
        permissions,
        Some(physical_address_bits),
        config.virtual_address_bits,
    ) {
        Ok(mapping) => mapping,
        Err(error) => {
            kprintln!(
                "candidate page-table probe failed: invalid mapping: {:?}",
                error
            );
            release_probe_frame(&mut boot_info.frame_allocator, frame);
            halt_forever();
        }
    };
    let cache_attributes = match mapping.select_cache_attributes(
        CachePolicy::WriteBack,
        pat,
        &mtrrs,
        boot_info.cpu_info.normal_caching,
    ) {
        Ok(attributes) => attributes,
        Err(error) => {
            kprintln!(
                "candidate page-table probe failed: cache policy: {:?}",
                error
            );
            release_probe_frame(&mut boot_info.frame_allocator, frame);
            halt_forever();
        }
    };

    let mut memory = LimineHhdmCandidateMemory {
        memory_map: &boot_info.memory_map,
        hhdm_offset: boot_info.hhdm_offset,
        physical_address_bits,
        virtual_address_bits: boot_info.cpu_info.active_linear_address_bits,
    };
    let mut candidate =
        match CandidatePageTables::new(&mut boot_info.frame_allocator, &mut memory, config) {
            Ok(candidate) => candidate,
            Err(error) => {
                kprintln!(
                    "candidate page-table probe failed to create root: {:?}",
                    error.cause
                );
                release_probe_frame(&mut boot_info.frame_allocator, frame);
                if let Some(root_frame) = error.frame {
                    release_probe_frame(&mut boot_info.frame_allocator, root_frame);
                }
                halt_forever();
            }
        };
    let root = candidate.root_physical_address();
    let frame_address = frame.address();
    if let Err(failure) = candidate.map_owned_page(
        &mut boot_info.frame_allocator,
        frame,
        mapping,
        cache_attributes,
    ) {
        kprintln!(
            "candidate page-table probe failed to map leaf: {:?}",
            failure.cause
        );
        release_probe_frame(&mut boot_info.frame_allocator, failure.frame);
        release_candidate_after_probe_failure(candidate, &mut boot_info.frame_allocator);
    }

    let walk = candidate.walk(virtual_address);
    let returned_frame = match candidate.unmap_owned_page(virtual_address) {
        Ok(frame) => frame,
        Err(error) => {
            kprintln!(
                "candidate page-table probe failed to unmap leaf: {:?}",
                error
            );
            release_candidate_after_probe_failure(candidate, &mut boot_info.frame_allocator);
        }
    };
    let translation_valid = match &walk {
        Ok(PageWalkOutcome::Mapped(translation)) => {
            translation.physical_address == frame_address
                && translation.page_size == rustix_kernel::paging::PAGE_SIZE
                && translation.permissions == permissions
                && translation.pat_index == cache_attributes.pat_index()
        }
        _ => false,
    };
    if returned_frame.address() != frame_address {
        kprintln!("candidate page-table probe failed: unmap returned the wrong frame");
        release_probe_frame(&mut boot_info.frame_allocator, returned_frame);
        release_candidate_after_probe_failure(candidate, &mut boot_info.frame_allocator);
    }
    release_probe_frame(&mut boot_info.frame_allocator, returned_frame);
    if !translation_valid {
        kprintln!(
            "candidate page-table probe failed: candidate walk: {:?}",
            walk
        );
        release_candidate_after_probe_failure(candidate, &mut boot_info.frame_allocator);
    }
    if let Err(failure) = candidate.release(&mut boot_info.frame_allocator) {
        kprintln!(
            "candidate page-table probe failed to release frames: {:?}",
            failure
        );
        halt_forever();
    }
    kprintln!(
        "candidate page-table probe passed: mapped, walked, unmapped, and released root {:#x}; CR3 unchanged",
        root.expect("candidate retains root until release")
    );
}

fn release_candidate_after_probe_failure(
    candidate: rustix_kernel::paging::CandidatePageTables<'_, LimineHhdmCandidateMemory<'_>>,
    allocator: &mut rustix_kernel::frame::FrameAllocator,
) -> ! {
    if let Err(failure) = candidate.release(allocator) {
        kprintln!("candidate page-table cleanup also failed: {:?}", failure);
    }
    halt_forever()
}

#[cfg(feature = "probe-hhdm-frame")]
fn verify_inherited_mapping(
    reader: &impl rustix_kernel::paging::PageTableReader<
        Error = rustix_kernel::memory::HhdmAddressError,
    >,
    root: rustix_kernel::paging::Cr3Root,
    config: rustix_kernel::paging::PageWalkConfig,
    label: &str,
    virtual_start: u64,
    physical_start: u64,
    length: u64,
) {
    use rustix_kernel::paging::{walk_virtual_address, PageWalkOutcome};

    let mut offset = 0;
    let mut pages = 0;
    let mut first_translation: Option<rustix_kernel::paging::PageTranslation> = None;
    let mut permissions_uniform = true;
    let mut pat_index_uniform = true;
    while offset < length {
        let virtual_address = match virtual_start.checked_add(offset) {
            Some(address) => address,
            None => {
                kprintln!("inherited mapping probe failed: {} virtual overflow", label);
                halt_forever();
            }
        };
        let expected_physical = match physical_start.checked_add(offset) {
            Some(address) => address,
            None => {
                kprintln!(
                    "inherited mapping probe failed: {} physical overflow",
                    label
                );
                halt_forever();
            }
        };
        let translation = match walk_virtual_address(reader, root, virtual_address, config) {
            Ok(PageWalkOutcome::Mapped(translation)) => translation,
            Ok(PageWalkOutcome::NotPresent { level }) => {
                if level == rustix_kernel::paging::PageLevel::Pml4 {
                    let pml4_index = ((virtual_address >> 39) & 0x1ff) as u16;
                    let root_entry = reader.read_entry(root.physical_address(), pml4_index);
                    kprintln!(
                        "inherited mapping PML4 detail: VA={:#018x}, index={}, root={:#x}, entry={:?}",
                        virtual_address,
                        pml4_index,
                        root.physical_address(),
                        root_entry
                    );
                }
                kprintln!(
                    "inherited mapping probe failed: {} absent at {:?}",
                    label,
                    level
                );
                halt_forever();
            }
            Err(error) => {
                kprintln!("inherited mapping probe failed: {}: {:?}", label, error);
                halt_forever();
            }
        };
        if translation.physical_address != expected_physical {
            kprintln!(
                "inherited mapping probe failed: {} {:#018x} mapped to {:#018x}, expected {:#018x}",
                label,
                virtual_address,
                translation.physical_address,
                expected_physical
            );
            halt_forever();
        }
        if let Some(first) = first_translation {
            permissions_uniform &= translation.permissions == first.permissions;
            pat_index_uniform &= translation.pat_index == first.pat_index;
        } else {
            first_translation = Some(translation);
        }
        pages += 1;
        offset += rustix_kernel::paging::PAGE_SIZE;
    }
    if let Some(first) = first_translation {
        kprintln!(
            "inherited mapping probe passed: {} ({} pages), first permissions={:?}, PAT index={}, leaf size={}, uniform permissions={}, uniform PAT index={}",
            label,
            pages,
            first.permissions,
            first.pat_index,
            first.page_size,
            permissions_uniform,
            pat_index_uniform
        );
    }
}

#[cfg(feature = "probe-hhdm-frame")]
fn verify_kernel_cache_aliases(
    boot_info: &boot::BootInfo,
    reader: &impl rustix_kernel::paging::PageTableReader<
        Error = rustix_kernel::memory::HhdmAddressError,
    >,
    root: rustix_kernel::paging::Cr3Root,
    config: rustix_kernel::paging::PageWalkConfig,
    pat: rustix_kernel::paging::PatLayout,
    mtrrs: &rustix_kernel::paging::ValidatedMtrrLayout,
    label: &str,
    kernel_virtual_start: u64,
    physical_start: u64,
    length: u64,
) {
    use rustix_kernel::paging::{walk_virtual_address, PageWalkOutcome};

    let mut offset = 0;
    let mut pages = 0;
    while offset < length {
        let physical = match physical_start.checked_add(offset) {
            Some(address) => address,
            None => {
                kprintln!("cache-alias probe failed: {} physical overflow", label);
                halt_forever();
            }
        };
        let kernel_virtual = match kernel_virtual_start.checked_add(offset) {
            Some(address) => address,
            None => {
                kprintln!("cache-alias probe failed: {} virtual overflow", label);
                halt_forever();
            }
        };
        let hhdm_virtual = match boot_info.memory_map.limine_hhdm_address(
            boot_info.hhdm_offset,
            physical,
            rustix_kernel::paging::PAGE_SIZE,
            boot_info.cpu_info.physical_address_bits,
            boot_info.cpu_info.active_linear_address_bits,
        ) {
            Ok(address) => address,
            Err(error) => {
                kprintln!(
                    "cache-alias probe failed: {} HHDM range: {:?}",
                    label,
                    error
                );
                halt_forever();
            }
        };
        let kernel_translation = match walk_virtual_address(reader, root, kernel_virtual, config) {
            Ok(PageWalkOutcome::Mapped(translation)) => translation,
            result => {
                kprintln!(
                    "cache-alias probe failed: {} kernel walk: {:?}",
                    label,
                    result
                );
                halt_forever();
            }
        };
        let hhdm_translation = match walk_virtual_address(reader, root, hhdm_virtual, config) {
            Ok(PageWalkOutcome::Mapped(translation)) => translation,
            result => {
                kprintln!(
                    "cache-alias probe failed: {} HHDM walk: {:?}",
                    label,
                    result
                );
                halt_forever();
            }
        };
        if kernel_translation.physical_address != physical
            || hhdm_translation.physical_address != physical
        {
            kprintln!(
                "cache-alias probe failed: {} physical {:#018x} has inconsistent translations",
                label,
                physical
            );
            halt_forever();
        }
        let kernel_type = match mtrrs.effective_memory_type_for(
            physical,
            pat,
            kernel_translation.pat_index,
            boot_info.cpu_info.normal_caching,
        ) {
            Ok(memory_type) => memory_type,
            Err(error) => {
                kprintln!(
                    "cache-alias probe failed: {} kernel PAT/MTRR: {:?}",
                    label,
                    error
                );
                halt_forever();
            }
        };
        let hhdm_type = match mtrrs.effective_memory_type_for(
            physical,
            pat,
            hhdm_translation.pat_index,
            boot_info.cpu_info.normal_caching,
        ) {
            Ok(memory_type) => memory_type,
            Err(error) => {
                kprintln!(
                    "cache-alias probe failed: {} HHDM PAT/MTRR: {:?}",
                    label,
                    error
                );
                halt_forever();
            }
        };
        if kernel_type != hhdm_type {
            kprintln!(
                "cache-alias conflict: {} PA {:#018x}, kernel {:?} vs HHDM {:?}",
                label,
                physical,
                kernel_type,
                hhdm_type
            );
            halt_forever();
        }
        pages += 1;
        offset += rustix_kernel::paging::PAGE_SIZE;
    }
    kprintln!(
        "cache-alias probe passed: {} ({} pages; effective types match)",
        label,
        pages
    );
}

fn release_probe_frame(
    allocator: &mut rustix_kernel::frame::FrameAllocator,
    frame: rustix_kernel::frame::Frame,
) {
    if let Err(error) = allocator.deallocate(frame) {
        kprintln!(
            "HHDM frame probe failed to return its frame: {:?}",
            error.error
        );
        halt_forever();
    }
}

#[cfg(feature = "inject-page-fault")]
fn run_fault_injection() {
    kprintln!("fault injection: triggering page fault at 0x00000000deadbeef");
    // SAFETY: This is an opt-in QEMU test that deliberately reads an unmapped
    // low virtual address; the installed page-fault handler is expected to halt.
    unsafe {
        core::arch::asm!(
            "mov rax, 0xdeadbeef",
            "mov rax, qword ptr [rax]",
            out("rax") _,
            options(nostack)
        );
    }
    kprintln!("fault injection unexpectedly returned");
    halt_forever();
}

#[cfg(feature = "inject-invalid-opcode")]
fn run_fault_injection() {
    kprintln!("fault injection: triggering invalid opcode with ud2");
    // SAFETY: This is an opt-in QEMU test that deliberately raises #UD; the
    // installed invalid-opcode handler is expected to halt.
    unsafe { core::arch::asm!("ud2", options(nomem, nostack)) };
    kprintln!("fault injection unexpectedly returned");
    halt_forever();
}

#[panic_handler]
fn panic(info: &PanicInfo<'_>) -> ! {
    arch::x86_64::serial::initialize();
    kprintln!("KERNEL PANIC: {}", info);
    halt_forever()
}

fn halt_forever() -> ! {
    loop {
        // SAFETY: The bootstrap has no interrupt handlers or scheduler to resume.
        unsafe { core::arch::asm!("cli; hlt", options(nomem, nostack)) };
    }
}

 ## What exists now

+`src/memory.rs` contains an allocation-free `MemoryMapBuilder` that copies Limine ranges into validated half-open physical regions. It rejects empty ranges, `base + length` overflow, overlapping ranges, empty maps, and maps exceeding the fixed 256-region capacity. Known Limine types remain distinct, and unknown type values are preserved. Host-side tests cover range validation/classification, canonical-address boundaries, physical-width bounds, and HHDM range arithmetic. `src/boot.rs` stores the resulting map in an owned boot snapshot and reports usable bytes.

-`src/frame.rs` provides a fixed-capacity allocator core with host-side tests. It only manages complete 4 KiB frames inside validated `Usable` regions, reserves the first MiB, and rejects invalid/double frees while merging adjacent ranges. Its bounded range metadata can report fragmentation exhaustion. The kernel initializes it from the validated map, retains it in `BootInfo`, and exposes counts through Crabshell's `meminfo` command. It does not yet allocate frames for kernel services or map/dereference any allocated frame. Rustix does not reclaim bootloader memory, own or replace the inherited Limine page tables, or provide a heap. The HHDM offset is checked and logged, not used for memory access. Bootstrap GDT/TSS/IDT setup and fatal exception diagnostics live in `src/arch/x86_64/interrupts.rs`; they do not enable maskable IRQs.
+`src/frame.rs` provides a fixed-capacity allocator core with host-side tests. It only manages complete 4 KiB frames inside validated `Usable` regions, reserves the first MiB, and coalesces adjacent free ranges. The ownership contract assumes one allocator instance per physical map: within that instance, each eligible frame is owned either by its free-range table or by a non-copyable `Frame` token while allocated. The public constructor does not enforce unique instances, so callers must not initialize multiple allocators for the same physical map; the boot path retains one allocator in `BootInfo`. `allocate` returns `None` when no free frame remains. `deallocate` consumes the token only on success; on any error, including free-range-table exhaustion, it returns a `DeallocationError` containing the original token and leaves allocator state unchanged. The range tables each have a fixed `MAX_FRAME_RANGES` capacity, so fragmentation can prevent a frame from being returned until nearby ranges coalesce. The active cloned page-table hierarchy owns its page-table frames; the frame allocator is otherwise not yet a general-purpose virtual-memory service.
+
+`Frame::address()` is a physical address value, not a dereferenceable pointer and not a proof that the frame is mapped. CPU diagnostics now read `CR4.LA57` to report the active linear-address width (48 or 57 bits) and query `CPUID.80000008H` for physical and maximum linear-address widths when available. Boot-protocol pointers are checked against the active width, with host tests for 48- and 57-bit canonical boundaries. These facts do not prove that any physical address is mapped.
+
+`src/paging.rs` contains host-tested mapping and cache policy plus a bounded candidate-root builder. The CR3 decoder validates physical-address width and reserved bits and interprets its low 12 bits according to active `CR4.PCIDE`; it does not dereference the root. The mapping-range validator requires known physical width, checked aligned bounds, canonical virtual endpoints in one canonical half, and rejects writable-executable permissions. It can encode one 4 KiB leaf PTE with supervisor/user and write permissions, NX when EFER.NXE is confirmed, and a bounded PAT index. `PatLayout` parses supplied `IA32_PAT` values and selects WB, UC, or WC indexes. `MtrrMemoryType`, `VariableMtrr`, `FixedMtrrRanges`, and `MtrrLayout` resolve address-specific MTRR types, including fixed-range priority and defined variable-overlap rules; undefined overlaps fail closed. `MtrrRegisters::validated_layout` validates captured capability/default-type bits, register counts and fixed-range presence, WC support, and variable-mask shape/alignment before producing an owned layout. Rustix supports contiguous power-of-two variable masks and explicitly rejects unsupported discontinuous masks. The layout combines address-specific MTRR type and PAT selection according to Intel SDM Table 11-7 only when `CR0.CD` and `CR0.NW` are clear. Host tests cover all 30 documented MTRR/PAT pairs and malformed inputs. A pure range selector chooses an index only when its effective type is uniform throughout all fixed/variable MTRR boundaries in an aligned extent; selected attributes remain bound to that physical extent. The selector itself does not inspect PTEs, aliases, or frame ownership. Boot reads CR0 without modifying it, validates captured MTRR/PAT state, and reports a diagnostic PA 0 resolution; this does not assert the live PTE's type. MTRR capture is bounded to 32 variable pairs and rejects excess capacity without partial state.
+
+`CandidatePageTables` owns a separate root, bounded to 32 table frames and 256 explicitly mapped leaf frames. It accepts only allocator-issued `Frame` tokens, requires NXE, supports four- and five-level paths, and holds one exclusive mutable borrow of its unsafe memory backend so prepared handles cannot be mixed across backends. The default boot path clones the complete reachable Limine hierarchy, rewrites inherited kernel HHDM aliases to text/rodata R/NX and data RW/NX while preserving PAT bits, verifies critical translations, activates the cloned CR3, and retains the candidate tokens for the active root's lifetime. The CR3 transition invalidates the active PCID and toggles CR4.PGE when enabled so cached global translations cannot retain the previous alias permissions; the same invalidation is used if verification requires restoring the inherited root. Active candidates reject mapping, unmapping, and release; the type never writes CR3. Host tests cover clone ownership, huge-page splitting, cache-bit preservation, mutation guards, transactional map rollback, and retryable release failure. The QEMU adapter derives table pointers only from complete allocator-owned `Usable` frames through checked HHDM arithmetic.
+
+The opt-in `just frame-smoke` probe reads the inherited root and follows paths for every page in kernel text/rodata/data and the requested stack span. The transition clones every reachable present table and preserves leaf mappings, then rewrites and validates the kernel-image HHDM aliases. The kernel and HHDM aliases retain the same PAT index; MTRR state is unchanged. This is not a fresh address-space policy or a hardware-level exhaustive inventory, and it does not reclaim the inherited root or bootloader memory.
+
+The effective-type resolver follows [Intel SDM Vol. 3A §11.5.2.2, Table 11-7](https://cdrdv2-public.intel.com/671447/325384-sdm-vol-3abcd.pdf), which applies when normal caching is enabled (`CR0.CD=0`, `CR0.NW=0`). Its footnotes distinguish UC selected by an MTRR from UC selected by a page-table entry (the latter involves cache snooping and aliasing concerns); they also identify combinations that older manual editions called undefined but current processors supporting both PAT and MTRRs resolve as shown. The resolver does not cover legacy PCD/PWT-only selection or model-specific combinations outside that table.
+
+The requested Limine base revision is 3. Its protocol maps only `Usable`, `BootloaderReclaimable`, `ExecutableAndModules`, and `Framebuffer` memory-map regions into the HHDM; reserved, ACPI, bad, and unknown regions are not in that mapping set. HHDM mappings use at least 4 KiB granularity and may cover page-aligned bytes beyond unaligned region boundaries. Limine's inherited HHDM mappings are supervisor RWX, normally write-back cached, with framebuffer mappings write-combining when PAT is available. Before activating the cloned root, Rustix splits inherited huge pages where needed and changes the kernel image HHDM aliases to the matching R/NX or RW/NX policy while retaining PAT bits. The rest of the HHDM remains inherited; an HHDM offset is not a blanket physical-memory access grant. See the [Limine base revision 3 protocol](https://github.com/limine-bootloader/limine-protocol/blob/trunk/PROTOCOL.md#base-revision-3) and its memory-layout/caching sections.
+
+The boot snapshot now rejects physical map ranges beyond the reported CPUID physical-address width when that CPUID leaf is available. For base revision 3 HHDM-mapped types, it also validates the page-rounded physical span, checked `offset + address` arithmetic, and canonical endpoints in the active linear-address width. If the CPU does not report a physical width, the physical-bound check is skipped and no mapping caller may treat the bound as known. These checks are derived from metadata and Limine's protocol contract; they do not inspect page tables or prove that a non-null loader pointer is readable. HHDM dereferences are limited to the opt-in QEMU frame probe and candidate-table backend. Both first validate a complete allocator-owned `Usable` frame and its checked HHDM address, then rely narrowly on Limine's base-revision-3 guarantee; this is not a general physical-memory access service. Rustix-owned mappings should be non-executable by default; executable kernel text must be explicit. MMIO requires an explicit device range and cache policy, and guard regions must remain unmapped. A page-table transition must preserve the kernel image, active stacks, boot data, descriptor tables, and any loader mappings still needed. Rustix does not reclaim bootloader memory or provide a general-purpose physical-memory service. It owns the page-table frames of the active cloned hierarchy but leaves inherited leaf frames and the old root unreclaimed. The initial 256 KiB global heap is a bounded BSS arena and does not grow from physical frames. Bootstrap GDT/TSS/IDT setup and fatal exception diagnostics live in `src/arch/x86_64/interrupts.rs`; they do not enable maskable IRQs.
+
+## Active-root preservation and remaining limits
+
+The transition clones the complete reachable inherited hierarchy rather than building a clean address space. It preserves all reachable present leaves and non-present entries, owns each cloned intermediate table, and fails closed on malformed entries, unsupported page sizes, cross-level table aliases, or fixed-capacity exhaustion. Kernel text/rodata/data HHDM aliases are then adjusted to avoid writable-executable aliases. Limine's original root and leaf frames remain intact.
+
+- **Kernel ELF image:** `linker.ld` places `.text`, `.rodata`, `.limine_requests`, `.data`, `.bss`, and `.got` in three `PT_LOAD` segments: RX text, read-only rodata, and RW data/BSS. It exports `__kernel_start` and `__kernel_end` around the complete loadable image, plus page-aligned bounds for each segment. `BootInfo` checks that Limine's reported virtual base matches the linker start, validates ordered contiguous segment bounds covering the rounded image, derives corresponding half-open physical ranges from the executable physical base with checked arithmetic, and validates canonical virtual and reported physical address widths. The release ELF and QEMU runtime report both showed the three aligned ranges on 2026-10-21. The RX, R/NX, and RW/NX labels describe the linker segment intent; these are linker/boot metadata, not proof that the inherited page tables map every page or enforce those permissions, nor proof that loader pointers are readable. The memory-map `ExecutableAndModules` entries remain illustrative, not an authoritative kernel-image extent.
+- **Active stack and `BootInfo`:** The assembly `_start` shim captures Limine's entry `RSP` before any Rust prologue. Under the SysV entry convention the synthetic return slot occupies 8 bytes, so `RSP + 8` is the exclusive stack top. Rustix requests a 256 KiB Limine stack and requires the stack-size response; `BootInfo` records and validates that requested span through the HHDM, including its `BootloaderReclaimable` backing. The loader may allocate more, and no guard page is inferred. QEMU transition tests walk all 64 requested stack pages.
+- **Kernel static data:** `RAM_FILESYSTEM`, GDT, IDT, TSS, the ring-0 stack, and double-fault IST stack are static BSS/data in the kernel image. Exception entry also requires the handler code and the TSS/IDT references to remain mapped. Preserve the complete relevant data/BSS pages and stack pages.
+- **Limine request data:** request records are in the kernel's writable `.limine_requests` segment. Response objects and the memory-map pointer array are bootloader-reclaimable; `capture_boot_information` copies the values used later, and the shell does not retain those pointers. Keep them mapped until the copy and validation finish; any later reclaim must be explicit rather than reclaiming the whole bootloader-reclaimable class.
+- **Inherited page tables:** Limine places its page tables in bootloader-reclaimable memory, but their layout is unspecified. `BootInfo` captures raw CR3 and validates the decoded root address and active low-bit mode. The default boot path clones all reachable page-table pages into allocator-owned frames and preserves all leaf entries, then changes only the kernel-image HHDM alias permission bits while retaining cache attributes. It verifies kernel segments, the requested stack span, and the candidate-root HHDM alias before switching; afterward it verifies CR3 and the critical paths again. The inherited root and its backing pages remain untouched and are not reclaimed.
+- **Devices:** COM1 uses x86 port I/O and needs no MMIO virtual mapping. Rustix does not currently request or use a framebuffer. Any future framebuffer or device-register mapping needs an explicit physical range and cache policy.
+
+## Permissions and cache policy of the active clone
+
+The active root preserves Limine's inherited kernel virtual mappings and their cache attributes. Before switching, Rustix requires NXE and enforces the linker permissions for every kernel-image HHDM alias: text and rodata are read-only/NX, and data/BSS/GOT are RW/NX. This prevents writable-executable aliases without discarding the HHDM alias. Huge-page leaves are split as necessary; unaffected entries retain their mappings and PAT/MTRR effective types. The remainder of the HHDM and all non-kernel aliases remain as Limine supplied them, so this is not yet a comprehensive Rustix mapping policy.
+
+Preserve the inherited PAT/MTRR configuration during the first transition. The boot report validates captured registers and computes a diagnostic effective type from the active PAT/MTRR values under normal caching. A separate pure selector can choose an index whose effective type remains uniform across an aligned physical range; the selector itself does not inspect PTEs or aliases. The opt-in `just frame-smoke` probe now compares effective types of the inherited kernel and HHDM aliases for kernel-image pages, but it is not a full alias inventory. The pure combination follows Intel SDM Table 11-7; it is not a generic rule for legacy PCD/PWT-only selection or model-specific combinations. The active transition retains the inherited PAT and MTRR state and changes no cache-selection bits. The page-table split copies large-page PAT selection to the equivalent 4 KiB/2 MiB entries. Future MMIO mappings must still use explicit device ranges and a verified cache policy; do not infer MMIO from generic reserved memory-map entries. COM1 uses port I/O and requires no MMIO mapping.
+
+Do not use huge pages in the first root; add them only when physical coverage, permissions, and cache attributes are uniform across the entire huge-page extent. Future Rustix-owned downward-growing stacks should have at least one 4 KiB unmapped guard page below them. The Limine bootstrap stack has no known guard, so none may be assumed there.
+
+Never modify Limine's active page tables in place. `src/paging.rs` builds an owned clone in allocator-issued frames, can split inherited large pages to update leaf permissions, and supports transactional 4 KiB map/unmap operations before activation. The default boot path validates critical translations and kernel alias permissions, switches CR3 while invalidating stale global translations via a CR4.PGE toggle when needed, verifies the active root, and retains its frame tokens for the active lifetime. The inherited root and backing memory remain intact. This preserves inherited mappings rather than constructing a new address space; broader mapping inventory, non-kernel permission policy, reclamation, and a general mapping service remain future work.

 ## Planned memory layers

 1. **Validated physical regions:** implemented as a fixed-capacity owned snapshot; allocator ownership and reclaim policy remain future work.
-2. **Frame allocator integration:** the bounded core is initialized from `BootInfo`; add real allocation callers only after the page-mapping policy and ownership rules are implemented.
-3. **Kernel virtual memory:** Rustix still runs on inherited Limine page tables. Before replacing them, preserve the executing kernel, bootstrap/Ring-0 stacks, request/response data, and exception stacks; define the HHDM extent and explicit mapping permissions/cache attributes. Keep writable-executable mappings disallowed by default and reserve MMIO and guard regions.
-4. **Heap:** add a global allocator only after frame allocation and page mapping are initialized. Define allocation failure behavior for kernel and interrupt contexts.
+4. **Frame allocator integration:** the bounded core is initialized from `BootInfo`; the active cloned hierarchy owns its table frames, while the opt-in QEMU frame probe is the only general frame allocation test. Add active mapping services only after a TLB and mapping-lifetime policy exists.
+3. **Kernel virtual memory:** Rustix runs on an active cloned hierarchy whose page-table frames it owns. The clone preserves Limine's mappings and applies R/NX or RW/NX permissions to kernel-image HHDM aliases. It is not a clean address-space rebuild, and general mapping/unmapping after activation is deliberately rejected without a TLB policy.
+4. **Heap:** an initial global allocator uses a fixed 256 KiB BSS arena and at most 128 live allocations. It has deterministic exhaustion and exact-layout free semantics, does not grow from frames, and must not be called in interrupt context.
 5. **Process address spaces:** isolate userspace; define copy-in/copy-out helpers and never treat user pointers as kernel references.

 ## Invariants to preserve

 - Physical ranges use checked arithmetic and the half-open convention `[start, end)`.
-- Reserved regions are never returned as free frames.
-- A failed allocation leaves allocator state unchanged.
+- Only complete frames in validated `Usable` regions enter the allocator; the first MiB remains reserved. Firmware and loader-reclaimable regions are not silently promoted to free memory.
+- Under the single-allocator-per-physical-map contract, a frame is represented by one allocator-free range or one caller-owned, non-copyable `Frame` token. Only a successful `deallocate` transfers the token back to the allocator; errors return the token and leave allocator ranges and accounting unchanged. The current public constructor relies on callers to enforce unique allocator instances.
+- `allocate` returns `None` on frame exhaustion. Metadata-capacity exhaustion is an explicit error, never silent loss of a frame.
+- A `Frame` address is physical, not directly dereferenceable. HHDM translation and table access are limited to checked full-frame token-based paths that rely on Limine's documented mapping contract. Candidate mutations are allowed only before activation and only in owned tables. The active cloned root retains its ownership tokens and rejects mutation/release until an explicit, reviewed CR3 transition away from it.
 - Mapping changes validate alignment, canonical addresses, ownership, and permissions before touching tables.
 - User-controlled addresses are validated on every syscall boundary; prior validation is not a substitute for access checks during later copies.
-- Tests cover unaligned edges, exact-boundary allocations, arithmetic overflow, overlaps, and exhaustion.
+- Tests cover unaligned edges, exact-boundary allocations, arithmetic overflow, overlaps, exhaustion, and unchanged state/ownership on failure.

-These are design requirements for future milestones, not functionality delivered by the current boot summary.
+The active root is a full clone of Limine's reachable hierarchy with kernel HHDM alias W^X hardening, not a clean-room Rustix address space. The fixed BSS heap is bounded and non-growing. General mapping policy, broader alias/MMIO coverage, frame reclamation, and physical-hardware validation remain outstanding.
