The normal boot path in this image also clones the full reachable inherited hierarchy, hardens kernel-image HHDM aliases to text/rodata R/NX and data RW/NX while retaining PAT bits, switches CR3 with active-PCID and global-TLB invalidation, verifies the active root and critical mappings, and exercises the global heap's alignment, reuse, and deterministic exhaustion. The smoke test requires a serial marker confirming the applicable TLB invalidation path. The workflow restores the default release kernel and ISO. These probes rely on Limine's HHDM contract and do not inventory every unrelated mapping or prove physical-hardware correctness. `just fault-smoke` separately builds opt-in kernel variants that deliberately trigger a page fault and an invalid opcode. It requires each QEMU run to report the expected exception (and CR2 for the page fault), avoid the shell prompt, and remain halted until timeout. It then rebuilds and restores the default release kernel and ISO. These are fatal-path diagnostics, not exception recovery tests; diagnostic Cargo features are disabled by default and mutually exclusive.
+
+Keep the Crabshell parser, VFS, memory-map validator, paging policy helpers, frame allocator, and fixed heap independent of hardware so syntax, path handling, address and leaf-PTE bit policy, PAT/MTRR policy, storage semantics, frame ownership, HHDM/root-range calculations, allocation alignment, reuse, and exhaustion can be tested without booting. Pure tests validate captured MTRR register snapshots, resolve the Intel SDM Table 11-7 PAT/MTRR combinations for one physical address, select a PAT index that remains uniform across MTRR boundaries in an aligned range, bind that selection to validated mapping metadata before encoding leaves, and walk synthetic four-/five-level page tables including large-page leaves. Host tests also exercise the candidate builder's owned-table walk, clone ownership, 4-/5-level mapping, 2 MiB/1 GiB splitting, permission/cache-bit preservation, active-state mutation/release guard, transactional allocation/prepare rollback, and retryable frame-release failure. Heap tests cover alignment, exact-layout free/reuse, zero-sized rejection, metadata exhaustion, and arena exhaustion. Tests reject malformed state, unsupported discontinuous masks, invalid indexes/ranges, out-of-range addresses, mismatched physical widths, and non-normal caching mode. The pure inherited-table walker does not access hardware tables; the opt-in QEMU reader and candidate backend use checked HHDM addresses. Boot-time QEMU checks a subset of live kernel/HHDM aliases but does not inventory all aliases or prove complete transition safety. Boot separately captures the registers and CR0 caching mode read-only and reports a diagnostic resolution; this is not a page-table or mapping test. The GDT/TSS/IDT and CPU-register paths are privileged kernel code; QEMU boot and fault-injection checks complement, but do not replace, static review and target builds. Add tests for boundaries and failure behavior when introducing new pure kernel helpers. The kernel binary is not a host test target.

 ## What current checks do not prove

 - `cargo check` does not perform a final target link.
 - A successful ELF link does not prove the boot protocol is recognized or `_start` is reached.
-- Host unit tests do not validate privileged instructions, UART behavior, memory-map pointer validity, page tables, interrupts, or actual hardware.
-- The automated QEMU smoke test checks only that the kernel reaches the shell prompt. A separate manual QEMU session exercised directory navigation and file create/write/append/read/copy/move/remove operations, including `cp` replacing an existing destination and rejection of `rmdir` on a nonempty directory. This is not exhaustive shell coverage and does not prove persistence across reboot.
+- Host unit tests do not validate privileged instructions, UART behavior, memory-map pointer validity, page tables, interrupts, or actual hardware. The QEMU boot path exercises the gated EFER/PAT reads and bounded MTRR capture and prints diagnostic summaries, but the prompt smoke assertion does not make those facts a mapping-safety proof.
+- The automated QEMU prompt smoke test asserts the cloned CR3 transition, active-PCID/global-TLB invalidation path, kernel HHDM alias permissions/cache preservation, heap probe, and shell prompt. `just frame-smoke` additionally exercises one allocator-owned frame, inherited paths, kernel/HHDM cache aliases, and a separate candidate mapping through Limine's HHDM contract. The clone preserves Limine's complete reachable hierarchy, but there is no clean-room mapping policy or exhaustive audit of unrelated aliases; emulator tests do not establish physical-hardware behavior. `just fault-smoke` exercises only the controlled page-fault and invalid-opcode fatal paths; it does not test every exception vector or recovery.
+- A separate manual QEMU session exercised directory navigation and file create/write/append/read/copy/move/remove operations, including `cp` replacing an existing destination and rejection of `rmdir` on a nonempty directory. This is not exhaustive shell coverage and does not prove persistence across reboot.
 - There is no on-disk filesystem integration test, syscall/userspace test, fuzz target, or physical-hardware test.

+def fault_smoke_test(kind: str, timeout: int) -> None:
+    qemu = require_tool("qemu-system-x86_64")
+    if not ISO_PATH.is_file():
+        raise BuildError("boot image not found; build the fault-injection image first")
+
+    serial_log = TARGET_DIR / f"rustix-qemu-fault-{kind}.log"
+    serial_log.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
+    serial_log.unlink(missing_ok=True)
+    serial_device = "file:" + serial_log.relative_to(ROOT).as_posix()
+    command = [
+        qemu,
+        "-machine",
+        "q35",
+        "-m",
+        "256M",
+        "-cdrom",
+        str(ISO_PATH),
+        "-boot",
+        "d",
+        "-display",
+        "none",
+        "-monitor",
+        "none",
+        "-serial",
+        serial_device,
+        "-no-reboot",
+        "-no-shutdown",
+    ]
+
+    timed_out = False
+    try:
+        result = subprocess.run(command, cwd=ROOT, timeout=timeout, check=False)
+    except subprocess.TimeoutExpired:
+        timed_out = True
+        result = None
+
+    output = serial_log.read_text(encoding="latin-1") if serial_log.exists() else ""
+    if kind == "page-fault":
+        expected = (
+            "fault injection: triggering page fault at 0x00000000deadbeef",
+            "KERNEL EXCEPTION: vector 14 (page fault)",
+            "page fault address (CR2): 0x00000000deadbeef",
+        )
+    elif kind == "invalid-opcode":
+        expected = (
+            "fault injection: triggering invalid opcode with ud2",
+            "KERNEL EXCEPTION: vector 6 (invalid opcode)",
+        )
+    else:
+        raise BuildError(f"unsupported fault-injection test: {kind}")
+
+    missing = [marker for marker in expected if marker not in output]
+    if missing:
+        raise BuildError(
+            f"QEMU did not report the expected {kind} exception; missing serial markers: "
+            + ", ".join(repr(marker) for marker in missing)
+            + f"\nSerial output:\n{output or '<empty>'}"
+        )
+    if "root@rustix:/home/rustix# " in output:
+        raise BuildError(f"kernel reached the shell after {kind} injection\nSerial output:\n{output}")
+    if "fault injection unexpectedly returned" in output:
+        raise BuildError(f"{kind} instruction returned instead of faulting\nSerial output:\n{output}")
+    if not timed_out:
+        status = result.returncode if result is not None else "unknown"
+        raise BuildError(
+            f"QEMU did not remain halted after {kind} (exit status {status})\n"
+            f"Serial output:\n{output}"
+        )
+
+    print(f"QEMU {kind} fault-injection test passed (halt observed within {timeout}s).")
+    print(f"Captured serial log: {serial_log.relative_to(ROOT)}")
+
+
+def build_kernel(features: tuple[str, ...] = ()) -> None:
+    command = ["cargo", "build", "--release", "--target", "x86_64-unknown-none"]
+    if features:
+        command.extend(["--features", ",".join(features)])
+    subprocess.run(command, cwd=ROOT, check=True)
+
+
+def frame_smoke_workflow(timeout: int) -> None:
+    failure: BaseException | None = None
+    try:
+        build_kernel(("probe-hhdm-frame",))
+        build_image()
+        smoke_test(timeout)
+        serial_log = TARGET_DIR / "rustix-qemu-serial.log"
+        output = serial_log.read_text(encoding="latin-1") if serial_log.exists() else ""
+        markers = (
+            "HHDM frame probe passed: wrote, read, cleared, and reclaimed one frame",
+            "inherited root HHDM probe passed: read 512 entries",
+            "candidate inherited-root clone probe passed:",
+            "candidate page-table probe passed: mapped, walked, unmapped, and released",
+        )
+        missing = [marker for marker in markers if marker not in output]
+        if missing:
+            raise BuildError(
+                "QEMU did not report successful HHDM access probes; missing markers: "
+                + ", ".join(repr(marker) for marker in missing)
+                + f"\nSerial output:\n{output}"
+            )
+        print("QEMU HHDM, inherited-mapping, cloned-root, and candidate-map probes passed.")
+    except BaseException as error:
+        failure = error
+
+    try:
+        build_kernel()
+        build_image()
+    except BaseException as restore_error:
+        if failure is not None:
+            raise BuildError(
+                f"HHDM frame workflow failed ({failure}); restoring the default image "
+                f"also failed ({restore_error})"
+            ) from restore_error
+        raise
+
+    if failure is not None:
+        raise BuildError(
+            f"HHDM frame workflow failed; the default release image was restored: {failure}"
+        ) from failure
+    print("Restored the default release kernel and ISO after the HHDM frame probe.")
+
+

+pub fn read_cr3_raw() -> u64 {

+/// must remain disabled during the transition.

+    // SAFETY: The caller establishes the page-table and transition invariants.
+    unsafe { asm!("mov cr3, {}", in(reg) value, options(nostack, preserves_flags)) };

+    // clear across the CR3 write so the target context starts without stale
+    // global translations, then restore the original control-register state.
+    // SAFETY: Only CR4.PGE is modified, and the original value is restored.
+    unsafe { write_cr4_raw(cr4 & !CR4_PGE) };

+fn harden_kernel_hhdm_aliases(
+    candidate: &mut rustix_kernel::paging::CandidatePageTables<'_, LimineHhdmCandidateMemory<'_>>,
+    allocator: &mut rustix_kernel::frame::FrameAllocator,
+    memory_map: &rustix_kernel::memory::MemoryMap,
+    hhdm_offset: u64,
+    physical_address_bits: Option<u8>,
+    virtual_address_bits: u8,
+    segments: rustix_kernel::memory::KernelImageSegments,
+    reader: &impl rustix_kernel::paging::PageTableReader<
+        Error = rustix_kernel::memory::HhdmAddressError,
+    >,
+    inherited_root: rustix_kernel::paging::Cr3Root,
+    config: rustix_kernel::paging::PageWalkConfig,
+) -> bool {
+    use rustix_kernel::paging::{
+        walk_virtual_address, PagePermissions, PageWalkOutcome, PAGE_SIZE,
+    };
+
+    let image_segments = [
+        ("kernel text", segments.text, false),
+        ("kernel rodata", segments.rodata, false),
+        ("kernel data", segments.data, true),
+    ];
+    for (label, segment, writable) in image_segments {
+        let length = segment.physical_end - segment.physical_start;
+        let mut offset = 0;
+        while offset < length {
+            let Some(physical_address) = segment.physical_start.checked_add(offset) else {
+                kprintln!(
+                    "kernel HHDM alias check failed: {} physical overflow",
+                    label
+                );
+                return false;
+            };
+            let alias = match memory_map.limine_hhdm_address(
+                hhdm_offset,
+                physical_address,
+                PAGE_SIZE,
+                physical_address_bits,
+                virtual_address_bits,
+            ) {
+                Ok(alias) => alias,
+                Err(error) => {
+                    kprintln!(
+                        "kernel HHDM alias check failed: {} address: {:?}",
+                        label,
+                        error
+                    );
+                    return false;
+                }
+            };
+            let source = match walk_virtual_address(reader, inherited_root, alias, config) {
+                Ok(PageWalkOutcome::Mapped(translation)) => translation,
+                result => {
+                    kprintln!(
+                        "kernel HHDM alias check failed: {} inherited walk: {:?}",
+                        label,
+                        result
+                    );
+                    return false;
+                }
+            };
+            let permissions = PagePermissions {
+                writable,
+                executable: false,
+                user_accessible: false,
+            };
+            if let Err(error) = candidate.set_inherited_page_permissions(
+                allocator,
+                alias,
+                physical_address,
+                permissions,
+            ) {
+                kprintln!(
+                    "kernel HHDM alias check failed: {} protection: {:?}",
+                    label,
+                    error
+                );
+                return false;
+            }
+            match candidate.walk(alias) {
+                Ok(PageWalkOutcome::Mapped(translation))
+                    if translation.physical_address == physical_address
+                        && translation.permissions == permissions
+                        && translation.pat_index == source.pat_index => {}
+                result => {
+                    kprintln!(
+                        "kernel HHDM alias check failed: {} candidate walk: {:?}",
+                        label,
+                        result
+                    );
+                    return false;
+                }
+            }
+            offset += PAGE_SIZE;
+        }
+    }
+    true
+}

+fn probe_kernel_heap() {
+    use core::alloc::{GlobalAlloc, Layout};
+
+    let full_layout = match Layout::from_size_align(rustix_kernel::heap::KERNEL_HEAP_CAPACITY, 1) {
+        Ok(layout) => layout,
+        Err(error) => {
+            kprintln!(
+                "kernel heap probe failed to construct full-arena layout: {:?}",
+                error
+            );
+            halt_forever();
+        }
+    };
+    // SAFETY: The heap static is initialized before use and maskable interrupts
+    // remain disabled; this probe requests a valid nonzero layout.
+    let full_arena = unsafe { KERNEL_HEAP.alloc(full_layout) };
+    if full_arena.is_null() {
+        kprintln!("kernel heap probe failed: full-arena allocation was rejected");
+        halt_forever();
+    }
+    let small_layout = Layout::new::<u8>();
+    // SAFETY: The heap lock serializes this valid nonzero allocation request.
+    let exhausted = unsafe { KERNEL_HEAP.alloc(small_layout) };
+    if !exhausted.is_null() {
+        // SAFETY: Both pointers are live allocations with their original layouts.
+        unsafe {
+            KERNEL_HEAP.dealloc(exhausted, small_layout);
+            KERNEL_HEAP.dealloc(full_arena, full_layout);
+        }
+        kprintln!("kernel heap probe failed: exhaustion was not deterministic");
+        halt_forever();
+    }
+    // SAFETY: `full_arena` is the complete live allocation created above.
+    unsafe { KERNEL_HEAP.dealloc(full_arena, full_layout) };
+
+    let layout = match Layout::from_size_align(257, 64) {
+        Ok(layout) => layout,
+        Err(error) => {
+            kprintln!(
+                "kernel heap probe failed to construct aligned layout: {:?}",
+                error
+            );
+            halt_forever();
+        }
+    };
+    // SAFETY: The heap is available after releasing the full-arena allocation.
+    let allocation = unsafe { KERNEL_HEAP.alloc(layout) };
+    if allocation.is_null() || allocation as usize % layout.align() != 0 {
+        if !allocation.is_null() {
+            // SAFETY: This is the live allocation returned for `layout`.
+            unsafe { KERNEL_HEAP.dealloc(allocation, layout) };
+        }
+        kprintln!("kernel heap probe failed: aligned allocation was rejected or misaligned");
+        halt_forever();
+    }
+    // SAFETY: The allocator returned `layout.size()` writable bytes.
+    unsafe { core::ptr::write_bytes(allocation, 0xa5, layout.size()) };
+    for index in 0..layout.size() {
+        // SAFETY: `index` remains inside the live allocation.
+        if unsafe { allocation.add(index).read_volatile() } != 0xa5 {
+            // SAFETY: The allocation is still live with its original layout.
+            unsafe { KERNEL_HEAP.dealloc(allocation, layout) };
+            kprintln!("kernel heap probe failed: allocation data did not round-trip");
+            halt_forever();
+        }
+    }
+    // SAFETY: The allocation is live and the original layout is supplied.
+    unsafe { KERNEL_HEAP.dealloc(allocation, layout) };
+    // SAFETY: The previous allocation was returned; first-fit should reuse it.
+    let reused = unsafe { KERNEL_HEAP.alloc(layout) };
+    if reused != allocation {
+        if !reused.is_null() {
+            // SAFETY: `reused` is a live allocation with `layout`.
+            unsafe { KERNEL_HEAP.dealloc(reused, layout) };
+        }
+        kprintln!("kernel heap probe failed: freed space was not reused");
+        halt_forever();
+    }
+    // SAFETY: The reused allocation is live and has the same layout.
+    unsafe { KERNEL_HEAP.dealloc(reused, layout) };
+    kprintln!("kernel heap probe passed: alignment, reuse, deterministic exhaustion");
+}

+#[cfg(feature = "probe-hhdm-frame")]
+fn probe_hhdm_frame(boot_info: &mut boot::BootInfo) {
+    use rustix_kernel::frame::FRAME_SIZE;
+
+    let frame = match boot_info.frame_allocator.allocate() {
+        Some(frame) => frame,
+        None => {
+            kprintln!("HHDM frame probe failed: no free frame");
+            halt_forever();
+        }
+    };
+    let hhdm_address = match frame.hhdm_address(
+        &boot_info.memory_map,
+        boot_info.hhdm_offset,
+        boot_info.cpu_info.physical_address_bits,
+        boot_info.cpu_info.active_linear_address_bits,
+    ) {
+        Ok(address) => address,
+        Err(error) => {
+            kprintln!("HHDM frame probe rejected frame translation: {:?}", error);
+            release_probe_frame(&mut boot_info.frame_allocator, frame);
+            halt_forever();
+        }
+    };
+
+    let words = (FRAME_SIZE / core::mem::size_of::<u64>() as u64) as usize;
+    let page = hhdm_address as *mut u64;
+    let mut verified = true;
+    // SAFETY: The non-copyable `Frame` token is held exclusively; its full page
+    // is within validated `Usable` memory and its HHDM arithmetic was checked.
+    // Limine base revision 3 guarantees usable memory in the HHDM, and no other
+    // Rustix mapping aliases this newly allocated frame. This is an opt-in QEMU
+    // probe; a broken loader mapping would fault and be caught by the fatal path.
+    unsafe {
+        for index in 0..words {
+            page.add(index)
+                .write_volatile(0xa5a5_0000_0000_0000 ^ index as u64);
+        }
+        for index in 0..words {
+            if page.add(index).read_volatile() != (0xa5a5_0000_0000_0000 ^ index as u64) {
+                verified = false;
+                break;
+            }
+        }
+        for index in 0..words {
+            page.add(index).write_volatile(0);
+        }
+    }
+
+    release_probe_frame(&mut boot_info.frame_allocator, frame);
+    if !verified {
+        kprintln!("HHDM frame probe failed: readback mismatch");
+        halt_forever();
+    }
+    kprintln!("HHDM frame probe passed: wrote, read, cleared, and reclaimed one frame");
+    probe_inherited_root(boot_info);
+}

+#[cfg(feature = "probe-hhdm-frame")]
+fn probe_inherited_root(boot_info: &mut boot::BootInfo) {
+    use rustix_kernel::paging::inherited_cr3_root_hhdm_address;
+
+    let root = match boot_info.inherited_cr3_root {
+        Ok(root) => root,

+            kprintln!(
+                "inherited root probe failed: CR3 decode rejected: {:?}",
+                error
+            );
+            halt_forever();
+        }
+    };
+    let address = match inherited_cr3_root_hhdm_address(
+        root,
+        &boot_info.memory_map,
+        boot_info.hhdm_offset,
+        boot_info.cpu_info.physical_address_bits,
+        boot_info.cpu_info.active_linear_address_bits,
+    ) {
+        Ok(address) => address,
+        Err(error) => {
+            kprintln!(
+                "inherited root probe failed: HHDM validation rejected: {:?}",
+                error
+            );
+            halt_forever();
+        }
+    };
+    let entries = address as *const u64;
+    let mut present_entries = 0;
+    // SAFETY: The complete root page was validated as bootloader-reclaimable
+    // and its HHDM range arithmetic was checked. The Limine base-revision-3
+    // contract maps that region; this read-only opt-in probe trusts that handoff.
+    unsafe {
+        for index in 0..512 {
+            if entries.add(index).read_volatile() & 1 != 0 {
+                present_entries += 1;
+            }
+        }
+    }

+        "inherited root HHDM probe passed: read 512 entries, {} present",
+        present_entries
+    );

+        Some(bits) => bits,
+        None => {
+            kprintln!("inherited page-table walk failed: physical width unknown");
+            halt_forever();
+        }
+    };
+    let reader = LimineHhdmPageTableReader {
+        memory_map: &boot_info.memory_map,
+        hhdm_offset: boot_info.hhdm_offset,
+        physical_address_bits,
+        virtual_address_bits: boot_info.cpu_info.active_linear_address_bits,
+    };
+    let config = rustix_kernel::paging::PageWalkConfig {
+        levels: if boot_info.cpu_info.active_linear_address_bits == 57 {
+            5
+        } else {
+            4
+        },
+        physical_address_bits,
+        virtual_address_bits: boot_info.cpu_info.active_linear_address_bits,
+        nx_enabled: boot_info.cpu_info.nx_enabled,

+        root,
+        config,
+        "kernel rodata",
+        segments.rodata.virtual_start,
+        segments.rodata.physical_start,
+        segments.rodata.virtual_end - segments.rodata.virtual_start,
+    );
+    verify_inherited_mapping(
+        &reader,
+        root,
+        config,
+        "kernel data",
+        segments.data.virtual_start,
+        segments.data.physical_start,
+        segments.data.virtual_end - segments.data.virtual_start,

+    verify_inherited_mapping(

+    let pat_value = match boot_info.cpu_info.pat_msr_value {
+        Some(value) => value,

+            halt_forever();

+#[cfg(feature = "probe-hhdm-frame")]
+fn probe_cloned_page_tables(
+    allocator: &mut rustix_kernel::frame::FrameAllocator,
+    memory_map: &rustix_kernel::memory::MemoryMap,
+    hhdm_offset: u64,
+    physical_address_bits: u8,
+    virtual_address_bits: u8,
+    source_reader: &impl rustix_kernel::paging::PageTableReader<
+        Error = rustix_kernel::memory::HhdmAddressError,
+    >,
+    source_root: rustix_kernel::paging::Cr3Root,
+    config: rustix_kernel::paging::PageWalkConfig,
+    spans: [(&str, u64, u64, u64); 4],
+) {
+    use rustix_kernel::paging::CandidatePageTables;
+
+    let mut memory = LimineHhdmCandidateMemory {
+        memory_map,
+        hhdm_offset,
+        physical_address_bits,
+        virtual_address_bits,
+    };
+    let mut candidate = match CandidatePageTables::new(allocator, &mut memory, config) {
+        Ok(candidate) => candidate,
+        Err(error) => {
+            kprintln!(
+                "candidate clone probe failed to create root: {:?}",
+                error.cause
+            );
+            if let Some(frame) = error.frame {
+                release_probe_frame(allocator, frame);
+            }
+            halt_forever();
+        }
+    };
+    if let Err(error) = candidate.clone_inherited_hierarchy(allocator, source_reader, source_root) {
+        kprintln!("candidate clone probe failed: {:?}", error);
+        release_candidate_after_probe_failure(candidate, allocator);
+    }
+    for (label, virtual_start, physical_start, length) in spans {
+        if !candidate_span_matches_source(
+            &candidate,
+            source_reader,
+            source_root,
+            config,
+            virtual_start,
+            physical_start,
+            length,
+        ) {
+            kprintln!(
+                "candidate clone probe failed: {} translation mismatch",
+                label
+            );
+            release_candidate_after_probe_failure(candidate, allocator);
+        }
+    }
+    let table_count = candidate.table_count();
+    if let Err(failure) = candidate.release(allocator) {
+        kprintln!(
+            "candidate clone probe failed to release frames: {:?}",
+            failure
+        );
+        halt_forever();
+    }
+    kprintln!(
+        "candidate inherited-root clone probe passed: {} owned table pages preserve critical paths; CR3 unchanged",
+        table_count
+    );
+}

+fn candidate_span_matches_source(
+    candidate: &rustix_kernel::paging::CandidatePageTables<'_, LimineHhdmCandidateMemory<'_>>,
+    source_reader: &impl rustix_kernel::paging::PageTableReader<
+        Error = rustix_kernel::memory::HhdmAddressError,
+    >,
+    source_root: rustix_kernel::paging::Cr3Root,
+    config: rustix_kernel::paging::PageWalkConfig,
+    virtual_start: u64,
+    physical_start: u64,
+    length: u64,
+) -> bool {
+    use rustix_kernel::paging::{walk_virtual_address, PageWalkOutcome};
+
+    let mut offset = 0;

+            (source, candidate) => {

+            || source_translation.page_size != candidate_translation.page_size
+            || source_translation.permissions != candidate_translation.permissions
+            || source_translation.pat_index != candidate_translation.pat_index
+            || source_translation.raw_leaf_entry & !hardware_tracking_bits

+            || candidate_translation.physical_address != expected_physical

+                virtual_address,
+                source_translation,
+                candidate_translation,
+                expected_physical
+            );
+            return false;
+        }
+        let Some(next_offset) = offset.checked_add(rustix_kernel::paging::PAGE_SIZE) else {
+            return false;
+        };
+        offset = next_offset;
+    }

+#[cfg(feature = "probe-hhdm-frame")]
+fn probe_candidate_page_tables(boot_info: &mut boot::BootInfo) {
+    use rustix_kernel::paging::{
+        validate_mapping_range, CachePolicy, CandidatePageTables, PagePermissions, PageWalkOutcome,
+    };
+
+    let Some(physical_address_bits) = boot_info.cpu_info.physical_address_bits else {
+        kprintln!("candidate page-table probe failed: physical width unknown");
+        halt_forever();
+    };
+    if !boot_info.cpu_info.nx_enabled || !boot_info.cpu_info.normal_caching {
+        kprintln!("candidate page-table probe failed: NXE or normal caching unavailable");
+        halt_forever();
+    }
+    let pat_value = boot_info
+        .cpu_info
+        .pat_msr_value
+        .expect("inherited cache-alias probe validated active PAT");
+    let pat = rustix_kernel::paging::PatLayout::from_msr_value(pat_value).unwrap_or_else(|error| {
+        kprintln!(
+            "candidate page-table probe failed: invalid PAT: {:?}",
+            error
+        );
+        halt_forever();
+    });
+    let registers = match &boot_info.cpu_info.mtrr {
+        rustix_kernel::paging::MtrrState::Captured(registers) => registers,
+        _ => {
+            kprintln!("candidate page-table probe failed: captured MTRR state unavailable");
+            halt_forever();
+        }
+    };
+    let mtrrs = match registers.validated_layout(physical_address_bits) {
+        Ok(mtrrs) => mtrrs,
+        Err(error) => {
+            kprintln!(
+                "candidate page-table probe failed: invalid MTRR: {:?}",
+                error
+            );
+            halt_forever();
+        }
+    };
+    let config = rustix_kernel::paging::PageWalkConfig {
+        levels: if boot_info.cpu_info.active_linear_address_bits == 57 {
+            5
+        } else {
+            4
+        },
+        physical_address_bits,
+        virtual_address_bits: boot_info.cpu_info.active_linear_address_bits,
+        nx_enabled: true,
+        page_2m_supported: true,
+        page_1g_supported: boot_info.cpu_info.has_1g_pages,
+    };
+    let virtual_address = 0xffff_9000_ffff_f000;
+    let permissions = PagePermissions {
+        writable: true,
+        executable: false,
+        user_accessible: false,
+    };
+    let frame = match boot_info.frame_allocator.allocate() {
+        Some(frame) => frame,
+        None => {
+            kprintln!("candidate page-table probe failed: no leaf frame available");
+            halt_forever();
+        }
+    };
+    let mapping = match validate_mapping_range(
+        virtual_address,
+        frame.address(),
+        rustix_kernel::paging::PAGE_SIZE,
+        permissions,
+        Some(physical_address_bits),
+        config.virtual_address_bits,
+    ) {
+        Ok(mapping) => mapping,
+        Err(error) => {
+            kprintln!(
+                "candidate page-table probe failed: invalid mapping: {:?}",
+                error
+            );
+            release_probe_frame(&mut boot_info.frame_allocator, frame);
+            halt_forever();
+        }
+    };
+    let cache_attributes = match mapping.select_cache_attributes(
+        CachePolicy::WriteBack,
+        pat,
+        &mtrrs,
+        boot_info.cpu_info.normal_caching,
+    ) {
+        Ok(attributes) => attributes,
+        Err(error) => {
+            kprintln!(
+                "candidate page-table probe failed: cache policy: {:?}",
+                error
+            );
+            release_probe_frame(&mut boot_info.frame_allocator, frame);
+            halt_forever();
+        }
+    };
+
+    let mut memory = LimineHhdmCandidateMemory {
+        memory_map: &boot_info.memory_map,
+        hhdm_offset: boot_info.hhdm_offset,
+        physical_address_bits,
+        virtual_address_bits: boot_info.cpu_info.active_linear_address_bits,
+    };
+    let mut candidate =
+        match CandidatePageTables::new(&mut boot_info.frame_allocator, &mut memory, config) {
+            Ok(candidate) => candidate,
+            Err(error) => {
+                kprintln!(
+                    "candidate page-table probe failed to create root: {:?}",
+                    error.cause
+                );
+                release_probe_frame(&mut boot_info.frame_allocator, frame);
+                if let Some(root_frame) = error.frame {
+                    release_probe_frame(&mut boot_info.frame_allocator, root_frame);
+                }
+                halt_forever();
+            }
+        };
+    let root = candidate.root_physical_address();
+    let frame_address = frame.address();
+    if let Err(failure) = candidate.map_owned_page(
+        &mut boot_info.frame_allocator,
+        frame,
+        mapping,
+        cache_attributes,
+    ) {
+        kprintln!(
+            "candidate page-table probe failed to map leaf: {:?}",
+            failure.cause
+        );
+        release_probe_frame(&mut boot_info.frame_allocator, failure.frame);
+        release_candidate_after_probe_failure(candidate, &mut boot_info.frame_allocator);
+    }
+
+    let walk = candidate.walk(virtual_address);
+    let returned_frame = match candidate.unmap_owned_page(virtual_address) {
+        Ok(frame) => frame,
+        Err(error) => {
+            kprintln!(
+                "candidate page-table probe failed to unmap leaf: {:?}",
+                error
+            );
+            release_candidate_after_probe_failure(candidate, &mut boot_info.frame_allocator);
+        }
+    };
+    let translation_valid = match &walk {
+        Ok(PageWalkOutcome::Mapped(translation)) => {
+            translation.physical_address == frame_address
+                && translation.page_size == rustix_kernel::paging::PAGE_SIZE
+                && translation.permissions == permissions
+                && translation.pat_index == cache_attributes.pat_index()
+        }
+        _ => false,
+    };
+    if returned_frame.address() != frame_address {
+        kprintln!("candidate page-table probe failed: unmap returned the wrong frame");
+        release_probe_frame(&mut boot_info.frame_allocator, returned_frame);
+        release_candidate_after_probe_failure(candidate, &mut boot_info.frame_allocator);
+    }
+    release_probe_frame(&mut boot_info.frame_allocator, returned_frame);
+    if !translation_valid {
+        kprintln!(
+            "candidate page-table probe failed: candidate walk: {:?}",
+            walk
+        );
+        release_candidate_after_probe_failure(candidate, &mut boot_info.frame_allocator);
+    }
+    if let Err(failure) = candidate.release(&mut boot_info.frame_allocator) {
+        kprintln!(
+            "candidate page-table probe failed to release frames: {:?}",
+            failure
+        );
+        halt_forever();
+    }
+    kprintln!(
+        "candidate page-table probe passed: mapped, walked, unmapped, and released root {:#x}; CR3 unchanged",
+        root.expect("candidate retains root until release")
+    );
+}
+
+fn release_candidate_after_probe_failure(
+    candidate: rustix_kernel::paging::CandidatePageTables<'_, LimineHhdmCandidateMemory<'_>>,
+    allocator: &mut rustix_kernel::frame::FrameAllocator,
+) -> ! {
+    if let Err(failure) = candidate.release(allocator) {
+        kprintln!("candidate page-table cleanup also failed: {:?}", failure);
+    }
+    halt_forever()
+}
+
+#[cfg(feature = "probe-hhdm-frame")]
+fn verify_inherited_mapping(
+    reader: &impl rustix_kernel::paging::PageTableReader<
+        Error = rustix_kernel::memory::HhdmAddressError,
+    >,
+    root: rustix_kernel::paging::Cr3Root,
+    config: rustix_kernel::paging::PageWalkConfig,
+    label: &str,
+    virtual_start: u64,
+    physical_start: u64,
+    length: u64,
+) {
+    use rustix_kernel::paging::{walk_virtual_address, PageWalkOutcome};
+
+    let mut offset = 0;
+    let mut pages = 0;
+    let mut first_translation: Option<rustix_kernel::paging::PageTranslation> = None;
+    let mut permissions_uniform = true;
+    let mut pat_index_uniform = true;
+    while offset < length {
+        let virtual_address = match virtual_start.checked_add(offset) {
+            Some(address) => address,
+            None => {
+                kprintln!("inherited mapping probe failed: {} virtual overflow", label);
+                halt_forever();
+            }
+        };
+        let expected_physical = match physical_start.checked_add(offset) {
+            Some(address) => address,
+            None => {
+                kprintln!(
+                    "inherited mapping probe failed: {} physical overflow",
+                    label
+                );
+                halt_forever();
+            }
+        };
+        let translation = match walk_virtual_address(reader, root, virtual_address, config) {
+            Ok(PageWalkOutcome::Mapped(translation)) => translation,
+            Ok(PageWalkOutcome::NotPresent { level }) => {
+                if level == rustix_kernel::paging::PageLevel::Pml4 {
+                    let pml4_index = ((virtual_address >> 39) & 0x1ff) as u16;
+                    let root_entry = reader.read_entry(root.physical_address(), pml4_index);
+                    kprintln!(
+                        "inherited mapping PML4 detail: VA={:#018x}, index={}, root={:#x}, entry={:?}",
+                        virtual_address,
+                        pml4_index,
+                        root.physical_address(),
+                        root_entry
+                    );
+                }
+                kprintln!(
+                    "inherited mapping probe failed: {} absent at {:?}",
+                    label,
+                    level
+                );
+                halt_forever();
+            }
+            Err(error) => {
+                kprintln!("inherited mapping probe failed: {}: {:?}", label, error);
+                halt_forever();
+            }
+        };
+        if translation.physical_address != expected_physical {
+            kprintln!(
+                "inherited mapping probe failed: {} {:#018x} mapped to {:#018x}, expected {:#018x}",
+                label,
+                virtual_address,
+                translation.physical_address,
+                expected_physical
+            );
+            halt_forever();
+        }
+        if let Some(first) = first_translation {
+            permissions_uniform &= translation.permissions == first.permissions;
+            pat_index_uniform &= translation.pat_index == first.pat_index;
+        } else {
+            first_translation = Some(translation);
+        }
+        pages += 1;
+        offset += rustix_kernel::paging::PAGE_SIZE;
+    }
+    if let Some(first) = first_translation {
+        kprintln!(
+            "inherited mapping probe passed: {} ({} pages), first permissions={:?}, PAT index={}, leaf size={}, uniform permissions={}, uniform PAT index={}",
+            label,
+            pages,
+            first.permissions,
+            first.pat_index,
+            first.page_size,
+            permissions_uniform,
+            pat_index_uniform
+        );
+    }
+}
+

+fn verify_kernel_cache_aliases(
+    boot_info: &boot::BootInfo,
+    reader: &impl rustix_kernel::paging::PageTableReader<

+    >,
+    root: rustix_kernel::paging::Cr3Root,

+    mtrrs: &rustix_kernel::paging::ValidatedMtrrLayout,
+    label: &str,
+    kernel_virtual_start: u64,
+    physical_start: u64,
+    length: u64,
+) {
+    use rustix_kernel::paging::{walk_virtual_address, PageWalkOutcome};
+
+    let mut offset = 0;
+    let mut pages = 0;
+    while offset < length {
+        let physical = match physical_start.checked_add(offset) {
+            Some(address) => address,
+            None => {
+                kprintln!("cache-alias probe failed: {} physical overflow", label);
+                halt_forever();
+            }
+        };
+        let kernel_virtual = match kernel_virtual_start.checked_add(offset) {
+            Some(address) => address,
+            None => {
+                kprintln!("cache-alias probe failed: {} virtual overflow", label);
+                halt_forever();
+            }
+        };
+        let hhdm_virtual = match boot_info.memory_map.limine_hhdm_address(
+            boot_info.hhdm_offset,
+            physical,
+            rustix_kernel::paging::PAGE_SIZE,
+            boot_info.cpu_info.physical_address_bits,
+            boot_info.cpu_info.active_linear_address_bits,
+        ) {
+            Ok(address) => address,
+            Err(error) => {
+                kprintln!(
+                    "cache-alias probe failed: {} HHDM range: {:?}",
+                    label,
+                    error
+                );
+                halt_forever();
+            }
+        };
+        let kernel_translation = match walk_virtual_address(reader, root, kernel_virtual, config) {
+            Ok(PageWalkOutcome::Mapped(translation)) => translation,
+            result => {
+                kprintln!(
+                    "cache-alias probe failed: {} kernel walk: {:?}",
+                    label,
+                    result
+                );
+                halt_forever();
+            }
+        };
+        let hhdm_translation = match walk_virtual_address(reader, root, hhdm_virtual, config) {
+            Ok(PageWalkOutcome::Mapped(translation)) => translation,
+            result => {
+                kprintln!(
+                    "cache-alias probe failed: {} HHDM walk: {:?}",
+                    label,
+                    result
+                );
+                halt_forever();
+            }
+        };
+        if kernel_translation.physical_address != physical
+            || hhdm_translation.physical_address != physical
+        {
+            kprintln!(
+                "cache-alias probe failed: {} physical {:#018x} has inconsistent translations",
+                label,
+                physical
+            );
+            halt_forever();
+        }
+        let kernel_type = match mtrrs.effective_memory_type_for(
+            physical,
+            pat,
+            kernel_translation.pat_index,
+            boot_info.cpu_info.normal_caching,
+        ) {
+            Ok(memory_type) => memory_type,
+            Err(error) => {
+                kprintln!(
+                    "cache-alias probe failed: {} kernel PAT/MTRR: {:?}",
+                    label,
+                    error
+                );
+                halt_forever();
+            }
+        };
+        let hhdm_type = match mtrrs.effective_memory_type_for(
+            physical,
+            pat,
+            hhdm_translation.pat_index,
+            boot_info.cpu_info.normal_caching,
+        ) {
+            Ok(memory_type) => memory_type,
+            Err(error) => {
+                kprintln!(
+                    "cache-alias probe failed: {} HHDM PAT/MTRR: {:?}",
+                    label,
+                    error
+                );
+                halt_forever();
+            }
+        };
+        if kernel_type != hhdm_type {
+            kprintln!(
+                "cache-alias conflict: {} PA {:#018x}, kernel {:?} vs HHDM {:?}",
+                label,
+                physical,
+                kernel_type,
+                hhdm_type
+            );
+            halt_forever();
+        }
+        pages += 1;
+        offset += rustix_kernel::paging::PAGE_SIZE;
+    }
+    kprintln!(
+        "cache-alias probe passed: {} ({} pages; effective types match)",
+        label,
+        pages
+    );
+}
+
+fn release_probe_frame(
+    allocator: &mut rustix_kernel::frame::FrameAllocator,
+    frame: rustix_kernel::frame::Frame,
+) {
+    if let Err(error) = allocator.deallocate(frame) {
+        kprintln!(
+            "HHDM frame probe failed to return its frame: {:?}",
+            error.error
+        );
+        halt_forever();
+    }
+}

The heap is fixed-capacity and does not grow from frames; allocation is prohibited in interrupt context. # Rustix roadmap

This roadmap describes an incremental path from the current bare-metal kernel to a useful Unix-like operating system. It is a dependency plan, not a schedule or a claim of compatibility. Features become current only after the implementation, tests, and exit criteria below agree.

## How to read status

- A checked box means the source/design work exists; it does **not** imply the code compiled, linked, booted, or passed an integration test.
- A milestone is not complete until its stated exit criteria are met and the evidence is recorded.
- Hardware work needs target build and emulator evidence. Host tests cannot validate privileged instructions, bootloader pointers, page tables, device I/O, or exception-entry assembly.
- Future work is intentionally not represented by placeholder APIs or dummy implementations.

## Current status

- **Milestone 0: local exit criteria met from a clean detached worktree; hosted CI pending.** On 2026-10-16, `just verify` passed in WSL2 Ubuntu 24.04 from both the working tree and a clean detached worktree with an empty `target` directory. The clean run downloaded and compiled the pinned Limine host utility, formatted and tested the workspace, checked and built the target, created the image, and passed the 20-second QEMU prompt smoke test. Hosted CI has not been observed.
- **Milestone 1: validation criteria met for the current Limine path.** The bounded boot snapshot, memory-range classification, and CPUID reporting were covered by host tests and QEMU reporting; the Limine pointer-readability trust boundary remains explicit.
- **Milestone 2: local exit criteria met on 2026-10-24; hosted CI and physical-hardware validation remain pending.** The boot path owns and activates a clone of Limine's reachable page-table hierarchy, preserves inherited mappings, hardens kernel HHDM aliases to R/NX or RW/NX while retaining PAT attributes, invalidates stale translations on CR3 transitions, and retains table-frame tokens. `just verify`, `just frame-smoke`, and `just fault-smoke` passed after final review; QEMU exercised the active-PCID/CR3 invalidation path with CR4.PGE clear. The PGE-toggle path is statically reviewed but was not exercised by this QEMU configuration. The bounded heap does not grow from frames; broad mapping policy, reclamation, IRQ-safe allocation, and physical-hardware validation remain outside this milestone's completed scope.
- **Milestones 3 and later: planned.** There is no general IRQ system, scheduler, userspace, syscall ABI, persistent filesystem, GUI, or networking stack.

## Dependency path

```text
Reliable boot
    -> validated boot state
    -> owned mappings + frame allocation + heap + fault diagnostics
    -> timer/IRQ model + scheduler
    -> isolated processes + syscall ABI
    -> VFS/storage + userland utilities
    -> graphical terminal and other optional services
```

Some device-driver work can proceed in parallel after the core ownership, locking, and testing rules exist. It must not bypass them with direct, unreviewed hardware access.

## Milestone 2 — memory ownership, paging, heap, and exceptions (local exit criteria met)

This milestone establishes a safe basis for future allocation and kernel services. HHDM access is limited to checked full-frame token paths that rely on Limine's documented contract. The boot path clones the complete reachable inherited hierarchy and activates it only after validating the requested stack span, kernel segments, candidate-root HHDM alias, and kernel-image HHDM permissions.

### Source work present

- [x] Fixed-capacity frame allocator over validated `Usable` ranges, with page alignment, first-MiB reservation, deallocation, coalescing, bounded metadata, and host tests (`src/frame.rs`).
- [x] Initialize allocator metadata from the boot snapshot and expose counts through Crabshell `meminfo`.
- [x] Specify frame-token ownership and failure semantics: `Frame` is non-copyable, failed deallocation returns the token without changing allocator state, and the current API documents (but does not enforce) one allocator instance per physical map.
- [x] Bootstrap GDT/TSS/IDT and fatal handlers for exception vectors 0–31.
- [x] Give double faults a dedicated IST stack; report saved register/error context and CR2/error bits for page faults.
- [x] Keep maskable IRQ delivery disabled; current exception handling is fatal-only.

### Required memory-management work

- [x] Read `CR4.LA57` and `CPUID.80000008H` when available to report active/max address widths; validate Limine pointers against active canonical width and host-test 48-/57-bit boundaries.
- [x] Document base revision 3 HHDM region coverage, page-boundary behavior, and x86 permissions/cache attributes. HHDM access is limited to opt-in, checked frame and candidate-table probes relying on the protocol contract; there is no general physical-memory service.
- [x] Reject physical map ranges outside the reported CPUID width when available; validate page-rounded HHDM address arithmetic/canonicality for base revision 3 mapped types. This is protocol-derived validation, not a page-table walk or proof of pointer readability.
- [x] Record current transition-critical objects, their mapping sources/permissions, and unresolved bounds in `docs/architecture/memory.md`.
- [x] Capture Limine's executable physical/virtual bases and resolve the complete linker-defined half-open kernel-image span in `BootInfo`; validate the linker/loader base agreement, canonical virtual span, arithmetic, and reported physical width.
- [x] Capture and validate the linker-defined page-aligned text, rodata, and data segment bounds in `BootInfo`; host-test their ordering, contiguity, rounded image coverage, and derived physical ranges. `just verify` reported all three in QEMU on 2026-10-21. This metadata does not prove inherited page-table coverage or live permissions.
- [x] Request a 256 KiB Limine x86_64 stack, require its response, and capture/validate the requested span from entry `RSP`; verify its HHDM translation and `BootloaderReclaimable` backing. `just frame-smoke` walked all 64 pages in QEMU. This request fixed stack-frame overflow in the diagnostic path.
- [x] Record that Limine guarantees at least the requested stack size but does not report the larger allocation's exact bounds or guard status; preserve the requested 256 KiB span and do not infer a guard page.
- [x] Decode the inherited CR3 root address and interpret its low bits using the reported physical-address width and active `CR4.PCIDE` state; host-test reserved-bit and width rejection. `just frame-smoke` reads the root, walks kernel segments and the requested stack span, compares effective PAT/MTRR types for kernel-image/HHDM aliases, and exercises the active-root transition.
- [x] Document the active clone's kernel alias W^X policy, inherited cache behavior, MMIO limits, huge-page splitting, stack bounds, and inherited-root preservation in `docs/architecture/memory.md`.
- [x] Clone every reachable present inherited page-table hierarchy entry into allocator-owned table frames, preserving inherited leaves and non-present entries. Validate kernel segments, the full requested stack span, candidate-root HHDM access, and critical paths; keep the inherited root and backing frames untouched.
- [x] Add pure host-tested 4 KiB mapping-range validation and leaf-PTE bit encoding. Validation requires alignment, checked bounds, known physical width, canonical virtual ranges, and W^X; encoding bounds the physical width and PAT index and requires NXE for non-executable entries. These helpers alone do not prove frame ownership, mapping coverage, or PAT cache semantics, and do not touch tables.
- [x] Implement a bounded candidate-root builder for 4 KiB mappings backed by allocator-issued table and leaf tokens. It requires NXE, uses range-bound PAT attributes, restricts walks to owned tables, and holds a unique mutable backend borrow. Mapping preflights the path and prepares all missing tables before linking them; host tests cover 4-/5-level paths, W^X, ownership rejection, and rollback. An active-state guard prevents candidate mutation/release while CR3 names its root.
- [x] Ensure candidate mapping failure (including frame exhaustion and prepare failure) rolls back partial page-table allocations without changing the active root. Host tests cover rollback and retryable release failure; `just frame-smoke` maps, walks, unmaps, and releases a separate candidate mapping in QEMU.
- [x] Validate and activate the cloned root in QEMU, preserving CR3 low-bit mode, invalidating the active PCID, and flushing global translations when CR4.PGE is enabled; verify the active CR3 plus critical translations after the switch. On failure, restore and verify the inherited root with the same TLB invalidation before releasing the inactive candidate.
- [x] Add host tests for raw PTE-bit encoding and parsing a supplied PAT layout to find WB/UC/WC indexes.
- [x] Read EFER.NXE only when NX is supported and read `IA32_PAT` only when PAT is supported; report these read-only values and recognized PAT indexes at boot.
- [x] Host-test that rejected deallocations preserve free-range state and return the frame token for unaligned, unmanaged, already-free, and range-table-full cases.
- [x] Add a pure host-tested MTRR decoder/resolver for supplied fixed and variable register values, including disabled-MTRR behavior and overlap rules. Host tests and `just verify` passed on 2026-10-21.
- [x] Capture supported MTRR capability, default-type, fixed-range, and variable-range registers read-only at boot. Retain at most 32 variable pairs; report capacity overflow explicitly without a partial snapshot. Host tests cover feature gating, supported fixed/variable register reads, unsupported fixed ranges, and capacity overflow. `just verify` passed on 2026-10-22; the QEMU serial log reported the live MTRR summary.
- [x] Validate captured MTRR capability/default-type bits, register counts and fixed-range availability, WC support, and variable-range mask/alignment; resolve the Intel SDM Table 11-7 PAT/MTRR combinations for one physical address only when `CR0.CD=0` and `CR0.NW=0`. Host tests cover all 30 documented type pairs and malformed inputs. Boot validates the captured PAT/MTRR state and prints a diagnostic resolution at PA 0; `just verify` passed on 2026-10-22. This policy helper does not establish the cache type of an inherited mapping.
- [x] Add a pure range-level PAT selector that returns an index only when it yields the requested effective type across every fixed/variable MTRR transition in the aligned physical range. Host tests cover variable boundaries, fixed-range transitions, no-uniform-index failure, and malformed range inputs. This remains policy-only and does not inspect live PTEs or aliases.
- [x] Compose range-level PAT selection with validated mapping metadata; bind the selected attributes to the physical extent and use them to encode individual 4 KiB leaves. Host tests cover a range crossing variable-MTRR types, width mismatch, and rejecting attributes for a different extent. This does not inspect inherited PTEs, establish frame ownership, or detect cache aliases.
- [x] Calculate HHDM addresses only for allocator-issued frame tokens whose complete page remains in a validated `Usable` region, with known physical width and checked protocol bounds. `just frame-smoke` passed in QEMU: one frame was written, read, cleared, and returned to the allocator. This relies on Limine's base revision 3 HHDM guarantee and does not inspect live PTEs or validate arbitrary physical addresses.
- [x] Validate the inherited CR3 root's numeric HHDM location only when its page lies wholly in a validated `BootloaderReclaimable` region and address-width arithmetic passes. Host tests reject unknown widths and other region types; `just frame-smoke` reads the 512 root entries in QEMU and confirms the HHDM access.
- [x] Add a bounded read-only 4-/5-level page-table walker with synthetic host tests for translations, permissions, PAT selection bits, 2 MiB pages, and absent entries. The opt-in QEMU probe follows every page in linker-defined text/rodata/data spans and the requested stack span, checking translations and effective cache types for kernel-image/HHDM aliases.
- [x] Add host-tested candidate page-table mapping/unmapping and transactional ownership handling; `just frame-smoke` verifies a separate candidate root can map, walk, unmap, and release one frame without changing CR3. The default boot path separately activates an inherited-root clone after critical translation and kernel-alias permission/cache checks.
- [x] Harden kernel-image HHDM aliases before activation: text/rodata become R/NX and data/BSS become RW/NX. Split inherited 1 GiB/2 MiB mappings as needed while preserving translation and PAT bits. Host tests cover both large-page splits; QEMU verifies every kernel-image alias retains its physical translation, desired permissions, and PAT index.
- [x] Add a 256 KiB BSS-backed global heap with 128 allocation records, first-fit aligned placement, exact-layout free/reuse, deterministic arena/metadata exhaustion, and an explicit prohibition on interrupt-context allocation. Host tests cover alignment, reuse, exhaustion, and invalid frees; the QEMU boot probe exercises the global allocator before entering the shell. The arena is fixed and does not grow from physical frames.

### Required exception/descriptor validation

- [x] Source contains GDT/TSS/IDT setup and normalized stubs for architectural exception vectors 0–31; double fault uses IST1.
- [x] Target-assemble/link and inspect the stubs and descriptor setup; ELF disassembly confirms call-stack alignment and the error-code normalization paths, while compile-time size assertions pin the IDT, TSS, and exception-context layouts.
- [x] Add QEMU fault-injection tests for a controlled page fault and invalid opcode. `just fault-smoke` verifies vector diagnostics, the exact CR2 address, no shell prompt or return marker, and that QEMU remains halted until its timeout; it then restores the default release kernel and ISO.
- [x] Boot the descriptor setup and both tested exception paths in QEMU. These checks cover only the injected page fault and invalid opcode, not all vectors or physical hardware.

**Exit criteria:** met locally on 2026-10-24. `just verify`, `just frame-smoke`, and `just fault-smoke` passed after final review, covering host tests, the target build, active cloned-root boot, frame and candidate-map probes, heap behavior, and fatal page-fault/invalid-opcode diagnostics. The QEMU configuration reported CR4.PGE clear and exercised the CR3 reload path; the PGE-toggle global-TLB path is statically reviewed but was not exercised in QEMU. The active hierarchy preserves Limine's complete reachable mapping graph and hardens the kernel-image HHDM aliases; it is not a clean-room address-space policy, does not reclaim the old root or leaf frames, and has no general active mapping service. Hosted CI and physical-hardware validation remain pending and are not claimed by this local exit status.

## Milestone 3 — IRQs, time, and kernel scheduling

Do not enable interrupts as a side effect of installing exception gates. IRQ delivery needs its own controller, acknowledgement, masking, ownership, and synchronization design.

### Planned work

- [ ] Select and document the initial interrupt controller policy for QEMU and target hardware (for example, legacy PIC compatibility versus local I/O APIC; do not enable both accidentally).
- [ ] Add IRQ vector allocation, controller masking/unmasking, end-of-interrupt acknowledgement, spurious-interrupt handling, and a policy for unexpected IRQs.
- [ ] Add a calibrated/verified timer source and monotonic timekeeping; test interval arithmetic and drift assumptions.
- [ ] Establish interrupt-safe lock primitives and rules for code callable from normal, exception, and IRQ contexts. No allocator or blocking console operation may run in an unsafe interrupt context.
- [ ] Add a minimal kernel-thread context and lifecycle model, stack ownership/guard policy, context-switch tests, and emulator scheduling tests.
- [ ] Add preemption only after lock, stack, timer, and interrupt-return invariants have deterministic tests.
- [ ] Keep application-processor startup/SMP as a separate sub-milestone after per-CPU state, TLB invalidation, and lock semantics exist.

**Exit criteria:** tested IRQ acknowledgement and timer behavior, deterministic thread lifecycle/context-switch tests, and bounded QEMU tests under repeated timer interrupts. No `sti` before the design and tests are ready.

---

## Milestone 4 — isolated processes and syscall ABI

Userspace begins only after page tables, exception handling, scheduling, and controlled memory allocation are trustworthy. The syscall ABI is a product interface and must not emerge accidentally from internal functions.

### Planned work

- [ ] Decide and document the x86_64 user-entry/syscall mechanism, register convention, selector/MSR setup, per-CPU state requirements, and safe return path.
- [ ] Add user/kernel page permissions and process-owned address spaces, including teardown and TLB invalidation rules.
- [ ] Implement copy-in/copy-out helpers that validate lengths, arithmetic, canonical ranges, permissions, and faults; never form a kernel reference directly from a user pointer.
- [ ] Specify version discovery, stable syscall numbers, argument layouts, error encoding, partial-I/O behavior, interruption/restart, and compatibility policy before exposing calls.
- [ ] Add initial process lifecycle and descriptor-table semantics: create/load, exit, wait, close, duplication/inheritance, and process cleanup.
- [ ] Load a deliberately small documented executable format with bounds/segment/permission checks; reject malformed binaries safely.
- [ ] Build adversarial tests for bad pointers, overflow, invalid mappings, process teardown, descriptor misuse, and failed exec.

### First user-visible target

A small controlled `init` process should start from a reproducible image, write through a descriptor, exit with a status, and be waited on by a kernel test harness. Do not claim userspace or process isolation from ring-0 tasks that merely use process-shaped structs.

**Exit criteria:** an isolated init process runs in user mode and uses a versioned, documented syscall subset; invalid user pointers and process teardown are tested without corrupting the kernel.

---

## Milestone 5 — VFS, storage, and device ownership

Keep the current RAM filesystem as a bootstrap/test implementation. Persistence and device drivers require explicit block ownership, error handling, and recovery behavior.

### Planned work

- [ ] Define VFS node, mount, path, metadata, and file-descriptor contracts independently of a particular disk format.
- [ ] Preserve volatile RAMFS as a test backend and add tests for mount/path errors, capacity, partial I/O, and object lifetime.
- [ ] Add a narrowly scoped block-device interface with request validation, timeout/error reporting, and a QEMU-supported initial device driver (such as virtio-blk after PCI discovery is ready).
- [ ] Choose and document the first on-disk filesystem format. Specify partition discovery, byte order, block size, metadata limits, corruption handling, and read-only/recovery behavior before writable support.
- [ ] Add persistent write/read/remount/reboot integration tests; never claim persistence from an in-memory cache alone.
- [ ] Add a driver ownership and DMA policy before any device can write into arbitrary kernel memory.
- [ ] Define file descriptors and basic process I/O semantics before exposing them to applications.

**Exit criteria:** a reproducible image mounts a documented on-disk filesystem, user-visible tools can create/read files across reboot, and corruption/I/O errors fail safely.

---

## Milestone 6 — initial userspace and command-line utilities

Crabshell is currently an in-kernel parser/frontend. The long-term terminal application should reuse its parser model without linking kernel internals or bypassing syscalls.

### Planned work

- [ ] Start a user-mode `init` process and establish executable search, environment, current directory, descriptor inheritance, and process startup rules.
- [ ] Port or adapt Crabshell into a userspace terminal application that uses only the documented syscall/VFS interfaces.
- [ ] Add a small utility set with explicit scope: file listing, text output, create/remove/copy/move, and system information.
- [ ] Add command-line quoting, escaping, history, redirection, and pipelines only with parser tests and process/descriptor/pipe semantics to support them.
- [ ] Add integration tests that launch tools from the filesystem image and exercise them through syscalls; keep unsupported features explicit.

**Exit criteria:** shell and basic tools run as isolated user processes from a reproducible image; no shell command directly calls kernel-private VFS internals.

---

## Milestone 7 — graphical console and GUI (long-term)

A GUI is intentionally downstream of stable memory management, interrupts/input, process isolation, drivers, and userspace. Keep Crabshell's parser independent so a graphical terminal frontend can reuse it.

### Planned work

- [ ] Add validated framebuffer discovery and memory ownership; implement a minimal text/graphics console without compromising serial panic diagnostics.
- [ ] Establish an input subsystem that separates raw device events from key mapping and terminal policy. Plan PS/2 and USB HID support separately; do not treat the current raw scancode poller as a keyboard driver stack.
- [ ] Define a graphics buffer ownership/presentation API, clipping rules, pixel format, and bounds/overflow checks.
- [ ] Implement a minimal compositor/windowing policy only after process isolation and input routing are ready.
- [ ] Run Crabshell as a terminal application in a GUI window using the same parser and userspace services as the serial/TTY path.
- [ ] Preserve serial as a headless recovery/debug console and add repeatable QEMU display/input tests.

**Exit criteria:** a documented GUI session starts from userspace, renders a terminal, accepts tested input, and does not require direct kernel-private VFS access.

---

## Milestone 8 — networking (long-term, after drivers and process isolation)

Networking is not implied by the current device drivers. The initial target should be a tightly scoped virtual-device path with clear ownership and bounded buffers.

### Planned work

- [ ] Complete PCI/device discovery and define DMA buffer ownership, address translation, cache synchronization, and reset/error behavior.
- [ ] Implement one virtual NIC driver with bounded queues and timeouts; test against QEMU user networking.
- [ ] Choose and document a minimal link/network protocol scope before implementation. Keep packet parsing length-checked and fuzzable on the host.
- [ ] Add interface configuration, routing, socket/descriptor ownership, and per-process access policy.
- [ ] Add adversarial packet tests and integration tests for link loss, malformed packets, queue exhaustion, and device reset.
- [ ] Add higher-level transports/services only when the required protocol semantics, entropy source, and security model are designed.

**Exit criteria:** documented user processes can communicate through a tested virtual NIC/network stack, with malformed input and resource exhaustion handled safely. Do not claim internet, TLS, or POSIX sockets merely from a packet driver.

---

## Cross-cutting acceptance gates

Every milestone should include the relevant subset of these gates:

1. **Design:** documented ownership, invariants, resource limits, error semantics, and unsupported cases.
2. **Tests:** host tests for pure policy and malformed/boundary input; integration tests for hardware-facing behavior.
3. **Safety:** review unsafe blocks, pointer provenance/access, integer overflow, privilege boundaries, concurrency, and cleanup/rollback paths.
4. **Build:** format, host tests, target check, and final ELF link as appropriate.
5. **Boot/integration:** QEMU tests for changes to boot, paging, descriptors, interrupts, drivers, processes, or persistence.
6. **Documentation/status:** update architecture and roadmap docs; never check off a criterion without evidence.
7. **Compatibility:** claim Unix/POSIX behavior only for the exact documented subset with conformance-style tests.

## Working rule

Prefer a small end-to-end vertical slice over broad, unbootable scaffolding. A source file, interface, or architecture document is not proof that the corresponding subsystem is operational. When a check cannot run, record the exact environment blocker and leave that acceptance gate pending.

```


**Tool Call: AGENTS.md**
Status: Completed

Diff: AGENTS.md
```
# Rustix agent instructions

These instructions apply to every coding agent working in this repository. Read this file before changing code. For the architecture and detailed subsystem contracts, use the linked documents under `docs/`; this file summarizes the rules agents must preserve.

## Project mission

Rustix is an experimental 64-bit, Unix-like operating system with its own Rust kernel. Limine is the external boot protocol/loader only. Do not describe Limine, a host shell, or a userspace project as the Rustix kernel.

The kernel is `no_std` and targets `x86_64-unknown-none`. Rust is the implementation language for kernel and OS components. The repository currently uses a Python standard-library script only to assemble and smoke-test the boot image; it does not replace kernel or OS functionality.

Unix-like behavior is a long-term design goal, not a claim of POSIX compatibility. Make unsupported behavior explicit rather than approximating it silently.

## Current project status — read before planning

The source contains:

- A Limine-based x86_64 kernel entry, linker layout, serial diagnostics, and boot-memory reporting.
- A separate allocation-free `no_std` `crabshell` parser crate and a kernel-mode COM1 shell frontend.
- A volatile, fixed-capacity RAM filesystem used by the shell.
- A validated, fixed-capacity boot memory-map snapshot, CPUID/address-width reporting, read-only CR0 caching-mode reporting, and gated read-only EFER.NXE/IA32_PAT/MTRR reporting.
- A fixed-capacity physical frame allocator retained in `BootInfo`; Crabshell's `meminfo` command reports counts. The opt-in `probe-hhdm-frame` QEMU feature allocates, validates, writes, reads, clears, and returns one `Usable` frame through Limine's HHDM contract. `src/paging.rs` has a bounded candidate-root builder that owns allocator-issued table/leaf tokens and maps/unmaps 4 KiB leaves transactionally. The default boot path clones and activates the full reachable inherited hierarchy, hardens kernel-image HHDM aliases to R/NX or RW/NX while preserving PAT bits, and retains the active table tokens. A 256 KiB BSS-backed global heap is installed; it has fixed capacity and does not grow from frames.
- Pure 4 KiB mapping-range validation, leaf-PTE bit encoding, PAT layout parsing, and host-tested MTRR/PAT policy in `src/paging.rs`; these helpers check alignment, address widths, canonical virtual ranges, W^X, NXE input, PAT indices, captured-register validity, MTRR overlap rules, and Intel SDM Table 11-7 effective types under normal caching. Discontinuous variable-MTRR masks are explicitly unsupported. A pure selector chooses a PAT index only when its effective type remains uniform across all MTRR boundaries in an aligned physical range, and range-bound selected attributes can encode 4 KiB leaves. The bounded candidate builder stores its unique mutable table-memory backend borrow, uses allocator-issued `Frame` tokens for table pages and leaf mappings, restricts walks to owned tables, and rolls back failures. Active candidates reject mutation and release. Boot captures CR0 caching mode, EFER.NXE, `IA32_PAT`, and a bounded MTRR snapshot read-only when supported, validates the captured state, and reports a diagnostic PA 0 resolution. QEMU checks the requested 256 KiB stack, active CR3 clone, kernel-image HHDM alias permissions/cache preservation, and heap allocation behavior; the old root and its leaf frames are not reclaimed.
- Bootstrap GDT/TSS/IDT setup and fatal exception handlers for vectors 0–31. Double faults use an IST stack and page faults report CR2. Opt-in QEMU tests inject a page fault and invalid opcode and verify diagnostics plus fatal halt; maskable IRQs remain disabled and exceptions are not recoverable.
